rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but two parts of the stated cause are wrong and must not be fixed as described.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS (440x440, measured by decoding the PNG, plus 4x-9x crops of the base, the blade edges and the spike): a single flat fan of about nine lanceolate blades all radiating from ONE point on the ground, over roughly 180 degrees. Green blade mass measures x104-342 by y185-327 = 239 px wide by 142 px tall, i.e. 1.7x WIDER THAN TALL, with the outermost left and right blades lying nearly horizontal and the ground shadow drawn as a flat ellipse under the convergence point. Rising from the same point is a bare dark-green wire stem that clears the foliage by ~90 px and carries an 11 x 46 px column of small yellow-orange beads (331 px total, hue ~30-45) at y93-138. Nothing else is in the frame.

MUST-READ 1 - 'fountain of broad upright ribbed leaves from ground level': FAILS, and the judge is right about the geometry. There is no fountain and no upright rise; it is a low splayed rosette/fan. Two further defects the judge did not name: (a) the blades are NOT on long sheathing stalks - there are no petioles or leaf sheaths at all, every blade springs from one bare point, so the pseudostem that makes a ginger read as a ginger is absent; (b) the venation is a dicot herringbone - one dark midrib with pinnate laterals branching off at ~45 degrees, clearly visible at 9x on every blade - where turmeric blades are 'ribbed', i.e. parallel longitudinal ribs running tip-to-base. Fixing the splay without fixing the venation and the sheathing stalks will not make it read as turmeric.

CORRECTION 1 - 'they are saw-toothed where turmeric blades are smooth-edged' is FALSE. At 9x magnification every individual blade has a perfectly entire, smooth margin - the right-hand outer blade is one long smooth curve from base to tip with no teeth, lobes or crenations anywhere. The saw-tooth appearance is purely a COMPOSITE SILHOUETTE artifact: the stacked lance blades overlap so their exposed tips form a zigzag along the top edge of the fan. Do not go 'de-serrate the leaves' - there is nothing to de-serrate; the fix is to stop the blades from stacking flat and to widen them.

CORRECTION 2 - 'it reads as nettle or mint' is also wrong. Nettle and mint are opposite-paired toothed leaves climbing an erect square stem; nothing here is paired and there is no leafy stem. What is actually on screen reads as a hosta / broadleaf-plantain rosette (or a small fan palm), topped by a Plantago-style bare flower scape. That matters because the wrong diagnosis points a fix at leaf margins instead of at leaf posture and blade width.

MUST-READ 2 - 'cone of pale green-and-pink bracts at the base': ABSENT, confirmed numerically. A full-image hue scan over all pixels with alpha>40, value>90 and saturation>0.2 returns ZERO pixels in the magenta/pink/red band (hue 290-360 and 0-20). The entire palette is 22,497 px at hue 90 (green), ~370 px at hue 105-150 (darker green veins/stem) and ~400 px at hue 30-45 (the bead spike). So there is no pink anywhere in the asset. The judge is correct that a thin wire with an orange bead spike stands in its place, and correct that the spike is not a bract cone - I would add that it is also in the WRONG PLACE: the bracted inflorescence belongs stout and low, nestled at the leaf bases, whereas this spike is lofted ~90 px clear ABOVE the foliage on a naked scape.

MUST-READ 3 - 'orange-fleshed rhizome': ABSENT, judge correct. The only orange in the image is the 331-px bead column at the top of the scape. The 6x crop of the base shows the blades converging to a bare point over a plain dark elliptical ground shadow - no knobby root mass, no cut face, no orange flesh, no soil line.

Two of the three must-reads are entirely absent and the third is inverted (splayed where it must rise, herringbone where it must be ribbed, stalkless where it must sheathe). FAIL stands. (Packet aspect 0.8 also asks for a form taller than wide; the drawn foliage is 1.7x wider than tall.)

rows.readsAs: a fern frond or a bottlebrush
rows.defect: The tall unbranched stem and the opposite pinnate ladder are present, but the flat-domed pale pink flower head — the crown identity and the harvest — is a tiny white pill barely wider than the stem, roughly a twentieth of the plant's width, with no dome, no florets and no pink. The leaflet ladder is so mechanically uniform (same blade, same pitch, top to bottom, no size gradient) that the silhouette reads as a single fern frond rather than a flowering herb, and it is the same asset as Yarrow in a different green.
rows.fix: Enlarge the terminal head to a wide flat-topped dome of many tiny pale pink-white florets, at least as wide as the foliage, and taper the leaflet ladder so the lower leaves are longer than the upper.

rows.readsAs: the same fern frond as Valerian, one shade greyer
rows.defect: This is Valerian's render with a hue shift — same stem, same shadow, same rung count and pitch, same white apex pill — so a stranger cannot tell the two apart, and neither yarrow must-read survives. The foliage is discrete little oval leaflets in a coarse ladder, not the feather-fine thrice-divided ferny fuzz that is yarrow's signature, and the flat dense PLATE of tiny white florets is reduced to a dot narrower than the leaf spread, when it should be the widest element in the silhouette. The stem is a smooth clean line with no stiff hairiness.
rows.fix: Replace the leaflet ladder with a fine feathery haze of hair-thin dissected segments and cap it with a broad flat white corymb plate spanning the full width of the plant.
rows.verifyWhy:
I read Yarrow.png at full size, then re-cropped and 6x-upscaled the apex (x150-290, y45-165) and the mid-column (y150-270), and ran a pixel diff against Valerian.png. The FAIL stands, and the judge's structural claim is substantially correct, but two of their details need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A single straight dark-olive stem, 4px wide, running from a flat black base-shadow ellipse (y~350) to a bare apex at y~85. Along y=110-305 the stem carries ~23 opposite rungs at a uniform ~8px pitch (measured peaks: 116,123,132,141,149,156,164,173,181,189,197,204,213,221,230,239,250,259,267,279,291,298,305). Each rung is a straight rachis spur angled up-and-out, bearing roughly 8-9 DISCRETE oval leaflets, colour 152,176,136 (a correct pale grey-green per the spec's leafColour). The leaflets are simple beans -- once-pinnate, with no secondary division into thread segments. At the top of a bare 25px section of stem sits a white cap: measured pure-white pixels span x205-235 (w=31px) by y75-84 (h=10px). It is a shallow CRESCENT/dome sitting on a dark triangular receptacle cone, not a flat plate.

MUST-READS. (1) 'ferny feather-fine foliage' -- NOT MET. Real yarrow is bi-to-tripinnate; the foliage should dissolve into a soft thread-fine plume with no countable units. Here every leaflet is individually countable at native size. The spec also says the leaves 'clasp an upright stem'; these do not clasp -- they are borne on projecting rachis spurs, which is Valerian's arrangement. (2) 'a flat dense plate of tiny white daisy florets' -- NOT MET, and this is the fatal one. The corymb is 31px wide against a foliage spread of 66-68px, i.e. LESS THAN HALF the width of the leaf column and about 7% of image width. Yarrow's corymb is the single most diagnostic thing about the plant and should be the WIDEST element in the silhouette; here it is a token pill on a stick. It also reads as one solid domed lozenge, with zero granulation into individual florets, and it is convex rather than flat-topped. (3) 'stiff hairy upright stems' -- half met: upright and stiff yes, but the stem is a perfectly smooth 4px bar with no hair or bristle texture at all.

VALERIAN COMPARISON -- the judge is right on the substance, wrong in two particulars. Same chassis is confirmed: Valerian has 22 rungs at the same ~8px pitch against Yarrow's 23; both stems are the same 4px olive bar; both base shadows are the same ellipse; both apex caps are the same crescent-on-a-cone at nearly identical size (Yarrow 31x10 at y75-84, Valerian 30x11 at y79-89). So 'same stem, shadow, rung count and white apex pill' is accurate. TWO CORRECTIONS. First, the difference is not hue ALONE: Yarrow's leaflets are visibly smaller and packed denser, so its column edge holds a near-constant width of 65-68px down its whole length, whereas Valerian's rungs pinch between tiers and its width oscillates 45-74px and reads as a more open ladder. Yarrow is therefore the denser, more plume-like of the two -- it is just nowhere near feather-fine. Second, the hue difference is not a defect to be dismissed: Yarrow's 152,176,136 grey-green vs Valerian's 101,136,79 mid-green, and Yarrow's pure-white cap vs Valerian's pink-tinted one, are both exactly what each species' spec asks for. The failure is that correct colour is doing all the differentiating work while the shape does none.

FIX DIRECTION. Two changes, in priority order. (a) Widen the corymb to be the widest element in the silhouette -- a flat-topped plate roughly 90-110px wide (wider than the 66-68px foliage), with a hard flat top edge and a shallow underside, granulated into many tiny white dots rather than one smooth lozenge; it should read as a dinner plate seen at a slight angle, not a pill. (b) Replace the once-pinnate oval leaflets with a bipinnate treatment: subdivide each leaflet into 3-5 thread-thin segments (1px) so no discrete unit is countable, and bring the whole plume tight against the stem so it clasps rather than projects on visible spurs. Fixing (a) alone would already break the Valerian collision, since the corymb becomes the dominant silhouette mass; fixing both is what earns a PASS.

rows.readsAs: a single broad green leaf blade, or a green wine glass on a stem
rows.defect: The reference calls for a hollow green sphere studded with many identical cells, daughter colonies visible inside, translucent jelly. The render is not a sphere and not a colony at all: it is the family's tapered spindle with the strands webbed into one solid opaque green membrane, flared to a straight square-cut top and pinched to a tiny green nub at the ground. There is no sphere, no cell studding, no daughter colonies, no translucency. It reads as a leaf, not a microbe.
rows.fix: Discard the seaweed spindle entirely for this one and draw a single large translucent circle whose rim is beaded with many small identical green cells, with two or three smaller beaded circles suspended inside it.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD after 440px full read plus 4x nearest-neighbour crops of the top, mid and base. What is actually on canvas: a single opaque yellow-green form occupying roughly x=150-290, y=65-350. Its top edge is a perfectly straight, horizontal, SQUARE-CUT line about 130px wide with hard 90-degree corners. From there the silhouette runs down with a slight outward bow, then pinches hard inward around y=230 into a narrow 12-15px stipe, which lands on a small bright-green elliptical disc holdfast (~40x14px) sitting on the standard drop-shadow ellipse. Fill is a flat vertical gradient (lighter at top, darker at the pinch), fully OPAQUE - the dark navy background is not visible through any part of it. The only internal detail is 3-4 faint pale, near-vertical lines that converge toward the stipe; at 4x they are 1px soft strokes, not outlines of anything. There are no circles, no dots, no stippling, no repeated units, no rim of cells, no interior blobs anywhere in the image.

Against the reference row, all THREE mustReads are absent, not merely weak: (1) 'hollow green sphere studded with many identical cells over its surface' - there is no sphere and not one cell; the form is a stemmed goblet, the opposite topology of a sphere. (2) 'smaller daughter colonies visible inside the parent sphere' - nothing is inside anything; the interior is a flat gradient. (3) 'clear jelly between the cells so the sphere reads as translucent' - the fill is fully opaque with a hard antialiased edge and zero background bleed-through. The row's kingdom is 'microbe' and this reads as a macroscopic seaweed blade or a piece of glassware. This is the wrong organism, not an under-detailed right one, so FAIL is the correct band and no amount of polish reaches the target - the primitive has to be replaced with a sphere.

Their claim is essentially correct and I confirm the chassis diagnosis specifically. Cross-reading Red_Algae.png and Sargassum.png: both are the identical spindle - a bundle of ~8 separate vertical strands, splayed slightly at the top, converging to a single point at the bottom on the same shadow ellipse. Green Algae is that SAME spindle with the gaps between the strands filled in to one solid membrane; the strand paths survive as the pale vertical lines, which is why they read as leaf venation. So 'the family spindle with the strands webbed into one opaque membrane and a square-cut flared top' is accurate and is the actionable root cause.

Two corrections/refinements to their wording, neither of which rescues the asset: (a) their read 'a single broad green leaf' is the weaker of their two readings - a leaf tapers to a tip, and this top edge is a dead-straight horizontal cut with square corners, so the dominant read is a wine glass / champagne flute / green vase; the leaf read only survives because of those venation-like strand lines. (b) They did not mention that Green Algae ALSO differs from its two siblings at the base: it terminates on a small bright-green elliptical disc holdfast rather than converging to a bare point, and its silhouette flares OUTWARD toward the top where Red Algae and Sargassum taper inward. That flare plus the disc is what pushes it from 'family seaweed' into 'goblet'. The fix is not to unweb the strands (that would just make a fourth seaweed) but to swap in a circular hollow-sphere primitive: a ring of many identical small circles around the rim, a scatter of the same circles across the face at reduced opacity to read as the far wall, 2-4 smaller filled spheres floating inside, and a low-alpha fill so the background shows through the jelly.

rows.readsAs: a husked ear of corn, or a closed mustard-yellow tulip bud
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing. There is no claw holdfast and no rock — the whole plant narrows to a single point on bare ground. There is no distinct stiff stipe, because the stalk and the body are the same continuous taper. The blade is not wide or flapping; it is a narrow closed spindle no wider than Red Algae's. The colour is mustard-gold, not olive-brown to dark chocolate. The three flat ellipse blobs pasted on the midline belong to Sargassum's float description and are the wrong feature on the wrong asset.
rows.fix: Rebuild as three elements: a splayed root-like claw gripping a rock at the base, a clear narrow stipe above it, and a single wide dark-brown strap blade split into finger segments that is at least three times wider than the stipe.
rows.verifyWhy:
I tried to refute this and could not. Zoomed crops at 3x-5x plus a pixel scan of the silhouette confirm all three must-reads are absent.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a single closed convex spindle built from ~9-11 vertical ribbon strands that all converge at BOTH ends. Body bounding box measures 62 x 286 px inside a 440 px canvas (aspect 0.217 — narrower even than the packet's requested 0.35). Scanned widths top-to-bottom: 57 / 61 / 60 / 49 / 34 / 24 / 18 / 9 px. It is widest near the TOP and tapers monotonically to a 9 px blunt tip. The top is a cluster of rounded finger tips curled inward like an unopened bud (with two thin slivers of background showing through where tips fail to meet — a visible seam). It reads as a husked ear of corn / a shaving brush / a closed tulip bud.

MUST-READ 1 'root-like claw holdfast gripping rock' — ABSENT, and the judge described this correctly. At 5x the base is a 9 px rounded point sitting on bare flat ground with nothing but a soft elliptical cast shadow. No claw, no splayed haptera, no rock, no substrate of any kind.

MUST-READ 2 'stiff stipe stalk' — ABSENT. There is no separate narrow stalk. The same ribbons run continuously from the ground point to the top; nothing marks a transition from stalk to blade.

MUST-READ 3 'wide flapping brown blade' — ABSENT. There is no strap. The form is a sealed lens/spindle, never opens, and has no free edge to flap. The finger-like divisions the packet allows are drawn as strands wrapped INTO the closed bundle rather than as splits in a broad flat blade.

CORRECTIONS TO THE FAILING JUDGE:
(a) 'Colour is mustard-gold instead of chocolate brown' is OVERSTATED. Sampled dominant body tone is #706030 with shading down to #404030 and highlights up to #907030. #706030 is a legitimate olive-brown and the packet's leafColour explicitly permits 'olive-brown to dark chocolate'. So the colour is inside spec in isolation. The REAL colour defect is separation, not spec: it is nearly the same palette as Sargassum ('golden olive-brown to tan'), so the two are indistinguishable by hue. Kelp must be pushed hard to the dark-chocolate end of its own allowed range, not merely 'made brown'.
(b) The three blobs claim is CORRECT and stronger than stated. They sit on the exact centreline at roughly 35%, 62% and 80% of body height. The upper two are horizontal capsule/lozenge shapes, the lowest is a circle — none are stalked. They are painted flat over the strands with no stalk, no attachment, no shading integration. Crucially I opened Sargassum.png: it has NO floats at all. So the float feature has genuinely landed on the wrong family member.
(c) DEFECT THE JUDGE MISSED, and it is the biggest one: KELP AND SARGASSUM ARE ONE CHASSIS. Side by side they are the same converging-ribbon spindle, same inward-curled finger tips at the top, same monotonic taper to a point, same ground-shadow ellipse, same strand count and stroke weight. Only hue (Kelp darker olive, Sargassum brighter gold) and Kelp's three pasted blobs differ. Fixing Kelp in isolation will not fix this — Kelp needs a genuinely different build (splayed claw holdfast on rock, a distinct rigid stipe, then a WIDE flat strap blade at least 2-3x the stipe width with finger splits and a wavy free edge), while Sargassum needs the bushy branched mass and the stalked round floats it is currently missing.

Band FAIL upheld: three of three must-reads are absent and the asset does not read as a kelp at all.

rows.readsAs: a furled crimson umbrella or a bundle of red spaghetti stood on end
rows.defect: The colour is right — deep crimson with a purplish sheen. Everything structural is wrong. The identity must-read is fine, repeatedly forking branch structure, and there is not one fork anywhere in the image: the fronds are eight straight parallel rods running the full height without dividing once. The small disc holdfast is absent; the bundle converges to a bare point. The dark tips at the top read as burnt or clipped ends rather than frond apices.
rows.fix: Replace the parallel rods with a repeatedly dichotomous branch tree — each frond forking into two at least three times up the height — and seat it on a small flat crimson disc holdfast.
rows.verifyWhy:
I looked at the 440x440 PNG at full size and then decoded it and re-rendered four brightness-boosted crops (crown, mid-shaft, base, and the whole organism at 3x). The FAIL stands, but two of the three stated causes are described wrongly and the fixer must not work from them as written.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a bundle of long, smooth, unbranched strands that all originate from ONE convergence point at the ground and fan/flare outward and upward, each ending in its own rounded cap. It occupies roughly x 175-270, y 60-360 of the 440px frame. Two depth layers are present: ~8 bright crimson-rose foreground strands and ~7 darker mauve strands behind them, so the true strand count is about 15-16, not eight. The silhouette reads as a shaving brush / whisk / fibre-optic lamp, not as a seaweed.

CLAIM ITEM 1 - 'not one fork in the image' - CONFIRMED, and this is the whole failure. I traced every strand from base to tip in the mid-shaft crop at 5x: not a single strand divides at any level. Zero bifurcations, zero dichotomies, no secondary or tertiary order at all. mustRead item 'fine repeatedly forking branch structure' is completely absent. A branching red seaweed (Chondrus, Plocamium) is DEFINED by repeated dichotomous forking; without it this is not the organism.

CLAIM ITEM 1 WORDING - PARTLY WRONG. They are not 'eight straight parallel rods' and they do not 'run the full height'. There are ~15-16 strands in two depth layers; they are curved, not straight; they are convergent-then-splayed, not parallel (they pinch to a single point at the bottom and flare at the top); and the mass spans only about two thirds of the frame height, floating with clear headroom above. Correcting this matters because 'make the parallel rods diverge' would not fix it - the strands ALREADY diverge; what is missing is subdivision of each strand into finer daughter branches, repeated 2-3 orders, with the branch tips getting progressively thinner.

CLAIM ITEM 2 - 'small disc holdfast is absent' - CONFIRMED. At 8x the base is unambiguous: all strands merge into one narrow bundle that terminates in a single rounded blunt tip resting on the dark ground ellipse. There is no disc, no basal plate, no crust, no widening of any kind - the base is narrower than the crown, the opposite of a holdfast. mustRead item 'small disc holdfast' absent.

CLAIM ITEM 3 - 'dark frond tips read as clipped ends' - WRONG. The dark elements at the crown are not tips of the crimson strands and they are not clipped. At 5x they resolve as SIX separate short slate/blue-grey rods, each with its own cleanly ROUNDED cap, standing behind and between the crimson strands and mostly shorter than the tallest pink one. Every crimson strand's own tip is also cleanly rounded - nothing in the image is clipped or square-cut. The real defect here is a colour defect, not a geometry defect: those six rods are desaturated blue-grey, an off-palette hue that has nothing to do with 'deep crimson to purplish-red, often with iridescent sheen'. They read as accidental grey filler, and they should either be removed or brought into the crimson/purple ramp.

COLOUR - the judge's 'colour is correct' is roughly fair but generous. Unboosted, the strands are a deep crimson-rose; that satisfies 'deep crimson' but sits on the pink/rose side with no purplish shift and no iridescent sheen. So the fix is not a tweak to Red Algae's tips: the algae family needs a real branching generator (recursive fork, decreasing thickness per order, 2-3 orders deep) plus a distinct basal form per species (disc holdfast for Red Algae, claw holdfast for Kelp, float-berries for Sargassum). Fixing only the grey tips would leave the asset failing for exactly the same reason.

BAND: FAIL. Two of three must-reads are entirely absent, and the missing one is the identity feature. The asset does not read as a branching red seaweed.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon bug / mascot beetle with one big googly eye — nobody says 'leafcutter'
rows.defect: The identity must-read is simply not drawn: there is NO leaf fragment carried overhead anywhere in the frame. The thorax is a plain smooth ovoid with zero backward-pointing spines. rows.fix: Rebuild it as an ant rig: put all six legs on the thorax with a visible femur/tibia elbow, cut a true pinched two-node petiole between thorax and gaster, add the backward-pointing propodeal spines on the thorax, replace the single mammal eye with a small compound eye plus a pair of forward cutting mandibles and elbowed antennae — and above all, add the semicircular green leaf fragment held overhead in those jaws, since that silhouette IS the species.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified by reading the PNG at native size and then re-cropping the head, mid-body, rear and both leg clusters at 8x-18x. FAIL stands, but three of the five stated causes are wrong or imprecise and the fixes must be made against what is actually on canvas.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a left-facing three-ball chain on a shadow ellipse. Ball 1 = a smooth sphere head. Ball 2 = a horizontal egg (thorax) that OVERLAPS the head with no gap and no neck; its topline runs continuously into the head's. Ball 3 = a striped sphere (gaster) with vertical pale striations, which is a legitimate read of tergite banding and is NOT a defect. Thorax and gaster each carry an off-white specular rim crescent along the upper-right - that crescent is a lighting highlight, not a spine or a plate edge, and it is the only thing on the dorsum.

CONFIRMED CORRECT IN THE ORIGINAL CLAIM:
1. NO LEAF ANYWHERE. I checked the entire 440x440 frame including the empty space above and behind the animal - it is uniformly the dark vignette background. The species-defining must-read ('spined thorax carrying a leaf fragment overhead') is 100% absent.
2. NO MANDIBLES. The anterior of the head sphere is an unbroken circular arc. Nothing projects forward of it at all - no jaws, no clypeus, no palps. The head is a bare ball.
3. NO THORACIC SPINES. Zero. The thorax dorsum is a perfectly smooth ellipse arc; there is not even a bump. Backward-pointing spines are wholly absent.

WRONG OR IMPRECISE IN THE ORIGINAL CLAIM - CORRECT THESE BEFORE FIXING:
4. LEG DISTRIBUTION IS MISDESCRIBED. The claim says 'two legs attach to the head plus three to the gaster with only one on the thorax.' The true count is 6 legs distributed 3 / 1 / 2. THREE distinct legs emerge from the underside of the HEAD SPHERE (at 18x they are three separate strokes fanning down-right from the head ball's bottom arc, all clearly forward of the head/thorax junction - the leftmost is short and near-vertical, the other two rake back). ONE leg drops from the rear underside of the thorax. TWO legs serve the gaster: one drops down-left from the gaster's front-underside, and the second is the far end of the petiole rod itself (see 5). So the head is carrying THREE legs, not two, and the gaster TWO, not three. The thorax - which should carry all six - carries exactly one.
5. THE 'WAIST' BAR IS THICKER THAN A LEG AND IT DOES NOT TERMINATE AT THE GASTER. It is a straight horizontal rod roughly 2.5-3x a leg's width, uniform thickness end to end, with no petiole node, no postpetiole, no taper. Critically it does not stop at the gaster: it passes BEHIND / THROUGH the gaster sphere and re-emerges on the far right side, where it runs on for another body-width and then bends 90 degrees downward to become the rearmost leg. The gaster is therefore impaled mid-sphere on a continuous dowel that doubles as a leg, rather than being hung off the end of a petiole. The head/thorax junction has no constriction of any kind - they simply interpenetrate. So 'no pinched waist' is right in verdict but the geometry is a skewer, not an attachment bar.
6. THE ANTENNAE ARE NOT 'SMOOTH BACKSWEPT WHISKERS'. Both statements are false. They project FORWARD and UP over the face (the animal faces left and the antennae extend up-left, well past the front of the head) - they are forward-swept, not backswept. And they are not smooth: each has a sharp angular apex where the long proximal segment stops and the stroke reverses into a curved distal hook, giving each antenna a shepherd's-crook profile. So a bend IS present - the failure is that it is the WRONG bend in the WRONG place: a geniculate ant antenna needs a long scape leaving the frons then a downward-angled funiculus, whereas here the crook is at the far tip and the shape reads as a curled feeler/moth antenna.
7. THE ANTENNA ORIGIN AND EYE ARE CORRECTLY DESCRIBED. Both antennae emerge from a single thick base that sits ON TOP OF the black eye disc, inside its outline, with the white specular dot immediately adjacent. The eye is one oversized round black vertebrate-style eye with a single glossy highlight - not a compound eye, no ocelli, and it occupies roughly a quarter of the head ball.

BAND: FAIL. Of the three must-reads, 'leaf carried overhead' is entirely absent, 'spined thorax' is entirely absent, 'elbowed antennae' is present only as a mislocated tip-hook growing out of the eye, and 'pinched narrow waist' survives only as a straight skewer. With no jaws, no leaf, no spines, one giant vertebrate eye and half the legs mounted on the head, the asset reads as a generic three-bead cartoon bug, not a leafcutter ant. This is a redraw, not a polish.

rows.readsAs: a small rust-coloured cartoon spider

The body is two fat spheres with a deep waist between them, not a flat unsegmented teardrop wedge - the silhouette is round and tall where a tick is a low flat plate. There are no mouthparts of any kind: the front sphere is a bare ball with no capitulum, no palps and no barbed hypostome spear jutting ahead, so the single feature that IS the tick is absent. Looked at the 440px master, then re-cropped and magnified the head at 5x and 7x, the rear at 6x, and measured the silhouette by decoding the PNG directly. Every part of the original claim holds, and the measurements make it sharper.

BODY (mustRead: 'flat teardrop unsegmented body', aspect 2.2). Confirmed two-sphere chassis, not a teardrop. Column-run profile of the rust mass: heights climb to 60px at x=203, PINCH to 45px at x=223, then swell to 69px at x=251-259. Surface detail is limited to a few soft dark mottled blotches on the rear sphere; there is NO scutum plate, no dorsal shield, no cuticle striation.

MOUTHPARTS (mustRead: 'barbed spear mouthparts jutting ahead'). Completely absent — verified at 7x. The forward edge of the front sphere is a clean, unbroken, uninterrupted arc from x=167. Nothing projects ahead of it: no capitulum/basis capituli, no pedipalps, no hypostome, no barbs, not even a nub or a dark ventral notch where a gnathosoma would attach. The two forward-most strokes in the frame (all-ink starts at x=117) are LEGS angling down-left, not palps — I checked specifically in case the judge mistook a spear for a leg or vice versa. This is the feature that IS the tick and it does not exist anywhere on the asset.

LEGS (mustRead: 'eight legs bunched toward the front'). Roughly eight thin bare wire legs with sharp single elbow bends, no tarsi, no claws, no thickening. They are split about 4 forward / 4 rearward in a near-mirror fan — claim confirmed. One correction that makes it WORSE than stated: the rear group visibly sprouts from the REAR sphere (clearly seen in the 6x rear crop, two legs arching off the top of the rear ball and two descending off its right flank). No arachnid does that — all eight legs attach to the prosoma. So the chassis is not even a correct spider; with legs hung off both balls of a waisted two-ball body it reads closer to a generic cartoon ant/insect than to either a spider or a tick.

EYES (reference says 'eyes: hidden'). Confirmed and unambiguous at 5x: four glossy black beads, each with a white specular dot, arranged in a tidy 2x2 grid on the upper-front of the leading sphere. This is a direct contradiction of the reference row and is the single loudest 'spider' signal in the image.

COLOR/READ. Mid-rust / terracotta with a lit dorsal top-light and a soft ground shadow ellipse below. Reads as a small rust cartoon spider-bug, exactly as claimed.

Nothing in the claim was described incorrectly. All three mustReads fail, the aspect is short by 0.4, and an explicitly-forbidden feature (visible eyes) is painted on. FAIL upheld. For the fix: this needs a ground-up rebuild, not a touch-up — one continuous flat unsegmented low teardrop/wedge at aspect >=2.2 with no waist and no seam, a forward-jutting barbed hypostome spear with a short capitulum and two flanking palps as the leading silhouette event, all eight legs attached to the single body mass and crowded into the front third with the front pair reaching ahead, and the eye cluster deleted entirely.

rows.readsAs: a pale cream cartoon spider
rows.defect: It is the Deer Tick image recoloured with longer legs - same two spheres, same 2x2 eye dots in the same position on the front ball, same mottled blotching on the rear ball, same stick legs, same shadow. The defining pycnogonid trait is inverted: the body here is the largest, fattest part of the animal instead of being reduced to a thin stick between the legs, so nothing suggests that the gut and gonads have migrated into the limbs. There is no proboscis at all - no long tubular sucking tube at the front, just a bare rounded ball - and no small ocular turret carrying the four eyes; the eyes are flat dots painted on the sphere. The legs, while longer, are still the same two-segment sticks with no joints, no claws and no visible attachment to a segmented trunk.
rows.fix: Shrink the body to a narrow segmented rod barely wider than a leg, hang four pairs of very long jointed legs off visible lateral tubercles along that rod, and add a proboscis at least as long as the trunk projecting forward with a small four-eyed turret on top.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with two corrections to the stated cause.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440, read at 1x then re-cropped and upscaled 5-8x at the head, the front, and both leg fans): a two-sphere body dead-centre. Left sphere = head/cephalothorax, near-perfect circle ~62px across. Right sphere = abdomen, a taller ovoid ~68x78px, carrying five or six soft brown blotches. The two spheres overlap with a thin light rim where they meet. Eight legs total, four per side, each a pale grey-brown stick of CONSTANT width (~3px) made of exactly two straight segments meeting at one sharp knee; the tips are blunt square cut-offs with no tarsus, no claw, no taper. The legs simply terminate at the sphere silhouette - there is no coxa, no attachment plate, no trunk for them to attach to. A soft black ellipse shadow sits below. Palette is cream/pink flesh; background is the standard dark navy vignette.

CORRECTION 1 - THE EYES. The claim says "the four-eyed ocular turret ... eyes are flat dots on the sphere". Half wrong. There ARE exactly four eyes, correctly arranged as a 2x2 cluster, and they are NOT flat dots: at 8x each is a glossy black bead with a distinct white specular highlight on its upper-left, drawn with visible volume. What is genuinely missing is the TURRET - the ocular tubercle. The four beads are painted flush on the anterior face of the head sphere like a spider's eye group, with no raised stalk or cone carrying them. So the fix is "lift the four eyes onto a short dorsal tubercle", not "add four eyes".

CORRECTION 2 - THE COPY CLAIM IS TRUE AND IS WORSE THAN STATED. I opened Deer_Tick.png (the only other member of this family batch) and zoomed its body. It is not merely "the same idea": it is the same chassis part-for-part. Same two overlapping spheres in the same proportion and the same overlap geometry. Same 2x2 four-eye cluster, same beads, same highlights, same relative position on the head sphere - and the Deer Tick's own reference row says eyes: hidden, so that eye cluster is generic chassis furniture, not a sea-spider read. Same soft brown abdomen blotches. Same constant-width two-segment jointless legs. The ONLY differences are colour (rust orange vs cream), overall scale (the tick is drawn ~45% smaller in frame), and leg length/sprawl angle. Both animals carry 8 legs, 4 per side. This family of 2 is one body in two colours.

MUST-READS, CHECKED ONE BY ONE:
1. "body reduced to a thin stick between the legs" - ABSENT, and inverted as claimed. The abdomen sphere is the single largest, fattest mass in the whole image; head + abdomen together occupy roughly 130px of the ~370px leg span and are by far the visual centre of gravity. A pycnogonid's trunk should be a narrow segmented rod that the eye barely registers. There is also no segmented trunk and no lateral leg-bearing processes anywhere - nothing for eight legs to hang off.
2. "long tubular sucking proboscis at the front" - GENUINELY ABSENT. I specifically cropped the region ahead of the head at 8x to check whether a proboscis had been drawn small or thin and missed. It has not. The leading edge of the head sphere is an unbroken clean arc. The one thing that reads at a glance as a forward-pointing tube is a horizontal front leg leaving the sphere at mid-height, but it is the same 3px width and colour as the other legs and it bends at a knee ~90px out and continues down-left, so it is a leg, not a proboscis. Nothing projects from the head.
3. "enormously long spindly legs holding the organs" - PARTIALLY present. The legs are long relative to the body (~150px per side) and thin and sprawled, which satisfies posture: sprawling and roughly hits aspect 1.8-2.0. But they are constant-width sticks with a single knee; they do not swell, they carry no gut diverticula or gonad bulges, and they read as generic spider legs stretched, not as the organ-bearing limbs the note calls for.

VERDICT: two of the three must-reads are absent and the defining pycnogonid inversion (tiny body, enormous legs) is drawn backwards. The asset reads as a pale bulbous spider/tick, not as a sea spider. FAIL stands. To fix: collapse the two spheres into one narrow segmented rod with four visible lateral processes, hang each leg off its own process with multiple articulations and a terminal claw, add a long straight tube projecting forward from the anterior segment roughly as long as the trunk, and set the four eyes on a small raised tubercle on top of the first segment. And it must stop sharing a body with the Deer Tick.

rows.readsAs: a numbat, or a striped short-legged cat
rows.defect: There is no armour anywhere. The bands are flat painted vertical stripes on a soft furry barrel with a fuzzy hair fringe along the topline and belly — no raised overlapping plate edges, no shadowed band gaps, no scapular or pelvic shield, no domed carapace breaking the topline. The topline is a smooth soft arc identical to a generic quadruped. The tail is a thin smooth up-curling cat tail with no rings or taper-plating, and the snout is only mildly pointed with a soft rounded ear rather than the long tube-snout and small tubular ears called for.
rows.fix: Rebuild the mid-back as hard geometry: a domed keratin carapace with a front and rear shield and 6-8 discrete banded plates between them, each band a crisp overlapping arc with a dark shadow line under its trailing edge, the band stack visibly stepping the topline; then run the same plating down the tail as tapering rings and lengthen the snout into a narrow tube.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the fullsize PNG and then at 4x/9x/12x crops of topline, belly, head and tail. VERDICT UPHELD - the defining must-read (armour) does not read - but several of the stated causes are wrong and would send a fix in the wrong direction.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. The barrel carries ~11 vertical bands running the full height of the body, alternating a mid-taupe band with a pale cream strip. CORRECTION 1: the bands are NOT 'flat painted stripes'. At 9x each dark band is tiled with rows of small crescent/arc scute motifs (an osteoderm micro-texture) plus tiny warm specular pips along the band edges. That texture is a genuine armour-material cue and it already exists - the fix must not start by adding scute texture, it is drawn.

WHY THE ARMOUR STILL FAILS (the judge is right here). (a) The pale strips BETWEEN the bands are LIGHTER than the bands, so they read as highlight stripes on a soft cylinder, not as the shadowed hinge gaps between overlapping plates - the value relationship is inverted. (b) There is not a single raised or overlapping plate lip anywhere; no band casts a shadow onto the band behind it. (c) The topline at 9x is one smooth unbroken arc with a soft blue rim light: the bands cross it without stepping, scalloping or notching the silhouette, so nothing at the edge says 'shell'. (d) There is no domed carapace sitting proud of the flesh, and no scapular/pelvic shields - the stripes run uniformly from shoulder to hip, whereas the reference row asks for bands 'across the MIDDLE of the back', i.e. a hinged mid-section between two solid shields. Net: it reads as a striped hide, not a shell.

CORRECTION 2 - THERE IS NO HAIR FRINGE. The claim of 'a hair fringe along topline and belly' is factually wrong. At 9x both edges are clean, smooth, hard-edged arcs with no hair, no broken edge, no fur strokes. The spiky look in the thumbnail is the pale inter-band strips FLARING WIDER as they approach the belly (wedge-shaped, wide at the bottom), which reads as light spikes. That is a value/shape bug in the band pass, not a fur bug - do not go looking for fur to delete.

CORRECTION 3 - THE SNOUT IS NOT 'ONLY MILDLY POINTED'. At 12x the head carries a long, thin, near-tubular proboscis that projects well beyond the face - if anything it is too long and too uniformly narrow (anteater-like), ending in a small rounded tip with a nostril dot. This must-read ('long pointed snout') is PRESENT and is the strongest thing in the asset. Because of it the animal cannot read as a cat; the honest wrong-organism call is numbat/anteater, not 'striped short-legged cat'.

CORRECTION 4 - THE EAR. Not 'a soft rounded ear' in passing: there is ONE large upright leaf/oval ear rising clearly above the skull line with a dark brown inner surface, alongside a small black eye bead with a white specular. It is a real defect, but the defect is that the ear is too LARGE and leaf-shaped where the row asks for 'small tubular ears' - only one is drawn, and it should be a short thick tube, not a saucer.

CORRECTION 5 - THE TAIL. Not an 'up-curling cat tail'. It leaves the rump rearward, arcs up, then hooks DOWN and forward into a blunt rounded tip. Critically it is essentially UNTAPERED - near-constant width from base to tip - and completely blank flat tan with zero texture: no rings, no plates, not even the scute tiling that the body has. So 'tapering armoured tail' fails on BOTH counts (no taper AND no armour), which is worse than the claim stated.

OTHER: feet are stubby with two dark oval claw shapes each - claws are present and legible. Legs are short and correctly proportioned; aspect and posture match the row.

SCORE AGAINST THE ROW: 1 of 3 must-reads clean (long pointed snout), 1 failed outright (tapering armoured tail - untapered and untextured), 1 failed as read (hinged bands - texture present, but no plate lips, no hinge shadows, no stepped topline, no fore/aft shields). Armour IS the identity of this organism; with it unreadable the asset fails. FIX ORDER: invert the inter-band values so the gaps are dark hinge shadows and the plates are the lit surface; notch the topline silhouette so each band steps over the one behind; add a domed carapace edge separated from the flank; collapse the stripes into solid scapular and pelvic shields with only the middle 8-9 bands hinged; re-cut the tail as a tapering cone of stacked rings; shrink the ear to a short tube.

rows.readsAs: a guinea pig or hamster taped under a dowel
rows.defect: The identity feature is entirely missing — the long hooked scythe claws. Both limbs terminate as blunt flat-topped rectangular straps that butt into the underside of the branch; nothing curls over or grips it, and there is no claw geometry of any kind. Only two limbs exist; the hind pair is absent. The limbs are featureless parallelogram slabs with no shoulder, elbow or wrist, so the body reads as an oval hung on two ribbons rather than a long-armed animal. The face is wrong too: a pointed rodent muzzle with a single bead eye on the side of the head instead of the small flat round forward-facing face with dark eye stripes and a faint smile. The fur is uniform pale cream with no greenish algal cast.
rows.fix: Replace the two straps with four long curved arms whose ends close into two or three big hooked scythe claws visibly wrapping over the top of the branch, and flatten the muzzle into a round forward-facing disc face with dark eye patches.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but three of the stated causes are wrong and the fix list must be corrected. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (read at 4x, then 9-12x crops of the limb tops, head and rump): a pale cream-khaki ovoid body slung under a horizontal brown branch, suspended by two straight vertical straps.

(1) CLAWS ARE NOT ABSENT — the judge's headline cause is factually wrong. At the top of EACH limb there is a distinct pale-ivory claw block, subdivided by vertical striations into roughly three digits, and it is a genuinely separate material: sampled claw pixels are ~(200,192,172) against limb fur at ~(110,105,88), a value jump you can see unaided at 12x. The claim also mislocates them: the limbs do NOT butt into the branch underside — they pass IN FRONT of the branch and the claw blocks overlay the branch's front face, terminating just short of its upper edge. What actually fails is the SHAPE: each claw is a short blunt straight vertical bar about as long as it is wide (~10px on a 440px canvas, ~1/12 of body length), with zero curvature. Nothing hooks, curls, wraps or closes around the branch. The must-read is 'long hooked scythe claws'; what is drawn is short straight rectangular nubs. The fix is to lengthen and CURVE them into a closing hook that visibly wraps the branch profile — not to add claws that already exist.

(2) FACE — the judge is right that the must-read 'small round flat face with a faint smile' fails, and wrong about the eye. It is a hard profile head with a long, narrow, TUBULAR snout that protrudes forward well past the skull, terminating in a single nostril dot — this reads anteater/shrew/opossum, not 'rodent muzzle' and not guinea pig. There is no mouth line at all, so no smile. But there IS a dark eye patch: a clearly-drawn medium-brown mask blotch surrounds the small glossy black eye, and a pale hooked ear-lobe sits above and behind it. So 'no dark eye patches' is incorrect — the patch is present, it is the flat round forward-facing DISC that is missing. Fix: collapse the tubular snout back into the skull to a blunt stub, rotate the face toward the viewer, and add the mouth line.

(3) LIMBS — the judge is right. Exactly two limbs exist, both planted in the anterior half of the body, so the entire rear half of the animal dangles unsupported. Each is a constant-width column with no shoulder mass, no elbow break, no wrist, no taper. No hindlimbs, no third or fourth limb.

(4) TAIL/RUMP — nothing. The rear is a bare rounded dome with a flat shading wedge; no tail, no rump structure, no hind-foot.

(5) FUR — 'uniform pale cream with no fur' overstates it. There IS directional strand texture across the flank, sparse hair spikes breaking the silhouette edge, and a fringe of long strands hanging off the belly, plus a darker shading plane over the rump. What is genuinely missing is the colour: sampled body pixels run (178,170,145), (168,158,129), (157,150,126) — R>G>B every time, a warm cream-khaki. There is no green channel dominance anywhere, so the 'greenish algal cast' must-read is absent as claimed, but the shagginess is partially present and should be amplified rather than added from scratch.

(6) PROPORTION — body spans roughly 175px wide by 105px tall, an aspect near 1.7 against the spec's 1.2; the blob is too long and too flat for the packet row.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440, examined at 4x-10x crops of head, withers, rump and both front feet):
A fleece-textured barrel torso on four thin tapering legs, a ball head with a stuck-on ball muzzle, and a large concentric-disc ear. It reads as a SHEEP/RAM, not a bear.

CONFIRMED - ONE CHASSIS WITH BROWN BEAR. Measured, not eyeballed: silhouette IoU against Brown_Bear.png = 0.822 (7247 px both-ink, 655 grizzly-only, 917 brown-only, sampled every 2px). Toplines agree within ~4px across the entire back. Same head-dome + separate muzzle-lobe + ear-disc construction, same limb form, same foot. Only 33% of overlapping pixels differ in colour at all - a hue shift to a warmer orange-tan. By contrast Grizzly vs Black_Bear is IoU 0.707 with 95.5% colour difference, so the pipeline CAN differentiate; Grizzly and Brown Bear specifically are the same drawing recoloured. 'Same sheep chassis with a marginally warmer fleece' is correct.

THE UNNAMED DEFECT - THE FEET ARE CLOVEN HOOVES. This is the strongest single reason the organism reads wrong and the judge never mentions it. Each leg is a thin ungulate cannon with a knit/fishnet texture, ending in TWO dark glossy rounded blobs set side by side - a cloven hoof, drawn identically on all four legs. There is no broad flat plantigrade paw anywhere on the asset. A bear rendered on hooves is a wrong-organism error and should lead any fix list.

CORRECTION 1 - 'Fur is a flat wash with no grizzled guard-hair contrast' is FALSE, and this is the one must-read the asset actually meets. At 6x the pelt is densely hatched with directional guard-hair strokes in three tones: pale cream tips, mid tan, and dark brown ground. Pale-tipped strokes over a darker base is exactly what grizzling looks like. Do not touch the pelt texture in the fix - it is the best thing here.

CORRECTION 2 - 'No shoulder hump (flat horizontal back, so it fails the note's own black-bear-opposite test)' is wrong on mechanism and wrong on the test. Measured topline (topmost non-background pixel per column): loin peaks at y=183 (x=132-156), sags to y=187 (x=174), then RISES to y=168 by x=228 before the head takes over at x=234. The shoulder end is ~15px HIGHER than the rump. Black_Bear.png measured the same way genuinely peaks at the rump (y=167, x=144-162) and sits at y=171-172 across the shoulder - rump-high, correctly opposite. So the family does encode the direction, and Grizzly passes the black-bear-opposite test as stated. What is genuinely absent is the hump as a FORM: the rise is a smooth monotonic ramp continuous with the neck ruff, with no discrete muscular apex sitting above the back line over the forelegs. The must-read says 'muscular hump over the shoulders' and that mass does not exist. Fix the form, not the direction - a fix aimed at 'flatten-to-rising' would be aimed at a defect that is not there.

CORRECTION 3 - claw count understated. It is not 'two white hatch ticks' but roughly four to five short white strokes clustered at the front edge of each front hoof (~1.5px each at native res). The characterisation is otherwise exact: they are micro hatch marks sitting on a hoof nub, not long pale digging claws. Must-read 'long pale front claws' fails on length and on the structure they are attached to.

CONFIRMED - FACIAL PROFILE. 'Convex curled muzzle instead of a dished profile' is accurate. The crown and forehead are one convex dome; the only concavity in the whole profile is a small notch/step where the muzzle attaches. Forward of that notch the muzzle is a separate convex lobe carrying a dark oval nose, and its lower edge curls back under toward the chin - ram-like. Must-read 'dished concave facial profile' fails.

ALSO WORTH FIXING (unlisted by either judge): a rigid straight brown bar runs from beneath the nose back-left across the cheek and overshoots the muzzle outline - it is meant to be the mouth line but reads as a twig held in the teeth. The ear is drawn as a large face-on dark disc with a darker oval inside it, sitting where a bighorn's horn base would be, which reinforces the ram read.

SCORECARD vs mustRead 'muscular hump over the shoulders / dished concave facial profile / long pale front claws and grizzled fur': hump ABSENT as form (direction weakly present), dished face ABSENT (convex), long pale claws ABSENT (micro ticks on hooves), grizzled fur PRESENT and good. One of four, on a chassis shared with Brown Bear and terminating in cloven hooves. FAIL stands.

REFUTED on the load-bearing point. I pixel-sampled and luminance-masked the 440x440 render (bbox x93-346 y122-303, W253 H181, aspect 1.40 vs target 1.5 - good). THE CLAIM 'ALL FOUR LEGS ARE WHITE' IS FACTUALLY FALSE. All four legs are BLACK: fill RGB(21,24,30) on both hind legs (x113-149 at y270) and both forelegs (x245-281 at y270), against a white body of RGB(244,244,242) and a background of RGB(5,6,12). A column scan at x=250 from y=150 shows white from y162-198 then UNBROKEN black from y202 all the way to y294 - i.e. the black chest/shoulder mass is CONTINUOUS into the black foreleg. Must-read #2, 'black shoulder band joining black forelegs', is therefore PRESENT and correctly built, not 'absent and contradicted'. What the judge read as 'a dark saddle plus a rear-flank wedge' is actually the panda yoke seen in 3/4: a black forequarter/chest mass abutting the white flank panel along a hard vertical edge at x~245, feeding both forelegs, with the hind legs black to the hip and the back/rump/flank white. That distribution (white back and rump, black all four limbs, white head with black patches) is diagnostically panda, NOT Jacob sheep - a Jacob has a BLACK head on a white body with random blotches and horns, none of which is present here.

WHY THE JUDGE PROBABLY SAW WHITE LEGS - and the real defect underneath it: the black fur is mixed at luminance ~24 while the backdrop sits at ~6 and the vignette glow reaches ~12. At 1x the limbs are only 18 luminance steps above the background, so they read as thin white OUTLINE strokes around empty space rather than as black legs. FIX: lift panda black to roughly #2b2c30-#33343a with a visible specular sheen so the limbs and yoke separate from the dark plate at display size. This is the single highest-value fix on the asset.

WHERE THE JUDGE IS RIGHT: (a) the topline IS flat - silhouette tops run y149-158 across x125-230, a 9px rise over 105px, a plank back rather than the rounded bulk the must-read asks for; the rear does round off correctly but the back does not. (b) The eye patches ARE perfect circles, not teardrops - and worse than reported: THE PATCHES CONTAIN NO EYES. There is exactly ONE eye on the whole face, a tiny gold-ringed pupil at x~287,y~163 sitting in the white gap BETWEEN the two black discs. Both discs are blank. That is a real anatomical error and must be fixed by teardrop-ing the patches, slanting them down-inward toward the nose, and seating one eye inside each. (c) Legs are spindly: each leg is ~17px wide against a 107px-deep torso (ratio 0.16); a panda's are short stout pillars, ~0.3.

WHERE THE JUDGE IS WRONG OR INCOMPLETE BESIDES THE LEGS: ears ARE present, just not black - at 4x I see a mid-grey disc (lum 90-175) at the upper-left of the skull and a second lighter grey rounded ear with a mauve inner sitting face-on over the forehead, both misplaced high and forward and both grey instead of black. So 'no black round ears are visible' should read 'two grey ears are drawn, wrongly coloured and wrongly seated'. The short white tail called for in the note IS present: a pale flat tab at x~93-110, y~200-230 at the rear - though it reads as a rectangular flap, not a round stub. The head is not 'only panda-ish' by accident - it is white with black patches and a dark nose blob at the muzzle tip, but the muzzle PROJECTS well forward (head+snout spans x245-346) so the skull is not the 'very round' panda head the must-read wants; there is also a stray grey bar running from mid-face to the muzzle tip that reads as a rendering artifact.

The genuine source of the ovine misread is not the marking layout - it is the SURFACE and the FEET: the white pelt is painted in long streaky vertical strands that read as fleece, and the toe caps are pale grey wedges that read as cloven hooves rather than the black clawed paws a panda has. Replace the fleece strokes with short dense pelage and darken the feet into the leg black.

BAND: POLISH, not FAIL. Two of three must-reads (black patches on a white face; black shoulder band joining black forelegs) are verifiably present, and the third (round bulky body) is half-present - the mass is genuinely bulky, only the topline is flat. The asset does not read as the wrong organism once the black is seen; it reads as a panda whose black is too dark to survive the backdrop and whose face has a mis-assembled eye. A FAIL resting on 'all four legs are white' and 'the shoulder band is absent' cannot stand, because both are contradicted by the pixels.

WHAT I SAW (440x440 PNG, cropped x110-320 / y140-270 and magnified 5x, then re-rendered at 3.2x brightness to rule out banding hidden in shadow). The animal is a three-sphere insect in side profile facing left: a head sphere (~45px), a larger thorax sphere (~55px), and a smaller abdomen sphere (~40px) mostly hidden behind the wings. Two long thin curved antennae sweep up and back from the head. One eye, a small black oval with a single white specular dot, top-front of the head. CORRECTION 1 - 'zero yellow' is FALSE, and this matters for the fix. Yellow IS being drawn and is unmistakable: a corona of roughly twenty radiating fuzz spikes rings the thorax, above and below, in a mustard/gold (measured ~rgb(84,84,36) raw, reading as bright yellow once brightness is normalised), plus a few shorter spikes at the front of the abdomen, and the legs are a dull olive-gold. So the palette is not missing yellow. The defect is DEPLOYMENT: the yellow exists only as a hair fringe on one segment's outline, never as pigment on the body surface. The fix is not 'add yellow' - it is 'band the thorax and abdomen surfaces'.

CORRECTION 2 - 'one flat dark chocolate-brown' is imprecise. The body is a desaturated warm greyish-taupe/mushroom brown, roughly rgb(90,80,68) on the lit side falling to rgb(50,42,36) in shadow, and it is NOT flat - every segment carries a smooth spherical gradient. It is however genuinely MONOCHROME across all three segments: head, thorax and abdomen are one continuous value ramp with no band, no stripe, no tonal break anywhere. So the substance of the claim stands - 'broad bands of black and yellow fuzz', the identity must-read, is entirely absent, and at brightness 3.2x I confirmed nothing is hiding in the dark.

CORRECTION 3 - 'not fat or bulky (same slim chassis as the others)' is right about the chassis but wrong about the shape word. The body is not slim; it is a rounded three-sphere blob. The real defect is that it is the IDENTICAL sprite to its two family siblings. I rendered Honeybee and Orchid_Bee side by side: same head sphere, same thorax sphere with the same hair corona, same abdomen sphere, same two antennae curves, same single highlighted eye, same five stick legs, same wing pair at the same angle, same shadow ellipse. Only the hue token changes - Bumblebee taupe-brown, Honeybee orange, Orchid Bee green. The packet asks for aspect 1.9 here and 2.4 for Honeybee; rendered, they are the same proportion. So the Bumblebee has no bulk advantage over the honeybee it is supposed to out-mass, and Honeybee fails its own banding must-read in exactly the same way, which points at one shared bee-drawing routine rather than three separate bugs.

CLAIM CONFIRMED AND UNDERSTATED - the wings. Two large translucent veined wings originate at the front of the thorax and run back to roughly 30px past the abdomen tip: a chord of about 82px against a 119px body, ~69% of body length and ~45% of the whole sprite width. They fully occlude the abdomen, which is why the segment that should carry the bands cannot be read at all even if bands were painted on it. WHAT IS THERE: a green sphere head with a single black eye carrying one white specular dot, two thin antennae, a green spherical thorax, a short rounded green abdomen, two pairs of clear veined wings, six dark-green hairline legs, on the shared bee chassis. (1) TONGUE - ABSENT, confirmed. I zoomed the entire ventral strip (src x150-280, y200-248) at 7x and the head at 13x: there is no proboscis anywhere, neither trailing rearward beneath the body nor projecting forward from the face. The three wires descending below the head are legs - each continues unbroken to the ground plane at the shadow. Nothing horizontal runs under the thorax or abdomen. (2) SWOLLEN HIND TIBIA - ABSENT, confirmed at 15x. The hind leg is a two-segment jointed wire (femur up-and-back, tibia down-and-forward) of constant ~2px stroke width along its whole length, the identical stroke to the fore legs, with no widening, no taper, no polished pad, no highlight. Nothing distinguishes hind from fore legs but angle. (3) METALLIC/JEWEL BODY - only half met. The hue is correct (a clean mid-green, ~#3ad48f), so 'brilliant green' is nominally satisfied, but the finish is wrong exactly as claimed: one broad soft diffuse gradient on the upper-left of each sphere, no hard specular hotspot, no rim light, no iridescent blue or gold secondary anywhere. It reads as matte painted plastic, not a jewel-metallic carapace. (4) THE ANTI-NOTE IS VIOLATED, and worse than the judge stated. The fuzz corona is not merely present on the dorsal thorax - it wraps the FULL circumference, dorsal AND ventral, roughly 30 separate bristles in a contrasting pale yellow-green (~#c8e85a) that is the single most salient element on the model, more eye-catching than the body itself. Side-by-side with Honeybee.png the corona is the same geometry, same bristle count band, same placement, only hue-shifted. The packet says 'shiny and jewel-like rather than fuzzy' - this is the fuzziest thing in the crop. CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM: 'nothing structural differs' is overstated. The Orchid Bee's occupied bbox is 152x98px against the Honeybee's 182x103 (matching aspect 1.9 vs 2.4), and the difference is real - the abdomen is markedly shorter, rounder and tucked further under the wings, and it carries NO segment banding, where the honeybee's abdomen is elongated with visible amber/dark segment ridges. So it is not a pure hue rotation of the honeybee; it is the same chassis with a shortened, unbanded abdomen. Related: the judge's phrase 'honeybee's ... striped' implies stripes are present here - they are not, the abdomen is uniform green. Everything else in the claim is accurate. NET: with no tongue, no swollen tibia, a matte finish and a full fuzz corona, the only orchid-bee signal in the asset is the color green. It reads as a green honeybee. FIX ORDER: delete the corona entirely and replace with a hard specular band plus a hue-shifted blue/gold rim on thorax and abdomen; add a long thin proboscis originating under the head and trailing rearward past the mid-legs, at least half body length; swell the hind tibia into a flattened polished blade with its own highlight, distinct from the fore-leg stroke.

MUST-READ 1, 'flat oval elytra blotched black and orange' - ABSENT, and more absolutely than stated. I ran a full-canvas scan: max(R-B) over all 193,600 pixels is 2. There is not one warm pixel in the file. Zero pixels have R-B>8. The elytra are not merely 'un-blotched', the entire asset is chromatically neutral-to-cool. Also absent is the 'flat oval' - the shell is a tall near-circular dome, not a flat elongate oval, which is a second half of this must-read the original judge did not call out. The elytral oval closes in a single smooth continuous curve at the bottom; the midline seam terminates exactly at that rim and nothing extends past it. The coat is unmarked but it is straw-yellow rather than reddish-tan and is overlaid with heavy pale woolly striations that read as fleece, further pushing it toward sheep/goat. One genuinely feline detail survives — a vertical-slit amber eye — and it is not enough to redeem the silhouette. As drawn this is a tan goat or hornless calf wearing correct caracal ear tufts. WHAT I DID: read the 440x440 PNG whole, then decoded it and re-read four zoom crops (head at 7x and 12x, face at 18x, feet at 5x, torso at 2.5x) plus a numeric silhouette profile (column top/bottom scan).

MUST-READ 1 — BLACK TEAR STRIPES EYE TO MOUTH: ABSENT. Confirmed at 18x. The face carries exactly ONE dark facial line: a thin black tapered wedge that leaves the lower-front rim of the eye and runs FORWARD and slightly down along the length of the muzzle, terminating at the lip under the nose. It is the mouth/lip line — it is the only mouth indication on the head, its axis is nearly parallel to the muzzle, and there is no second stroke. A cheetah's tear stripe is a broad dark band crossing the muzzle roughly PERPENDICULAR to that line (inner eye corner straight down the side of the muzzle to the lip). Nothing crosses the muzzle anywhere. The defining identity feature is missing. The judge is right on this one and it alone carries the FAIL.

MUST-READ 2 — SOLID ROUND SPOTS, NOT ROSETTES: PRESENT AND GOOD. ~90 solid black round spots, dense on the flank, shoulder and haunch, thinning on the belly, with a few clustered into 2-3 spot blobs. No rings, no hollow centres. This must-read passes cleanly and should not be touched by the fix.

MUST-READ 3 — SMALL HEAD ON A DEEP NARROW CHEST WITH A LONG THIN TAIL: SPLIT. Tail passes (long, thin, smoothly tapering, sweeping down and forward past the hock; plain tan, no rings/black tip, but rings are not a must-read). Head SIZE passes — measured skull-back-to-nose is 58px against a 278px bbox width, headFrac ≈ 0.21 against the 0.20 target, and it reads visually small. Chest/proportion FAILS: measured torso underline depth runs 72px at the chest (x≈266), 51px at the loin (x≈226), 60px at the haunch — so the greyhound tuck IS there, but it is only ~29% and the topline is dead level with no withers rise, so the deep-chest/narrow-waist contrast does not read. Worse, the whole animal is far too short-bodied: nose-to-rump ≈ 200px over a shoulder height of ≈154px (ratio 1.30) and an overall bbox aspect of 1.44, against the card's aspect 2.0. Legs are straight vertical columns and the neck rises almost vertically from the shoulder with the head carried high — llama/deer carriage, not the low horizontal head carriage of a cat.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM:
• "Feet are hoof wedges" — WRONG. At 5x each foot is a flattened brown OVAL PAD with three faint toe grooves scored across it. They are low-detail disc paws, not hooves. Do not spend the fix on the feet; they read as paws already (they could stand a knuckle/toe bulge, but that is polish).
• "Head is large" — WRONG. It is on spec at headFrac ≈ 0.21 and reads small. The head defect is SHAPE, not size: a long blunt tapering wedge with no forehead stop, the forehead sloping continuously into the muzzle, and a big dark oval nose set on the SIDE of the muzzle mid-length rather than at the tip (reads as an equine nostril). The ears are two flat brown caps lying on the skull rather than the cheetah's small rounded upright ears. "Horse-muzzled" is the correct half of that claim.
• "No whippet waist" — OVERSTATED. There is a real but shallow tuck (72→51→60px). The failure is that the chest is not deep enough and the back is too level for the contrast to register, plus the body is far too short for its height.
• "Reads as a spotted fawn" — CORRECT and the right summary: tall, short-backed, level-topline, pillar-legged, upright-necked, small long-muzzled head, cream coat with scattered black spots. Only the yellow slit-pupil eye argues for cat.

CHASSIS NOTE for the family audit: the straight-column limbs, small oval foot pads, dead-level topline and vertical neck carriage here are the generic quadruped chassis, not a cheetah-specific build.

FIX PRIORITY: (1) add the tear stripe — a bold dark band from the inner eye corner down across the muzzle to the lip corner, and give the mouth its own separate shorter line; (2) shorten the muzzle, add a forehead stop, move the nose to the muzzle tip; (3) lengthen the body / drop the leg column so the aspect reaches ~2.0, deepen the chest and cut the loin harder.
