Overlaid on Cougar the outline is the SAME PATH: identical dorsal topline with the same shallow saddle dip and the same high croup, the same neck-to-shoulder junction, the same long tapering muzzle ending in a big round dark nose disc, the same pair of small rounded ears on top of the skull, the same four straight untapered pillar legs with no elbow, stifle or hock articulation, the same flat rounded pad-blobs for feet with two vertical grooves scored in them, and the same short flat-tan hook tail. Only the coat texture and the stamped markings differ. So 'reads as a pony stamped with paw prints' is fair; more precisely the chassis reads as a hornless calf/goat - an ungulate head and ungulate legs - not a felid. One thing the judge did NOT credit: the eye IS a correct gold felid eye with a vertical slit pupil, the only genuinely cat-like feature on the asset. It is not enough to carry the identity.

MUST-READ 1 - 'large cloud-shaped dark-edged blotches': ABSENT, judge correct. Every marking is the shared paw-print stamp: a round central pad with four small toe dots arranged around it. I counted roughly 20 of them across flank, shoulder, haunch and neck. CORRECTION to the judge's wording: they are not uniformly 'small'. Along the topline from about x=160 to x=205 the stamps are scaled up ~2.5x and overlap each other into an irregular dark saddle band; at thumbnail size that band is the only thing approaching a large blotch. Zoomed, it resolves unambiguously into merged paw prints - pad + toes still legible - not a cloud. There is no dark-edged, pale-centred rosette anywhere on the animal, and no marking is filled with anything but flat near-black. The coat is uniformly pale tan with hair-stroke texture and no dark edging at all.

MUST-READ 2 - 'tail as long as head and body combined': FAILS, but the judge's number is wrong. Head-body is ~217px (nose tip x=345 to rump rear edge x~128). The tail root is at ~(146,201); it arcs up over the croup to an apex at ~(122,193), sweeps left-down to ~(97,222) and hooks to a tip at ~(103,247). Traced along its centreline that is ~90px, i.e. ~0.41 of head-body, not 'a fifth' (0.2). Straight root-to-tip span is ~64px (0.30). So the tail is roughly two-fifths of the required length, not one-fifth - still less than half of the must-read, so the must-read fails, but a fix brief built on '5x too short' would overshoot. TWO DEFECTS THE JUDGE MISSED ON THE TAIL, and they matter as much as the length: (a) it is drawn in flat solid mid-tan with NO fur texture and NO markings whatsoever, while the clouded leopard's tail is the most heavily blotched part of the animal; (b) its form is a thin upward hook curled over the rump like a pig's or a spitz dog's, tapering to a rounded point, where the species has a thick, uniformly heavy, low-carried tail.

MUST-READ 3 - 'very short stout legs': FAILS, and the judge did not mention it at all. Belly line sits at y~223 at mid-body, ground contact at y~280, so free leg is ~57px against a chest depth of ~51px (top y~172 to belly y~223). The legs are ~112% of body depth and about 52% of standing height - long, straight and evenly thick top to bottom. The species reads by having a low-slung barrel on stubby legs; this reads leggy. Aspect is also off: body-only length/height is 217/139 = 1.56 against the required 2.3, so the torso is far too short and deep for the frame.

Net: two of three must-reads absent (cloud blotches, long tail), the third (short stout legs) also failed, and the underlying body is the shared big-cat/canid chassis rather than a cat. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a plain tan goat or donkey
rows.defect: Because the coat is correctly plain there is nothing left to sell the cat, and everything structural is ungulate: hoof feet, long horse muzzle, side-set eye, pony barrel. The very long heavy black-tipped tail is instead a short thin unmarked hook; the muzzle has no black bars; the hindquarters sit level with rather than above the shoulder hump.
rows.fix: Give it a tail longer than the body with a dark tip, black muzzle bars on a short round skull, and raise the croup above the withers over big paw feet.
rows.verifyWhy: Upheld, but two parts of the original claim need correcting. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a deep-barrelled tan quadruped, body bbox x82-356 / y125-298, standing square on four straight columnar legs. mustRead 2 ('completely plain unmarked tawny coat') is GENUINELY SATISFIED and should not be re-fixed - the flank at 6x is plain tawny with long shaggy fur strokes, zero spots, zero rosettes, no mane. CORRECTION 1 to the claim: it is NOT true that 'there is nothing left to sell the cat'. The eye IS feline and is the one correct read on the asset - a large amber iris with a hard vertical slit pupil, ringed in cream (visible at 16x, centred approx x=320,y=142). The ears are also small, rounded and low-domed, which is correct for cougar (two brown rounded lobes on the crown at approx x=296-318, y=126-140). Those two features are present and drawn; they are simply overwhelmed by an ungulate body. CORRECTION 2: the coat texture is not donkey-slick, it is a long-fibre shaggy fleece with a hard-edged fur 'cape' terminating along the shoulder (visible at 8x, x=255-325) that reads as a saddle blanket - closer to a plush llama/sheep than a donkey, and the cape edge is itself part of the pack-animal read. WHAT GENUINELY FAILS: (a) mustRead 1, the tail. Verified by dark-pixel scan - every dark cluster in the image is at the ears (x~300-312,y~132), the nose (x~336-348,y~132-144), the four feet (y~288) and some stray leg ticks; there is not one dark pixel anywhere in the tail region (x<140). The tail runs from a root at approx (133,195) in a rigid hook out to (85,225) and down to a blunt rounded tip at (98,258): arc length ~110px against a 216px head-body, i.e. roughly half the length required, ~9px thick against an ~18px leg, uniform flat mid-tan with no taper, no volume shading and no black tip. Calling it a 'short thin unmarked hook' is exactly right. (b) mustRead 3, the head. There are no black muzzle bars, no dark whisker pads and no white chin - confirmed at 16x, the muzzle is flat unmarked tan with a single plain dark-brown oval nose set on the SIDE of the snout rather than at the front. The head is also not small and round: it is a long tapering wedge with a protruding donkey/tapir muzzle, and it measures ~66px against a 216px head-body = headFrac 0.30 against the specified 0.22, so it is oversized as well as the wrong shape. (c) the note's 'hindquarters sit higher than the shoulders' fails, and the judge described this correctly. Measured topline: croup top y=158 at x=162-182; withers top y=152-155 at x=282-292. The FRONT is a few px higher, so the rear is level-to-marginally-lower - the opposite of the cougar's rising rump. CORRECTION 3, matters for the fix: the feet are not literally hooves. Each is a dark-brown flattened ellipse, wider than the leg and seated under it like a clog, but it does carry three vertical toe grooves (clear at 14x). At card size it reads hoof, so the fix is not merely 'recolour' - the pad must be rebuilt as a rounded cat paw with separated toes and claws sitting on a digitigrade ankle, because the legs above it are straight ungulate columns with no carpal break in front and only a shallow hock behind. Also note stray small black tick marks partway up the left hind shank (approx x=118-135, y=238-268) that read as scratches or dirt, not as claws or markings, and should go. VERDICT: with 2 of 3 must-reads and the posture note failing, and with the silhouette (deep barrel, tucked waist, short level back, columnar legs, clog feet, long-muzzled head) reading as hoofstock, the asset does not read as a cat at card size. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a golden pony stamped with paw prints
rows.defect: The rosettes are literal paw-print shapes — a pad with toes above it — rather than broken rings with a central spot. The jaw is a slim tapering horse muzzle, the exact opposite of the massive blocky jaguar head. The build is a deep barrel on hooved posts, not a low stocky cat on short legs.
rows.fix: Redraw the markings as broken dark rings each holding one or two central dots, and give the skull a heavy broad blocky jaw with a wide nose.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 5-10x magnification on head, flank, tail and both feet. FAIL stands, but two of the three stated causes need correcting.

WHAT KILLS IT (and the original judge never named it): THE FEET ARE HOOVES. At 10x each foot is a flat brown oval plate sitting on the ground with two-to-three short vertical incised grooves down its face - a cloven/keratin hoof, not a cat's rounded metacarpal pad with four toe pads. All four legs are straight tapering columns with a fetlock/hock notch above the hoof, i.e. the shared pony chassis. Nothing about a jaguar's broad plantigrade-looking paw, splayed toes or heavy forearm is present. This is the single most decisive wrong-organism signal in the render and it should be the first thing fixed.

MUST-READ 3 'massive broad blocky jaw' - GENUINELY ABSENT. Confirmed. The skull is a small rounded cranium and the muzzle is a long tapering snout roughly as long as the braincase, narrowing to a rounded tip with a large dark oval nose set on the side of the tip. The lower jaw is a thin wedge closed by a single hairline mouth stroke that runs straight back; there is zero cheek/masseter breadth, no wide zygomatic flare, no chin mass. CORRECTION to the claim: it is not a 'horse' muzzle - a horse muzzle is blunt and square-ended; this is a dog/bear snout with a bulbous nose. The substance of the claim (slim, tapering, the opposite of blocky) is right, the animal named is wrong, and calling it 'horse' would send a fix in the wrong direction.

MUST-READ 2 'rosettes with spots inside them' - PARTIALLY PRESENT, the claim that they are all literal paw prints is OVERSTATED. At 5x on the flank I count at least a dozen markings that are unmistakably broken rings: 4-6 small black dots arranged in a circle with a single smaller dot in the middle and open field between the dots. Clear examples sit on the mid-flank, just behind the shoulder, and one very legible one on the side of the neck below the ear. So the rosette-with-central-spot logic IS implemented. It fails for three other reasons: (a) the ring is drawn as loose solid dots rather than a dark broken outline enclosing a tawny field, so there is no enclosed interior; (b) roughly half the clusters have one oversized blob plus 3-4 satellite dots and merge into a pad-and-toes silhouette - that is where the paw-print reading comes from, and it is a size/merge problem, not the wrong shape being drawn everywhere; (c) the pattern does not wrap the animal - the tail is a completely plain flat orange tube with no marks and no black tip, the legs below the elbow/stifle carry nothing, and the head carries only two stray flecks. Fix the merging and the coverage before rewriting the rosette primitive.

MUST-READ 1 'stocky muscular build on short legs' - HALF PRESENT but as the wrong animal. The barrel is deep and the legs are short-ish, so the proportion reads stocky, but it is ungulate stocky: a smooth sausage barrel with a pinched waist crease, a thick short neck carrying a small high-set head, and no shoulder blade, no deep chest drop below the elbow, no visible scapular hump.

OTHER OBSERVATIONS. The eye IS correct and should be preserved: a large round eye with a bright amber iris and a true vertical slit pupil - the one felid signal in the asset. The ear is not a cat ear: at 10x it is a rounded low brown lobe on the crown with a second darker rounded lobe overlapping in front of it, reading as a ram's curled horn plus a hound flap; there are no erect triangular pinnae. Coat colour is a flat pale gold with painterly straight fur streaks, closer to a palomino hide than a jaguar's warm ochre. Silhouette edge is clean, no clipping, shadow ellipse sits correctly under the feet.

SUMMARY: the animal an unprompted viewer names is a hooved goat/pony with spots. Two of three must-reads (blocky jaw, cat paws implied by the build) are absent, the third is drawn but reads wrong at size. FAIL upheld; the fix order is hooves to paws, then skull mass to a short broad jaw, then de-merge the rosettes and extend them onto tail and legs.

rows.readsAs: a pale pony with paw-print stamps
rows.defect: The rosettes are solid paw-print clusters, not hollow open rings — the single feature separating a leopard from a jaguar is missing, and this image is interchangeable with the Jaguar one at a different fill. The tail is a short thin upward hook nowhere near body length, and the body is a high-humped deep barrel on hooves rather than a low-slung slender cat.
rows.fix: Make every rosette an open ring with an empty centre, lengthen the tail to nearly body length, and drop the topline flat onto paw feet.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 3x full-frame and 6-10x on head, flank, feet and tail. UPHELD, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and would send the fix in the wrong direction.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS: a pale hoofed grazer on the shared ungulate/pony chassis. Barrel chest, dipped back with a pronounced hump at the withers and hindquarters that sit HIGHER than the shoulders, a sagging belly line, a thick upright neck carrying the head high, and four long straight columnar legs with a visible knee band. Feet are wide splayed pads with three rounded toe lobes in a darker tan, wider than the leg shaft - not cat paws, not true cloven hooves, the generic chassis toe-pad. The head is a long downward-tapering ovine/equine muzzle ending in a large dark oval nose disc; the 'ears' are two flat brown discs laid on the crown reading as ear ROOTS, not cat ears. The eye is a big amber almond with a VERTICAL SLIT pupil - wrong for a leopard (round pupil) and the only cat-ish cue on the whole animal. mustRead 'low-slung slender body' is absent in every respect: this is tall, barrel-bodied and long-legged.

CLAIM CONFIRMED - interchangeable with the Jaguar: yes, and strongly. Rendering Jaguar.png at the same crop gives the SAME silhouette pixel-for-pixel in outline - same barrel body, same hooked tail, same two-disc head with the same muzzle and nose disc, same three-lobed feet. Only the spot layout and a slightly cooler/paler fill differ. Ironically the Jaguar's clusters read MORE like rosettes than the Leopard's, so the pair also inverts the packet note that distinguishes them.

CLAIM PARTLY WRONG - 'rosettes are solid clusters, not hollow open rings': under 8x a substantial number of the marks ARE rings/arcs of 4-6 small dots enclosing an unmarked tawny centre, mostly on the lower shoulder and mid-flank. The open-ring intent IS present in the paint. The real defect is that it does not survive to legibility: the coat is buried under several hundred loose isolated single dots scattered with no organisation, plus two or three large amorphous SOLID black masses (the worst is ~30 src-px across on the mid-flank above the hind leg, an inkblot with a couple of tawny holes in it). At viewing size the whole coat reads as dalmatian/appaloosa splatter, and a handful of clusters resolve as pad-plus-toes paw-print stamps (one unmistakable one on the shoulder just behind the jaw). FIX DIRECTION: do not 'add rings' - reduce dot COUNT hard, enlarge the ring diameter, regularise ring spacing into flank rows, and delete the solid masses. Adding rings on top of the current noise will not help.

CLAIM PARTLY WRONG - 'short upward hook': the tail is not merely an upward hook. It leaves the rump, arcs UP and BACK, then bends DOWN, ending around mid-thigh height - a J. Measured on the source pixels its path is roughly 80px against a ~200px body, i.e. about 40% of body length. So the substance is right (nowhere near the required 'nearly as long as the body') but it is a half-length descending J, not a stub. It is also a flat, hard-edged, unshaded solid orange-tan tube MORE saturated than the body and completely unmarked - no spots, no rings, no dark tip - reading as a pasted-on element rather than an extension of the animal.

SCORECARD vs mustRead: 'long thick tail nearly as long as the body' ABSENT (~40%, wrong colour, unmarked). 'hollow ring rosettes with empty centres' PRESENT BUT ILLEGIBLE (drowned in dot noise and solid blobs). 'low-slung slender body' ABSENT (tall barrel ungulate). Two of three must-reads fail and the organism reads as the wrong animal entirely. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a lion — but a lion mask bolted to a pony
rows.defect: The mane and the black tail tuft are both present and legible so the species does land, but the mane is a flat undifferentiated fan disc that swallows the whole head instead of framing it, and the head inside it is the same long horse muzzle with a side-set eye. The back is not level — it dips then humps like a pony's — and the feet are hoof wedges, not paws.
rows.fix: Cut the mane back so a short round felid face reads clearly inside it, and rebuild the four legs as felid limbs on broad paws under a level topline.

rows.readsAs: a spotted goat kid
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent: no black ear tufts (the ear is a small folded triangle), no flared facial ruff, and no oversized snowshoe paws — the feet are tiny dark hoof blocks, the smallest-footed thing in the batch. The hind legs are not longer than the fore. Identical in silhouette to the Bobcat entry with slightly different splatter.
rows.fix: Add tall black ear tufts and a wide flared cheek ruff, and make the paws visibly oversized, round and spread-toed.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, but one of the three stated causes is factually wrong and the fix list must be corrected before anyone works from it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440, inspected at 6x and 12x nearest-neighbour crops of head, hindquarter and feet):
The organism is a barrel-chested quadruped with a dead-level topline, a long smooth neck, four long straight columnar legs ending in small pads, and NO TAIL WHATSOEVER (the haunch simply terminates in a rounded rump; there is not even a bobbed nub). Coat is cream/bone with dense irregular black blotches concentrated on the flank and shoulder, thinning to speckles on the throat. At thumbnail size this reads as a spotted goat kid / appaloosa foal. The judge's organism call is correct.

CORRECTION 1 - 'No black ear tufts' is WRONG. The ear tufts ARE drawn and ARE black. The single viewer-side ear is a tall dark-brown filled triangle on the crown, and from its apex rise five thin near-black bristle strokes fanning up and back, roughly 40% of the ear's own height. They are legible at 6x and unmistakable at 12x; they are merely thin (1px strokes at native size) so they wash out in a thumbnail. The real defect is different and worse: the identical tuft cluster is present on the Bobcat AND on the Caracal in this same batch, so the tuft is a family-wide default decoration, not a Lynx identifier. It carries zero discriminating power. Fix = make the Lynx tuft long, thick and unmistakable, and make sure the Bobcat's is the short one.

CORRECTION 2 - 'the feet are the smallest hoof blocks in the batch' is imprecise on both counts. They are not hoof blocks: at 6x each foot is a flattened oval pad with three or four vertical toe-division lines scribed into it - a small splayed paw, not a cloven hoof. And they are not the smallest in the batch; they are pixel-for-pixel the SAME foot as the Bobcat's and the same size class as the Caracal's (the Caracal's actually read more hoof-like, being darker and two-lobed). The true finding: the Lynx is using the shared default paw at default scale, when its whole identity requires a paw that is conspicuously oversized - a snowshoe disc wider than the cannon bone above it. Nothing about this foot is enlarged at all.

CONFIRMED AS STATED:
- Flared facial ruff: genuinely absent. The jaw line runs straight back into an unbroken cylindrical neck; the silhouette edge from chin to chest has no flare, no cheek whisker fan, no muttonchop mass. There is a pale diagonal band crossing the neck below the jaw, but it is a shading seam (the same seam appears on the Bobcat and Caracal) and it does not break the outline, so it cannot be counted as a ruff.
- Long hind legs: absent. Rump top and withers top sit level; the hind limb has more angulation (a visible stifle/hock bend swept rearward) than the foreleg but is not longer, and the hindquarters do not stand higher than the shoulders.
- Identical to the Bobcat: fully confirmed and it is the most damning finding. Rendering Lynx.png and Bobcat.png at the same crop and scale gives two images that differ ONLY in spot density and a slight coat-tone shift. Same skull, same long tapering wedge muzzle with the nose oval set back from the tip, same yellow slit-pupil eye, same triangular tufted ear, same neck, same level topline, same barrel, same four legs, same feet, same missing tail, same shadow ellipse. They are one chassis in two speckle patterns.

HEAD DETAIL FOR THE FIX: the skull is the batch's generic chassis head and is not feline at all - a long tapered snout with a downturned rounded tip, a large dark nose oval sitting on TOP of the muzzle well back from the end, and a long straight mouth line running past the eye. It reads lizard/canid. The only feline cue anywhere on the animal is the vertical-slit yellow eye. A lynx needs the opposite: a very short blunt muzzle, a wide flat-topped skull, and cheek mass wider than the braincase.

rows.readsAs: a spotted pony
rows.defect: The markings are the same scattered paw-print stamps as Jaguar and Leopard, with no chain-like streaking running lengthwise along the flank, and there are no black cheek stripes on the face. The build is the same full-sized pony barrel as its batch-mates with no housecat scaling cue at all. Feet are hooves.
rows.fix: Run the rosettes into linked chains streaming lengthwise along the flank and add the two black bars on each cheek on a smaller, shorter body.
rows.verifyWhy:
I zoomed the 440x440 PNG at 6-12x on the head, ear, flank, feet and tail before deciding. The FAIL stands, and the organism failure is WORSE than stated — it is not merely a spotted pony, it is a spotted HOOFSTOCK. Corrections and additions to the original claim, feature by feature:

MUST-READ 1, chain-like rosettes running in streaks along the flank — ABSENT, judge correct, but their description of the marks is partly wrong. The marks are not uniformly 'paw-print stamps'; at 8x the flank carries ~14 discrete clusters of 4-7 small round dots, and several of them (mid-flank, over the hip, on the shoulder) are genuine broken-ring rosettes with a hollow tan centre. So the rosette PRIMITIVE is there. What is absent is the ocelot's actual signature: the rosettes never coalesce, never elongate, and never align. They are scattered at random angles with no directional field, so nothing forms the oblique chains/continuous streak-bands that run shoulder-to-haunch on a real ocelot. A few marks on the neck and shoulder DO read as literal paw-print stamps (a large blob with 3-4 toe dots above it) — the generic mammal stamp — but that is the minority case, not the whole coat. The fix is directional, not new shapes: elongate and chain the rosettes already present into 4-6 continuous oblique streaks, and clear the belly/lower flank so the streaks read.

MUST-READ 2, two black stripes on each cheek — ABSENT, judge fully correct. At 12x the cheek is completely flat unmarked tan from the eye back to the jaw hinge. Zero facial marking of any kind. One thing the judge missed and should be preserved by the fix: the eye IS feline — a yellow/amber iris with a hard VERTICAL SLIT PUPIL, correctly drawn. That slit pupil is the only cat cue on the entire asset.

MUST-READ 3, housecat-sized build with a shortish tail — ABSENT, judge correct but understated. The chassis is the shared pony/ungulate chassis: barrel ribcage, straight topline with a dip behind the withers, short thick neck carried level, and — decisively — the FEET ARE HOOVES. Each of the four legs terminates in a dark-brown splayed cleat block wider than the leg column, with no toe separation, no digital pads and no claws. Hind legs are straight columns with an ungulate hock, not a feline crouch. The tail is a flat, solid-fill, uniform-width tan hook curving up and back, with no taper, no banding, no dark tip and no fur shading — it reads as a pasted-on shape, not a tail. It is shortish, so the 'shortish' half of the must-read is technically satisfied by accident, but nothing else about it reads as cat.

HEAD (the judge did not examine this and it is the single biggest defect). At 12x the skull is a long, tubular, slightly downturned equine/canid muzzle roughly 1.6x the length of the braincase, with a dark oval nose set on the SIDE of the muzzle tip and a long horizontal mouth line running most of the muzzle length. A cat skull is short, round and blunt with the nose on the front plane — none of that is present. The ears are two small ROUNDED BROWN LOBES on the crown (a larger flap set back, a smaller lobe forward beside the eye); neither is a triangular feline ear. There is no cheek ruff, no whisker pad, no brow.

VERDICT: three of three must-reads fail on their defining half, and the underlying organism reads as a small hoofed ungulate with cat eyes. This is a chassis-level rebuild (feline skull, digitigrade toed paws, low crouched topline, long tapering banded tail), not a markings pass. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a spotted goat kid or fawn
rows.defect: The defining feature — legs longer relative to the body than any other cat — is inverted: the legs are the same short pony posts as everything else in the batch and the barrel is deep rather than small and slung high between them. The ears are slightly larger than its siblings' but still laid flat on the skull, not big upright ovals. Feet are hooves and the spots are splatter, not bold bars and spots.
rows.fix: Roughly double the leg length and shrink the barrel so the body hangs high between them, and stand two large upright oval ears on top of a small round head.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL stands, but BOTH stated causes are factually wrong and must not be worked from. I decoded the PNG and measured every row, and I cropped the head, ear, face, feet and legs at 6-12x.

CORRECTION 1 - THE LEGS ARE NOT INVERTED AND ARE NOT 'the same short pony posts as the rest of the batch'. Serval has the LONGEST legs in the family in absolute pixels and the second-highest leg-to-body-depth ratio of all 13. Measuring belly-line to ground vs topline-to-belly across the whole batch: Serval 82px leg / 59px depth = 1.39; Cheetah 1.45; Lynx 1.14; Caracal 1.15; Bobcat 1.09; Cougar 1.09; Ocelot 1.03; Clouded Leopard 1.00; Leopard 0.98; Tiger 0.88; Jaguar 0.81; Snow Leopard 0.70; Lion 0.55. Family median is ~1.03. Legs are 43% of total figure height, the highest in the batch. There is a genuinely airy open gap under the belly. Whoever fixes this must NOT lengthen the legs - that axis is already correct and differentiated. Nor is the barrel 'deep': body runs x142-x305 (163px) by 59px deep, aspect 2.76, which is slender, not a barrel.

CORRECTION 2 - THE EARS DO NOT LIE FLAT ON THE SKULL. The near ear is a large oval pinna with a tan rim and a fully rendered dark-brown inner bowl, ~32px wide x 34px tall, standing clear above the skull line (skull top ~y140, ear tip y116) and roughly as tall as the entire visible skull. Its inner bowl is a clear elongated ellipse, not a disc. The real defect is that it is CANTED BACK ~25-30 degrees instead of standing vertical, and that it is accompanied by TWO spurious extra lobes - a shapeless brown blob at lower-left (nominally the far ear, but it has no rim, no bowl, no shape) and a stray triangular point poking up at x285-292 that belongs to no ear at all. Three ear-ish masses, one of which is correct.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS - it is organism-level, not serval-level. All three must-reads are technically present (long legs: yes, measured; large oval ear on a small head: the near ear, yes; short tail and bold spots: yes, tail is ~1/3 body and the flank carries big coalescing black blotches). The asset fails because the underlying chassis is not a felid at all:
(a) THE MUZZLE. The face is a long smooth taper with the nose drawn as a dark oval on the SIDE of the snout rather than a nose-pad at the tip, plus a long thin mouth line running back to the jaw. No muzzle pad, no whisker-pad bulge, no short cat face. This is a canid/ungulate snout and it is the single loudest wrong signal in the image.
(b) THE FEET. Each foot is a broad flat elliptical PLATE with 3-4 vertical toe grooves, splaying far wider than the leg column, with the leg landing on it like a post on a saucer. Reads as a hoof-pedestal, not a paw.
(c) THE LIMB MODEL. Both legs are straight undifferentiated columns - the hind leg runs as one unbroken post from hip to foot with no hock and no stifle, the fore leg has only a token bend. This IS the shared chassis the packet warns about; it is shared in FORM even though it is not shared in LENGTH.
(d) HEAD CARRIAGE. Head hangs low and forward on a thick neck (browsing posture), not the cat's level alert carriage.
(e) TAIL. Short is correct, but it is a fat uniform-width tan tube with a blunt round end, no taper, and crucially NO rings and NO black tip - a serval tail is barred with a black tip. The 'barred' half of must-read 3 is absent here.
(f) THE LEGS ARE COMPLETELY UNSPOTTED. Bold blotches cover the flank and belly but stop dead at the shoulder and hip; both legs are plain cream from top to foot. A serval is spotted right down onto the feet. This is a cheap, high-value fix and it also stops the long legs reading as bare posts.
Net gestalt: a long-snouted, plate-footed, straight-posted spotted quadruped with a low head. The prior judge's 'spotted goat kid' impression is a defensible read of the result, but they reached it by blaming the two things this asset actually got right.

rows.readsAs: a white spotted pony with a horse's tail
rows.defect: The tail is a short grey feathered plume hanging like a horse's tail rather than an enormously long thick ropy cat tail. Rosettes are the family paw-print stamp, not large open rings. The muzzle is long and pointed instead of short under a domed skull, and the feet are small hoof wedges — the opposite of the big paws called for.
rows.fix: Replace the plume with a very long thick uniform ropy tail as long as head plus body, and shorten the muzzle under a high domed forehead over big paws.
rows.verifyWhy: Verified at 440x440 plus 5x-11x nearest-neighbour crops of head, rump/tail, feet and flank. The FAIL stands: two of the three must-reads are absent and the note's head spec is inverted. (1) TAIL - must-read is 'enormously long thick ropy tail', note says 'as long as the head and body'. What is drawn is a short radiating fan of grey strands with a white rounded lobe laid over it, socketed HIGH on the rump like a horse dock, projecting back-and-down roughly 55px against a ~265px head-and-body. That is ~20% of the required length, and it has no cylindrical mass, no taper, no dark rings, and no continuation of the spine line. The judge's 'short grey feathered plume' is exactly right; their headline word 'horse's tail' is the same object described loosely - it is a feather-duster fan, not a horse's hair fall, but it lands in the same place and fails identically. (2) COAT/ROSETTES - must-read is 'pale smoky coat with large open rosettes'. Base coat is chalk white with a faint grey brush texture, no smoky grey-cream cast at all. The markings are dark chocolate-brown, and the dominant motif genuinely is the family paw-print stamp the judge names: repeated clusters of one larger pad blob with three or four small toe dots above it, scattered over shoulder, flank and haunch. CORRECTION to the judge: it is not exclusively paw prints - there ARE perhaps six genuine broken-ring open rosettes on the shoulder and the top of the foreleg (open C and O shapes with a hollow centre). They do not rescue the read, because every mark is roughly 1/12 the flank depth where a snow leopard's rosettes should be ~1/5 and read as large open rings; at thumbnail scale the whole coat reads as speckle/appaloosa freckling, not rosettes. (3) LEGS AND PAWS - must-read is 'short stout legs and big paws'; the judge did not mention this and it also fails. The legs are long slender straight columns with a pronounced knee/hock and no forearm mass. The feet are small flat grey ellipses with three vertical toe grooves - they are marginally wider than the shin so 'paw not hoof' is technically readable, but they are nowhere near snowshoe-sized. (4) HEAD - the note says 'muzzle is short and the skull domed'. Drawn is the exact inverse: a long, deep, near-parallel-sided muzzle tube extending forward about as far again as the braincase, and a low flat skull with no dome. CORRECTION to the judge: the muzzle is NOT pointed - it is blunt and rounded at the tip. Two further head defects neither judge recorded: the nose is a dark brown oval planted on the SIDE flank of the muzzle well back from the tip instead of at the tip, and the lower jaw is missing entirely - the mouth is a floating grey stroke that runs out under the muzzle and hooks up at the end, with the chin merging into the neck so the muzzle appears to float. WHAT IS RIGHT: the eye is a good cat eye (amber iris, vertical slit pupil), and the ears are two small rounded grey ovals on the crown, which is a defensible snow-leopard ear and is NOT part of the defect. Overall silhouette - barrel chest, dipped back, high rump, small head on a thick arched neck, four straight columnar legs - is the shared pony/quadruped chassis, and the fix here is chassis-level (cat spine and crouch, short heavy limbs, huge paws) plus a rebuilt tail primitive and a rosette primitive that draws large open rings instead of the paw-print stamp.

rows.readsAs: a tiger — but the stripes are doing all the work

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a plump, egg-shaped, ground-standing bird. The body is a fat rounded ovoid, wider than tall, carried horizontally on two short yellow legs whose three-toed feet are planted flat on a cast elliptical ground shadow. Do not "add a hook" - the fix is contrast and shape refinement (dark horn tip, distinct yellow cere at the base, slimmer profile).

CORRECTION 2 - THE TAIL IS NOT SHORT AND BLUNT. There is a distinct tail: a long, narrow, sharply POINTED dark-brown wedge projecting back and slightly down from the rump, roughly a third of the body length beyond the body edge, terminating in a fine point. A large rounded ovoid wing pad occupies the whole flank, ringed by a soft dark arc that traces its leading edge from the shoulder around to a ROUNDED trailing corner that stops well short of the tail. Immediately behind and below it are four or five thin dark radiating strokes that read as a token flight-feather fan. The problem is that this is a broad, blunt, folded-and-rounded wing (a buteo/gamebird wing) that is tan-on-tan with almost no value separation from the body, so it half-disappears; there is no narrow scythe-like planform and no pointed primary projection reaching the tail tip. Combined with the planted feet and ground shadow, the declared posture:flying is contradicted outright - this bird is standing.

CONFIRMED ABSENT (judge right): no dark malar/moustache stripe - the face is uniform flat tan from bill to nape with nothing below the eye. The back is NOT rufous and carries NO black spotting; the plumage texture is pale cream flecking scattered over mid-tan (light-on-dark speckle), i.e. the inverse of the required dark-on-rufous spotting, which is what makes it read as cryptic gamebird camouflage. The eye is a plain glossy black bead with no supraorbital ridge; head is round and dovelike rather than slim and small-headed on a slim body.

BAND: FAIL. Of the three must-reads, only "hooked bill" survives; the moustache stripe is absent, the rufous/black-spotted back is absent and inverted in polarity, the barring is absent, and the pointed falcon wing is absent (replaced by a rounded folded one). WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN. A single fat egg/ellipse body, roughly x=145..312, y=155..265 in the 440px frame — about 167 long by 110 tall, so a body aspect near 1.5 (about 1.8 counting the tail fan) against the packet's 1.9. The ellipse is close to top/bottom symmetric about a full-length horizontal lateral line. A dark fan-shaped caudal fin with radiating rays is butted straight onto the blunt rear of the ellipse with no peduncle and no taper. There is no dorsal fin, no anal fin, no pelvic fins. The whole body INCLUDING the head is tiled with a mechanical, evenly repeating scale-row texture — Lophius is scaleless, so the texture is itself off-species. A single eye, small, white-ringed, sits high and forward. A proper illicium is present and is the one genuinely good element: a thin arched stalk rising off the top of the snout carrying a glowing pale-blue esca bulb.

The silhouette is widest just aft of centre and tapers to a rounded nose, so the front of the animal is the NARROWEST part. Nothing in the outline says 'a head that is the animal.' 'Huge upturned mouth ringed with inward-slanting teeth' is also absent: the mouth is a single STRAIGHT HORIZONTAL dark line, closed, with no gape, no opening, and no lower jaw drawn at all. 'Frilly skin flaps along the jaw' are absent — the silhouette edge is smooth and unbroken for its entire circuit, no fringe anywhere. Two of the three must-reads are gone and the third (lure) is the only one delivered. With an egg body, a fang line and a lure it reads as a generic deep-sea anglerfish, not Lophius.

CORRECTIONS TO THE STATED CAUSE.
(1) 'No head/body boundary' is wrong. There IS a faint vertical curved gill/head line at x~258 running the full height of the body. It reads as a head boundary. The problem is what it bounds: it puts the head at only ~32% of body length against the packet's headFrac 0.5, and the segment it isolates is the tapering NOSE end, so the boundary actively confirms a small head rather than establishing a huge one. Fix the proportion, don't add a line that already exists.
(2) 'Just a small notch of straight vertical teeth' is wrong on both counts. The tooth row is not small — about eight white fangs spanning roughly a third of the body length, from x~250 out to the snout tip. And they are not vertical: they hang DOWN off the upper jaw line and slant slightly BACKWARD toward the tail, i.e. outward-and-aft rather than the required inward-slanting ring. The real defect is that they are upper-jaw-only teeth pendant from a flat closed line — there is no opposing lower jaw, no cavity, and no upward hinge — so no gape reads at any zoom.
(3) 'No pectoral fins' is wrong. There IS a small pectoral fin: a triangular fan of radiating rays with a dark tip, sitting immediately behind and below the mouth line around x=225-250, y=225-240. It is drawn entirely INSIDE the body silhouette at very low contrast, so it never breaks the outline and contributes nothing to the read. It needs to be enlarged and pushed proud of the silhouette, not created from scratch.

Also failing the packet: posture is 'sprawling' but the fish is drawn as a neutral lateral swimmer with no bottom-propping stance.

FIX ORDER: (a) rebuild the silhouette so the front third is the widest, flattest mass and the rear tapers to the caudal — head must own ~half the length and exceed body height; (b) replace the flat mouth line with a wide upturned gape hinged well back under the eye, with an opposing lower jaw and an interior, and re-aim the fangs inward; (c) add the jaw fringe so the ventral silhouette edge is ragged; (d) enlarge the existing pectoral fan out past the outline; (e) drop the uniform scale tiling for scaleless mottled skin. Keep the lure exactly as drawn.

Head is the narrow terminal point of the lens; the source confirms it is unavoidable, since profile 'fusiform' uses heightAt = depth*sin(pi*t^0.85), which is EXACTLY ZERO at t=1, so the snout is a mathematical point and the widest girth sits at t=0.44, i.e. just AFT of centre. Nothing in the sprite reads as a skull, let alone a broad flattened one; headFrac 0.35 is not met by any measure. (2) Huge fan-like pectorals: the judge's wording is WRONG and this needs correcting for the fix. There IS a pectoral fin. faunaoverrides3.ts draws one in the non-wings branch as c.ellipse(0,0,len*0.22,depth*0.34) rotated 0.44 rad, filled rgba(cr,cg,cb,0.86) -- i.e. THE BODY'S OWN COLOUR -- with five 1.5px ray strokes. At 16x I can see it: a same-hue ellipse roughly 30x15 px with two or three thin dark slanted ray lines, lying entirely INSIDE the silhouette just behind and below the gill arc, reading as a crease or a smudge rather than an appendage. So the correct statement is 'the pectoral is vestigial, body-coloured and wholly interior to the outline, contributing nothing to the silhouette', not 'there are no pectoral fins at all'. Either way the identity feature -- the huge fanned props -- is not readable, so the must-read fails. Note for the fixer: the same file already has the exact mechanism needed, spec.wings:'fan' (the gurnard path, span len*1.30, chord depth*3.60, 12 rays, drawn once behind the body and once over it). Sculpin's override at line 809 simply does not set it. (3) Scaleless tapering tadpole body: FAILS on both halves, judge correct. The body is fore-aft near-symmetric rather than tapering (see the sin profile above), and it is explicitly coated with a scale material -- coatMaterial(..., 'scale') clipped to the body -- which at 4x is plainly visible as a dense diamond scale mesh over the whole dorsal half and belly. A sculpin is naked-skinned; this one is armoured in fish-scale wallpaper. OTHER OBSERVATIONS. Posture is 'swimming' and the sprite is a free-floating midwater fish with a cast shadow well below it -- there is no bottom contact, no propped stance, no splayed base of support, which is half of what the pectoral must-read is actually asking for. The eye, spec'd 'prominent', is a small white ring stuck on the very apex of the snout, high on the taper; it reads as a bubble on the nose rather than the big high-set eye of a sculpin. The dorsal comb is the only feature with any character and it pushes the read the wrong way -- toward a perch or a small sunfish. Overall the asset is currently the shared generic 'fusiform + fan tail + spiny dorsal + mottle' fish chassis with no sculpin-specific geometry at all; two of three must-reads absent and the third inverted. FAIL stands.

Upheld, but one load-bearing part of the original claim is factually WRONG and must not drive the fix.

WHAT I ACTUALLY SAW (440x440, inspected at 5x and 8x nearest-neighbour crops of the umbel, mid-foliage and base):

1. FOLIAGE — claim CONFIRMED, and it is the fatal defect. At 5x the foliage resolves into roughly 30 DISCRETE, OPAQUE, HARD-EDGED oval lozenges per row, each ~8x5 px, sitting on dead-straight horizontal pinna rachises drawn as solid 2px olive bars. Each leaflet is a filled ellipse with a highlight, individually countable, with black gaps between neighbours. There is not one thread, hair, filament or soft edge anywhere in the plant. The must-read 'cloud of thread-fine feathery foliage' is 0% present. As drawn this reads as a rowan / mimosa / Nephrolepis fern pinna — a pinnate COMPOUND leaf with visible leaflets — which is precisely the organism fennel is not. Fennel's silhouette should have no countable elements at all; it should be a soft, semi-transparent haze whose outline dissolves at the edge.

2. UMBEL — claim PARTLY WRONG. The judge said 'no spoke rays'. There ARE spoke rays: at 8x, a fan of about a dozen thin dark-olive radiating lines springs from the stem apex out to (and slightly past, below) the rim of the yellow cap, clearly visible as a splayed brush under the cap. The defect is not absence, it is CONTRAST AND OCCLUSION — the rays are drawn dark-olive against a near-black background and are then covered by an opaque yellow lid, so at fullsize nothing of them survives. Do not 'add rays'; lighten them and let them emerge past the rim. What IS genuinely wrong with the umbel: (a) it is a CONVEX DOMED CRESCENT — a shallow banana/mushroom-cap shape with the high point in the middle — where the must-read demands FLAT-TOPPED, so the profile silhouette is wrong; (b) it is a single flat fill of one yellow with zero floret articulation — no dotted rim, no separated umbellet clusters, no ray-tip terminals; (c) it is tiny relative to the plant (~55px wide on a ~135px-wide plant) and sits on a long bare stem section, so it reads as a lamp-shade finial rather than a compound umbel.

3. STEM — claim CONFIRMED. A plain flat olive/yellow-green cylinder with one lighter left edge and one darker right edge. No rib lines, no flutes, no hollow read, and no blue tint whatsoever.

4. BULB — claim CONFIRMED. The stem runs at constant width straight down and simply stops on a soft dark elliptical ground shadow. No swelling, no overlapping sheath layers, no white, no roots. The harvest object ('swollen white bulb base') is entirely absent, and so is the alternative harvest read (ribbed seeds).

5. COLOUR — an error the original claim UNDERSTATED. It only flagged the stem's missing blue. In fact the WHOLE plant is bright chartreuse / acid yellow-green, the opposite end of the axis from the specified 'blue-grey green, feathery'. Desaturating and cooling the entire foliage toward glaucous blue-grey is as important as the thread rewrite.

6. 'BOXED INTO A MECHANICAL RECTANGLE' — right in spirit, slightly overstated in letter. The pinna rows do vary in length and the top ~quarter tapers into a rough triangle, so the outline is not literally a rectangle. But the left margin is a near-perfect vertical line, the rachises are perfectly horizontal, evenly stacked at a fixed pitch, and the herringbone alternation is rigidly periodic — the mechanical read is real, it comes from the regular pitch and the ruler-straight rachises rather than from a rectangular bounding box.

BAND: FAIL stands. The single defining must-read (thread-fine feathery cloud) is absent, the second (flat-topped umbel with readable rays) reads as neither flat nor rayed at size, the third (blue-tinged smooth hollow stem) fails on colour, and the harvest bulb does not exist. The asset reads as a fern frond or rowan sprig with a yellow finial, not as fennel.

FAIL upheld. I decoded the PNG and zoomed the base (crop 160,250 120x90 @8x), the mid-leaf zone (90,170 130x90 @7x) and the crown (180,70 90x90 @8x), and also opened Garlic.png for the chassis comparison. What is actually on screen: a tuft of ~18 long strap blades radiating from one point at the soil line, plus one straight vertical scape carrying a small white cap, over a flat black soil ellipse.

MUST-READ 1 (hollow round tube leaves, not flat) - ABSENT. The judge is right and the description is accurate. At 7x the blades are unmistakably FLAT swords: widest just above the base, tapering along their whole length to whip-thin arching points, each carrying a single pale longitudinal streak down the centre that reads as a midrib/keel. A hollow allium tube would be near-constant in diameter, blunt-tipped, and shaded as a cylinder (dark rim, soft central specular running the length). Nothing here is cylindrical. Worse in family context: Garlic.png in the same batch is drawn with the IDENTICAL blade, and Garlic's own must-read is literally 'flat folded leaves, unlike onion tubes' - so the single contrast the packet demands between these two species does not exist in the art at all.

MUST-READ 2 (swollen papery bulb with a fringe of wiry roots) - ABSENT, and this is the named harvest organ. One correction to the judge's wording: the fan does not taper 'to a point'. It converges into a narrow wedge that is cut off FLAT at roughly 12px wide where it meets the shadow ellipse. The distinction matters for the fix - the base is not merely un-swollen, it is the NARROWEST point of the entire plant, an inverted taper. There is no bulb ellipse, no papery skin, no horizontal onion-skin banding, no neck/shoulder transition, and not a single root hair below the soil line. The soil ellipse is a plain flat drop shadow with nothing entering or emerging from it.

MUST-READ 3 (leaves splaying in one flat fan plane) - PARTIALLY PRESENT. This is the one point where the judge understated the asset. The leaves genuinely do splay left-right in a broad fan and the outermost pairs arch over almost horizontally, so the fan-plane read is there. It is the only must-read that lands, and it is not enough to carry identity on its own.

CROWN - the judge's 'same recoloured crescent lid' is confirmed by direct comparison, and is in fact stronger than stated: it is not recoloured, it is the same white crescent in the same colour as Garlic's, just scaled larger. At 8x it is a white arc-shaped lid (thick at the top, hollow underneath) sitting on a dark grey-green triangular wedge, on a bare green stalk. It is a mushroom-cap/parasol form. An allium umbel must be a SPHERE - a dense globe of dozens of tiny six-pointed florets with a papery spathe remnant below it. There is no sphere, no floret texture, no radial structure.

Net: two of three must-reads are absent, and the missing pair are the two that define the organism - the harvest organ (bulb + roots) does not exist in the picture, and the leaf cross-section is the wrong one. The silhouette reads as an ornamental grass tuft (liriope/agave-like) with a single mushroom on a stick; nothing in it says allium. This asset also shares one chassis with Garlic (same blade form, same fan, same scape, same crescent cap, same bulb-less flat-cut base, same soil ellipse), differing only in overall scale - so the fix must differentiate them, not just add a bulb to one.

FIX TARGETS: (1) draw the swollen bulb - a squat papery ellipse wider than the leaf fan's base, sitting ON the soil surface with visible curved skin bands and a distinct narrow neck where the leaves emerge; (2) a fringe of fine wiry roots spreading below it into/through the soil ellipse; (3) rebuild the leaves as hollow round tubes - constant diameter, blunt tips, cylinder shading with a soft specular ridge rather than a hard midrib line; (4) replace the crescent cap with a spherical umbel of small pale florets on the scape.

UPHELD, but two of the four stated causes are factually wrong and must not be fixed as written.

WHAT I DID: read Alpaca.png and Llama.png at full size, then decoded both PNGs and rendered (a) an 11x crop of the crown/ear, (b) a 6x crop of the head, (c) 3x of the whole body, 5x of the neck/shoulder, 6x of the rump and 6x of the feet, and (d) a two-colour SILHOUETTE OVERLAY of Alpaca vs Llama aligned on the bbox top-right (nose) corner.

CONFIRMED — ONE CHASSIS. The overlay is decisive. Alpaca bbox 208x238, Llama 212x258. Across the entire head, muzzle, skull dome, ear, eye socket, neck arc, withers, topline, barrel, belly line, shoulder disc and hip flap the two silhouettes coincide pixel-for-pixel (grey in the overlay). The ONLY divergences are (1) the Alpaca's hair spikes along the neck edges, topline, belly and rump, and (2) the Llama standing ~20px taller on slightly longer legs. Head, eye (same oversized brown iris with the same white catchlight in the same place), same grey mouth line, same hooked nostril, same grey inner-ear fill, same grey ear-base patch, same little grey pad feet. The packet's own Llama note demands the Llama be 'larger, longer-faced and less woolly than an alpaca' — one head cannot satisfy both, and this head is the llama's.

MUST-READ 1, 'dense woolly fleece covering the whole body' — FAILS, but NOT for the reason given. The judge's sentence 'the fleece is a straw-streaked patch on the mid-torso ending in a hard straight cutout seam while neck, legs and rump stay smooth and bare' is wrong in three of its four parts:
  - The NECK IS NOT BARE. It carries vertical wool streaks for its whole length plus a dense spike fringe on BOTH edges (throat side and back-of-neck side), running from the jaw down to the withers. It is the second most fleece-treated region in the drawing.
  - The RUMP IS NOT BARE. Streaks plus a continuous spike fringe wrap the entire rear edge from the topline round to the belly.
  - There is NO hard straight cutout seam on the mid-torso. What actually interrupts the fleece are two inherited-chassis artefacts: a pale flat ROUND SHOULDER DISC (~35px across, a lighter circle laid over the shoulder joint) and an angled HIP-FLAP plate at the rear quarter, both of which the streaks stop dead against. Both are present on the Llama too.
  - The one part that IS right: the LEGS are genuinely bare — clean smooth cylinders from elbow/stifle to foot with zero wool, texture or fringe.
The real defect is that the fleece is surface TEXTURE, not VOLUME. The silhouette is the llama's smooth outline with hair spikes appliqued onto its edge; the body never swells into the rounded fleece mass an alpaca reads as, and the wool stops hard at the top of every leg.

MUST-READ 2, 'blunt short face under a topknot fringe' — ABSENT, judge fully correct. The muzzle is a long tapering wedge that drops away below the eye to a hooked nose tip, identical to the Llama's. And the crown is completely bare and smooth: at 11x the entire dome from behind the eye to the ear base is flat unbroken cream with no strand, no clump, no fringe. The nearest hair is BEHIND the skull, on the neck. No topknot exists anywhere on the head.

MUST-READ 3, 'short straight spear-shaped ears' — the judge's claim 'no short spear ear clears the skull outline' is WRONG as stated. An ear IS drawn and it DOES clear the crown: a cream-rimmed leaf/almond ~18px tall x 12px wide rising up-and-back off the skull dome with a grey inner surface, plus a second smaller grey wedge behind it (the far ear seen edge-on). Do not 'add an ear' — one is there. The failure is its SHAPE: it is broad-based, leaf-outlined and tilted back, and it is bit-for-bit the same ear the Llama wears. It is neither the alpaca's short straight spear nor the llama's long banana curve; one generic ear is doing both jobs and matching neither.

BAND: FAIL stands. Two of three must-reads are absent or wrong-shaped, and because head, ear, muzzle, neck, hip flap and feet are shared with Llama, the asset reads as a llama with hair spikes glued to its edge rather than as an alpaca.

FIX DIRECTION: (1) shorten and blunt the muzzle to a short square box under a domed forehead — it must not be the Llama's wedge; (2) put an actual topknot on the crown, a bushy forelock clump between and in front of the ears breaking the skull outline; (3) replace the leaf ear with a short straight narrow spear standing upright, and give the Llama back a long banana ear so the two diverge; (4) push the fleece into the SILHOUETTE — swell the barrel and neck into a rounded woolly mass and carry wool down the legs to the knee instead of ending it at the shoulder disc and hip flap.

rows.verifyWhy:
I read the 440x440 PNG at 1:1, traced the alpha silhouette numerically column by column, cut 4x-8x crops of the dorsal line, neck/chest, head, feet and tail, and rendered a 110px downscale to simulate display size. The FAIL stands: zero of the three mustReads ('two separate humps · shaggy hanging hair on the neck, chest and hump crowns · long curved neck and long legs') survive at display size. But two parts of the stated cause need correcting before anyone fixes it.

MUST-READ 1, two separate humps — DEFECT CONFIRMED, and the judge's geometry is right, so here are the numbers to fix against. The humps ARE drawn, they are just far too shallow. Traced dorsal outline (canvas coords, y down): withers/rear rise from y=195 at x=118 to a first crest y=136 at x=186-190; saddle bottoms out at y=144 at x=208-212; second crest y=136 at x=248-252; then the line falls away to y=147 at x=274 and drops to the neck at x=286. So the inter-hump saddle is 8px deep on a body that is 122px from back (y=136) to belly (y=258) — 6.5% of body depth — and the entire dorsal line from x=150 to x=284 (a 134px span, the whole back) stays inside a 13px band, y=134..147. At 6x the V notch is unmistakable; in the 110px display render the back is one continuous flat-topped loaf with no notch whatsoever. The two lobes also each span ~45px, so they are wide low mounds, not the two tall discrete cones a Bactrian needs. Fix target: raise both crests well above the flanking back line and cut the saddle to at least 25-30% of body depth.

MUST-READ 2, shaggy hanging hair — CONFIRMED ABSENT, exactly as claimed. All the fur in this asset is INTERIOR brushwork (pale straw strokes and dark scribble on the flanks and belly panel); the silhouette itself is smooth everywhere. The dorsal edge is smooth over both hump crowns. The neck edge is monotone smooth from withers (x=286,y=98) to poll (x=312,y=84) — not one broken pixel. The only ragged edge in the entire figure is a single small pointed flap at the chest/shoulder junction near (298,225) and a faintly scalloped skirt along the belly line; neither reads as camel shag at any zoom. There is no neck mane, no chest bib, no hump-crown thatch.

MUST-READ 3, long curved neck and long legs — CONFIRMED ABSENT. The neck is a short straight thick diagonal cone with no S-curve; the head crown (y=84) sits only ~52px above the hump line (y=136), about a quarter of standing height, where a Bactrian carries it far higher on a curved neck. Legs: hoof bottoms at y=336, belly line at y=255-262, so the exposed leg is ~78px against a 200px standing height. CORRECTION to the claim: that is 39%, not 'about a third', and the belly does not hang to the hocks — it sits above mid-cannon. The substance is still right (a camel wants ~55-60% leg), but the body depth is the bigger offender: 61% of standing height is trunk. Overall silhouette bbox is 298w x 254h = aspect 1.17 against the packet's spec aspect 1.4, so the whole animal is currently too stumpy/deep rather than long-legged.

WHERE THE JUDGE IS WRONG: 'it reads as a shaggy straw-coloured sheep' is not what I see, and fixing toward 'not-a-sheep' would waste effort on parts that are already right. The head is properly camelid, not ovine — an 8x crop shows a long tapering muzzle with a drawn drooping lower-lip line, a large ringed prominent eye with a specular highlight, and one small dark rounded ear laid back against the skull (no ram/ewe brow, no downturned Roman nose). The tail is a thick arched tail springing off the rump and ending in a dark fanned brush tassel, clearly visible even in the 110px render — sheep have no such tuft. The feet at 6x are broad splayed dark-brown pads with toe divisions, i.e. camel footpads, not cloven hooves; that detail is good and should be kept. What it actually reads as is an OVERWEIGHT ALPACA/LLAMA — the head, tail and feet say camelid, the deep humpless dome body and stubby legs say wool-bearer, and it is directly confusable with the Alpaca that sits at row 1 of this same batch card. That confusion, plus a defining two-hump must-read that is invisible at display size and a shaggy-coat must-read that is entirely absent from the silhouette, is what makes this a FAIL rather than a POLISH.

rows.readsAs: a camel - a stumpy, overfed one, or at a glance a bison with a long neck

The hump is also not read as a hump so much as the whole torso being one round dome, because the back and the barrel are the same continuous circle with no shoulder or rump line to sit between. rows.readsAs: a llama - the long neck, small head, flat hump-free back and slim legs do carry it

What sits on the head is a flat grey teardrop painted INSIDE the skull outline, so the silhouette is completely earless and the profile reads slightly reptilian. The body has the same hard straight cutout seam at the shoulder and a wedge notch at the rump where the paler wool patch ends against the body, reading as a pasted panel. And because the Alpaca asset is this same drawing, the two species are visually undifferentiated.

rows.readsAs: a sandy Shetland pony / hoofed foal with a bushy tail
rows.defect: Two of three must-reads are absent and the third is contradicted. The frame is not lean or wolfish — it is a deep barrel torso with no flank tuck, four straight posts and dark HOOVES at the ground (visible as split dark caps at 4x). The white feet are missing entirely: the feet are the darkest part of the animal and the only white on the model is a blob on the tail tip. The ears are not erect pointed triangles — they are one dark triangular hood laid flat on top of the skull. The tail is bushy but hooks down and forward, not straight.

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with two of their stated causes corrected. Viewed at 1x, then cropped and nearest-neighbour upscaled 4x/8x/16x/24x on head, ears, feet, tail and underline.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE:

CHASSIS (judge correct). Unmistakable pony/donkey-foal. Deep barrel ribcage, dead-level topline, thick crested (arched) neck, and four long straight column legs with almost no joint articulation — only a faint hock crease on the near hind leg; the two front legs are unbroken posts. The judge said 'no flank tuck': not quite — there IS a shallow scallop in the underline just forward of the hind leg, but it is a horse's shallow belly curve, not a canid's abrupt loin tuck, so the effect they describe is right. The shoulder and hip carry mid-brown patches that read as harness/blanket markings rather than muscle. Coat is pale sand-cream with yellow straw striations; the sandy-ginger of the mustRead is only weakly present (too pale/creamy, ginger missing).

FEET (judge correct, and this is the decisive failure). At 8x and 24x each leg terminates in a squat dark saddle-brown flattened oval disc resting on the ground plane, carrying 2-3 vertical grooves that read as a cloven split. These are hooves, not digitigrade paws — no toes, no pastern, no paw pad shape. They are also the DARKEST value anywhere on the animal, a deep brown against a pale sand leg. The mustRead 'white feet' is therefore not merely absent, it is inverted: the one feature that must be the brightest is instead the darkest. Confirmed the judge's claim that the only white on the whole animal is the tail tip — no socks, no white on any of the four legs.

EARS (judge's CAUSE is WRONG, their verdict on the feature still stands). It is NOT 'one dark triangular hood'. At 16x there are clearly TWO triangular facets on the crown: a darker far-side triangle on the left and a lighter near-side triangle on the right, separated by a vertical ridge line, with a thin spike breaking the head silhouette at the apex. So two ears ARE modelled. The defect is that they are drawn as flat, wide-based, low-set colour wedges lying flush against the skull crown — inset inside the head's outline rather than standing proud of it, with no air gap between them and no ear thickness. Only one narrow spike escapes the contour. At 1x the pair reads as a dark pointed cap or bandit hood. So 'erect pointed triangular ears' does fail, but the fix is to lift the existing ear geometry off the crown into two separate silhouette-breaking cones, not to add ears that aren't there.

TAIL (judge understated it). The bushy brush IS present and is one of the better-drawn parts: a thick club with a fringe of dark radiating hairs. But it is hooked strongly forward and down over the rump in a squirrel/husky curl, not the 'bushy straight tail' the packet requires. The white tip is a hard-edged pure-white circular disc with zero blending into the surrounding fur — it reads as a golf ball glued on rather than a white tail tip.

HEAD (in the asset's favour, unmentioned by the judge). The muzzle is genuinely the most canid element: a long tapered snout with a dark rounded nose button, a slight mouth line, and a forward-set round eye with a pale sclera ring. It is credible as a dog head. That is not enough to rescue the read.

NET: a sandy pony wearing a canid head and a hooded cap, standing on four dark hooves. Two of three mustReads fail outright (white feet absent/inverted; erect pointed ears not readable; and of the third, 'lean wolfish frame' is a barrel pony while 'bushy straight tail' is bushy but curled). FAIL is correct.

Note for the record: partway through this verification the source PNG at apps/game/smoke/species-fullsize/earth-fauna/Dingo.png was deleted out from under me by a concurrent regeneration wave. All observations above were taken from the file as it existed at read time.

rows.readsAs: a cream pony / donkey foal, not a dog of any breed
rows.defect: Identical silhouette to the Dingo with a paler fill — same barrel, same four hoofed posts, same hooded head. The plumed tail carried above the back is absent: the tail is set low and swings DOWN and forward past the hocks. The ears are not erect or folded dog ears, they are the shared dark triangular hood on the skull crown. The only must-read that lands is the dark nose blob at the end of the snout, and that snout is a tapered anteater wedge with no jaw or lip line.
