rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two-fifths of the stated cause is wrong. Looked at the full 440x440 plate, then at 5-7x crops of head (250,100 110x90), hindquarter (90,150 130x160) and feet (140,240 180x70), plus a numeric compare against Dingo.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE.
(1) EARS -- THE JUDGE IS WRONG. This is not 'the shared skull hood'. At 7x the skull carries a genuine erect pointed ear: a tall narrow triangle whose apex rises a clear ~20px ABOVE the crown line, with a darker chocolate inner-ear triangle nested inside it, and a second shorter triangular point behind/right of it reading as the off-side ear. The mustRead 'erect or folded ears' READS and should not be listed as a defect or a fix target.
(2) NOSE -- lands, as they said: a distinct dark near-black oval cap at the muzzle tip with a specular highlight.
So TWO of three mustReads are present, not one. Their 'only the dark nose blob lands' understates the asset.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS.
(3) TAIL -- absent as claimed, but described in the wrong place. It is NOT 'low-set and hooked down past the hocks'. The root is HIGH, right at the croup (y~178, level with the topline). From there it hangs DOWN AND FORWARD across the hindquarter as a flat pale-orange oval paddle with a fringe of stiff dark bristles along its outer/left edge, bottoming out around y~250 -- that is stifle/mid-thigh level, well ABOVE the hock (~y275) and nowhere near past it. It reads as a horse's tail or, worse, a broom head lying against the rump. The plume over the back is genuinely gone; the fix is direction and set, not height of origin.
(4) FEET -- the judge missed the single most damning detail. All four feet terminate in dark rounded HOOF caps bearing a central vertical cleft line. Cloven hooves. No toes, no pads, no claws, no digitigrade break. A canid drawn on hooves is the wrong organism on its own.
(5) LIMBS -- the hind leg is a straight tapering column from body to hoof with no hock angulation and no visible stifle; the forelegs are the same column. That plus the hooves and the brush tail is exactly why it reads donkey/pony foal -- their read of the gestalt is right, they just never named the parts causing it.
(6) MUZZLE -- present but drawn far too long and thin for a dog, with a separate thin stick-like lower-jaw line floating detached beneath it, pushing the head equine/vulpine.

CHASSIS. 'Pixel-for-pixel the Dingo' is an overstatement but functionally true. Body bbox Dog 240x166 vs Dingo 248x172 -- the same drawing at ~3% scale difference, same pose, same topline, same ear wedge, same columnar legs, same hooves, same paddle tail. On a 3px sampling grid only ~384 of ~21600 samples differ in silhouette occupancy (edge-level). The only real distinctions are coat tone (Dog paler cream, Dingo more ginger) and the Dingo's white tail tip, which the Dog lacks. This is the family pony chassis recoloured; the Dog has no species-specific geometry whatsoever.

BAND: FAIL. The identity-carrying mustRead (plumed tail over the back) is absent, the feet are hooves, and the asset is not distinguishable from its family neighbour except by hue. POLISH would be wrong -- this needs a new limb/foot model and a re-drawn tail, not a tweak.

rows.readsAs: a white shaggy pony or a long-nosed goat
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads survive. The coat is a flat bone-white over the whole animal — no grizzled grey saddle on the back and no tawny legs; back, barrel and legs are one value. The tail is low-carried and bushy but has NO dark tip; it is the palest thing on the model. The ears are not large triangles — they are the same small dark hood shape shared with the other three, and it is smaller relative to the skull here than a Pampas fox's ears should be. The body is the shared hoofed barrel chassis with no canid tuck or hock.
rows.fix: Paint a distinct three-zone coat — grizzled grey-and-black saddle over the back, tawny-rufous legs and cheeks, and a black-tipped tail — then enlarge the ears to genuinely oversized side-set triangles.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but three of the four stated causes are wrong and the worst defect was not named at all. WHAT I SAW (440x440, creature bbox x101-338 y140-283, measured aspect 1.66 against the packet's 2.0 -- too short-bodied and too long-legged).

CORRECTION 1 -- THE EARS ARE NOT A 'SMALL SHARED HOOD'. At 14x zoom there are two distinct triangular ears separated by a raised pale spine that terminates in a small apex spike: a near ear rendered as a solid dark grey-brown triangle right of the spine, and a paler far ear left of it. The ear mass runs from an apex at (302,142) down to a base at y~158 spanning x278-334. So the defect is scale and set, not absence: the mass is only ~16px tall on a ~37px-tall head while ~56px wide, i.e. a squat wide pyramid butted flush to the skull with no sky between the ears, so at 1:1 it reads as a helmet plate. The fix is to make each ear a TALL NARROW triangle standing clearly proud of the crown with a gap between them -- not 'add ears'.

CORRECTION 2 -- MUSTREAD 1 IS HALF PASSING. 'Pointed narrow muzzle' is present and clean: a long tapering wedge with a distinct dark round nose and a dark mouth line, plus an amber eye. The blanket 'all three must-reads fail' overstates.

CORRECTION 3 -- THE TAIL IS NOT 'THE PALEST ELEMENT'. Carried-low and bushy both READ: a broad fan hanging off the rump below the backline with a fringe of dark hair bristles along its whole outer arc. Measured: back L=173, rump L=167, tail proximal L=153, tail distal lobe L=135, bristle fringe L=86. The back and rump are PALER than the tail, and after the feet the tail carries the densest dark on the animal. The judge's verdict half is still right -- there is NO DARK TIP. The dark is a rim fringe distributed evenly along the entire outer arc from base to end, and the extreme distal lobe (x112-124, y214-232) is a pale rounded blob at L=135 with highlights to 178. So the dark reads as fur texture, not as a terminal marking. Fix = a discrete dark band on the distal third, and stop putting dark bristles at the base.

CORRECTION 4 -- THE COAT IS NOT 'FLAT'. It is not flat in VALUE: there is a broad top-lit ramp, back L=173 -> flank 162 -> belly 150 -> legs 126-146 -> feet 82-91. It is flat in HUE: every region sampled (back, flank, belly, foreleg, hindleg, tail, head, ears) sits at hue ~38 deg and saturation 14-22%, one warm bone/greige. So the judge is right in substance -- no grizzled grey back (the back is warm bone and is the LIGHTEST area on the animal, the exact inverse of a grey saddle) and no tawny legs (the legs are the identical hue, merely shaded darker; the darkening is lighting, not marking). Fix must be a HUE split (cool grey saddle vs ochre/tawny limbs), not a value split, because a value split is already there and does nothing.

THE DEFECT THE JUDGE MISSED, AND THE REAL REASON IT READS AS A PONY/GOAT: the chassis is an ungulate. At 16x the feet are dark, wide, flattened DISCS at the base of columnar legs, marked with faint vertical cleft lines -- hooves, not paws with separated toes -- and they are darker than the leg above them, which is exactly the hoof-vs-cannon-bone read. Above them the legs are straight columns with a pronounced hock and a distinct pastern joint. The body is a deep barrel chest under a level back with a wither hump, and there is a shaggy mane-like ruff over the neck and shoulder. Colour changes alone will not rescue this: the silhouette is the shared quadruped/pony chassis and the feet must become canid paws with visible toes and a digitigrade stance before any coat work matters.

rows.readsAs: an orange pony / a fox-coloured hoofed foal
rows.defect: The colour says fox and the body says horse. The black stockings are entirely absent — the legs are the same orange as the barrel right down to a small dark hoof cap, and at 4x those caps are split hoof shapes rather than paws. The pointed ears are absent, replaced by the family's dark triangular skull hood. The white-tipped brush is present but it is a modest low-hooked tail, not the enormous brush that is the species' single loudest read; it is no bigger than the Dingo's. The deep barrel torso with no flank tuck and the level thick neck make this read as the same pony as the other three.
rows.fix: Double the tail's mass into a true brush that sweeps horizontally back at hock height with a bold white tip, and paint solid black from the elbow and hock down to real black paws.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but three of the four stated causes need correcting before anyone fixes against them.

WHAT I SAW (440x440 render; ink bbox x89-350, y145-278, so 262px long x 134px tall; head/nose at right, tail low-left; inspected at 6x-14x crops of head, ear crown, hind+fore legs, one foot, and tail).

CHASSIS - the real failure. Rendered beside Pampas_Fox.png (the only other file in this packet that exists on disk) the two are the SAME DRAWING in different colours: identical barrel torso with a dead-straight topline and deep brisket, identical short thick neck carrying the head high and level, identical four column limbs at identical stances, identical wide flat foot plates, identical head block with the ear panels inset, identical tail root position and 45-degree down-back tail angle. This is the one-pony-chassis defect, and it is what makes the asset read as a foal/pony in fox paint rather than as a fox. The judge's headline 'colour says fox, body says horse' is correct and is the load-bearing finding.

MUST-READ 1 - 'enormous bushy white-tipped brush tail': PARTLY present, and the judge under-credited it. There IS a real brush: a fringed, spiky-edged plume with individual hair strokes breaking the outline, and at its end an unmistakable bright cream-white round tip blob. The white tip genuinely registers. What fails is scale: the tail occupies only x89-140, about 51px of a 262px silhouette (~24% of body length) and is thinner than the torso. A red fox brush should be roughly as long as the head-body and as thick as the chest. So the fix is 'grow the brush 2-2.5x and thicken it', NOT 'add a white tip'. CORRECTION: the judge's yardstick 'no larger than the Dingo's' cannot be checked and should not be actioned - Dingo.png and Dog.png (packet rows 1 and 2) DO NOT EXIST in species-fullsize/earth-fauna. Only Pampas_Fox.png and Red_Fox.png are on disk. The verifiable comparison is the Pampas Fox, whose tail is the same size, same fringe treatment and same attachment point.

MUST-READ 2 - 'black stockings on the legs': ABSENT. Confirmed, and this is the cleanest miss. CORRECTION to the description: the legs are not 'barrel-orange'. They are a pale peach/cream-orange that is visibly LIGHTER than the torso, with a single mid-brown shading strip down the caudal edge of each upper leg - the opposite value direction from the black stocking the species needs. Nothing anywhere on the limb approaches black; the darkest limb pixel is a rust brown.

FEET - CORRECTION: the caps are not 'small'. Each foot is a wide, flat, rounded rust-brown plate that is WIDER than the pastern above it, carrying three dark vertical slits. It reads as a splayed hoof/ungulate pad plate, not as a cloven hoof and certainly not as a fox's small dark paw. Fix target: narrow it below the leg width, darken it to near-black, and give it a compact digitigrade toe cluster.

MUST-READ 3 - 'sharp pointed ears and narrow muzzle': SPLIT. The muzzle PASSES and the judge did not mention it - it is a long, narrow, cleanly tapering wedge ending in a dark brown/black nose button, with the mouth line drawn under it. That is a correct canid/fox muzzle and should not be touched. The ears FAIL, but not by the mechanism claimed. CORRECTION: they were not 'replaced by a dark skull hood'. At 12x there are two discrete dark-brown triangular EAR PANELS on the crown, a left one and a right one, meeting at a shared apex over the forehead - the geometry is there. They fail because they are painted flat INSIDE the head silhouette: only about 4px of a thin spike breaks the head contour at the apex, so at normal size the pair reads as a dark blaze/hood marking on the forehead. The fix is to lift the same two triangles clear of the skull outline as erect standing ears with visible outer edge and inner pinna, not to invent ears from scratch.

NET: two of three must-reads do not register (stockings absent; ears do not break silhouette; brush present but a quarter of the size it needs), and the body is a shared pony chassis with the Pampas Fox. FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: a generic gold aquarium fish — a stranger would say 'goldfish' or 'bream', not 'carp'
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are simply not on the canvas. There are NO barbels — the snout is a bare point with no mouth line at all, let alone two pairs of whiskers at the mouth corners, and barbels are the single feature that makes a carp a carp. The long single dorsal fin running most of the back is also absent: the back carries one tiny rounded nub the same size as the ventral nub, covering maybe 12% of the topline. The body is a symmetric lens, not deep and heavy-shouldered — the dorsal and ventral curves mirror each other, so there is no shoulder mass ahead of the dorsal. Side by side with Goldfish.png it is the identical silhouette in a different colour.
rows.fix: Draw four barbels — a short pair at the upper lip and a longer, thicker pair trailing back from the mouth corners past the gill cover — and replace the dorsal nub with a long low dorsal that starts at the shoulder and runs two-thirds of the back to the peduncle; raise the front third of the topline so the shoulder sits above the belly line.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and the fix brief needs the corrected geometry. I read the PNG at 1x, then re-cropped and upscaled the head (12x), the dorsal (6x) and the whole body (3x) with a 3.2x brightness boost, and additionally ran a per-row background-differenced silhouette trace on Carp, Goldfish and Minnow to get numbers.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Subject bbox x107-333, y132-281. Caudal fin x107-143; body proper x143-333 = 191 px long, max depth 108 px (aspect 1.77). Dense concentric arc-row scale texture over the whole flank (genuinely carp-ish, keep it). A full-length pale lateral line runs x=157 to x=320 at y=209. Eye at x~310,y~202: white sclera ring with a dark angular pupil. A pectoral fin IS drawn -- a darker translucent triangle at roughly x240-270, y207-232; the judge did not mention it and it is fine. Caudal is a big splayed triangular wedge, 137 px tall at its outer edge (wider than the body is deep), tapering to a 22 px peduncle.

CAUSE 1 -- BARBELS. CONFIRMED, and this is the killing defect. I scanned every pixel in x330-400, y180-235 (the whole cone ahead of and below the snout) against the per-row background. Every deviation there is <=10, identical to the deviation measured at y=180 where no fish exists at all -- i.e. it is the background vignette gradient, not ink. There is no barbel, no whisker, no stub, at any threshold. Nor is there a mouth: the snout tip (x=333) is a bare geometric point. The only stroke near it is the LATERAL LINE, which passes under the eye and stops at x=320, 13 px short of the tip -- the judge missed that this stroke exists, and at thumbnail size it is the thing a viewer would misread as a mouth. Fix: give it an actual downturned sucker mouth at the snout underside, then TWO pairs of barbels off the mouth corners -- a short pair on the upper lip and a longer pair trailing back past the gill, thick enough to survive downscale.

CAUSE 2 -- DORSAL FIN. The judge's DESCRIPTION IS WRONG, the verdict on it is right. It is not a nub and it is not the same size as the ventral. The dorsal is a low rounded lobe spanning x=206 to x=265 (~60 px), with 5-6 fine ray strokes rising above it to y=136. The ventral/anal lobe spans only x~198 to x~232 (~34 px). The dorsal is ~1.8x the ventral's chord. The REAL defect is proportion, not existence: 60/190 = ~32 percent of the back where the reference says 'most of the back', and it projects only 13 px above the topline = 12 percent of body depth, so it reads as a bump rather than a fin. Fix: extend the dorsal base to ~60-70 percent of the back, origin just behind the shoulder, and raise it -- and note a real carp dorsal is long and slightly concave along its top edge, which is the silhouette cue this needs.

CAUSE 3 -- BODY / SHARED CHASSIS. Substantively confirmed, but 'identical silhouette to Goldfish in a different colour' overstates it and would send the fix to the wrong place. Measured: Carp body 191x108 (aspect 1.77), Goldfish body 173x109 (aspect 1.59) -- the Carp is ~10 percent longer. The caudals genuinely differ (Carp = splayed triangular wedge widest at the outer edge; Goldfish = a rounded fan lobe, max 93 px). Colour differs (Carp gold-yellow, Goldfish orange). What IS shared, and shared to within one or two pixels, is everything in between: the dorsal lobe top-edge samples run Carp 224:145, 227:144, 233:143, 239:143, 245:144, 251:146, 257:149, 263:153 against Goldfish 225:146, 228:145, 234:144, 240:144, 246:146, 252:148, 258:152, 264:157 -- that is the same fin translated ~1 px. The head taper, ventral nub, pectoral triangle, eye and lateral line are likewise common. So it is one chassis with two tails, not one chassis in two colours. Independently of Goldfish, the body also fails its own must-read: it is a SYMMETRIC pointed lens with maximum depth at x~222, which is 58 percent of the body length back from the snout, and it tapers to a sharp point at BOTH ends. 'Deep' is satisfied (depth/length 0.57); 'heavy-shouldered' is not -- a carp's greatest depth sits ~35-40 percent back, at the dorsal origin, above a blunt fleshy rounded snout. Fix: push the depth maximum forward to the dorsal origin, blunt and round the snout end (a carp head is not a point), and let the taper run long and shallow into the peduncle so the mass sits forward.

VERDICT: the one uniquely diagnostic must-read (barbels) is wholly absent, a second (heavy-shouldered) is absent, a third (long dorsal) is present at a third of the required extent, and the animal shares a chassis with its sibling. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: an orange fish — 'goldfish' is a reasonable guess, but only because of the colour

rows.readsAs: a small slim silvery baitfish — the right ballpark, though it could equally be a sardine or a smelt

rows.readsAs: A striped pony, okapi, or thylacine — a small hooved ungulate. No stranger names this a cat.
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. (1) Triangular upright ears on a round short-muzzled head: there are no triangular ears at all — a single large flat GREY DISC sits on the side of the skull like a ram's horn boss or a pasted-on mouse ear, and the head is a long tapering snout that droops downward at the tip, the opposite of a round short muzzle. rows.fix: Rebuild the head and forequarters on a felid skull instead of repainting the pony: shorten the muzzle to about one third of its current length so it is a rounded dome with a short blunt nose, replace the grey side-disc with two TRIANGULAR ears standing upright off the top of the skull, move the eye back onto the cheek plane and give it a hard vertical slit pupil, and add radiating whisker strokes; then swap the hoof blocks for toed paws and lengthen the tail to at least body length with a smooth taper in body colour.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at full size and at 7x-20x crops of head, ear, muzzle, tail, flank and both feet (subject bbox 117,154 -> 321,267; 205x114 px in a 440px canvas). VERDICT UPHELD, but two of the judge's three stated causes are wrong and must not be fixed as written.

MUST-READ 1 - 'triangular upright ears on a round short-muzzled head' - GENUINELY ABSENT, and this alone carries the FAIL. Zoomed on the crown (crop 262,140 55x40 @16x) the top of the skull is a single smooth circular arc with NOTHING breaking the silhouette. There are no triangular points, not even small ones. What is there is a large pale-grey ball (the cranium) with one darker brown-grey filled oval inside it - a rounded, wholly non-triangular ear pinna painted flat on the side of the head, never crossing the outline. CORRECTION to the judge: they called it 'one flat grey disc stuck on the side of the skull like a ram's horn boss'. It is not stuck on the side - the grey disc IS the braincase, and the darker oval inside it is the ear. Fixing this means adding two upright triangular pinnae that break the topline, not moving a disc.

Head shape: the judge is right. From the cranium ball the muzzle runs forward AND downward as a long tapered wedge whose tip drops well below the level of the eye, with a dark nose blob at the tip and a dark mouth line along its underside. Profile reads tapir/okapi calf, not cat. The eye sits at the base of that wedge rather than on a flat face plane, which makes the snout look even longer.

MUST-READ 2 - 'long expressive tail' - THE JUDGE IS FLATLY WRONG. There is no 'short blunt grey club'. The tail is a long, smooth, continuously curving tube that leaves the rump around (157,190), arcs up and back to about x=119, then hooks down to about y=234 - roughly 60-65 px of arc length against a 205 px body, clearly readable as a tail at 1:1. Its real defects are different and milder: it is a constant-width untapered tube with a blunt rounded tip, it is a flat blue-grey that does not match the body's warm off-white and carries none of the body striping, and its pose is a limp downward hook rather than an expressive carriage. This is POLISH-grade, not a missing feature. Do not 'add a tail' - retaper it, recolour it to the pelt, and lift the carriage.

MUST-READ 3 - split. The vertical slit pupil IS PRESENT AND IS THE BEST-DRAWN THING ON THE ASSET; the judge's 'yellow blob with a broad smeared pupil ... no vertical slit' is wrong. At 14x-16x the eye is a clean yellow-gold almond with a distinct narrow black vertical lens pupil and a white catchlight to its upper-left. Keep it. WHISKERS, however, are genuinely absent - zero radiating strokes anywhere on the muzzle or cheek.

Compounding defects, corrected: FEET - the judge is substantially right. Each leg ends in a near-black, splayed, lens-shaped slab noticeably WIDER than the leg above it, sitting flat like a clog or cloven hoof. Slight correction: there are two faint vertical toe grooves incised in each, so it is a hoof-shaped block with vestigial toe lines, not a bare hoof - but it does not read as a paw and there are no visible pads or claws. STRIPES - right in substance: a solid dark-brown dorsal saddle band runs unbroken along the entire spine from shoulder to rump, with dense vertical bars hanging off its lower edge across the whole ribcage, plus 3-4 bars crossing the muzzle. Reads zebra/tiger fringe, not mackerel tabby. STRAY MARK - the shin fragment is real but the judge overstates it: it is a ~3x2 px brown speck at roughly (171,244) on the near hind leg, essentially invisible at 1:1. They MISSED a larger and more damaging stray: a dark chevron/bird-shaped blob about 12 px wide floating on the cheek/jaw at roughly (288,181), directly below the eye, which at full size reads as a smudge on the face.

Also not mentioned by the judge and relevant to the fix: the whole chassis is wrong for a felid. Straight level topline, deep barrel ribcage, straight columnar unangulated legs front and rear with almost no hock or elbow bend, and a wide standing stance. Nothing about the body carries feline crouch, flexible spine or digitigrade limb. At 1:1 the organism reads as a striped hoofed ungulate calf, so the failure is identity-level, not a checklist miss.

rows.readsAs: a fleecy tan goat or young sheep with lyre horns

rows.readsAs: a brown ox with white socks
rows.defect: White lower legs are present and correct, but the white rump patch is absent — the rump is plain brown and is further hidden by the oversized brush tail arcing across it. There is no white band above the muzzle; the face is uniform dark brown. The horns are two small pale crescents perched on a dark cap with no bald forehead plate joining them.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy capybara or a hairy tapir — nothing on it says bison
rows.defect: It has NO HORNS AT ALL. There is no shoulder hump: the topline is the family's plain convex arc and the hindquarters are as deep as the chest, so the silhouette is rear-heavy rather than front-heavy. The head is small, carried HIGH on a level neck, and clean-shaven — no beard, no low-slung massive skull, no forehead mop. The specified small eye is instead the family's large white-ringed cartoon eye.

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and one is understated; fix against THIS description, not theirs. I read the 440x440 PNG whole, then re-cropped and upscaled the skull (8x), the throat/chin (8x), the topline (6x), the tail (6x) and the feet (4x), and measured the silhouette column-by-column. Animal faces RIGHT.

CONFIRMED — NO HORNS. At 8x the crown of the skull is a smooth unbroken dome from the brow to the poll. There is no horn, no nub, no boss, no keratin curve anywhere. The only feature on the upper skull is a small dark soft-edged almond OVAL lying flat against the side of the cranium, tilted up-and-back — that is an ear, not a horn stub; do not mistake it for one when fixing. Every bison carries horns in both sexes; a hornless bovid cannot read as Bison.

CONFIRMED — NO BEARD, but the reason is finer than stated. The throat is not bare: along the jaw/throat leading edge there are roughly eight to ten thin dark hair wisps, each about 6-10px long. They are the SAME generic edge-fur strokes that appear along the topline, the belly and the flank — a rim-fur pass, not a beard. There is no hanging chin mass, no throat curtain, no dark bib. Below the jaw the brisket is a large SMOOTH flat dark-brown wedge with no hair strokes on it at all. So the fix is not 'add hair to a bare chin' — it is 'replace the rim-wisp pass under the jaw with an actual bearded mass'.

CONFIRMED — HEAD CARRIED HIGH, and I can quantify it. Crown of the head sits at y=95. The highest point of the body topline is y=149 (at the withers, x=248). The head is therefore 54px ABOVE the shoulder line, on a short thick level neck. That is the exact inversion of the bison silhouette, in which the head hangs BELOW the hump line. This is the single most damaging defect and it survives independently of the hump.

CONFIRMED — HEAD IS NOT MASSIVE AND IS THE WRONG SHAPE. headFrac 0.27 is roughly met by area, but the mass is in the wrong place: it is a rounded cranium drawn out into a LONG TAPERING WEDGE SNOUT ending in a slightly bulbous down-turned nose pad with a small hooked nostril and a thin straight mouth line. Bison needs a broad, blunt, boxy skull that is nearly as wide as it is long. The eye is also wrong for the row: it is a large rimmed eyeball with a pale sclera ring and a specular highlight — that reads prominent, and the reference row asks for eyes: small.

CORRECTION 1 — THE HUMP IS NOT SIMPLY 'ABSENT' AND THE TOPLINE IS NOT THE FAMILY'S PLAIN ARC. There IS a modest front-heavy topline here. Measured tops: rump x=136 y=180, mid-back x=176-200 y=170-173, withers x=248 y=149. So the back does rise ~31px front-to-rear, and at 6x there is a visible small rounded withers bump with a shallow SADDLE DIP in front of the mid-back arc, plus a short row of standing bristle hairs (a nascent mane) along that dip. The defect is magnitude and placement, not total absence: a ~20-30px rise on a ~227px-tall figure is a bump, not the 'huge muscular' hump the row demands, and it is nullified because the head then rises 54px above it — the eye reads the head as the highest point, so the whole silhouette parses as level-backed. Fix by growing the withers mass so its crest is the tallest thing in the frame and dropping the head under it.

CORRECTION 2 — 'THE HINDQUARTERS ARE AS DEEP AS THE CHEST' IS FALSE. The chest/brisket column is measurably deeper: at x=250 the body runs y=149-278 (~129px); the mid/rear barrel at x=190 runs y=172-265 (~93px). The front is ~35% deeper than the rear and the rump top is 31px lower than the withers. Partial credit is genuinely due on 'narrow tapering hindquarters' — a taper exists — it is just far too gentle, and the haunch is still drawn as a full rounded thigh mass.

OTHER DEFECTS NOT IN THE ORIGINAL CLAIM:
- COAT DISTRIBUTION IS INVERTED. The shaggy hair strokes and the dangling belly fringe cover the mid and REAR barrel, while the forequarters (neck, shoulder patch, brisket) are large SMOOTH flat dark-brown panels with no hair strokes. Bison is the reverse: a long shaggy chocolate cape over head, hump and forelegs, short hair behind. Move the shag forward.
- LEGS ARE TOO LONG AND TOO PALE. They are slim cream/bone-coloured columns; ground is ~y=325 and the belly bottom ~y=264, leaving ~61px of daylight under a 93px-deep barrel. Bison is low-slung on short dark stumpy legs. Feet themselves are FINE and should be kept — at 4x each foot is a correct small dark two-toed cloven hoof.
- TAIL IS WRONG. It is a long, thick, uniform-width smooth tube arcing stiffly out and down from y~195 to y~325 (nearly to the hooves), ending in a straight-cut fan of straw strands. Bison's tail is short with a small terminal tuft. This is a family-chassis donkey/lion tail.

CORRECTION 3 — WHAT IT ACTUALLY READS AS. 'Capybara' is ruled out by the correct cloven hooves and the long tufted tail, and it is not a tapir either — there is no proboscis, the snout is a plain tapered wedge. The high-carried small head on a short neck, the long tapering muzzle, the shaggy pale barrel, the long slim legs and the fan-tufted tail read closest to a shaggy LLAMA/ALPACA, or a generic long-nosed sheep. Naming it correctly matters because the fix direction differs: it does not need de-rodenting, it needs the head dropped, broadened and bearded, the withers massed up, and the shag moved onto the forequarters.

SCORE: zero of the three must-reads read. No hump, no low-slung massive bearded head, and only a token hindquarter taper — plus no horns at all. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a pale cream goat or a generic antelope

But there is no tall muscular ridge along the shoulders — the topline behind the neck actually DIPS before the barrel rises, the opposite of the gaur's dorsal ridge. rows.readsAs: a pale cream goat — and it is visibly the same picture as Antelope and Impala

The horns are smooth, not ringed. The legs are thick fleecy tubes, not fine and delicate, and the neck is the family's short thick one rather than long. The specified prominent eye is the same size as every other asset's.

rows.readsAs: a generic tan antelope, the same one as Antelope and Impala
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. The face is the family's short rounded wedge with a stubby muzzle — nothing about it is extremely long or narrow, despite the 0.32 headFrac. The back does not slope to the hindquarters: it is the same smooth convex arc, and the rump is actually the HIGHEST point of the body rather than the lowest. The horns are the standard lyre pair set flat on the skull with no bony pedestal and no bracket shape.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 1x and at 4x/6x/8x crops of the head, horn bases, topline and hindquarters, plus a per-column silhouette profile (luminance>70 against the navy plate) and the same profile run on Antelope and Impala for comparison. Verdict FAIL stands, but the stated causes are only one-third correct and one of them is FLATLY INVERTED — fix against this description, not theirs.

MUST-READ 2 (back sloping steeply down to the hindquarters) IS PRESENT, and the claim that 'the rump is the highest point, the opposite of the reference' is WRONG. The animal faces right. Measured top-of-silhouette by column: over the front legs / withers (x=250-270) the topline sits at y=142-156; over the hind legs / rump (x=158-190) it sits at y=186-196. The topline climbs monotonically front-ward from x=202 (y=186) to x=266 (y=142) with no rump hump anywhere. That is ~38-40px of drop across a ~110px torso, roughly 20 degrees of downward slope from withers to rump — the correct hartebeest direction. Do NOT 'fix' this; touching it will destroy the one identity cue the asset has. The comparison species confirm it is a real differentiator: Antelope's torso topline is 176 at 20% of torso length and 178 at 80% (dead level), Impala the same. So 'reads as the same generic tan antelope as Antelope and Impala' is also wrong — this asset has a visibly heavier, taller forequarter, a sloping back, a thicker neck and a fringed tail those two do not have; it is distinguishable from them at thumbnail size. The only fair complaint about the slope is that it could be steeper (~20 deg vs the ~28-30 deg of a real kongoni), which is POLISH, not FAIL.

MUST-READ 1 (extremely long narrow elongated face) IS GENUINELY ABSENT — this is the real reason it fails. The head is a rounded, deep cranial blob with a short blunt tapering muzzle ending in a rounded pinkish-tan nose pad and a drawn mouth line. Measured: eye center ~x=302,y=119; nose tip x=347, so eye-to-nose is only ~45px, while head depth at the eye (skull top y=105 to jaw/cheek bottom ~y=160) is ~55px. The muzzle is SHORTER than the head is deep; a hartebeest needs roughly 2x the opposite. Head length nose-to-poll (~62px) over body length nose-to-rump (~229px) is 0.27, i.e. the declared headFrac 0.32 is not even being spent, and what is spent goes into cranial bulk rather than length. Relative to the family this head is no longer than Antelope's (0.29) — it reads as a cow/bull head, not a hartebeest face. The judge's phrase 'short rounded wedge' is accurate.

MUST-READ 3 (bracket horns on a bony pedestal) IS ABSENT, but the description needs correcting. The horns are not a flat lyre: each is a pale cream tube that leaves the skull at EYE LEVEL (bases at y~120, x~291 and x~312, i.e. BELOW the top of the skull at y~105 — anatomically the horns are pinned to the sides of the face, not the crown), rises, and carries a shallow S-kink in its upper third with the tip turning up-and-outward; the two peak at y=72 about 40px apart. So there is a faint kink, but no common pedicel and no bracket/Z profile: the pair splays into a wide U from two widely separated eye-level roots. What might be mistaken for a pedestal is NOT one — the dark-brown mass at the horn bases resolves at 8x into two EARS: a brown crescent ear laid back on the left/rear of the skull and a small brown triangular ear tucked between the horn bases. The fix is a single raised bony pedicel on the crown with both horns leaving it together, then out, then sharply back.

Other details actually seen (none of which change the band): the tail is a thick tan arc springing from the rump ending in a dark brown fringed tuft (right idea, should be black and thinner); hooves are dark and cloven with a visible pastern; the hind leg is a straight column with essentially no hock angulation (the shared quadruped chassis showing through); there is a pale grey-white arc over the shoulder and a flat mid-brown quad on the upper foreleg that read as unresolved patch shapes rather than the hartebeest's dark thigh/shoulder blazes.

Summary of the fix list, in priority order: (1) elongate the face — pull the muzzle to ~2x head depth and narrow the cranium; (2) rebuild the horn root as one tall pedicel on the crown and re-profile the horns to the bracket; (3) leave the sloping topline alone (optionally steepen slightly); (4) blacken and thin the tail tuft.

rows.readsAs: a tan fleecy goat — the third copy of the Antelope drawing in this batch
rows.defect: No vertical black stripes on the rump; the hindquarters are plain tan and there is no white rump for them to sit on. No black tuft above the hind hoof. The legs are thick woolly tubes rather than extremely fine, and the horns are smooth putty crescents with no rings and no out-then-up lyre sweep.
rows.fix: Add the white rump with two black vertical bars flanking the tail and a black tuft at each hind fetlock, and slim the legs to half their current width.

rows.readsAs: a broken decal — a striped animal with a black slab stuck on its side
rows.defect: The flank markings have collapsed into a solid dark rectangular bar spanning nearly the whole barrel with comb-like tines hanging off its lower edge; it reads as a rendering artifact pasted over the body, not as stripes, and its hard rectangular top and bottom edges cut straight across the topline shading. The stripes are also inverted — thick BLACK bars where the reference calls for 6-10 thin WHITE ones. Heavy dark bands also wrap the neck and face, making the head read as masked. The ears are small nubs, nowhere near enormous rounded satellite dishes.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but two of the three stated causes are factually wrong and the real defect is different in kind. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (inspected at 1x, then 3x/6x/10x/12x crops of head, flank, topline, feet, tail, muzzle).

CORRECTION 1 - NOT a 'solid dark rectangular slab'. At 6x the flank carries ~14 DISCRETE dark-brown stripes, each a tapered wedge that radiates down and slightly forward from the topline, with clearly visible pale cream gaps between them. They are individually legible as stripes. What makes them collapse into a slab at 1x is a separate object: a single SOLID HORIZONTAL RULED BAR, ~4-5px thick and ~110px long (src coords roughly x=155..268 at y=232 in the 440x440 canvas), with blunt SQUARE ends that both float in open flank - the left end stops mid-barrel, the right end stops mid-ribcage. Every vertical stripe terminates on this bar, so the assembly literally draws a comb: a straight machined spine with tines hanging off it. THE BAR IS THE ARTIFACT, not the stripes. Removing the bar and thinning the tine count would fix most of the 1x read.

CORRECTION 2 - the stripes do NOT cut across the topline. At 9x the topline is clean: the stripes are correctly clipped to the body silhouette, and there is even a pale rim highlight running along the back that they respect. No marking anywhere overruns the outline - I also checked the muzzle bar at 12x and it stops at the jaw/nose, it does not overshoot into empty space. The 'hard straight edges' the judge saw are the interior ruled bars, not silhouette breaks.

CORRECTION 3 - the ears are NOT small nubs. Behind and left of the horn bases there is a substantial ear cluster: a rounded tan lobe roughly 19x34px on a head ~82px long (i.e. ~40% of head length), plus a dark-brown angular wedge overlapping it, plus a smaller pale triangular flap below. Comparison with Impala.png from the same batch confirms this is a deliberate enlarged-ear parameter, not generic head geometry - Impala's head is a bare wedge with nothing there.

WHY IT STILL FAILS. (a) Must-read 'thin WHITE vertical stripes' is inverted and over-counted: what is drawn is ~14 DARK brown bars on a pale tan coat, where a kudu is thin pale stripes on a darker grey-brown coat. The single most diagnostic kudu marking is delivered in reverse polarity. (b) The comb bar above is a non-anatomical rendering artifact welded across the barrel, and it is not alone - there are three more ruled horizontal bars with blunt square ends on the neck and cheek, one of which crosses the neck striping to form an unmistakable '+' at the shoulder. (c) The ear cluster, while large, is a muddle of three overlapping shapes half-buried behind the horn base and jaw; it does not resolve as the required 'enormous rounded satellite dish'. (d) The face carries 4-5 zebra-like dark bars across the muzzle; a kudu has a plain face with a single white nose chevron.

WHAT IS GOOD AND SHOULD NOT BE TOUCHED: the horns read correctly - two cream, tapering, double-S helical shafts with faint ridge lines, rising ~27% of total figure height above the head, clearly distinct from Impala's lyre. Legs are fine and correctly cloven (two-toe hooves at 6x). Tail is a thick tan rope with a proper fringed brush tuft. Silhouette, stance and proportions read as a large antelope.

FAMILY NOTE: Bongo.png in the same directory is the identical chassis with the identical comb artifact and the identical inverted dark striping, differing only in coat hue. This is one shared stripe-generator defect, not two per-species defects - fix it once at the generator.

FIX ORDER: (1) delete the horizontal ruled bar(s) that the stripes anchor to; (2) invert stripe polarity to pale-on-darker-coat; (3) cut the count from ~14 to 6-10 and make them near-vertical rather than a converging fan; (4) resolve the ear cluster into one broad rounded paddle clear of the horn base; (5) drop the muzzle barring in favour of a single nose chevron.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy ox with one broken tusk

The curtain of hair is missing: the coat ends in a ragged hem above the elbow and the whole lower half of all four legs is bare tan, so nothing hangs near the hooves. Upheld, but two of the stated causes are factually wrong and must not be fixed as written.

WHAT I DID: read the 440x440 PNG whole, then decoded it and re-rendered 5 magnified crops (head at 6-8x, horn cluster at 8x, topline at 5x, lower legs at 5x, rump/tail at 7x). Subject bbox is x87-352, y91-331 = 266w x 241h, aspect 1.10 against the packet's aspect: 1.5 — the figure is far too tall/square, and the reason is the high head carriage (see below).

CORRECTION 1 - HORN COUNT. The claim "only ONE horn is drawn... visibly asymmetric" is WRONG. At 8x there are clearly TWO horns: a bright cream near-side horn and a slightly darker tan far-side horn behind and above it, offset by roughly 6-8px, each a tapering crescent. What the first judge read as asymmetry is the near/far pair rendered as a stacked double-crescent. Do NOT "add the missing second horn" — it is already there and adding a third will make this worse.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG WITH THE HORNS (and this is what fails the must-read). Both horns are rooted at the TOP-REAR of the skull and sweep UP AND BACKWARD over the neck, tapering to points that end in open background above and behind the crown. That is a yak / Highland-cattle horn set. The must-read asks for horns meeting in a helmet-like BOSS across the forehead, then hooking DOWN AND OUT. There is no boss: the forehead between the horn bases is covered by a dark-brown elliptical cap (same dark shading tone as the cheek mass), not a pale keratin plate, and the pale horn material never spreads across the frontal bone. There is no downward hook anywhere — the horn tips are the highest points on the whole animal. So: two horns present, boss absent, hook absent. Fix = re-root both horns low on the forehead, fuse their bases into one pale cream boss plate spanning the frontal, and re-curve them down past the eye line before flaring out.

CORRECTION 2 - THE COAT. The claim "the curtain of hair is missing entirely" is an overstatement. The coat IS long and shaggy: the whole flank is painted with long vertical streaky guard-hair strokes, there are stray hair spikes breaking the dorsal silhouette from rump to withers, a hair fringe along the throat/brisket, and a handful of genuine hanging strands that drop past the belly line at the mid-barrel and at the rear flank. The defect is LENGTH, not absence. The hem sits at the ordinary belly line (real y ~276-284) with wisps to ~y292; hooves are at y~328. So roughly 45-50px of bare pale leg is exposed on all four legs — about 20% of the standing height. The must-read wants that skirt down to just above the hooves, i.e. the bare leg reduced to the cannon/pastern only. Fix = extend the existing hair strands ~35-40px further down and close the hem into a continuous skirt; the texture engine already produces the right strand look, it just stops too high.

CONFIRMED - POSTURE. The claim is right. The neck rises steeply off the shoulder and the head is carried level-to-HIGH: the muzzle tip sits at about the same height as the withers and the crown sits ~180px above the back line, which is what inflates the aspect to 1.10. There is only a very slight withers rise; the back is essentially a flat-to-gently-domed line from rump to shoulder with no musk-ox hump. The head must drop so the poll sits below the shoulder, and the shoulder must gain a real hump.

OTHER OBSERVATIONS: eyes are correctly small — two small dark ovals set high and wide on a 3/4-front face, the near one carrying a white crescent highlight. All four legs terminate in properly drawn dark cloven hooves. No tail is visible at the rump, which is acceptable for this species. Head shape is a long horse-like bovine muzzle, too narrow and too long for a musk ox's short blunt face.

BAND: FAIL stands. All three of the packet's must-reads fail on form (curtain too short, no boss and no down-out hook, head high and shoulders unhumped) and the asset currently reads as a shaggy yak / Highland bull rather than a musk ox. This is not a polish-level gap.

rows.readsAs: a white antelope with long back-swept horns — oryx is a fair guess

But the facial mask is two isolated black discs around the eye and cheek that read as goggles or panda eyes, not the oryx's black bands running down the face; there are no black markings on the legs at all, and no black flank line. The body is the slender fleecy antelope chassis rather than blocky and horse-like.

rows.readsAs: a pale woolly goat or sheep with straight ringed horns

rows.readsAs: a grey woolly ox or tapir with a single tusk

What is drawn is one pale ivory tusk-like curve laid across the top of the skull (the identical element reused on the Wildebeest and Yak), not a pair of enormous swept-back crescents sweeping out and back from the brow. rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at full size and then at 4-5x crops of the head, the feet and the tail. UPHELD, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and one credit is missing.

HORNS (mustRead 1: 'enormous swept-back crescent horns') — GENUINELY ABSENT, the claim is right. There is exactly ONE horn: a pale ivory/bone tapering rod that roots on the top of the skull just above and behind the eye, crosses the crown right-to-left and curves up to a blunt upturned tip that clears the head by about a head-width. No second horn anywhere — not mirrored, not foreshortened, not tucked behind the ear. I cropped Wildebeest.png and Yak.png at the same magnification to test the 'reused element' part of the claim and it is CONFIRMED: both carry the identical single ivory hooked rod in the identical crown position, just shorter and more strongly hooked. Three bovids, one horn part. NOTE one refinement: the rod IS swept backwards (base forward at the brow, tip trailing back over the neck), so 'swept-back' is not the missing property — what is missing is (a) the PAIR and (b) the mass/breadth of a crescent. The fix is a mirrored pair of thick, flattened, broad-based crescents leaving the skull sideways at the brow and sweeping back-and-up over the shoulders, not a longer version of the shared rod.

MUZZLE (mustRead 3: 'broad flat wet muzzle held low') — FAILS, but NOT for the stated reason. The claim that it is 'a small rounded goat nose' is WRONG. The muzzle is large: a long, deep, rounded snout occupying roughly the front third of the head, ending in a big blunt dome, with a thin dark lipline running its whole length and a small hooked nostril tick set high on the front face. The actual defect is that it is a smooth tapered sheep/tapir snout with no broad flat nose PLATE — no dark wet rhinarium pad, no wide paired nostrils, no squared-off front. Head carriage part of the claim is CORRECT: the skull sits clearly above the topline on an upward-angled neck and juts forward; nothing is carried low and there is no shoulder boss or forward-of-the-chest neck drop.

BODY — mustRead 2 ('heavy low-slung body with a straight back') is the one that partly reads: the topline is genuinely straight and the barrel is deep. But the pelt is drawn as fine streaky pale-grey fleece strokes over a light grey ground, the neck is slim, and the ears are small (a dark rounded lobe behind the eye plus a dark pointed lobe forward of it, with a dark brown mask ring around a large glossy eye). Combined with the single ivory rod, it reads closer to a grey woolly SHEEP/RAM than to the 'generic grey woolly ox' the claim names — it is not ox-massive.

CREDIT THE JUDGE DID NOT GIVE: the feet are correct — all four end in two small dark cloven hoof-toes, cleanly separated. The tail is also correct — long, thin, with a broad bushy dark terminal tuft. Neither needs work; the failure is entirely the horn pair and the muzzle plate.

rows.readsAs: a striped grey pony or a badly drawn zebra
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are wrong on screen. The head is not a heavy boxy cow-like skull -- it is a flat pale oval disc held out horizontally from the neck, painted with dark bars, reading as a mask or shield plate rather than a head, and its horns are the same single pale tusk borrowed from the buffalo and yak instead of paired hooks curving out sideways. There is no shaggy chin beard and no neck mane; the dark bars over the neck and barrel read as zebra striping. The topline is level, so the high withers sloping down to a low rump is absent too, and a large pale plume disc hangs off the rump. A stranger names this a striped pony.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a long deep box-shaped skull hanging low off a maned neck, with a visible beard hanging under the chin and two dark horns that leave the top of the skull sideways then hook up, and raise the withers so the back slopes down to the hips.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at 1:1, at 3x, and at 5-9x crops of the head, throat, rump/tail and feet; also measured the silhouette's top edge column-by-column from the decoded pixels. The FAIL stands, but one of the three stated causes is factually wrong and the single worst defect went unmentioned.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY READS AS: a pale bone-grey pony/quagga. The dominant signal is bold dark-brown VERTICAL BARS painted across the whole barrel, over the shoulder, up the neck AND across the face. A real wildebeest is a plain dark slate animal with at most faint brindle on the forequarters; this is zebra livery applied head-to-tail. Body is a smooth equine barrel on four thick pale columnar legs.

MUST-READ 1 - 'heavy boxy cow-like head with sideways-curving horns': FAILS, and the judge described it correctly in substance. The head is a flat pale ELLIPSE, wider than tall, with a second larger translucent grey ghost-ellipse stacked behind/under it so the head reads as a doubled disc roughly as deep as the neck is long. Two corrections: (a) it is NOT held horizontally - it is tilted about 25-30 degrees nose-down toward the lower right, muzzle end at approx (350,175) in a 440px frame, cranium end at approx (265,120); (b) there IS a feature the judge missed sitting on the skull - a solid mid-brown ellipse at roughly (285,95) reading as an ear or horn boss, the only non-striped element up there. Horn: exactly ONE cream/bone tusk, base at approx (275,105), sweeping up and curving back to the LEFT and terminating at approx (248,80). It reads as a warthog/boar tusk or a small mammoth tusk, not as a pair of cow horns sweeping out sideways and hooking up. No second horn anywhere, no lateral spread, no dark horn boss across the brow.

MUST-READ 2 - 'shaggy chin beard and neck mane': FAILS, absent. At 7x the entire leading edge of the neck from jaw to chest is one clean unbroken smooth curve - no fringe, no dangling hair, no silhouette break at the throat. The top of the neck is likewise smooth; the only thing along it is a thin pale highlight seam over the shoulder, which is a shading arc, not a crest. Nothing on this animal is shaggy.

MUST-READ 3 - 'high shoulders sloping to a slight rump': THE JUDGE IS WRONG HERE. The topline is not level. Measuring the topmost non-background pixel per column: croup at x=136 is y=198, and the back rises monotonically to the withers at x=248, y=154. Ground line is y~330, so withers stand ~176px above ground versus ~132px at the croup - a 1.33 ratio and a ~25%-of-body-height rise. The forequarter-high sloping topline is genuinely present and readable. This must-read should be scored as MET; do not spend a fix on it.

OTHER DEFECTS THE JUDGE DID NOT REPORT:
- TAIL (worst unlisted problem): a huge grey radiating FAN, a disc about 90px across with ~20 spiky bristles fanning off its left edge, held out horizontally from the rump at approx (60-135, 190-260). It is larger than the head. A wildebeest tail is a long thin black horse-like switch hanging to the hocks; this is a peacock/turkey fan and it dominates the rear silhouette.
- FEET: partial credit against the 'pony' read - each of the four legs ends in a tiny paired dark-brown CLOVEN toe cap (two distinct blobs per foot, ~6px each), so the hooves are correctly artiodactyl. They are just far too small to register at thumbnail size against the equine leg columns above them.
- A wide dark brown horizontal band runs the full length of the flank at belly height (y~215) like a saddle girth strap, adding to the harnessed-pony impression.

VERDICT: two of three must-reads (boxy horned cow head; beard and mane) are absent, the identity-carrying head is a striped mask disc with a single boar tusk, and the coat is zebra-striped. It reads as the wrong organism. FAIL upheld.

FIX TARGETS, in order: (1) replace the single tusk with a PAIR of dark horns emerging low and wide from a heavy brow boss, sweeping out sideways then hooking up; (2) rebuild the head as a deep boxy squared-off skull carried LOW on a level or downward neck, kill the ghost underlay disc; (3) add a shaggy fringe on the throat/chin and a coarse crest along the neck top; (4) replace the fan tail with a thin long dark switch; (5) strip the stripes back to a few faint brindle marks on the forequarter only and darken the base coat to slate. Do NOT touch the topline - it is already right.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy brown highland cow or yak
rows.defect: The best asset here -- the long hair pass over the flanks genuinely reads -- but the curtain stops well above the ground, ending at mid-shin and leaving four bare pegs and hooves fully exposed, so the signature skirt-to-the-ground silhouette is lost. The humped shoulder is not visible: the topline runs flat from neck to rump with only a faint darker patch where the hump should be, and the head is carried high and level rather than slung low. The tail is the family's pasted-on horizontal fan-and-disc rather than a bushy plume dropping from the rump, and the horn is again the single shared ivory tusk instead of a symmetrical pair.
rows.fix: Extend the flank hair down past the hocks so it nearly touches the ground and hides the upper legs, and raise a distinct hair-covered withers hump so the neck and head fall away below it.

rows.readsAs: a striped paper-lantern jellyfish with two cat eyes
rows.defect: The W-shaped pupils are genuinely there and correct — the best-observed feature in the batch — and a dark fin ellipse does run the full mantle length behind the body. But the fin is a flat backdrop plate, not an undulating skirt: it has no wave, no edge modulation, and does not attach to the mantle anywhere I can see. The arms are six or seven thin dangling twigs of near-equal length with teardrop tips, so the eight-arms-plus-two-longer-tentacles split does not read; nothing has a sucker. The mantle is a front-on ellipse about 1.4 wide, not the broad flattened aspect-2 cuttlebone body, and the vertical stripes read as lantern ribs rather than chromatophore banding.

rows.readsAs: a red balloon with a cartoon face and spider legs
rows.defect: All three must-reads miss. The eyes are inset in the middle of the red bulb as two small black dots with catchlights, so the bulb reads as a HEAD with a face — precisely the error the packet note warns about; the mantle never sits above the eyes and there is no head/arm crown beneath it. The arms are about seven smooth hairlines with no taper, no mass and not one sucker, splaying in a symmetric fan; unequal length is not expressible when every limb is the same wire. The pupil is a plain round dot with no horizontal slit. The dark lobes flanking the bulb read as ears, which an octopus does not have. Beyond its own row it is pixel-for-pixel the Octopus card in a redder hue.

rows.readsAs: the same red balloon-and-threads octopus as the Giant Octopus card, with two long strings added
rows.defect: Nothing here says giant squid. The mantle is a plump egg roughly 1.4 tall, not the aspect-5.5 torpedo the row demands, and the fins are the same soft rounded ear-lobes that appear on every other card in this batch, flanking the mantle's upper flank rather than forming a small triangular pair at a pointed tail. The dinner-plate eyes — the one feature that IS this animal — are two pinprick black dots with catchlights, smaller relative to the body than a housecat's. The two feeding tentacles with knobbed tips are present and are the only correct element. Stood next to the Giant Octopus card it is the identical silhouette in the identical red; a stranger would name it octopus.
rows.fix: Stretch the mantle to a true 5:1 torpedo with a sharp tail-end triangular fin pair and blow the eyes up to at least a quarter of the mantle's width so the head-lamp scale reads instantly.
rows.verifyWhy:
I read the 440x440 PNG, then re-read it at 3x-6x magnification on the mantle apex, the fin lobes, the eyes and the limb tips, and I ran scanline width profiles over the body. The FAIL stands: two of the three must-reads are absent. But three parts of the stated cause are wrong and would send a fix at the wrong target.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Upright portrait pose, arms hanging down. Mantle apex at y=31, core mantle 96px wide, bottom of mantle at y~180 where the eyes and arm crown sit: a 1.5:1 vertical egg (145 tall / 96 wide), rounded at BOTH ends. A single dark horizontal ellipse is drawn BEHIND the mantle, spanning y58-110 and 146px wide against the mantle's 96, so it shows as two rounded lobes ~25px wide x ~50px tall protruding from the flanks - a Saturn-ring, not two separate fins. Two black eye discs at y167-182, left eye x195-208 (14 wide x 16 tall) with a 5px white catchlight. Below that a fan of ~6 visible arms, plus two limbs that run far past the rest to y=407 and terminate in 22x14px oval clubs.

MUST-READ 1 (two feeding tentacles far longer than the eight arms, clubbed tips): PRESENT AND FULLY READABLE. The two clubbed limbs are unmistakable, drop well past the arm fan, and the knobs are clean ovals. No fix needed here.

MUST-READ 2 (torpedo mantle with a small triangular fin pair at the tail end): FAILS, but not for the reason given. The judge said the fins sit 'on the mantle's upper flank instead of at a pointed tail' - the POSITION is actually defensible. The fin ellipse occupies y58-110 on a mantle spanning y31-180, i.e. it hugs the tail (top) third, which is where a squid's terminal fins belong. The real defects are (a) SHAPE: the fins are one continuous rounded ellipse passing behind the body, showing as ear-lobes - the identical primitive the Giant Octopus and Vampire Squid cards use - with no straight edges and no apex; a triangular pair is nowhere in the drawing; and (b) the mantle apex is a smooth dome, not a point: the silhouette is already 30px wide only 4px below the tip (y=31 span 7, y=35 span 30). There is no terminal tail point for fins to attach to. And (c) the proportion: 1.5:1, so the judge's '1.4-tall egg' is essentially correct as measured.

MUST-READ 3 (dinner-plate eyes): FAILS, but 'two pinprick dots' overstates it. The eyes are legible 14x16px black discs with a white catchlight, about 16% of mantle width - visible, just generic. The damning measurement is the comparison: I mapped the Giant Octopus card's eye at the same threshold and it is 15x15px with the same catchlight in the same relative spot. The eye received ZERO enlargement for the one animal in the batch whose eye is the identity feature. The Vampire Squid card in this same batch draws a ~30px orange-irised eye, so the renderer plainly supports a large eye - this is a parameter that was never set, not an engine limit.

CORRECTING THE HEADLINE CLAIM. 'Reads as the Giant Octopus card recoloured' is the wrong sibling and understates the problem. It is not the octopus: the octopus mantle is a near-circle (~1.05:1) and has no clubbed tentacles. What this IS is the plain SQUID card recoloured. I ran the row-width profile on both and they are identical span-for-span at every scanline (30/46/56/65/100/126/140/146/144/138/126/110/96/96/96/95/94/92/90/88/84/80), differing only by a ~24px horizontal offset and hue (deep red vs pink). Giant Squid and Squid are one drawing at one scale, despite the packet asking for aspect 5.5 and 3.2 respectively. There is no size, slenderness or eye differentiation between the two at all - that is the sharper finding and the thing a fix must break.

FIX TARGETS, in order: (1) stretch the mantle to a slender torpedo, roughly 4:1, and taper the tail (top) end to an actual point instead of a dome; (2) replace the behind-the-body ellipse with two straight-edged triangular fins attached at that point, small - a giant squid's fins are modest, unlike the Squid card's; (3) scale the eyes up several-fold to read as plates at the base of the arm crown, borrowing the Vampire Squid card's iris treatment; (4) differentiate Giant Squid from Squid so the two profiles are no longer identical. Keep the clubbed tentacle pair exactly as drawn.

rows.readsAs: a coiled cream rope, or an ammonite fossil
rows.defect: The render is headless — there is no animal. Not one of the dozens of short tentacles is drawn, there is no leathery hood, and there is no opening: the spiral simply closes on itself. The only thing near the aperture is a stray flat translucent grey disc stranded half off the shell's right edge and a faint grey circle overlapping the coil, both of which read as render debris rather than a body. The shell itself is wrong too: it is a rope of overlapping identical scallops wound like a cinnamon roll, with no septa, no widening whorl and no red-brown flame striping at all — it is uniform cream.
rows.fix: Open the outer whorl into a real aperture and fan thirty-plus short suckerless tentacles out of it under a dark leathery hood, then stripe the outer whorl with radiating red-brown flames.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 1x, 2x, and 6-7x crops of the core, the top-right edge, the bottom-left quadrant and the grey blob, plus a contrast-boosted silhouette pass and a pixel histogram. The FAIL stands, but three of the stated causes are wrong and one defect was missed.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Subject bbox is 99,87-339,335 (241x249, aspect ~0.97 against the packet's 1.2). The silhouette is a near-perfect disc with exactly one protrusion: a small oval bump at the lower right. Nothing else breaks the circle anywhere on the perimeter.

MUST-READ 1, coiled chambered shell striped with red-brown flames - FAILS. Coiled: yes. Flames: absolutely absent - a histogram over every non-transparent pixel returns ZERO pixels satisfying even a loose warm test (r>70, r-b>45, r-g>18). The entire palette is cream/beige/taupe/neutral-grey (dominant buckets 224,224,192 / 192,192,160 / 160,160,128 / 128,128,96). Chambers: what is drawn is EXTERNAL bead ribbing - the whorl is subdivided into dozens of near-identical rounded crescent segments with hard dark grooves between them, each individually shaded, like a coiled sausage or a rope laid in a spiral. A real nautilus exterior is SMOOTH; its chambers are internal and are read on the outside only via the flame stripes. So the coiled-rope / cinnamon-roll / ammonite read the other judge describes is correct.

CORRECTION 1 - "no widening whorl" is WRONG. The whorl does widen, and properly: the innermost beads at the umbilicus are ~4px across and the outer whorl beads are ~28px, an honest expanding logarithmic coil with a small pearly bulb at the centre. The rope read is caused by the identical repeated bead segmentation and the hard inter-bead grooves, NOT by a failure to widen. The fix is to remove the bead segmentation and make the whorl surface smooth and continuous, then lay red-brown flame stripes radiating outward from the umbilicus across the outer whorl - widening the spiral would not help and would make it worse.

MUST-READ 2, dozens of short tentacles fanning from the opening - ABSENT. There is no aperture, no fan, no single tentacle anywhere on the perimeter. Confirmed on the boosted binary silhouette: the only thing off the disc is the grey oval.

MUST-READ 3, leathery hood over the head - ABSENT. No head, no hood, no pinhole eye.

CORRECTION 2 - the grey disc is OPAQUE, not translucent, and it is not truly "stray". At 7x it is a flat, single-value mid-grey ellipse (~#808080, roughly 57x44px, centred near 306,275) with a hard geometric edge, zero gradient, zero internal modelling. It OCCLUDES the shell's scallop texture where it overlaps, so it is opaque and drawn after the shell. Its position is anatomically where the head/hood/tentacle mass BELONGS on this coil orientation (lower-right, at the mouth of the outer whorl) - so this is almost certainly the head/hood/tentacle group emitted as a bare unpainted primitive rather than random render debris. That distinction matters for the fix: the geometry hook exists at the right anchor, it is the painting of it that never happened.

MISSED DEFECT (not in the original claim). There is a SECOND stray element: a thin pale stroked circular arc, roughly 1-2px wide, that is offset from the shell and does not follow it. It enters over the bead texture at the upper right (around 262,120), sweeps outside the shell's right silhouette edge, crosses OVER the grey oval, and terminates near the lower left. It is stroked on top of both the shell and the grey oval and is clearly visible in the top-right crop cutting diagonally across the ribs. Two separate unpainted/misplaced primitives, not one.

BAND. Two of three must-reads (tentacle fan, hood) are entirely absent, the third has none of its diagnostic colour, and the shell form reads as an ammonite or a coiled rope. Nothing in the image reads as a living cephalopod. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a salmon balloon with a cute dot-eyed face and six threads
rows.defect: Same three misses as the Giant Octopus card. The eyes sit inside the bulb, so the mantle reads as a head and the note's warning is violated. Only about six arms are visible, all identical hairline strokes with no taper and not a single sucker anywhere; two sweep wide to the frame edges and the rest hang straight, giving a symmetric daddy-longlegs fan rather than a boneless eight-arm crown. The pupils are round black dots with white catchlights — no horizontal slit. The dark ear-lobes behind the bulb are cephalopod-inaccurate. It is the Giant Octopus image recoloured.

rows.readsAs: a pink octopus with two extra long knob-tipped strings
rows.defect: The two long clubbed tentacles read clearly and are correct. Everything else misses: the mantle is a plump egg, not a torpedo, and nowhere near the stated 3.2 aspect; the fins are the batch's standard soft rounded ear-lobes set on the mantle's upper flank instead of a triangular pair at a pointed rear; and the eyes are two tiny dots placed high on the mantle rather than a large eye at the base of the arms. The eight arms are again featureless hairlines with no suckers and no taper. It is the Giant Squid card in pink.

rows.readsAs: a small cloaked deep-sea cephalopod — the only card here that names its own animal
rows.defect: The webbed cloak joining the arms is present and genuinely reads as a cape, the ear-like flap fins on the mantle are there, and the huge glowing red-orange eye is the strongest eye in the batch. The defect is that there is only ONE eye: the mantle, ears and cape are drawn bilaterally symmetric and dead front-on, so the missing second eye reads as cyclopean deformity rather than as a three-quarter view. The cape's lower edge is scalloped into shell-like lobes that read as a clam rather than a webbed membrane, the arm tips do not emerge past the web anywhere, and the whole animal sits small in a large empty frame.

rows.readsAs: a pink fish — a salmon or trout in side view
rows.defect: The identity must-read is entirely absent: there is NO long narrow tweezer beak and no teeth. At 8x the head simply tapers to a sharp fish point, with a straight taper where the bulging melon should be, so there is no rostrum/melon break at all. The eye is a large glossy round fish eye, not the tiny reduced eye of a river dolphin. The tail is a symmetric vertically forked fish caudal fin, not a horizontal fluke. The pectoral is a dark ellipse hanging fully below the belly line, unattached. The blowhole is a grey ellipse floating in open water above and clear of the topline — a stranded fragment. The dorsal is a detached oval blob sitting on the back rather than a low ridge blended into the topline.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: extend a long, thin, parallel-sided beak forward for roughly a third of the head length with a fine tooth comb along it, and set it off with a distinct rounded melon dome rising behind it — then reseat the blowhole into that dome and turn the caudal into a broad horizontal fluke blade.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but two of the four stated causes are wrong and one real defect was missed. I decoded the 440x440 PNG and re-rendered crops at 8x and 12x.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (packet mustRead: 'very long narrow tweezer beak crowded with teeth · low ridge or hump instead of a tall dorsal fin · bulging flexible melon and a mobile neck'; aspect 4, headFrac 0.22, eyes small, posture swimming).

1. BEAK / TEETH / MELON — CONFIRMED ABSENT, and worse than described. At 12x (source region x62-132, y195-240) the head is a single flat triangular wedge: the dorsal line and the ventral line converge in a straight run to one sharp point at x=68, y=212. There is no rostrum, no separation between rostrum and forehead, no melon bulge (the forehead is a straight-to-slightly-concave ramp), and — not noted by the first judge — NO MOUTHLINE OF ANY KIND. Not a short one, not a stub: zero jaw geometry is drawn on the head. Nothing to hang teeth on. There is also no neck break, no post-cranial crease. Two of the three mustReads are simply not rendered.

2. EYE — CONFIRMED and I would sharpen it. It is a hard-edged black disc ~9px across centred near (95,214), with a bright white specular dot at its upper-left and a darker rim ring. Against a headFrac of 0.22 and 'eyes: small' this reads as a large glossy teleost eye, and it is the single loudest fish cue after the tail.

3. TAIL — CONFIRMED. At 8x (x280-390, y180-270) the caudal is a symmetric vertical fork: upper lobe tip at ~(360,192), lower lobe tip at ~(368,232), with a deep V notch biting forward to ~(358,212). Upper and lower lobes are near-equal in reach and both extend perpendicular to the body axis. That is a homocercal fish caudal fin. A lateral-view cetacean fluke must read as a low, wide, near-horizontal blade with a shallow median notch, its mass spread fore-aft rather than up-down.

4. PECTORAL — THE CLAIM IS WRONG. It is NOT 'a detached ellipse hanging clear of the belly line.' At 8x (x120-230, y215-285) the flipper ellipse is centred ~(152,240), tilted ~30 degrees down-and-back, and roughly its upper-left third lies INSIDE the body silhouette, drawn as a dark overlay on the pink belly; it emerges through the ventral edge and the rest hangs below. It is attached. The real defect is different and should be fixed as such: it is an unmodelled flat ellipse — no taper toward a tip, no leading/trailing-edge asymmetry, no shoulder socket — painted as an opaque dark blob that CROSSES the ventral contour instead of growing out of it, so the belly line runs visibly through it.

5. BLOWHOLE — CONFIRMED. A pale grey-white ellipse sits at roughly x110-121, y184-191. The dorsal topline (white rim highlight) at that x is at y~195. So the ellipse floats ~4px clear in open water above the back with dark background visible between it and the body. It also sits well forward of where a blowhole belongs relative to the (nonexistent) melon.

6. MISSED BY THE FIRST JUDGE — the one mustRead that IS satisfied, and its own bug. There is a low rounded dorsal hump at ~x195-232, y178-193, correctly a hump rather than a tall falcate dorsal fin, which is what the packet asks for. But it too is a floating cap: its anterior base touches the topline near x=197, while its posterior base ends at y~193 where the topline has already dropped to y~199, leaving a ~6px dark water gap under its rear flank. Same seam bug class as the blowhole. Any fix pass should re-seat the hump, not just add a beak.

VERDICT: the organism on screen is a generic pink fish — wedge head with no jaw, big glossy eye, forked vertical caudal fin. Two of three identity mustReads (tweezer beak with teeth, melon plus mobile neck) are wholly absent, so the FAIL stands. Fix order: (a) build a long narrow rostrum roughly 0.35-0.4 of body length with a visible mouthline and a tooth row, (b) put a bulging melon behind it with a neck crease, (c) replace the forked caudal with a horizontal fluke, (d) re-seat blowhole, dorsal hump and pectoral onto the silhouette, (e) shrink and de-gloss the eye.

rows.readsAs: a large grey fish
rows.defect: The packet's own note says the flukes must be horizontal and never vertical like a fish — and they are drawn as a vertical fish caudal fin: two equal lobes above and below the axis with a concave notch, confirmed at 8x, and undersized relative to the body. The flippers must-read fails too: one short rounded dark ellipse drooping below the belly line, not a long paddle. The render is also broken at the head — the pale rim-light stroke has divorced from the silhouette, arcing well above and in front of the snout and terminating in mid-air as a stranded hairline in empty black. The snout comes to a sharp point rather than a blunt baleen rostrum, and the blowhole ellipse sits off the topline rather than in the head.
rows.fix: Replace the forked caudal with a wide horizontal fluke blade — a shallow crescent with a central notch, drawn broad and flat across the tailstock — and clamp the rim-light stroke to the body path so it cannot overshoot the snout.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but for ONE defect only - the head render - and TWO of the three stated causes are wrong. Fixes must be aimed at the head, not the tail or the flipper. Measured on the 440x440 PNG (background sampled at 5,5 = rgb 5,6,12; a pixel counts as ink at |dR|+|dG|+|dB| > 18). Body runs snout x~23 to fluke tip x~417, so ~394px long; max body depth 173px at x=220.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN (their third claim, and it is real and worse than described). The pale rim-light topline stroke is a 4-6px hairline that runs detached from the body FILL across the entire head. Column dumps: at x=30 the stroke occupies y=205-210, then 10px of pure background (y=211-220), then the body fill starts at y=221. At x=40 stroke y=198-201, gap y=202-211, fill y=212+. At x=50 stroke y=190-194, gap 195-202, fill 203+. At x=80 stroke y=174-177, gap 178-182, fill 183+. At x=100 stroke y=166-170, gap 171-172, fill 173+. The two paths finally merge at x~125. So the divorce spans x=22 to x=125 - about 26% of the animal's length - with the gap widest (10-11px) over the front of the head and closing to zero at the neck. The stroke's leading tip is at x=22,y~213; the fill's snout tip is at x~24,y~229, i.e. the hairline ends ~2px forward of and ~16px above the actual snout. The blowhole IS drawn and IS correctly placed longitudinally (bright ellipse, R>110, x=83-92, y=163-168 - about 16% of body length behind the snout, correct for a baleen whale), but it sits ~4px ABOVE the already-floating stroke and ~13px above the body fill, so at 1x it reads as a dust speck in empty black, not as a blowhole on a head. CORRECT THE DIAGNOSIS: it is not that the stroke 'divorced from the silhouette' and wandered off - the stroke and the blowhole agree with each other and describe a deep, blunt, correctly-proportioned baleen head. It is the head FILL that is collapsed/short and sits ~10px below its own outline. The fix is the fill path (or the head-depth term feeding it), not the stroke. Secondary: because the fill is collapsed, the fill's snout tapers to a sharp point and reads as a dolphin/fish rostrum rather than the blunt rostrum with a heavy lower jaw the stroke implies.

THEIR TAIL CLAIM IS WRONG. The flukes are NOT 'a vertical, symmetric, notched fish caudal fin'. Measured: peduncle waist is 7px tall at x=356, the fin then flares to x=417. Fin chord (fore-aft) = 61px; fin span (dorsoventral) = 37px (y=196 to y=232). It is 1.65:1 WIDER THAN TALL. A fish homocercal caudal in lateral view is the opposite - span >= chord, usually 1.5-2x taller than long, with a deep fork. The notch here is shallow and posterior-facing: a row scan shows solid ink through x=404, the notch opening at x=406 (13px of background at mid-height), widening to x=416, so the median notch is only ~12px deep on a 61px chord (~20%), which is fluke-like, not fork-like. On the brightness-boosted render the tail reads as a swept, wing-shaped bilobed fluke, and the whole animal reads unmistakably as a cetacean, not a fish. The two genuine (minor) tail problems are: (a) it is undersized - 37px span on a ~394px body is 9.4%, where baleen flukes should read ~20-25% of body length; and (b) it is symmetric about the body axis with no shading, foreshortening or edge cue establishing the horizontal plane, so the horizontal-vs-vertical read is merely unforced rather than wrong. Neither is FAIL-grade on its own; POLISH at most.

THEIR FLIPPER CLAIM IS WRONG. It is not 'a short rounded blob'. It is a tapered ellipse whose major axis runs from about (122,238) to (180,277) - ~70px long - with a minor axis of ~25px, so aspect ~2.8:1, angled back and down off the shoulder, tapering at the distal end. 70px is ~18% of body length, a defensible generic-baleen paddle. Its real (minor) flaw is tonal, not geometric: it is filled near-black (R<70) and abuts the equally dark ventral shadow mass behind it, so it barely separates from the belly at 1x. That is a value problem, not a shape problem.

BAND RATIONALE. Two of the three mustReads - 'long paddle flippers and a smooth streamlined body' and 'horizontal notched tail flukes' - are present and readable (flukes small and unforced, flipper low-contrast: POLISH-level). The third, 'blowhole on top of the head', is drawn in the right place but is not attached to the head, and the surrounding head is a hard render break: outline and fill disagree by up to 11px across the whole front quarter of the animal, visible at 1x as a hairline arc and a floating white dot in empty black. A silhouette whose stroke and fill are separated is a broken render, and a named identity mustRead floating off the body is not readable as that feature. FAIL stands - on the head fill only.

rows.readsAs: a generic grey bream or moonfish; a plain silver disc fish with no face
rows.defect: Two of three must-reads are simply not drawn. The flat square human-like teeth — the entire reason anyone recognises a pacu — are absent; there is no mouth at all, not even a line. The blunt steep forehead with underslung jaw is absent too: the head tapers to a smooth point identical to Tetra's and Piranha's, so there is no forehead plane and no jaw to be underslung.
