What remains is the shared lens body in grey with hatched scale texture, and it is a lens rather than a coin (too long and pointed to read as the round compressed disc the reference asks for).
rows.fix: Cut the pointed rostrum back into a steep near-vertical forehead that drops to a small terminal mouth set low on the snout, and draw the mouth open enough to show a visible row of broad flat white square teeth — the human-teeth read must be legible at thumbnail size or the species has no identity.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at native size, then at 6x-14x magnification with contrast stretched over the head (crops at x245-345/y150-260 and x295-335/y190-240), plus a numeric scan of the anterior silhouette and of pixel luminance across the lower head. The FAIL stands, but two parts of the stated cause need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS. The fish faces RIGHT. Body spans x145-323, y148-272 -> length:depth 1.44. Anterior silhouette scanned row by row: y150 x265, y160 x273, y170 x287, y180 x299, y190 x309, y200 x317, y213-216 x323 (max), then back to x294 at y249. That is a single smooth monotonic convex curve with NO notch, NO step, NO break anywhere along it. Head furniture consists of exactly three marks: (1) the eye at ~x300,y202 - a white sclera annulus with a dark pupil and a single specular dot; (2) a dark operculum/gill curve at x~273 running from the dorsal line down to the belly; (3) a soft ventral shading band at y226-229.

CORRECTION 1 - 'not even a line' is very slightly overstated, and this matters for the fix. There IS a darker horizontal band at y=226-229 running x~282 to x~310, ending ~13px short of the snout tip. I measured it: luminance ~50-61 against a surround of ~78-85. That is a 25-value soft drop spanning four rows, i.e. a shading/scale-row transition, not a drawn stroke - compare the eye pupil (lum 0-20) and the operculum line, which are hard marks. Anyone fixing this should NOT mistake that band for an existing mouth to 'strengthen'; there is no mouth primitive there to build on. A mouth must be added from nothing.

CORRECTION 2 - the report omits the single most actionable fact in the batch. Piranha, the neighbouring asset on the SAME chassis, does have a mouth: a long drawn gape line with a row of white triangular teeth above and below it, clearly legible at native size. So the renderer already has a mouth+teeth path and it is simply not being invoked for Pacu. The pacu's flat square human-molar dentition - the one feature the animal is famous for - is absent while its batchmate gets a full tooth row. That is a wiring/parameter gap, not an engine limitation.

MUST-READ VERDICTS. 'deep coin-shaped compressed body' - PARTIAL, and the fix should NOT target body depth. At 1.44 length:depth the body genuinely is deep and laterally compressed. What is wrong is its outline: a symmetric almond/lens pointed at BOTH ends, identical in Pacu, Piranha and Tetra, rather than a truncated disc. 'blunt steep forehead with an underslung jaw' - ABSENT. From y150 to y200 the profile advances 52px horizontally over 50px vertically, a ~45 degree gradual taper; a pacu's forehead is close to vertical above the eye and the head terminates in a short blunt snout with a small terminal-to-superior mouth. There is no jaw structure of any kind - no lower-jaw mass, no lip, no chin. 'flat square human-like teeth' - ABSENT, confirmed at 14x with contrast stretched.

CHASSIS. Confirmed by direct side-by-side: all three characins are one lens hull with the same anterior taper, the same dorsal-fin placement, the same swept forked caudal, and the same regular scale hatching. Pacu is differentiated from the chassis by NOTHING - Piranha at least earns its teeth and Tetra its cyan. The gradual anterior taper is a chassis property, so Piranha's 'steep blunt forehead' must-read fails on the same geometry; fixing the head profile is a family-level change, not a per-asset one.

BAND. Two of three must-reads absent, and both absent ones are the head architecture that constitutes the species identity. What ships reads as a generic silver deep-bodied minnow. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a piranha — the tooth row carries it, but it is a toothy generic disc fish rather than a piranha's head
rows.defect: The teeth are present and do sell the species, but they are pasted onto the outside of the shared silhouette as a long saw of eight triangles running from below the eye diagonally down past mid-belly — that is a serrated keel, not a jaw. There is no jaw line, no mouth aperture and no gape for them to sit in, so they float outside the body edge. The undershot jutting lower jaw is absent entirely and the steep blunt forehead is absent: the head is the same smooth taper to a point as Pacu and Tetra. The deep chunky body is the one must-read genuinely satisfied.
rows.fix: Build an actual head — break the snout with a steep forehead and push a chunky lower jaw forward past the upper lip, then set the triangular teeth inside that gape as a short bite line at the front of the head instead of a saw running along the belly.

rows.readsAs: a small teal disc fish — closer to a cichlid or a generic aquarium fish than to a tetra
rows.defect: The bright lateral stripe from eye to tail, which is the whole identity of a tetra, is not there. The only horizontal feature is a faint darker shading line across the mid-flank that stops short of both the eye and the tail and has no contrast against the body; because the entire fish is flooded the same cyan, nothing reads as a stripe at all. The tiny adipose fin behind the dorsal is absent — there is no second dorsal element anywhere on the topline. The silhouette is also the shared deep lens at roughly 1.5:1 rather than the slimmer 2.5 aspect the reference calls for, and the body is saturated cyan rather than silvery, so 'small deep-bodied silvery fish' only half lands.
rows.fix: Slim the body toward the specified 2.5 aspect, drop the flank to silver, and lay a single high-contrast stripe (neon blue over red, or at minimum one bright band) running unbroken from the eye to the caudal base, then add the small adipose nub between the dorsal and the tail.
rows.verifyWhy:
REFUTED ON THE CENTRAL CLAIM. I decoded the PNG and measured it pixel-by-pixel (row-luminance profiles, a whiteness/min-channel isolation map, and a 1px-step top/bottom silhouette-edge scan), plus 8x-26x nearest-neighbour crops of the head and the dorsal-to-tail topline.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE.
(1) THE LATERAL STRIPE IS PRESENT AND RUNS THE FULL SPECIFIED EXTENT. The claim that it 'stops short of both eye and tail' is false. Isolating the whitened (min-channel) pixels shows a continuous light band at rows y=197-207 running from x~172 -- which is the caudal peduncle, the body's left edge is x=167 -- rightward to x~290, terminating exactly at the eye (eye centre ~x=279, y=203, so the band passes through eye height and dies at the eye ring). That is literally 'eye to tail'. What the other judge called 'a faint low-contrast shading line crossing the mid-flank and stopping short' is NOT the stripe at all: it is the PECTORAL FIN, drawn as a darker diagonal line from the peduncle that widens into a dark triangle at x~250-262, y~213-222. They graded the pectoral fin and missed the stripe.
(2) The stripe's real defect is different and it is a POLISH defect: it is not the ONLY light band. There are THREE parallel whitened longitudinal bands -- the main one at y=197-207, a second at y=217-222, and a shorter belly band that tapers out around 60% of body length -- plus a dense horizontal scale-hatch texture across the whole flank. So the identity stripe has to compete with two near-identical siblings and reads as generalised sheen rather than THE stripe. Contrast is real but modest: stripe rows measure rgb(85,204,210) L~170 against flank rows rgb(29,150,165) L~115, i.e. ~1.5x, and the whitening (r channel 58-87 vs 25-33) is what carries it. FIX: keep band 1, delete or heavily damp bands 2 and 3, and push band 1 toward a distinct hue (neon blue-green) rather than a desaturation of the body colour, because the body is a single flat cyan so a white sheen is the only contrast mechanism available.
(3) THE ADIPOSE FIN IS GENUINELY ABSENT -- this part of the claim is correct and verified twice. The 1px top-edge scan (dark-fin top vs bright-body top) shows a gap of >=5px only across x=214-250, which is the single dorsal fin (a short-based mid-back fin with visible ray striations, spiking to 13-15px at the ray tips x=218,219,227,235). From x=213 back to the peduncle at x=167 the gap is only 1-4px, i.e. pure antialiasing on a smooth body curve. A 14x crop of that stretch confirms it visually: clean rim-lit topline, no bump. FIX: add a small blunt lobe on the topline at roughly x=195-203 (about 60-70% of the way from snout to tail-base), 3-4px tall, in the same darker fin teal as the dorsal.
(4) ASPECT: the direction of the claim is right, the number is wrong. Not '~1.5:1' -- the bright body alone is 128 x 72 px = 1.78:1, and the full silhouette including tail and fins is 152 x 92 = 1.65:1. Spec is 2.5, so it is ~30% too deep, but it is not as squashed as claimed.
(5) 'THE SHARED DEEP LENS' IS OVERSTATED AND 'TEAL CICHLID' IS WRONG. Measured against its two family-mates: Pacu is 175x124 body = 1.41, Piranha 163x111 = 1.47, Tetra 128x72 = 1.78. So the Tetra is measurably SLIMMER and smaller (152px overall vs 208/193) than the other two -- it is not the identical chassis at the identical ratio. It does share the family's almond/lens outline, the deeply forked caudal and the same scale-hatch texture, which is the legitimate criticism. And it does NOT read as a cichlid: a cichlid needs a long-based spiny dorsal running most of the back, whereas this has a SHORT-based dorsal over ~29% of the body plus a deeply forked tail -- that silhouette reads characin.

OTHER OBSERVATIONS: eye is prominent and correct -- white sclera ring with a dark pupil at x=279,y=203, sitting right on the stripe line. Snout is sharply pointed, gill/operculum line is drawn as a faint dark arc at x~272. Anal fin is present but very shallow (only 3-5px below the body line, x=205-220). 'Silvery' is not met -- the body, fins and tail are one flat cyan flood, where Pacu and Piranha in the same batch are correctly grey-silver; that is a hue-assignment problem, not a drawing problem.

VERDICT: POLISH, not FAIL. The organism does not read as the wrong animal -- it reads as a deep-bodied characin with a full-length lateral stripe, which is a defensible tetra. The FAIL rested on the stripe being missing, and the stripe is there at exactly the specified eye-to-tail extent. The four remaining defects (missing adipose lobe, stripe diluted by two competing bands and low saturation contrast, body 1.78 instead of 2.5, cyan instead of silver) are all additive corrections to a readable asset, not a re-draw.

rows.readsAs: a generic pointed leaf-shaped fish decal with a paper crown taped to its back and a tail fin floating separately behind it — closer to a sunfish clipart or a leaf than to a tilapia
rows.defect: The caudal fin is fully DETACHED: a rounded grey fan sits in open background with a clear gap between it and the body's rear point, and a thin dark line runs vertically through it and off both top and bottom edges — a stranded fragment plus a stray stroke. The blunt steep forehead must-read is absent: the head end tapers to a sharp point exactly mirroring the tail end, with the eye sitting almost on the snout tip. The dorsal must-read is wrong too — instead of a long spiny fin running the whole back it is a flat opaque sawtooth block covering only the middle ~45% of the topline, floating above the outline with background visible under part of its base and one spike hanging off the body edge. The body is a lens, not a deep laterally flattened disc, and there are no pelvic or anal fins; the pectoral is a grey chevron that reads as a rendering glitch.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette so the caudal fin joins a real peduncle at the rear of the body (no gap, no stray stroke), give the head end a short blunt vertical forehead so the snout stops mirroring the tail, and replace the floating sawtooth plate with a spiny dorsal whose membrane is anchored to and runs the full length of the topline from nape to peduncle.

rows.readsAs: a spotted goat or fawn - an appaloosa pony with leopard blotches
rows.defect: The must-read 'low elongated body on short legs' is absent and inverted: the barrel is deep and slab-sided and it stands on four LONG straight columnar legs whose dark feet are cloven hooves with toe scores, not paws. Belly clearance is roughly a full body depth. The 'masked face' is not a pair of bands through the eyes but one enormous solid black disc painted over the cheek plus a second dark ring around the actual eye, which reads as panda blotching. The ringed tail is the only civet cue present, and it hangs off the rump of a hoofstock body.
rows.fix: Rebuild on a viverrid chassis: halve the leg length, drop the belly to about a quarter of body depth, stretch the trunk to a low tube with a slight lumbar arch, and replace the hooves with short plantigrade paws showing four toes; then repaint the mask as two dark bars running through the eye onto the muzzle rather than a solid disc.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld, but three parts of the stated cause are wrong and one major defect was missed. WHAT I MEASURED (silhouette scan, lum>60 over the 440x440 png): bbox x117-322 / y149-274, 206x126, aspect 1.63 -- already BELOW the spec 1.9 even though that box includes the tail AND the projecting muzzle. At mid-torso (x=210..250) the back sits at y~172 and the belly at y~223, so torso depth is ~51px; belly-to-ground is y223->y274 = 51px. Belly clearance is 100% of body depth. Sampled (216,240) and (216,270) are background (9,15,20 / 4,7,10) -- the void under the barrel is real, not shadow. The mustRead 'low elongated body on short legs' is therefore genuinely INVERTED, exactly as claimed: a deep barrel with a straight level topline, a withers hump and a rounded rump, standing on four long columnar legs. Spot organization compounds it -- irregular blobby black splotches scattered at random over the barrel (appaloosa), where a palm civet's spots run in longitudinal rows along the flank. It reads as a spotted goat/pony. CORRECTION 1 - the feet are NOT cloven hooves. At 24x each foot is a broad flat olive-brown pad that projects both fore and aft of the leg column, carrying 3-4 faint vertical toe divisions; it reads as a splayed slab/plate, not a two-toed hoof. The defect is real (a civet foot is a small compact digitigrade paw) but the fix is 'shrink the pad to a compact paw', NOT 'remove hooves'. CORRECTION 2 - the mask description is half wrong. At 26x the RIGHT/near eye is a genuine eye: dark brown iris with a white square specular highlight -- it is not a 'dark eye ring' marking. The real defect is the LEFT/far eye: a flat disc of near-background navy, sampled (287,161) = 21,24,30 against bg 5,6,12, with NO iris and NO highlight, ringed only by a thin dark outline. It is an EMPTY SOCKET reading as a black hole. The judge was right that there are no dark bands running through the eyes: the only face markings are a broad flat olive-brown cap over the left half of the crown and a short vertical brown blaze down the forehead between the eyes -- both run OVER the top of the skull, not through the eye line. Masked face: ABSENT. MISSED DEFECT - there are NO EARS AT ALL. At 26x the skull is one smooth unbroken dome from nape to muzzle root; the brown crown cap is flat colour, not an ear shape. The reference calls for small round ears and none exist. CORRECTION 3 - the tail is not a clean survivor. It IS ringed (7 dark bands on cream with a blunt solid dark tip, unambiguous at 14x) but it is SHORT: ~90px against a ~200px body, roughly 45% of body length, and it hooks down and forward in a ringtail/lemur curl. The mustRead asks for a LONG ringed tail; only the ringing survives. ONE THING THAT IS RIGHT and the judge did not credit: the muzzle IS long and pointed per the note -- but it is drawn as a separate horizontal cylinder tacked onto the eye line with a dark oval nose at the tip, not blended into the skull, so it reads as a tapir/anteater tube rather than a civet's tapering face. Also a thick downward-flaring neck/dewlap wedge runs from skull to chest, pure ungulate. SCORE: mustRead 1 of 3 partially present (ringed tail, but short), 2 of 3 absent/inverted, plus missing ears. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: an armless tan sack balanced on one leg - a bowling pin with a snout
rows.defect: The render is anatomically broken: at 8x on the chest there are NO forelimbs at all - no shoulder, no arm, no hands - the torso is one smooth featureless bag from throat to groin, and only a SINGLE hind leg is drawn, ending in the same dark cloven hoof used on the Civet and Mongoose. Neither remaining must-read survives: there are no dark rings around the eyes (the eye is a plain pale-blue bead on bare cream fur), and the tail is a flat uniform tan tube with a blunt rounded end and no black tip, hanging free beside the leg rather than propping as the third leg of a tripod. The ears are large brown blobs on TOP of the skull, not small and low on the sides.
rows.fix: Draw the tripod: two short forelimbs tucked against the chest with visible paws, two hind legs planted with clawed digitigrade feet, and the tail angled back to touch the ground with a black terminal third; then add the dark orbital rings.
rows.verifyWhy:
Examined at 8x whole-body, 14x chest, 16x feet, 22x head and 36x eye (nearest-neighbour crops from the 440x440 master), plus direct pixel sampling. Measured bbox x176-266 / y139-283, w=91 h=145, aspect w/h = 0.628 (target 0.5). VERDICT UPHELD, but three of the five stated causes are wrong and must not be fixed as stated.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN (fix these):
(1) NO FORELIMBS - confirmed, this is the judge's one fully correct anatomical call. At 14x the torso is a smooth featureless sack: the front (right-facing) contour is an unbroken curve running from the chin, past where a shoulder and chest should be, down the belly to the hip, with nothing crossing it. No shoulder mass, no upper arm, no forearm, no paw, not even a seam or a shading break suggesting a tucked forelimb. The only marks on the torso are diagonal fur-texture streaks. A sentinel meerkat's whole silhouette read is the tucked forepaws held against the chest; there is nothing there.
(2) ONE HIND LEG, and it is a featureless cone - a single tapered tan wedge from hip to foot with no knee, no hock, no ankle articulation. A pure side view could excuse the occluded second leg, but the head is drawn three-quarter, so the near/far leg pair should separate.
(3) NO BLACK TAIL TIP - confirmed absent by pixel sample. The tail is solid RGB(181,161,132) at every sampled row from y=250 through y=282; the last 1-2 rows are (104,93,78), which is the ordinary edge/contact shadow every limb in this asset has, not a tip marking. It is also a flat, uniform-width (~8-9px) UNTAPERED tube with zero fur texture and a blunt rounded end - so 'thin TAPERING tail with a black tip' fails on both the taper and the tip.
(4) NO DARK EYE RING - fails, but not for the stated reason (see corrections). There is a warm chestnut oval on the head, but it sits on the brow/crown offset up-and-back from the eye, touching only the eye's upper-rear edge. Nothing encircles or bands the eye, so no ring or mask reads.
(5) EARS - two rounded domes sit on the CROWN of the skull: a cool grey-brown one (approx RGB 96,86,70) on the top-rear, and the warm chestnut oval in front of it. Whichever of the two is meant to be the ear, both are large and on top of the skull; nothing is small and set low on the side of the head, which the packet note explicitly calls for.

CORRECTIONS TO THE FAIL CLAIM (do NOT act on these as written):
(a) WRONG - 'a bare pale-blue bead on cream fur'. The eye is a small DARK, near-black bead (sampled core around RGB 20-30) with a grey-white catchlight on its upper-left. It is a correctly dark eye. The defect is the missing ring around it, not the eye colour.
(b) WRONG - 'ending in the same cloven hoof as the Civet and Mongoose'. At 16x the single visible foot is a splayed dark-taupe padded foot with 3-4 lighter vertical separations reading as toes, roughly twice as long as it is tall, planted flat. It is not a hoof and not cloven; it is the one genuinely mammalian extremity in the image.
(c) WRONG - 'the flat tan tube tail hangs free instead of propping the tripod'. Bottom-extent scan: tail occupies x176-185 and bottoms at y=283; the foot occupies x197-216 and bottoms at y=283. They sit on exactly the same ground line, so the tail DOES contact the ground and DOES prop. The tripod geometry is one of the few things this asset gets right.
(d) UNDERSOLD - the judge did not credit the posture must-read, which is present and readable: bolt upright, tall and narrow at 0.628 w/h, weight stacked over the hind foot, long pointed muzzle with a dark nose. That is a correct meerkat stance and a correct herpestid muzzle.

BAND REASONING: this is not the wrong organism - an upright tan mammal with a pointed muzzle and a grounded tail still reads 'meerkat' at a glance. But it fails as FAIL rather than POLISH on absent defining content, not on finish: two of three packet must-reads are absent (dark rings around the eyes; black tail tip - and the taper with it), and the asset carries a hard anatomy break in the complete absence of forelimbs plus a single unarticulated hind leg. Missing an entire limb pair is a build defect, not a polish pass. Priority order for the fix: forelimbs tucked against the chest first, then a black tail tip + taper, then the eye ring, then move the ears down and shrink them.

rows.readsAs: a long-bodied white goat or a shaggy sheep-dog on hooves
rows.defect: The must-read that IS the identity - a very long LOW tubular body on SHORT legs - is absent. The trunk is long but it is a deep shaggy fleece-textured barrel carried high on four long columnar legs with dark cloven hooves, so the animal is tall rather than ground-hugging. The tail is not a thick tail tapering to a point: it is a short bushy squirrel plume stuck horizontally off the croup, blunt at the end and paler than the body. The head is the identical wedge skull, brown ear-blob, blue bead eye and smile line used on the Civet and Meerkat, which gives a generic muzzle rather than the fine pointed herpestid snout.
rows.fix: Cut the leg length by more than half so the belly nearly grazes the ground, slim the barrel into a straight low tube of even depth, swap the hooves for small five-toed paws, and redraw the tail as a thick continuous cone tapering smoothly from the rump to a fine point.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at 1x, then re-cropped and nearest-neighbour upscaled the head (8x), the leg/foot band (16x) and the tail (6x), and column-scanned the silhouette for hard numbers. The FAIL stands, but ONE OF THE THREE STATED CAUSES IS WRONG and must not be 'fixed'.

MEASURED SILHOUETTE (light-pixel scan, background 5,6,12): bbox x117-323, y162-260 => 207 x 99, aspect 2.09 against a spec of 2.4. Barrel topline sits flat at y=184-185 from x=197 through x=262; belly at mid-body is y=225-227; the feet ground out at y=260. So barrel depth = ~41px and BELLY-TO-GROUND CLEARANCE = ~35px. The legs are 46% of standing height and the ground clearance is 85% of the barrel depth. That is goat/sheep-dog architecture. An Indian grey mongoose carries the belly at roughly a quarter of standing height, clearance well under half the barrel depth. THE DEFINING MUST-READ - 'very long LOW tubular body on SHORT legs' - IS GENUINELY ABSENT. The barrel is also long-ish (croup x~165 to shoulder x~290 = 125px, 3.0x its depth) so the tube is half there; it is the LEG LENGTH and the ride height, not the trunk length, that kill it. Fix the legs, not the body length.

LEGS AND FEET at 16x: each limb is one smooth pale column from the body mass to the ground with NO visible hock angle on the hind leg and no carpal break on the fore - a straight ungulate post. The judge called the feet 'hoofed'; strictly they are not hoofs. Each foot is a wide, dark-brown, flat-bottomed oval pad with three vertical toe grooves and three tiny pale claw/nail nubs poking out under the front edge - a clawed paw, drawn far wider than the leg column and rendered as one dark block. At 1x it READS as a cloven hoof, so the judge's conclusion is right and their anatomy label is wrong: the defect is that the paw is a wide dark unarticulated block on a jointless column, not that a hoof was drawn.

COAT: the whole barrel is covered in long shaggy directional hair strokes with a pale highlight ridge running the full topline, plus a shaggy skirt over the shoulder and thigh. This is fleece. A grey mongoose is short, tight, grizzled/ticked fur. The fleece is a major contributor to the sheep read and is a separate fix from the proportions.

HEAD - THE JUDGE IS WRONG HERE. It is NOT 'the shared generic wedge skull'. At 8x the head has a genuinely long, narrow, straight-tapering snout that runs well past the eye and ends in a small dark nose button; a small dark almond eye set high and forward; and TWO small rounded ears - a dark chocolate-brown rounded ear on the side of the skull and a paler rounded lobe forward and above it. That is a creditable herpestid/mustelid head and satisfies the 'pointed tapering snout with small round ears' must-read. DO NOT REDRAW THE HEAD. What IS wrong in that region is the NECK CARRIAGE: the topline climbs from y=184 at the withers to y=163 at the crown, so the head is held clearly ABOVE the back on a raised, upward-curving neck. A mongoose carries the head low, in line with or below the topline, continuous with the tube. The raised neck is what makes an otherwise correct head look caprine.

TAIL: runs x=117 to about x=175, so ~58px against a 125px trunk - under half body length, where a mongoose tail is 70-90% of head-body. At 6x it is a broad flat paddle/plume with a fringe of individual hair strands along its lower edge and a ROUNDED BLUNT end - it does not taper to a point, so that must-read fails too. Correcting the judge on one detail: it is not 'held horizontally'. It leaves the croup (y~196) and angles DOWN and back, the tip sitting at y~220-240, i.e. drooping below the croup.

VERDICT: two of three must-reads (low body on short legs; thick tail tapering to a point) are absent; the third (pointed snout, small round ears) is present and good. At 1x the organism reads as a pale shaggy sheep/goat-dog, i.e. the wrong clade at a glance, which is a FAIL not a POLISH. Priority of fixes: (1) drop the belly - halve the ground clearance and shorten the limb columns; (2) put a hock in the hind leg and lower the head onto the topline; (3) replace the fleece strokes with short grizzled fur; (4) lengthen the tail to ~80% of trunk and taper it to a point. Leave the muzzle and ears alone.

rows.readsAs: a needlefish or a juvenile gar — a slender silver fish with a long wire beak
rows.defect: The must-read is a short pointed CONICAL snout that overhangs the mouth. What is drawn is a hairline needle spike projecting roughly a fifth of the body length past the head, no thicker than a drawn line, with no taper and no jaw beneath it. That single prop moves the animal into a different family: a stranger reads needlefish/houndfish, never bonefish. The flank is also not plain mirror-silver — it carries the same diamond+dot scale mesh as the other two — and the caudal fork is shallow, not the deep sharp fork the row calls for.
rows.fix: Delete the wire spike and replace it with a short fleshy cone: a snout about one head-length long that tapers with visible volume and clearly overhangs an inferior mouth set back underneath it, then deepen the tail notch to a true deep fork and strip the scale mesh off the flank so it reads as plain polished mirror.
rows.verifyWhy:
Measured on the 440x440 PNG (pixel scans + 12x zooms of the head and caudal). VERDICT UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are wrong.

MUST-READ 1 - 'deeply forked tail': PRESENT. The judge's 'the caudal fork is shallow rather than deep' is WRONG and should not be actioned. The caudal is a proper concave V: upper lobe tip at (81,177), lower lobe tip at (81,228), notch vertex at (93,203), fin root/peduncle at (115,203). That is a 34px fin with a 12px notch (~35% of fin length) and long, sharply pointed, swept-back lobes with visible ray striation. It reads unambiguously as a forked caudal. At most it is marginally shy of 'deeply' (a live Albula cuts back 50-60%); it is nowhere near shallow and it is not a fail driver.

MUST-READ 2 - 'pointed conical snout overhanging the mouth': FAILS, and this is the fail driver. The head itself DOES taper to a sharp cone, ending at (307,203). From that cone apex, on the body centreline, springs a separate dark grey rod running to (360,203) - 54px long. Total animal length is 279px (tail tip 81 to rod tip 360), so the rod is 19% of the whole and 24% of the body proper; the judge's 'a fifth of the body long' is accurate. The judge's 'no taper' is WRONG - the rod does taper, 5px thick at its base down to ~1.4px at the tip. The real defect is that it begins as a hairline (5px against a 51px body depth, ~9%) and is a straight rigid spar rather than a short fleshy cone. 'No jaw beneath it' is CONFIRMED: there is no mouth line, no gape, no inferior lower jaw anywhere under the rod - the cone's ventral edge simply runs into the same apex point, so the projection overhangs nothing. A bonefish snout should overhang by roughly one eye-diameter above a small inferior slit mouth; here it overhangs by ~5.4 eye-diameters above nothing. The organism call is correct - it reads as a needlefish/gar/billfish.
  Compounding factor the judge did not name: the eye (a small cream ring with dark pupil, ~10px, centred at (293,194)) sits directly at the cone apex/rod base instead of set back on the head, which reinforces the needlefish read. Moving the eye back and replacing the rod with a short blunt cone plus a visible inferior mouth slit is the fix.

MUST-READ 3 - 'plain mirror-silver flank': FAILS, CONFIRMED. A dense diamond crosshatch scale lattice covers the entire flank from operculum to peduncle, plainly visible even at 1x. 'Family scale mesh' is also confirmed correct - I opened Mullet.png and it carries the identical lattice at the identical pitch, plus the same fusiform outline, same caudal fin, same pectoral triangle and same eye ring. Bonefish and Mullet are one chassis with the rod bolted on the front; the differentiating plain mirror-silver flank is simply not drawn.

Two of three must-reads fail and the failing one produces a wrong-organism silhouette, so FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a generic silver perch or bass with a stray grey bubble stuck to its face
rows.defect: The identity must-read — a blunt, FLAT-TOPPED head — is absent: the head is the family cone, tapering to a single sharp point at the nose exactly like the Bonefish and Tarpon, with no flat crown and no squared-off muzzle. Worse, a translucent grey ellipse floats off the front of the mouth, unattached to the silhouette and overlapping the snout tip; it reads as a render artifact, not anatomy. The two widely separated dorsal fins are present only as two faint ghost lobes so pale and so rounded they read as smudges rather than fins, and the faint body stripes are entirely missing.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a broad flat-topped wedge with a squared blunt muzzle and a tiny triangular mouth at the very front, remove the floating grey ellipse, and redraw the two dorsals as opaque, clearly separated fins — a small spiny triangle forward and a soft-rayed one well behind it.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 440px, at 7x head crop, at 5x contrast-stretched flank, and against a luminance silhouette mask, plus a per-column top/bottom edge profile of the fish. FAIL stands, but two of the four stated causes are wrong and must not be fixed as written.

HEAD (must-read 1 — CONFIRMED ABSENT, this is what fails the asset). The column profile shows the topline running in one unbroken straight taper from the rear of the anterior dorsal (x=260, y=169) to a needle point at x=303, y=194, while the ventral line rises 216->201 over the same span. There is no vertical or near-vertical snout wall, no flat plateau over the eye, no squared-off leading edge — the head is a plain isoceles cone, the same construction as Bonefish's (whose own must-read is literally 'pointed conical snout'). Correction to the judge: it is not pixel-identical to Bonefish — Bonefish carries a much longer, thinner needle rostrum that projects well clear of the skull, whereas Mullet's cone is shorter and broader-based. But the distinguishing read — blunt, flat-topped, squared skull — is entirely absent, so the two still collide in the family lineup.

MOUTH / THE GREY ELLIPSE (must-read 1, second half — FAILS, but the judge's description is WRONG). The judge calls it 'a translucent grey ellipse floating unattached off the front of the mouth.' It is neither translucent nor unattached. It is an OPAQUE flat slate-grey lozenge (~#4c525c, exactly the fill used for the caudal, pectoral and both dorsals), spanning x=303..337, y=191..210 — roughly 34px long by 19px tall — and its left end abuts/slightly overlaps the snout tip at x=303, so it is anchored to the head, not floating in space. The real defect is SCALE and SHAPE: the snout tip it hangs off is only ~7px deep, so the lozenge is ~2.7x the height of the head it is attached to and reads as a grey bubble or balloon stuck on the nose. The reference asks for a 'tiny triangular mouth'; this is a large soft-edged oval. Fix it by shrinking it to a small dark triangle notched into the snout, not by re-anchoring an ellipse that is already anchored.

TWO SEPARATED DORSALS (must-read 2 — the judge is WRONG; this one PASSES). They are not 'faint ghost lobes'. The silhouette mask shows two solid, unambiguous fin lobes that both genuinely break the dorsal topline: anterior peak at x~248 rising to y=159, posterior peak at x~204 rising to y=154, with the body's own topline recovering to y=166-168 across the gap between them (x=216..236). They are widely separated (~28% and ~65% of body length back from the snout) and correctly small. They read low-contrast only because they use the same muted slate grey as the other fins against a near-black ground — a contrast tweak at most, not a missing feature. Do not redraw these.

STRIPES (must-read 3 — CONFIRMED ABSENT). The contrast-stretched flank (130..310 x 150..230, luminance 130-230 remapped to full range) shows only a regular diamond scale lattice with speckled specular highlights, one dark curved opercular arc behind the eye, and the triangular pectoral fin. There is not one longitudinal line anywhere on the flank. No stripes at any strength.

ONE EXTRA DEFECT NEITHER JUDGE NAMED: the packet asks for aspect 4 and a 'silvery torpedo body'. Measured body (snout x=303 to caudal peduncle x~140) is ~163px long against a max depth of ~62px — aspect ~2.6 excluding the caudal fin. The silhouette is a deep rounded almond, closer to a sea bream than a mullet's slim cylinder. That deep oval, plus the cone head, is why the fish does not read as a mullet even before the missing markings.

Net: 1 of 3 must-reads (the two separated dorsals) is genuinely present and readable; the identity must-read (blunt flat-topped head with a tiny triangular mouth) is absent and replaced by a Bonefish-style cone plus an oversized grey nose lozenge, and the stripes are absent. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a generic deep-bodied silver fish — a shad or a herring, nothing more specific
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail. The huge silver-dollar plate scales are rendered as the same small diamond-and-dot mesh used on the Bonefish and Mullet, so the scale that defines a tarpon has no distinct size at all. The upturned bulldog lower jaw is absent — the mouth line slants DOWNWARD to the same pointed family cone, the opposite of the signature scooped, jutting lower jaw. And the long trailing filament off the rear of the dorsal, the single most recognisable tarpon feature, is nowhere on the image: the dorsal is just a dark triangular shadow on the back with a clean trailing edge.
rows.fix: Add the trailing dorsal filament first — a long whip streaming back from the rear of the dorsal nearly to the tail — then rotate the mouth so the lower jaw juts up and forward past the upper, and blow the flank scales up to large overlapping discs roughly a third of body depth so the plate armour reads at thumbnail size.
rows.verifyWhy:
I upheld the FAIL after reading the PNG at full size, then at 4x on the whole body, 12-16x on the head, 10-12x on the dorsal and its rear, 22x on the flank texture, and a 2.6x brightness-boosted pass to hunt for faint low-contrast strokes against the near-black background. I also rendered Bonefish and Mullet at identical crops for direct family comparison. All three of the mustReads are absent, but two of the three stated CAUSES need correcting so the fix targets the right primitive.

MUSTREAD 1 — 'huge silver-dollar plate scales': ABSENT, and worse than 'the same small mesh'. At 22x the flank is not a mesh at all: there are no scale outlines, no overlapping plate rims, no lattice lines. It is a scatter of 1-2px lighter/darker square pixels on a flat grey gradient — a speckle/glint noise texture at roughly 4px pitch across a ~275px body, i.e. ~60+ speckle columns. Mullet's identical crop is the same speckle primitive at ~3px pitch; Bonefish is the same primitive finer still. So the judge is right that it is shared and far too fine, but wrong in kind: the parameter that differs between the three siblings is only the noise density, and there is no scale GEOMETRY to enlarge. The fix is not 'increase mesh cell size' — it is to draw actual overlapping rounded plates (a tarpon reads at ~12-16 rows of big rimmed discs down the flank, each disc wide enough to carry its own highlight crescent and a visible dark trailing rim).

MUSTREAD 2 — 'upturned bulldog lower jaw': ABSENT, but the stated cause is wrong. The judge says 'the mouth slants downward into the family cone'. There is NO mouth drawn at all. At 16x the head carries exactly two marks: the eye and a single curved gill-cover arc well behind it. From the eye forward the head is a symmetric spear point — the dorsal profile slopes gently DOWN toward the tip and the ventral profile slopes UP toward the tip, meeting at a needle apex at roughly mid-body-height. No jaw line, no gape, no lip, no chin. So the defect is a missing feature, not a mis-angled one; nothing is 'slanting downward' because there is no mouth stroke to slant. This is also a family-wide omission (Bonefish and Mullet likewise have no mouth line), which is why it should be fixed at the family level: the tarpon needs a near-vertical, forward-jutting lower jaw whose tip sits ABOVE the eye's lower edge, with the mouth line running steeply up-forward — the single silhouette cue that separates it from the two pointed-snout siblings.

MUSTREAD 3 — 'long trailing filament off the rear of the dorsal fin': ABSENT. Confirmed, and I looked hard for it in the two places it could hide. The dorsal is a single low rounded dome sitting on the front half of the back (roughly x200-285 of 440, peak near x235), filled dark grey with faint vertical ray lines. Those ray lines DO overshoot slightly above the membrane as short hairs — I want to flag that so it is not mistaken for a partial filament: they are all the same short length, they are vertical, and there are ~6 of them across the fin, so they read as ray tips, not as one trailing streamer. Behind the dorsal the topline is a completely clean, smooth silhouette curve all the way to the caudal peduncle — at 12x and under brightness boost there is nothing there at all. I also checked the ventral line in case the filament had been drawn on the wrong fin: the belly carries only a small rounded anal lobe, no streamer. Fix: extend the LAST dorsal ray rearward as a single long tapering whip reaching roughly to the tail base.

WHAT IS PRESENT AND CORRECT: 'eyes: prominent' is satisfied — the eye is a large dark pupil in a bright cream ring, noticeably bigger than Bonefish's or Mullet's. Body depth reads deeper than Bonefish, consistent with aspect 3.5.

FAMILY OBSERVATION (relevant to the batch's chassis question): these three are one chassis. Same lens/almond body outline, same deeply forked tail with the identical ray fan, same single pectoral triangle at the same place, same gill arc, same eye ring, same speckle flank. The only per-species differences are dorsal count/shape (Tarpon one dome, Mullet two humps, Bonefish one dome), a snout appendage (Bonefish a thin needle rostrum, Mullet an odd dark lozenge blob), and overall grey value. Stripped of the packet labels, this asset reads as a generic silver fish — specifically as the Bonefish minus its rostrum — not as a tarpon.

rows.readsAs: A generic pink-flowered garden herb — lavender, heather, or oregano; nobody would say sea grape or even name it a coastal tree
rows.defect: Every must-read is missing and the wrong ones are substituted. The leaves are small narrow lance-shaped leaflets, dozens of them in near-opposite pairs along wiry stems — the exact opposite of the large round leathery dinner-plate alternate leaves that ARE the sea grape's identity; there is no red venation anywhere and no orange-red older leaf. The harvest is rendered as five upright terminal mauve-pink pompom flower heads sitting on top of the stems, where the reference calls for long DANGLING strings of round grape-like fruit — nothing hangs in this image at all. The habit is a narrow upright vase/broom taller than wide, fanning from one thin basal trunk, which contradicts the low windswept spreading coastal shrub the note explicitly warns about; the thin whippy stems even read as the vine the note says it is not.
rows.fix: Rebuild the plant from the leaf outward: a low wide-spreading stout woody shrub with a few thick crooked branches, each bearing a small number of very large flat circular leathery leaf plates with heart-shaped bases and bold red-pink midrib and veins (a couple turning orange-red), and hang two or three long pendulous strands of round green-to-purple berries down from the branch joints — drop the terminal flower pompoms and the small lance leaflets entirely.
rows.verifyWhy: I looked at the full 440x440 render and at 5x bicubic crops of the crown, the mid-stem zone and the base, plus a pixel bounding-box measurement. The FAIL stands: all three mustReads are absent or inverted. (1) LEAVES — the required 'dinner-plate round leathery leaves with red veins' are nowhere in the image. What is drawn is roughly 60-70 tiny narrow lanceolate blades, each about 22x8 px, pointed at both ends, distributed in sub-opposite/decussate pairs up seven whippy canes. Their fill is a flat mid sage-green with a slightly PALER GREEN midrib and two faint pale side-strokes; there is no red, pink or orange anywhere on any leaf, so both the bold red-pink venation and the orange-red older leaves are missing entirely. The single largest leaf is smaller than one flower head, which is the exact inverse of Coccoloba, where the leaf is the biggest, most identity-carrying object on the plant. (2) HARVEST — the judge called these 'pompom flower heads'; I am correcting that detail because it changes the fix. Zoomed to 5x, each of the five terminal heads is a flat rosette of eight to ten ROUND GLOSSY BEADS with specular highlights arranged in a ring around a small brown-tan receptacle. Those beads are drawn as fruit, not petals, so the grape-berry primitive already exists in the asset. The failure is structural and chromatic, not that they are flowers: the berries are packed into an upright terminal disc sitting flat on top of a stem tip, when they must hang as long pendulous strings that dangle BELOW their attachment point. Nothing in the image hangs; every element points up or out. Colour is also wrong — the beads are a uniform mauve-pink/orchid, with no green-to-purple-red ripening gradient along a string. So 'nothing dangles' is correct; 'they are flowers' is only half correct. (3) HABIT — the required low windswept spreading form is inverted. Measured bounding box of the drawn plant is x145-299 by y100-326, i.e. 155 wide by 227 tall, aspect w/h = 0.68, against the reference aspect of 1.3. The asset is nearly twice as tall-and-narrow as the spec instead of nearly twice as wide-and-low; it is a narrow upright vase/fountain. I partially dispute the judge on the vine reading, though: the base is NOT herbaceous. There is a genuine solid woody trunk about 25 px wide at the bottom, tapering upward, with four dark vertical bark striations, from which the seven canes split at around y=290. The canes themselves are straight, rigid and upright, not twining, trailing or clinging. So the silhouette reads as a flowering cane shrub of the spirea / butterfly-bush / crepe-myrtle-sucker type, not as a vine and not as a pure herb — the note's 'not a vine' clause is arguably satisfied while its 'stout coastal shrub with rigid round leaves' clause is not. The organism as drawn would be identified by any viewer as a generic pink-flowering garden shrub, with zero coastal or Coccoloba signal. FIX PRIORITY: the leaf is the identity and must be rebuilt first — a handful (6-12, not 60) of large near-circular leathery plates with a heart-shaped notch at the base, held nearly flat and alternate, with bold red-pink primary veins radiating from the petiole and one or two blades tipped orange-red. Second, take the existing berry beads and restring them into two or three long pendulous racemes hanging down and clear of the foliage, graded green at the tip to purple-red at the base. Third, invert the frame: shorten and splay the canes into a low, wind-leaning, wider-than-tall crown so w/h lands near 1.3.

rows.readsAs: a plump brown grub or bumblebee abdomen with two horns — a soft segmented balloon-bug, not a cockroach
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are simply absent. (1) No flat glossy oval wing-covers: the dorsum is an inflated barrel of two ballooning segments ringed by pale outlined hoops, fully three-dimensional and rounded in section, with no tegmina oval and no central seam. (2) No shield-shaped pronotum hiding the head: the largest volume in the whole render IS an exposed spherical head with a visible bead eye on it, which inverts the identity — the roach's head must be concealed under a flat plate. (3) The antennae read but are wrong: two short, thick, rigid dark rods angled forward and upward, not long threadlike whips trailing back over the body. On top of the missing must-reads there is loose geometry: a fan of pale radiating filaments streams off the rear like a shrimp tail-fan or a wing spray, a stray pale outlined arc floats detached above the rear dorsum attached to nothing, and the legs are five unbent parallel sticks (three raked together at the front, two at the back) with no joints, no spines and no visible attachment to a thorax.
rows.fix: Rebuild the body as a single low flat oval: collapse the sphere-plus-barrels into one shallow ellipse whose top surface is nearly planar with a specular glossy highlight, draw a centre seam where the two tegmina overlap, lay a separate darker shield-shaped pronotal plate over the front third so the head is not visible at all from above (delete the bead eye on the dome), delete the rear filament fan and the floating arc, and replace the stick legs with six spined two-segment legs whose femora splay out sideways beyond the shell outline.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 render, then decoded it and re-cropped the subject at 5x, 8x and 10x (whole subject, head, rear, leg band). Subject bbox is x187-313, y173-243 (127x71 px of warm brown on the navy field), plus antennae reaching left to about x=128 and a pale filament spray reaching right past x=320.

UPHELD. Both identity must-reads are genuinely absent, and I could not find them anywhere in the frame at magnification.

(1) NO FLAT GLOSSY OVAL WING-COVERS. The dorsum is a chain of inflated barrel/hoop segments. At 8x the region immediately behind the head resolves as two concentric ring-collars, each drawn with a bright pale outlined rim arc that reads as a hoop seam on a swollen ring — the topline bulges up and over between each seam instead of running as one flat plate. There is no tegmina pair, no long straight wing-suture down the midline, no glossy specular strip. The one thing that could be mistaken for a wing-cover — and which the first judge did not mention — is a lighter-brown ellipse laid over the REAR third of the abdomen (roughly source x=285-315) that carries its own pale rim. It does not deliver the must-read: it is convex and inflated rather than flat, it covers only the last third rather than the whole thorax-to-tail dorsum, it has no suture partner, and it is almost entirely buried under the filament spray. So the finding stands, but a fix should be aware there is already a rear ellipse in the stack to convert, not nothing.

(2) NO SHIELD PRONOTUM; THE HEAD IS THE BIGGEST VOLUME. Correct, and worse than stated. The head is a TWO-part form: a small forward snout nub carrying a dark bead eye with a white specular dot, and behind it a very large smooth brown SPHERE that is the single largest mass in the render. I measured it at roughly 52 px of the 127 px body length, i.e. headFrac ~0.41 against the packet's spec of 0.14 — about 3x over. Nothing overlaps or hides it; the collar rings sit BEHIND it, so the pronotum shield is not merely small, it is on the wrong side of the head. The overall body aspect is 127/71 = 1.79 against the spec 2.5, so the animal is also too short and too deep for a roach.

(3) ANTENNAE — the first judge's description is partly WRONG and should not be copied into the fix. They are not short. They run from about x=128 to the head at x=190, i.e. ~62 px against a 127 px body, roughly half body length, which is a legitimate starting length. The real defects are form, not length: each is a solid tapering ROD 2-3 px thick in the same body brown, dead straight with no curve or whip, and swept forward-and-up off the snout like a pair of horns/tusks. They need to be hair-thin, curved, tapering to a point, longer than the body, and swept back over the dorsum.

(4) LEGS. Confirmed unjointed, but the count and the placement are described imprecisely. I count roughly six straight brown rods, and the problem is the DISTRIBUTION more than the number: four of them crowd into one fan directly beneath and behind the head/neck seam (including one short near-horizontal stub), one or two sit at the far rear near x=305, and the entire midbody is legless. Every rod is uniform-width, perfectly straight, with no femur/tibia bend, no tarsus, no foot, no spines, and the anterior cluster springs from the head-neck junction rather than from a thorax, so they read as whiskers or as a stool's legs.

(5) STRAY GEOMETRY — confirmed, and there are TWO detached grey objects, not one. (a) A grey outlined arc shaped like a suitcase handle floats over the anterior-dorsal abdomen at roughly source x=265-280, y=178-186, standing clear of the topline and attached to nothing. (b) A second, smaller grey outlined rectangle/staple sits near the rear hip at roughly x=300-310, y=218-224, also floating. Both look like leftover outline strokes from a limb or spiracle primitive whose fill never drew.

(6) FILAMENT FAN — confirmed. A dense spray of pale, near-white straight filaments radiates from a single point on the mid-dorsum (about x=238, y=205) and sprays rightward and downward across the whole abdomen, with many strands overshooting the silhouette on the right and bottom edges. Together with a set of short vertical pale bristle strokes across the abdomen it gives the animal a furred/feathered read. This is the loudest single thing in the render and it is what pushes the stranger read toward bee or fishing-fly lure.

STRANGER READ: I agree with grub / fuzzy bee. Specifically it reads as a segmented grub with a bee's fuzz, or a tied fishing fly. A cockroach silhouette — flat, low, one continuous glossy oval deck, head tucked out of sight under a shield, whip antennae trailing back — is not recoverable from this by polish; the dorsum construction, the head volume and the leg rig all have to be rebuilt. FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: A generic gold-tan pointed-oval bait fish with a paddle stuck on the back end; nobody says cod.
rows.defect: At 10x the chin is a bare knife point - no mouth, no jawline and NO BARBEL, which is the one thing that makes a cod a cod. The back carries only TWO rounded lobes, not three separate dorsal fins, and both are drawn behind the body so they read as shadows. The lateral line is a straight pale stroke, not a curved one. The tail is a rounded blocky trapezoid separated from the body point by a dark seam so it reads detached, and a stray thin diagonal stroke runs straight through the tail and out into empty background above and below it - a render artifact. The white eye ring sits half outside the topline.
rows.fix: Draw a single thick barbel hanging down from the chin and split the back into three clearly separated dorsal fins in front of the outline, not behind it.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of their four stated causes are wrong in mechanism and must not be fixed as described. I decoded the PNG and inspected crops at 12x-22x plus a numeric silhouette scan (bg luminance sum ~38; creature spans x=104..337, y=154..231 in the 440x440 canvas; head at RIGHT, tail at LEFT).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. The body is a symmetric pointed lens - a leaf/almond pointed at BOTH ends - with no head mass, no peduncle, and no change of section anywhere. Silhouette top profile: x=200 top=170, x=214..222 top=154 (lobe 1), x=254 top=170 (trough), x=266..270 top=159 (lobe 2), then a clean unbroken run down to the tail at x=145. Bottom profile has a single bulge, bot=231 at x=210..214.

MUST-READ 1, single chin barbel: ABSENT. Confirmed at 22x (crop x=290..345, y=190..220). The lower jaw edge is one clean straight anti-aliased rim converging to a needle point at x=337, y=197. Nothing hangs below it, no stub, no dot, no faint stroke. The judge is right.

MUST-READ 2, three separate dorsal fins: ABSENT - only two, confirmed numerically above. Their description understates it in two ways they should know about. (a) There is also only ONE ventral/anal lobe where cod carries two, so the fin count is 2 dorsal + 1 anal against a required 3 + 2. (b) Both dorsal lobes are low-opacity olive hemispheres painted BEHIND the body silhouette with no ray lines, no membrane and no base attachment - they genuinely read as drop-shadow blobs, not fins, so even the two that exist do not deliver the must-read. Nothing sits between x=145 and x=200, which is exactly where cod's third dorsal belongs.

MUST-READ 3, pale curved lateral line: PRESENT and clearly readable - a bright cream stroke running the full flank at mid-height from the peduncle to just under the eye. The judge did not mention this and did not need to; it is the one must-read that lands.

CORRECTION A - the head is NOT wholly featureless, but the SNOUT is. Their 'no mouth, no jawline' is right at the snout: from the eye forward it is a bare knife wedge. But there IS a gill-cover arc they missed - a dark curved stroke at x=282..286 spanning nearly the full body depth, correctly placed behind the eye. Head fraction measured off it is ~0.23 against a spec of 0.28. So the fix is to build a head IN FRONT of that arc (blunt heavy cod snout, overhanging upper jaw, mouth line, and the barbel), not to add a gill line.

CORRECTION B - the tail is NOT separated by a dark seam. This part of their claim is factually wrong. Sampling rows y=196..199 across x=138..156 shows continuous fill: fin body (57,53,37) -> (75,76,68) -> (112,112,104) -> the body's white rim (145,142,122) -> flank (108,99,64). There are no background pixels between fin and body at the midline; they touch. Background wedges appear only immediately ABOVE (x=144, y=193 = 17,22,28) and BELOW (x=144, y=202 = 9,13,19) the contact, which is presumably what was read as a seam. The real cause of the detached read is different and needs a different fix: the body tapers to a needle point with zero caudal peduncle, so the contact patch is a ~6px-tall hairline, and the body's bright white outline rim runs straight across that junction, drawing a light line between the two masses. Fix = give it a peduncle and break the rim at the join; do not go hunting for a seam that is not there.

CORRECTION C - the stray stroke is TWO strokes, not one, and neither runs through the fin. They are the two outermost caudal rays drawn past the fin outline into empty background: a faint diagonal from ~(110,165) to (121,176) off the fin's upper-front corner, and its mirror from ~(119,219) to (110,230) off the lower-front corner. Luminance ~50 against ~38 background, so they read as faint ghost whiskers hanging in space at the fin's leading corners. The fin fill itself is a rounded-corner slab x=104..145, y=177..218 (41x41) with interior spokes converging to the apex. Note that blockiness alone is not the defect - cod's caudal IS truncate/squared; the defects are the unclipped rays, the missing peduncle, and the fin being nearly as deep as the body.

UNREPORTED DEFECT - the eye. It is a white sclera ring with a dark pupil placed ON the topline, and roughly its upper third protrudes OUTSIDE the silhouette into the background (top profile dips to 183 at x=314..320 against 186..192 on either side). It reads as a bead stuck onto the back edge, not an eye set into a head.

BAND. Two of the three must-reads are absent, and they are precisely the two that separate a cod from any other fish; the chin barbel is the single diagnostic feature of the species. With a needle snout, no mouth, no jaw, an eye riding on the outline and two shadow-blob fins, the asset reads as a generic pointed leaf-fish or a needlefish, not Gadus morhua. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: A generic grey pointed-oval fish; reads closer to a small silver minnow than a haddock.
rows.defect: The dark thumbprint blotch above the pectoral - the single feature that identifies a haddock - is completely absent; the only dark area is the same generic mid-flank shading blob that Cod and Pollock also carry. The lateral line is drawn PALE WHITE, the opposite of the required black line. The first dorsal is a low rounded ellipse half hidden behind the body, not tall and not pointed, and there are only two dorsal lobes instead of three. Head is the same mouthless knife point as the other two, and the eye ring straddles the topline.
rows.fix: Paint a hard dark thumbprint blotch on the shoulder just above the pectoral fin and switch the lateral line stroke to black.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 4x-9x zoom plus a numeric silhouette/topline trace. The FAIL stands, and every substantive part of the original claim checks out, but two details need correcting and one large defect the first judge did not name is arguably the biggest one.

MUST-READ 1 - dark thumbprint blotch above the pectoral: GENUINELY ABSENT. I went looking for it in the places a judge could miss. The pectoral is a dark radiating ray-fan set low on the flank at mid-body (orig px approx x 240-275, y 190-210) with one long dark pointed spar trailing aft. The flank directly above it (x 245-280, y 165-190) carries nothing but the diamond scale texture - no oval, no smudge, no patch at any size. The only dark mark anywhere on the shoulder is a thin CURVED STROKE arcing from the topline down and forward just behind the eye (approx x 285-300); that is the gill-cover / operculum line, it is a line not a blob, and it is anterior to the pectoral rather than above it. It is not a mis-placed blotch. Confirmed: the entire flank is free of any dark marking.

MUST-READ 2 - black lateral line: PRESENT BUT INVERTED IN TONE, exactly as claimed. A distinct near-white / pale-lavender stroke runs from just behind the eye straight back to the caudal peduncle at eye height, clearly LIGHTER than the mid-grey flank it sits on. Additional correction the first judge missed: it is also drawn dead straight and horizontal, whereas the haddock's lateral line arches noticeably high over the pectoral. So this feature is wrong in two ways - tone and path. As drawn it is indistinguishable from the 'pale curved lateral line' spec'd for Cod in the same packet, which destroys the one marking meant to separate the two.

MUST-READ 3 - tall pointed first dorsal, three dorsals in all: FAILS, and the topline trace makes it exact. Scanning the first lit row per column gives exactly TWO humps on the back: a rear lobe peaking at y=145 (x 216-219) and a front lobe peaking at y=151 (x 264-267), with the contour falling back to y=163 between them and y=180+ toward the snout. Both are low rounded domes drawn as flat ellipses set BEHIND the body plane, so each is half-occluded by the back. The fish faces right, so the FIRST dorsal is the x=264 lobe - and it is the SHORTER of the two (151 vs 145), i.e. the opposite of the spec'd tall pointed leading dorsal. Two dorsals, not three; neither pointed. One correction worth recording so a fixer does not miscount: a third rounded lobe of the same shape hangs BELOW the belly at mid-body (the anal fin), so a quick count of 'three lobes' is reachable - the DORSAL count is definitively two.

UNNAMED AND LARGER: the silhouette is the wrong organism before any marking is considered. Luminance bbox is 224 x 93 px = aspect 2.41 against a spec'd 3.5 - roughly 31% too short. The outline is a symmetric lens/almond, pointed at the snout AND pointed again at the peduncle, with maximum depth dead centre and no separation between head and trunk. That reads as a generic deep-bodied panfish/leaf shape, not a gadid, which needs a long tapering fusiform trunk and a distinct head. Also, the eye (white ring, dark pupil) is jammed onto the dorsal silhouette edge near the snout tip rather than set inside the head.

Net: all three must-reads fail, plus the body proportion is off by a third. Nothing here identifies a haddock and little identifies a cod-like fish at all. FAIL upheld. Fix priority: (1) re-proportion to a 3.5 fusiform trunk with a distinct head, (2) add the third dorsal and rebuild the first as a tall pointed triangle standing clear of the back rather than an ellipse behind it, (3) add the dark thumbprint blotch on the flank above the pectoral, (4) re-tone the lateral line to black and give it the arch over the pectoral.

rows.readsAs: An elongated olive-green fish with a pale side stripe and a forked tail - plausibly a pollock to a fisherman, just 'a fish' to a stranger.
rows.defect: The olive-green back and the pale lateral line are genuinely present and legible, but the fin architecture and the jaw are not. The snout is a symmetric knife point with no mouth drawn at all, so the protruding lower jaw is absent. There are two rounded dorsal lobes rather than three separate dorsals, and one anal lobe rather than two, and every one of them is drawn behind the body outline so it half disappears. The white eye ring is punched through the topline and sits partly outside the silhouette.
rows.fix: Cut the underslung lower jaw into the snout so it juts past the upper lip, and draw three dorsals plus two anals as separate fins in front of the body outline.

rows.readsAs: a generic green coiled cartoon snake
rows.defect: The blotching is INVERTED - pale washed-out light spots scattered over olive instead of the required dark oval blotches, so the signature anaconda pattern is absent. The eye is a huge lateral white lollipop with a vertical slit set on the SIDE of the head, not the small eye set high on top of the skull the reference demands, and no nostrils read at all. Body is reasonably thick but is a constant-diameter tube with no muscular swell.
rows.fix: Repaint the pattern as dark olive-black oval blotches (darker than the base) and move the eye and nostrils onto the dorsal surface of the head so both are visible from above.

rows.readsAs: a plain brown coiled cartoon snake
rows.defect: The saddle blotches are present only as vague soft brown smudges with no defined saddle edges, and because the tail is buried inside the coil the required reddening toward the tail never reads. The head is the shared smooth oval - no heavy arrow shape, no widened jaw, and no dark eye stripe anywhere. The body does not taper.
rows.fix: Give the saddles hard-edged dark outlines that grow rust-red along a visible tail that exits the coil, and rebuild the head as a broad arrow with a dark stripe running from eye to jaw angle.

rows.readsAs: a plain sand-coloured rope, no species at all
rows.defect: The net-like geometric pattern that IS the identity of this animal is completely absent - the body is a flat unmarked khaki tube with only faint tonal shading, so there is nothing on it to name. No heat-sensing pit row along the lips is visible; the lip line is blank. The coils do not overlap heavily, they lie in one flat spiral doughnut.
rows.fix: Paint an actual reticulated net - dark chain-link outlines enclosing pale diamond centres - across the entire body, and add a visible row of dark pits along the upper and lower lip.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but two of the three stated causes need correcting and the judge missed three further defects. WHAT I SAW at 1:1 and at 4x/12x crops with a 3x contrast stretch (440x440 canvas):

(1) PATTERN — 'entirely absent' is not quite right, and the correction matters for the fix. A marking layer DOES exist: under a 3x levels stretch of the coil field there are perhaps six isolated, soft-edged CIRCULAR blobs (a dark one on the upper-left coil at ~(105,155) src px, two more on the right coil at ~(255,215) and ~(258,240), a bright oval smear on the lower-left coil), plus a few broad soft transverse tonal bands. At native contrast they are invisible — measured body luminance over the crop runs min 40 / mean 91 / max 150, and the blob delta is buried well under the ambient shading amplitude. So the defect is not 'no markings drawn' but 'the marking layer is sparse round DOTS at near-zero contrast'. The fix is not merely 'raise contrast' — the geometry is wrong too: reticulated python needs a continuous dark-outlined MESH of pale polygonal cells tiling the whole dorsum, not scattered spots. Nothing net-like, geometric, or chained is present at any contrast.

(2) SURFACE — the judge's 'unmarked khaki tube with only faint tonal shading' badly understates what is actually there and mis-describes the dominant read. The body is not smooth: it carries a dense, high-contrast, per-segment TRANSVERSE RIB running the FULL circumference of the tube, up over the dorsal midline and down the far side. Ventral scutes belong only on the belly; wrapping them all the way round makes the whole animal read as a corrugated vacuum-cleaner hose, which is the single loudest signal in the image and is actively wrong, not merely missing. Any fix must strip the ribbing off the dorsum (keep it only on the belly-facing arcs of the coil) before adding pattern, or the mesh will fight the corrugation.

(3) HEAT PITS — the judge is right that no pit row reads, and it is worse than stated: there is NO MOUTH LINE AT ALL. At 12x the head is a perfectly smooth tan lozenge — no jaw line, no lip line, no labial scales, therefore no surface for a pit row to sit on. Related: the red forked tongue does not emerge from anything. It starts in empty background roughly 4-5 px clear of the snout tip and floats detached from the head.

(4) MISSED BY THE JUDGE — EYE. The eye is grossly oversized (roughly a third of the head width) and rendered as a bright WHITE sclera ring around a black vertical slit pupil. The reference row specifies eyes: small. As drawn it reads as a cartoon gecko/lizard eye, not a python's small dark bead, and it is the second-loudest signal after the ribbing.

(5) MISSED BY THE JUDGE — SKULL. The head is no wider than the neck it sits on: a narrow rounded lozenge with no temporal flare. Python and boa alike need a heavy arrow/wedge skull distinctly broader than the neck; there is no widening whatsoever.

(6) MISSED BY THE JUDGE — TAIL. The tail tip, tucked inside the inner coil near src (165,190), does not taper. It terminates in a blunt rounded knob at full body diameter with a small swelling just behind the end, and the ribbing stops there leaving it smooth. It reads as a cut hose end.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY RIGHT (so it is not destroyed in the fix): the vertical slit pupil is correct for a python; the posture is a genuine coil with real overlap (the outer coil passes over the rear body and the tail tucks inside the ring), and the tube is thick enough that 'heavy-bodied overlapping coils' — the third must-read — is arguably satisfied. So 1 of 3 must-reads present, 2 absent.

BAND: FAIL, not POLISH. Both identity must-reads (net-like geometric pattern, labial pit row) are unreadable, and the two loudest features in the frame — full-circumference hose corrugation and an oversized white cartoon eye — are positively wrong rather than merely thin. 'Sand-coloured rope' is close but should be 'ribbed sand-coloured hose'; the corrugation, not the colour, is what stops it naming a species.

rows.readsAs: the same coiled cartoon snake as the other three, in gold
rows.defect: Reference says crawling at aspect 3.5 and the render is the identical coiled doughnut used for the other three, only with a slightly fatter tube - the short stubby proportion never reads because the animal is wound into a ring of the same overall length. The blunt wedge snout is absent (same pointed lozenge head as the rest), the eyes are the same big lateral lollipops rather than tiny upward-facing dots, and the abruptly blunt stub tail is hidden inside the coil so the defining head-and-tail-look-alike trait is invisible.
rows.fix: Redraw it uncoiled and crawling, half-buried in sand, as a short fat sausage with a shovel-wedge snout, pinprick eyes on TOP of the head, and a blunt stub tail clearly visible at the far end.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and the underlying defect is worse than stated. What I saw at full size and at 6-14x crops of the head, the snout, the coil interior and the silhouette edge:

POSTURE (the judge did not name this, and it is the largest miss): the reference row says posture: crawling. The asset is drawn as a closed torus doughnut coil, topologically identical to the three coiled siblings in this same batch. It is not a crawling pose at all -- there is no ground-line body axis, no serpentine track, just a ring.

ONE CHASSIS -- CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT. Non-background bounding boxes: Sand_Boa 289x152 (aspect 1.91), Boa 278x147 (1.89), Python 275x136 (2.02), Anaconda 269x141 (1.91). All four occupy the same footprint within 5%. Head is at the lower right in all four, neck sweeps left along the bottom, coil closes over the top, red forked tongue exits at the same angle with the same fork geometry.

CORRECTION 1 -- "only a slightly fatter tube" is too generous; the tube is not meaningfully fatter at all. Vertical scanline runs at x=200 give Sand_Boa upper-coil 56px / lower-coil 67px; Boa 52/73; Anaconda 56/68; Python 38/60. So the Sand Boa is 8% fatter than the Boa on the upper coil and 8% THINNER on the lower coil -- a wash. Its coil hole is actually WIDER than the Boa's (24px vs 21px at x=180), the opposite of what a stubbier, fatter body would produce. It is dimensionally identical to the Anaconda, which is spec'd at aspect 6 and "thick as a thigh". Aspect (3.5 vs 6 vs 7) is exerting essentially zero influence on this renderer. mustRead "thick stubby cylindrical body" therefore does not read: it reads as a normal-gauge boa rope wound into a ring.

CORRECTION 2 -- the eyes are not "lollipops" / dots. At 6x the eye is a large white almond sclera containing a black VERTICAL-SLIT pupil, roughly 24% of head length, sitting mid-height on the lateral face. It is form-for-form the same stamp as the Boa's and the Python's -- I compared the three head crops at identical window and scale and they are interchangeable. The judge's conclusion (not tiny, not upward-facing) is right; the description of the shape was wrong. Real sand boa eyes are pinhead-sized and set on the TOP surface of the skull; nothing here is dorsal.

CORRECTION 3 -- "no blunt wedge snout" is correct. The head is the shared lance/almond ellipse tapering to a soft point, same as Boa and Python, only fractionally blunter at the tip. Partial credit where due: there IS one small feature the judge may not have seen -- a soft round darker blotch low on the jowl behind the snout. It is NOT a nostril: it sits mid-jaw, far back from the tip, and reads as a dermal spot (the same spot family that appears scattered over the coil). It does not rescue the snout.

CORRECTION 4 -- "the blunt stub tail is buried inside the coil" is right but understates it. I could find NO tail terminus anywhere in the image. I traced the inner-coil tube into the doughnut hole and cropped it at 14x: the tube simply passes under the outer coil and vanishes with no end cap, no taper, no stub. Crucially, the Python in this same batch DOES render a visible hooked, tapering tail tip poking into its coil hole at the equivalent location -- so the engine can draw a terminus, and the Sand Boa's is fully occluded rather than merely small. mustRead "very short abruptly blunt tail" is absent, not just faint.

MARKINGS: plain sand-tan with faint pale speckles and heavy uniform scale-hatching. That is the one thing arguably right for the species, and it is also the only thing distinguishing this file from Boa.png.

SCORE: three of three must-reads absent, posture spec violated, and the asset is a recolour of the family chassis. FAIL stands.

FIX DIRECTION: this one must leave the torus. Draw it low and horizontal in a shallow S or straight crawl at aspect ~3.5 with the body a near-constant cylinder; cap BOTH ends bluntly and expose the tail end fully so head and tail look almost interchangeable per the note; replace the almond head with a short wedge whose widest point is just behind the jaw and whose tip is squared off; shrink the eye to a pinprick and move it to the dorsal surface so it reads as a dot on top of the skull, not an oval on the side; drop the vertical-slit sclera stamp entirely for this species.

rows.readsAs: a kiwi, or a grey duckling with an orange carrot for a bill
rows.defect: The identity feature is absent: the bill is a dead-straight orange cone, not a slender strongly decurved crimson bill — it has no curvature whatsoever and reads as a carrot glued to the face. Plumage is mid-grey with heavy pale mottling and a grey scribble texture, so the glossy all-black requirement is not met; the bird is the lightest thing in the batch. The red legs are the only must-read present, and even those are two disembodied footprints floating in the air below the belly with no leg connecting them to the body. Silhouette is the shared legless egg with no neck.
rows.fix: Redraw the bill as a long thin arc curving smoothly downward through about 30 degrees in saturated crimson, and darken the body to near-black with a blue-violet gloss highlight so the red bill and red legs are the only warm marks on the bird.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are wrong or imprecise and the fix will miss if made against them. WHAT I ACTUALLY SAW (440x440, read at 1x then re-cropped and nearest-neighbour upscaled 5x over head, feet and tail, plus pixel sampling): a plump, neckless, round-bodied dark bird with a long straight red-orange spike bill, near-black wing band and tail spike, a slate-grey speckled body, and two flat red toe-clusters at the very bottom of the belly. Silhouette bbox x100-335 y144-283, aspect 1.69 (packet asks 1.7 — the aspect spec is met, but only because the 60px bill pads the width; the body mass alone is close to circular).

MUSTREAD 1 — 'slender curved red bill': FAILS on curve, and the judge's description of it is right in effect but should be stated precisely so the fix is aimable. I scanned the bill edges every 4px from tip to base: top edge runs y=167 (tip, x=104) to y=162 (base, x=164); bottom edge y=167 to y=171. The MIDLINE is y=166-167 at every single sample from x=104 to x=164 — i.e. it is a perfectly symmetric isoceles wedge with a dead-horizontal axis. Zero decurve, and zero asymmetry between culmen and gonys, which is what would sell a decurved bill even at this size. Length ~60px against a ~41px head diameter (~1.5x head), which is actually the correct chough proportion — so do NOT shorten it, only bend it. Hue is #E2451C, a vermilion ORANGE-red, not the crimson/scarlet the species needs; the judge calling it 'orange' is fair but it is not a flat orange, it is red-orange. Slender: yes, that part lands.

MUSTREAD 2 — 'bright red legs': the judge's stated cause here is FACTUALLY WRONG and would send the fix in the wrong direction. They are NOT 'two footprints hovering unattached in the air below the belly.' I measured the vertical gap between the lowest body pixel and the first red pixel for every 5px column across the foot zone: gap = 0 at x=215, 220, 225, 230, 235, 240 (body bottom y=266, first red y=267 — flush, contiguous). The only non-zero gaps (8-15px at x=200-210) are the outer TOE tips of the near foot splaying down-forward away from the body, which is normal foot geometry, not floating. The real defect is the exact opposite of 'hovering': there is NO LEG AT ALL. No tarsus, no tibia, no ground clearance — two red three-toed foot shapes are stamped flat onto the underside of the belly, sitting directly in the cast-shadow ellipse. A species whose identity line is 'bright RED LEGS' shows no leg segment whatsoever, only red feet. Colour of the feet is #D83A12/#992A0F, again orange-red rather than crimson. Fix = grow visible red tarsi and lift the body off the ground, not 'reattach floating feet'.

MUSTREAD 3 — 'glossy all-black crow-like plumage': FAILS, and the judge is right in substance but the colour call needs correcting. The body is not 'mid-grey' — it is dark slate blue-grey, sampled #353841 at mid-flank, #363942 upper back, #23252B lower belly (~20-22% luminance), overlaid with dense pale flecking and a light rim highlight peaking at #717884. Crucially the asset IS two-tone and the judge missed that half: the wing band, the rear wing and the tail spike ARE effectively black (#080D13 / #0F1013). So the failure is not 'the whole bird is grey' — it is that the black is confined to the wing-band and tail while the entire flank/breast/rump mass that dominates the read is grey and speckled. Against 'all-black glossy' that still fails, and the speckling actively pushes it toward a barred/mottled ground bird.

ORGANISM READ: I agree it reads kiwi, and I can name why beyond the judge's list — three things stack. (a) The long straight horizontal probe bill. (b) No neck at all: the head is a plain sphere set directly onto the shoulder mass with no visible neck column or chough head-carriage.
