(c) No legs plus a near-circular plump body means zero ground clearance and a rounded rump; the tail is only a short dark pointed spike projecting rearward at y~230 with a few sparse feather strokes under it, so from any distance the bird reads as tail-less. Long straight probe bill + no neck + no legs + round tail-less body IS the kiwi gestalt. Only the red foot colour argues for a chough, and it argues weakly because it is orange-red on feet rather than crimson on legs.

BAND: FAIL. Two of three defining must-reads (curved bill, all-black plumage) are absent, the third (red legs) is half-present as feet-only, and the resulting silhouette is a different order of bird.

FAMILY NOTE for the chassis question: this body is the same round speckled egg-mass with an arcing dark wing band, a spike tail and stamped-on feet that the other corvid cards in batch-001 will need checking against; the corvid-defining feature here is being carried entirely by bill shape and accent colour, which is exactly the one-chassis failure mode.

rows.readsAs: a Common Blackbird, or a charcoal duckling — a yellow-billed thrush, not a crow
rows.defect: Wrong organism. The bill is bright yellow-ochre; a crow's bill is black, and a dark bird with a yellow bill is the diagnostic read of a Eurasian Blackbird. It is also a short blunt triangle rather than a stout deep pointed crow bill. The plumage is charcoal-grey with grey mottled scribble, not all-black glossy. The square-tipped tail is absent — what is there is a thin grey spike tapering to a point off the right flank, in a different colour from the body. Feet are two yellow prints floating unattached under the belly and the body is a neckless egg.
rows.fix: Make the bill black, deep at the base and clearly longer than the head is wide, and rebuild the tail as a body-coloured fan of even-length feathers with a flat square end.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of the stated causes are wrong and the biggest cause was not stated at all. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440, pixel-sampled): a fat, near-spherical charcoal ovoid with a small ball head on effectively no neck, a bright golden-yellow bill, bright golden-yellow toes, and a near-black pointed tail spike. Sampled values: bill #E0B13C (224,177,60); toes #C9A24F (201,162,79); body #292B35 (41,43,53) with pale scribble highlights at #3C3F4B (60,63,75); tail #0F1014 (15,16,20) and #090D13 at the tip; backdrop #05060C (5,6,12).

MUST-READ 1, all-black glossy plumage - ABSENT. The body is a matte blue-charcoal (#292B35) covered in a pale grey hatched scribble that reads as mottling/streaking, not gloss. The only bright value on the bird is a thin cool rim-light along the top of the head and back. So the judge is right on this point.

MUST-READ 2, stout straight pointed bill - the judge described this INCORRECTLY. It is NOT 'a short blunt triangle.' Zoomed 11x, it is a fairly LONG (roughly 0.6 of head width), SHARPLY POINTED straight wedge with a clean straight culmen, a clean gonys line, and a fine tip - the geometry is closer to a starling/thrush bill than to anything blunt. The two real defects are (a) it is a flat 2D triangle with zero depth, no curve to the culmen, no nostril bristles, so it never reads 'stout,' and (b) it is coloured brilliant golden-yellow, and a crow's bill is jet black. The colour, not the length, is what breaks the organism.

MUST-READ 3, square-tipped tail - ABSENT, and again described with the wrong direction. The tail is a thin wedge that tapers to a needle point, correct - but it is NOT a 'grey spike lighter than the body.' Do not fix this by recolouring the tail; fix the attachment, the taper and the texture.

5) BILL — CLAIM CORRECT. x=77-106 (~30 px), a small triangular gold wedge, rgb ~222,175,60. A magpie bill must be heavy, straight, deep-based and BLACK. Torso-only aspect (220 wide / ~67 tall at the deepest, x=254) is 3.3 against a spec aspect of 5. So the judge is RIGHT and the number is right: the tail is a flat triangular wedge whose ventral edge runs as one straight diagonal from the hip up to a bluntly truncated point, with zero thickness, zero taper stages and no lateral compression. This is the identity-defining must-read for a crocodilian and it is absent — everything about the read (stocky torso, stub tail, corrugated flank, sprawl) collapses into salamander/newt/gecko-toy, which I agree with.

CORRECTION 1 — 'no jaw seam, no teeth' is WRONG on both halves. There IS a jaw seam: a continuous dark mouth line that runs the full length of the head from the snout tip (x~112, y~207) back to the rear of the skull (x~170), dipping slightly then turning UP at the rear corner. That upturn is what the judge read as a 'smiley', but a real crocodilian mouth line in profile does exactly that. It is under-contrasted and too smooth (it should be a shallow sinusoid with a visible lip scallop), not missing. And 'no teeth' is NOT a defect — the reference row explicitly requires 'teeth hidden when the mouth shuts', and the note says a crocodile, not an alligator, shows the fourth tooth. Do not add teeth to this asset.

CORRECTION 2 — the judge missed the single strongest correct cue and it must be preserved through any fix. The eye is a large amber iris with a hard VERTICAL SLIT PUPIL, mounted on a raised dome turret that sits proud of the top of the skull (turret centre ~x=152, y=173, dome rising ~6px above the cranial line). That is textbook crocodilian eye placement and it reads at full size. Keep it.

CORRECTION 3 — 'the scute rows are not on the back' is only half true. There IS a dorsal element on the back: a dark olive band tracks the whole topline from x~176 to the tail tip, and over the rear third and along the tail's dorsal edge it carries a row of ~20 fine sawtooth serrations (clearly visible x=280..325) that genuinely are a scute crest. The real defects are (a) the serrations are ~1-2px, far too fine to read as armour at any size, (b) over the front two thirds the band degenerates into a smooth ruled strip with a bright steel-grey specular highlight that reads as metal trim / a zipper pull rather than keratin, and (c) the detachment the judge described is real and worse than described — at roughly x=176..205, y=168..182 a dark olive lozenge with a kinked notch in its underside sits ABOVE the body outline separated from it by background pixels, and its forward end terminates in empty air ahead of the shoulder, while the steel highlight line passes underneath it at a different angle. That is an off-model floating shape, not just a misplaced band.

CONFIRMED — the flank pinstripes. ~25 evenly ruled vertical lines of uniform width and spacing run the full depth of the flank from topline to belly, front to hip. They read as accordion corrugation / a bellows, not as transverse osteoderm rows (which should be a small number of broad, raised, keeled blocks with cast shadow, concentrated dorsally and fading before the belly).

NOSTRIL — judge's placement description is slightly off. It is not 'high on the cheek'; it is a dark oval at MID height on the side of the snout, ~20% back from the tip (centre ~x=127, y=196), i.e. it reads as a side-facing ear/blowhole. An alligator's nostrils are at the very tip of the snout, on the dorsal surface, on a raised naris bulge.

OTHER — head is fairly called a rounded-rectangle slab: constant depth from tip to skull with no dorsal taper and no step behind the eyes. Feet are actually decent (splayed multi-toed pads on a sprawling stance) but the fore and hind limbs are the same smooth tapered tube with no elbow/knee articulation and near-identical mass; a crocodilian's hind limb is markedly heavier and longer.

FIX ORDER: (1) extend the tail to at least 55% of total length with real thickness at the base and a laterally-compressed taper, (2) delete the floating shoulder lozenge and the steel specular strip, (3) rebuild the dorsal armour as a small number of broad shadowed keels, (4) move the vertical flank ruling off the belly, (5) reseat the nostril at the snout tip. Keep the slit-pupil eye turret and keep the mouth shut with no teeth.

rows.readsAs: a green cartoon salamander -- pixel-for-pixel the Alligator in another colour
rows.defect: The bony ridge between the eyes -- the one feature that separates a caiman from an alligator -- is not there. What stands in for it is a single thin dark stroke drawn BEHIND and below the eye on the cheek, which reads as a scratch or a crack in the skin, and it is placed nowhere near between the eyes. The heavily scuted armoured back and neck are absent too: the armour is vertical pinstriping on the flank plus the same detached dark trim band floating off the topline. The whole silhouette -- slab head, nostril dot, smiley mouth, slit eye, corrugated torso, mid-torso forelimb, nub tail -- is identical to the Alligator card with only the hue changed, so the two cannot be told apart.
rows.fix: Build a distinct caiman skull: raise a visible bony bridge across the top of the snout between the eye sockets so it breaks the dorsal profile, and armour the neck with a separate band of raised nuchal scutes the Alligator does not get.
rows.verifyWhy:
I read the full-size PNG, then re-read six magnified crops (head at 6x, eye region at 16x, topline strip at 8x, body at 5x, feet at 8x) and ran a numeric top-edge profile against Alligator.png. The FAIL stands, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and one is understated.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Strict lateral profile, facing left. Head is one broad rounded blob with a blunt squared-off snout tip, a small dark oval nostril dot near the tip, and a single closed curved mouth line that arcs up into a smile with NO teeth showing. One large amber vertical-slit eye sits on a raised darker-green turret that bulges above the skull outline. Body-plus-tail is a single flat trapezoidal slab: straight-ish rise from the neck, a shallow peak around 60% of the length, then a taper to a sharp point at the tail tip, with no waist and no join between body and tail. The slab is filled with ~28 evenly spaced thin vertical pinstripes running its full height. Floating just above the dorsal edge is a detached horizontal ribbon (dark upper edge, white/grey highlight beneath) that starts at the neck and dies out around mid-back; in places background shows through the gap between it and the body. Four straight tapered tubes for legs, splayed outward, each ending in a small flat toe-fan. Belly underside is a hard-edged polygon with a V-notch at mid-body.

MUST-READ 1, 'bony ridge between the eyes' — ABSENT, and their DESCRIPTION OF THE MARK IS WRONG. There is exactly one extra mark on this head that the Alligator does not have: a short dark-green tapered bar, roughly 13px at native scale, with soft rounded ends. It is NOT 'behind and below the eye on the cheek'. It sits ANTERIOR to the eye — in front of it and slightly below — on the dorsal/loreal surface of the snout, angled about 25 degrees down-and-forward, pointing toward the snout tip. Direction and placement are actually a defensible location for a preorbital/interorbital ridge, so the artist was aiming at the right anatomy. It fails anyway for a different reason than the judge gave: it is rendered as a flat shadow-only stroke with no lit edge, no highlight, and zero effect on the skull silhouette (the top-of-snout outline in front of the eye is a dead-smooth line). A ridge that casts no relief and breaks no contour reads as a scratch or a crack in the surface, which is what the judge saw even though they put it on the wrong side of the eye. Compounding it: in pure lateral view only one eye exists, so 'between the eyes' has no readable stage — the fix has to be a bump in the dorsal skull contour, not a line on the flank of the snout.

MUST-READ 2, 'heavily scuted armoured back and neck' — ABSENT, judge correct. The vertical pinstripes are flank striping, not scutes: they run top-to-bottom across the whole slab including the belly zone, they are uniform pencil lines with no width variation, and none of them touches or deforms the dorsal edge. The floating trim ribbon is evidently the intended osteoderm row, but it is detached from the back with visible background between, it is smooth with no keels or serration, it covers only the front ~55% and stops dead, and it never reaches the neck at all — the neck between skull and shoulder is bare flat green. So the back reads as a corrugated-metal panel, not armour, and the neck reads as unarmoured.

MUST-READ 3, 'broad blunt snout with the teeth hidden when shut' — PRESENT and readable. Snout is genuinely broad and rounded, mouth is a single closed curve, no teeth. This is the one must-read that lands, and the packet note explicitly allows it to look like an alligator's, so it cannot carry the identity by itself.

CHASSIS. The 'pixel-for-pixel the Alligator with the hue changed' claim is very nearly literal and I verified it numerically rather than by eye. I extracted the top-edge y for every column x=100..340 in both PNGs: the two profiles are the same curve, with Caiman sitting a near-constant 2-3px lower — a uniform ~4% downscale consistent with aspect 4.5 vs the Alligator's 5, not a redraw. Every landmark matches, including the small step-notch in the topline behind the skull (Alligator x=171, Caiman x=173, i.e. the same feature phase-shifted by the scale factor). Head blob, nostril dot, smile arc, eye turret, eye slit, the trapezoid slab, the pinstripe count and spacing, the floating trim ribbon with its highlight, the four tube legs and toe-fans are all shared. One correction: in the low-res view the Alligator's darker purple made its dorsal band look serrated where the Caiman's did not; at 8x that is a hue artefact — neither topline is serrated, both are equally smooth. So the two are not distinguishable as species by anything except colour plus one 13px scratch, and the family-level question the packet asks must be answered YES: these crocodilians are one chassis in different hues.

FIX DIRECTION: give the Caiman a real interorbital crest that breaks the dorsal skull contour as a lit bump between the eye turret and the snout (silhouette change, not a stroke), and replace the detached trim ribbon with a keeled scute row that is attached to the back, carries individual raised bumps that notch the topline, and continues forward onto the neck and back onto the tail.

rows.readsAs: a crocodilian -- but most strangers would say alligator
rows.defect: The double-crested laterally flattened tail is absent: the tail is the family's short blunt cone with a single row of small bumps, about a third of body length, with no lateral flattening and no paired crest. The snout is not narrow or V-shaped either -- it is a deep, blunt, rounded slab barely different from the Alligator card, so the alligator-versus-crocodile call goes the wrong way. Dorsal osteoderm bumps along the back are the one clear win here.

rows.readsAs: two unrelated blobs - a spotted tan egg with four pins, and a separate curled grub next to it
rows.defect: The render is broken: there is a clear black GAP between the head oval and the abdomen, so the animal is in two disconnected pieces. Worse, the two white eye dots sit on the ABDOMEN (upper right of the tail unit, next to a black wedge), not on the head - the head carries only a single stray speck at the antenna root. None of the must-reads are present: the body is opaque solid tan, not translucent; the limbs are four bare straight pins, not a row of leaf-like paddles; and the tail ends in a downward-pointing blade fan tucked under the body, not a slender abdomen with a forked tail fan.

rows.verifyWhy:
I tried to refute this and could not. Measured on the 440x440 PNG, the render is TWO fully disconnected tan bodies. I scanned every row from y=160 to y=300 across x=258..300: a true-background channel runs the entire vertical extent, 19px wide at y=190, narrowing only to 4px at y=200-205, and it NEVER closes. So the 'clear black gap' claim is CONFIRMED and is not an artifact of low-res viewing.

WHAT THE TWO PIECES ACTUALLY ARE (the judge described this wrong): the right-hand piece is NOT a bare abdomen with eyes stuck on it. At 8x zoom it is a complete little shrimp in its own right - a smooth un-segmented round HEAD BULB at the top carrying two dark spherical eyes with white specular highlights (one riding just off the top-right edge on a short stalk, one seated on the bulb), a dark V-shaped rostrum/mandible chevron between them, then a curl of 5-6 clearly ringed abdominal segments running down, ending in a fan of 3-4 darker blade lobes plus a thin dark stalk. The eyes are placed CORRECTLY relative to that piece's own head. The real defect is not 'eyes migrated onto the abdomen' - it is that the generator emitted two separate head-bearing assemblies into one frame. Any fix aimed at 'move the eyes forward onto the head' would be aimed at the wrong bug; the bug is that head/trunk and abdomen/tail are laid out as two independent bodies with a background gap between them.

WHAT THE LEFT PIECE IS: a speckled, opaque, egg-shaped oval (~1.3:1) with mottled darker blotches, two long brown whip antennae sweeping far left plus a shorter third whip, FOUR straight uniform-width brown pin legs hanging dead-vertical from its underside onto a hard ground-contact shadow ellipse. At 20x zoom its only 'eye' is a single ~2px white square floating in the BLACK just OUTSIDE the tan silhouette, with no dark eyeball behind it - a detached specular speck, not an eye. Judge's 'the head carries only a stray speck' is CONFIRMED and if anything understated (the speck is not even on the body).

MUST-READ CHECK against 'translucent segmented body with a row of leaf-like paddle limbs / two stalked eyes on the head / slender abdomen ending in a forked tail fan':
- Translucency: ABSENT, confirmed. Both masses are 100% opaque saturated salmon-tan with a rim highlight and a broad specular sheen. Nothing reads through the body; it is painted like solid flesh, not glass.
- Row of leaf-like paddle limbs: ABSENT, confirmed on the left piece - four bare sticks of constant width, no blade, no taper, no beating wave, and only four rather than a dense row. PARTIAL CORRECTION to the judge: leaf/blade-like lobes DO exist in the image, but they are all bunched at the tail end of the right piece as the fan, not distributed as a row along a trunk.
- Two stalked eyes on the head: technically present on the right piece's head bulb, but useless - they belong to the wrong half of a broken animal, and the piece bearing the antennae and legs has none.
- Slender abdomen with forked tail fan: PARTIAL CORRECTION to the judge, who said this is 'a downward blade fan tucked under the body NOT a slender abdomen with a forked fan'. There genuinely IS a segmented abdomen on the right piece and it genuinely DOES terminate in a fan. What is wrong is that the fan is an asymmetric 3-4 lobe spray pointing back/down-right under the curl (reads as a swimmeret cluster) rather than a symmetric bilobed uropod fork, and the abdomen is short and stubby rather than slender.

DEFECTS THE JUDGE MISSED: (1) aspect - the reference asks 3.5; the full ink bbox measures 196x100 = 2.0, and neither individual piece is elongate (left ~1.3:1 oval, right a stubby curl). (2) posture - the reference says 'swimming' and the note says 'swims upside down with no carapace over the trunk'; this render is planted on a hard drop-shadow ellipse on four stiff vertical pins, reading as a standing terrestrial animal, right-side-up.

WHAT IT READS AS: a speckled tick/mite standing on four pins with two long whip antennae, sitting next to an unrelated small curled prawn. Two organisms, neither of which is a brine shrimp. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a pale grub or witchetty larva with long whiskers
rows.defect: The glassy colourless body and the long sweeping antennae do read. But the abdomen curls FORWARD and DOWN so the tail fan ends up underneath the walking legs instead of trailing behind, which breaks the shrimp silhouette; the segment arcs are ruled lines on a smooth sausage rather than a stepped abdomen; and the four legs are featureless straight pins with no joint or foot. rows.readsAs: the Cave Shrimp again in cream - a bottom-crawling grub with whiskers
rows.defect: Every part of the fairy shrimp's identity is absent. It is drawn RIGHT WAY UP standing on four stiff pin legs, not swimming inverted on its back. There is no wave of eleven pairs of leaf-like legs - just four bare pins. rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG, then re-cropped and upscaled three regions (whole animal 4x, head 8x, tail 8x) to hunt for small features. The FAIL stands: all three mustReads are absent. WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a hunched, fully OPAQUE cream prawn-ish creature in two masses. Left mass is a large smooth egg/oval (the head-cephalothorax) with a small snout bump at its front, speckled with ~8 soft darker blotches; it is solid painted cream with a specular top highlight - no translucency, no gut line, nothing shell-less about it. Four long thin dark filaments (antennae) sweep off the snout to the left/down-left. Right mass is a second oval that arches up and curls down to the right, banded with ~7 overlapping segment plates - a conventional shrimp abdomen. At bottom right, a bulbous terminal knob with a splayed fan of ~5 broad pale blades: a tail fan (uropods). A dark cast-shadow ellipse sits on the ground under the animal.

CONFIRMED PARTS OF THE CLAIM: (1) Posture. It is right way up, grounded, standing on FOUR straight stiff bristle-pins that drop vertically from the underside of the head oval to the shadow. The cast shadow makes the standing read unambiguous. Reference demands 'swims upside down on its back' with posture:swimming - completely absent. (2) No leaf legs. There are exactly four pins, all clustered under the head oval only, each a plain straight dark stroke with no blade, paddle or leaf shape, no phase offset, no wave, and NOTHING at all along the trunk/abdomen. Eleven pairs of phyllopods beating in a wave is the single defining feature of this animal and there is no trace of it. (3) No stalked eyes. At 8x the only eye-like mark is ONE tiny white dot (~3px) at the very tip of the snout - a specular highlight, unpaired, no dark pupil mass, no stalk, no eye socket. Reference says eyes:prominent, stalked. Absent. (4) Opacity/carapace. The reference note is explicit: 'no carapace at all - the body is a bare translucent tube.' Both masses here are heavy opaque solids and the head oval reads as a carapace shell. (5) Shared chassis. I opened Cave_Shrimp.png, Vent_Shrimp.png and Brine_Shrimp.png side by side. All four are the SAME drawing - identical mottled head egg, identical 3-4 sweeping antennae, identical four vertical leg pins, identical arched segment-plated abdomen, identical splayed tail fan - differing only in hue and scale (Fairy cream, Vent pink, Cave white/small, Brine orange-brown). Fairy and Vent are near-superimposable in silhouette.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM: the second mass is not a plain lobe - it is a distinctly segmented, plated, curled shrimp abdomen ending in a genuine 5-blade tail fan, so 'two-lobe body' undersells what is there; the chassis reads not as a 'grub' but as a generic hunched prawn / mosquito-larva hybrid. That fan is itself off-reference anyway (fairy shrimp end in a slender abdomen with paired cercopods, not a prawn fan) but the packet does not list it, so it is chassis carryover rather than the stated defect. The claim also omits two further failures worth fixing: (a) ASPECT. Required 4.5. Measured alpha bbox is 240x137 = 1.75 INCLUDING the outstretched antennae; excluding them the body proper is ~143x136 = 1.05. The animal must be an elongated horizontal tube and is instead a compact hunched blob - the aspect miss is as large as the anatomy miss. (b) COLOUR. The note asks for orange or pink toward the tail; the whole animal is one flat cream with no posterior warm shift, which is also what makes it read as merely a recolour of the Vent/Cave siblings.

FIX DIRECTION: this needs a new chassis, not adjustment - a long straight bare translucent tube laid horizontally and inverted (dorsal side down), stalked eyes on visible peduncles at the head end, a dense wave of eleven paired leaf paddles running the full length of the underside, no carapace oval over the trunk, no ground shadow, and a warm orange-pink gradient toward the tail.

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the full 440px render plus 5x-12x crops of the head, eye, underside and tail, and measured the alpha bbox. FAIL upheld: two of three must-reads are absent and the third is not drawn as a carapace.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Animal faces LEFT. Front two-thirds is a single smooth tan EGG-OVAL with a 3D specular gloss running along its top-left rim and a soft inner ellipse of shading. Behind it, attached at its right SIDE (not emerging from under it), a segmented trunk of ~5 crescent bands curls DOWNWARD to the right and terminates in a broad multi-blade telson fan. Four thin straight pin-sticks hang from the underside of the oval. Three long thin whiskers sweep off to the left (two off the oval's top, one off its mid-left edge, arcing down-left). A hard ground-contact shadow sits under the whole thing.

MUST-READ 1 (broad flat shield carapace covering the front half): FAILS, but the judge's stated cause needs correcting. The front oval is NOT merely 'the family head oval scaled up' in coverage terms - measured, it spans roughly 60% of the body length, which is about the right proportion for a triops shield, and the trunk does trail behind it. What fails is its FORM: it is a rounded 3D egg with a highlight along the dorsal rim, no flat plate edge, no shield rim/lip, no dorsal keel, no free posterior margin the trunk passes beneath. The trunk butts against its flank instead of disappearing under it. So it reads as a head blob, not a plate. The fix is to flatten and widen it into a plate with a visible rim and tuck the trunk UNDER its rear margin - NOT simply to enlarge it further.

MUST-READ 2 (two long thin forked tail filaments): FAILS. The tail ends in the shared broad blade fan - I counted 6-7 blades, not the 'five' the judge stated. Correction to the claim: there ARE two thin dark bristle strokes back there (one crossing the abdomen segments diagonally, one at the lower-left base of the fan), so the file is not entirely filament-free - but they are short, dark, lie ACROSS the body rather than trailing off the terminus, and are visually read as spines/hairs. Nothing long, paired, forked, or projecting past the fan.

MUST-READ 3 (dozens of wriggling leaf legs beneath the shield): FAILS. Exactly FOUR bare straight pin sticks, uniform width, blunt-ended, no leaf/paddle blade at all, widely spaced with dark gaps between them. There are some faint short hatch ticks inside the oval's lower edge, but they sit inside the silhouette and read as shading texture, not legs.

NOTE (two dark eyes close together on top of the shield, helmeted): FAILS. There is exactly ONE eye - and calling it a 'faint scribble' is slightly off: at 12x it resolves as a small circular RING with a lighter center, correctly placed near the front of the oval. Its problem is not shape but contrast and count - it is tan-on-tan, essentially invisible at display size, and there is no second eye and no paired helmet mass.

ANTENNAE: judge said two; there are THREE long left-sweeping whiskers. A triops shows only vestigial antennae, so all three should go (or be replaced by the long forward-reaching first-thoracic filaments).

GEOMETRY: packet asks aspect 2.5, posture swimming. Measured body bbox (antennae excluded) is 147 x 117 px = aspect 1.26, i.e. half the required elongation, and the drooping trunk plus ground shadow read as a slumped sitting pose, not swimming.

Net: an unshielded, four-legged, fan-tailed, one-eyed generic crustacean blob. Not a triops.

But it is still the same stamped chassis - round barrel-stave carapace, arms starting mid-shell, two walking legs per side instead of four - and the eyes are NOT reduced: two straight pins topped with bright white dots rise from the top of the shell, which reads as normal stalked eyes rather than the blind or vestigial eyes the reference asks for.

rows.readsAs: a pink grub with long whiskers - the Fairy Shrimp asset in pink

rows.readsAs: A kiwi, or a plump quail with a stick taped to its rump
rows.defect: The identity must-reads are absent or inverted. Legs: the reference calls for long strong bare legs and the render gives short thin twigs with almost no visible tarsus, belly nearly touching the ground, so the whole bird reads as a squat percher instead of a runner. Crest: a tiny pale-gold spiky tuft, not a shaggy black crest, and it is the same value as the body so it barely separates. Bill: a thin needle-like yellow spike, not a heavy pointed bill. rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD, with three corrections to the stated causes. I read the 440x440 PNG whole and then at 5x on the head, feet and tail, and pixel-sampled the silhouette. Silhouette bbox is x68-373, y126-301. WHAT I SAW: a fat ovoid body with a heavy round hip/rump mass, a small round ball head set DIRECTLY on the shoulder with NO NECK AT ALL, short gold legs, and a long flat slab tail. The real defect is proportion and mass, not bareness: 26px of leg under a ~100px-deep body is ~15% of the 175px standing height, and the leg is a uniform ~7px-wide stick with no tibiotarsal thigh mass, no visible knee/heel articulation, and no taper. The crest is four splayed thin filaments spraying back off the crown, topmost pixel y=126 on a ~55px head ball, and I sampled it at RGB 157,135,98 against body 147,124,89 - it is the SAME warm tan as the body, not black, and it is a thin comb/wisp (lark- or quail-like) rather than a shaggy erectile black mane. It is therefore UNIFORM WIDTH with no taper, DESCENDS ~28px over its ~100px run (drooping below horizontal, never cocked), and terminates in a blunt squared-off end. It carries ~4 dark cross-bars plus hatch shading and shows no separation into individual rectrices, no graduated feather tips, no white terminal corners. It reads as a wooden batten or paddle glued to the rump, exactly as claimed. Tail LENGTH is actually acceptable (~110px against a ~140px head+body) - the failure is form and carriage, not length, so do not lengthen it. DEFECT THE JUDGE DID NOT NAME, and the biggest one: there is NO NECK. A roadrunner's identity is a lean, long-necked, horizontally-carried cursorial body; here the skull ball abuts the shoulder mass and the torso is a rotund egg. Fixing crest, legs and bill without rebuilding the neck and slimming the torso will still leave a quail. VERDICT: two of the three must-reads (shaggy black crest; long strong bare legs and heavy pointed bill) fail outright, the third reads as a plank, and the chassis reads as the wrong organism. MUST-READ 3 - sweeping backswept rack: ABSENT. Verdict upheld at FAIL — 0 of 3 must-reads land — but one load-bearing part of the original claim is wrong and must not be carried into the fix.

WHAT I SAW (440x440, head crop at 5x from (220,40), neck at 6x from (210,130), feet at 6x from (100,290), rear at 6x from (95,170)).

1. ANTLER — 'forward-sweeping brow shovel over the face': ABSENT. Confirmed. Both beams rise from directly above the eye and sweep UP and BACKWARD (leftward; the animal faces right). Each beam carries a terminal tip plus two short lateral tines that project outward-and-upward from mid-beam — a mirrored 3-point fork. Nothing descends, and nothing projects forward past the brow: the space over the muzzle and nose bridge is completely empty. There is no palmate flattening anywhere; every element is the same uniform rounded rod of the same width. The reindeer brow shovel — a flattened plate dropping forward and down over the face, the single feature that separates Rangifer from every other cervid — is not drawn.

2. NECK MANE — 'thick pale neck mane': ABSENT. Confirmed, and I measured it rather than eyeballing it. Sampled 14x14 patch means: throat-front (275,175) = rgb(179,143,97); mid-neck (262,180) = rgb(182,150,109); upper neck (258,160) = rgb(171,139,95); shoulder (235,205) = rgb(178,147,109); mid-flank (190,215) = rgb(180,148,107); rump (130,215) = rgb(182,151,110). Neck and flank are the same colour to within ~3/255 — there is no value break at all. The silhouette confirms it: the throat line from jaw to brisket is a single smooth unbroken curve with no ventral bulge, no fringe, no hair-tip serration on the edge. The only tonal event on the whole neck is the flat shoulder-patch polygon (a hard-edged wedge, the shared chassis shading plate), which sits BEHIND the neck on the scapula and is not a mane.

3. HOOVES — 'broad splayed hooves': ABSENT. Confirmed, with one correction to the wording. The judge said 'the same tiny dark caps'; more precisely, each foot DOES split into two toes and carries TWO small dark caps side by side, so a cloven read technically exists. But the pair together spans no more than the width of the cannon bone above it and the caps taper inward to points — total foot width is roughly equal to leg width. Nothing splays, nothing broadens, there is no snowshoe spread. Whoever fixes this should widen the toe pair to ~2x cannon width and give it outward splay, not merely add a cloven split, because the split is already there.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM — 'the render is effectively the Elk image in the same batch' is FALSE and should not be used as the fix rationale. Silhouette IoU Reindeer vs Elk = 0.61; Elk's bbox is 252x312 against Reindeer's 234x264. Elk is visibly a bigger, taller, longer-necked animal with a raised head carriage, a dark neck/chest mass and a pale rump/saddle break; Reindeer is shorter-necked, level-toplined and a flat uniform cream-gold with no markings. A stranger would not confuse the two bodies. What IS genuinely reused between them is the ANTLER ASSET specifically: the Elk head crop shows the identical beam curve, the identical two lateral tines at the same relative heights, and the identical terminal tip, only scaled — so the antler-reuse half of the claim stands and is the sharpest evidence, while 'same image' does not.

The real near-duplicate is CARIBOU, not Elk: IoU 0.88, bbox 231x256 vs 234x264 — the same chassis with a colour swap. Per the packet note that is the same species, so it is defensible in principle, except that Caribou is drawn with a shaggy bristled fringe running along the neck and underline and Reindeer has none, and Caribou is supposed to be the LEANER, LEGGIER of the two while both are the same body. Reindeer is the weaker of the pair despite the two rows demanding nearly the same features (Caribou's row also asks for a forward brow shovel, white neck ruff and wide splayed snowshoe hooves).

Other observations: tail is a short blunt triangular flap at the rump, appropriate and not at issue. Ear reads as a dark rounded lobe set behind and below the antler base — small and rounded, which is right for reindeer and not a must-read. Eye is the standard glossy sphere. Muzzle is a plain tapering tube with a small dark nostril dot; a reindeer's blunt, downturned, densely furred rhinarium is not indicated, though the packet does not require it.

NET: with the brow shovel, the pale mane and the splayed feet all missing, nothing on this render says Rangifer. It reads as a generic tan cervid — 'a deer' — and FAIL is correct.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 5-8x on the head, rear quarter, tail and feet, plus a pixel probe of the silhouette. VERDICT UPHELD, but two of the stated causes are wrong and the real defect is more specific than described.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Ink bbox is 247 x 188 px inside the 440 frame -> aspect 1.31 against a spec of 1.9. The animal is a deep-barrelled, level-toplined quadruped with a thick arched crest of neck running from a high wither up to the poll. All four legs are single tapered columns that drop essentially vertically for ~35 of the 60 silhouette rows with NO stifle, NO hock, NO carpal break on either the fore or the hind pair - the hind leg in particular is one smooth taper from hip to foot. Feet are dark-brown blocky caps. CORRECTION: they are not literally hooves - each carries 3 faint toe divisions, so toes ARE drawn - but the block is dark-capped, wider than the shank and reads as a boot/hoof at thumbnail size. This is the shared pony chassis.

THE EAR - the claim is directionally right but mislocated. It is NOT 'a brown disc sitting on the skull like an earmuff'. The large mid-brown circle IS the entire cranium; the only thing acting as an ear is a darker brown ellipse painted INSIDE that circle, flush with the surface, with the eye sitting on its lower rim. The consequence is worse than the claim states: the head silhouette is exactly circle + narrow muzzle wedge, so the ear contributes ZERO to the outline. There is no second ear, no paddle, nothing rising above or standing clear of the skull. For an African wild dog the huge round upright ears are the entire identity read and they are absent from the silhouette - this alone is the FAIL.

THE TAIL - this part of the claim is WRONG. The tail does NOT attach mid-back. Its root is correctly set at the top of the croup, at the rear terminus of the topline behind the hip, and it sweeps down-and-back. Tail set is one of the few things this asset gets right. The white tip is genuinely present and clean: a crisp near-white disc, ~16 px across, at the very end of the brush (pixels x109-124, y234-246). Do not touch either.

BLOTCHES - partly land. There are irregular, genuinely ragged dark-brown patches over a tan ground, well distributed on flank, shoulder and haunch, and their shape language is right. But the palette is brown-on-tan ONLY: no true black, and no white patchwork (the pale cream on chest/underline reads as shading, not as a white patch). So 'black, tan and white' is delivered at about half strength.

FIX ORDER: (1) build real ears - two tall rounded paddles that break the head outline, near ear large and face-on, far ear behind it, each at least a third of the skull height; (2) stop drawing the cranium as a plain circle, give it a canid skull with a stop and a flatter braincase; (3) rebuild the limbs on the established canid limb model - long slender shanks, real stifle and hock angulation, small compact paws with visible toes rather than dark blocks; (4) lengthen and shallow the body to hit aspect 1.9 and lose the cresty neck; (5) push the blotch palette to true black plus white patches.

Only the white tail tip, the tail set, and the blotch shape language survive.

rows.readsAs: a small white pony or a white goat
rows.defect: Same barrel, same cresty neck, same four straight columns, same grey hoof-blocks. Nothing about the silhouette says fox. The 'dense round tail' is a thin grey-and-white striped cylinder held out horizontally from mid-back with a flat open end - it is neither dense, nor round, nor white, and it contradicts the all-white coat. Ears are one tiny pale nub; the muzzle is the same generic horizontal bar every other asset uses, so 'blunt and short' cannot register against anything.

rows.verifyWhy:
I read the PNG whole and then re-cropped and magnified the head (x274-354,y132-194 @9x), the tail (x92-197,y165-265 @7x), the feet (x140-320,y235-295 @8x) and the whole body (x95-345,y125-290 @4x), and I sampled raw RGB to check colour (a caution for later passes: at some crop scales the image renderer gave a false tan/orange cast; pixel sampling is authoritative). VERDICT UPHELD - 2 of the 4 must-reads are absent and a 3rd does not register - but three of the four specifics in the original claim are wrong and must not be handed to a fixer as written.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE.

CHASSIS (claim CORRECT). A long slab-sided barrel with a dead-level topline, a short thick neck carried level-to-low into a heavy shoulder mass, and four columnar legs with essentially no stifle or hock angulation - the hind leg is a near-straight post with one shallow kink. Feet are small flat grey ovals with two toe-slits scribed across them, reading as cloven pads/hooves. Together this reads as a white pony or a long-legged white dog, not a fox. Confirmed.

TAIL (claim WRONG in four particulars, verdict still right). It is NOT thin, NOT grey-and-white striped, NOT horizontal, and NOT out of mid-back. Measured: it roots at approx (152,200) - about 20px below the topline, just behind and above the hip, i.e. on the upper croup - and runs back-and-DOWN at roughly 45 degrees to a tip at approx (110,235). The mass is WHITE (sampled 242,245,248 and 251,251,251), roughly thigh-thick at the root, so it does NOT contradict the all-white coat as a mass. What actually fails is two things. (a) A hard-edged, slightly warm cream ellipse is pasted over the distal half of the tail with a visible seam; it reads as a separate flat egg, or as the flat cut-open end of a tube, sitting on top of the brush rather than being its tip. (b) The outer contour is not a dense round brush at all - it is a comb of thin, separated, dark-grey to near-black hair strokes with dark background visible between them along the upper-left and under edges, so the outline reads wispy, spiky and banded. That dark fringe is also the only large dark mass on an otherwise white animal, so it fights the all-white read even though the tail body is white. NET: 'dense round tail' does not register. FIX = fill the silhouette to a solid, blunt, cylinder-to-teardrop brush at least as thick as the thigh for its whole length, drop the separate cream cap, and re-tint the fringe to white/pale-grey so it stops reading as a banded raccoon-ish appendage.

EARS (claim WRONG - not 'a tiny nub'). There is NO ear anywhere in the silhouette: the cranium is one unbroken rounded dome from y142 to the brow, with at most a 2-3px bump on the crown. What exists are TWO small dark-grey POINTED TRIANGLES painted flat INSIDE the forehead - the near one sitting directly above/behind the eye, the far one behind and slightly higher - each about a fifth of the skull height. They are pointed, not rounded, and they carry no outline, so at any real display size they read as face markings, not ears. 'Short rounded ears' therefore fails, but the fix is to build actual ear geometry that BREAKS the skull line (short, wide-based, round-topped, set well back on the dome), not to scale up a painted triangle.

MUZZLE (claim CORRECT). The snout is a long, narrow, straight-sided bar projecting well clear of the face - about 75-80 percent of the cranium's length (cranium x282-316, nose tip x~345) - capped by a dark oval nose. Underneath it sits a SEPARATE grey lower-jaw plate that is offset below and behind the upper bar, leaving a visible step/seam so the head reads as two stacked sticks. This is a red-fox/collie snout, the exact opposite of the required blunt short muzzle, and it is the single biggest reason the head does not read arctic. Minor secondary: the eye is amber/gold; arctic fox eyes are dark brown.

WHAT PASSES. 'Thick fluffy all-white coat' is genuinely present and is the one must-read I would defend: sampled body pixels are 232-251 across R,G,B, near-neutral with a faint cool cast, with fine painted fur strokes over the whole barrel and a visibly fluffier ruff at the chest and throat. The exception is the feet - grey pads plus grey stockings running up the back of the cannons - which an arctic fox should not have; its paws are furred and white.

SCORE AGAINST THE ROW (mustRead: short rounded ears - blunt short muzzle - thick fluffy all-white coat and dense round tail; note: everything shortened and rounded vs a red fox). Ears ABSENT. Muzzle ABSENT (and it is longer than a red fox's, the reverse of the note). Coat PRESENT. Dense round tail DOES NOT REGISTER. The note's whole point - shortened and rounded everywhere - is contradicted by long legs, a long muzzle and no ears. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a dun pony
rows.defect: This is the clearest pony in the batch - arched crest, withers hump, deep barrel, straight tubular legs ending in dark hooves. Of the three must-reads: the ears are a single small triangle laid back on the skull, not large erect triangles; the tail is carried horizontally out of the middle of the back, not bushy and not low; only the pointed muzzle half-lands, and it is the same muzzle bar as the Wolf and Fox.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified by decoding the 440x440 PNG and re-rendering zoomed crops of head (6x), ear (14x), tail (6x), foot (16x) and whole body (3x). The FAIL verdict stands, but TWO of the three stated causes are wrong and must not be used as the fix brief.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS (the pony chassis) — CONFIRMED. Silhouette bbox is x94-345, y87-335. The topline runs level from the rump then RISES into a distinct withers hump over the shoulder (~x230-260), from which a thick, deeply ARCHED CRESTED NECK sweeps up-and-forward to a small head carried well ABOVE shoulder height. Beneath it is a deep rounded barrel with a sharp flank tuck ahead of the hind leg. All four limbs are long straight tapering tubes: the forelegs are near-vertical posts, and the hind leg is a nearly straight post from stifle to ground with NO readable hock angle and no digitigrade metapodial rise — there is no canid crouch anywhere in the leg. Coat is a uniform pale cream with brush-stroke fur texture; none of the coyote's grizzled grey-buff saddle or rufous legs/ear-backs. This composite reads as a small pony with a foxish head bolted on, exactly the family-wide one-chassis defect. It also directly contradicts the packet note 'slighter and leggier than a wolf' — this is a heavy, deep-bodied animal.

FEET — the judge's 'straight tubes on dark hooves' is CORRECT in effect. At 16x each foot is a wide dark-brown horizontal ELLIPSE that overhangs the leg on both sides, meeting the tube leg with no pastern or carpal joint. There are three faint vertical toe grooves scored into the disc and two small pale lobes protruding below its front edge, so a paw was attempted — but the dominant read is a flat hoof plate, not splayed digits on a pad.

EARS — the judge's claim is WRONG and must be corrected. At 14x there are TWO triangles, not 'one small triangle laid back'. They are a symmetric pair sharing ONE central apex spike at the crown: a left/near triangle whose base sweeps down-left and a right/far triangle whose base sweeps down-right, each with a tan rim and a dark-brown interior. Both are ERECT (apex up, slightly forward), and each stands roughly half the skull height (~16px against a ~62px head length) — a defensible size. The real ear defect is that they are FUSED into a single pitched tent/pyramid spanning the full width of the skull top, like a tepee or a folded paper roof, instead of two separate ears with a gap between them and forward-facing cups. That is a malformation of a present feature (POLISH-grade on its own), NOT an absent must-read.

TAIL — the judge's claim is WRONG. The tail does NOT come level out of the middle of the back. It attaches correctly at the TOP OF THE RUMP (~x160,y188) and angles DOWN-and-back at roughly 35-40 degrees, its tip reaching ~y250, below the belly line. It carries a genuine fringe of hair strands along its upper/rear edge, so it reads as moderately bushy and low-carried. Its actual defects are (a) it is drawn as a smooth CYLINDER with the fringe applied only as an edge fray, so the mass reads as a tube rather than a brush, and (b) the tip is terminated by a flat dark-brown DISC END-CAP — a cut-off cylinder face, not a tapering black tail tip. The packet asks for a tail that 'hangs down rather than out'; this one is carried out-and-down, which is a miss but a much smaller one than claimed.

MUZZLE — partially present. It is long and slender relative to the skull and is the single most canid-suggestive element, but it is a wedge that WIDENS toward the tip and terminates in a large bulbous dark nose ball with a thin straight stick-line for the mouth. WHAT I SAW (440x440, subject bbox x103-337 y124-299, standing height 176px). MISSING MUST-READ / NOTE: the note asks for a golden/black-backed jackal. The black saddle -- the single strongest species cue available -- is entirely absent. The coat is uniform gold with pale streak strokes, no dorsal saddle, no contrast field of any kind.

Zoomed to 16x on the crown there are TWO erect pointed ears, each with its own dark-brown inner-ear concha, splayed left and right around a pale central septum that runs up to a shared apex spike. Carriage is already low/out-and-down and matches the must-read. The genuine tail defect is bushiness: it is a smooth tapering CYLINDER with a comb of short stroke marks along its edge, not a plume -- and it is the Coyote's identical cylinder.

4) 'mid-back cylinder tail' -- the ROOT position is right where it should be, at the croup / rearmost edge of the barrel (root ~x155-162, y~190-196, just under the topline), not mid-back. The 'same cylinder as the Coyote' half of that claim is correct.

BAND: FAIL stands, on (a) the equine body plan -- barrel, unarticulated columnar limbs, hoof plates; (b) the absent black-backed saddle; (c) being the Coyote asset re-tinted, so it carries no jackal identity of its own. It is NOT failing for missing ears or a level tail.

(1) NO MANE. Confirmed and worse than described. The barrel is a pale cream/peach with fine orange fur striations; the neck and head are mid-orange; there is one slightly darker orange saddle patch on the point of the shoulder. Each leg ends in a very short dark-brown block ~8px tall. Correction: that block is not a pure hoof — its lower edge carries a faint 3-lobe scallop, i.e. an attempted paw — but at this scale and with zero stocking above it, it reads as a hoof cap and reinforces the fawn read. WHERE THE CLAIM IS WRONG:
(3) EARS — 'one small triangle' is wrong. There are TWO ear masses. The near ear is a broad triangle with an apex at ~(270,86), a base spanning ~(256..292,110), and it has a rendered darker inner-ear plane inside it — roughly 26px tall against a ~67px head length (~38-40%), which is NOT small and is already bigger than the generic canid ear in this family. A second, smaller pointed tip sits just behind/right of that apex (the far ear). The real defect is shape and carriage, not size: the near ear is a flat wedge that sits flush inside the skull silhouette, backswept, so it reads as part of the head outline rather than as an appendage. Maned wolf needs two tall, wide, forward-cupped paddles standing clear of the skull with air visible around them. Do not simply 'add an ear' — the ear exists; enlarge it, stand it upright, and separate it from the head outline.
(4) TAIL — 'mid-back cylinder with a white flat cap' is wrong on two counts. It attaches at the RUMP, not mid-back (base ~x=165, at the rear of the barrel), though it is pinned at mid-body HEIGHT rather than springing off the top of the croup, and it juts forward/down across the flank so it looks pasted on the side. And it is NOT a bare cylinder: it is genuinely bushy, with a fringed spiky fur silhouette all around an orange core. Its tip is a WHITE CIRCLE, not a flat cap — and a white tail tip is a CORRECT maned wolf marking, so the fix is to blend/feather that white into the brush and re-root the tail on the croup, not to remove the white.
(5) 'Only the leg length lands' undersells it slightly. Leg length measures ~98px of a ~196px standing height (~50%, a little short of the 60% note but clearly the leggiest canid in the set), and the small slim barrel lands too, as does a long, sharply pointed fox-like muzzle with a dark nose button. What does not land is leg STRUCTURE: the hind leg is a straight post with no hock break, and the whole rig is the shared pony/fawn chassis — level topline, thick deer neck, high-set small head, big glassy eye, hoof-like feet.

Verdict upheld, but the stated cause is WRONG on its single biggest point and must not be used as the fix brief. I decoded the PNG and inspected it at 8x plus a pixel-luminance map of the head.

EYES — THE CLAIM IS FLATLY WRONG. There are no 'two tiny white-ringed dots on a smooth ball'. Those white pixels are 4-5px SPECULAR HIGHLIGHTS sitting on two LARGE dark eye globes. The luminance map (x120-165, y126-180) shows a continuous dark-slate mass filling x129-x150 across y143-y177 on a head that only spans x126-x152 / y139-y178 — i.e. the eye mass covers essentially the ENTIRE head, ~22px wide by ~35px tall on a ~26px head. There are two stacked globes: a lower slate-blue one (highlight at x132-136,y159-161) and an upper near-black one whose top bulges ABOVE the blue head's dorsal outline at y139-145, which is correct dragonfly anatomy. The only bright blue left of the head is a thin crescent rim on the lower-left. The must-read 'huge globe compound eyes filling the head' IS PRESENT AND SATISFIED. Its one real weakness is contrast, not size: the upper globe is rendered at luminance <45, statistically identical to the #0d1420 background, so at 1x it silhouettes away and the head looks emptier than it is. A fix pass aimed at 'enlarging tiny eyes' would damage the one must-read this asset actually delivers; the correct note is 'lift the upper eye 15-20% in value so it separates from the plate'.

WINGS — CLAIM DIRECTIONALLY RIGHT, DETAILS WRONG. There are FOUR blades, not three, and they are correctly arranged as TWO PAIRS: an up-swept upper pair and a down-swept lower pair, four distinct tips visible at the trailing edge. So 'two pairs' and 'long' (they overshoot the abdomen tip by ~20px) are met. The claim that they all sweep 'back and down' is wrong — the top blade sweeps back and UP. What genuinely fails is the membrane treatment: each blade is a milky mid-grey lanceolate shape (interior luminance ~90-100 against a ~15 background, so nothing shows through and it reads opaque), bounded by a bright leading rim and carrying a bright longitudinal shaft line down its centre that reads as a feather rachis. Net venation is nearly absent — only a faint dotted crosshatch inside the upper blade. And they fan from a single thoracic origin rather than being held out flat. So the read is 'four grey feather quills' rather than 'two pairs of glassy net-veined membranes'. Note the abdomen is painted OVER the wings, so the overlap gives no transparency cue at all.

ABDOMEN — THE REAL, DECISIVE FAILURE, though the numbers in the claim are off. Measured on the blue body: total x126-302 (177px). rows.readsAs: a flat sage-green leaf, or a lancetfish/needlefish blade - a stranger would not say eel and would never say electric eel

Worse, the two features the reference explicitly forbids are both drawn: a hard triangular blade sits on the spine at ~65% length reading as a dorsal, and a translucent leaf lobe hangs below it reading as a pelvic. Looked at the PNG at 1x and then at 6x/16x/20x magnifications with a 10px source grid and a column-by-column pixel classifier. Silhouette bbox is x 108-348, y 175-210 (241 x 36 px, measured aspect ~6.7 against the packet's aspect 8). VERDICT UPHELD, but three of the four specifics in the original claim are wrong and the fix list changes because of it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. The body is a lozenge of solid body-green (approx 80,97,84) running x 127-348, and around it, from x~118 to x~345, is a distinct translucent bluish-grey band (approx 53,63,68) with a hard, crisply-terminated outer edge -- a drawn shape, not a glow. Column dumps: at x=221 the stack is membrane 176-182 (7 px), bright rim 181-183, green flank 183-202, bright rim 202-203, membrane 203-210 (8 px). At x=200: 6 px above / 8 px below. At x=245: 7 above / 8 below. At x=170: 5 above / 5 below. At x=308: 5 above / 4 below.

CORRECTION 1 (the biggest one). The claim that the ribbon anal fin is 'entirely absent' and 'the belly is just the plain body outline' is FALSE. There IS a translucent fin-fold band running the entire underside, roughly 7-8 px deep on a 20 px flank (~35-40% of body depth), from the tail cap to the snout. The actual defect is that it is MIRRORED at essentially identical depth along the entire BACK -- top and bottom differ by at most 1-2 px anywhere on the fish. So nothing on this animal is asymmetric, and the single feature that makes a knifefish a knifefish (one deep ventral ribbon, a bare back) is destroyed by its own mirror image. Worse, the mirrored top band IS the 'eel's continuous dorsal fringe' the packet note explicitly forbids. THE FIX IS NOT 'add a missing anal fin' -- it is: delete the dorsal band outright so the topline is bare, then deepen the ventral band to roughly 2x the flank depth and give it its own fin rays.

CORRECTION 2. There is no 'hard triangular dorsal blade'. The topline is a smooth unbroken lens from x=118 to x=345 -- I checked every sampled column and the top-of-silhouette value never bumps (it holds at y=176 flat across x=203-266). What exists is a flat dark-grey wedge painted INSIDE the flank: apex touching the dorsal margin at approximately (252,186), hypotenuse sweeping down-and-back to a point at approximately (274,196), with a short vertical left edge dropping to y~200. It never breaks the outline. Its position is 28-37% back from the snout tip (i.e. 63-72% measured from the tail), so '~65% length' is only right if you measure from the tail, not the head. It still fails the 'no dorsal fin' must-read because it reads as a folded dorsal / swept fin plate on the upper flank, but it should be removed as a shading wedge, not as a protruding blade.

CORRECTION 3. The lobe under it is neither translucent nor pelvic-positioned. It is opaque body-green (classified solid green all the way to the silhouette edge: at x=290 the green runs y 184-208 with no membrane below it) and it hangs below the ventral line from x~275 to x~299, dipping ~6 px past the normal belly line at y=202. The dark gill arc sits at x 289-292. So the lobe straddles/leads the gill -- it is in the PECTORAL position, not the pelvic position, and it is behind-and-below the wedge, not directly beneath it. Electric eels DO have small pectorals, so the correct fix is to shrink this into a small paddle at the gill, not to delete it as a forbidden pelvic.

CORRECT IN THE ORIGINAL CLAIM. The flank tick marks are real and are the problem described: a dense row of short vertical dashes covering the FULL depth of the green flank along essentially the whole length, so they read as scale/segment rows on a blade-shaped body rather than as fin rays confined to a ventral ribbon. Combined with the leaf/lancet outline and the tiny terminal eye, the animal reads as a lancetfish or needlefish, not a knifefish.

DEFECTS THE ORIGINAL CLAIM MISSED. (a) The tail is wrong in a way that matters as much as the fin: the body does not taper at all -- it ends in a BLUNT ROUNDED CAP at x~127, and a thin dark whisker/spike then juts out along the midline from x~127 to x~107. A knifefish tapers to a fine point over the last third of its length; this is a blunt lozenge with a hair glued on. (b) The gill arc at x~290 is 58 px behind the snout tip on a 241 px silhouette = 24% of length, which contradicts the packet's headFrac 0.12 and makes the head read twice as long as specced. (c) 'Blunt rounded flattened head' does not read: the head is just the front taper of the leaf body ending in a rounded point, with no flat-topped skull and no distinct head mass. (d) Measured aspect ~6.7 vs the specced 8.

BAND: FAIL stands. Two of three must-reads fail outright (the identity ventral ribbon does not read because it is mirrored; a dorsal fringe plus an upper-flank fin wedge are both present where the spec forbids them), the third (blunt flattened head) is absent, and the silhouette reads as the wrong organism.

The big lobes behind them (x~300-334) have distinct cyan cores; the front few have simply lost the blue fill and shrunk as the body narrows, so they read white. rows.readsAs: a startled hedgehog, or a brown potato with straw stuck in its back

Verified by eye at 4x-12x crops and by a pixel classifier over the 440x440 source (non-background bbox x112-327, y151-285). FAIL stands, but one of the stated causes is WRONG and must not be fixed as described.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. The asset is a single smooth brown ellipse (body, roughly x145-318 / y231-266) sitting on a soft drop-shadow ellipse, with a fan of long cream quills radiating out of its dorsal arc and a small tubular snout at the right.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM - THE SNOUT IS NOT THE DEFECT. The other judge called it 'a sharply tapered cone'. It is not. At 10x the snout reads as an elongated TUBE: it leaves the face just below and forward of the eye, runs down-and-right well clear of the head profile, holds roughly constant width (it actually swells very slightly toward the middle rather than tapering), and terminates in a BLUNT ROUNDED TIP carrying a small dark oval nose/nostril pad. There is no mouth line anywhere on the head. That is must-read #2, 'short tubular beak-snout with no visible mouth', and it is PRESENT and READABLE - it is the single best-executed feature on the asset. Do not redraw it into something else; if anything it is slightly thin and slightly droopy at the root (a shallow notch where the cheek meets it), so the only useful polish is to thicken it a touch and fuse the root into the skull.

CONFIRMED DEFECT 1 - NO LEGS, NO FEET, NO DIGGING CLAWS (must-read #3, wholly absent). The ventral outline from x145 to x318 is one uninterrupted elliptical curve; nothing breaks it, nothing descends below it. Column scan finds no body-coloured pixel below the ellipse edge anywhere - the only thing under the body is the drop shadow. The one and only near-miss is a stray cream speck about 3x2 source pixels at approximately (165, 266) on the lower-left edge; that is almost certainly a claw/foot primitive being drawn at sub-2px scale, and it is completely unreadable at any display size. So must-read #3 is absent, and the declared posture 'quadruped' is not met at all - this is a legless blob, not a standing animal. Stocky splayed foreclaws are the echidna's second silhouette signature after the beak and they need to be real, load-bearing shapes.

CONFIRMED DEFECT 2 - THE SPINES ARE A HALO, NOT A DOME (must-read #1, half-failed). Colour is right: long quills in cream with black tips and black streaking, which reads as echidna/porcupine spine material. Placement is wrong. The classifier puts nearly all cream in the band y195-235 while the brown body occupies y231-266, i.e. the spine mass sits essentially ABOVE the dorsal line as an outward-radiating fan rather than as a cap lying ON the animal. Only a small central patch of cream intrudes into the body (deepest reach y247 near the shoulder). Consequently the entire lower two-thirds of the silhouette - both flanks, the whole rump, the shoulder and the belly - is bare flat brown with no quill texture at all. The other judge's phrase 'sprouting from a single line along the back' is close but slightly off: the roots do form a band across the upper dorsal arc rather than one hairline, and the fan is dense rather than thin. The accurate statement is that the quills are drawn outside the body outline instead of clothing it, so the body silhouette itself never becomes spiny. A real echidna is a spine DOME - quills blanket the back, sweep down over the flanks and completely cover the rump, and only the face, underside and legs are bare.

WHY IT FAILS AS AN ORGANISM. With one must-read absent, one half-met, and no limbs, the combination of 'bare brown ellipse + quills only on the topside' is the hedgehog/spiny-ball silhouette, exactly as claimed. The good beak is not enough to carry it on its own because there is no second echidna cue anywhere else in the shape. There is also no stubby tail nub at the rear (minor). Measured aspect is 1.60 against the specified 1.7, which is acceptable. Fix order: (1) build real stocky splayed digging claws and short bowed legs so the quadruped posture exists, (2) extend the quill field down over flanks and rump so the spines read as a dome on the body rather than a fan behind it, (3) leave the beak alone apart from a slight thickening.

(1) 'no whiskers at the blunt muzzle' -- half wrong. The muzzle IS present and correct: a short blunt snout projects from the front of the dome head with a visible nostril dot and a fine mouth/cheek line running back under the eye. Only the whiskers are missing. Do not redraw the muzzle; just add the long whisker spray.
(2) 'a dark face mask' -- wrong feature. There is no mask; the entire head+neck unit is a uniformly darker taupe than the cream body (a colour-block seam at the shoulder, not a facial marking). The distinct dark rounded patch on the upper-left of the head that likely got read as mask shading is in fact a small rounded EAR, drawn in near-profile with a matching step/notch in the head silhouette beside it. The 'small rounded ears' must-read is therefore MET and must not be listed as a defect or 'fixed' -- it is one of the few correct things here.
(3) The feet are not lamb hooves. Each foot terminates in three dark rounded toe-nubs, which is closer to a hyrax's padded, blunt-nailed foot than to a cloven hoof. The defect is leg LENGTH and slenderness, not the foot.
(4) Body proportion is not the problem either -- the barrel measures ~133px long x ~54px deep, aspect ~2.5:1, already longer than the packet's 2.0. Lengthening the body would make it worse.

Must-read scorecard: 'tailless rounded body' -- tailless CONFIRMED (rump is a clean rounded curve, no tail stub anywhere), but the volume reads as a woolly sheep barrel with a defined brisket/shoulder, not a guinea-pig loaf. 'short blunt muzzle' MET, 'long whiskers' ABSENT. 'Small rounded ears' MET. 'Stubby legs' ABSENT -- this is the single biggest defect.

FIX DIRECTION: halve or better the leg length and drop the belly line to ~10-15% clearance so the silhouette sits as a loaf on the ground; strip the long raked fleece streaks and replace with a short dense agouti/speckled coat (this is doing most of the sheep signalling); add a long whisker spray at the existing muzzle; keep the ear, the tailless rump, the toe-nubs and the current body length as-is.

(1) CASQUE — ABSENT, and the judge described it slightly wrong. At 6x on the head (crop 100,10 130x110) the crown is a plain smooth dark ball with a rim-light stroke. There are ZERO red-hue pixels anywhere in the render, so the wattles are not merely small or dark, they do not exist. The neck is a single uniform smooth cylinder from skull to body with no lobes, no dewlap, no bulge, no colour break — I re-checked under a 3.2x contrast boost, which would have surfaced any low-value blue/red, and it stayed flat. "Flat slate grey" is accurate.

(3) GLOSSY HAIR-LIKE PLUMAGE — ABSENT. The body carries rows of leaf/lozenge-shaped scallop marks, plus a stipple field of small ovals on the lower-left flank. It reads as overlapping scales or a guineafowl pattern, never as loose hanging hair. No strand-work, no drooping filaments, no specular gloss band.

(4) SHARED CHASSIS — the judge's core charge is CORRECT and I confirmed it by opening Emu.png side by side. The two are the same drawing. Verdict upheld, but the stated cause is half wrong and must not be fixed as written.

WHAT I DID: read the 440x440 PNG, then a 6x nearest-neighbour crop of the head (x110-240, y60-180) and a 2.5x upscale of the whole figure, then rendered Emu.png and Ostrich.png at 2x for side-by-side chassis comparison.

CORRECTION 1 - THE BILL IS NOT THE EMU WEDGE. The judge's claim that it 'wears the identical short yellow triangular wedge as the emu and ostrich' is factually false. At 6x the bill is a broad orange-yellow upper mandible that starts deep at the face, sweeps forward-left and then CURVES DOWN into a point that hangs well below the jawline - a genuine parrot hook, with a small dark-green lower mandible / gape tucked under it. Emu and Ostrich (verified at 2x) both carry a small straight forward-pointing yellow triangle sitting flush on the neck-head junction, roughly a third the mass and with no downturn at all. The hooked bill is present, it is readable, and it IS the one thing on this asset that says 'parrot'. Do NOT ship a fix that redraws a bill that is already there; the bill's real faults are lesser and cosmetic - it is oversized for the skull, it is planted too high so it emerges from the brow rather than the face, and the pale eye blob bleeds into its base so the cere/eye boundary is mush.

CORRECTION 2 - 'nothing parrot about it' overstates. It reads as a green ratite wearing a parrot's bill, not as a bird with zero parrot cues.

WHAT THE JUDGE GOT RIGHT, AND WHY IT STILL FAILS:

(a) NO FACIAL DISC. Confirmed at 6x. The head is a plain green sphere with a smooth gradient. There is no flattened facial plane, no disc rim, no radiating rictal bristles/whiskers, no owl-like forward-set eye pair. The only marks on the cheek are two faint dark-green dashes below and behind the gape, and they read as shading noise, not bristles. This is a mustRead ('owl-like whiskered facial disc') and it is genuinely absent - this is the single defining kakapo trait and the primary reason the FAIL stands.

(b) THE EYE. Described by the judge as 'one dot eye'; more precisely it is a large white/cream oval highlight with a small dark crescent at its lower-right. The white dominates, so at 1x it reads as a blank pale patch rather than an eye, and the packet asks for eyes:small. It sits so close to the bill base that it half-reads as a cere.

(c) SHARED CHASSIS - CONFIRMED AND WORSE THAN STATED. This is the emu asset recoloured, not merely 'the shared chevron map recoloured'. Overlaying Kakapo against Emu: identical egg-shaped body, identical chevron/scallop feather map in the same layout, identical stippled dot field down the left flank, identical circular sunken medallion disc on the flank (Emu, Ostrich, Rhea and Kakapo all carry this same disc in the same relative position), identical rounded wing/tail lobe at lower right (Emu's exact shape), identical yellow three-toed foot rig. Kakapo differs from Emu only by hue, a shortened neck stub, and the swapped bill. So the family's answer to 'do these share one body' is yes - the chassis reads as a generic plump upright ratite/egg-bird.

(d) COLOUR. Moss-to-lime green with lighter yellow-green chevrons and a darker green shadow. There is no black anywhere in the plumage, so 'mottled with black and yellow' is unmet; the variegation present is the inherited chevron map, exactly as claimed. The overall value is too high/saturated - it reads lime rather than moss.

(e) LEGS/POSTURE. The feet emerge almost directly from the body's underside with virtually no visible tarsus - squat, which incidentally suits a kakapo better than it suits the emu it was copied from. Posture is upright-egg rather than the kakapo's low, horizontal, waddling carriage.

BAND: FAIL, not POLISH. A defining mustRead (the whiskered facial disc) is absent outright, the body is a verbatim recolour of a sibling in the same batch, and the required black-and-yellow mottling is absent. Fixing this needs a new body silhouette (low, broad, forward-leaning, heavy-hipped, short broad barred tail dragging behind), a flattened whiskered facial disc with visible bristles either side of the bill, and a black-barred yellow-green feather map - not a colour tweak. Keep the hooked bill; scale it down about 20 percent and re-seat it on the face.
