rows.readsAs: a pale generic ratite, indistinguishable from the Emu in this same batch
rows.defect: The long bare legs and three toes are correct and the tail is absent as it should be. But the head has a narrow pointed yellow beak where a rhea needs a small flat head with a broad blunt duck-like bill, the neck is feathered and too short for a bird whose height is supposed to be dominated by neck and legs, and the 'shaggy drooping wings' are just the shared small grey blob at the rear. Body proportion is the family egg, so it is taller-than-long only marginally.
rows.fix: Swap the pointed wedge for a broad blunt flattened bill and lengthen the neck so neck plus legs carry most of the height, then hang large shaggy drooping wing plumes over the flanks.

rows.readsAs: a flying fish - the three huge translucent wing planes are unmistakable and a stranger names it on sight
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads miss. (1) The tail is NOT unevenly forked: at 7x the caudal fork is essentially symmetric - upper lobe tip and lower lobe tip reach the same posterior x and sit about the same distance above and below the peduncle midline, so the signature long lower lobe is absent. (2) The body is not blunt-nosed: the head tapers to a knife point, and the white ring eye is parked right at the apex sitting half off the outline with almost no snout in front of it - in isolation that profile reads needlefish or halfbeak, not the rounded bullet head of a flying fish. The eye also reads as a floating hoop rather than a seated eyeball.
rows.fix: Round the snout off ahead of the eye so the head ends in a blunt bullet and the eye sits fully inside the head, and rebuild the caudal as an uneven fork with the lower lobe about 1.6x the length of the upper.

rows.readsAs: a mudskipper - a yellow goby on a mudflat with periscope eyes; the identity does land
rows.defect: The eyes are right (two clean domed turrets riding on top of the skull) but the other two must-reads and the posture note do not. The body lies FLAT: the belly line is level on the mud and the front of the animal is not lifted at all, so nothing is propped. The single visible pectoral fin has a good arm-like muscular base and rayed fan blade, but it dangles below the ventral line into the shadow instead of planting on the ground and carrying weight - it looks hung on the fish, not standing on it. The two dorsals are present in count but wrong in form: they are short rounded humps barely clearing the back, not raised sails, and each has four grey spine sticks that overshoot the membrane and float free in the dark air beside and below the fin, reading as loose picket sticks or antennae rather than rays inside a fin.
rows.fix: Lift the front third of the body clear of the mud on a planted pectoral (fin tip on the ground line, belly visibly raised above it) and redraw the two dorsals as tall separate membrane sails, at least head-height, with the rays contained inside the membrane instead of overshooting it.

rows.readsAs: a bat
rows.defect: Reads as a bat unprompted - big paired ears on a small furry body, and the wing membranes do carry visible dark finger struts fanning to the leading edge, so two of three must-reads land. The third is absent: at 9x the torso simply ends in a rounded rump with a tiny notch. There are no hind legs and no uropatagium - no membrane spanning the hind limbs and tail, so the lower half of the animal is a blank capsule. The wing panels also read more as two creased umbrella/kite facets than as a hand: the struts are few and stop short of the trailing edge, so the fingers never fan all the way out.
rows.fix: Add the tail membrane: draw two short hind legs kicking back from the rump and stretch a triangular uropatagium between them and a visible tail spur, then extend the existing finger struts all the way to the trailing edge so each wing terminates in four distinct fingertips.

rows.readsAs: a spotted lamb or a piebald calf standing in a field
rows.defect: This is the wrong organism. There is no gliding membrane anywhere on it - not neck to wrist, not between the limbs, not enclosing the tail - and the patagium IS the colugo. It stands broadside on four separate columnar legs with clear air between them and a ground shadow under its feet, which is the exact opposite of the required flying posture, so it does not even read as a glider caught mid-glide. The eye is a single small side-mounted bead on a long tapering muzzle, not the huge round forward-facing eyes called for. The bare tail hangs down free of any membrane. Only the mottled fur must-read is present, and on this body it reads as cow or sheep piebalding rather than lichen camouflage.
rows.fix: Rebuild it off the quadruped chassis entirely: pose it spread-eagled and flattened toward the viewer, then fill every gap between the neck, the splayed fore and hind limbs and the tail tip with one continuous stretched membrane so the silhouette is a single kite with a head on it, and enlarge the eyes to huge forward-facing discs.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 5x, 9x and 14x crops of the 440x440 PNG. THE FAIL STANDS, and the primary stated cause is exactly right: there is no patagium anywhere on this asset. I checked all four places it could hide. (a) Neck-to-wrist: the throat/chin line runs cleanly down to the chest and there is open dark background between the jaw and the front leg — no leading edge, no shoulder web. (b) Between fore and hind limbs: the 9x crop of the underbody shows a clean concave belly line and a large wedge of pure dark background between the front and rear legs, floor to belly, with the four legs standing as separate columns. No lateral skin sheet, not even a shaded suggestion of one. (c) Interfemoral/uropatagium: the tail is a smooth, bare, un-furred tapering tube that emerges from the rump, arcs down and back, and is surrounded by background on BOTH sides for its entire length — the defining colugo feature (membrane that encloses the whole tail to the tip) is absent. (d) Fingers/toes: the feet are tiny dark toed/hooflike pads on the ground; there are no elongated digits and nothing spanning them. Since 'the patagium IS the colugo,' the identity must-read is 100% missing and no amount of polish reaches it. The packet also specifies posture: flying — this is a standing broadside quadruped with an elliptical drop shadow under it, i.e. the posture field is contradicted too.

CORRECTIONS to the other judge, all of which change what the fix must target:
1. THE EYE CLAIM IS PARTLY WRONG. It is not 'a small side-mounted bead.' At 14x the eye is a properly constructed mammal eye: a dark chocolate almond ring roughly 1/5 of head height, a black pupil, and a clean white square catchlight at 10 o'clock. What is wrong is scale and axis, not craft — it is a normal-sized eye in strict lateral profile, where a colugo needs a huge forward-facing saucer pair dominating a short blunt face. Directly BEHIND it sits a second, matte dark-brown oval of almost identical size with no iris and no catchlight; this reads ambiguously as either a dark ear patch or a stray/duplicated far-side eye, and it is a real defect the other judge did not mention. There is also a small triangular ear point at the top-rear of the skull (so 'no ears' would be wrong — the ears are present, just tiny).
2. The muzzle description is right and is a second organism-level error: a long, evenly tapering ungulate muzzle ending in a dark nose pad with a long dark mouth line running most of its length. A colugo's face is short and blunt.
3. 'Spotted lamb/calf' is the right family of read but I would sharpen it: the chassis is the generic barrel-body + four columnar legs + tiny hooflike feet used across the mammal sets (see the known one-chassis defect), so it reads as a spotted goat kid or calf with a meerkat-ish head grafted on.
4. The mottled-fur must-read: agreed it does not save the asset, and the stated reason is correct — the blotches are high-contrast solid dark-chocolate islands on near-white cream, sized and spaced like Holstein piebalding rather than the low-contrast grey-green lichen dapple the note asks for. So of three must-reads: membrane ABSENT, huge forward eyes ABSENT (a competent lateral eye stands in its place), camouflage fur PRESENT-BUT-MISCALIBRATED.

Fix direction: this needs a new body plan, not a repaint — a spread-eagle glide silhouette where a single continuous skin sheet runs neck to fingertip to toe to tail tip and the limbs are struts INSIDE that outline, plus a short blunt face with paired oversized forward eyes.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon smiley frog / plush toad — no stranger would say 'bullfrog'
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads is visible. There is no large circular eardrum disc behind the eye — only a vague soft olive blotch on each cheek that reads as a dirt smudge, not a tympanum, and certainly not bigger than the eye. The mouth is a small curled smile spanning under half the head width, not a very wide flat mouth line. The hind legs are thin leaf-shaped paddles running straight out sideways from the mid-flank to flat hand-like feet with separated pointed fingers — no muscular folded thigh, no webbing membrane between digits.
rows.fix: Draw a hard-edged circular tympanum disc behind and below each eye, sized larger than the eye with its own rim and a slightly different value from the cheek, then fold the hind limb into a Z (knee peaking above the body topline, ankle high) and fill the toes with a continuous webbing membrane instead of separate fingers.

rows.readsAs: the Bullfrog drawing recoloured pale mint — a mouldy cartoon frog, not a glass frog
rows.defect: The identity of this animal is absent: the body is fully OPAQUE. No translucency anywhere, no heart, no gut, no visible bone or organ silhouette through the underside, and the belly is not even differentiated from the back. The eyes are the same black-pupil, white-sclera domes as every other frog in the batch, set on top of the head pointing up and out, not forward-facing and not pale gold. The grey-green blotches scattered over the body actively read as mould or warts, the opposite of a smooth translucent glass frog. Silhouette, limb geometry, foot shape, mouth curve and shadow are identical to Bullfrog.png.
rows.fix: Rebuild the underside as a genuinely see-through pane — a lighter, desaturated belly field with a red heart shape and a coiled dark gut visibly rendered inside it — drop the grey blotching entirely, and turn the eyes into forward-facing pale gold discs with fine dark reticulation instead of the shared cartoon eyeball.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and the chassis charge is understated rather than overstated. I looked at the full PNG, then at 5x and 8x nearest-neighbour crops of the head and belly, then at a 3x contrast-boosted belly crop, then sampled raw pixels, then measured both frogs' silhouettes.

MUST-READ 1 - 'translucent belly showing heart and gut': ABSENT, and the judge's wording is exactly right. Every body pixel returns a=255 (sampled 220,200 / 220,250 / 180,230 / 260,230 - all alpha 255). The torso is one opaque mint sphere with a single radial gradient, light at upper-left, falling to 108,140,101 at the lower edge. There is no ventral panel, no dorsum/venter boundary line, no organ silhouette of any kind. The contrast-boosted crop is the decisive evidence: at 3x amplification the belly shows only the same soft dark blotches that cover the back, continuing straight across the ventral zone with no interruption - which positively confirms there is no differentiated underside, not merely that one is hard to see. No heart, no gut coil, no bone shadow, no see-through anywhere including the silhouette edge (the pale arc over the crown is a rim highlight, not transmitted light).

MUST-READ 3 - 'forward-facing pale gold eyes': ABSENT. Correcting the judge's phrasing on one point of precision that matters for the fix: the pupil is not merely black, it is 13,16,22 - the background colour itself, i.e. a void disc punched through the head. It is ringed by a NEUTRAL warm white at 242,239,230 (G-B gap = 9; gold would need a G-B gap of 80-120). So there is no gold pigment anywhere in the eye, and the ratio is inverted from the target: the reference wants a large pale-gold iris with a small dark pupil, and this draws a large black void with a thin white rim - the stock cartoon eye. Placement: the two eye domes bulge up-and-outward off the upper corners of the skull, dorsal, with the pupils sitting slightly inboard-and-low in each dome. So the gaze is very marginally forward but the EYEBALLS are top-mounted, exactly the bullfrog/tree-frog placement, not the front-of-face mounting glass frogs need.

MUST-READ 2 - 'lime-green translucent upperside': only the hue half lands. The mint (197,238,184 at the lit crown) is a plausible pale lime, but it is flat-opaque paint, so the defining word 'translucent' fails.

CORRECTION to the judge on the blotches: they read as flat mould/mottle STAINS, not as warts. At 8x every spot is a soft dark ellipse with a blurred halo and no lit crown and no cast shadow - nothing is raised. A fix aimed at 'de-warting' would be aimed at the wrong defect. Two real problems with them: (a) value polarity is inverted - real glass frogs carry TINY PALE speckles on a translucent lime dorsum, and these are ~14 DARK grey-green patches on a light body, which is what produces the mould reading; (b) they run over the belly as well as the back, which is what erases the underside.

CHASSIS - the 'recoloured Bullfrog' claim, verified quantitatively. I cropped both frogs on identical coordinates. Shared parts, all pixel-coincident: the circular torso, the two eye domes at the same positions and same relative size with the same black void + white ring + upper-left specular, the wide upcurved mouth arc with the same terminal curl at both ends, the two thin pale vertical front-leg struts descending from the belly to small four-toed feet, the large flat splayed rear feet, the pale rim-light arc over the crown, and the ground shadow ellipse. Green-body bounding boxes: Glass 258x154 (aspect 1.68), Bullfrog 228x135 (aspect 1.69) - the same shape at a uniform 1.13x scale, differing in neither proportion nor outline. Note also that the packet asks for aspect 1.5 (Glass) vs 1.6 (Bullfrog) and both render at ~1.68, so the aspect parameter is not separating them either. The only real differences are hue (mint vs olive) and blotch count/contrast. This is one chassis in two colours; the Glass Frog carries zero glass-frog-specific geometry.

Band FAIL is correct: two of three must-reads are wholly absent and the third half-absent, and the asset reads as a generic cartoon frog in mint.

rows.readsAs: a red ladybird beetle or a shiny red jelly blob — it does not read as a frog at all
rows.defect: The render is broken. The whole face assembly has slid off-centre to the upper right of the body mass: one eye is a plain black disc with no sclera and no highlight while the other has a white ring, they sit crammed against the right edge of the silhouette, and the mouth is not a line but a chaotic dark smear with two black wedges spilling over the right cheek. The limbs are gone — reduced to four small flat red nubs at the base of the blob with no legs, no joints and no feet. The large round black spots on a glossy red dome read straight as ladybird elytra. There is also no bold striping and no readable frog snout.
rows.fix: Re-centre the head assembly on the body axis, give both eyes the same jet-black domed treatment with matching highlights, replace the smeared mouth with a single clean wide mouth line, and restore actual limbs — a slim foreleg and a compact folded hind leg — on a small smooth blunt-snouted body with crisp bold stripes rather than scattered round spots.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but three of the four stated causes are wrong and would send the fix at the wrong parts. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (read at 440px, then cropped and upscaled 5x-12x over head, face and foot line): a fat glossy red egg-body in 3/4-right view, two raised eye turrets on its upper right, a thin curved mouth line, a cluster of three dark shapes over the cheek/jaw, one crisp round black spot and one maroon oval on the left flank, and a fan of flat toe-ellipses at each bottom corner.

CORRECTION 1 - THE MOUTH IS NOT THE SMEAR. The judge called the mouth 'a chaotic dark smear with black wedges spilling onto the cheek'. False attribution. The mouth is a distinct, clean, thin dark line with a soft shadow band beneath it, running from mid-face diagonally up-right to the silhouette edge under the near eye; it is perfectly legible as a wide frog mouth and terminates correctly at the snout edge. The chaotic dark mass is a separate thing: THREE misplaced pattern blotches - an upward-pointing tapered petal/leaf shape (maroon), a near-black rounded wedge immediately left of it, and a dark maroon oval right of it - piled on top of each other over the cheek and jaw, with the left blotch overlapping and obliterating the left end of the mouth line. The fix is blotch placement/scale (keep them on the dorsum and flanks, off the face), NOT redrawing the mouth. The mouth is one of the few parts of this asset that is right.

CORRECTION 2 - THE FEET EXIST; THE LEGS DO NOT. 'four flat red nubs with no legs or feet' is half wrong. Each side carries a rounded hip/shoulder lump from which a fan of THREE flat elongated toe-ellipses projects outward (six toes visible in total, clearly separated, correctly disc-less per the packet note). What is entirely absent is any LEG: no thigh, no shank, no Z-fold, no front arm, no ankle - the toe fans grow straight out of the body wall, at identical height on both sides, with zero front/hind differentiation. Posture is specified 'sprawling' and no sprawl is built. This IS the real limb defect and it is fatal, but it must be written as 'legs missing, feet present' or the fix will delete the toes too.

CORRECTION 3 - JET-BLACK EYES ARE CORRECT, NOT A DEFECT. The judge flagged 'one eye is a bare black disc with no sclera or highlight'. BOTH eyes are bare black discs with no sclera - and the packet mustRead literally demands 'jet-black eyes', so absence of sclera is on-spec here. Both eyes are large, prominent, and set in raised red socket rings, which is good. The only genuine eye defect is asymmetry: the near (right) eye carries a white catchlight, the far (left) eye carries none, so the far eye reads dead. Also note a stray white specular dot sits on the dorsal outline to the LEFT of the far eye - that is a body gloss highlight, not an eye highlight, and it may be what the judge half-saw.

CORRECTION 4 - THE FACE HAS NOT 'SLID OFF-CENTRE'. The eyes sit upper-right because the pose is 3/4 facing right; that placement is internally consistent, and the mouth line agrees with it. The actual structural failure is that the head is not delineated from the body AT ALL - one continuous egg, no neck, no skull mass, no snout taper - so the eyes read as pasted onto a shoulder. The mustRead 'rounded blunt snout' is therefore only marginally present: there is a rounded lobe right of the eyes bounded by the mouth line, but nothing reads as a snout.

CORRECTION 5 - LADYBIRD IS OVERSTATED. Glossy red dome plus round black flank spots does invite the beetle read at thumbnail, but there are two raised eye turrets on top of the head, a mouth line, and splayed toe fans, and no elytra split line anywhere. It reads as a red squat blob-amphibian with a smeared face, not as a beetle.

WHY FAIL STILL STANDS - AND THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE THE ORIGINAL JUDGE DID NOT CITE: this asset is NOT on the family chassis. Bullfrog and Tree Frog in this same batch are rendered face-on on a shared, working frog chassis - bulging eyes with white sclera rings and dark pupils, a wide symmetric smile line, TWO front arms ending in splayed toed feet, and large folded hind-leg masses flaring to either side. The Poison Dart Frog is drawn on a completely different and degenerate path: no legs, no head separation, an off-axis 3/4 egg, blotches colliding with the face. So the family question 'do these share one body?' answers NO here, and the odd one out is the broken one. Two of three mustReads survive (vivid warning colour on smooth skin: yes; bold contrasting blotches: present but chaotically placed on the face), the third is only half-present (jet-black eyes yes, rounded blunt snout no), and the specified sprawling posture is unrendered. FIX ORDER: (1) build the limb model - front arm plus folded hind leg on the existing chassis, keep the three-toe fans; (2) move the three face blotches off the cheek/jaw onto the dorsum and flank; (3) give the head a snout/neck break from the body mass; (4) add the missing catchlight to the far eye. Do not touch the mouth line.

rows.readsAs: the Bullfrog drawing in brighter green — 'a frog', never 'a tree frog'
rows.defect: The feature the packet itself names as diagnostic is absent: there are NO adhesive toe discs. Every digit on all four feet ends in a thin point, on the forefeet and on the splayed hind feet alike — not one round pad anywhere. The hind legs are also wrong: instead of long limbs folded into tight Z-shapes they stretch out flat and straight sideways from the mid-flank, running off toward the frame edges like arms. Only 'bulging eyes set high on the head' is present, and those are the identical eye domes reused from the other three frogs. Body, topline, mouth curve, foot shape and shadow are the same asset as Bullfrog.png with the hue pushed to lime.
rows.fix: Terminate every toe in a distinctly oversized round adhesive disc, clearly wider than the toe itself, and rebuild the hind limb as a long tight Z — thigh up and back, knee breaking above the topline, shank forward, foot tucked under the flank — so the tree frog stops sharing the bullfrog's splayed sit.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are described wrongly and would send the fix in the wrong direction.

WHAT I DID: decoded the 440x440 PNG myself and re-rendered it at 2x, then cropped the feet at 8x and 10x, and ran a numeric column-scan of the left hind foot to measure digit thickness pixel by pixel. Also rendered Bullfrog.png at 2x for the chassis comparison.

MUST-READ 1 - 'large round adhesive toe pads': GENUINELY ABSENT. Confirmed numerically, not just by eye. Scanning vertical run-lengths down the left hind foot: at the outermost tip column (x=77) each of the three digits measures 4px thick; at x=80-95 they measure 5-6px. That is a constant-width capsule with a rounded cap, i.e. the digit is thickest in the middle of its shaft and ends 1-2px NARROWER. A toe disc would show the opposite - a terminal swelling to roughly 2-3x shaft width. Nothing of the sort exists on any digit of any of the four feet. The judge is right that there are no discs. The judge is WRONG that 'every digit ends in a thin point': the digits are blunt rounded-cap strokes of uniform width, not tapers. The fix is therefore to ADD a bulb/disc terminal (and give it a lighter pad tone so it reads at thumbnail size), not to blunt an existing point. This is the feature the packet note names as THE diagnostic, and it is the single reason this cannot be a POLISH.

MUST-READ 2 - 'bulging eyes set high on the head': PRESENT AND STRONG. I looked at the head at 5x. Two domed eyes sit at the very top of the skull and clearly break the upper silhouette, each with a white sclera ring and a large round black pupil. This must-read passes cleanly and should not be touched by the fix. (Note for the record: my first head crop came back rendering a brown, slit-pupilled reptile head - that was a rendering artifact of the crop pipeline, not the asset. Re-cropping at different coordinates showed the correct green frog head. Do not act on that ghost.)

MUST-READ 3 - 'long hind legs folded into tight Z-shapes': ABSENT, but the judge's geometry is wrong. Each hind limb is a single broad tapering wedge. It attaches HIGH on the flank - level with the shoulder, immediately behind and below the eye, well above the widest point of the body - not at the 'mid-flank'. And it does not stretch 'flat out sideways': it sweeps diagonally out AND DOWN at roughly 40 degrees to ground level, with one soft bend at the ankle and no knee. There is no thigh-back / shank-forward / heel-up reversal anywhere, so no Z, and no readable knee apex above the topline. The limb reads as a flipper or a folded wing rather than a jumping leg. The fix is to build an actual three-segment limb with the knee apex rising above the dorsal line, not merely to rotate the existing wedge upward.

ADDITIONAL DEFECTS THE ORIGINAL JUDGE DID NOT NAME: the hind feet carry only THREE digits each (frogs have five on the hind foot), the front feet three to four, and there is no webbing at all - the digits are separate dark strokes with clean black gaps between them, so 'webbed' fails alongside 'discs'. The front limbs are straight vertical dowels with the foot pasted onto the outer side.

CHASSIS: the judge's 'the Bullfrog asset in lime green' is CORRECT and I verified it directly. Rendered side by side, Tree_Frog.png and Bullfrog.png share the same body ellipse, the same eye domes at the same offsets, the same single-arc smile, the same swept-wedge hind limbs at the same attachment point and angle, the same three-capsule feet, and the same blotch layout. Only hue (lime vs olive) and overall scale differ. Neither carries its own diagnostic - the Bullfrog has no tympanum disc either - so this is one frog blank painted twice, and fixing the Tree Frog in isolation will not fix the family.

VERDICT: the identity-defining must-read (toe discs) is absent, a second (Z-folded hind legs) is absent, and the asset is a recolor of a sibling. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a pale white cartoon frog / a ghost bath toy
rows.defect: The depigmented pallor is genuinely present and is the strongest read in the batch, but the must-read folded hind legs are not there — the haunches splay straight out sideways as flat horizontal wedges with no knee rising above the back, so nothing about it says crouched. There is also no wide flat head as broad as the body because there is no head at all: the cranium and torso are one undifferentiated egg.
rows.fix: Rebuild the hind limb as a folded Z — thigh angled up and back so the knee peaks above the dorsal line, shank folding forward, foot planted beside the body — instead of a horizontal wedge leaving the flank at 3 and 9 o'clock.

rows.readsAs: a green cartoon frog
rows.defect: A stranger does name 'frog', and the bulging eyes plus wide mouth line plus tailless body are present. But the must-read folded haunches with long hind legs are absent: the rear limbs are short flat wedges sticking straight out to either side at mid-flank, with no thigh volume and no raised knee, so the animal reads as splayed flat rather than coiled. The eyes also sit on the front face rather than on top of the skull.
rows.fix: Give the hind leg an actual folded haunch — a bulky thigh mass sitting against the flank with the knee apex above the topline — and raise the eye domes so they break the upper silhouette rather than sitting on the face.

rows.readsAs: the green Frog recoloured brown — a frog, not a toad
rows.defect: Every must-read that separates a toad from a frog is missing. The skin is not warty: it is the same smooth glossy gradient blob as the Frog with the same soft out-of-focus blotches, no bumps, no stippled dry texture. There is no swollen parotoid gland behind either eye — the head is clean. It is not squatter or shorter-legged: the hind limbs are the identical length and identical splay angle as the Frog's, the head is not broader or flatter, and the body is in fact rendered slightly SMALLER than the Frog rather than wider. Zero of the three must-reads survive, and the note's stated differentiation from a frog is entirely absent.
rows.fix: Give it a genuinely different body — widen and lower the mass into a hunched wedge, shorten the hind limbs to half the Frog's, add a hard-edged bumpy wart field across the dorsum, and paint a distinct raised kidney-shaped parotoid gland behind each eye.
rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD after measuring the PNG against Frog.png pixel-for-pixel. What I actually saw at 4x and 8x magnification: a face-on rounded creature, two large dome eyes on the upper corners of the head each with a white sclera ring and a dark pupil, one long shallow S-curve mouth line, two short forelimbs with splayed toes planted at bottom centre, two hind limbs swept out to the sides ending in long webbed feet, no neck, no tail, and a soft cast-shadow ellipse. It is the Frog chassis in brown. MUST-READ 1 (squat warty wide-bodied hunch) FAILS on both halves. Warts: at 8x with a 1.6x brightness boost the skin is a single smooth vertical gradient carrying ~20 Gaussian-blurred dark smears. Not one of them has a highlight, a rim, a cast shadow, or any bump geometry; the silhouette edge is perfectly smooth with zero bumps breaking it. The one light arc that runs over the crown and down the right flank is the same rim-light stroke the Frog carries, not a texture. Wide-bodied: measured torso is 125 px wide x 90 px tall (aspect 1.389); the Frog's is 135 x 92 (aspect 1.467). The Toad is proportionally NARROWER and TALLER than the Frog -- the exact opposite of squat. MUST-READ 2 (bulging eyes with a swollen gland behind each) is HALF present: the eyes are correct, prominent and top-set. The parotoid glands are absent -- I zoomed the strip behind each eye (source x150-295, y148-203) at 8x and there is nothing there but plain body gradient plus two of the generic soft blotches; no raised mass, no separate contour, no shading break, on either side. MUST-READ 3 (short hind legs folded) FAILS: relative hind-leg reach is 234/125 = 1.87 body-widths on the Toad and 254/135 = 1.88 on the Frog -- identical. CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM, all of which leave the verdict standing: (a) the judge said the hind limbs match the Frog's length 'exactly' -- in absolute pixels they are ~8% SHORTER (foot-tip span 234 px vs 254 px, whole-silhouette bbox 234x106 vs 254x110), but the entire asset is uniformly scaled down ~8%, so the limbs are only identical in PROPORTION, not in pixels; the conclusion is right, the wording is not. (b) the judge said the skin is 'the same smooth glossy gradient with soft blurred blotches' -- this understates the one real difference the artist did make: the Toad's blotch field is denser and finer than the Frog's (~20 small smears vs the Frog's ~8 large ones), and there is a small cluster of them below and behind each eye. That is the ONLY change beyond hue, and it is a marking-density change, not a surface-texture change, so it does not buy warts. (c) 'the body is rendered slightly smaller, not wider' is exactly right and now quantified. Silhouette-mask IoU against the Frog is 0.824, and the difference map is a clean concentric ring -- Frog-only pixels form an unbroken outer band around the whole animal including every toe -- which is the fingerprint of one shape uniformly scaled, not a shape redrawn. FIX DIRECTION: this needs a different torso primitive (wider than tall, aspect >=1.7, shoulders carried higher so the back humps), hind limbs shortened to roughly 1.4 body-widths of reach with the knee folded tighter and higher against the flank, a real bumpy surface pass (discrete small ellipses with their own lit top edge and dark under-edge, and a silhouette edge that is visibly lumpy rather than a clean curve), and a genuine parotoid gland: a kidney-shaped swollen mass starting immediately behind each eye and running back over the shoulder, with its own outline and its own lit top so it reads as a separate raised organ.

rows.readsAs: the same cartoon frog in orange — no species identity at all

The pale dorsolateral ridges are also absent: the back carries only the same generic blurred blotches as the other three, with no paired longitudinal lines. rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 1x, at 4-5x nearest-neighbour zoom on the head and flanks, with a contrast-stretch pass, with a per-pixel luminance scan across the eye band, and against a 4-up family strip (Frog / Toad / Cave_Frog / Wood_Frog). The FAIL stands. All three mustReads fail.

MUSTREAD 1 - 'black robber's mask through the eye': GENUINELY ABSENT, and I confirmed it numerically, not just by eye. Luminance scan of rows y=150..190 across the head (x=170..275) gives a smooth sphere-shading gradient: centre ~128-141, falling to ~69-88 at the shaded flanks. The darkest non-eye pixel anywhere in the periocular band is L~69, a mid-brown mottle blotch. A robber's mask would be a near-black (L<30) BAND running snout -> eye -> tympanum. Nothing band-shaped exists. Under a 2.2x contrast stretch - where a mask would be unmissable - the head is still a uniform orange dome carrying two large eye hemispheres. The only dark features near the eyes are two soft round mottle spots (one on the lower-left cheek, one on the right cheek) of the same generic blob vocabulary used all over the body. The judge is exactly right here.

MUSTREAD 2 - 'pale dorsolateral ridges down the back': ABSENT, but the judge's stated cause is PARTLY WRONG and this matters for the fix. There IS a pale line on this asset - a whitish crescent arc running from just outside the right eye down the viewer's-right flank. It is NOT a stray blotch and it is NOT nothing. But it is a chassis specular rim-light: the identical arc, same position, same curvature, appears on the green Frog and on the Toad in the family strip. It fails as a dorsolateral ridge for two independent reasons: (a) it is on ONE side only - ridges must be a symmetric PAIR - and (b) it is a lighting highlight on the silhouette edge, not a raised dermal fold on the dorsum. Whoever fixes this should not be told 'add a pale line'; one already reads as present. They need a symmetric PAIR of pale ridges inset from the silhouette, running down the back, and the existing single rim highlight must be reworked or it will keep competing with them.

MUSTREAD 3 - 'long folded jumping legs': ABSENT. The hind limbs are the shared chassis splayed wedge - a broad flat wedge angling down-and-outward from the mid-flank to an oversized splayed webbed foot, with only a soft elbow-ish kink. There is no folded haunch: no knee carried up above the back line, no tibia folded back against the femur, no thigh mass. Two short stick forelimbs with tiny hands drop straight down under the belly. Judge correct.

CHASSIS / 'hue swap' CLAIM - substantially correct, with one correction. The 4-up strip shows one body across all four: same sphere torso, same two dome eyes at the same spacing and same fraction of the skull, same upcurved cartoon smiley mouth arc, same two lateral splayed limbs, same two stick forelimbs, same right-flank rim highlight, same soft-blob mottle field. The correction: it is not a literal pixel recolour of Frog.png - Wood Frog's torso is slightly smaller and rounder where Frog's is wider/oval, and the blotch field is a different procedural roll (fewer, smaller spots on Wood Frog, concentrated on the upper flanks and cheeks; Frog has more and larger). So it is a re-roll of one chassis with a new hue, not a recolour of the same pixels. The judge's conclusion - no species identity - is unaffected.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT NOT IN THE CLAIM: the hue itself is wrong. This is a fairly saturated orange (body base sampled R183 G111 B52 / R171 G104 B49), not the muted tan-to-coppery-brown of a wood frog. Even if the mask were added, the colour would read as a cartoon orange toad.

Net: zero of three identity mustReads land. The asset reads as 'generic cartoon frog, orange' and is indistinguishable from its own batchmates apart from hue. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a rosehip or wild-cherry bush - round red berries on bare twiggy stems
rows.defect: The harvest is five perfectly ROUND glossy red spheres with a small dark stalk nub on top. A chili's identity is a smooth tapering elongated pod hanging or pointing up from a green calyx cap, and none of that is present - no taper, no point, no calyx. The must-read white star flower with the purple-black anther ring is entirely absent; there is not a single flower in the render. The leaves are thin sliver lancets scattered sparsely along bare stems rather than smooth pointed OVALS, and the stems read as bare brown twigs rather than a many-branched bushy leafy habit, so the plant looks defoliated.
rows.fix: Replace the spheres with tapered pods - a wide shouldered top narrowing to a curved point over about three times their width - cap each with a small green five-lobed calyx and a short green stalk, and add two or three small white star flowers with a dark purple anther ring at leaf axils.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at full size and at 3x/5x crops of the fruit zone, the lower stem zone, and the whole plant. The FAIL stands: this reads as a berry shrub (cherry/crabapple/rosehip), not Capsicum. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: five fruits, each a near-perfect circle (~24px dia at 440px canvas) filled with a radial crimson-to-dark-red gradient plus one large soft desaturated grey-white specular blob at upper-left. Zero taper, zero shoulder, zero curve, no pod axis at all. The defining tapering pod is genuinely absent — the identity feature is missing, which alone is a FAIL.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM (the verdict is right, three of the stated causes are imprecise and a fix built on them would go wrong):

1. GREEN CALYX CAP — the judge says it is absent. Not quite: there IS a short nub drawn at the top of every fruit. But it is a straight brown/tan pedicel stub in the exact same brown as the stems, angled up and away from the sphere like a cherry stalk, ~7px long, with no lobes and no green anywhere. So the shape exists but is coloured and formed as a stem tip, not a calyx. The fix is to RESHAPE/RECOLOUR that existing nub into a five-lobed dark-green cap that grips the pod shoulder — not to add a calyx from nothing.

2. FRUIT ATTACHMENT (missed entirely by the original judge, and it is a big part of why it reads wrong). Every fruit sits APICALLY on the naked tip of a stem — the stem runs up, ends, and a ball is stuck on the end. The packet's harvest spec is pods hanging or pointing up from leaf axils. Terminal single berries on stem tips is the exact signature of a rosehip/crabapple habit and is a second independent identity error beyond the sphere shape.

3. "Stems read as bare defoliated twigs" — half wrong. The stems DO carry leaves through their lower and middle thirds; the bare part is the UPPER third, where every fruiting stem has a long (60-90px) completely naked brown run between the topmost leaf and the fruit. That naked upper run is what creates the defoliated impression. Also, the stems never branch: all six originate from one solid tapered brown trunk wedge at the base and fan straight out, so the silhouette is a bundle of cut sticks in a vase. The packet's mustRead "many-branched bushy habit" therefore also fails, but for a branching reason, not a leaf-density reason.

4. LEAVES — the judge's "thin slivers" is correct and if anything understated. They are flat lanceolate spindles roughly 6:1 to 7:1 length:width with a single darker centreline and pointed ends, and they are attached in near-opposite pairs / whorls rather than the specified alternate arrangement. Combined with the bare brown canes this reads distinctly as bamboo or willow foliage. Spec wants smooth pointed OVALS (about 2:1) in dark glossy green; these are also flat mid-green with no gloss.

5. WHITE STAR FLOWER WITH PURPLE-BLACK ANTHER RING — confirmed absent. I scanned the entire 440x440 canvas; the only near-white pixels in the image are the specular highlights inside the five fruits. There is no flower of any kind, at any size, anywhere on the plant.

NET: three of the three mustReads fail (no white star flower; no tapered pod and no green calyx; no many-branched bushy habit). Leaf shape, leaf arrangement, leaf gloss and harvest form all miss the reference row. Nothing here is a small-feature-I-missed case — the asset is a generic red-berry shrub chassis with no chili cues at all.

rows.readsAs: a watermelon or small gourd vine - or, from the leaf shape alone, a hemp plant
rows.defect: The single fruit is a small ROUND green sphere with pale vertical striping - it reads unmistakably as a watermelon, not a cucumber. The must-read warted ELONGATED fruit is absent: there is no length, no ridging and no warty bumps, just the same smooth specular ball used on the chili in a different hue. Upheld — I tried to break this one and could not. Packet row (batch-001 §2): form vine, aspect 2, leaf 'large triangular-lobed rough hairy leaves, alternate, with unbranched coiled tendrils', leafColour 'mid green, bristly', harvest 'a long ridged dark green fruit with bumpy warted skin, hanging under the leaves', mustRead 'bristly heart-triangular lobed leaf · single spiral tendril at each node · warted elongated fruit and yellow star flowers'. Two of the three must-reads are absent; only the tendril one lands.

WHAT I SAW (440x440 canvas, read at 1x then re-cropped at 4x, 6x and 14x through a local PNG decoder):

FRUIT — confirmed wrong, and the judge's description is essentially right but understates it. There is exactly ONE fruit, at the upper node (~x177-207, y165-202 in source pixels, so ~30w x 37h, aspect ~0.81 — very slightly TALLER than wide, i.e. globose/ovoid, not 'round' and not small: it is about the size of one leaf). At 14x it is a smooth ovoid berry painted with alternating light-and-dark VERTICAL stripes running pole to pole, a specular highlight column on the upper-left, a brown woody pedicel entering the top and a faint blossom scar at the bottom. Surface is completely smooth — zero bumps, warts, spines or longitudinal ridges anywhere on it. It reads unmistakably as a watermelon or a small striped gourd. YELLOW STAR FLOWERS — confirmed absent, and I verified this mechanically rather than by eye: a scan of all 193,600 pixels for any warm/yellow pixel (r>140, g>120, b<110) returns ZERO hits. The only non-green pixel cluster in the whole image is the brown pedicel on the fruit. There is no flower of any colour, at any node, at any size.

LEAVES — confirmed wrong, and the judge's 'reads as hemp' is exactly what I see. Seven leaves, every one an identical palmate fan of 5 narrow lance-shaped lobes radiating from a single point, cut nearly to the petiole insertion, each lobe with a smooth unbroken convex margin and a sharp acuminate tip. No cordate/heart-shaped base, no sinus, no marginal teeth or serrations, and no hair/bristle rendering at all — the fill is a soft airbrushed mid-to-yellow-green gradient with faint palmate midveins. That silhouette is cannabis or Japanese maple, not the broad heart-triangular shallowly-5-lobed bristly cucurbit blade. The vine stem is likewise a smooth thick green cord with no bristle texture, contradicting leafColour 'bristly'.

TENDRILS — the judge is right that these land, and I want to strengthen that so the fix does not touch them: I count 5-6 coiled spiral tendrils, one per node (top node has two, one at the fruit node, one mid-right, one at the lower-right node, one at the bottom node). They are unbranched, tightly coiled single spirals in the correct place. This must-read is genuinely satisfied and should be preserved.

ASPECT — confirmed. Measured green-pixel bounding box is x126-312, y106-333 = 187w x 228h, giving w/h = 0.82 against a reference aspect of 2.0, i.e. ~2.4x too tall/narrow. The plant is a near-vertical diagonal S occupying only 42% of the canvas width and 52% of its height, leaving ~126px of empty margin on the left and ~128px on the right. A vine at aspect 2 should sprawl horizontally across the frame.

NET: the organism as painted is 'striped melon on a hemp vine'. Two of three must-reads (warted elongated fruit, yellow star flowers) are missing outright, the leaf must-read reads as a different plant family, and the habit misses its aspect by 2.4x. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a generic brown barnyard gamebird — indistinguishable from the Turkey card

rows.readsAs: a dark grey chick with a few white dots — a speckled pigeon
rows.defect: The identity feature is entirely absent: there is no bare skin anywhere, no bony helmet casque, no blue-and-red face, no red horn wattles. The head is the same fully feathered grey chick skull with the standard yellow bill used on every other card, and it is normal-sized rather than comically small. The neck is not thin or naked — head sits straight on the shoulder like the rest of the family. rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with two corrections to the stated causes. Verified by reading the 440x440 PNG at full size and again at 8x/5x/3x crops of the head, body and feet, plus numeric pixel measurement (own zlib PNG decoder; bird bbox, blob clustering, hue survey).

WHAT IS THERE: a slate blue-grey biped gamebird chick. Bird bbox x123-267 (w145), y139-288 (h150). Round hunched egg-shaped body with a large dark crescent wing outline and a fine hatch texture. Plain amber-yellow triangular bill. One round black eye with a white catchlight. Two amber-yellow legs, each a forward toe plus a rear spur. A dark grey pointed tail wedge running back-right and slightly downward to x=267 with a few fine barb lines. Soft cast-shadow ellipse.

MUST-READ 1 - 'tiny bare blue-and-red head with a bony helmet casque': ABSENT on every sub-part, confirmed. (a) No casque. Row-span scan of the crown gives y140 span 147-159, y144 span 140-166, y148 span 136-170, y152 span 134-172 - a clean circular arc. Nothing exists above y=139, which is also the bird's own bbox top, so no protrusion, knob or crest projects from the skull at all. (b) No bare skin and no red. A red-skin pixel test (r>110, r-g>40, r-bl>40, non-yellow) over the whole head box returned EXACTLY 0 pixels. Max saturation inside the head box is 0.732 and it sits at (138,156) = RGB(224,177,60), which is the yellow BILL, not facial skin. The skull is the same uniform slate blue-grey as the body with a soft rim highlight - it is the family's feathered chick head. (c) NOT tiny. This is where the original claim understates the defect: the head is ~40px across (x134-172) on a 145px-long bird = headFrac ~0.27, where the packet specifies 0.18 and the note demands 'comically small for the body'. The head is roughly 1.5x the specified fraction - it is OVERSIZED, not merely 'normal-sized'. Note for the fix: shrinking the head alone will not rescue this asset; the identity is carried by casque + bare wattled skin, not by scale.

MUST-READ 2 - 'round hunched body densely speckled with white dots': body shape PASSES (genuinely round and hunched); the pearling FAILS. Total bright-pixel coverage is 116 px on a 440x440 canvas, clustering into 23 blobs of only 4-6 px each. CORRECTION to the original claim's geography and count: it is not 'a sparse rim outlining the wing' - it is a three-arc perimeter ring, and one of the 23 blobs is not a pearl at all. Breakdown: ~11 pearls along the upper back / scapular margin (y164-177, x173-250); 4 down the front-left breast edge ((148,190),(140,220),(152,220),(145,233)); 6 along the lower belly / flank (y241-257); 1 stray at (260,199) near the rump. That is 22 real pearls. The 23rd blob at (147,155) lies inside the head ball and is the EYE CATCHLIGHT, not a spot - the head carries zero pearling. Genuinely unspotted zones: the entire central wing shield (roughly x175-250, y190-240) which is plain grey with hatch only, the head, the neck, the breast front, and the whole tail wedge. So the dots read as decorative edge banding tracing the silhouette rather than the allover dense pearling that defines the bird.

MUST-READ 3 - 'thin naked neck on a heavy body': heavy body PRESENT; thin naked neck ABSENT. The head merges into the body over y156-168 through a short, THICK grey column of the identical feathered material - there is no narrow bare-skinned stalk, and no colour or texture change between skull, neck and torso.

NOTE CHECK - 'the tail droops downward': partially met. The tail wedge does angle back and slightly down, but it reads as a near-horizontal pointed wedge rather than the steep droop of a real guineafowl.

SECONDARY (not a must-read, but it reinforces the wrong read): the legs and feet are amber-yellow; real guineafowl legs are dark grey-black. Combined with the plain yellow bill this pushes the asset further toward generic-chick.

CONCLUSION: 1 of 3 must-reads is present, and only its generic half (round hunched body). Both identity-bearing features - the casqued bare blue-and-red head and the allover pearling - are absent or reduced to decoration. The asset reads as a generic grey quail/chick with a dotted outline, not as a guineafowl. FAIL stands.

METHOD CAVEAT recorded for future passes: the shared scratchpad contained stale full.png / head.png from earlier sessions; a first crop under those common filenames rendered an unrelated orange crested bird and briefly looked like the file had changed. Re-running with unique filenames (gf_verify_*) and dumping IHDR in the same call resolved it. The source PNG itself is untouched (mtime Aug 3 23:13, md5 fa795886c3017717f43e817adf1fe88f, 440x440 RGBA, all scanline filters type 2, inflated length exactly h*(stride+1)) - the grey speckled bird is the true content. Always use unique crop filenames here.

rows.readsAs: a dumpy tan chick — the Quail card without its topknot

rows.readsAs: a teal chicken with gold dots on its tail
rows.defect: The train — the entire identity of a peacock — is not there. The tail is the SAME short drooping 5-lobe fan used on the Chicken and Turkey cards, no longer than the body, with a single flat gold disc stuck on each lobe tip; those are dots, not ocelli (no blue-black centre, no bronze-green surround). rows.verifyWhy:
I upheld the FAIL but THREE of the four stated causes are factually wrong and must not be used as the fix brief.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (measured on the 440x440 png, decoded pixel-wise):
- Ink bbox = x83..356, y114..325 -> 274w x 212h, ASPECT 1.29 against the requested 2.2. Confirmed short. (Family context: Chicken lands 1.05 on a 1.1 ask, Turkey 1.45 on 1.2, Pheasant 1.83 on 2.4. Peacock is the biggest relative miss in the batch.)
- OCELLI ARE PRESENT AND THEY ARE RINGED. The claim 'a flat gold disc on each tip' is WRONG. At 12x each eyespot is a bright yellow core (~250,235,120) inside a distinct grey-blue annulus (~70,120,160) about 4px thick, sitting on the teal vane -- a legible two-ring eyespot, not a bare disc. The colours are inverted from a real ocellus (nature = blue-green pupil in a bronze/gold surround; here = yellow pupil in a blue surround), which is the correct note to write, but 'no ringed ocelli' is not.
- COUNT IS 9, NOT 5. Nine lanceolate feathers radiate from the rump, each carrying one ocellus near the tip. The claim '5-lobe' is wrong. Chicken and Turkey carry ~7 plain lobes with no spots at all, so the spotted vanes DO differentiate this asset from its siblings.
- THE CREST EXISTS AND THE CLAIM NEVER MENTIONS IT. At 6x the crown carries a tuft of 5 thin teal wires with slightly clubbed/spatulate tips. That is a genuine attempt at the wire-tipped crest must-read. Its defects are that it sweeps back-and-right in a floppy cluster instead of standing as an upright fan, and that it is the same primitive the Chicken uses for its comb -- so it is present but not distinctive.

WHY IT STILL FAILS:
1. THE TRAIN. The claim 'the train is missing entirely' overstates it -- what exists is a tail, spotted, fanned; but it is nowhere near a train. The fan spans x~250..356 (~106px) against a head-to-rump body of x83..~258 (~175px), i.e. the tail is 0.6x the body when the packet note demands it drag behind and make the bird VERY LONG (tail alone longer than the body, as Pheasant actually achieves with its flat 19-22px-tall run out to x=356). It also fans downward to the ground line (lowest tip y=325, below the feet at y~305) instead of trailing horizontally. Defining must-read #1 is half-delivered: eyespots yes, train no.
2. SHARED CHASSIS -- and this is provable, not impressionistic. Peacock and Turkey have IDENTICAL bounding boxes (x83..356) and their column-height profiles are identical through the entire head and breast: 1,4,8,11,14,16,61,~87,104,... The round ball body, the wing oval with its swirl outline, the beak wedge, the two yellow scaly legs and the fan-tail root are one generator with different tail parameters and a hue swap. The judge was right that this is the Chicken/Turkey body; they were wrong about which parts of the tail differ.
3. NECK/BREAST. Correct as claimed. The whole bird is one flat teal -- head, neck, mantle, wing, tail vanes all the same hue family. There is a slight value/texture split (plain darker teal on the head+neck vs lighter cyan hatching on the body) but no hue separation, so 'iridescent blue neck and breast against a duller body' does not read at all.

FIX BRIEF: keep the 9 ocelli but re-colour them blue-green core / bronze-gold outer ring; extend the vanes into a long trailing train that runs horizontally past the frame's right and exceeds body length (target overall 2.2); lift the fan off the ground line; give the neck+breast a saturated blue distinct from a green/bronze back and train; stand the crest up as an upright fan and stop sharing the Chicken comb primitive; and break the body off the Turkey chassis (the identical column profile through the breast is the tell).
