FAIL upheld, but the stated cause is only partly right — the tail half of the claim is wrong on measurement and must not be fixed as described.

WHAT I SAW (440x440 PNG, read at 1x then re-cropped at 3x/5x/7x nearest-neighbour, plus per-pixel hue sampling).

HEAD — the judge is completely correct here, and this is what sinks the asset. The head is a plain round ball in exactly the same russet brown as the rest of the bird. Sampled average RGB: crown [136,77,41] hue 23deg, cheek [137,78,36] hue 25deg, ring-of-eye [149,79,37] hue 23deg, neck junction [126,67,32] hue 22deg, breast [129,70,34] hue 23deg, upper back [175,93,44] hue 22deg, tail [107,57,27] hue 23deg. Every region is the same hue within 3 degrees — there is literally no colour break anywhere between beak and tail tip. A 70x70px box over head+neck (4900 opaque pixels) contains ZERO green-family pixels (hue 70-180 with sat>15), ZERO saturated-red pixels (hue<12/>345, sat>=55), and 2 near-white pixels, which are the eye catchlight. So all three head must-reads are provably absent: no iridescent green-black hood, no red bare facial wattle around the eye, no white neck ring. The eye is a plain black bead with a white highlight sitting directly on brown feather; the neck reads as an unbroken brown column into the shoulders. One correction to the judge's wording: the head is not 'plain tan' and not featureless — it is mid russet-brown (identical to the body), and at 5x there IS a crest of about five thin wispy rearward feather-quills rising off the crown. That crest is real and drawn; it just is not any of the three required cues, and its warm-brown colour makes it invisible at 1x.

BEAK — an additional defect neither judge named: the bill is a short bright-yellow triangular seed-eater/finch beak (pure yellow, hue ~45), not a pale grey-horn galliform bill. It pushes the read further toward songbird.

TAIL — the judge's description is FACTUALLY WRONG on length and should not be used to drive the fix. Measured silhouette bounding box (alpha>140, ink threshold): x 80-359, y 138-290. The round body mass runs x~105 to x~232 (127px). The tail runs x~232 to x=359 (127px). That is a 1.00:1 tail-to-body ratio, NOT 'about a third of body length'. The tail is roughly as long as the body, so the failure is that it is not long ENOUGH (the packet note demands 'the tail alone is longer than the body'), not that it is a stub. What the judge got right: it is a flat parallel-sided plank. Per-column ink height along the tail is 19,19,19,20,20,20,21,21,20,21,23,19 — dead constant from root to tip, ending in an abrupt square cut at x=359 with no taper. So 'pointed' is genuinely missing. Barring is partially present: at 4x I can see 4-5 thin dark transverse strokes crossing the plank, so the 'barred' cue is drawn but faint and lost at 1x. Attachment: the tail root sits at y 196-236 at x=235 while the body spans y 177-232 there — it emerges from the lower rear flank and overlaps the wing, so it reads as bolted onto the side rather than springing off the rump; the judge's 'mid-flank' is a fair read of that even though the geometry is lower-rear.

PROPORTION — overall silhouette is 279x152 = aspect 1.84 against the packet's 2.4, so the bird is also too stubby.

NET: the ring-necked pheasant male's entire identity lives in the head trio plus a tail visibly longer than the body. The head trio is measurably 0/3 present and the tail is 1.0x body, blunt-cut, and side-mounted. The asset currently reads as a generic brown partridge/quail hen with a finch beak. FAIL stands.

FIX DIRECTION: (1) recolour the head+upper neck to a dark iridescent green-black distinct from the body, (2) add a saturated red bare-skin wattle mask around and behind the eye, (3) add a clean white ring at the head/neck junction separating hood from body, (4) lengthen the tail to ~1.6-1.8x body and taper it to a point instead of a square cut while keeping and strengthening the existing cross-bars, and re-root it at the rump top rather than the lower flank. Do NOT 'lengthen the tail from a third of body length' — it is already at parity.

rows.readsAs: a white chick or a small white dove
rows.defect: The white winter plumage is present and correct, but the other two must-reads are absent: the feet are the family's bare bright-yellow scaly rods with no feathering at all, which is exactly backwards for the one gamebird defined by snowshoe-feathered toes, and there is no red comb above the eye — no red pigment appears anywhere on the card.
rows.fix: Bury the legs and toes in shaggy white feather boots so no bare scale shows, and add a small scarlet fleshy comb arc directly above the eye.

rows.readsAs: a quail
rows.defect: Reads correctly — round feathered-ball body, very short wedge tail, short legs, small head tucked to the shoulder, and the topknot helps. The only weakness is that this is the family's default chassis, so it passes partly because the chassis happens to be quail-shaped.
rows.fix: Curve the topknot plume forward over the bill instead of splaying it into three straight spikes, so it reads as a quail plume rather than the generic tuft shared with Chicken and Rooster.

rows.readsAs: a rust-red robin or a generic brown songbird
rows.defect: Nothing that makes a rooster is present. The comb is the same small 3-spike tuft as the Chicken and Quail, not a tall red blade; there are no wattles hanging from the chin. The tail is two straight flat planks angled backwards and DOWN — the exact opposite of arching sickle plumes, and the same part used on the Pheasant card. The posture is the family's horizontal ovoid, not an upright puffed chest, and there is no hackle cape at all — the neck-to-shoulder transition is the same smooth featureless join as every other card. Requested aspect 1.0 (upright/square) is ignored.
rows.fix: Stand the body up on longer legs so the breast faces forward, add a tall serrated red comb and two long red wattles, cape the shoulders in pointed hackle feathers, and replace the plank tail with two long sickle plumes that arch up above the topline and curve down behind.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 5x-8x zoom on the head, throat, neck-shoulder junction, tail and feet, and side-by-side against Chicken.png and Quail.png from the same batch. FAIL stands: zero of the three must-reads ('tall red comb and long wattles' / 'arching sickle tail plumes' / 'upright puffed chest with hackle cape') survive. But three parts of the original claim are wrong and would send a fix in the wrong direction.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE
- Comb: the claim of a 'small 3-spike tuft' is wrong on both count and size. It is FIVE thin curved quills rising off the crown and swept BACKWARD over the nape, roughly 60% of head height, and it is the one rooster-ish concession in the asset: it is tinted a hot orange-red distinctly brighter than the rust body, where Chicken's is cream and Quail's is tan. It still fails, but for a different reason: it is the family's generic backswept crest PRIMITIVE, identical in outline to Chicken's and Quail's with only a hue swap. A rooster comb is a single fleshy blade standing UPRIGHT on the midline with a serrated saw-tooth top edge, rooted along the whole skull; this is a punk quill crest. Fix = replace the primitive, not enlarge the tint.
- Wattles: CONFIRMED ABSENT. Checked at 8x with 2.6x brightness lift in case they were lost in shadow. The chin and throat are entirely bare — the head ball meets the neck tube with no lobe, no dewlap, no red geometry of any kind.
- Hackle cape: CONFIRMED ABSENT. The neck is a smooth featureless tube, same flat fill as the head, running forward-and-down from skull to body with a hard silhouette edge at the shoulder. No cascade of pointed neck feathers, no shoulder spill, no separate cape shape.
- Tail: the claim is CORRECT and precisely stated. Two broad blunt-cut planks with square ends and thin horizontal barring, angled back and DOWN, the lower one drooping further; a small spray of fine dark bristle lines fans out beneath them. No arch, no upward launch, no long C-curve. Note the irony that Chicken.png's tail — a five-blade UPSWEPT fan — is closer to sickle geometry than the Rooster's own tail is; the Rooster has been given a strictly worse tail than the hen.
- Posture: the claim of 'the family's horizontal ovoid' is WRONG as stated. The body is a round-to-slightly-tall ovoid, roughly as tall as wide (aspect row asks 1, and the torso itself is close to that). What actually fails is carriage, not proportion: the head sits LOW and FORWARD on a short down-angled neck tucked against the shoulder, so there is no upright S-curve neck, no lifted head, no thrown-back breast. The chest is a plain gold crescent on the front of the egg — the same egg Chicken uses — with no puff.
- Feet: thin twiggy yellow perching legs, one forward toe cluster and one back toe, no scale plating and NO SPUR — the same foot as Chicken and Quail.

THE CHASSIS FINDING
Rooster is a recolour of Chicken.png. Overlaying the two: identical round head ball, identical double-triangle yellow beak with the same slit eye, identical five-quill crest, identical neck tube and its angle, identical body egg with the same wing-disc-and-ring construction and hatch texture, identical leg/foot geometry, identical ground shadow. The only two differences in the whole asset are the palette (rust/gold vs cream/tan) and the tail primitive. So 'reads as a rust-red songbird' understates it: it reads as the hen, repainted, and the hen herself is the batch's generic plump gamebird.

FIX ORDER: (1) upright serrated midline comb + a pair of long pendulous wattles under the bill — these two alone carry rooster recognition; (2) hackle cape as pointed feather lobes spilling from nape over the shoulders; (3) replace the two down-planks with 2-3 long plumes that launch UP off the rump and arc back and over in a C; (4) lift the head onto an S-curve neck and throw the breast forward; (5) scaly shank with a spur, so the foot stops being the passerine perch foot.

rows.readsAs: a brown grouse — literally the Grouse card in a slightly darker tone
rows.defect: The head is a small fully-feathered brown chick skull with the standard yellow cone bill: no bare blue-and-red warty skin, no snood, no dangling wattle. There is no bristly beard on the breast. The tail is not a broad upright fan; it is the same drooping 5-lobe fan as the Chicken and Grouse, hanging below the body line. Nothing about the mass says turkey — the body is the same small round chick ovoid as the quail, not a heavy deep-breasted bird.
rows.fix: Replace the head with a small bare knobbly blue-and-red skull with a red snood drooping over the bill, hang a black bristle beard from the mid-breast, and raise the tail into a broad vertical semicircular fan standing above the topline.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 6x zoom on the head, 4x on the tail, 6x on the feet, plus a pixel diff against Grouse.png and a hue scan of the whole head/breast box.

HEAD (must-read 1: 'bare warty blue-and-red head with dangling wattle') - ABSENT, and the claim is correct. At 6x the head is a smooth, fully feathered dark-brown dome with a soft rim-light along the crown, one small round black eye with a single white catchlight, and a large flat triangular golden bill (224,177,60) with a straight gape line. There is no caruncled/warty texture, no snood over the bill, no dewlap or wattle under the chin, no bare skin of any hue. I scanned every pixel in x=60..260, y=90..260 for reddish (R>110 and R>G+45 and R>B+45) and for bright bluish (B>120 and B>R+40): the ONLY hits were 278 pixels, all of them the golden bill color 224,177,60 and three antialias neighbours of it. Zero red pixels, zero blue pixels anywhere on the head or neck. The turkey's single most diagnostic feature is not merely small or hidden - it does not exist in the render.

BREAST (must-read 3: 'bristly beard hanging from the breast') - ABSENT, claim correct. The breast is an unbroken smooth brown ovoid with a darker crescent shading seam; nothing hangs off it, no bristle tuft, no dark filament cluster at the crop line.

TAIL (must-read 2: 'broad fanned tail') - this is the one place the FAIL wording needs correcting, though it does not rescue the card. The tail is NOT a 'drooping lobe'. At 4x it resolves into roughly 8 discrete, individually drawn lanceolate rectrices radiating from a common base across about 80-90 degrees, alternating light-brown and dark-brown, i.e. it genuinely is a spread fan of separate feathers. What is wrong is the orientation and the ownership: it is a lateral fan swept backward and downward off the rump (lowest feather tips drop well below the foot line and into the ground shadow), not the broad UPRIGHT vertical fan that reads as turkey. And it is the same asset as the neighbour - see below - so it carries no species information.

GROUSE COMPARISON - the judge's 'effectively the Grouse card in a darker tone' is confirmed quantitatively. A per-pixel diff of Turkey.png against Grouse.png at 440x440 gives 85.1% of pixels within a delta of 12/765, and the silhouette XOR (8,090 px) renders as nothing but a thin 2-3px outline tracing the identical bird - same head dome, same bill wedge, same wing scapular oval, same two yellow three-toed legs at the same stance, same 8-feather drooping fan. Turkey is the identical chassis scaled up a few percent and shifted a couple of pixels, with the palette pushed darker/warmer. Grouse's mustReads are being satisfied by the same geometry, so this asset carries no Turkey identity at all.

FEET - fine but generic: two golden legs, a hock kink, three forward toes and a short hind spur each. Not a defect, not a turkey signal either.

Band: FAIL upheld. Two of three must-reads (bare warty blue-and-red head with wattle; breast beard) are wholly absent, and the third is present in form but is a shared drooping lateral fan rather than the broad upright fan, delivered by an asset that is 85% pixel-identical to Grouse. Fix needs: bare red/blue caruncled skin from bill base over the crown and down the neck, a snood drooping over the bill, a red dangling wattle at the throat, a dark bristle beard off the mid-breast, and the rectrix fan re-rotated to a broad upright semicircle standing above the back line.

rows.readsAs: a speckled easter egg or a river pebble with five holes drilled in a row
rows.defect: There is no animal here at all - just a smooth mint-green domed ellipse floating over a shadow. The huge muscular foot is absent, the frilly sensory tentacle fringe around the rim is absent, and the shell is a fat 3D egg rather than the flat ear-shaped plate an abalone is. The only must-read present is the row of five holes, and it sits on an egg. It is the identical stamp used for Cowrie and Limpet.
rows.fix: Flatten the shell into a low ear-shaped oval seen from above with the spire knob at the rear-left, and let a pale muscular foot bulge out all around the rim with a dense fringe of short tentacles along its edge.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and the shared-stamp part is worse than stated. What I actually saw at full size and at 4x crop-zoom, plus a brightness-boosted silhouette pass (alpha/luma threshold) to hunt for small appendages: a single tilted ellipse, pale sage-green, filled with soft blurred pink/mint/cream blotches, five evenly spaced flat black dots running left-to-right across the upper third of the face, and a detached dark ellipse shadow floating well below the body. That is the entire drawing.

MUST-READ 1 - 'flat ear-shaped shell with a row of open holes along one edge': FAILS on both halves. The shell is not ear-shaped: measured body bbox is 181x129 px, aspect 1.40, against the packet's aspect:2, and it is a symmetric egg-oval with no narrow end, no off-centre coiled apex, no growth lines, no muscle scar, no aperture or underside. The hole row exists but is NOT correctly present, contrary to the original judge's concession that it is the one must-read that lands: the five dots are uniform flat black circles with no countersunk shading and no raised rim, and at col x=220 the row sits at y~172 where the body spans y128-y256, i.e. about one third down the face, inboard on the shell rather than hugging the near margin. They also run the full width of the body instead of clustering along the anterior portion. They read as polka dots on an easter egg, which is exactly the wrong reading.

MUST-READ 2 - 'huge muscular foot': ABSENT. Confirmed by the brightness-boosted pass, where the body blows out to pure white against the background: the silhouette is a mathematically clean unbroken ellipse. Nothing protrudes anywhere on the perimeter, top, bottom, left or right. There is no foot, no sole, no skirt, no mantle spilling past the shell.

MUST-READ 3 - 'frilly sensory tentacle fringe around the rim': ABSENT. Same evidence - zero perturbation of the rim contour at any point. The only edge detail is a thin pale crescent rim-light along the upper-right margin, which is a lighting highlight, not anatomy.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM (the verdict stands, two of the stated causes are wrong or imprecise):
(a) 'the shell is a fat 3D egg' is wrong in direction. There is no volumetric egg modelling here at all - it is a FLAT 2D disc with soft airbrushed blotches and one thin edge highlight. The defect is not excess roundness in Z, it is total absence of shell architecture in the plane: no ear outline, no spiral apex, no ribbing, no rim. Fixing this by flattening the shading would change nothing; the outline itself has to be redrawn as an asymmetric ear plate.
(b) 'the only must-read present is the hole row' overstates what survives. Nothing survives. The hole row is misplaced (mid-face, not along the margin) and misdrawn (flat dots, not open perforations).
(c) 'sitting on the same stamp used for Cowrie and Limpet' is CONFIRMED and understated. I opened both siblings. Measured body bboxes: Abalone 181x129 aspect 1.40, Cowrie 149x109 aspect 1.37, Limpet 212x149 aspect 1.42 - same tilt angle, same detached shadow ellipse, same five-dot row, differing only in hue and scale. Critically, Limpet's own mustRead is 'simple uncoiled cone shell like a hat - ribbed radiating ridges to a slightly off-centre apex - clamped flush against rock' with NO holes, and Cowrie's is 'glossy egg-smooth shell with no visible spire' with a toothed underside slit, also NO holes - yet both carry the identical hole row. So the perforations are family wallpaper applied to three species indiscriminately, which means they do not distinguish the Abalone from anything; the one feature the judge credited is the very feature proving the chassis is shared. All three specified aspects (2, 1.8, 1.8) collapse to the same rendered ~1.4, so the aspect field is not being honoured either.
(d) One defect neither of us listed: posture:crawling is unreadable. The body hovers with a gap above a separate soft ellipse shadow, reading as a floating object, not an animal clamped to or gliding over a substrate.

The 'speckled easter egg / holed river pebble' reading is exactly right. Zero of three must-reads are readable, and the organism does not read as an animal at all. FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: a peeled banana or a yellow chilli lying on its side
rows.defect: The bright yellow shell-less loaf is right and it does carry slug mass, but the head end is a 5-pixel jagged crest - there is no pair of long upper eyestalks with eyes on the tips and no pair of short lower feelers, so the animal has no readable head. The pneumostome (breathing hole) on the mantle saddle is nowhere on the body, and the mantle saddle itself is not delineated from the tail.
rows.fix: Grow two long upper tentacles with dark bulbs at their tips and two short lower feelers from the head end, and cut a visible dark breathing hole into a raised mantle saddle over the front third.

rows.readsAs: a fossil ammonite, or a coiled rope mat
rows.defect: Wrong organism. It is a flat planispiral ridged disc - the same disc used for all six snails here - with no flared lip, no knobby pointed spire, and no stalked eyes; the packet calls for prominent eyes and there are none. There is also a stray unattached brown blob half-hidden behind the shell at the lower right and no foot at all, so the whole thing hangs in mid-air over its shadow.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as a heavy asymmetric shell with a stepped knobby spire at the top-left and a wide glossy pink flared lip sweeping down the right, and push two long stalked eyes out from under that lip.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the PNG at 1x and then at 4x and 8-9x crops of the left lobe, the bottom edge and the lower-right quadrant. The FAIL stands: this reads as a nautilus/ammonite, not a conch. But three parts of the stated cause are wrong or incomplete, and the fix should be made against this description instead.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN. A single PLANISPIRAL coil — every whorl lies in the picture plane, coiling ~2.5 turns counter-clockwise into a small smooth sphere-boss at the geometric centre (~x232,y205 of 440). The whorl surface is built from densely packed crescent rib segments that read as a coiled rope. The terminal (outermost) whorl ends at about 9 o'clock as a fat, fully CLOSED rounded lobe — there is no aperture opening cut into it at all, so there is nothing for a lip to flare from. Under the shell sits a detached soft elliptical ground shadow at y~290-320; the shell body's lowest ribs stop ~15px above it, so the animal does hang in mid-air. Aspect measures ~1.25 wide against a spec of 1.5, and the silhouette is a disc, not a spindle.

MUST-READ 1, broad flared lip — ABSENT, but the judge's 'no lip' is worth refining: there IS a lip-shaped element in the draw list and it has misfired. A hairline pale blue-grey stroke (~1.5px, colour ~#c8d0d8) sweeps from x~168,y~128 up over the crown, down the right side and terminates at x~285,y~272. Its radius and centre do not match the shell: at the top it floats clear of the shell in empty space, and down the right side it cuts THROUGH the shell body and straight across the brown blob. It is an unfilled, mis-centred outline — so the correct diagnosis is 'lip stroke drawn as a stray mis-registered hairline with no fill and no thickness', not 'lip omitted'. That stroke is the single most conspicuous artifact in the image.

MUST-READ 2, knobby pointed spire — ABSENT, and the judge is right. The spire here is a flat central boss: one small smooth ball sitting in the eye of the spiral, with zero elevation off the plane and zero nodules. A conch spire must project out of the plane as a stepped cone with a ring of blunt knobs on each whorl shoulder. There is not one knob anywhere on this asset.

MUST-READ 3, two long stalked eyes peering out from under the lip — ABSENT, fully confirmed. eyes:prominent, headFrac 0.15, and there is no head, no eyestalk, no eye highlight, no tentacle anywhere in the frame. I checked every edge of the silhouette at 8x.

CORRECTION TO THE JUDGE ON THE BROWN BLOB. They called it a 'stray unattached brown blob stranded behind the shell' and separately said 'no foot at all'. Those are the same element counted twice, and 'unattached' is wrong. The blob is a flat dark-brown ellipse (~55x45px, colour ~#6d5045, no shading, no texture, no rim light) centred near x~305,y~255, and the shell's lower-right whorl clearly OVERLAPS it — it is z-ordered behind the shell and emerges from beneath the rim, i.e. it is attached, it is almost certainly the foot/soft-tissue emitter firing. The real defect is that the foot is emitted (a) far too small relative to the shell, (b) at 4-5 o'clock on the shell's SIDE instead of extending forward and underneath, (c) as an untextured flat ellipse with no sole, no ripple, no taper and no head end, and (d) not reaching the ground plane, so it neither supports the shell nor reads as tissue. So 'no foot at all' should be restated as 'foot present but degenerate and mis-placed'.

NET. Two of three must-reads (spire, stalked eyes) are genuinely absent, the third (flared lip) survives only as a stray unfilled hairline that actively damages the image, the posture:crawling contract is broken because nothing touches ground, and the overall silhouette identifies the organism as a fossil ammonite. FAIL is correct and I am not overturning it.

rows.readsAs: a mottled orange egg with five holes punched in it - the Abalone in a different colour
rows.defect: This is the Abalone stamp recoloured apricot: same ellipse, same tilt, same row of five black holes in the same positions. Those holes are the abalone's diagnostic and they are anatomically wrong on a cowrie. The identity must-read - the long toothed slit running the length of the underside - is entirely absent, and so are the patterned mantle flaps folding up over the shell. Nothing is left that says cowrie.
rows.fix: Delete the hole row, view the shell from below-side so the full-length slit with its comb of teeth on both lips is the dominant feature, and lap two lobed patterned mantle flaps up over the shell from each side.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and the claim is confirmed at BOTH the pixel and the source level.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (read at 1x, then re-cropped and upscaled 4x around the body): a single tilted ellipse, body bbox 152x111 px at x145-296 / y132-242 in a 440x440 frame, filled with a warm sienna-to-apricot radial gradient and overlaid with ~26 blurred pastel blotches (mint, peach, lilac) that read as soft airbrush noise rather than any marking. Across the upper third runs a row of FIVE dark circular holes of steadily decreasing radius on a slightly descending arc. A thin pale specular rim runs along the upper-left edge. Below the body sits a flat elliptical drop shadow. That is the entire asset. There is no head, no tentacles, no eye, no foot, no aperture, no mantle edge, no separate lobe of any kind, and no line, groove or notch anywhere on the lower half - the bottom of the ellipse is unbroken gradient plus blotch.

COMPARED SIDE BY SIDE WITH Abalone.png: identical ellipse, identical -0.18 rad tilt, identical five-dot descending arc in the same relative position, identical rim arc, identical shadow. Only the hue differs (Abalone seafoam green, Cowrie sienna/apricot). This is not a resemblance - it is literally the same draw call. packages/art/src/faunaoverrides2.ts line 1382 registers 'Cowrie': marineShell(..., { hue: '#8b5a2b', kind: 'abalone' }) against line 1378 'Abalone': marineShell(..., { hue: '#6b8f80', kind: 'abalone' }). The kind:'abalone' branch (lines 1060-1071) draws exactly one ellipse, 26 softMark blobs, then a loop `for (let i=0;i<5;i++) arc(cx - w*0.5 + i*w*0.26, cy - h*0.42 + i*3, 5.5 - i*0.4)` commented "THE RESPIRATORY HOLES - the abalone read", then the rim. Nothing species-specific is reachable. NOTE FOR THE FIX: Limpet (line 1379) is on the SAME stamp too - this is a three-species chassis collision inside one family, not a two-species one.

MUST-READ AUDIT against the packet row (aspect 1.8 / headFrac 0.15 / eyes small / posture crawling / mustRead: glossy egg-smooth shell with no visible spire - long toothed slit running the length of the underside - patterned mantle flaps folding up over the shell):
1. Glossy egg-smooth, no spire - HALF PRESENT. The dome is spireless and smooth, which is the one thing the stamp gets right by accident. But it is punctured by five holes, and the surface is a fuzzy pastel airbrush rather than the wet-porcelain gloss with crisp spots/bands that carries a cowrie.
2. Long toothed slit down the underside - ABSENT. I looked specifically for it at 4x. The entire lower half is featureless gradient. Not small, not faint, not off-frame: not drawn.
3. Patterned mantle flaps folding up over the shell - ABSENT. No flap silhouette, no papillae, no seam where a flap would meet the shell. The blurred blotches are inside a clip of the same ellipse and never break the outline.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM (verdict stands, two details need sharpening): (a) the judge called it 'recoloured apricot' - the source hue is #8b5a2b, a sienna/brown; it reads apricot only because the radial gradient lightens the upper-left. Cosmetic, but the fix should target the hue token, not a literal apricot. (b) The judge said 'nothing left says cowrie', which is right, but understates the damage: the abalone stamp it inherits is not a complete abalone either - Abalone's own must-reads (huge muscular foot, frilly sensory tentacle fringe) are equally missing from that branch. So what the Cowrie inherits is not 'an abalone in the wrong colour' but a bare mottled ellipse with five pores. Additionally, unreported by the judge: posture is specified 'crawling' and eyes 'small', yet no foot and no eye exist at all, and the rendered aspect is 1.37 against a specified 1.8.

FIX DIRECTION: Cowrie needs its own branch, not a hue on kind:'abalone'. Required: drop the five-pore loop entirely (anatomically wrong - cowries have no tremata); keep a smooth spireless ovate dome but give it a hard glossy specular streak; draw the aperture as a long narrow slit running nearly the full length of the underside with a comb of short perpendicular teeth on BOTH lips; and add two patterned mantle flaps rising from the slit and folding up over the left and right shoulders of the shell so they break the ellipse outline and read as living tissue over shell.

rows.readsAs: a snail, but on second look a small ammonite parked on a slipper sole
rows.defect: Coiled shell and gliding foot are both present and the silhouette does read snail-shaped, but the shell is a perfectly flat ammonite disc with no spire height and no aperture, and the pair of thin head tentacles is reduced to a 3-prong fork with no head behind it - the animal is a shell sitting on a lens with no body between them.
rows.fix: Wind the shell into a low helical cone so the spire steps back and up, and model an actual head lobe emerging from under it carrying two long thin separated tentacles.

rows.readsAs: a generic snail - indistinguishable from Snail, Water Snail, Sea Snail and Freshwater Snail except for the tan colour
rows.defect: The packet's explicit note is violated: there are no eyes at the tips of long upper tentacles, and there is no second pair of tentacles either - only the same 3-prong fork that every other shelled asset in this batch wears. The foot has no rippling sole, it is a plain flat lens with a hard edge. The shell is a flat coil, not carried up on the back.
