Over the whole animal 87.6% of lit pixels sit in one hue bin (150 deg, green); the only off-green clusters are hue 30 (the brown bill), hue 45 (the yellow feet) and hue 210 (low-saturation background/rim bleed). Restricting the sample to a tight head+throat box (x175-240, y155-215) gives the SAME distribution — 86.2% hue 150, no second chromatic cluster anywhere. So the chin, throat and upper breast are the identical green as the mantle, with only value shading between them. There is no ruby/magenta/violet/orange patch, and no hard-edged gorget boundary. CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM: their conclusion and their three named defects are all accurate, but two details need sharpening for whoever fixes this. First, 'no hover blur' is not literally true at pixel level — there IS a set of faint dark diagonal streak strokes in the image, but they sit UNDER AND BEHIND THE TAIL, not at the wing, they are very low contrast against the shadow, and they read as tail-feather hatching, not as motion. A fixer grepping for 'add blur' should know a streak primitive already renders there and is simply in the wrong anatomical slot. Second, the claim omits the pointed tail wedge, which is a real part of why the silhouette reads waterfowl: small ball head on a thick neck, dome back, pointed rear wedge. Their 'plump green kiwi or quail chick' is directionally right; I would call it a green duck/rail chick with a probe bill. The identity is carried entirely by the bill; strip the bill and nothing in the silhouette says hummingbird. TO FIX: rotate the body to a near-vertical hover axis, delete the ground feet and shadow (leave at most two tucked pin-feet), replace the single folded ovoid with a pair of narrow swept blades plus a translucent arc/ghost sweep, slim the torso off the sphere, and paint a distinct high-saturation contrasting-hue patch across the chin/throat with a hard lower edge.

rows.readsAs: An Appaloosa pony / spotted Shetland pony
rows.defect: The identity must-read is absent: the back is level (with a slight rise at the croup) instead of sloping sharply from high shoulders down to low hips. The neck is a short pony neck, not a massive fused shoulder-neck, and the head is a domed foal skull with a drooping blunt muzzle and no jaw mass at all — no crushing bite is readable. Limbs are four equal straight columns ending in blocky hoof-like feet with no digitigrade paw and no hock/elbow angulation. Ears are small rounded pony ears on top of the dome. Only the blotchy black spotting gestures at the reference, and on this body it reads as Appaloosa coat marking.
rows.fix: Rebuild the topline and limb skeleton: raise the withers well above the croup so the spine falls in a continuous steep line to the hips, shorten and angulate the hind limb (visible hock well above the foot, hip mass inside the silhouette), and replace the hoof-blocks with compact four-toed digitigrade paws; then hang a deep-jawed short-faced skull with heavy cheek/mandible bulk off a thickened neck.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but THREE parts of the original claim are wrong and must not be used as the fix brief. I read the 440x440 PNG, then re-read it at 3x-14x on the head, both feet, the tail, and with a per-column silhouette trace overlaid so the topline is measured, not eyeballed.

CORRECTION 1 - THE SLOPING TOPLINE IS PRESENT, NOT ABSENT, AND THE CROUP IS NOT HIGHER. Measured top-of-silhouette per column (animal faces right, ground line y~312): withers/back-front at x=245 -> y=157; x=220 -> 166; x=200 -> 173; x=180 -> 175; rump top x=150-190 -> y=175-179; then it falls away into the tail base. So the back drops ~22px over ~95px front-to-back, ~13 degrees, in the CORRECT direction. The claim 'level, croup slightly higher' is factually reversed. What is actually wrong: (a) the drop is only ~24% of shoulder body-depth (withers 157 to belly ~250 = 93px) where a hyena needs roughly double that; (b) there is no withers/scapula hump at all - the line is one smooth even arc off the neck instead of a high shoulder crest ramping to a low sacrum; (c) the hindquarters are not crouched - the hind limb is the same length as the fore and both terminate on the same flat ground line at y~312, so the rear end never sits down. FIX = steepen the ramp, build a withers hump behind the neck, and shorten/crouch the hind limb. Do NOT 'reverse a backwards slope'; there is none to reverse.

CORRECTION 2 - THE NECK IS NOT MISSING. There IS a heavy pale-tan neck-and-chest mass behind the jaw, running from the throatlatch down to the brisket with a visible collar seam; it is arguably the bulkiest single region on the animal. What fails is its ATTACHMENT and carriage: the mass hangs low and forward like a foal's throatlatch/dewlap and merges into the barrel without ever rising into a shoulder crest, so it reads as a thick throat rather than a hyena's power-column neck feeding a humped shoulder.

CORRECTION 3 - THE EARS ARE NOT SMALL. The ear is a fairly large rounded taupe disc (~20px on a ~100px head), with a second smaller darker oval just forward of it. The must-read asks for 'rounded ears' and the SHAPE is correct. The defect is construction, not size: both are flat discs painted onto the side of the skull and they break the crown silhouette by exactly zero pixels - the top contour from x=305 to x=320 is an unbroken smooth dome at y=111. Ears need to be cut into the silhouette.

WHAT THE ORIGINAL CLAIM GOT RIGHT, and why FAIL still stands:
- HEAD/JAW - correct and decisive. The cranium is a smooth featureless dome: no sagittal crest, no zygomatic arch, no masseter/cheek mass. The muzzle is a long blunt snout that DROOPS below the mouthline and overhangs a receding lower jaw, capped by a big rounded near-black nose; the mouth is a single thin horizontal score. The lower half of the muzzle is a dull olive-brown wedge that reads as a draping upper lip, not a mandible. This is a tapir/moose/foal head. The 'massive thick neck AND heavy jaws' must-read is half-satisfied at best.
- FEET - correct, and if anything understated. Both fore and hind feet are identical dark-brown clogs, distinctly WIDER than the leg above them, flat-bottomed, with a coronet-like flare and three faint vertical scores as the only hint of toes. Above each foot is a dark banded fetlock joint and a pale pastern with an angle change. That is an ungulate foot with a fetlock, not a digitigrade carnivoran paw with four toes and blunt claws. This alone puts the organism outside Carnivora.
- LIMBS - correct. Four near-straight columns, near-equal length, only the faintest stifle hint on the hind. Hyena forelimbs must be conspicuously longer than the hind.
- MARKINGS - correct that this is the only good read. The blotching is genuinely decent: irregular merged dark blotches, denser over flank and haunch, sparser on neck and legs. On this chassis it does read as Appaloosa.
- ONE DEFECT THE CLAIM MISSED: the tail. It is a pale flat rounded paddle/fan with a fringe of individual hairs along the trailing edge only, and NO black tip - not a bushy black-tipped brush. It reads more like a fan or a folded wing than any hyena tail.

VERDICT: of the three must-reads, one (topline) is present but roughly half the amplitude it needs and lacks the shoulder hump; one (massive neck + heavy jaws) is half-present - neck yes, jaw/skull emphatically no; one (rounded ears + blotchy spots) is half-present - spots yes, ears drawn as flat non-silhouetted decals. Combined with ungulate hooves, fetlocks, equal-length columnar limbs and a drooping hornless-foal muzzle, a viewer shown this names it a spotted pony/foal, not a hyena. FAIL is the right band.

rows.readsAs: A shaggy cream pony or a long-haired goat
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are missing outright. There is NO erect crest of mane hair along the spine — the topline is a clean smooth level curve with only a faint fur texture, so the single most diagnostic feature of this animal is invisible. The back does not slope: shoulders and hips sit at the same height and the croup is if anything higher, and the front legs are the same length as the hind legs, directly contradicting the packet note. Ears are small rounded pony ears, not the large pointed ears named. The body striping is a soft pale hatched texture rather than bold vertical black bands, and the legs — where the banding is most legible on the real animal — are unmarked. It is the identical silhouette to the Spotted Hyena in this same batch, recoloured.
rows.fix: Add a tall standing crest of coarse mane hair breaking the spine outline from nape to croup, and re-cut the topline so it drops steeply from high shoulders to low hips on longer forelegs; then restate the stripes as bold dark vertical bars, including on the legs.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but three of the five stated causes are wrong and the fix should be made against what is written here, not against the original claim. I read the PNG at 1x, then re-cropped and re-read the head at 8x, the topline at 6x, the flank at 6x, the tail at 4x and the legs at 4x, and I ran a per-column silhouette scan (top/bottom opaque pixel every 4px) so the topline and leg claims are measured, not eyeballed.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Cream/bone quadruped facing right on a 440px canvas. Body spans x=132..366. Head is a rounded skull at x=270..366 carrying ONE very large face-on circular ear disc (~55px across on a ~110px skull) with a darker crescent concha on its leading edge, a separate brown oval inboard of it, and a small amber eye with a black pupil below-right of the oval. Muzzle is a slender tapering tube ending in a bulbous knob with a big dark nose, plus a flat grey lower-jaw/tongue wedge projecting forward under it. Trunk is covered edge to edge in fine light/dark fur-hair hatch strokes. Tail is an oversized bushy fan/paddle at x=76..130 with radiating hairs and pale chevron banding. Four slender legs ending in small dark toed feet; a thin dark cuff above the hind foot.

CLAIM 1 - 'NO erect spinal crest at all; topline is a smooth unbroken curve.' CORRECT, confirmed at 6x. The dorsal edge from rump to poll is one clean vector curve; not a single hair breaks the silhouette. There is a faint pale ridge stroke running inside the edge along the neck and withers, but it sits under the outline and reads as sheen, not as a mane. The single most defining feature of Hyaena hyaena - the erect crest that doubles the animal's apparent height - is absent.

CLAIM 2 - 'the back does not slope; shoulders and hips are level.' WRONG. Measured: hip/rump top edge y=175 at x=180; withers top edge y=146 at x=250. The shoulders sit ~30px ABOVE the hips, which is ~27% of body depth (belly at the shoulder is y=259, so depth 113px), and the downhill run is visible in the render. The real defect is different and should be described differently: the slope is a GENTLE, CONTINUOUS rise (~12-13 degrees across the trunk) that never breaks into a distinct high-withers hump - the topline just keeps climbing straight on into the neck and head with no shoulder peak and no dip behind it. So the must-read 'sloping steeply down from high shoulders to low hips' is under-delivered, not missing. Fixing this means adding a withers hump and a saddle behind it, not adding slope from zero.

CLAIM 3 - 'the forelegs are the same length as the hind legs.' WRONG. Both feet do land on the same ground line (front foot bottom y=315, hind foot bottom y=315), but the exposed leg lengths differ and differ in the WRONG DIRECTION: front leg from belly y=259 to y=315 = 56px; hind leg from belly y=247 to y=315 = 68px. The front leg is visibly SHORTER than the hind. The packet note ('Front legs are noticeably longer than the hind legs') is therefore inverted, not merely unmet - the art is doing the opposite of the note.

CLAIM 4 - 'ears are small and rounded.' HALF WRONG. The ear is not small - it is the largest single feature on the head, a big saucer disc roughly a third of the skull. 'Large' is satisfied. What fails is (a) it is perfectly ROUND with no point or triangular tip anywhere on its outline, and (b) it is drawn face-on as one frontal disc pasted on the side of the skull rather than as a paired erect pinna, which is what makes it read as a ram/possum ear rather than a hyena's. Also failing quietly: the muzzle is a slender tapering tube, not the 'heavy blunt muzzle' the must-read calls for, and there is no massive jaw mass behind it.

CLAIM 5 - 'stripes are a faint pale hatched texture with completely unmarked legs.' CORRECT. At 6x the flank carries ONLY fur-hair hatching in the base cream - there are zero dark vertical bars anywhere on the body, and the legs are entirely unmarked except for one small dark cuff above the hind foot. The species' second diagnostic marking is absent outright.

CLAIM 6 - 'it is the Spotted Hyena's silhouette recoloured.' CORRECT, and stronger than stated. Rendered side by side with Spotted_Hyena.png from the same batch, the two share: the same topline curve, the same trunk mass and belly line, the same four-leg placement and slender leg form, the same small dark toed feet with the same hind-leg cuff, the same big round ear disc plus brown oval plus amber eye, the same knob muzzle with dark nose and grey jaw wedge, and the same bushy fan tail with the same chevron banding. It is not a recolour - it is the identical chassis with the blotch layer DELETED. The two hyenas are one body, and the body reads as a shaggy pony/ram, not a hyaenid.

BAND. FAIL stands. Of three must-reads: the crest is absent; the large-pointed-ear / heavy-blunt-muzzle read fails on shape (large but round, and the muzzle is fine not heavy); the sloping back is present but shallow and hump-less. Add the absent stripes and the shared chassis and there is nothing on this asset that identifies a Striped Hyena.

rows.readsAs: a small hunched brine shrimp
rows.defect: The C-curl and the fanned tail do read, but the underside carries only four identical straight bristles - not the many segmented legs of differing shapes the reference calls for - and nothing about the body reads as laterally flattened; there is also only one antenna pair plus a stray, not two clear pairs. It is the identical painting used for Copepod.
rows.fix: Rebuild the underside as three distinct leg banks - forward-hooked gnathopods, straight walking legs, then backward-raked swimming legs - and flatten the body into a compressed blade so the side view is visibly the widest view.

rows.readsAs: a white lampshade or a paper lantern
rows.defect: A smooth ivory cone with evenly spaced vertical seam lines, wide at the base and cleanly truncated at the top. There are no trapdoor plates - just a small dark notch - and there are ZERO feathery cirri sweeping out of the opening, which is the one thing that makes a barnacle read as alive. It is not attached to any substrate, so it floats as a piece of furniture.
rows.fix: Open the summit into a pair of interlocking beak-shaped opercular plates and sweep a fan of curled feathery cirri out of the gap; roughen the plate walls with chalky overlapping ridges and seat the cone on a rock.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, but one of the two stated causes is factually wrong and must not be used as the fix brief.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (measured + zoomed at 5x body / 12x summit and base):
Silhouette bbox is 139 x 105 px inside a 440 px canvas — width/height = 1.32. The reference row calls for aspect 0.9 (taller than wide, a volcano). The drawn form is ~47% too squat and too wide, which is the single biggest driver of the lampshade read: the profile is a low dome-frustum, not a volcano cone. Row-width scan is a smooth monotonic flare (73 -> 89 -> 103 -> 117 -> 129 -> 137 px) with no waist, no rim flare, no basal spread.

MUST-READ 1 — 'volcano-shaped chalky cone of fused plates': PARTIAL, weak. There ARE ~8 longitudinal panel divisions, so the plate COUNT is nominally represented, but they are hairline 1px dark pinstripes ruled over a perfectly smooth ivory gradient. No chalk grain, no relief, no shadow on either side of a suture, no overlapping/interlocking plate edges, no growth ridges, and the panels are exactly evenly spaced. That is a pleated fabric shade, not fused calcareous plates. The base terminates in a dead-straight horizontal cut with a soft contact shadow under it — a flat 2D bottom with no elliptical perspective and no basal encrusting rim, which is why it reads as a manufactured object resting on a table.

MUST-READ 2 — 'trapdoor plates at the summit': PRESENT. THE OTHER JUDGE IS WRONG ON THIS POINT. It is not 'only a small dark notch'. At 12x the summit carries a dark brown elliptical orifice, and inside it two bright near-white wedge/triangular plates, left and right, meeting along a dark vertical central slit — a legible pair of opercular valves. Do not 'add' the operculum; it exists. What it needs is scale and legibility: the whole aperture is only ~40 px wide against a 139 px body and it is crushed flat by the squat proportion, so at thumbnail size it collapses to the notch the other judge described.

MUST-READ 3 — 'feathery cirri sweeping out of the opening': GENUINELY ABSENT. Zero. There is nothing above, through or around the aperture but flat background pixels. No filaments, no fan, no curl, not even a suggestion at 12x. This is the defining animacy signal for the species and it is the reason the asset fails: with the cirri missing, nothing on the image marks it as a living animal, and the two opercular plates alone are too small and too geometric to carry that load.

ALSO CORRECTING THE CLAIM: 'unattached to any substrate' is true as an observation (no rock, shell or encrustation — just a soft drop shadow) but is NOT one of the three reference must-reads, so it should not be counted as a failed criterion. It is a supporting weakness for the sessile posture, not the defect.

FIX BRIEF: (1) restore the volcano proportion to aspect ~0.9 — take the height up, not the width down; (2) sweep a fan of curled feathery cirri out of the summit opening, biased to one side as if beating — this is the missing identity feature; (3) give the sutures real width, offset shading and slight irregularity so the plates read as chalky and fused rather than ruled; (4) enlarge the operculum that is already drawn so the two valves survive at thumbnail scale; (5) give the base an elliptical footing seated on a substrate.

rows.readsAs: a generic garden spider
rows.defect: Two tan spheres with a pinched waist and eight symmetrical thin legs, topped by an eight-dot spider eye cluster. Every identity cue is missing: no enormous forward-jutting chelicerae, no long leg-like pedipalps held out front, and no hairy segmented abdomen - the rear is a smooth egg. The note says it should appear to have ten front appendages; it has eight ordinary spider legs and nothing in front of the head.
rows.fix: Mount a pair of huge vertical scissor chelicerae on the front of the head - a third the body length - and add two extra long palps reaching forward past them so the animal reads as ten-limbed.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, and the original claim is accurate on all three counts; I add two further defects and one correction of emphasis. Viewed at 1x and again cropped 5x/11x on the head, left leg fan and abdomen (440x440 source).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a two-lobe top-down spider. Front lobe = a smooth tan egg (cephalothorax), rear lobe = a slightly larger smooth tan egg, joined at a wide waist with no pedicel. Eight legs total, four per side, ALL attached to the front lobe, all splayed laterally and rearward in a symmetric fan with a single knee bend each. A soft cast shadow ellipse sits under the body. This is the generic orb-weaver/garden-spider chassis.

MUST-READ 1 - 'enormous forward-jutting pincer jaws': ABSENT, and absent in the strongest sense. At 11x the front (left) edge of the head lobe is a clean unbroken elliptical arc. Nothing projects past that silhouette - no chelicerae, no pincer halves, no fangs, no mouthparts, not even a shaded bump suggesting them. The judge did not simply overlook something small; there is zero geometry forward of the carapace. This is the single defining feature of Solifugae (jaws ~1/3 of body length, held out front like a pair of nutcrackers) and the render has none of it.

MUST-READ 2 - 'long leg-like pedipalps held out in front like extra legs': ABSENT. Confirmed by direct count on the 5x left crop: exactly four limb roots leave the head sphere on the left side (one up-left, three left/down-left), mirrored on the right. Eight limbs, not ten. Not one limb is carried forward of the head as a feeler; the frontmost pair still sweeps backward at roughly 20-30 degrees off the body axis. The ten-limbed 'walking on eight, feeling with two' silhouette the note requires is not attempted.

MUST-READ 3 - 'hairy segmented tan abdomen': the tan is right, the rest is not. The abdomen is a smooth glossy egg with a specular highlight and three or four soft blurred darker blotches - a mottled paint pattern, not structure. There are NO segmentation rings, NO tergite bands, and NO setae on the abdomen at all. PARTIAL CORRECTION to the original claim: 'hairy' is not wholly missing from the asset - each leg segment does carry three to five small pale bristle spurs, clearly visible at 5x. So the hair vocabulary exists in the renderer; it is simply never applied to the body. A fix should reuse those leg bristles on the opisthosoma and add the ~10 transverse segment bands.

TWO DEFECTS THE ORIGINAL JUDGE DID NOT NAME: (a) EYES - a 2x2 grid of four glossy black domes sits on the side of the head lobe. That is an actively wrong, actively spider-signalling cue. A camel spider has ONE pair of median eyes on a raised ocular tubercle at the front-centre of the propeltidium. The four-eye grid is a second reason the asset reads 'garden spider' even before the missing jaws are noticed. (b) NO PROPELTIDIUM - headFrac 0.3 in the packet asks for a distinct head plate; the front lobe is one undifferentiated sphere with no carapace plate, no ocular tubercle and no head/thorax break.

BAND: FAIL is correct and not a close call. Zero of three must-reads read, the eye cue contradicts the species, and an untrained viewer shown this image would name it a spider, which the note explicitly forbids ('Not a true spider'). Nothing here is a polish-level miss - the identity geometry (jaws, forward palps, segmented abdomen) has to be authored from scratch.

rows.readsAs: a legless grub or a mealworm larva
rows.defect: A horizontal chain of ten identical tan spheres with a dark round head-ball at the right end. It has no legs at all - not even stubs - no antennae of any kind, and no arched hump; the topline is dead flat. Every one of the three must-reads (humped back, whip antennae longer than the body, huge folded hind legs) is absent, and the silhouette is the same bead chain used for the centipedes with the legs deleted.
rows.fix: Rebuild it as an insect: a strongly arched thorax-plus-abdomen hump, two hair-thin antennae running two body lengths off frame, and a pair of massively folded jackknife hind legs with the knees standing above the back.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and worse than stated. I read the PNG at 1x, then re-cropped and re-read the body at 3x (x55-395, y110-260) and the head at 6x (x290-380, y130-210), then ran a pixel scan of the whole 440x440 canvas. Every non-background pixel in the entire image lies inside ONE blob: bbox x78-361, y142-217 (a stray 5-pixel antialias column at x=361 is the head's own edge). Nothing whatsoever protrudes from that blob.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a single horizontal chain of ~9 overlapping tan spheres, largest at the left (tail) end and tapering gently rightward, terminating in a tan sphere that carries a dark-brown circular face disc with one tiny white eye-highlight dot. A detached dark ellipse sits well below at y~258-292 — that is the ground shadow, not any part of the animal. A thin white crescent arc on the second-from-left sphere (approx x95-135, y152-185) is a rim/specular highlight on the tail segment; it is the only thing on the asset that could be mistaken for an appendage, and it is not one.

MUST-READS, ONE BY ONE:
1. 'strongly humped arched back' — ABSENT. Measured topline per column: y=156 at x108, shallow peak y=142 at x192-198, back to y=160 at x330. That is 14 px of camber across a 283 px body (~5%). Effectively flat.
2. 'whip antennae far longer than the body' — ABSENT, verified: zero non-background pixels exist beyond x=361 or before x=78. Antennae longer than the body would need to span 280+ px; there is not one pixel of them. The head zoom shows a bare sphere with no mandibles, no palps, no antennal bases.
3. 'hugely long folded hind legs' — ABSENT, verified: zero non-background pixels below y=217 apart from the separate ground shadow. There are no legs of any kind, not even stubs.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM (the verdict stands, but three details are wrong and the fix must not be built against them):
- 'a dark head ball' is WRONG. The head is NOT a dark sphere. It is a TAN sphere the same colour as every body segment, overlaid with a dark-brown circular face patch and a single white eye pip. The fix needs a real head capsule shape, not a recolour of the existing terminal ball.
- 'ten tan spheres' — I count nine body lobes plus the head lobe; near enough, but note they are undifferentiated: there is no thorax/abdomen break, no pronotal shield, no segmentation ridges, just identical overlapping circles of one radius.
- 'dead-flat topline' is slightly overstated. It is a shallow 14px bow, not literally flat. It still reads flat and is nowhere near a humped back, so the conclusion holds.

DEFECT THE ORIGINAL JUDGE MISSED, and it is the biggest one: the silhouette aspect is 283x76 = 3.72, against a reference aspect of 1.4. The body is ~2.7x too elongated. That elongation, more than any single missing appendage, is what forces the mealworm/grub read; even if legs and antennae were bolted on, a 3.7-aspect tube would still not read as a camel cricket. Any fix must recompose the chassis to a short, deep, strongly domed body near aspect 1.4 with a distinct head capsule, then add the whip antennae and the massive folded hind femora.

Packet note 'wingless - do not give it the folded wing-covers of a field cricket' is technically satisfied, but only vacuously: the asset has no wings because it has no features at all.

rows.readsAs: a centipede, or a legged caterpillar on a bad read
rows.defect: Antennae and a side leg fringe are present so the centipede read mostly lands, but the body is a chain of round beads - visibly tubular, not the flattened plated ribbon the note demands - and the legs only appear under the rear two thirds, leaving the front third bare so you cannot see one pair per segment. At roughly 3:1 rendered it is nowhere near the 8:1 length the reference asks for.
rows.fix: Swap the sphere chain for overlapping flat tergite plates and hang one leg pair off EVERY plate from the head back, then stretch the whole body to about eight times its depth.

rows.readsAs: a small purple crab
rows.defect: It is the Crab painting in purple - same striped barrel carapace, same two lollipop claws, same two stick legs per side. Both claws are the same size and both are small flat paddles, so the massive crushing claw with one much larger is absent; the legs are thin wires that barely exceed the shell width rather than long heavy armoured limbs spanning far wider than the body; the tucked calcified abdomen is not indicated at all.
rows.fix: Give it one huge armoured crusher claw dwarfing the other, thicken and lengthen all eight walking legs to twice the shell width with visible segment armour, and tuck a plated abdomen under the rear.

rows.readsAs: a shrimp - specifically, the Amphipod again in orange
rows.defect: This is pixel-for-pixel the Amphipod chassis recoloured. It reads as the wrong organism: the body is a hunched two-hump shrimp rather than a teardrop that is widest at the front and tapers back, the antennae trail loosely behind rather than standing outstretched as wide as the body is long, and it carries one large glossy paired-looking black eye where a calanoid has a single tiny median eyespot. The forked bristly tail is buried in the same fan the Amphipod uses.
rows.fix: Redraw from scratch as a smooth teardrop prosome with a narrow tapering urosome, two rigid antennae held straight out sideways at full body length, a clean forked caudal ramus with long bristles, and a single dot eyespot.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG, then re-cropped the creature bbox and upscaled it 4x to inspect the head, antennae, legs and tail. FAIL stands, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and must not be fixed against.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a two-lobe hunched body. Front lobe is a mottled ovoid head-thorax; behind it and OVERLAPPING it sits a SECOND, LARGER, HIGHER rounded hump. The silhouette is therefore widest at the REAR and tapers FORWARD - the exact inverse of the mustRead 'teardrop head-body wider at the front and tapering back'. Measured silhouette is roughly 260x230px, an aspect near 1.1:1 against the spec aspect of 2.2 - it is far too stubby and there is no elongate prosome->narrow urosome axis anywhere in the drawing. This is the single defining must-read and it is absent.

CORRECTION 1 (judge wrong on antenna direction and length): the antennae are NOT 'trailing loosely behind'. There are three thin strokes and ALL THREE project ANTERIORLY, forward of the head - two rise from the top of the head sweeping up-and-left off the frame, and a third, much longer one leaves the head just under/behind the eye and sweeps down-and-left, exiting bottom-left. The longest is roughly equal to the body length, so the LENGTH criterion ('as wide as the body is long') is broadly met. The real defect is POSE and WEIGHT: a calanoid holds its first antennae as two stiff, straight, near-symmetric rods held out LATERALLY, perpendicular to the body axis, forming a hard T-crossbar silhouette. Here they are limp, curved, asymmetric hair-thin whiskers drooping forward-and-down like a shrimp's. Fix the pose (symmetric pair, straight, held at ~90 deg to the body), not the length.

CORRECTION 2 (judge wrong on eye count): the packet note asks for a SINGLE simple median eye spot and not paired stalked eyes, and the drawing does show exactly ONE eye - so the count is already correct. Beware: the shell surface carries a scatter of mottled mid-gray blotches, which at thumbnail size could be mistaken for internal organs -- they are decorative speckle, not a gut tube or brood chamber, and they must be replaced by an actual translucent shell with a dark gut line and a brood pouch behind the neck. (3) The aspect claim is the weakest part and is wrong as stated. The full ink bbox is 185 wide x 217 tall (W/H 0.85) -- i.e. TALLER than wide and close to the 0.8 spec -- but only because the long down-left antenna whip stretches the box. The BODY mass alone (luminance-thresholded, >120) is 86 x 78, W/H ~= 1.10. So it is MILDLY wider than tall, not 'much wider than tall'; the miss is 1.10 vs 0.80, real but modest, and re-proportioning alone would not save this asset. (4) The judge did not mention the two loudest wrong-organism signals, which belong at the top of any fix list: the exposed straight stick legs under the body (Daphnia's thoracic limbs are hidden INSIDE the carapace and never read as walking legs) and the spread shrimp caudal fan at the rear (Daphnia has a single fine tail spine and no fan whatsoever). rows.readsAs: a cartoon mouse wearing a firework of straw

rows.readsAs: a small grey duck-billed lump, closest to a platypus or a shaved guinea pig

Aspect and neckless-cylinder read are the ONE must-read that lands (mustRead 3, 'cylindrical neckless velvet body') - though the streak texture reads coarse/wiry rather than velvet-plush. A short dark stub tail sits at the rear (left) end.

HEAD (right end): a rounded skull carrying a LARGE dark bead eye with a bright white specular highlight - unmissable at 10x and still visible at full-size. It is a narrow tube of near-uniform thickness attached low and forward of the eye, running horizontally with a slight downward set and ending in a BLUNT ROUNDED tip - anteater/tapir proboscis rather than a duck's spatulate bill. It is the same grey-brown as the pelt with no pink at all. So the judge's core point is right - it is NOT a pink pointed fleshy cone - but the described shape is wrong, and the fix is 'shorten it, taper it to a point, tint the distal half pink', not 'narrow a flat bill'.

FOREPAWS - the identity must-read - CONFIRMED ABSENT, and worse than reported. Zooming the fore region shows two short cylindrical peg legs (near and far side) each terminating in a dark glossy HOOF-LIKE toe cap with a white specular glint. They are trotters, not paws: no broad palm, no outward rotation, no pale pink shovel, no claw fringe. The hind foot is the same construction with slightly more toe separation and the same glossy hoof cap. This is the ungulate/pony chassis foot showing through on an insectivore, which is a family-chassis symptom worth flagging alongside Hedgehog and Shrew.

WHERE THE JUDGE IS WRONG ON PLACEMENT: they say the front limb 'sits near mid-body instead of beside the head'. It does not. The forelimb position is broadly acceptable; it could move ~5px further forward to satisfy the note 'almost beside the head', but position is NOT the defect. The defect is that the forelimb is a tiny hoofed peg where a huge outward-turned spade should be. The judge's 'both limbs are identical tiny belly-line nubs' is essentially right on form (same hoofed stub both ends) even though the placement clause is not.

NET READ: hoofed peg legs + a blunt grey tube snout + a highlighted bead eye on a long barrel body reads as a miniature tapir/anteater lump (platypus-ish only at thumbnail size), not a mole. Two of three must-reads fail (spade forepaws absent, pink pointed snout absent) plus the eyes:hidden constraint is violated. FAIL upheld.

FIX ORDER: (1) replace both forelimbs with large outward-rotated spade paws - broad pale-pink palms facing the viewer, splayed claw fringe, sized to read at 44px, seated hard against the shoulder; (2) delete the bead eye and its highlight entirely, leaving at most a faint fur dimple; (3) shorten the snout by ~30%, taper it to a point and tint the distal half pink; (4) optionally soften the fur streaks toward plush velvet and de-gloss the hind toe caps into claws.

rows.readsAs: a fat cartoon mouse

So the engine already draws the elongated low body and the forward-projecting snout that the Shrew needs. The Shrew (spec aspect 2.8, even longer than the mole) was built off the Hedgehog's 1.6 loaf instead. The fix is not new geometry, it is picking the other chassis that already exists: start from the Mole body, lengthen it to 2.8, and put a longer, thinner, more mobile proboscis on it than the mole's.

MUST-READ 1, 'long mobile pointed proboscis-like snout' -- ABSENT. Upheld, with a correction to their wording. The face is not a bare blunt dome: the muzzle does taper slightly down-and-forward, and at its front tip there IS a small grey nose-pad wedge from which the whiskers root. So it is not featureless. The single defining feature of the organism is missing.

MUST-READ 2, 'tiny bead eyes' -- ABSENT. Upheld, and I measured it. The eye's outer white ring is ~10.6px across against a head height of ~52px, i.e. ~20% of head height, and it is drawn as white sclera ring + black pupil + specular catchlight. That is a cartoon-rodent eye. The spec asks for a tiny featureless dark bead barely distinguishable from fur.

MUST-READ 3, 'short velvety body and thin tail' -- HALF PRESENT. The tail is genuinely there and is genuinely thin and tapered, curving up off the rump; give the asset that one. The body fails: measured, the torso alone is ~99px long by ~80px tall (aspect ~1.24, essentially circular), and head+torso is ~149x80 (~1.9). Spec is 2.8. Those are two positive rodent tells, not just missing shrew tells. A shrew has no visible buck incisors (its teeth are small, pointed, red-tipped and not displayed) and its ears are small and largely buried in fur. Deleting the incisor block and shrinking/burying the ears is required in addition to adding the proboscis, or the asset will keep naming as a mouse even after the snout is fixed.

NET: two of three must-reads absent, the third half-met, the body proportion off by ~45%, two active rodent features that must not be there, and the whole thing is the Hedgehog chassis. FAIL is correct.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Head (bbox x149-319, y129-186 for the lit body): a plain orange dome with TWO stacked dark navy eyes on the same side of the head - a large lower disc and a smaller upper disc, each with a single white specular dot. The forward edge of the head is a bare unbroken curve: there is no antenna, no antennal stub, no socket, no mouthpart, no proboscis of any kind. Nothing at all projects forward of the head; the leftmost non-background pixel in the whole frame (x=149) IS the head dome. Wings: FOUR long narrow lanceolate blades (two pairs), cold blue-grey, hard-edged, glassy-transparent with faint straight streak veins. They attach at the thorax/first-abdominal-segment junction around x=205 and sweep back almost horizontally, ending past the abdomen tip at x=319. They fan apart with visible dark gaps between blades and sit entirely ABOVE the abdomen, which is left fully exposed underneath. There is no roof/tent fold, no midline ridge, no hair fringe, no smoky moth-scale texture. mustRead #1 (hairy wings folded tent-like over the back) fails on both counts - shape and surface.

Body: bright amber-orange with high-contrast alternating dark-brown bands - the abdomen is a chain of five bead-like balls in light/dark/light/dark/light. Thorax is a single orange ball. Three dark-brown V-hooked legs hang below, all bunched under the head and front thorax rather than spread across the thorax. Nothing here reads drab or moth-like; mustRead #3 fails.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM.
(1) 'Reads as a small orange mosquito' is the wrong diagnosis. A mosquito reads from ONE pair of wings, a long piercing proboscis and long trailing legs; this render has TWO pairs of splayed glassy blades, no proboscis at all, and short forward-bunched hooks. What it actually reads as is a generic wasp/bee toy chassis with dragonfly wings bolted on - a banded bead abdomen plus oversized stacked eyes. Fixing it toward 'less mosquito' would aim at the wrong target.
(2) The composition defect is real but described backwards. Measured: lit body bbox x149-319 / y129-186 (centre 234,158); shadow ellipse x122-278 / y281-310 (centre x=200). The frame centre is 220, so the body STRADDLES the vertical midline and sits slightly RIGHT of centre - it is upper-CENTRE, not 'upper-left quadrant'; only the head is left of the midline. And the shadow is offset 34px to the LEFT of the body centre, not right. The shadow is also ~95px below the feet, roughly a body-and-a-half of empty space, so the animal reads as floating - which additionally contradicts the packet's posture: crawling. The body occupies only 13% of frame height (57px of 440) and the entire lower half of the canvas is dead space.

One thing that is NOT a defect: overall proportion is close to spec. Body-plus-legs bbox is about 170x70, giving ~2.4 against the requested aspect 2.2, so the fix should not touch the aspect - it should add long forward thread antennae (at least a body-length each), refold the wings into a single steep roof-tent that covers and hides the abdomen with a fuzzy/hairy edge, desaturate the body to drab moth-brown with the banding removed, and re-seat the subject on its shadow.

rows.readsAs: an ant painted cream

rows.verifyWhy:
I decoded the PNG, cropped the head, the thorax/abdomen junction and the antennae at 14-22x, ran a per-column body-height profile, and did the same to Ant.png side by side. BOTH of the judge's named anti-ant discriminators are stated BACKWARDS -- the asset actually gets both of them RIGHT, which is why I am not upholding the FAIL.

(1) ANTENNAE -- claim says 'bent/elbowed instead of a straight bead string'. FALSE on the elbow. At 22x the termite carries exactly two antennae, both perfectly STRAIGHT rays diverging from a single base point at the fore-top of the head (orig ~x152,y188): one at ~45deg up-left ending near (141,170), one near-horizontal left ending near (139,186). Uniform width, slight distal taper, zero inflection. The Ant at the same magnification has a textbook hairpin ELBOW -- the scape climbs up-left and the flagellum reverses sharply back down, forming a closed hook. They are not the same drawing. What IS true is the second half nobody stated: the termite antennae are NOT beaded. They are smooth continuous strokes with no moniliform segmentation, so 'bead-string' is unmet even though 'straight' is met.

(2) WAIST -- claim says 'same rod waist' and 'a clear pinched constriction where the joint must be broad'. The 'rod' half is FALSE. Column profile at y=205: the Ant has a literal BREAK -- body pixels end at x=254 and do not resume until x=268 (13 columns of empty sky), with the petiole rod drawn lower at y~211-217. The Termite has NO break and NO rod anywhere: thorax and abdomen are in continuous unbroken contact. Thorax peaks at h=41px (x=207-217), abdomen peaks at h=40px (x=255-264), and the junction minimum is h=21px at x=235-236. So the joint is ~51% of adjacent body height -- continuous flesh, not a petiole. The 'pinched' half of the claim survives in weakened form: at 14x you can see two matching V-notches top and bottom where the two ellipse outlines cross, and 51% is narrower than a termite's genuinely broad abdomen-thorax union should be. That is a widening fix (target ~75-80% of body height, and let the segment banding run across the seam), not evidence of an ant.

(3) WHAT IS CORRECTLY PRESENT: 'pale soft translucent segmented body' reads well -- ivory/cream (~#EDE3C0) with soft sphere shading and a cool rim light, and the abdomen carries 8-9 clear vertical segment bands. Six legs confirmed by row scan at y=230 (six discrete strokes at x=167,174,181,222,254,285), correct count. headFrac measures 33/135 = 0.24 against spec 0.25. Aspect measures 135/43 = 3.1 against spec 2.2, i.e. somewhat overlong.

(4) THE CLAIM'S ONE FULLY CORRECT POINT -- THE EYE. This is the real defect and the top fix. The packet sets eyes: hidden and the note says 'workers are blind and unpigmented', yet the head carries a large glossy black eye ~9px across on a 33px head, complete with a bright white specular square at its upper-left and a lighter surround ring. It is the single highest-contrast mark in the whole asset and it is the one thing that most makes the head read 'ant'. Delete it, or reduce it to a faint slightly-warmer pale patch with no black and no specular.

(5) OTHER SHARED-CHASSIS ISSUES THE CLAIM GESTURED AT AND WAS RIGHT ABOUT, though they are family-wide rather than termite-specific: the leg anchors are anatomically wrong -- three legs spring from beneath the HEAD sphere (x 167/174/181, head spans 158-190), one from the thorax, and two from beneath the ABDOMEN (254, 285); on any real insect all six mount to the thorax. The ground shadow ellipse is the same primitive. The head is also a bare sphere with no mandibles -- a termite worker's head should be squarer and carry visible jaws -- though mandibles are not in the mustRead row.

VERDICT: the three mustReads are present at roughly 1 full + 1 half + 1 partial, and the asset is distinguishable from Ant.png on precisely the two axes the packet named. It reads as a pale soft banded termite, not as a recoloured ant. POLISH, with the fix order: (a) remove the glossy black eye, (b) bead the two straight antennae into 9-10 round segments, (c) widen the thorax/abdomen junction to ~75-80%, (d) re-anchor all six legs to the thorax, (e) square off the head and add mandibles.

rows.readsAs: a small pale bee or fruit fly

Yellow-body bbox measures x160-264 by y184-221 = 105 x 38 = aspect 2.76; even the strongly-read head+thorax portion alone is 71/38 = 1.87. So the drawing is longer than claimed, but still well short of the required 3.5, and the failure is the SILHOUETTE TYPE (two waisted constrictions, a bulging thorax that is the tallest point, a ball-ended rear) rather than a bare number. A fix that only stretches the existing chassis to 3.5 will still fail; the three balls have to be fused into one smooth parallel-sided tube with a taper at each end.
2. 'narrow strap wings fringed with long hairs' - ABSENT, and this is the identity-defining feature of the order. The wings are broad plates (upper wing ~60 x 26px, ratio ~2.3) where thrips need near-linear straps at roughly 10:1 whose apparent width is doubled by a comb of long marginal setae. The internal streaks are vein highlights and stop at the margin - they are not hairs and do not read as any.
3. 'asymmetrical cone-shaped rasping mouth' - ABSENT. At 14x the head is a featureless sphere: a smooth circular front arc, the big glossy eye, and nothing below or in front of it. No cone, no stylet, no mouthparts of any kind, and no asymmetry.

CROSS-CHECK against Bee.png confirms the prior judge's core charge: same head ball with the same single glossy eye, same antenna curve, same leg rig, same two-plate wing set with the same crosshatched overlay disc, same shadow ellipse. CORRECTION: it is not a plain desaturation of the Bee. The Thrips body is measurably more elongated (2.76 vs the Bee's 2.08) and the Bee's radiating thorax fur bristles have been removed. It is the Bee chassis with paler pigment, no fur, and a modest stretch - which is why it still reads as a small pale bee or fly rather than as a thrips.

One further defect neither of us listed: the packet asks for eyes 'small'; the drawn eye is a large high-gloss bee/fly eye occupying about a third of the head, which reinforces the wrong-organism read.

rows.readsAs: a glowing yellow bee or midge

The abdomen is a single unbroken saturated yellow ellipse with a soft glow and no black banding and no point at the tip. The wings are broad smoky plates rather than narrow smooth blades, and the reference aspect of 3 is nowhere near the squat ball shape rendered. Side by side with the Bee asset it is the same drawing with the fuzz removed.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but three of the stated causes are wrong and the fix must be aimed differently.

CORRECTION 1 - the waist IS drawn, it is just buried. I pixel-scanned the warm-mask (R-B>28) vertical body extent column by column: thorax depth peaks at 43-45px across x=156-172, then collapses to 17px at x=182, 12px at x=188-192, and a minimum of 8px at x=198, before rising again to 32px at x=218 and 48px at x=234 (abdomen). That is a genuine drawn petiole with a ~0.2 constriction ratio - thread-thin by the numbers. At 17x zoom on the junction (orig x=172-218, y=190-236) you can see it: a narrow tapering strip sloping down-right from the thorax's lower-right into the abdomen. So 'not drawn at all' is false. What kills it is occlusion and value: the strip is rendered dark olive against a near-black background, and an opaque light-grey WING ROOT wedge - apex planted exactly on the thorax's right flank, plus a blown-out white specular flare at that same apex - is painted straight over the junction. The 'solid wedge' the first judge saw is wing, not body. Net effect matches their read (the eye goes ball -> white flare -> blob) but the fix is compositing/value, not 'add a waist': draw the petiole in saturated yellow against a dark-rimmed edge and re-order or drop the opacity of the wing root so it stops sitting on the identity feature.

CORRECTION 2 - the abdomen is NOT unbroken. Sampling R,G,B along y=210 from x=195 to x=263 gives a clear alternating profile: 226 (x205) / 194 (x215) / 235 (x220) / 193 (x229) / 235 (x235) / 168 (x244) / 226 (x252) / 191 (x258) - four to five cross-bands with ~40-60 levels of amplitude, and at 8x zoom they are plainly visible, crossed by longitudinal lines so the whole thing reads as a woven plaid. The real defect is CHROMA, not absence: there is no black anywhere on the abdomen. The darkest band pixel is R168 G168 B148 - a pale mid olive - and the light band is ~R235 near-white. So the correct finding is 'banding present but rendered yellow-on-cream with zero black; needs true near-black bands', not 'no banding'.

CORRECTION 3 - the proportion claim is measurably false. Front of head is x=99, rear of abdomen x=263 => body length 164px; max body depth is 42px at the thorax (strong-yellow extent y=188-229, x=156-165). Aspect = 3.9, i.e. slightly MORE elongated than the spec's 3, not squat. Do not send this back for 'lengthen the body'. The squatness the first judge perceived is local silhouette, not global ratio: head and thorax are two near-equal glossy SPHERES and the abdomen is a 64x39 ellipse (1.6:1), so every one of the three body units is round.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS. (a) mustRead 'pinched thread-thin waist' - drawn but not readable at 1:1; the identity beat is invisible. (b) mustRead 'yellow-and-black banded POINTED abdomen' - no black, and not pointed: the gaster is a blunt ellipse. There IS a small pale rounded nub at the rear (x~262-276, seen at 11x) but it is the same grey value as the wings and reads as a wing fold, not a sting - so 'no sting point' is nearly right, the honest description is 'a blunt grey nub where a taper-to-sting belongs'. (c) mustRead 'narrow smooth hairless wings' - the wings are broad, near-opaque light grey, run off past the abdomen to the frame edge, are painted OVER the abdomen (which is what washes the banding out to cream), and the lower wing carries a visible patch of short white bristle strokes, i.e. hairy. This wing treatment is the single upstream cause of (a) and (b) being unreadable. (d) The note says 'Sleek and shiny - do not draw the fat furry body of a bee' - the two-equal-spheres head+thorax chassis is precisely the bee body the note forbids; it is shiny and not furry, so only half the note is met.

Other anatomy seen at zoom: head is a clean sphere with one small round black eye plus a white specular dot and two straight (not elbowed) antennae, no mandibles; legs are thin yellow lines but several emerge from under the HEAD and from under the ABDOMEN rather than all six from the thorax; a hard ground-shadow ellipse under a 'flying' posture makes it read as standing.

Organism read: a glowing yellow bee/gnat. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a generic brown ladybug or an engorged tick — nothing about it says water
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are simply not drawn. The hind legs are not flattened and not hair-fringed: all six legs are identical grey hairline arcs of uniform width, unsegmented, with no oar blade, no swimming fringe and no visible joint or coxa where they meet the body — they float behind the elytra edge like whiskers rather than attaching to it. The short clubbed antennae are absent entirely; the head is a featureless dark mushroom-cap blob with two white dots. Only the smooth domed oval wing case reads correctly. Since the oar-shaped fringed hind leg IS the identity of a water beetle, the asset resolves to a land beetle.
rows.fix: Redraw the hind pair as thick paddle limbs — a broad femur, a flattened tibia and a spatulate tarsus with a visible comb of stiff swimming hairs along the trailing edge — swept back and clearly wider than the front two pairs, attached at a visible joint under the elytra margin, and add two short clubbed antennae projecting forward from the head.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but three parts of the stated cause are wrong and the fix should be made against this description instead.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A dark navy field; a portrait brown egg-shaped body with a pale rim light down both edges, one thin dark vertical hairline as the elytral suture, and a large glossy specular stripe on the LEFT half only (the right half has no matching highlight, so the two wing cases are not symmetric). Above it a near-black mushroom shape = a round head dome on a wide flared collar. Six thin dark strokes, three per side, radiating down-and-out from the mid-height edge of the wing case. A hard black elliptical drop shadow sits directly under the body.

Two sub-defects: the left-only highlight breaks the paired-elytra symmetry, and the shape is far too round (measured brown-elytra footprint ~145px wide x ~160px tall, aspect ~1.1) against the packet's aspect 1.6. A dytiscid must be an elongated streamlined teardrop; this is an egg.

MUST-READ 2, 'flattened hair-fringed hind legs used as oars' — ABSENT. This is the defining read and it is gone, so the claim's verdict stands. But the description of it is imprecise. Measured stroke thickness per leg along its length: 8px where it meets the body, 7px mid, 5px at the tip — so they are NOT 'uniform-width', they taper, which makes them read even more like whiskers/antennae than the claim says. They ARE identical: on each side the three strokes are pixel-for-pixel the same curve translated down by ~44px (left side at x=130 gives runs y200-206, y244-250, y288-294, all t=7), and the left and right triples mirror each other. So there is zero differentiation of a hind pair — no flattening, no fringe, no segmentation into femur/tibia/tarsus, no tarsal paddle, no joint anywhere. Colour correction: they are not 'grey'. They are RGB(32,36,44), a near-black desaturated blue, against a background of RGB(5,6,12) — barely above the backdrop, so at thumbnail size they nearly vanish. The low contrast is an additional defect the claim understated.

Correct the 'unattached, floating behind the elytra edge' wording — that is wrong. The strokes are still present at x=145, which is INSIDE the elytra fill boundary (x=152), i.e. they run under and behind the wing case rather than floating in space with a gap. The real anatomical error is different and should be fixed as such: all six legs emanate from the mid-height margin of the WING CASE, so they insert into the abdomen. There is no thorax and no coxa; the legs sprout from the elytra.

MUST-READ 3, 'short clubbed antennae on a tucked head' — ABSENT, confirmed. Row-by-row silhouette scan of the head zone (background-vs-not, y=98 to y=173) gives a span that widens monotonically and smoothly: 12, 26, 34, 40, 42, 46, 48, 48, 48, 48, 50, then 66, 78, 84, 88, 90 as the collar flares, then merges into the elytra. There is no row anywhere where the outline juts out and back in, so there is not even an antenna stub. Nothing projects from the head.

Correct 'the head is a featureless dark mushroom-cap blob' — overstated, though the conclusion survives. There ARE eyes: two dark pupils each carrying a white specular catchlight, measured at exactly four bright pixels, (211,117),(212,117) and (225,117),(226,117). They are real but so small they contribute nothing at any display size. Everything else about the head is a single flat value — sampled RGB(36,28,21) identically at (220,110), (220,140), (180,150) and (260,150), i.e. the head dome and the pronotum collar are one undifferentiated silhouette with no tonal modelling and no head/pronotum boundary.

DEFECT THE CLAIM MISSED. The packet specifies posture: swimming. The asset is drawn dorsal, upright, static, and carries a hard black ground-shadow ellipse beneath it — that shadow reads unambiguously as an object resting on a surface. It actively signals land, compounding the missing oars.

NET. One of three must-reads present, and the two absent ones are precisely the pair that encode 'water' and 'beetle head'. With uniform tapering whisker-strokes for legs, no antennae, a round rather than streamlined body, and a ground shadow, the asset resolves to a generic brown land beetle — or, as the claim reasonably put it, an engorged tick. Nothing indicates water. FAIL is correct.

FIX PRIORITY: (1) replace the six identical strokes with a proper three-pair leg set — short front/mid legs and a genuinely differentiated hind pair drawn as broad flattened blades with a visible swim-hair fringe along the trailing edge, swept back into a power stroke; (2) attach all legs at a thorax under the pronotum, not at the elytral margin; (3) add short clubbed antennae breaking the head silhouette; (4) elongate the body toward aspect 1.6; (5) delete the ground shadow and replace it with a water cue.

There is no dark distal segment continuing past the yellow (the silhouette's own leftmost pixel, x118, IS the yellow tip), so nothing is hiding. Read at full size it looks like a finch or a stubby carrot beak. FIX = roughly double the bill length (target tip near x~95-100, i.e. ~70-75px) and keep the existing wedge profile and near-horizontal carriage; do NOT 'straighten' it and do NOT thin it into a needle, both of which the current draw already gets right.

MUSTREAD 2, 'oversized head with no visible neck' — FAILS, and here the judge's diagnosis is half wrong. Head is right that it is UNDERSIZED: the blue cranial sphere runs x150..187 (37-38px across) and y~159..197, against a body-proper length of ~129px (front of breast x150 to rump x280). That is headFrac ~0.29 measured on body length, ~0.19 against the full 200px silhouette — well under the specified 0.4. But 'sits behind a CLEAR concave neck dip' overstates it. The throat notch is shallow: the left silhouette edge runs 150 at y173, pinches to 156 at y175-183, and returns to 151 by y185 — a 6px indentation, not a rendered neck. The head is a discrete ball perched on the shoulder with a visible seam where its outline crosses the wing, but there is no column of neck. So the fix is 'grow the skull to ~0.4 and let it swallow the 6px throat notch', NOT 'delete a long neck'.

MUSTREAD 3, 'stubby body and very short tail' — FAILS, and this part of the claim is accurate. A dark navy pointed wedge leaves the lower rear of the body and projects well past the rump: the blue right edge is 278-279 at rows 232-238, then runs out to 285/291/296/302/308/314/318 through rows 240-252 before cutting back to 294/261 at 254-256. That is ~39px of tail beyond the rump, about 29% of body length, angled down-and-back like a duck's or a jay's — the opposite of a stub. The body itself is a deep plump ovoid (~129 wide x ~94 tall from the breast line y178 to the leg line y~272), duck-round rather than compact. FIX = cut the tail to ~10-12px of projection and lift it, and shorten/deepen-less the barrel.

OTHER THINGS I CHECKED AND FOUND FINE, so nobody wastes a pass on them: the render is clean, centred, well-lit, with a correct contact shadow; the crown carries a spiky 3-4 point shaggy crest (x164..190, y142..158) which is actually a legitimate kingfisher/belted-kingfisher cue and should be KEPT; the eye is a single dark bead with a specular highlight, correctly placed high and forward on the skull; the yellow feet (x187..229, y~272..287) are small, biped, and correctly under the body's centre of mass; the wing is drawn as a distinct scapular oval over the flank rather than being fused into the body blob. So the asset is not a rendering failure of any kind — it is purely a proportion failure, and the single highest-leverage change is the bill: at 0.95x skull it is the one feature that makes a stranger name this a bluebird, a jay, or a cartoon duckling instead of a kingfisher.

MUST-READ 1 - 'white winter coat': ABSENT. Judge is correct and understated it if anything. I counted the near-white pixels in the entire image: 110 of them, ALL inside the eye ring at (262-270, 210-212) plus the tiny incisor block. There is not one white pixel anywhere on the pelt, rump, belly, feet or tail. The coat is uniformly mid-brown. This alone is a FAIL on a species whose catalogued identity is the winter pelage.

MUST-READ 2 - 'black-tipped ears': ABSENT. Judge is correct. I sampled the ear straight down its length: (232,130) near the apex = rgb(47,35,23); (245,175) mid-ear = rgb(47,35,23); (265,135) = rgb(47,35,23). Identical values from tip to base - the ear outer is one flat fill with no darker terminal patch, no black cap, no gradient. The tip is drawn as a plain rounded taper. Second, unremarked defect: the ears are TOO LONG for this species. Ear top y=118, ear base at the skull ~y=193, so ~75px of ear on a 175px-tall figure - 43% of the animal's height, slender and pointed. The must-read specifies ears SHORTER than a jackrabbit's; these are jackrabbit ears.

MUST-READ 3 - 'oversized furry hind feet': THE JUDGE'S DESCRIPTION IS FLATLY WRONG, though the must-read still does not carry. There is no 'tiny dark stub with no foot form at all'. That is an unmistakable foot form, and it is comfortably the largest foot on the animal: the front leg (a separate shape at x226-237, y265-283, only 9px wide, terminating in a 16px pad at y285-289) is less than half its length. I believe the judge looked at that front leg, or read the two dark shapes as interchangeable, and reported the front one as the hind limb. The claim 'shorter than the animal's own ear' happens to be true in raw linear terms (38px foot vs 75px ear) but is measured against an ear that is itself drawn wrong, so it is not a usable diagnosis. What the foot actually fails on is quality, not existence: it is a featureless dark slab with no fur texture, no toe splay, no fringe, no separation of hock from foot, and it is filled with the same rgb(47,35,23) as the front paw and the ears, so nothing signals 'snowshoe'. BAND. Two of three must-reads are wholly absent (white coat, black ear tips), the ear length actively contradicts the fourth clause of the row, and the third must-read is present only as a generic rabbit foot. Read cold, this asset is a brown cottontail rabbit, not a Snowshoe Hare in winter. FAIL upheld.

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and the shared-chassis claim is literally verifiable. I rendered Marine_Iguana.png next to Iguana.png and Land_Iguana.png from the same folder at matched crops (x20 y130 400x150, gamma-lifted so the dark asset is readable). All three are ONE construction: the same rotated head ellipse with the same thin white rim-light arc over its top-front edge, the same single vertical-slit eye in the same socket position, the same straight hairline mouth stroke running from mid-head to the snout tip, the same dorsal spine row, the same banana tail with the same darker inner stripe, and the same two-capsule legs. Marine differs only in hue (sooty grey-brown instead of green/gold), a plumper body ellipse, a shorter tail and darker/slightly smaller spines. Point-by-point against the packet row (aspect 4, headFrac 0.25, mustRead 'blunt square salt-crusted snout / laterally flattened paddle-like swimming tail / low spiny crest and long curved claws', note 'stubby blunt face and dark sooty body - not the long pointed green-iguana profile'):

(1) SNOUT — judge is RIGHT. At 9x the head is a plain ~1.7:1 ellipse tilted nose-down, terminating in a smooth continuous round curve. There is no squared-off muzzle plane, no salt-crust patch or white nasal blotch, no nostril mark, no distinct upper-lip/jaw break. The single piece of head modelling is a ~3px nub on the top of the skull. Small correction to their wording: the snout is not 'pointed' (the ellipse tip is fairly broad and rounded) — the failure is that it is generic and UNMODIFIED, not that it is sharp. It is the identical primitive the green Iguana uses, which is exactly what the note forbids.

(2) TAIL — judge is RIGHT, and it is worse than stated. At 7x the tail is a near-CONSTANT-WIDTH round tube from base to tip, capped by a rounded hemisphere, carrying the same interior dark stripe the green Iguana carries. There is no lateral flattening, no depth taper, no dorsal fin/crest continuing onto the tail, no oar-blade widening — nothing that reads as a sculling organ. It is also the SHORTEST of the three iguanas' tails, so the one feature that should be exaggerated is the one that got reduced.

(3) CLAWS — judge is RIGHT. Zoomed to 8x on the feet: each limb is two overlapping capsules (upper + lower segment) ending in a plain rounded stub. No foot plate, no digits, no claw arcs, nothing. What looks like toes in the small view is just the elbow overlap of the two capsules. Also only one leg per pair is drawn; the far-side leg exists as a single darker capsule behind the front limb.

(4) VALUE/CONTRAST — judge is RIGHT and I can put numbers on it. Sampled raw pixels: body core (36,38,41), head (36,38,41), tail (28,31,33), LEG (4,7,10) against a backdrop of (5,6,12) at the corner and (8,13,18) above the animal. Body-to-backdrop is roughly a 1.3:1 contrast ratio, and the legs are numerically INDISTINGUISHABLE from the backdrop — they vanish entirely at 1:1. Important nuance for the fix: the note ASKS for a dark sooty body, so the hue/value choice is on-spec; the defect is that no separation was preserved. The only things keeping the silhouette legible are the thin white rim stroke on the head arc and small white highlight ticks at the base of each crest spine. A rim light along the back/belly/limb edges would fix the read without lightening the body.

WHAT THE JUDGE MISSED / one must-read that IS present: the 'low spiny crest' is there and is the most readable feature on the asset — about 9-10 dark triangular spines along the dorsal line, each with a white highlight tick at its base, running from the shoulder to the hip. They are not absent; they are the wrong shape (tall shark-fin triangles cloned from the green Iguana, where a real marine iguana's crest is low and rounded). So the score is not 0/3 — it is roughly 0.5/3: crest present-but-generic, snout absent, paddle tail absent, claws absent. Additionally the body carries big soft brown leopard blotches which push it further from the uniform sooty black the note calls for.

Band stands at FAIL: two of the three must-read clauses are wholly absent, half the third is absent, and the explicit 'not the green-iguana profile' instruction is violated by reusing the green Iguana head primitive verbatim. The asset currently reads as 'generic iguana, dark palette', not as a swimming marine iguana.

rows.readsAs: a brown cartoon newt or a salamander plush

The limbs are the family's thin vertical pegs, not muscular or sprawled, and they end in rounded stumps with no hooked claws. The reference's headline note — a long snake-like neck unlike the neckless build of most lizards — is directly contradicted: the head ellipse is fused straight onto the body with zero neck, making this the MOST neckless asset in the batch.

rows.verifyWhy: Verified at 440x440 plus 5-10x nearest-neighbour crops of head, tail and feet, and a 3x brightness lift so the near-black limbs became legible against the dark background, plus a column-by-column silhouette profile. The FAIL stands: zero of the three must-reads are readable. (1) TONGUE - absent entirely. The mouth is a single 1px hairline stroke running from x~365 back to x~410 that stops roughly 8px SHORT of the snout tip; nothing protrudes past the silhouette anywhere. No fork, no tongue of any colour, no yellow anywhere on the asset. (2) TAIL - the judge's wording needs correcting on length but the must-read still fails. So the tail IS longer than the trunk ellipse (1.3x) - the claim 'no longer than the body' is wrong on that reading - but it is SHORTER than snout-vent length (174 vs 210), which is the convention the must-read means, so 'tail longer than the body' is not met. The far worse defect, which the judge understates, is that the tail does not TAPER AT ALL: its depth is 35px at the base, holds 35-40px across its whole length, and actually SWELLS to 44px near the free end before capping off in a blunt round dome at x=24. That is over half the trunk's 64px depth carried all the way out. There is no lateral flattening cue of any kind - no dorsal keel, no ridge, no depth increase; the only internal detail is a dark olive stripe painted down the inside of the tube, which reads as a shading stroke, not a keel. It is a constant-width plush tail, curled upward at the tip. (3) LIMBS/CLAWS - accurate as claimed. Two near-side limbs are visible (rear at x~180-245, fore at x~305-375) plus one faint far-side ghost limb behind the rear. Each is two overlapping tapered capsules (thigh + shank) ending in a blunt rounded cap. Zero digits, zero toes, zero claws, no foot plate. One correction in the asset's favour: the limbs DO angle outward and downward from a low-slung belly, so the 'sprawling' posture token is partially honoured - the failure is specifically the absent feet/claws, not the stance. (4) NECK - the headline note is contradicted, essentially as claimed, with one factual correction: it is not a seamless fusion. The profile shows a real pinch at x=328-336 where the head ellipse edge crosses the trunk ellipse edge (depth drops 38 -> 27 -> 29px over 8px), and at 8x zoom you can see the two outlines intersect with a small concave notch. But the neck has literally zero LENGTH - the head ellipse directly overlaps the trunk with no connecting segment - so 'long and snake-like' is absent and the exact opposite is drawn. Additional defects the judge did not mention: the head is a plain unmodified ellipse with a blunt rounded snout, no jawline, no nostril, no ear, and no loose scaly neck skin; and the eye is a white sclera with a thin VERTICAL SLIT pupil, whereas monitors have round pupils - a further wrong-clade cue. The only monitor-adjacent detail present is the scatter of soft brown blotches over the dorsum, which is a genuine (if blurry) nod to monitor ocelli, but it is not a must-read and cannot carry identity. Net read: a generic brown newt/salamander plush with a curled sausage tail. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a grey cartoon newt, indistinguishable from the Monitor and Komodo except for hue
rows.defect: The identity must-read is absent: the head is the same smooth rounded ellipse every other asset in this batch wears — not massive, not blocky, and with no jowls at all (the jaw line is a single straight ruled stroke, so there is no cheek mass to jowl). The body carries scattered random speckles rather than heavy transverse bands, and there is no beaded scale texture anywhere — the surface is a flat airbrushed gradient. Only the thick body-length tail is roughly right, and that is the shared banana shape arriving by default rather than by design.
rows.fix: Widen the rear of the skull into a heavy blocky wedge with bulging jowls behind the jaw line, and replace the speckles with bold white transverse bands across the trunk and tail.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD after zooming the PNG at 6-7x on the head, legs and tail. Reference row: aspect 3.6, headFrac 0.28, eyes normal, posture sprawling, mustRead = 'massive jowled blocky head | heavy banded body with beaded scales | thick tail slightly longer than the body'. Two of the three must-reads are absent and the third is malformed.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS. The whole animal is three primitives: a head ellipse, a body ellipse, and a tail band, plus two leg stubs. HEAD (verified at 6x): a plain smooth ellipse, wider than tall, butted directly against the body ellipse with no neck and no join blending - you can see the two outlines cross. Its only interior marks are (a) one perfectly straight ruled dark stroke running from about 25% to 100% of its length at mid-height, ending flush at the muzzle edge, and (b) a round white eye with a vertical slit pupil. There is no jowl mass, no widening at the quadrate, no temporal bulge, no distinction at all between skull and snout - the ellipse is the same width at the ear as at the nose tip. headFrac reads roughly 0.22-0.24 by measurement, under the specified 0.28. So 'massive jowled blocky head' is ABSENT, and the original judge described this correctly.

BODY: a single smooth ellipse filled with a soft vertical airbrush gradient (lighter top, darker belly) and a thin white rim-light arc along the dorsal edge only. Markings are ~25 small soft-edged brown ovals scattered at random - no row, no column, no alignment, no transverse organisation whatsoever, and several sit isolated near the flank. They read as leopard/dalmatian spotting, not Tegu banding. There is zero beaded, pebbled, granular or tiled scale texture anywhere on the figure; the surface is uniformly smooth. So 'heavy banded body with beaded scales' is ABSENT - the original judge was correct on both halves of this.

CORRECTIONS AND ADDITIONS THE ORIGINAL JUDGE MISSED. (1) The tail is not simply 'fine' - it is broken. At 7x it is a constant-width flat band that hooks up and forward into a J, and its interior is a large solid near-black lozenge that runs most of the tail's length, giving it a hollow, punched-through look like a bag handle or a horseshoe. It does not taper: the free end is a blunt rounded cap the same width as the base. Length is roughly body-length, so the proportion in the must-read is arguably satisfied, but 'thick muscular tail' does not read - it reads as a hollow hook. That black core needs diagnosing (it looks like a marking or occlusion shape drawn at full opacity over the tail interior) and the tail needs a real taper to a point. (2) Posture 'sprawling' is not achieved. Only two leg stubs are visible, both dark olive-green, both hanging straight DOWN as vertical tapered columns from the belly line, and both are so close in value to the elliptical drop shadow beneath the animal that they nearly disappear. There are no feet, no toes, no claws, no ankle, no elbow, and no lateral splay. (3) The head, body and tail read as three separate un-merged shapes, not one animal.

FAMILY CHASSIS: the original judge's comparative claim is CORRECT and I confirmed it by opening Monitor_Lizard.png and Komodo_Dragon.png. All three are literally the same construction - head ellipse abutting body ellipse, scattered soft brown ovals, dorsal rim-light arc, two olive downward leg stubs, and the identical hollow-cored hooked tail band. The only variables are hue (Tegu grey-green, Monitor olive-brown, Komodo warm grey-mauve) and overall aspect. Nothing in the Tegu says Tegu; nothing in the Monitor says Monitor. This is one chassis in three colours, and the family read is the more urgent defect than any single asset's markings.

FIX DIRECTION: rebuild the skull as a wide wedge with a distinct jowl bulge behind the eye narrowing to a blunt short snout, break the ruled jaw stroke into a curved gape line that stops short of the muzzle tip; replace the random ovals with 8-10 heavy dark transverse bars wrapping the flank perpendicular to the spine plus a beaded/granular scale pass; taper the tail to a point and remove the black interior void; give the limbs a lateral sprawl with visible clawed feet in a value that separates from the shadow.

On top of it sit roughly EIGHT discrete dark rounded ovals, sampled RGB(64,79,58) / (66,80,59) / (68,81,61), arranged as a radial PINWHEEL around the centre — each oval is a separate smooth egg shape with its long axis pointing outward, tips overlapping the neighbour clockwise. At the exact geometric centre of that pinwheel is a hard sphere with a radial gradient and a specular hotspot at its upper-left: RGB(192,218,175) at (215,195), RGB(175,202,159) at (220,200), peaking brighter still. It is ~50px across, ~26% of head width, and it is the brightest object in the frame by a wide margin. Pale off-white lines: ~1-2px, smooth, single-stroke, non-branching, and almost all of them sit ON the boundary between two dark ovals (they are edge highlights on the lobe silhouettes) or sweep as a single arc from near the sphere out along a lobe's flank. Lower-right/right of the head, three narrow lance-pointed leaves fan down and out, each carrying one straight pale midrib, over a lighter sage wedge. Soft cast-shadow ellipse under the head. Background is the standard near-black navy.

MUST-READ 1 (tight overlapping ball head at the centre) — PRESENT and the strongest thing in the asset. The silhouette is a solid ball and the lobes do overlap. But they overlap as a radial pinwheel of eight SEPARATE ovals, not as nested concentric layers wrapping inward, and each lobe edge is a smooth ellipse with no ruffle or wave. That structure plus the boss at the centre is exactly the geometry of a camellia/rose-form flower, which is what the head reads as on first sight.

MUST-READ 2 (loose flaring outer leaves around the base) — PARTIAL, and the original claim is FACTUALLY WRONG here. It is NOT 'a single pointed leaf low-right': there are THREE overlapping pointed leaves fanning from about 5 o'clock to 3 o'clock, plus a lighter sage wedge behind them, and they are the only place in the asset where a real midrib is drawn. What genuinely fails is (a) they are confined to one quadrant — the left, bottom-left and top of the base have no separated outer-leaf silhouette at all, only the lit rim of the underlying disc, so there is no skirt 'around the base'; and (b) they are narrow lance/spear shapes with straight edges, not the 'very large smooth waxy leaves flaring open and wavy-edged' the row asks for.

MUST-READ 3 (thick white midribs branching across each leaf) — ABSENT on the head, and this is the correct core of the original claim. Not one of the eight head lobes carries a thick midrib, and nothing branches anywhere in the asset. The white marks on the head are hairline lobe-outline arcs. The only midribs present are the three single strokes on the outer lance leaves.

PALETTE — the hue criticism is right, the value criticism is wrong. Hue of every sampled green is 93-111 degrees, i.e. green to yellow-green/olive; glaucous blue-green would be ~150-170. There is no waxy bloom, no cool desaturated dusting. But it is NOT 'near-black olive': the dark lobes are RGB(64,79,58), about 31% lightness, and they sit over a distinctly lighter sage disc RGB(75,108,67) that reads clearly around most of the rim. The value range is acceptable; only the hue and the missing bloom need fixing.

WHY IT STILL FAILS. The glossy centre sphere is the decisive defect and the original judge described it accurately: it is hard, specular, mint-pale, dead-centre, and the brightest thing in frame, so it reads as a pistil boss, a pearl, or an egg set in dark leaves. Combined with eight smooth radial petal-ovals and hairline petal-outline arcs, the organism I read is a dark-green flower or an artichoke, not a cabbage. Two of three must-reads are compromised and a large foreign feature actively mis-signals the identity. FIXES: delete the specular sphere entirely and replace the centre with a tight inward spiral of the two or three smallest innermost leaves; re-cut the head lobes as nested concentric wraps with wavy/ruffled outer edges instead of a pinwheel of discrete ovals; draw thick, tapering, BRANCHING white midribs across each visible head leaf (currently zero); extend the outer flaring skirt all the way around the base, especially the left and bottom-left, and widen those leaves from lances to broad wavy blades; shift all greens ~40-60 degrees toward blue-green and add a cool pale bloom overlay.
