What the delivered PNG shows to the naked eye matches the other judge: a black lens/leaf, a big white oval up front, a grey oval mid-back, a white ventral crescent, a faint dark bump on the spine, and a hairline running off to the right that ends in nothing. But I pulled the actual pixel values and re-mapped the 8-16 luminance band, and every 'missing' feature is DRAWN AND CORRECTLY SHAPED -- it is just painted in RGB(9,12,16) on a card background of RGB(6-8,9-11,15-17), i.e. a contrast ratio of roughly 1.1-1.3:1, which is sub-perceptual.

Flukes are present and are a good silhouette: a broad blade spanning x=330-393, y=209-245 (63px wide, 36px tall) with a clean concave notch cut into the trailing edge. Fill RGB(9,12,16); background immediately above at (365,190) is RGB(7,11,17) and below at (365,265) is RGB(8,11,17). Luminance 11.5 vs 10.5 -- a one-level difference. They are invisible, not absent. CORRECTION 2 -- 'the tall triangular dorsal is a ~10px stub' is FALSE. The dorsal is a full fin: apex at approx (217,154), base from x=198 to x=240 on the back line at y~190. That is ~36px tall against a body depth of ~55px at that station, and ~42px wide at the base -- proportionally a proper cetacean dorsal. Same RGB(9,12,16) fill. The ONLY reason any of it is perceptible is that it is very slightly DARKER than the radial glow behind the creature (11.5 vs 13.8-14.2 at (190,160)/(245,160)), so it shows as a shadowy notch in the glow -- and the glow only reaches the fin's lower third, which is why it looked like a 10px stub. The one shape criticism that does survive: the apex is ROUNDED and hump-like, not the crisp backswept triangle the mustRead asks for -- it reads closer to a dolphin's falcate fin than an orca's blade.

CORRECTION 3 -- 'the body tapers to a hairline and simply ends'. The hairline is real but it is not the body. It is the dorsal-ridge RIM-LIGHT stroke (1-2px, lum ~41 at (320,220)) which correctly runs along the top edge to the tail stock and terminates at x~335 exactly where the flukes begin. The body silhouette itself does not taper away -- it carries full depth through the peduncle into the flukes; it merely drops below visibility once the fill hits RGB(9,12,16) around x>250 (body is lum 33 at x=120, 32 at x=160, 28 at x=200, 20 at x=240, then 11.5). So there is also a value RAMP running head-to-tail that fades the animal out, on top of the flat-black appendage fill.

CORRECTION 4 -- the eye patch claim is HALF wrong. There is a white ellipse ~48x40px centred near (88,210), and there IS a separately drawn eye: a small dark pupil with a white catchlight at approx (72,232), below and forward of the patch, plus a third small pale dot at ~(90,178) above it (blowhole). So the patch is not 'sitting where an eyeball would be' -- the eyeball is drawn elsewhere. The judge's READ is nonetheless fair: the patch is roughly twice the size it should be, too circular (a real orca patch is a slanted oval about half this size set behind and above the eye), and because it is an empty white blob with the real eye a full patch-width away, it does dominate as a cartoon eye.

Only the third mustRead partly lands, and weakly: the saddle is a mid-grey oval (lum 86) rather than the crisp white it should be, and the eye patch is oversized. Raise the appendage/limb fill from RGB(9,12,16) to at least the body value (RGB ~26,34,39) or brighter, kill the head-to-tail value ramp that fades the rear half into the background, sharpen the dorsal apex to a backswept point, blunt the rostrum, shrink the eye patch to a slanted oval sitting just behind and above the (already-drawn) eye, and brighten the saddle toward white.

rows.readsAs: a plain grey whale-shaped lozenge, same chassis as Gray Whale and Porpoise

The crusty white callosity patches on the head are also missing; the only white on the card is the single blowhole speck shared with every other cetacean here. The dorsal-free broad back is correct but it is the only must-read that lands.
rows.fix: Cut a deep strongly arched mouth line running a third of the body length with the lower lip bowing up over it, and stipple rough white callosity patches on the rostrum, above the eye and along the lower jaw.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but TWO of the three stated causes are factually wrong and would send a fixer to the wrong place. Measured on the 440x440 PNG (opaque bg 5,6,12; ink bbox x62-376, y107-323).

CORRECTION 1 - 'No mouth line is drawn at all' is FALSE. A mouth line IS drawn. Traced by local-minimum scan it runs from x=74,y=242 (snout tip, just under and forward of the eye) back to x=132,y=257, where it disappears behind the flipper ellipse; a faint continuation is visible as a darker band inside the flipper at x=136-172, y=253-257. It is a ~3px hairline at luminance ~56-59 against body ~80-82 - only a 23-level dip, which is why it vanishes at thumbnail scale and why the previous judge missed it. So the defect is NOT absence. The defect is (a) CONTRAST - the line is too faint to read; (b) LENGTH - visible span 74->132 = 58px against a body length of ~247px (snout x=68 to peduncle pinch x=315), i.e. ~23%, short of the required third; and above all (c) SHAPE - it is essentially STRAIGHT. Sampled y at x=76/100/128 is 242/249/255: a monotonic ~15px droop over a 56px run with zero curvature. There is no bow, no rising rictus, no plunging front corner. It reads as a generic dolphin/manatee mouth slit. The must-read 'enormously arched jawline' is therefore genuinely absent as an ARCH even though a line exists. Fix = re-curve and thicken this existing stroke, do not add a new one.

CORRECTION 2 - 'the white callosity patches are missing' is HALF wrong. Exactly one white callosity IS drawn: an 8x5px light blob at x107-115, y159-163 (the only >125-luminance cluster on the whole asset apart from the 4px eye specular at x88-91,y222-224 and the 1px-wide back rim-light run at x184-219). The bug is that it is drawn OFF THE ANIMAL. At y=160 the body silhouette does not begin until x=120; the blob occupies x=108-114, i.e. it sits entirely in the background with a ~6px gap of pure bg between it and the whale.

NEW DEFECT the previous judge did not name, and the likely root cause of Correction 2: there is a DETACHED FLOATING STROKE arcing over the head. A ~4px light-grey stroke (RGB ~100,108,119) runs from about (65,215) up over the crown to ~(175,145), where it finally merges with the back's rim-light. Over its whole front half it is separated from the silhouette by clean background: row y=185 stroke at x82-85, bg at 86-91, body from 92; row y=200 stroke at x72-75, bg at 76-80, body from 81; row y=210 stroke at x66-69, bg at 70-75, body from 76. So the head's dorsal-ridge/callosity stroke has been laid on a curve offset ~5-6px outside the body path, carrying the sole callosity blob with it. At full size it reads as a stray wire or hair hovering over the whale's head. This is the single highest-value fix: snap that ridge path to the silhouette and it both removes the artefact and puts the bonnet callosity back on the rostrum.

WHAT ACTUALLY LANDS: must-read 3 is fully correct - the back is smooth and completely dorsal-fin-free, with a clean unbroken dorsal profile peaking around x=157 and tapering to a narrow peduncle (column height only 6px at x=312) into a small forked fluke (x322-376). The eye is small, dark, low and set forward just above the mouth corner, which is right for the species. So the judge's 'only the dorsal-free back lands' is a fair summary of the outcome even though the reasoning is wrong.

OTHER PROPORTION MISS: packet asks aspect 3. Measured body is ~247 long by ~127 deep excluding the flipper (~142 including it) = roughly 1.75-1.95:1. The animal is nearly twice as deep as specified - a fat lozenge rather than a long rotund whale. headFrac is closer: the implied head (snout to flipper/mouth end, 68->132) is ~26% against the specified 0.28.

BAND: FAIL stands. Of three must-reads only the dorsal-free back is readable. The identity-defining feature - the enormous bowed jawline over a third of the body - is present only as a faint straight scratch, and the callosity that would confirm the species is rendered in the background rather than on the head. Nothing in the image says Right Whale; a viewer would read it as a generic blunt-headed cetacean.

rows.readsAs: a tan dachshund or a stubby otter standing on four short dog legs
rows.defect: There are no flippers anywhere. The fore-limbs are short cylindrical dog legs ending in small rounded paw pads planted flat on the ground, not long paddle fore-flippers lifting the chest clear; the hind limbs are matching dog legs, not rotated-forward hind flippers. The body is a shallow level sausage with a nub tail. The one thing that could carry the identity, the small external ear flap, is drawn as an ambiguous angular wedge behind the cheek that is identical to the shape on the true Seal, so it separates nothing. Muzzle and eye are generic cartoon-dog. Nothing in the silhouette says marine.
rows.fix: Replace all four legs with pinniped flippers: broad flat elongated fore-flippers angled back from a high shoulder and propping the chest and neck up off the ground at a steep angle, and short rotated-forward hind flippers with visible splayed digit tips under the rear — then give the head a small but clearly separate pointed ear cone standing off the skull.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 4-6x zoom on head, limbs and full silhouette, and side-by-side against Seal.png from the same packet. The FAIL stands, but one of the stated causes is factually wrong and must not be fixed as described.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A long tan cylinder body (fur-textured with dry shaggy stroke marks, not sleek wet hide) on four SHORT limbs of equal length. Darker brown blunt muzzle with a dark oval nose, a big cartoon eye with a white ring, and a smiling mouth line. Behind the skull sits an angular wedge with two sawtooth step-notches on its rear edge. A blunt darker cap closes the rump at the far left; no tail.

CORRECTION 1 — 'rounded paw pads planted flat' is WRONG. Each of the four limbs ends in an ELONGATED dark-brown flattened oval carrying faint parallel digit striations, angled forward and downward, i.e. a small webbed/flipper-ish pad, not a round dog paw. The rear pair's pad even points forward under the body, which is a partial hit on the note's 'hind flippers rotated forward'. The defect is scale and the limb above the pad, not the pad shape: the pad is roughly one-eighth the limb length and sits on the end of a short cylindrical dog leg with a hock bend, so the flipper reading is destroyed by everything above it. A fix that replaces the pads with rounder shapes would make this worse.

CORRECTION 2 — the wedge is not literally identical to the Seal's, but the judge's conclusion is right and if anything understated. Sea Lion's wedge has two step-notches; Seal.png's has one deeper single notch. Same part, same place on the skull, same size, same colour on both. Since the Seal's own mustRead is 'no external ear flaps', this wedge is not merely non-discriminating, it is actively wrong on the sibling asset — and it does not read as a pinna in either case; it reads as a crest or a chunk of jagged ruff at the back of the head.

MUST-READS. (a) 'small external ear flaps' — MISS as an identity cue, per above. (b) 'long fore-flippers lifting the chest clear of the ground' — MISS outright. The forelimb is the same short length as the hind, there is no broad flipper blade, and the belly hangs at the same height as the tops of the legs, so the chest is not lifted at all; the topline is flat and low. This is the defining sea-lion cue and it is absent. (c) 'blunt dog-like whiskered muzzle' — HALF. The blunt dog muzzle is genuinely present and readable; whiskers are entirely absent (no vibrissae strokes, no whisker dots on the muzzle).

SHARED CHASSIS. Confirmed against Seal.png: identical body cylinder, identical head-and-wedge assembly, identical four short legs with the same striated oval pads, differing only in hue (tan vs grey) and a slightly lower crouch. The two assets that most need to be told apart are one chassis in two colours.

The judge's 'tan dachshund' summary is a fair read of the silhouette; add that the shaggy dry fur texture pushes it further from a pinniped, which should be smooth and wet-looking.

Band: FAIL. Two of three must-reads absent, the identity-defining one (chest lifted clear on long fore-flippers) entirely so, and the asset is not separable from its sibling Seal.

rows.readsAs: a grey dachshund or a grey otter-dog on four legs
rows.defect: It is the Sea Lion asset recoloured grey — identical topline, identical body depth, identical four stumpy legs at identical attachment points, identical paw pads, identical skull and nose. A true seal cannot stand on four limbs at all, yet this one is propped up on four of them with the belly clear of the ground, which is precisely the error the reference note calls out. The hind limbs point down and are planted as feet instead of trailing straight back as a joined flipper pair, there is no smooth torpedo taper, and the same angular flap sits behind the cheek where a true seal must show a bare earless head.
rows.fix: Redraw it belly-down on the ground with the whole body a smooth torpedo taper, the hind flippers fused and trailing straight back off the tail end as one splayed paddle, the fore-flippers as short paddles tucked low against the ribs, and delete the ear flap entirely so the skull is a clean round earless dome.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, and I tried hard to break it. I read the PNG at full size, then cropped and 6-14x upscaled the head, muzzle, occiput, forelimb and rear end, and ran a pixel silhouette diff of Seal.png against Sea_Lion.png.

WHAT THE ASSET ACTUALLY IS: a grey, long parallel-sided furred loaf standing on FOUR separate planted limbs, two under the shoulder and two under the hip, each ending in a small grey paddle-shaped foot with digit striations pressed flat on the ground. There is a clear elliptical cast shadow and an unambiguous air gap between the belly and the ground along the whole trunk. Posture spec says 'sprawling'; what is drawn is a standing quadruped. This is precisely the failure mode the note names: 'drawing it propped up on rotated hind flippers makes it a sea lion.'

SILHOUETTE DIFF (hard evidence for the 'recoloured Sea Lion' charge): thresholded masks of the two PNGs overlap 21,038 px of Seal's 24,091 lit px (87%), and the diff image is nothing but a thin outline halo. Same trunk, same topline, same four limb positions, same limb form, same foot, same head shape, same face-on eye with white sclera ring, same nose blob, same mouth crease. Seal is ~4% larger with a marginally larger head. The judge's core claim is confirmed: this is the Sea Lion chassis in grey. Note also that the packet gives Sea Lion aspect 2.4 and Seal aspect 3, yet the two render at effectively the same proportions, so the aspect spec is not differentiating them either.

MUST-READ BY MUST-READ:
1. 'smooth torpedo body with no external ear flaps' - FAILS twice. The trunk is a constant-width loaf, blunt-capped at BOTH ends, with zero taper toward either the head or the tail. And on the back of the skull, above and BEHIND the eye, there is a hard flat-topped wedge that sweeps back to a sharp point and then has a small square notch cut into its trailing edge - a distinct protruding appendage that juts outside the head's rounded outline. It is pixel-for-pixel the same shape carried by Sea_Lion.png, where it is the ear flap. CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM: the judge called it a 'cheek flap'; it is not on the cheek, it is the occiput/crown region, high and rearward. The substance stands - an earless head has a protruding pointed flap on it.
2. 'hind flippers trailing straight back, unable to fold under the body' - FAILS. The hind limbs are rotated forward and downward under the hip and are planted. Nothing trails back. CORRECTION/ADDITION: the judge said only that there is no fused rear paddle. True, but what IS drawn at the rear is worse than nothing - a short truncated grey CYLINDER stub projects backward from the upper rear of the body, capped with a flat elliptical cut face, reading as a docked/amputated tail. That stub is the thing occupying the space the fused hind-flipper paddle should own, and any fix must delete it, not just add flippers.
3. 'round dog-like head with large dark eyes and whiskers' - PARTIAL, mostly fails. The large dark eye with a bright catchlight and white ring is present and readable (the one must-read element that lands). But the skull is not round: it is a hard-edged pentagon/wedge with a straight sloping occipital facet. And whiskers are ABSENT - at 14x the muzzle shows only a dark oval nose, one curved mouth line, and a short dark jaw crease bar running back from under the nose. No whisker array, no whisker spots.

NOTHING in the judge's verdict is refutable. Zero of three must-reads read correctly; the organism reads as a stubby grey quadruped mammal on planted paddle feet, i.e. the Sea Lion, which is the exact confusion the reference row exists to prevent. FIX ORDER: (a) drop the belly to the ground and delete the two hind standing limbs; (b) delete the rear cylinder tail stub and replace it with a fused rearward paddle; (c) taper the trunk toward both ends; (d) delete the occipital wedge and round the skull; (e) add whiskers; (f) the front limbs should become long fore-flippers laid alongside the chest, not columns.

rows.readsAs: a generic small whale — a pilot whale or a dugong
rows.defect: The head is a soft rounded nose cone occupying maybe a sixth of the body and blending seamlessly into the back; the enormous square blunt head that IS the sperm whale, taking a third of the length and ending in a flat vertical wall, is absent. There is no narrow underslung toothed lower jaw — the mouth is a thin faint smiling line right at the nose tip with no separate slender jaw beneath the head mass. There is no knuckled dorsal hump; the back carries one soft low bump in the middle that reads as a rounded dorsal fin. No blowhole is visible at the front-left of the head. What remains is a smooth grey-green torpedo with one small pectoral and a fluke, i.e. the default cetacean shape.
rows.fix: Rebuild the front third as a tall flat-fronted rectangular block that is deeper than the trunk and ends in a vertical wall, hang a thin pencil-like lower jaw well below and behind that block so the jaw is obviously narrower than the head, replace the mid-back bump with a low triangular hump followed by three or four smaller knuckles running to the tail, and put a single blowhole notch at the top-left front corner of the block.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld, but two of the three stated causes are described wrongly and would send a fixer to the wrong places. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (measured off the pixels, body bbox x=23..415, y=159..280; flukes start ~x=352, so the trunk is ~328x122 = aspect 2.7, 3.22 including flukes, against a target aspect of 4 — it is too stubby): a smooth generic cetacean chassis, side-on, swimming right-to-left with the head at the left. HEAD (must-read 1) — genuinely FAILS, but NOT because it is 'a sixth of the body'. The mouth line runs from the snout tip at x=23 back to roughly x=140, i.e. about a third of the trunk, so the head MASS fraction is close to the required 0.33. The defect is purely SHAPE: the leading edge is a single smooth convex arc (tip y=220 at x=23, rising to the dorsal crest y=159 by x=103) — a rounded nose cone / melon. There is no flat vertical front face, no squared box, no straight-cut brow. Fix the profile, not the length. LOWER JAW (must-read 2) — FAILS, and it is not merely 'a faint smile line at the nose tip': there IS a long scribed mouth line running the full length of the head from the tip back to the pectoral flipper. What is missing is the geometry — the ventral silhouette below that line is the full body wall, not a separate slender rod-like jaw hanging under an overhanging head, and there are no teeth. It reads as a mouth drawn on, not a jaw built. DORSAL (must-read 3) — FAILS, and the judge's description is factually wrong. There is NO bump and NO dorsal fin anywhere. The top profile is strictly monotonic: flat crest at y=159 from x=103 to x=131 (rel 0.20-0.28, i.e. directly over the head/shoulder), then an unbroken descent to the tail (x=171 y=167, x=219 y=184, x=267 y=195, x=315 y=206). No knuckles, no triangular nub, nothing at the two-thirds mark where a sperm whale's hump belongs. (For contrast, the sibling Pilot_Whale.png DOES carry a small dorsal nub at ~x=200 — the sperm whale does not, so 'reads as a pilot whale' is true for the body but the judge imported the pilot whale's fin into this description.) BLOWHOLE — partially wrong to call it absent: there IS a small pale ellipse, ~9x8 px, RGB ~(177,189,183), centred near x=88 y=179, sitting high on the melon at rel 0.20 of body length. It may be intended as a blowhole, but it reads as a specular highlight, not a vent: it is near-white rather than a dark slit, it sits behind the melon rather than at the extreme front-left of the head, and the identical pale dot appears on Pilot_Whale.png and other cetaceans in this set, so it is a chassis default, not a sperm-whale feature. DECISIVE EVIDENCE — this is a SHARED CETACEAN CHASSIS, not a sperm whale. Sperm_Whale.png and Beluga.png occupy the identical vertical band (y=159..280, height 122 px to the pixel) and share the same rounded snout, same pale melon dot, same eye dot with catchlight, same low ovoid pectoral flipper at x=119..170, same notched fluke. Only colour and trunk width differ. Every one of the three must-reads that constitute sperm-whale identity is absent as drawn form. FIX ORDER: (1) rebuild the front third as a rectangular block with a near-vertical flat front face and a level flat top from the very tip; (2) hang a narrow underslung lower jaw as separate geometry beneath the overhanging head, with the head mass clearly wider/deeper than the jaw; (3) replace the smooth crest with a low triangular hump at ~0.6-0.7 of body length followed by three or four knuckles down the caudal peduncle; (4) move the blowhole to the extreme front-left top of the snout and render it dark; (5) stretch the trunk toward aspect 4.

rows.readsAs: a walrus — but only because of the tusks; the body alone is a pink dachshund
rows.defect: The tusks read and carry the name, so a stranger will say walrus. Everything else is the shared pinniped chassis recoloured pink: the same level topline, the same shallow sausage torso with no blubber mass, no wrinkling and no rolls, and the same four short cylindrical dog legs on rounded paw pads rather than short broad flippers. The dense bristle moustache is not there — only a couple of thin hairline strokes at the muzzle, so the squared muzzle reads as a dog nose with two teeth stuck on it. The tusks also emerge from the side of the cheek rather than descending from under a heavy overhanging upper lip.
rows.fix: Swap the four dog legs for short broad flippers and inflate the torso into a heavy sagging blubber mass with visible neck and shoulder wrinkle folds, then thicken the muzzle into a bulbous overhanging bristle pad — a dense stippled block of whiskers — with the tusks dropping from beneath it.

rows.readsAs: a kangaroo
rows.defect: The upright macropod silhouette, ears and muzzle land, but two of the three must-reads are not visible: the tiny forearms are absent entirely — the chest is an unbroken slab with no arm shape held against it — and the hind leg is one soft undifferentiated blob with no deep-folded thigh-over-shank, so the 'massive muscular hind leg' never reads. The long foot is a flat dark plank projecting to the right that does not visibly attach to the leg above it and reads as a board the animal is standing on.
rows.fix: Build the hind limb as a visible zig-zag — heavy pear thigh, narrow shank folded back, then a long foot hinged off the shank's base — and add two short forearms with paws tucked against the upper chest.

rows.readsAs: a koala
rows.defect: Ears and the big black spoon nose are present and the trunk is there, but the koala has no limbs at all — it is a fur ball pasted in FRONT of the log with nothing gripping it; the two pale smudges on the chest do not resolve into arms and no hands or feet wrap the trunk's edges, so 'gripping a vertical trunk' fails. The coat is rendered as a halo of straight white spikes that reads as thistle or frost rather than plush fur, and the eyes are large white googly discs rather than the specified small beady ones.
rows.fix: Draw two forelimbs crossing the trunk with visible clawed hands hooked over its near edge and one hind foot braced below, and shorten the fur spikes into a soft dense fringe.

rows.readsAs: a lamb or a small sheep
rows.defect: Wrong organism. It is the shared barrel-bodied lamb chassis: fleecy off-white body, four long straight columnar legs ending in dark cloven-looking hooves, a small rounded head with tiny round ears and a soft muzzle. Every must-read is missing or inverted — the tail is a short, thin, FURRED grey hook, not a long naked scaly prehensile rat tail; there is no pointed white face and no pink nose (the face is dark grey and blunt); and the coat is smooth fleece, not grizzled shaggy guard hair, with no thin bare ears.
rows.fix: Replace the whole chassis with a low crouching short-legged body and draw the identity feature first — a long bare pink-grey scaly tail as long as the body — then a sharply pointed white face with a pink nose tip and thin naked black ears.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but several stated causes are wrong and the fix list below supersedes them. What I actually saw at 6-14x zoom on head, tail and feet: a cream/off-white barrel body carrying a fine curly stipple that reads unmistakably as fleece, standing square on four straight columnar legs, high withers, short neck, small head carried up. The overall silhouette is a lamb or goat kid. Against the reference row (mustRead: naked scaly rat-like prehensile tail | pointed white face with a pink nose | grizzled grey shaggy coat and thin bare ears; eyes: small; note: read as the Virginia opossum, tail bare and scaly not furred), the single defining feature is absent and the coat is wrong, so FAIL stands.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM:
(1) 'the tail is a short furred grey hook' — half wrong. The tail is NOT furred. At 6x it is a completely flat, untextured, uniform taupe (#9d968a-ish) tube with zero stipple, while the body immediately adjacent carries a heavy fleece stipple; the tail is smooth-shaded, so texture is not the problem. The problems are LENGTH, SHAPE and COLOUR: it runs from the rump at ~x=190 to a blunt rounded tip at ~x=125, roughly 40% of the ~195px body length, and it arcs up-and-forward in a cat-like hook. A Virginia opossum tail must be near body-length, trailing/dragging or curled around a support, pink-grey flesh colour, and ringed with visible scale bands, with a furred base collar only for the first 15%. None of that is present.
(2) 'no pointed white face' — wrong as stated. There IS a pale wedge muzzle: the crown is grey-taupe and the muzzle is a distinctly lighter cream tapering wedge with a mouth line, so a light pointed face exists in embryo. What is missing is the CONTRAST and the PROPORTION — it needs to be near-white against a dark grizzled head and roughly twice as long and narrower, a true rat-like cone.
(3) 'no pink nose' — correct. The nose is a small dark brown/black oval dot at the wedge tip. It should be a broad pink rhinarium.
(4) OMITTED BY THE ORIGINAL JUDGE — ears ARE present and must be reshaped, not added. There is a large rounded taupe disc lying flat across the crown (a face-on saucer ear) plus a small pointed nub protruding at the back of the skull (the far ear). They are wrong for the species: opaque grey with no pink inner membrane and no naked leathery translucency, and disc-shaped rather than the tall thin oval bare ears the row calls for.
(5) OMITTED — the eye is wrong and is a large part of why this reads as a lamb/meerkat. It is a single big prominent eye with a white sclera ring around a large dark pupil and a catchlight. The row specifies eyes: small; opossum eyes are tiny black beads with no visible sclera.
(6) 'four straight hooved legs' — near enough but imprecise. The feet are dark grey rounded caps with two or three faint toe-division lines scored across them: a blunt clog/pad, not a cleanly cloven hoof. Either way they are not the opossum's five long splayed fingers with the divergent opposable hallux on the hind foot, which is a strong secondary identity cue and is entirely absent.
(7) 'fleecy barrel body' — confirmed and correct. Cream/off-white with a curly stipple. It must become a grizzled grey shaggy coat: dark guard hairs over a pale undercoat, a ragged rather than smooth silhouette edge, with the belly and legs darker than the back.

FIX PRIORITY: tail first (length to ~90% of body, pink-grey, scale-ringed, trailing not hooked), then coat (grizzled grey shaggy, ragged edge), then head (shrink the eye to a black bead, lengthen and whiten the muzzle, pink rhinarium, convert both ears to thin bare pink-grey ovals), then feet (splayed fingers with opposable hallux, replacing the toe-capped pads).

rows.readsAs: a small white lamb standing on the ground
rows.defect: Wrong organism and wrong posture. Despite posture 'flying' it is the identical lamb chassis standing four-square on straight legs with a cast ground shadow. The gliding membrane — the single feature that IS the identity — is completely absent: there is no skin stretched from wrist to ankle, and the flanks are plain fleece. There are no huge black eyes and no dark facial stripe running to the nose (the face is a small grey lamb muzzle with one small dark eye), and the tail is a short white tuft, nowhere near body length.
rows.fix: Redraw as a spread-eagled glide from above or three-quarters, with a taut kite-shaped membrane joining outstretched fore and hind limbs, oversized black eyes and a dark dorsal-to-nose stripe.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD after zooming the 440x440 PNG (subject occupies roughly x150-x305, y150-y260; cropped and 5-11x nearest-neighbour upscaled to inspect head, feet, tail and silhouette edge). The asset reads unambiguously as a small woolly white lamb/sheep standing four-square in profile on flat ground, with a hard black elliptical cast shadow under it. Packet spec for this row is aspect 1.8 / headFrac 0.26 / eyes prominent / posture FLYING, mustRead: skin membrane wrist-to-ankle, huge black eyes with dark facial stripe to the nose, long bushy tail as long as the body. All three must-reads fail.

WHAT I ACTUALLY SAW, feature by feature:
(1) MEMBRANE - genuinely, completely absent. The judge is right. The gap between the foreleg and hind leg is pure background black all the way from the belly line down to the ground; there is no patagium panel, no scalloped flank edge, no wrist-to-ankle web anywhere on the silhouette. The four limbs are straight vertical columns dropping from a barrel torso, not splayed outward as a gliding animal's must be. The one thing on the flank that could be mistaken for a membrane at thumbnail size is a flat pale-grey shoulder/haunch shading patch, but it sits INSIDE the body outline and connects nothing.
(2) FEET - not mentioned by the first judge but part of the same defect: each limb ends in a blunt two-toed grey hoof-like tip. A sugar glider needs five-fingered grasping hands with an opposable digit; these are ungulate feet, and they are what makes the lamb reading stick.
(3) TAIL - judge is right that it is a short tuft, and the measurement is worse than they implied. It is a rounded pale-grey fan/pom at the rump with a fringe of individual hairs radiating left, hanging DOWN toward the hocks, about 30px against a ~150px body, i.e. roughly one fifth of body length. Spec wants a bushy plume equal to the whole body.
(4) EYES AND FACE - here the judge's stated cause is PARTLY WRONG and should be corrected before any fix is attempted. Dark facial marking is NOT absent. The head carries a charcoal/mid-grey cap over the crown and cheek, and there are TWO distinct rounded black patches flanking the single visible eye - one behind it toward the ear, one forward of it between eye and muzzle. The eye itself is drawn with a gold/amber iris ring around a black pupil plus a bright specular highlight. So the correct statement is: dark facial pigment exists but is misdrawn - the iris reads AMBER, not the solid black a glider needs; the eye is small relative to the head (roughly one eighth of head width, nowhere near 'huge'); and the dark patches read as two random blotches of a mask rather than a single continuous stripe, because the stripe stops dead at the base of the muzzle and the whole snout beyond it is pale white/grey with only a tiny dark nostril dot. Nothing runs to the nose.
(5) HEAD SHAPE - the muzzle is a long tapering wedge in the sheep/deer register, and headFrac reads nearer 0.20 than the specified 0.26. A sugar glider needs a short blunt pointed face on a proportionally large head.
(6) POSTURE - specified 'flying'; delivered is a grounded standing quadruped, confirmed by the contact of all four hooves with the shadow ellipse. The judge's description of this is accurate.

Net: the organism identity is wrong (ungulate chassis, hoofed, woolly fleece texture), and the single feature that IS the species - the patagium - is not present in any form. This is a chassis/silhouette rebuild, not a polish. FAIL stands.

FIX DIRECTION implied by what I saw: replace the ungulate chassis with a small splay-limbed arboreal body, add the wrist-to-ankle membrane as an actual silhouette element spanning fore and hind limb (it must break the leg gap, which is currently empty background), swap hooves for grasping paws, extend the rump tuft into a full body-length bushy tail carried behind, blacken the iris and enlarge the eye, and merge the two existing black cheek patches into one continuous stripe that carries forward across the pale muzzle to the nose.

I decoded the PNG myself and re-rendered the subject at 5x-11x, plus a 10x crop of the abdomen tip with a 4.5x contrast boost specifically to hunt for hair-thin filaments that a normal read would lose against the dark vignette. The FAIL stands, and all three of this row's must-reads fail. The judge's phrasing 'ends in a bare bead' is correct; I would only refine it to note the terminal bead is very slightly smaller than its neighbours, which reads as a rounded full stop, not as a taper toward filaments.

They spring from the thorax and sweep almost horizontally BACKWARD across the top of the abdomen, and the two blades diverge at the tips so the pair splays open rather than closing into one upright sail. Nothing about them is triangular, nothing is vertical, and they do not meet over the back. The read is a swift/dragonfly-style streamlined sweep - the exact opposite of the mayfly's signature upright butterfly-held wing.

MUST-READ 3 - 'slender upcurved abdomen': FAILS. It is a straight, dead-level string of seven spheres in alternating pale-cream and dark-olive, each essentially the same diameter, with no taper along its length and no upward hook at the end. The judge called this correctly. It reads as a bead necklace, not as a segmented tapering tube.

WHAT THE JUDGE GOT WRONG / MISSED: (a) They did not mention the head, which is actually the one part in the asset's favour - the eyes are drawn as TWO large stacked dark spheres per side, an upper and a lower, each with a specular highlight, which is a fair nod to the male mayfly's turbinate upper eyes. 'eyes: prominent' is satisfied. This is not enough to save the asset but a fix pass should keep it, not flatten it. (b) There are no antennae at all in front of the head (not a must-read for this row, so not a defect, but worth knowing before a fix touches the head). On top of that blob sit ~28 individual leaf blades arranged as a radial starburst about the crown centre: they point up, up-left, sideways and diagonally down, i.e. every direction except straight down. It is still wrong (there is no blue cast, no grey, no matt waxy bloom, and the crown haze reads warm), but the accurate correction is 'plain leaf-green, needs a blue-grey shift and a matt bloom', not 'oversaturated'. The only real polish notes on it are (a) it is fused flush to the jaw with no hinge line or hyoid rod, so it looks painted on rather than extended, and (b) the single internal crease is what is making it read tongue-ish to a fast look - swap that crease for two or three radial fan ribs and the ambiguity disappears. MUST-READ 2 (tail longer than head and body together) GENUINELY FAILS, and the other judge's phrasing understates it only slightly. Measured from the alpha silhouette: creature spans x=44..397. The tail is a constant ~37px-thick strap from the tail base at x~180 out to the tip at x~44, rising from y~208 to y~180, so its arc length is roughly 145-150px. Head+body runs x~180 to the snout tip at x~397 = ~217px. So the tail is about 0.68x head+body when the spec wants it clearly longer than 1.0x (a real anole runs 1.5-2x SVL). Against the trunk ovoid alone (x~180..310, ~130px) the tail is roughly equal, which is what the other judge described. Worse than the length: the tail does not taper. It is a uniform-width sausage that ends in a fully ROUNDED BLUNT CLUB, hooked upward, with a dark inner stripe - it reads as a stubby hook or a tadpole tail, not a whip. Fixing this needs both a ~2x length increase and a taper to a fine point. MUST-READ 3 (adhesive toe pads on long slender limbs) - the other judge is CORRECT that no pads register, and correct about the reason. There are literally zero digits. At 11x zoom the hind limb is a two-segment zigzag (thigh down-forward, shank down-back) terminating in a featureless rounded stub; the forelimb is a single tapered rod terminating in a rounded club. No toes, no splay, no lamellae, no widened tip - nothing for a pad to sit on. The 'long slender limbs' half of the must-read IS satisfied; only the foot is missing. ADDITIONAL DEFECT NEITHER OF US SHOULD MISS: the packet note demands 'the pointed wedge head is longer and narrower than a gecko's,' and the drawn head is the opposite - a blunt rounded dome with a fat convex snout tip, closer to a frog or a cartoon gecko than to an anole wedge. Combined with the club tail and toeless limbs, the overall thumbnail read is a generic green amphibian-ish blob with a red throat pouch, not a Carolina anole. Verdict: 1 of 3 must-reads present (dewlap), 1 inverted (tail proportion + no taper), 1 wholly absent (toes/pads), plus the head-shape note missed. That is shape-level rework, not polish, so FAIL is upheld.

rows.readsAs: a beige speckled newt or a salamander
rows.defect: The identity must-read - huge lidless eyes with vertical pupils - is not merely weak, it is inverted. Despite the row specifying prominent eyes, this render has the SMALLEST eye in the whole batch: a single tiny black dot with no iris, no vertical slit and no bulge above the skull line, smaller than the ordinary-eyed Agama, Skink, Wall Lizard and Whiptail beside it. The broad splayed lamellae toes are absent entirely - the limbs are the standard toeless cones. The skin is drawn as the same smooth gradient with the same generic dark blobs as every sibling, so the granular bumpy texture never reads either.
rows.fix: Blow the eye up to fill most of the side of the head - a domed globe bulging past the skull silhouette, gold iris with a hard black vertical slit pupil and no eyelid - and fan the front foot into broad flat pads with visible lamellae ridges.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two specifics in the original claim are factually wrong and must not be carried into the fix.

CORRECTION 1 — the eye is NOT 'a bare black dot with no iris, no vertical slit'. Zoomed 22x on the eye (source rect 288,175 26x24) it is a clean white sclera oval containing a crisp, narrow, BLACK VERTICAL SLIT PUPIL with a grey inner highlight down its left edge. The pupil shape called for by the row is present and correctly drawn. Any fix that 'adds a vertical pupil' would be re-adding something already there.

CORRECTION 2 — it is NOT the smallest eye in the batch. I measured near-white sclera pixels across all six family PNGs: Wall Lizard 78 px (13x13), Agama 62 px (12x11), Skink 62 px (13x12), Anole 55 px (11x10), Gecko 38 px (10x9), Whiptail 33 px (10x8). Gecko is SECOND smallest. The defensible statement is: the Gecko, alone flagged eyes:prominent, renders a smaller eye than FOUR of the five eyes:normal siblings, roughly HALF the sclera area of the Wall Lizard.

THE REAL AND WORSE DEFECT THE ORIGINAL JUDGE MISSED — the vertical-slit eye is the FAMILY DEFAULT GLYPH, not a gecko trait. I zoomed the Wall Lizard eye at the identical 22x scale: it is the same white-oval-plus-vertical-slit component, just bigger. Every sibling carries it. So the eyes:prominent flag produced no differentiation whatsoever; it produced anti-differentiation. Fix must scale the eye up (target ~1/3 of head height, roughly 20-22 px across against the current 10) AND break it out of the shared glyph: give it a domed, bulging orb that visibly breaks the head's outline, a fixed clear brille/spectacle scale instead of a lid line, and no eyelid seam.

CONFIRMED ABSENT — splayed lamellae toes. At 10x on the leg band (source 150,225 170x45) all four limbs are featureless tapered olive sausages ending in a BLUNT ROUNDED CAP. There is not a single toe division, no splay, no pad, no lamellae banding, nowhere on any of the four feet. This is the same footless stub used on Skink and Wall Lizard.

CONFIRMED ABSENT — granular bumpy skin. The body is one smooth airbrushed vertical gradient carrying soft-edged brown blotches with no relief shading, several stamped in identical 3-blob clusters. Identical blotch stamp appears on Skink and Wall Lizard. Nothing reads as a tubercle: no highlight-plus-shadow pairing, no silhouette break along the topline or belly edge.

PARTIAL CREDIT the original claim did not give — the plump tail is arguably half-present. The tail is genuinely thick, thicker relative to its length than any sibling's. But it is the same flat band-with-a-hard-dark-inner-stripe component as Skink and Wall Lizard, it does not taper at all, its tip is a blunt round cap, and it hooks UPWARD AND FORWARD over the back like an opossum or chameleon, which no gecko does. It also overlaps the body oval with a visible seam rather than continuing the topline.

ADDITIONAL, NOT IN THE ORIGINAL CLAIM — proportion and chassis. Measured creature bbox is 241 x 110 = aspect 2.19 against a spec aspect of 3.0, the largest miss in the batch (Agama 2.97, Wall Lizard 3.00, Anole 3.34, Skink 3.43, Whiptail 4.08). The body is inflated into a rotund egg rather than an elongated trunk. Combined with the short round head and the thick forward-curled tail, the SILHOUETTE READS AS A SHELL-LESS TURTLE OR A FAT NEWT, not a gecko. Gecko, Skink and Wall Lizard are demonstrably ONE CHASSIS: same egg body oval, same detached head ellipse joined at a visible seam, same straight ruled mouth line running to the snout tip, same eye glyph, same four toeless stub limbs, same banded tail with a dark inner stripe. Only hue, tail length and spot density change.

VERDICT: two of the three must-reads (lamellae toes, granular skin) are flatly absent, the identity must-read (huge prominent eyes) is inverted rather than merely weak, the aspect is 27% short, and the animal is separable from two siblings only by colour. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a small brown lizard-ish creature, though closer to a newt than a skink
rows.defect: This is the row the shared chassis accidentally suits best - elongate, short-legged, tapering tail - so it survives, but the must-reads are still not visible. The smooth glossy OVERLAPPING polished scales are absent: the surface is a flat matte gradient wearing the same generic dark speckles as the other five, with no scale rows and no specular sheen. rows.readsAs: an olive-drab newt, indistinguishable from the Skink render except for hue
rows.defect: Every one of the three must-reads is missing. The tail should be roughly TWICE the body length; on this render the tail is about the same length as the body ovoid, so the defining proportion of a lacertid is simply not there. The flattened slender body pressed to the surface is instead the family's deep fat egg, taller than it is thin, held up off the ground on stumps. The long splayed toes are absent - the two limbs are the standard featureless cones with no feet at all. Nothing in the silhouette separates it from the Skink beside it.

rows.verifyWhy:
I looked at the PNG at 1x and then re-cropped the tail, the legs and the head at 7-9x, and measured the silhouette by decoding the alpha/bg mask. The FAIL stands on all three must-reads, but two of the three stated causes need correcting and there are three further defects the original judge did not name.

MEASURED GEOMETRY (440x440 canvas, creature bbox x=56..383, y=157..266, so 328 x 110 px, aspect 2.98 against a spec aspect of 4.5). Segment boundaries: tail tip x=56, tail/torso junction x~182, torso ends / head begins x~302, snout tip x=383.

1. TAIL - defect confirmed, but WORSE and DIFFERENTLY WRONG than stated. Tail = 126 px. Head+body (snout to vent) = 201 px. Tail/SVL = 0.63. Even measuring against the torso ellipse alone (123 px) the ratio is 1.02. Spec wants 'roughly twice the body length'; under the generous reading it is half what it should be, under the correct SVL reading it is under a third. The judge said 'roughly the same length as the body' - that is only true if 'body' means the torso ellipse; against the head-and-body it is markedly shorter than that, so the fix budget is bigger than the claim implies. The judge ALSO missed that the tail is the wrong SHAPE, not just the wrong length: it is a near-constant-width sausage (base ~43 px deep, still ~30 px deep at three-quarters out) that ends in a rounded CLUB cap with no taper, and it curls UP and FORWARD over the back in a cartoon hook, with a dark inner racing-stripe running down its length. A lacertid tail is a straight, continuously tapering whip carried in line with the spine. Lengthening this tube alone would not fix the read; it has to be re-drawn as a taper.

CROSS-CHECK THAT SEALS IT: measured bbox aspects across the family - Wall Lizard 2.98 (spec 4.5), Skink 3.41 (spec 3.5), Whiptail 4.04 (spec 5.5). The Wall Lizard should be the second-longest of the six; it is in fact the STUBBIEST of the three long-tailed forms, shorter-looking than the Skink whose spec is a full point below it. The proportion is not merely soft, it is inverted relative to its neighbours.

2. FLATTENED BODY PRESSED TO THE SURFACE - defect confirmed exactly as described. The torso is a deep egg ellipse ~123 px long by ~75 px deep (1.6:1), belly line at y~238 with the feet at y=266, so the belly is held ~28 px clear of the ground - a quarter of the entire silhouette height is empty air under the animal. Nothing about it is flattened or appressed. 'Deep fat egg propped on stumps' is an accurate description.

3. LONG SPLAYED TOES - absent, confirmed, but the limb description in the claim is wrong and should not be used as the fix brief. There are only TWO visible limbs, not four (one hind, one fore). The hind limb is NOT a featureless cone: at 6x it resolves as a two-segment jointed limb - a backswept thigh with a clear knee, then a shank angling down-and-forward, built from two overlapping capsules. The forelimb IS a single tapered cylinder. Both terminate in a plain rounded cap: zero digits, zero splay, no foot geometry of any kind, not even a wedge. So the limb model already has articulation to build on; what is missing is strictly the foot/toe fan. Additionally both limbs are held VERTICALLY UNDER the body (parasagittal, mammal-like pillars), not sprawled out to the sides with the elbow and knee held wide - so the packet's 'posture: sprawling' also fails, which the original judge did not flag.

4. SHARED CHASSIS - confirmed, and worth stating precisely. Side by side with Skink.png the two are the same body with a hue swap: identical up-curled club tail with the same dark inner stripe, identical fat-egg torso, identical blunt oval head, identical straight scribed mouth line running nearly the full head length, identical two pillar legs, identical spot-blob speckling. Only the colour (olive vs brown) and the spot placement differ. The claim's 'nothing in the silhouette separates it from the Skink' is literally true.

5. FURTHER DEFECT NOT IN THE CLAIM - the eye is a white sclera with a black VERTICAL SLIT pupil. The packet's row for Wall Lizard says 'eyes: normal'; vertical pupils are the Gecko row's must-read. Real wall lizards have round pupils. The same slit eye appears on the Skink, so this is a chassis default leaking a nocturnal-gecko cue onto a diurnal lacertid.

6. HEAD - a plain rounded oval, no snout taper, no neck constriction (it abuts the torso ellipse directly), no jaw line, no ear opening, no temporal shape. headFrac measures 81/328 = 0.25 against a spec of 0.24, so the head SIZE is the one number that is right; its FORM carries no lacertid information.

VERDICT: FAIL upheld. The asset reads as a generic stumpy quadruped blob with a curled sausage tail, not as a wall lizard, and it is indistinguishable in silhouette from the Skink in the same batch. Fix brief: re-draw the tail as a straight tapering whip roughly 2x SVL carried in line with the spine (not a curled club); flatten the torso to a shallow depressed slab with the belly close to the substrate; splay both limbs laterally with elbow/knee held out and add long spreading digits on all feet; give the skull a slight wedge and a neck; and swap the slit pupil for a round one.

rows.readsAs: a long-tailed brown lizard, but not identifiably a whiptail

rows.readsAs: a winged ant, or a small bee with an oversized head
rows.defect: The identity must-read is not merely missing, it is inverted: instead of a strongly humped thorax over a bowed head, the render is two grey spheres of near-equal size sitting level on the same centreline, and the HEAD sphere is the LARGER and no lower than the thorax. There is no bowed head, no shoulder hump, no dorsal arch at all. rows.verifyWhy:
Verified by decoding the PNG and re-reading it at 5x, 11x, 13x and 20x with a 2.9x brightness boost, plus a column-by-column pixel scan of the silhouette (440x440 canvas; content bbox x99-339, y87-335).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a light lavender-grey ball at x153-195 / y178-218 (~43 wide x 40 tall) carrying one large dark eye with a specular highlight and two thin antennae sweeping up-left and left; tangent to it a second lavender-grey ball at x198-~232 / y179-219 (~35 wide x 40 tall); behind that an opaque, flat-white, cloud-lobed wing mass spanning x219-270 / y188-208 with a notch splitting it into two lobes; a comb of ~12 alternating light/dark vertical bars hanging under the wing root at x237-263 / y200-225; three thin straight legs dropping from beneath the HEAD ball, one or two from beneath the thorax ball, and one very long angular hind leg at the right; a flat elliptical ground shadow.

THE CORE CLAIM IS CONFIRMED, AND I CAN QUANTIFY IT. The must-read 'strongly humped thorax over a bowed head' is not merely weak, it is absent and mildly inverted. The two spheres' toplines are y178 (head) and y179 (thorax) and their bottoms y218 and y219 - level to within one pixel. The head is the WIDER of the two (43px vs ~35px, and headFrac reads ~0.35 of body length against a spec of 0.24). There is no dorsal hump anywhere on the topline, no drop of the head below the thoracic crown, no neck, and no forward bow. Read cold this is a two-ball insect - closest to an ant or a small bee - not a black fly.

NO ABDOMEN - CONFIRMED, BUT THE MECHANISM IS DIFFERENT FROM WHAT WAS CLAIMED. There is no third grey mass, but the abdomen is not simply omitted into empty space: the opaque white wing blob is painted exactly over the abdomen's territory (x219-270), so the rear third of the animal is solid flat white. Under 2.9x boost I searched that band for any grey body pixels behind the thorax and found none. The fix is both 'add an abdomen' and 'stop letting the wing paint opaquely over the body' - the wing is rendered as flat 100% white with no translucency, which also breaks the 'clear wings' must-read. Of the three must-reads, only 'short broad wings' is even partly readable, and it reads as a fluffy cloud puff rather than a clear membranous wing.

TWO PARTS OF THE CLAIM ARE WRONG AND MUST NOT BE FIXED AS STATED.
(1) 'A long angular two-segment line meets at a vertex far off the right side, DISCONNECTED from the body.' It is not disconnected and it is not a stray fragment - it is the hind leg, and it is attached. Its coxal end starts on the ventral rear of the body at approximately x261, y203, right under the wing base and touching the body silhouette; it runs back near-horizontally to a sharp vertex at approximately x294, y201, then descends forward-and-down to a foot at approximately x276, y247. The real defect is that the hind leg is drawn far too long (its reach exceeds the entire body length), with a hard near-90-degree elbow and zero taper, so it reads as a drafting '7' rather than a leg - but the fix is to shorten/soften/taper that leg, NOT to reconnect a floating line.
(2) 'A comb of short vertical black bars ... stray fragments stranded OUTSIDE the silhouette.' The comb is contiguous with the wing: it hangs directly off the wing's ventral/trailing root and its top edge is inside the white wing mass. It is a wing-fringe artifact, not a floating fragment. It is still a defect - black flies have no such fringe, and rendered as ~12 hard alternating light/dark vertical bars it reads as a barcode or a radiator grille - but the fix is to remove/soften the fringe primitive at the wing root, not to reattach orphaned geometry.

ADDITIONAL DEFECTS NEITHER JUDGE NAMED: three of the six legs attach beneath the HEAD sphere rather than the thorax, which is anatomically impossible for an insect and is a large part of why the front ball reads as a thorax-substitute; there are no mouthparts of any kind (a black fly's short stout piercing mouthparts are absent); and the body is a pale lavender-grey, roughly mid-luminance against a near-black field, which contradicts the 'stubby compact dark body' must-read for an organism literally named Black Fly.

Band FAIL stands: the single identity must-read (humped thorax over bowed head) is absent, the body plan is two segments instead of three, and the organism does not read as a black fly.

rows.readsAs: a mosquito — the plumose antenna and long narrow wings carry it

rows.readsAs: A cartoon tadpole or a fat smiling grub/slug with two little peg legs — most strangers would say tadpole or caterpillar before amphibian.
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail, and the identity one is the worst. (1) The paddle tail is absent: instead of a tapering laterally flattened vertical blade, the tail is a thick blunt club that is wider than the trunk at its midpoint and ends in a rounded stump; behind it sits a semi-transparent brown lobe that does not connect to the tail outline and reads as ghosted/stray geometry, not as a fin. (2) Four small splayed limbs are not present: only two peg-stubs are legible, both crowded into the FRONT half (one under the head, one at mid-belly), so the rear third of the trunk and the entire tail base are limbless — no hind-limb pair at the pelvis at all. The pegs are featureless dark spikes with no splayed toes or foot pads. (3) The skin is a smooth glossy gradient with two soft airbrush highlights — no granular, warty or moist-bumped texture anywhere. Compounding it, the head is a separate oval visibly seamed onto the trunk with a constriction, giving a bowling-pin silhouette, and the single large cartoon eye plus curved smile push it further toward mascot than organism.

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of the four stated causes are factually wrong and must not be fixed as stated.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (measured off the pixels; body-pixel column spans, origin = 440x440 canvas). Silhouette runs x=67..370 (303px) with max depth 53px, so aspect ~5.7 against the spec's 4. Head occupies x~312..372 (~60px) = headFrac ~0.20, close enough to the 0.22 target.

1) TAIL — must-read 'laterally flattened paddle tail' is ABSENT. Confirmed, but NOT for the reason given. The claim that it is 'WIDER than the trunk at its midpoint' is measurably false: the tail column-span is 24px at the tip (x=70), peaks at 49px near x=95-100, then holds a near-constant 41-45px all the way from x=110 to x=195, while the trunk peaks at 53px (x=245-280). The tail is ~80-85% of trunk depth, not wider. The REAL defect is that it has essentially ZERO taper over its whole length (43px +/-2 across a 100px run) and terminates in a full hemispherical round cap, so it reads as a fat round tube/sausage swept up-and-left, not a blade. There is no dorsal or ventral fin membrane, no lateral compression, no knife edge, no crest — nothing that says 'newt' rather than 'thick lizard tail'.

2) THE GHOST LOBE — the claim is CORRECT and is the ugliest single artifact. A large soft-edged translucent dark-olive ellipse (~100px wide x ~85px tall, centred ~x=127, y=206) sits BEHIND and BELOW the tail. Its centre is ~20px below the tail's own axis, it bulges well past the tail's ventral edge, and it stops short of the tail tip (its left edge is x~76 vs tail tip x=67). If this was meant to be the caudal fin it is in the wrong place, the wrong shape (a circle, not a lens), and the wrong alpha — on screen it reads as a smudge or a second shadow floating off the animal.

3) LIMBS — the claim 'only two peg-limbs are legible and both sit in the front half, leaving the pelvis and tail base limbless' is WRONG. At 8-16x magnification there are FOUR limbs, correctly paired and correctly placed: a crossing pair at the pelvis (x~195-215, i.e. exactly at the tail base the judge called limbless) and a crossing pair at the shoulder (x~305-335). The near limb of each pair is darker, the far limb paler and behind. The judge miscounted because the limbs are a near-black olive against a near-black navy field and merge into two smudges at 1x. What IS correct: every limb ends in a blunt rounded peg — no toes, no splay, no ankle, no foot plate (there is at most a faint tonal lobe at the fore-foot tip). So must-read 'four small splayed limbs' is HALF met: four limbs, zero splayed feet, and they are badly under-contrasted. Additional defect neither judge named: the far-side limb of each pair pokes ABOVE the dorsal topline as a dark nub at both shoulder and hip (visible at x~200 and x~310, sitting on top of the back outline) — a z-order/placement error that makes the back look like it has two spikes.

4) SKIN — must-read 'moist granular skin' is ABSENT. Confirmed. Smooth airbrush gradient only: one broad pale specular band running the length of the dorsum plus about six soft blurred yellow discs used as spots. Zero granularity, zero pebbling, no wet speckle, no pore/tubercle noise.

5) HEAD/SILHOUETTE — substantially correct. The head is a discrete ellipse whose own light rim-stroke is drawn OVER the trunk, so the join is a visible arc-shaped seam at x~310, and the column span dips 53 -> 40 -> 50 across it (a pinched waist between two ovals of nearly equal depth). The face is cartoon: a large round white-sclera eye with black pupil and a highlight dot, set high and far forward, plus a long upcurved 'smiling' mouth line. I would soften the 'tadpole' read — four limbs are present, so it lands nearer a smiling cartoon blob-salamander than a tadpole — but the two-oval bowling-pin construction, the untapered fat tail and the toeless pegs do push it into cartoon-larva territory.

VERDICT: two of three must-reads (paddle tail, granular skin) are outright absent and the third is only half met, so FAIL stands. Fix list in priority order: (a) rebuild the tail as a laterally compressed blade — taper the core to roughly one third of trunk depth by mid-length and add a continuous dorsal+ventral fin membrane that widens toward a pointed, not rounded, tip; (b) delete the detached translucent disc entirely rather than trying to reposition it; (c) add splayed 3-4 toe feet and raise limb luminance so they separate from the background, and drop the far-side limbs below the dorsal outline; (d) add granular skin noise; (e) merge the head ellipse into the trunk so the rim-stroke does not cut a seam across the neck.
