rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with three corrections to the stated cause. I decoded the 440x440 PNG and measured it pixel-by-pixel (the render is very dark; a 3.0-3.6x brightness boost was needed to see anything, and all the geometry below is measured on the raw pixels, not the boosted view).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. The fish faces RIGHT. The bright body fill runs x=117 (caudal peduncle) to x=317 (snout), 200px long; a thin round spear bill runs x=317-367 (50px, ~17% of the 295px total length); a forked tail sits x=72-117; body depth peaks at 64px around x=200.

CORRECTION 1 - the sail is NOT absent. There IS a dorsal element: a filled mid-blue (24,33,71) shape sitting on the back from x=176 to x=287. It is a smooth, soft-edged, symmetric rounded DOME - no straight leading edge, no spine tips, no scalloped membrane margin, no hard silhouette. Its apex is at x=220-230, y=155; the back line beneath it is y=177. So the fin stands 22px above the back over a body 61px deep at that station = 36% of body depth. The mustRead demands TALLER THAN THE BODY IS DEEP, i.e. >=61px. The drawn fin is under a THIRD of the required height - it must roughly triple. The judge's "about a third of body depth" is exactly right.

CORRECTION 2 - the position claim is WRONG, and this matters for the fix. The judge says the bump sits "over the front third of the back." It does not. It spans x=176-287 of a back running x=117-317, i.e. the MIDDLE ~55% of the back, centred at x=231, only slightly forward of the body midpoint (x=217). What is actually missing is the REAR: the last 30% of the back (x=117-176, from behind the dome to the tail stalk) carries no fin at all, where a sailfish sail runs nearly to the caudal peduncle. The fin also stops 30px short of the head. Fix = extend it fore and aft AND triple its height; do not "move it back from the front third," it is not at the front.

CORRECTION 3 - there IS a latent sail-ray pass, and it is invisible. About eight thin diagonal strokes are drawn from the back upward past the dome's fill boundary into the background. At normal exposure they are unreadable: at y=145 they measure (13,18,25) against a background of (9,15,21) - a ~4/255 delta, ~1.5% contrast. Only a 3.6x boost reveals them. They also OVERSHOOT the dome's silhouette by ~15px into empty water, so even if their contrast were raised they would read as scratches above the fish rather than as spines inside a membrane. Whatever code draws them is drawing rays for a sail that was never made tall enough to contain them - that is the likely single root cause.

PELVIC FINS - judge is nearly right but not literally right. They are not "missing": there is one shallow, soft, rounded ventral lobe spanning x=176-208 (32px) that hangs ~6px below the belly line. It is a low blob, not two long filaments. So the fin object exists; the THREAD-LIKE quality - the defining part of the mustRead - is entirely absent. Note this same lobe appears on the Swordfish, whose mustRead explicitly says "no pelvic fins."

INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE MARLIN - CONFIRMED, and now quantified. Marlin's dorsal dome: span x=170-292, apex x=220-230 at y=159, back at y=179 => 20px over a 56px body = 37%. Sailfish: span x=176-287, apex x=220-230 at y=155, back at y=177 => 22px over 61px = 36%. Two pixels of difference in height, the same horizontal span, the same apex station, the same soft dome profile. Stacking Sailfish / Marlin / Swordfish at identical crop confirms ONE CHASSIS: identical leaf-shaped fusiform outline, identical forked tail with the same radiating ray streaks behind it, identical white lateral midline stripe, identical checker scale pattern, identical tiny white-ringed circular eye at the same coordinate, identical small triangular pectoral fan inside the flank, identical ventral lobe, identical rounded dorsal dome. The only real variables are hue (Sailfish deep blue, Marlin cyan, Swordfish pink) and bill length - and even that is inverted: the Sailfish's bill (50px) is SHORTER than the Marlin's (63px), where the sailfish's should be the longer, thinner one.

BAND: FAIL. Two of the three mustReads fail - the enormous sail (the entire identity of the animal) is drawn at ~1/3 height over ~55% of the back as the family's generic fin dome, and the thread-like pelvics are a generic lobe. The only mustRead that survives is the thin spear bill, which is the one feature it shares with two other species in the same batch. As drawn this asset does not read as a sailfish; it reads as a blue recolour of the Marlin.

rows.readsAs: a mauve-purple marlin
rows.defect: The bill is the exact same thin round spike used on the Marlin -- the packet's own note says it must be flat and blade-like, not round -- and it is roughly a fifth of the total length, not a third. The tall stiff crescent dorsal is absent; the back carries the same soft dark lump as the marlin and sailfish. The body is also the shared crosshatched scale patch, which contradicts 'smooth scaleless body'. The mauve/purple colour reads as an alien fish rather than a swordfish's dark bronze-and-silver.
rows.fix: Widen and flatten the bill into a visible blade with parallel edges and lengthen it to a third of the total length, and drop the crosshatch scale texture so the body reads smooth.

rows.readsAs: a generic deep-bodied blue fish
rows.defect: The body is acceptably deep and spindle-like, but the two marks that make a tuna a tuna are both missing. There is no stiff crescent-moon tail on a narrow keeled stalk -- the tail is the same soft notched triangular fan the barracuda and wahoo get. There is no row of small yellow finlets between the second dorsal and the tail; the dorsal region is instead two vague dark humps of the same blurred blob type. Nothing on the fish is yellow.
rows.fix: Swap the fan tail for a high-aspect lunate crescent with a pinched keeled peduncle, and add a visible line of small bright-yellow finlets along the top and bottom of the tail stalk.

rows.readsAs: a blue barracuda
rows.defect: This is the best of the six: the body is genuinely elongate and there ARE faint blue vertical bars on the flank, and the snout is drawn to a point. But the bars are so low in contrast against the blue body that they nearly vanish, the beak-like jaws are the same symmetrical taper as every other fish rather than a distinct long beak, there is no row of finlets running to the tail, and the head region is cluttered by two soft dark blobs (the dorsal and pectoral) that read as smudges rather than fins.
rows.fix: Raise the contrast of the vertical bars to clearly dark navy on a lighter flank and add the finlet row to a stiff forked tail.

rows.readsAs: a generic brown crested songbird or a small partridge
rows.defect: The two features that ARE a hoatzin's face are simply not drawn: there is no bare blue facial skin and no staring red eye — the face is the same plain brown as the body and the eye is the same tiny black bead used on the other three birds. The crest is present but is a small, thin, body-coloured fan of spikes rather than a tall shaggy rufous punk crest, and it reads as an incidental tuft. The 'heavy chest over a slim neck' is impossible to see because the chassis has no neck at all — the skull sits directly on the shoulder. The tail is a flat striped plank of slats, not a broad rounded feathered fan.
rows.fix: Paint a bare cobalt-blue mask over the whole face from bill base past the eye, drop a large red iris with a black pupil into it, and rebuild the crest as a tall ragged rufous spray twice the head's height.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the full 440x440 render, then a 6x nearest-neighbour crop of the head (40,80,140,120) and of the legs (100,260,200,90), and ran a pixel census of the whole image.

WHAT IS THERE: a plump side-on brown bird perched on a ground shadow, facing left. Rounded oval body in mid-brown, one folded wing drawn as a hatched/cross-stitched tan panel with two darker chevron coverts, a long banded tail of 4-5 flat straps sweeping right and well past the body (roughly 45% of total length), and two thin pale-yellow stick legs with three toes each. Head is a small ball fused straight onto the chest.

CLAIM 1 - blue face and red eye absent: CONFIRMED, and stronger than stated. I counted every non-transparent pixel: ZERO pixels anywhere in the image satisfy red (R>150, G<90, B<90) and ZERO satisfy blue (B>110 and B > R+30). The dominant non-background colours are 55,34,18 and 125,79,42 - browns. The face is uniform body-brown with no bare-skin patch of any hue, and the eye is a ~7px black bead with a single white specular dot, upper-left. The packet asks for eyes: prominent; this bead is the family's default small eye, not prominent. So the single most diagnostic hoatzin feature - the blue bare face carrying a staring red iris - is not merely faint or mislocated, it is chromatically impossible in this render.

CLAIM 2 - crest 'reduced to a small body-coloured tuft': PARTLY WRONG, correct this before any fix. The crest is NOT a soft tuft. At 6x it is a genuine spiky splayed comb: five to six thin tapered spikes fanning up and back from the crown, plus a longer swept-back spine at the rear - the punk form is correctly drawn. It is also NOT body-coloured; it is a slightly hotter orange-brown than the crown, so 'rufous' is arguably satisfied. The real defect is SCALE and ROOT: the comb is only about 35% of head height (a hoatzin's crest is a ragged fan roughly as tall as the skull) and it sits on a bare hinge stalk that leaves a visible gap between comb and crown, so it reads as a cockade pinned on rather than crown feathering. Fix by enlarging, not by redrawing.

DEFECT THE ORIGINAL JUDGE MISSED: the bill is actively wrong for the species. It is a large, bright saturated-yellow triangular cone with a visible gape line - a finch/seed-eater bill occupying about a third of head length. A hoatzin's bill is short, stubby, deep-based and dark horn/blackish. This yellow cone is doing as much damage to the read as the missing face, because it is the loudest colour on the animal and it actively asserts 'passerine seed-eater'.

MUST-READ 3 - 'long broad tail and heavy chest over a slim neck': half met. The long banded tail is present and reads well; the chest is suitably heavy. But there is NO neck at all - the head ball is welded directly to the shoulder, so the slim-neck/heavy-chest contrast that gives a hoatzin its top-heavy prehistoric line is missing.

NET: two of three must-reads fail (face/eye absent outright, neck absent), the third is undersized, and the bill contradicts the organism. Rendered at thumbnail size this is a generic brown crested finch, not a hoatzin. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a generic kingfisher-ish bird with an oversized yellow bill
rows.defect: The huge dagger bill is genuinely present and the body is correctly stocky and short-tailed, so the silhouette is in the right neighbourhood — but the head is uniformly dark grey-brown with no whitish crown and no dark brown eye stripe, so the single most recognisable head pattern is missing entirely. The bill is also seated too low on the face, hanging off the jawline rather than continuing the line of the forehead, which reads as a stuck-on beak. The head is not visibly oversized relative to the body; it is the same small round skull the other three birds use.
rows.fix: Repaint the head whitish-cream and lay a broad dark chocolate stripe from the bill base through the eye to the nape, then raise the bill so its upper edge continues the forehead line.

rows.readsAs: a green quail
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads survive. The tail is a short horizontal plank of green slats roughly the same length as the body and pointing straight back — nowhere near 'two streaming plumes far longer than the body', and nothing about it streams or hangs. The belly is the same green as the rest of the bird, so the crimson underside that gives the quetzal its contrast is completely absent. The crest is a tiny spiky green tuft, not a round bristly helmet. What is left is the identical partridge egg-body from the other three assets recoloured green, with the same beady eye, the same mid-belly straw legs and the same flank wing-lens.
rows.fix: Replace the tail plank with two ribbon-thin emerald streamers that trail two to three body-lengths down and behind, and paint the entire belly and undertail crimson.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, but two parts of the stated cause are wrong and must not be fixed as written.

WHAT I SAW (440x440, sprite bbox x87-352, y131-292 = 266w x 162h, landscape). A plump perched galliform standing on two yellow legs over a ground shadow: round breast, one large teal wing ellipse outlined in darker green filling the flank, short neck, small round head, long yellow-amber triangular dagger bill, black bead eye with a white catchlight.

CORRECTION 1 - "no helmet crest" is FALSE. A crest IS drawn and is clearly visible at 8x: a splayed, hand-like topknot of about five thin finger-shaped fronds rising ~20px off the crown behind the eye and fanning up and backward, in the same teal as the body. The defect is its FORM, not its absence - it is a cockatiel/hoatzin-style wispy spiky topknot, whereas the must-read wants a dense ROUND BRISTLY HELMET mounding forward over the forehead and the base of the bill. Fix = reshape/thicken and move it forward over the bill base; do not "add a crest", one is already there and a second would double it.

CORRECTION 2 - the tail is more nuanced than "a plank of green slats". At 6x there are TWO overlapping straps: a lighter upper strap ruled with 4-5 dark cross-bars, and a darker plank tucked behind/below it, plus a small fan of short dark bristle strokes at the tail base. So the COUNT of two is nominally present; what fails is their shape, length and direction. They are broad, flat, rigid, non-tapering slats with a blunt squared-off tip, aimed horizontally back and very slightly down. Measured: breast front x=97 to rump x=233 = ~136px of body; tail projects x=233 to x=352 = ~119px, i.e. the tail is ~0.87x body length. The must-read demands plumes FAR longer than the body (real streamers run 2-3x), and the packet note says they hang far BELOW a perched bird - nothing on this sprite hangs below the body at all, the feet are the lowest point. The packet aspect spec of 0.35 (tall, narrow) is contradicted by the actual landscape 266x162 bbox. So the judge's "short, body-length, pointing straight back" is correct in substance.

CORRECTION 3 - "no crimson belly / uniformly green" is CORRECT and I confirmed it numerically. Hue census over 16,807 non-background pixels: 93.8% at hue ~160 deg (teal-green), 1.5% at h200 and 1.3% at h180 (blue rim light), and 3.0% at h40 - and the h40 warm pixels are ONLY the bill and the two legs/feet. Zero pixels anywhere satisfy r>90 with r>1.3xg and r>1.3xb, so there is no red or crimson pixel on the bird. Belly, vent and undertail are the same teal as the mantle. The green is also flat-teal rather than metallic emerald with the iridescent gold-green sheen the must-read calls for.

CORRECTION 4 - "shared partridge body recoloured" is CORRECT and identifiable. The Hoatzin in this same packet (batch-001 #1) is the same chassis in brown: identical round breast, identical outlined wing ellipse, identical splayed frond topknot, identical yellow triangular dagger bill, identical twin cross-barred plank tail, identical yellow legs and feet. Silhouette IoU Quetzal vs Hoatzin = 0.67 (the residual is mostly overall scale - Hoatzin renders 24,221 lit px vs Quetzal 16,843); vs Kookaburra only 0.39. So the recolour twin is the Hoatzin, not a generic partridge.

SCORE AGAINST THE THREE MUST-READS: (1) two streaming plumes far longer than the body - ABSENT (two rigid slats at 0.87x body, horizontal, nothing hanging). (2) metallic emerald over a crimson belly - HALF (green present but flat, crimson belly entirely absent). (3) round bristly helmet crest above a yellow bill - HALF (yellow bill present, but a wispy spiky topknot instead of a helmet). Two of three defining identity reads are missing or wrong, and the silhouette is a shared perched galliform, so the asset reads as a green quail/hoatzin rather than a resplendent quetzal. Also worth logging: the packet specifies posture: flying, but the render is a standing perched bird with both feet planted.

rows.readsAs: a grey-brown quail or guineafowl chick
rows.defect: The forehead horn — the one feature the horned screamer is named for and the only thing separating it from any other dumpy grey bird — is entirely absent; the crown is bare and smoothly rounded. The bony wing spurs are also absent: the wing is the same dark-outlined feather lens used on the other three birds with nothing at the bend. The body is not goose-like or bulky, it is the family's standard small egg with a short dark wedge tail, and although the posture is called biped the legs are the same thin mid-belly straws as the flying birds, so there is no heavy standing waterfowl stance.
rows.fix: Add a long thin pale horn curving forward and up off the forehead, and put a visible sharp spur at the leading bend of the wing.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 5x and 6x zoom on the head, the wing bend, and the whole silhouette. The packet's three must-reads are (a) thin curved horn projecting from the forehead, (b) goose-like bulky body with a small chicken-like bill, (c) sharp bony spurs on the wing bends. Two are entirely absent and the third is only half-served, so the FAIL stands.

WHAT I SAW. HORN: absent, confirmed. The 5x head crop shows a perfectly smooth spherical crown in flat grey-taupe with a soft rim highlight along the top-left. Nothing breaks the crown silhouette anywhere between the bill base and the nape — no horn, no filoplume, no crest, no wattle, no knob, not even a stray dark stroke that could be read as one. The single defining feature that names the species is not drawn. WING SPURS: absent, confirmed. The folded wing is a large oval covering most of the flank, outlined by a thick dark chocolate arc; I zoomed the wing bend (the upper-front carpal region where the arc meets the shoulder, orig px ~120-240 x, ~160-270 y) at 6x. The arc is a smooth continuous curve into the shoulder mass. No spur, claw, thorn or projection, and the outer body silhouette on the leading edge is an unbroken convex curve. Both are true absences, not small-and-missed features.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS WRONG. The judge says 'the body is the family's small egg' — that is inaccurate and would send the fix in the wrong direction. The body is NOT small: it is a broad, plump, deep egg at roughly the packet's 1.4 aspect, filling most of the frame and considerably bulkier than a chick's. The actual proportion defect is the NECK, which the judge did not mention: there is essentially no neck at all — the round head is pasted directly onto the shoulder line with about one head-radius of grey between skull and back. A screamer is an anseriform with a distinctly long, thick, upright goose neck carrying the head well clear of the body; without it the mass reads galliform. So the fix is 'add a long thick goose neck and lift the head', not 'enlarge the body'.

Also uncorrected by the judge: the BILL is wrong in the opposite direction from what the packet asks. It is a long-ish, sharply pointed yellow-amber triangular wedge — a generic seed-eater/finch cone — where the packet's note explicitly requires a SHORT, HOOKED, chicken-like bill. That is a third must-read miss the original claim skipped over.

MINOR NOTES. Plumage is grey-brown with pale cream dash/scale speckling across the flank and wing — the judge's 'grey guineafowl' read is fair as a mis-identification, though the closest real match is a quail or partridge. The TAIL is not chick-like at all: it is a long dark pointed wedge sweeping back and up to the right past the body edge, with a fan of thin dark barb lines under it — too long and too pointed for a screamer, which has a short broad tail. Feet are thin yellow legs with three forward toes and a visible hind toe, entirely unwebbed; the packet's note calls for partly webbed feet, so this is a further (smaller) miss. Eye is a plain black bead with a single white catchlight, correct for 'normal'.

NET: as drawn this is a generic small galliform ground bird. Zero of the three identity must-reads read; the organism itself is wrong. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a quail or partridge chick
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. The body is not carried high on long bare legs — the legs are two short yellow stubs barely clearing the belly, with the whole bird squatting on the ground shadow. There is no thick upright neck; the round head is welded directly onto the shoulder. The head is not flat-crowned and the bill is not short and stout — it is a domed skull with a thin pointed yellow dagger. Nothing in the silhouette says 'large terrestrial bird'.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette off the chassis: stilt the legs to roughly half total height as bare pale columns, lift the body into a horizontal barrel above them, and insert a thick vertical neck column between shoulder and a flat-crowned head with a short conical bill.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld — all three mustReads fail — but two of the three stated causes are described wrongly and the biggest driver was not named at all. Measured off the 440x440 source (creature spans y=118..309, ~191px tall; body-only x120..281 = 161 wide by y140..268 = 128 deep).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON SCREEN: a near-spherical egg body with a big scalloped wing-oval plastered on the flank inside a dark swirl outline, a large round head set forward and LOW, a yellow wedge bill, short bare yellow legs, a plain dark-grey pointed tail wedge projecting back-right with a small spray of thin dark filaments beneath it, and an elliptical ground shadow.

1) 'heavy horizontal body carried high on long bare legs' — FAILS, but NOT because the legs are 'two short yellow stubs'. Zoomed to 5x, the legs are properly articulated: each has a tibia dropping from the belly, a distinct rearward-bent hock at about 40% down, a tarsus, and a foot with a forward toe bar plus a small rear spur. They are bare and yellow, which is right. The defect is purely PROPORTION: yellow runs y266..309, so exposed leg is ~43px against a 128px body depth and a 191px standing height — legs are 21% of standing height where a bustard needs ~40%+. The belly hangs almost to the hocks. Second half of the mustRead also fails independently: the body is not a heavy HORIZONTAL mass, it is a circle (body-only aspect 161/128 = 1.26). The card's 1.3 aspect is met only by counting the tail wedge (bill tip x~101 to tail tip x~340 = 239 wide / 191 tall = 1.25) — the aspect number is satisfied by a tail, not by a deep horizontal torso. FIX: roughly double exposed leg length, lift the belly clear above the hock, and stretch the torso horizontally into a deep-chested oval instead of a ball.

2) 'thick upright neck' — FAILS, and the judge is right in substance, but 'the head is welded to the shoulder' is slightly overstated. A short pale neck/throat column IS drawn: at 6x you can see a ~30px-wide pale column dropping from the back of the skull into the breast around y160..180, with a visible contour break where it meets the shoulder. It simply does not RISE. The crown sits at y=118 while the back line is at y~140, so the head clears the back by only ~20px; it reads as a jowl/chin, not a neck. FIX is to lengthen and verticalise the existing column (lift the head ~60-80px clear of the back on a thick straight neck), not to add a neck from nothing.

3) 'flat-crowned head with a short stout bill' — FAILS. Domed skull: judge is CORRECT, the cranium is a plain sphere with no flattening, no flat shelf over the eye. 'Thin dagger': WRONG. The bill is not thin — it is a deep-based stout wedge, ~22px deep at the base against a ~48px head, with a clear gape line splitting upper and lower mandible. Its real defects are LENGTH and TIP: it runs x101..131 = ~30px, i.e. ~0.6 of head length, and tapers to a fine sharp point. A bustard bill should be ~0.4 head length with a blunt, slightly heavy tip. FIX: shorten by a third, blunt the tip, keep the existing base depth, and flatten the crown into a low shelf.

4) CAUSE THE JUDGE MISSED — the single strongest driver of the 'chick' read is HEAD SCALE. The head ball measures x119..167 by y118..168, ~48-50px, against a 161px body length — headFrac ~0.30, nearly double the card's specified 0.16. Combined with the large white-highlighted eye set high-forward on the skull, that alone forces a juvenile/galliform read regardless of the leg and neck fixes. Head must be shrunk to roughly half its current area.

5) CHASSIS COLLISION (family-level, decisive). Sandgrouse in this same batch is the SAME construction: identical egg torso, identical swirl-outlined wing oval, identical short yellow hocked legs, identical round small-billed head, identical dark pointed tail wedge — the Bustard is essentially a scaled-up recolour of it. Sandgrouse's own mustRead is 'plump pigeon-like body on very short feathered legs / small head on a short neck', which is close to the INVERSE of the Bustard's 'carried high on long bare legs / thick upright neck'. The Bustard has been drawn to the Sandgrouse's spec. Fixing this asset means giving it a different chassis from Sandgrouse, not retinting this one.

The judge's summary read of 'quail chick' is accurate: round head at ~2x spec, no neck rise, ball torso, short legs, cocked pointed tail.

rows.readsAs: a small crested diving waterbird — roughly right
rows.defect: The thin sharply pointed bill and the puffy rounded tailless rear both read correctly, and the crest is a nice touch. But the lobed toes must-read is entirely invisible — nothing of the foot is drawn above or through the waterline. The body is a short round egg rather than the long low hull the 2.6 aspect calls for, and it is the identical swimming chassis used for the Loon, so the two are separable only by hue.
rows.fix: Break one lobed foot out to the side of the hull at the waterline so the scalloped toe flaps are visible, and stretch the floating body longer and lower so it is not the Loon's egg in brown.

rows.readsAs: the Grebe asset recoloured black
rows.defect: The identity must-read — the checkerboard black-and-white back — is completely absent; the back is a flat unmarked dark grey with the generic wing-scallop arc on it. The dagger bill is not held level, it tilts noticeably upward, which is the grebe/anhinga cue and the opposite of a loon's carriage. The body is a short round egg sitting high rather than a long body riding low. Side by side with the Grebe it is visibly the same drawing with the brown swapped for black and the crest deleted.
rows.fix: Paint an actual checkerboard — a grid of hard white squares over the black mantle — and level the bill horizontally on a thicker straight neck over a longer, lower-riding hull.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD as FAIL, but two of the four stated causes are wrong and the fix must be made against the corrected description below.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440, measured by pixel, and viewed at 4x and 8x zoom with brightness boost): a charcoal-grey near-hemispherical body dome sitting on a waterline, a smooth uniform-width grey neck tube curving up-forward from the mid-body, a plain grey head ball with a white crescent rim-light over the crown, a prominent black bead eye with a square white specular, a bright saffron-YELLOW straight dagger bill, and two concentric thin blue ripple ellipses with a blue-grey elliptical wake shadow beneath. No legs, no feet, no tail are drawn anywhere (that part is fine - the packet note says it must not be drawn walking, and the swimming posture honours that by omission).

CORRECTION 1 - 'the mantle is flat unmarked grey' is WRONG in detail. There IS a marking layer on the back: a spray of fine white flecks/dashes across the upper mantle, plus two dark charcoal arcs (an upper wing-bar sweeping across the mantle and a lower folded-wing edge), plus the white rim highlight along the dorsal edge. It is genuinely painted, not bare. BUT the substantive charge stands: this is not a checkerboard and it is not black-and-white. Measured luminance over the mantle box (180,175)-(280,205): base ~42, p95 ~93, max ~120 out of 255 - the 'light' marks top out at mid-grey on charcoal, a contrast ratio well under 2:1, and at 1x the whole back reads as flat dark grey with a faint smudge. The marks are also irregular random flecks, not discrete alternating squares. So the identity must-read 'checkerboard black-and-white back' is ABSENT as a readable mark; the mantle is not literally unpainted.

CORRECTION 2 - 'the dagger bill tilts upward instead of level' is FLATLY WRONG; this must-read is the one thing the asset gets right. Yellow-bill mask runs x=91..148. Centreline y = 147.0 at the tip (x=91) and 146.5 at x=142 near the gape: a 0.5px rise over 51px, i.e. under 1 degree - dead level. The illusion of an upward tilt comes from the asymmetric taper (top edge falls ~5px toward the tip while the bottom edge rises), but the axis is level and the bill is straight and sharply dagger-pointed. The real bill defect is COLOUR: it is bright saffron yellow and is by far the highest-contrast element in the entire image, which reads grebe/heron and actively fights the black-and-white loon identity that is supposed to be carried by the plumage.

CORRECTION 3 - 'short high-riding egg, not a long low hull' is CORRECT. The body dome spans x~158..290 (132px wide) with its crown at y~181 and the waterline crossing at y~253, so only ~72px of exposed height: roughly 1.8:1 above water against a spec aspect of 3. It is a hemisphere pushed up out of the water, not a long low hull, and the topline peaks well above the neck root instead of running long and flat behind it.

CORRECTION 4 - 'visibly the Grebe asset with the brown swapped for black and the crest deleted' is CORRECT, and is stronger than the judge stated. Numeric comparison against Grebe.png in the same batch: yellow bill length identical at 58px in both; bill top-edge slope identical (falls 5px over 48px in both); silhouette topline across bill, head, body dome and water is the same curve offset by only (-4,-12)px; foreground bbox 83..355 / 107..323 vs 87..353 / 107..317; the water ripple ellipses and wake shadow are the same primitives; and at 8x the mantle fleck spray plus the two dark arcs are the SAME texture layer fleck-for-fleck, only hue-shifted from brown to charcoal. The Loon is the Grebe chassis translated up-left, recoloured, with the crest tuft removed.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY READS AS: a plump quail or partridge wearing a punk crest. A seriema is a long-necked, long-legged terrestrial runner in the crane/roadrunner mould; nothing about this silhouette — no neck, no leg, no tail — carries that. Measured, the hub spans ~60-85px (rows y=225-249 give 85, 64, 58, 56, 60) while arm length from base to tip is ~72px (top), ~75-90px (lateral), ~54px (lower). That is roughly ONE hub-width per arm, not two. Against a mustRead of 'many times longer than the disc is wide' the asset is off by something like 5-8x. Nothing readable as brittle-star identity is present anywhere in the image, small or hidden. FIX DIRECTION: shrink the hub to a small distinctly-outlined pentagonal/round disc, break the join so each arm springs off the disc edge as a separate part, and extend the arms to at least 4-6 disc-widths with segment banding and a couple of arms curled rather than straight.

rows.readsAs: An earthworm in grey

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified by rendering the PNG, then re-cropping the body at 4x and the head at 6x, and by pixel-diffing against Earthworm.png from the same batch. UPHELD, but two parts of the original claim need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a fully ROUND, cylindrically shaded tube in charcoal grey, laid in the same three-crest S-wave as the Earthworm (nose low-left, arch up over centre, dip, second arch, tail curling down-right), sitting on the same soft elliptical drop shadow. The tube is covered end to end in overlapping annular rings with a bright specular rib running along the top of each — the classic earthworm annulus routine. Scanline groove counts confirm the same generator: ring pitch is 6-8 px on BOTH assets and per-scanline groove counts land within 1-3 of each other. The head is a smooth EGG-SHAPED BULB, wider than the neck, terminating in a continuous convex curve with no taper and no apex. It carries ONE glossy black eye dot with a white specular highlight, set high on the left cheek — a vertebrate-style eye, not a pigment cup.

CORRECTION 1 — it is NOT a pure recolour. Silhouette IoU against Earthworm is ~0.75, not ~1.0. The Flatworm's head bulb is markedly LARGER and rounder (the packet's headFrac 0.16 vs Earthworm's 0.03 was in fact honoured), the body tube is a touch thicker, and the whole figure is a few px bigger (bbox x106-333/y171-263 vs Earthworm x112-327/y175-262). So the sculpt was parameterised, not copy-pasted — but every parameter that was moved is the WRONG one. The chassis, the pose, the ring routine, the shading model and the eye are shared verbatim, so the judge's substantive point stands: this reads as an earthworm, and specifically as a big-headed grey earthworm.

CORRECTION 2 — 'same ring count' is approximate, not exact; the Flatworm's rings are marginally broader and there are 1-3 fewer across a given scanline. Do not chase that number in a fix; it is not the defect.

MUST-READS, checked one by one at zoom:
1. 'arrowhead triangular head with two cross-eyed spots' — ABSENT on both halves. I looked specifically for a small second spot or a faint paired pigment cup at 6x: there is exactly one eye, it is glossy black with a highlight, and the head outline is a rounded ovoid with zero triangular taper. Not present-but-small; genuinely not drawn.
2. 'ribbon-flat unsegmented body' — ABSENT and actively contradicted. The body is round in section (top specular rib, dark underside rolloff) and is the single most heavily SEGMENTED surface in the whole asset. This is the loudest failure: a planarian's defining read is an unbroken, matte, paper-flat sheet.
3. 'ear-like auricle lobes at the head corners' — ABSENT. The head-bulb edge at 6x is one continuous convex curve; there is not even a bump where the auricles belong.

Zero of three must-reads read. The organism on screen is an annelid. FAIL is correct.

FIX DIRECTION: this needs a different silhouette generator, not a retint. Flat ribbon body with a parallel-sided outline and a soft rounded tail, matte unshaded top surface with NO annular rings and no specular rib; head widened into a triangular arrowhead with two pointed auricle lobes at the rear corners; two small matte black crescent eyespots set close together and angled inward (cross-eyed) on the dorsal surface, not one glossy sphere on the cheek. Keep aspect ~4 but read it as a flat gliding ribbon, not a coiled tube.

rows.readsAs: A white sea anemone

The identity must-read — the BLOOD-RED feathery plume — is absent; the plume is the same bone-white as the tube, so there is no red anywhere in the image. The tube is also a short wide cone rather than a tall white chitin tube, and there is no cluster: one column stands alone.

FAIL upheld, and the judge's core reading is literally correct — I could not refute any of it. What I saw at full size, then at 4x/8x crops of the crown, rim and base, then under a gamma-0.32 lift to hunt for anything faint: a single squat vase-shaped cone with a bright elliptical rim, from which ~14-16 smooth, cylindrical, blunt-tipped, UNBRANCHED tentacles splay up and outward, several curling over at the tips. The column flares slightly at the rim and again at a flat pedal-disc bottom that sits on a cast-shadow ellipse. This is an anemone, unambiguously.

CORROBORATION THE JUDGE DID NOT CITE, which makes the 'Sea Anemone chassis' phrasing exact rather than rhetorical: Sea_Anemone.png in the same folder is the SAME artwork — same silhouette, same pose, same tentacle count and splay, same rim, same flared cone, same shadow — only recoloured. Sea_Anemone measures 86.61% strongly-red pixels; Giant_Tube_Worm measures 0.00%. The asset is the anemone chassis with the hue removed. The red the tube worm needs is sitting on the anemone.

MUST-READ 1 — 'tall white chitin tube standing upright in a cluster': FAILS on both counts. Silhouette bbox is 180 x 165 px, aspect w/h = 1.09, against packet aspect 0.25 (should be ~4x taller than wide) — off by ~4.4x. The tube column proper is only ~110 px tall by 55-75 px wide, and it is a flared cone (widest at rim and at base, narrowest mid-column), not a straight chitin cylinder. Horizontal scanlines through every row of the column return exactly ONE filled run, and the gamma lift revealed no second tube anywhere in the frame — so 'standing alone' is confirmed; there is no cluster, not even a faint background one. (The only other mark is one dim pale lump low on the column's left, which reads as painterly mottling, not a neighbouring tube.)

MUST-READ 2 — 'blood-red feathery plume protruding from the tube top': ABSENT, and absent in FORM as well as colour, which the judge understated. Colour: zero pixels in the entire image satisfy r>g+30 and r>b+30; mean foreground is 167,167,162 (neutral grey-white); only 3.5% of pixels are even mildly warm. Form: not one tentacle is pinnate, branched, barbed or filamentous — they are smooth tapering fingers. Even recoloured red this crown would still not read as a feathery branchial plume.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM (a): 'the plume is the same bone-white as the tube' is very slightly imprecise. The crown is a warm cream/ivory (dominant buckets 216,216,192 and 216,192,192) against a cooler grey-green tube (dominant 216,216,216 / 192,192,192 / 144,144,144). There IS a faint warm/cool separation between crown and tube — it is just nowhere near red, and far too subtle to register at thumbnail size. The judge's conclusion stands; the fix must add saturated red, not merely raise contrast between the two parts.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM (b): 'rimmed mouth' is the one piece I would restate. There is no painted mouth aperture. At 8x the rim is a bright specular ellipse and the disc inside it is the SAME pale value as the tube; the two dark slots the judge read as a mouth are background showing through the gaps BETWEEN tentacle bases, not a drawn opening. It still fails must-read 3 ('no mouth, gut or eyes at all') because the rim-plus-dark-slots reads as an open oral disc at a glance — but a fix that paints out a 'mouth' will find nothing there to paint out; what has to go is the flared anemone oral-disc rim itself.

WHAT THE FIX NEEDS: not a recolour of this chassis. It needs a new form — a tall narrow near-parallel-sided chitin tube (aspect ~0.25) with 2-3 shorter companion tubes behind it to make the cluster, capped by a compact BLOOD-RED plume of fine branched/pinnate filaments emerging from the tube mouth, with the tube lip drawn as a thin chitin edge rather than a flared oral disc.

rows.readsAs: An earthworm in olive-green

FAIL upheld, and the chassis charge is confirmed by direct comparison — but one part of the stated cause is wrong and must not be fixed as written.

CHASSIS (confirmed, decisive). I rendered Leech.png, Earthworm.png and Flatworm.png cropped to the identical window and stacked them. They are ONE worm body in three hues. Same lazy horizontal S-curve (head low at left, dip, hump right-of-centre, descend to a tail at far right), same ~22 coarse overlapping annular rings, same bulbous ovoid head cap at the left, same soft ellipse ground shadow, same footprint: subject bounding boxes are Leech [117,180 -> 326,254], Earthworm [114,176 -> 326,260], Flatworm [111,172 -> 331,258] — agreeing within ~5px on all four edges in a 440px frame. The ONLY per-species differentiation across the three is hue (olive / pink / grey) plus the presence of a small black eye dot on Earthworm and Flatworm, which Leech omits. It reads as 'earthworm, olive', not as a leech.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM — the head end is NOT a plain rounded stub. Brightened 16x, the anterior bulb carries a deliberately drawn dark circular patch on its front-left face with a HARD, crisp arc boundary — unlike the smooth gradient shading everywhere else on the bulb, so it is an authored shape, not a terminator artifact. It sits where the eye dot sits on the two siblings but is much larger and moved onto the leading face. Charitably it is an intended oral sucker / mouth. It still does not deliver the must-read: it is a flat unrimmed brown ellipse with no cup, no raised rim, no radial structure, and it is narrower than the head bulb it sits on — it reads as a shaded end cap or a mouth blob at thumbnail size. Do not 'add a sucker' at the head from scratch; the fix is to give the EXISTING disc a rim/cupped flange and flare it wider than the trunk.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS RIGHT.
- Posterior sucker: genuinely absent. Brightened 16x, the tail is just the terminal ring segments stacking and closing in a rounded cap, slightly NARROWER than the trunk. No disc, no flange, no widening. This is the worse miss of the two — on a real leech the posterior sucker is the LARGER and more diagnostic of the pair, and here the more prominent end is the head.
- Round tube, not a flattened ribbon: correct. Cross-section is fully circular, shaded as a cylinder, with no dorso-ventral flattening and no lateral body margins anywhere along the length.
- No inchworm arch: correct. The two ends sit ~209px apart, i.e. the full span of the body, in a flat sinusoid. The looping crawl needs the ends brought close together with the mid-body raised in a tall loop; nothing of the sort is present.

ADDITIONAL DEFECTS THE CLAIM MISSED.
- Segmentation is the wrong grain: ~22 heavy coarse rings inherited from the earthworm chassis, where the must-read asks for FINE ring segments (a leech has ~100 shallow annuli). The rings here are deep-cut and read as caterpillar/millipede banding.
- Silhouette proportion: the rendered subject bounds are 209 x 74 (~2.8:1) against a requested aspect of 6 — too short and thick even allowing for the curved posture.

SATISFIED: no limbs; eyes hidden (correct, and the one place this asset diverges from its siblings).

Two of the three must-reads are absent or unreadable and the third (segmentation) is present at the wrong grain, on a body shared verbatim with two other species in the same batch. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: A cream starfish

The wedges between arms are pure background navy running almost all the way to the hub (verified at 7x on the centre crop and confirmed in the stretch, where interarm space clips to black). The packet's own note says it "only reads face-on" and this IS drawn face-on, so the pose is not an excuse - the face-on view is exactly where the disc and petals were supposed to appear and neither is there. That is not merely 'scaled' — it is aggressively, glossily scaled, the single loudest read in the image. Snailfish are naked, gelatinous and semi-transparent; nothing here suggests that. The head end additionally carries a full curved OPERCULUM/gill-cover arc running from the dorsal edge down past the pectoral to the ventral edge (a detail the first judge did not mention) plus a small white-sclera/black-pupil eye and a curved smiling mouth line — three more bony-fish signals a snailfish should not show.

MUST-READ 2, 'sucker disc on the belly' — ABSENT, judge correct. I zoomed the entire ventral surface at 9x. The belly is one unbroken, smooth, scaled convex curve from snout to tail; there is no disc, no ring, no ventral cup, no pelvic structure, not even a tonal patch that could be read as one. There is nothing small or off-frame being missed — the feature simply was not drawn. This is the identity-defining feature of the family (the pelvic fins fused into an adhesive disc) and its absence alone forecloses PASS or POLISH.

MUST-READ 3, 'fins merging into a tapering pointed tail' — ABSENT, judge right about the outcome but WRONG about the mechanism. There is a separate dark mauve-brown fan tail with radiating ray lines, correct — but it is NOT 'on a narrow peduncle'. There is no peduncle at all. The fan is a squared-off, nearly rounded-rectangular plate whose straight vertical proximal edge is butt-jointed / overlapped flat against the full-height rounded left end of the ovate body, with a hard tone and colour discontinuity at the seam and a small dark notch above and below. So the defect to fix is 'body ends bluntly and a squared fin plate is stuck on the end', not 'body narrows to a stalk then a fan'. The tail also does not taper — its distal edge is as tall as its proximal edge (~55% of body depth). No dorsal fin and no anal fin are drawn at all, so there is nothing that could merge; the only other fin is a tiny dark pectoral triangle mid-flank, drawn as a small folded fan.

'READS AS A PINK PERCH' — fair. I would say pink crucian carp or sunfish (no dorsal spines are present), but the judge's genus-level point holds: a viewer sees a generic glossy scaled bony fish. Zero of the three must-reads survive, the aspect ratio is off by a third, and the one non-negotiable family marker (belly sucker disc) is entirely missing. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a chinchilla or a fat guinea pig

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Facing right. A near-spherical trunk with a second, smaller sphere fused to its front as the head, no neck. Two upright ears. One eye. Four straight whisker strands. Two ivory rectangular incisors. Two dark stub limbs. One thick smooth hooked tail arcing up over the back to the left. Colour is a flat olive-tan with a vertical light-to-dark gradient and thin white contour strokes along the topline, around the head, and around a large circular haunch disc on the flank. The white strokes read as decal seams, not as fur.

SNOUT — THE IDENTITY MUST-READ IS GENUINELY ABSENT (claim CORRECT). At 14x the front of the head is a single smooth convex arc running from forehead down to jaw. Nothing projects. The only muzzle cue is a ~5px grey wedge nose pad appliqued at the tip of that arc where the whiskers attach. Measured from the eye, the face carries roughly 12-14 px of forward extension on a ~65 px head ball, i.e. essentially none. A tree shrew's defining feature is a long, narrow, forward-projecting pointed rostrum, longer and finer than a squirrel's; there is no rostrum here at all.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM (the verdict stands, but three of its stated causes are imprecise):
1. "blunt flat face" is wrong in shape. The face is not flat — it is a rounded convex dome that tapers slightly forward to the nose pad. The defect is that the taper is a ball's own curvature rather than an added snout, not that the face is a flat plane. A fix that only 'unflattens' the face will not produce a snout.
2. "big rounded ears" is wrong. The ears are two TALL, NARROW, UPRIGHT TRIANGULAR ears with pointed tips and pink-tan inner surfaces, rising well clear of the skull like a rabbit's or a chinchilla's. They are the single loudest wrong-organism signal in the drawing and they push the read toward lagomorph/chinchilla, not away from it. A real tree shrew has small, low, thin, rounded, close-set ears. Any fix must SHRINK and ROUND these ears, which is the opposite of what "big rounded ears" would suggest to someone reading only the claim.
3. "feet are invisible stubs" overstates invisibility. Two dark-brown limbs ARE plainly visible against the navy background below the belly: a hind limb at roughly x=180-215 ending in a rounded paddle/flipper foot pointing forward, and a much smaller forelimb peg at roughly x=245 that ends in nothing at all. The real defects are (a) zero digits, zero toe separation, zero claws on either; (b) only one limb per pair reads — the far side pair is entirely absent; (c) the forelimb is set too far back under the mid-belly and is half the size of the hind, so the animal has no shoulder; (d) both limbs are so dark they nearly merge with the ground shadow ellipse.

CLAIMS I CONFIRMED AS STATED. The buck teeth are real and are exactly as described: two ivory rectangular slabs with a vertical split, hanging below and in front of the nose. This is a rodent incisor appliqué; tree shrews are not rodents and have no such visible incisors, so this feature actively asserts the wrong clade. The body is a sphere: I measured the full silhouette bounding box at 217 x 150 px (aspect 1.45 including the tail), and the trunk alone at roughly 110 x 105 px — a circle — against the required 2.2 slim low form. Head fraction measures ~0.37 of body length against the specified 0.28, so the head is oversized as well. The tail is a smooth-edged thick club with a soft rounded tip and a lighter interior lozenge highlight; its outline has no fur strands, no serration, no silhouette break-up whatsoever. One partial credit the claim did not give it: the tail's arc length (~165 px) is roughly body-length, so "as long as the body" is approximately met — it is only the "bushy" half of that must-read that fails.

NET READ. Ball body + ball head + tall pointed ears + buck incisors + smooth clubbed tail + toeless stubs = a generic chunky rodent. Chinchilla is the closest single match, as the original judge said; a fat cartoon squirrel is equally close. Guinea pig is the weakest of their guesses since guinea pigs are tailless. Nothing in the silhouette would let a viewer arrive at tree shrew. FAIL is correct.

FIX PRIORITY. (1) Build an actual rostrum: a narrow tapering cone projecting forward from the skull, roughly 35-40% of head length, with the nose pad at its tip and the eye set back behind it. (2) Delete the rodent incisors entirely. (3) Shrink the ears to small low rounded flaps set close to the skull. (4) Stretch the trunk to the 2.2 aspect and drop the belly line so the body is long and low, not spherical. (5) Give four limbs with separated digits and visible claws, forelimb under the shoulder. (6) Break the tail outline with fur strands along its whole length.

The ring is of near-uniform slender width (~8px against a ~90px skull), it never tapers, it sits ON TOP of the skull as a hoop rather than sweeping down and around BESIDE the head, and it does not spiral (a spiral advances outward and downward across turns; this is a single flat closed loop that returns to its own start). 'Massive spiralling horns curling beside the head' therefore fails, but it fails as 'wrong horn architecture', not as 'no horn'.

THE HUE-SWAP IS PROVEN, AND IT IS TOTAL. Critically, the Tahr's horn is ALSO the ribbed ring, same radius, same anchor point, same annuli. My initial hope that the ribbing differentiated the sheep was wrong. The two assets differ only in hue (Tahr warm brown, Sheep cream) and nothing else. Same body, same leg placement, same hoof, same shadow ellipse. This is one chassis painted twice.

COAT — THE JUDGE DESCRIBED THIS INCORRECTLY. It is NOT 'a fluffy cream fleece'. There are no curls, no crimp, no woolly clumping anywhere. What is drawn is the TAHR'S LONG SHAGGY-HAIR OVERLAY, recolored cream and extended across the whole trunk: long diagonal straggling strands over the flank, a fringe of long hanging locks dangling clear of the belly line, and a spiky bristle fringe along the dorsal and rump silhouette. It still fails the must-read 'short coarse hair coat' — because it is LONG, not because it is woolly — and it fails for the specific reason that it is the neighboring species' shoulder-mane treatment applied body-wide. The fix is to strip/shorten the long-strand overlay to a short close-lying coarse pelt; there is no fleece to remove.

BODY — JUDGE CORRECT. Shallow barrel, flat topline, no chest depth, no shoulder mass, no brisket, on four straight thin near-columnar legs with a wide open gap under the belly. 'Muscular blocky body on sturdy legs' fails.

ADDITIONAL DEFECTS THE JUDGE DID NOT REPORT. (1) There is NO TAIL AT ALL — the rump crop (x90 y150) shows a bare rounded haunch and nothing behind it; wild sheep carry a short stubby tail. (2) The haunch shows a hard-edged flat quadrilateral plate with a visible straight seam cutting across the hip — raw chassis polygon showing through the paint, a construction artifact, also present on the Tahr. (3) CREDIT WHERE DUE: the feet are genuinely correct and well drawn — each foot terminates in two distinct dark cloven toes with a pale coronet above, readable at 4x. That detail is real and should be preserved through any rebuild.

NET: all three must-reads fail, the organism reads as a pale goat/domestic-sheep and is pixel-for-pixel the Tahr chassis in a different hue. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a cabbage or a pale hosta

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at 1x, then at 2x and at 2.5-3x crops of the crown, the left leaf mass, the right leaf mass and the bottom-centre junction. The FAIL stands, but the stated cause is only two-thirds right and one must-read the judge never mentioned is actually PRESENT and correct - do not let a fix destroy it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Six large orbicular blades, three per side, all radiating from a SINGLE point at the bottom-centre of the plant (approx x=220, y=368 in 440px space). Leaf mass spans x=65-378, y=155-370, so it is genuinely wider than tall - the 'low mound' half of 'tight low alpine cushion' is met in outline, but it reads as one cabbage/hosta head, not a cushion of many small leaves. Above it, a bare olive stem (sampled #617D66 mid, #415C34 low) rises to a beaded, lobed spike of brick-coral segments (sampled #B85040 throughout, roughly y=60-100, ~40px tall) held well clear of the foliage.

CORRECTION 1 - THE SEED SPIKE IS PRESENT AND HITS ITS MUST-READ. The claim omits it entirely. Must-read 2, 'red-pink winged seed spike on bare stem', is drawn: a knobbly two-column beaded spike on a leafless stalk, clearly above the leaves, clearly red. It is on the brick/tomato side of the target crimson-pink and it is small (spike head is ~9% of image height against a leaf mass ~50%), but it is legible and correct in kind. Any fix must keep it and should only warm it toward pink and enlarge it slightly.

CORRECTION 2 - THE COLOUR CALL IS RIGHT BUT UNDERSPECIFIED. Sampled blade pixels: #69837A, #8BAC9D, #769388, #6E897F, #8CAC9D, #6B857C, #566C66, #546964, #627B73. Every one has B > R, i.e. a COOL sea-green/sage, saturation ~18-20%. It is not 'grey-white' (no sample is near-neutral); it is a desaturated cold sage with a heavy white specular sheen laid over each blade, which is what pushes it to read as pale cabbage. Target is a warm bright fresh green (R>B) at high saturation with red-flushed margins and stalks - there is zero red anywhere on the foliage or in the leaf edges. So the fix is hue rotation warm + saturation up + a red margin/stalk flush, not just 'brighten'.

CORRECTION 3 - 'NO VISIBLE LEAF STALKS' IS CORRECT AND IS THE PRIMARY DEFECT. Confirmed at 3x on the bottom-centre crop: the blades meet in a hard V at one point with no petiole segment at all between origin and blade. The reference wants reniform blades held out on LONG stalks in a low basal rosette, so the rosette architecture is entirely missing - you should see a ring of separated small blades each on its own visible stalk, with dark background between them, not a continuous fused wall of leaf.

CORRECTION 4 - 'PLAIN ROUND WITH NO BASAL NOTCH' IS CORRECT, but two details the judge missed matter for the fix. (a) The outer margins ARE faintly crenate - small scallop bumps are visible along the upper-left and upper-right silhouette - so the crenate edge of a sorrel leaf is already half there and only needs deepening. (b) The venation is actively fighting the reniform read and the judge did not name it: every blade carries a STRAIGHT MIDRIB from the origin point out to the tip with herringbone side veins branching off it - pinnate venation, which is the signature of a plain ovate/lance leaf. Oxyria's reniform blade is PALMATELY veined, with 5-7 primary ribs fanning out from the base sinus and no dominant midrib. The frontmost right-hand leaf is the worst offender; its herringbone is the clearest structure in the whole image and it reads unmistakably as a generic ovate leaf. Fix the vein model along with the outline or the kidney shape will still not read.

CORRECTION 5 - minor, unmentioned. The 'bare' seed stem is painted as a continuous 2px hairline running from the spike all the way DOWN over the front of the leaf mass to the bottom V. It should emerge from the rosette centre and be occluded by, not overlaid on, the nearer blades.

SCORE: must-read 1 (kidney-shaped basal leaves) ABSENT - blades are orbicular, base is a point not a sinus, venation pinnate, no petioles. Must-read 2 (red-pink spike on bare stem) PRESENT. The packet note explicitly guards the leaf shape ('leaves are round-kidney, never long and lance-shaped') and while these are not lance-shaped, they are not kidney either. rows.readsAs: a bundle of dead winter twigs
rows.defect: The huge pendulous trumpet flowers ARE the identity and they are not present. rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are factually wrong and would send the fix in the wrong direction. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS (440x440; plant bbox x133-308, y85-341, so 175w x 256h => aspect 0.68 against the packet's 0.9): a broom/fan of six straight, almost unbranched rods rising from a single tapered conical trunk at the base, every rod densely lined with small opposite lance-shaped leaves, and at the six stem tips small white blobs. THE FLOWERS: I thresholded near-white (r>200,g>195,b>180) and connected-component labelled them. There are TWENTY discrete white blobs, not six, arranged as six or seven clusters of 2-3 pips each, one cluster per stem tip. Every single blob measures 5x8 or 4x7 pixels; total white area is 620 px, i.e. 0.3% of the canvas. At 5x upscale each one is a plain vertical rounded capsule -- a flat-ish top, a rounded bottom, no flare at either end, no bell mouth, no corolla lobes, no recurved rim, no tube, no pedicel. So the judge is right that the huge pendulous trumpets are absent, but WRONG to call this 'the Datura error.' Datura's error mode is an upward-FACING FLARED TRUMPET; nothing here is a trumpet in any orientation. These are featureless buds/pips -- they read closest to lily-of-the-valley or unopened berry buds. The fix is therefore NOT 'flip the trumpets to hang down'; it is 'draw a trumpet at all': long tubular corollas roughly 5-8x current linear size, attached to the UNDERSIDE of the upper branches, hanging on a visible pedicel, with a clearly flared, recurved, five-pointed mouth at the lower end. Until a flare exists there is nothing to flip. THE FOLIAGE: the judge's 'sparse dead-tan brushwood' is half wrong. It is not sparse -- I counted 10,585 foliage pixels and the leaves crowd every stem from base to tip; density is fine. The colour claim IS correct and is a second hard miss: mean foliage RGB is 95,82,63, and 10,388 of 10,585 foliage pixels have R>=G (only 197 are green-dominant); the modal buckets are 96,80,64 / 112,96,64 / 112,96,80 -- warm khaki-brown. The packet demands 'mid green, softly downy,' so leafColour fails outright. Shape also fails the must-read: the packet wants 'large soft oval leaves with slightly wavy edges' and 'coarse soft foliage'; what is drawn is small, narrow, hard-edged lanceolate leaves with a stiff pale midrib, so tightly opposite-paired that overlapping pairs read as chevrons/arrowheads rather than leaves. Stems are 107,74,46 mid-brown, clean and rod-straight with no taper or side branching. WHY IT STILL FAILS: of the two must-reads, the first ('big trumpets hanging straight down with flared recurved tips') is 100% absent -- the defining organ of the species, the thing it is named for, is not depicted -- and the second ('coarse soft foliage on a small multi-stemmed tree') is only half met: multi-stemmed yes, but the stems form a bundled broom with no crown, and the foliage is fine and dry, not coarse and soft. Stripped of the name, this asset reads as a bundle of pussy-willow or a dried-flower broom, not as Brugmansia.

rows.readsAs: a fern with a crumb of white fluff on top
rows.defect: Angelica is defined by architecture this image has none of: the stem is a thin plain green rod, not a thick, hollow, ridged, purple-flushed column, and there is no inflated sheath where any leaf stalk meets it. The huge domed globe umbel is rendered as a single white crescent about 25px across sitting on the stem tip — smaller than one leaflet, so the plant's biggest feature is its smallest mark. The twice-divided leaf of broad toothed leaflets is replaced by the generic fine pinnate ladder shared with Alfalfa and Anise.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at native 440x440 and again at 3x/5x zoom crops, plus a pixel census. FAIL stands: two of the three must-reads are absent and the third is present only as a token. CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM FIRST, because two parts of it are wrong and would misdirect the fix.

(1) The judge called the flower head 'a single white crescent ~25px wide' with nothing under it. That undersells what is actually drawn. Zooming the tip (source rect x180-270, y70-160 at 5x) shows a real umbel ARMATURE: a fan of ~14 dark-green radiating rays converging on the stem apex, with a cream cap sitting on top of them. So the pedicel/ray scaffold exists and is correctly built; the artist did not simply stamp a crescent. Measured extents: cap occupies y82-96 (15px tall) and x206-237 (32px wide, of which the opaque cream core rgb(232,236,216) runs x208-236 = 29px). It is not a crescent in the sense of a thin arc either - it is a solid opaque half-dome with a flat underside, which is exactly why it reads as a MUSHROOM CAP or a lampshade rather than a flower head. There is zero floret granulation, no dotted/stippled texture, no sub-umbellet clustering, and no sphericity - the top surface is a smooth uniform fill, so nothing signals 'a globe of hundreds of tiny greenish-white flowers'.

(2) 'Smaller than one leaflet' is FALSE and should not be written into the fix ticket. Individual leaflets measure roughly 13x7px; the cap is 29x15px, about four times a leaflet's area. The correct statement of the size defect is relational: the plant's foliage spans x127-311 (185px wide) over a 263px-tall body, and the umbel is 29px = 16% of the foliage width, while each single pinnate tier reaches 70-90px out from the stem on each side. So one leaf TIER dwarfs the umbel three-fold. On real Angelica the terminal umbel is the widest single element of the plant, frequently 20-25cm across and wider than the leaf spread. It needs to be roughly 4-6x its current diameter, spherical (domed above AND bulging below the ray attachment), and broken into visible sub-umbellets of tiny florets.

WHAT I CONFIRMED AGAINST THE JUDGE. mustRead 'thick hollow ridged stems, often purple' - ABSENT on all three counts. Sampling the axis at y=100,140,180,220,260,300,330,340 gives a constant stem width of 4-5px that never tapers or thickens across the entire 260px height, flat-filled at rgb(46,83,26) mid-green. Ridging: none - there is a faint one-pixel darker edge on the left side at some rows (a hint of cylinder shading, so the judge's 'plain' is slightly harsh) but no longitudinal ribs, flutes, or hollow-tube read. Purple: a full-image hue census over all 14,842 non-background pixels returned ZERO pixels where r>g and b>g. There is not one purple pixel anywhere in the asset, despite the packet's leafColour line calling for purple-tinged stems. Angelica's stem is its signature - a fat, bamboo-thick, glaucous purple-flushed hollow tube; here it is a 5px twig.

mustRead 'inflated sheath where each leaf stalk meets the stem' - ABSENT. At 3x zoom over the mid-body (x130-320, y150-270) each leaf rachis meets the stem as a bare 1-2px diagonal line with no swelling, no bract, no clasping boat-shaped collar at any of the ~13 junctions. Nothing at any node.

ORGANISM READ. The judge is right that it reads as a fern, and here is the mechanism so the fix targets it. The leaves are drawn as ~13 short once-pinnate ranks stacked closely up both sides of the stem, each rank carrying two rows of small narrow untoothed oval pinnules, forming two mirrored vertical columns that hug the axis. That is frond geometry - Dryopteris/Athyrium silhouette, or a young conifer. Angelica needs the opposite construction: a small number (3-4) of very large TWICE-DIVIDED leaves carried out on long stalks from a few widely spaced nodes, each division ending in BROAD, ovate, coarsely TOOTHED leaflets several times the width of what is drawn. The packet's leaf line says 'very large twice-divided leaves of broad toothed leaflets'; the asset delivers small narrow smooth-edged pinnules and no second order of division.

Aspect is fine and is not part of the defect - bbox 185x263 gives 0.70 against the requested 0.6, close enough. The base is a plain dark ground-shadow ellipse with the stem entering it, no basal rosette, which is a minor miss but not a must-read.

Band: FAIL. Fix priority - (a) thicken the stem 3-4x, flute it, and flush it purple; (b) enlarge the terminal umbel 4-6x into a true globe of sub-umbellets and keep the existing ray fan, which is the one correct piece; (c) add inflated clasping sheaths at each node; (d) rebuild the foliage as a few large twice-divided leaves of broad toothed leaflets instead of a fern frond.

rows.readsAs: a fern — and specifically, the same fern as Angelica
rows.defect: This is Angelica's picture with slightly finer, yellower leaflets: same straight central stem, same rectangular pinnate ladder, same white crescent speck at the tip, same height and shadow. The must-read that IS anise — two clearly different leaf shapes on one plant, rounded toothed leaves below and fine feathery threads above — is absent, every leaflet is identical top to bottom. rows.verifyWhy: Upheld, but with three corrections to the stated causes. WHAT I SAW (440x440, then 4x crops of the top half y=80-190 and bottom half y=220-330, an 8x crop of the flower head, and an 8x crop of the bare stem): a single perfectly straight vertical rachis running floor to head, carrying about eleven evenly spaced tiers of paired pinnate fronds. Every frond is the same length, so the silhouette is a hard-edged RECTANGLE roughly 90px wide by 190px tall, not a slender herb - it reads as a conifer or fern column. MUST-READ 1 (two clearly different leaf shapes on one plant, round below and feathery above) IS GENUINELY ABSENT, and this is the verdict. At 4x the lowest tier and the topmost tier are the same object: a straight side-rachis bearing ~14 small oval leaflets in two opposed rows. There is no rounded toothed leaf on a long stalk anywhere on the plant, and no thinning toward fine threadlike segments at the top; if anything the topmost fronds are slightly SHORTER, which is the opposite of nothing but is not a shape change. The identity of Anise is the dimorphic foliage and it is not drawn. MUST-READ 2 (small loose white umbrella flower heads) is only half-present: there is exactly ONE terminal head, and the judge is wrong to call it a bare 'white crescent speck' - at 8x it is a visible fan of ~20 radiating dark-green umbel rays springing from the stem tip, capped by an opaque solid white crescent arc. The ray fan is a real umbel scaffold, so the geometry is not nothing; the failure is that the white is a single solid unbroken cap with no floret texture and no gaps, so it reads as a parasol mushroom cap rather than a loose lace of tiny white flowers, and there is one head where the packet asks for plural loose heads. MUST-READ 3 (slender ribbed stems) is half-present: the stem is slender and tapers slightly, but at 8x it is a smooth flat two-tone green cylinder (lit left edge, darker right) with zero ribbing, grooving or fluting. CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM: (a) 'same stem' is not exact - Angelica's rachis carries horizontal node bands at each leaf tier, Anise's is an unbanded smooth taper; neither is ribbed. (b) 'same white crescent speck' understates it - both heads are crescent-on-ray-fan, identical in construction, but the ray fan exists and should be kept in the fix. (c) 'every leaflet is identical top to bottom' is true WITHIN Anise, and the near-clone charge against Angelica is substantially right, but the two files are not pixel twins: Anise's fronds are denser with more and smaller leaflets and are a distinctly BRIGHT YELLOW-GREEN, while Angelica's are sparser, larger and mid/dark green. So leafColour ('bright yellow-green') is the one packet line the asset actually hits. What shipped is a recolour plus a leaflet-density tweak of one shared umbellifer chassis, not a literal duplicate. FIX DIRECTION: the bottom three or four tiers must become single ROUND toothed blades on long visible petioles (one blade per stalk, scalloped rim), the top four or five tiers must dissolve into fine hair-thin thread segments with visible dark gaps, and only the middle should keep anything ladder-like; cut the rectangle silhouette so the plant narrows upward; break the white cap into separate floret clusters sitting on the ray tips; and add two or three vertical rib lines to the stem.

rows.readsAs: a berry bush — the blue fruit does land

rows.readsAs: a cabbage — and it is Alpine Sorrel's cabbage in a different hue
rows.defect: Silhouette, disc count, disc overlap order, the central notch, the vein rake and the orange bead spike are all identical to Alpine Sorrel; only the fill has been shifted from pale mint to olive. On its own terms it also misses everything: the clump of LONG-STALKED oblong, arrow-based basal leaves is drawn as six giant stalkless round discs, the stem is olive-green not reddish, and the dense rose-pink papery seed spire is a thin orange bead column narrower than the stem it sits on.

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but two parts of the stated cause are wrong and the fix should be made against this description instead.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440). A single fused dome of ~7 overlapping round discs, symmetrical about a centre notch: four discs fanning back-to-front down the left lobe, three on the right with the frontmost carrying a midrib plus a pinnate side-vein rake. The discs are khaki-olive (leaf-body mean RGB 118,130,83) with a pale specular highlight top-left of each. One dark olive stem, ~4 px wide, runs from the notch straight up through the dome and emerges above it carrying a column of ~7 discrete round coral/brick beads (x 211-220, y 62-110). Leaf mass bbox x57-377, y62-377.

MUST-READS. (1) 'clump of long-stalked basal leaves' - ABSENT. There are zero petioles. The blades meet in a bare V notch directly at the ground (verified in a 2x crop of the base); there is no stalk, no clump, no stout rootstock. Nothing separates the blades into countable leaves - they read as one head. (2) 'reddish stems' - ABSENT, hard-verified: I scanned every pixel below y=130 for r>g+25 AND r>b+25 AND r>70 and got a count of exactly 0. The stem is uniformly olive-green over its whole length. (3) 'bright pink-red papery seed spire' - the only must-read that is present, and only weakly: it is 48 px tall and 9 px wide on a 440 px canvas, rendered as ~7 discrete round beads (a caterpillar/bead necklace) rather than a dense spire of overlapping papery discs, and its colour is brick-salmon (~182,79,64) rather than bright rose-pink.

Also missed and not named by the first judge: the spec leaf is 'long-stalked oblong to arrow-based' - these are round orbicular discs, i.e. Alpine Sorrel's reniform spec, not Arctic's; leafColour is spec'd 'fresh mid green' and is drawn khaki-olive; and aspect 0.7 (taller than wide) is violated - the mound is ~320 px wide by ~215 px tall, markedly wider than tall.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM. (a) 'Identical silhouette' is FALSE as stated. Pixel comparison against Alpine_Sorrel.png: silhouette IoU 0.873, symmetric difference 7,807 px, Arctic leaf area 54,325 px vs Alpine 60,422 px (Arctic ~10% smaller), right edge x377 vs x383, top y62 vs y60. It is the SAME generator re-rolled with slightly different disc radii, not a pixel copy. Disc count, overlap order, vein-rake placement, stem path and bead-column geometry ARE identical, so the 'one chassis, two hues' diagnosis stands - just not 'identical'. (b) 'The seed spire is thinner than the stem' is FALSE. The bead column measures 8-9 px across on every row sampled (y=70,80,90,100,108); the stem measures 4 px at y=125. The spire is roughly TWICE the stem width. The real spire defect is scale and texture, not width: it is far too short, it is a string of separate beads rather than a papery-disc spire, and it floats as an isolated stick above a cabbage head because there is no clump for it to rise out of. (c) 'Olive instead of mint' is CORRECT (Arctic 118,130,83 vs Alpine 124,154,142). (d) 'Reads as a cabbage' is CORRECT - it reads as a cabbage or hosta rosette head, not a sorrel clump.

BAND. Two of three must-reads are flatly absent and the third is present only as a token, so the organism does not read. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: an upright willow sapling or an olive shrub

The leaves are narrow grey-green lances rather than small glossy rounded ovals, and the catkins are pale cream rather than red-tinged, so they read as seed heads on a reed.

The reference row asks for aspect 2.8 and a 'prostrate mat creeping over the ground, only a few centimetres tall'. CORRECTIONS to the original claim. (1) It is NOT 'an upright vase of tan trunks'. Zooming the base (crop y250-360) shows a SINGLE fused tapering bole: the silhouette narrows monotonically to 13 px wide at ground level (row widths 47px@y270, 30@280, 23@290, 19@300, 17@310, 13@320), flares upward, and only splits into five or six upright stems at roughly 40% of the plant's height, with short incised gouges marking the split.
