The reference wants 'small rounded oval leaves, glossy above' and 'small glossy round leaves' in mustRead. Nothing in the render is round or oval; the leaf reads as weeping-willow/olive foliage. Must-read absent.

(3) Catkins: present and, on their own, the one must-read genuinely delivered. Six upright fuzzy bumpy cylindrical spikes stand at the stem tips, correctly rendered as beaded/hairy rather than smooth. The judge is right that they are cream rgb(216,200,152), with no red pixels anywhere in the image. But this is the mildest of the three faults and their description overstates it: the harvest line explicitly permits 'red or yellow', so cream/straw is a washed-out yellow, a near-miss on an allowed variant, not a contradiction. Only the mustRead's stricter 'red-tinged' is missed. Do not spend the fix budget here.

Band rationale: two of three must-reads (prostrate creeping mat; small glossy round leaves) are flatly absent, the explicit never-do note is violated, and the aspect is off by 4x. The catkins, correct in form, sit above a tree canopy instead of above a mat, so even the passing feature is staged wrong. FAIL upheld. The fix is a re-draw, not a tint: creeping horizontal stems radiating low across the ground plane, wider than tall, small round glossy leaves along them, catkins as short red-blushed uprights poking a little way above the mat.

rows.readsAs: a ghost-white agave with a sunflower sticker on a wire
rows.defect: Reuses African Ginger's stiff radial sword-blade fan, so the basal rosette of plain OVAL untoothed leaves is drawn as a spray of sharp pointed spikes, and the colour is a bleached cream-white instead of mid green — the plant does not read as living foliage. The 1-2 opposite stem leaves never appear. The flower is present but tiny and mechanical: a neat symmetric gear-toothed yellow disc, where the must-read is ragged ray petals that visibly droop.
rows.fix: Swap the spiky fan for a flat rosette of six soft mid-green oval leaves, add one opposite pair partway up the stem, and enlarge the head with long uneven drooping ray petals.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 8x nearest-neighbour crops of the flower head (src 180,50 80x80) and the rosette (src 60,170 320x190), and side-by-side against African_Ginger.png and Agave.png in the same folder.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Lower ~55% of the canvas is a symmetric fan rosette of about 11 blades springing from one point at ground level, arcing outward and up, tips reaching roughly canvas mid-height. Each blade is a broad-based pointed lanceolate blade with a drawn midrib and 6-10 pinnate lateral veins in translucent grey; the outermost pair on each side sweep nearly horizontal. Fill is bleached cream-white / bone (roughly #E6E9DC to #F2F3E9) with faint warm-grey shading, over a dark navy plate with a soft elliptical ground shadow. A single bare olive-green stem rises from the rosette centre, straight, unbranched, no leaves on it at all, terminating at ~y=95 in one small yellow flower head: a disc ~40px across with about 12 short blunt triangular ray teeth radiating stiffly and a distinct darker olive-brown central disc.

THE CHASSIS-REUSE CLAIM IS CORRECT IN SUBSTANCE. African Ginger, Agave and Arnica are unmistakably one generative rosette plus one bare central stalk carrying a terminal organ. African Ginger is the same fan in mid green with narrower spikes and a yellow bead spadix on the stalk; Agave is the same fan in pale grey-green; Arnica is the same fan bleached whiter than the actual Agave asset, with the yellow bead spike swapped for a yellow gear disc. So the identity of the plant below the flower is entirely borrowed.

CORRECTIONS TO THE STATED CAUSE. (a) The blades are not "sharp spikes" in the agave sense - they are broad-based leaf blades with full pinnate venation drawn in, aspect roughly 4:1, wider than either African Ginger's or Agave's. Because of that the thing reads less like an agave and more like a bleached white water-lily / lotus rosette or a giant white chrysanthemum leaf-fan. That does not rescue it: the must-read wants SMALL PLAIN OVAL leaves and these are large pointed lances, so the leaf shape is still wrong, just wrong in a different direction than stated. (b) The daisy is not merely "a gear-toothed disc" - it does have a properly differentiated darker central disc and ~12 rays, so it reads as a daisy head and the must-read "one yellow daisy head per stem" is genuinely satisfied. What is missing is exactly what the judge said next: the rays are short, stiff, blunt, evenly spaced and swept slightly UP, with zero raggedness and zero droop, and the head is small (~9% of canvas width) where arnica's head is conspicuously large relative to the plant.

WHY IT STILL FAILS. Two of three must-reads are not met and the failure is in the most legible property of the image. leafColour is specified as mid green, slightly hairy; the rendered foliage is cream-white and occupies ~55% of the canvas, so the dominant read of the asset is a white-foliaged rosette succulent, not a green herb. "Basal rosette of plain oval leaves" gets the arrangement right and the blade shape and colour wrong. "Ray petals slightly ragged and drooping" is absent outright. The packet's "plus 1-2 opposite pairs on the stem" is also absent - the stem is completely bare.

FIX TARGETS, in order: (1) recolour the foliage to mid green with a slight grey-hairy bloom, not bone-white; (2) replace the pointed lanceolate fan blades with short broad blunt-tipped ovals lying low and outward, 4-6 of them, so the rosette is squat rather than a tall fan; (3) enlarge the flower head and rebuild the rays as ~12-15 long narrow strap petals of uneven length with notched/tattered tips, angled downward below horizontal; (4) add one opposite pair of small oval leaves partway up the stem.

rows.readsAs: a cabbage — the same cabbage as both Sorrels, in green

Must-read 3 (whorls of three-petalled white flowers with a dark purple centre, spaced up a bare stem) fails on petal count, on centre colour, and on whorl count - there is exactly one bloom at the very tip of a thin dark-green stem that runs unbroken from the crown to the top. CONFIRMED as claimed: no waterline and no emergent stance. The plant floats on plain void with the leaf mound hanging below the crown. rows.readsAs: a fountain of pampas or fountain grass, or a spray of wheat
rows.defect: The culms arch outward and droop like a fountain grass instead of standing as tall straight hollow culms; the nodes are drawn as bare cross-ticks on naked stems with no leafy sprays anywhere; and the harvest itself — the fat brown-sheathed pointed shoot at the base of the clump — is completely absent, so the thing named on the card does not exist in the picture.

rows.verifyWhy:
I read the 440x440 PNG at 1x, then re-cropped the base (x140-310, y220-330) at 5x, the mid-clump at 4x, and the whole subject at 2x, and ran a pixel scan for ink bbox and hue histogram. The FAIL is correct on every point it makes, and the asset is worse than the claim states.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a low, wide, symmetrical fan of roughly 14 smooth strands radiating from ONE point at ground level, over a flat dark elliptical shadow. Every strand tapers continuously from base to a bare blunt tip. Two alternating tones are used (pale straw for the front strands, darker olive for the back ones) to fake depth. The only surface detail anywhere is a scatter of thin flat horizontal light-yellow bars laid across the strands.

CLAIM POINT 1 - ARCHING/DROOPING: CONFIRMED. At 2x the outermost strands on both sides sweep past horizontal and their last third hangs tip-down; the second rank curls over at roughly 45 degrees. Exactly one near-central strand is genuinely straight and vertical. The silhouette is a fountain/pampas grass or a firework burst, not a stand of canes. It also is not a 'clump' in the bamboo sense - real culms emerge as separate parallel verticals from a spreading rhizome mass, whereas here all 14 strands converge to a single sub-pixel point, which reads as a tussock/grass crown.

CLAIM POINT 2 - BARE CROSS-TICKS FOR NODES: CONFIRMED, with a precision correction. The bars are not merely 'bare', they are the wrong geometry: each is a flat horizontal light bar that overhangs the strand it crosses by 2-3x the strand's own width on BOTH sides, so it reads as a tick mark or a plus sign painted on top rather than as a swollen ringed node in the strand's own silhouette. The strand edge never bulges or steps at a bar - the outline passes straight through. Several bars in the upper centre also sit at spacings and angles that do not track their strand, so at a glance a few read as detached floating dashes. Additionally nothing in the drawing reads as HOLLOW or as a rigid cane: the strands taper the whole way like grass blades instead of holding near-constant diameter between joints, so the mustRead 'tall hollow jointed culms with clear ringed nodes' is only weakly gestured at, not delivered.

CLAIM POINT 3 - NO LEAFY SPRAYS: CONFIRMED, and total. There is not a single leaf blade anywhere in the image. At 4x the tips of every strand terminate bare and rounded with nothing attached. The mustRead 'leafy sprays only near the top' and the leaf spec 'narrow lance leaves in sprays on the upper branches only' have zero pixels.

CLAIM POINT 4 - THE HARVEST IS ABSENT: CONFIRMED, and this is the decisive failure. The 5x base crop shows the 14 strands funnelling to one point directly on the shadow ellipse with clear empty background either side. There is no cone, no fat pointed shoot, no sheath, no scale texture, nothing pushing up from the ground. The hue histogram over all lit pixels returns ONLY hues 45-105 (yellow through yellow-green); there is not one brown, red-brown or tan pixel in the whole 440x440 canvas. The named item - 'a fat pointed cone-shaped shoot pushing up from the ground, sheathed in brown hairy scales' - is entirely unrepresented, and the packet note is explicit that this ground-level cone, not the tall culm, IS the harvest. The species is named Bamboo SHOOTS and the shoots do not exist.

TWO FURTHER DEFECTS THE ORIGINAL JUDGE DID NOT REPORT (fix these too):
(a) ASPECT IS INVERTED. Reference aspect is 0.5, i.e. twice as tall as wide. Measured ink bounding box is x 47-392, y 118-310 = 345 wide by 192 tall, a w/h of 1.8 - about 3.6x too wide for spec. The subject also floats: it occupies only the middle vertical third of the canvas and its top is 118px down from the frame edge, so there is no sense of height at all. Bamboo's single strongest silhouette cue is verticality and this asset spends its budget on horizontal spread.
(b) COLOUR IS WRONG. leafColour is specified 'mid green'. Every lit pixel measures hue 45-75 (straw yellow to yellow-olive) with a handful up to 105; there is no green in the image. The palette reads as dried/dead ornamental grass, which compounds the fountain-grass misread rather than correcting it.

VERDICT: two of the three mustReads (leafy sprays near the top; brown-sheathed shoots at the base) have literally zero pixels, the third (jointed culms with ringed nodes) is served only by overhanging cross-ticks on tapering non-vertical grass blades, and the harvest item the species is named for is missing. The asset reads as ornamental fountain/pampas grass. FAIL upheld.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS: straighten the strands into near-parallel vertical canes of constant diameter with the aspect flipped to about 0.5 (tall, narrow, top of the clump near the frame top); build the node as a slight bulge and a ring band contained WITHIN the cane silhouette rather than a bar overhanging it; add narrow lance-leaf sprays branching off the upper third only; recolour the canes to mid green; and add two or three fat pointed brown-sheathed cones at ground level, overlapping the cane bases, big enough to read at thumbnail size, since those cones are the harvest.

rows.readsAs: a palm or a cycad
rows.defect: It is drawn with a woody brown FORKED trunk and a radial crown of stiff feathery pinnate fronds — exactly the two things the note forbids. There is no smooth green false trunk of rolled sheaths, no torn paddle blades, no hanging bunch and no purple-red terminal bud; the only fruit cue is a small yellow floret cluster sitting up in the crown instead of a bunch hanging below an arching stalk.

rows.verifyWhy: Verified at full size, at a 3x crop of the crown and a 4x crop of the trunk, plus a programmatic colour scan of all 193,600 pixels. The FAIL stands: all three must-reads are absent and the note's two explicit prohibitions ('no woody trunk, no branches') are both violated. WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: (1) TRUNK — a single flat mid-brown stem (sampled ~#604830 / RGB 96,72,48, the 4th most common colour in the image at ~1,100 sampled px) rising from a dark ground ellipse, bare and unmarked for its whole lower two-thirds, then splitting into a clean Y: two short upright branches with rounded cap ends diverging left and right just under the crown. Woody colour AND branching, both forbidden. There is no green false trunk, no overlapping rolled leaf-sheath edges, no sheath lines or vertical striation of any kind — the stem has zero internal detail. (2) CROWN — a radial semicircular fan of roughly 13 fronds all springing from one point at the top of the trunk. Each frond is a narrow solid green strip (~12px wide at source) with a darker midrib line, flanked on BOTH sides by fine needle-like teeth that extend well PAST the blade outline, with gaps wider than the teeth. That is pinnate leaflets — a palm/cycad frond — not a torn paddle. I looked specifically for the charitable reading (a banana paddle tears into ribs along the midrib, which could be drawn as slits) and it does not hold: a torn paddle keeps a broad ovate outline with slits cutting INWARD, whereas here the blade is narrow and the teeth project OUTWARD past the silhouette, and there are 13 narrow fronds in a fan rather than 5-8 huge blades spiralling up a false stem. Silhouette overall = bare pole + hemispherical feather fan = palm. (3) HARVEST — I corrected one part of the judge's description. What sits in the crown is not a 'small yellow floret'; it is a tight roughly spherical knot of about 14 rounded pale cream-yellow beads (~30x28px at source, ~244 yellow-ish pixels total), wedged into the CROTCH of the trunk fork, held UPRIGHT and tucked under the fronds. It reads as a coconut/date/palm drupe cluster or a berry knot, not as a hand of fingers. There is no arching stalk, nothing hangs downward anywhere in the image, and no elongated finger shapes. (4) BUD — I scanned every pixel for any purple/magenta/red-violet value (R>70, B>60, R>G+25, B>G+10): the count is exactly 0. There is no purple-red bud, not even a small or dark one. NET: an unbriefed viewer would name this a palm or a cycad. Zero of the three must-reads (green false trunk of rolled sheaths / torn paddle leaves / hanging bunch tipped with a purple-red bud) are present. FIX DIRECTION: replace the woody forked stem with a single unbranched smooth GREEN pseudostem showing overlapping sheath edges; replace the pinnate fan with 5-7 very large green paddle blades spiralling out from the pseudostem top, each blade broad and ovate with slits cutting inward to the midrib but the outline staying paddle-shaped; and add a single stalk arching out and DOWN from the crown carrying tiers of upcurved yellow-green fingers, terminating in a pendant purple-red teardrop bud below the bunch.

rows.readsAs: a saguaro or an organ-pipe column cactus with a sunflower stuck on it
rows.defect: The body is a tall narrow tapering spire roughly four times taller than wide — the fat squat accordion-ribbed BARREL that is the whole identity is absent. The crown is a point, not a flat top ringed with fruit; the harvest ring of scaly yellow barrel fruits is reduced to one tiny beige cluster tucked to one side; and the spines are sparse straight white sticks with none of the long flattened hooked central spines.
rows.fix: Squash the body to a wide squat ribbed barrel with a flat top, ring that flat crown with scaly yellow fruits, and give each rib crest stout red-brown hooked spines.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with three corrections to the stated causes.

MEASURED SILHOUETTE (440x440 canvas, green-body pixels): bbox x198-241, y112-342 = 44 px wide x 231 px tall. Width/height = 0.19 against the packet's aspect: 0.9. Sampled widths: row 120 = 8 px, row 160 = 24, row 200 = 34, row 240 = 40, row 300 = 44 (max, at the very base), row 335 = 43. So the body is a 5.3:1 straight-sided column that swells slightly from the base upward for the first third and then tapers continuously to a needle apex. It reads as a saguaro / organ-pipe spike. The judge is right: the fat squat barrel that IS this species is absent, and the aspect miss is ~4.7x, not a nudge.

CORRECTION 1 - THE RIBS EXIST, THE CHASSIS DOES NOT. The claim implies accordion ribbing is missing. It is not. Zoomed 4x on the trunk I count roughly 10-12 fine vertical flutes running the full length of the column, shaded in alternating light/dark green bands with a specular file down the centre-left. The rib renderer is working. What is wrong is only the body it is wrapped around. Do NOT re-derive ribbing; re-derive the form: a squat barrel roughly as wide as tall (aspect ~0.9-1.0), widest at mid-height or slightly above, with a rounded shoulder, and the ribs should read as 12-18 CHUNKY vertical accordion pleats with visible depth, not 10+ hairline flutes.

CORRECTION 2 - THE CROWN IS NOT JUST 'POINTED', IT IS CROWNED BY A LARGE DAISY THE JUDGE DID NOT MENTION. The single most dominant element in the top third is a ~35 px yellow composite flower with about 12 sharply pointed petals and a dark brown central disc, sitting directly on the apex like a sunflower on a stalk. This is the main reason the asset reads as 'generic flowering desert plant' rather than cactus, and it is a bigger defect than the fruit. Barrel cactus blooms are short cup-shaped funnels borne in a RING around a flat, woolly, slightly depressed apex - many small cups, never one big rayed daisy on a point. Fix: kill the composite daisy entirely, flatten the crown to a wide woolly disc, and ring it.

CORRECTION 3 - THE FRUIT IS NOT BEIGE. The claim calls it 'one tiny beige clump'. Zoomed 6x it is a cluster of about 6 distinctly golden/amber round berries, each ~7 px, each carrying a pale grey-white specular highlight - it reads as a small grape-like berry bunch, roughly 20x14 px overall. What IS right in the claim is the placement and the count: the cluster hangs to the RIGHT of the stem, below the flower, entirely off-axis, so there is no ring and no crown-crowding. The must-read wants a ring of scaly, barrel/torpedo-shaped yellow fruits crowded shoulder-to-shoulder AROUND the flat apex, each with visible overlapping scales - not smooth spheres, not a side bunch.

SPINES - CLAIM CORRECT, SHARPENED. About 20 straight cream/bone-white dashes, 8-14 px long, angled down-and-out, arranged in two loose vertical files on the left and right margins. Critically, most of them are drawn 2-8 px DETACHED from the silhouette edge, floating in the background void with no contact point, and several are doubled into little parallel pairs. There are no areoles, no attachment to any rib crest, no hook, no flattening, and no red-brown colour (packet: 'red-brown spines'). They must become dense clusters seated ON each rib crest, tinted red-brown, with a long flattened downward-hooked central spine per areole.

COLOUR - unstated by the judge but off: the body is a mid grass/olive green with a fairly saturated highlight, where the packet asks for grey-green.

Band FAIL stands: the organism is the wrong shape at the silhouette level, and two of three must-reads (fat ribbed barrel; flat-topped crown ringed with yellow fruit) fail outright while the third (long flattened hooked central spines) is present only as detached white sticks.

rows.readsAs: a sparse bare cane shrub or a dying willow whip with pom-pom seedheads
rows.defect: Drawn on the shared cane-vase chassis: mostly naked brown sticks, airy and see-through, when the must-read is a DENSE CONICAL EVERGREEN. The leaves are tiny thin mid-green slivers, not thick leathery very-dark glossy lances with a rippled margin, and there are so few of them the plant reads as leafless. The cream flowers are white pom-pom balls stuck on the cane tips rather than small clusters tucked into the leaf axils.
rows.fix: Fill the silhouette into a solid dark conical evergreen mass of large leathery wavy-edged near-black-green leaves, and move the cream flower clusters down into the leaf joints.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the full 440px render and at a 4x nearest-neighbour zoom of the crown (crop 130,70 180x180). What is actually drawn: a short tapered brown trunk stub at the ground (with the standard soft black shadow ellipse under it) from which FIVE bare mid-brown canes splay outward in a fan, widest at the TOP. Each cane carries roughly 4-6 narrow lance/sliver leaves attached directly to the cane with no petiole and no secondary twigs, and each cane terminates in a rosette of 5-6 pale spheres. Background is visible through the whole mass; there is no crown, no branch armature, no canopy fill.

Packet row (batch-002 item 4): form tree, aspect 0.7; leaf 'stiff leathery lance-shaped leaves with a wavy edge, alternate'; leafColour 'very dark glossy green'; harvest 'small shiny black-purple berries in the leaf axils'; mustRead 'thick leathery dark leaf with a rippled margin - dense conical evergreen shape - clusters of tiny cream flowers at the leaf joints'.

All three must-reads fail. (1) LEAF: the slivers are straight-edged, uniform-width, with a single pale midrib highlight - zero rippled/wavy margin, zero leathery thickness cue, no alternate-along-a-twig arrangement. Colour is a medium forest green, clearly lighter than 'very dark glossy'. (2) SILHOUETTE: not dense and not conical - it is an inverted fan/vase, narrow at the base and splayed wide at the apex, i.e. the inverse of a conical evergreen, and see-through at every point. (3) FLOWERS: five clusters exist but every one is strictly TERMINAL on a cane apex; there is not a single cluster at a leaf joint. They are also mis-coloured - cold grey-white spheres with dark outlines and specular dots, which read as pearls/berries rather than tiny cream florets, so they simultaneously miss the cream-flower must-read and the black-purple axillary berry harvest.

CORRECTIONS to the original claim, all of which stand alongside the upheld verdict:
- 'bare naked brown sticks' overstates it slightly: the canes are not literally bare, they do carry leaves along their mid-length. The real defect is density and distribution - the lower third of every cane and the top ~25% below each flower head ARE naked, and the leaf count is far too low, so the sparse read is correct even though 'bare' is not literally accurate.
- The claim treats this as a bespoke bad drawing. It is not: this is a SHARED BATCH CHASSIS. Beach_Plum.png in the same batch is pixel-for-pixel the same construction - trunk stub, five splayed canes, leaves directly on the canes, pom-pom cluster on each cane tip, same shadow ellipse - with broader oval leaves and purple spheres. Bay Laurel is that chassis with the leaf swapped to a narrower sliver and the sphere colour swapped to white. Fixing this asset in isolation will not fix the read; the shrub chassis is the defect.
- Not raised by the original judge but material: Bay Laurel is spec'd form 'tree' and is drawn on the multi-stem cane shrub chassis with no trunk of any height, no branching, no canopy. It does not honour its own form token, which is the upstream cause of the missing conical evergreen mass.
- Bay Laurel is NOT drawn on the Bamboo Shoots chassis (item 1 in this batch), which is a separate arching pale-yellow grass fountain - in case the sparse-cane description invited that inference.

As rendered this could be almost any generic flowering cane shrub; nothing in it says evergreen bay tree. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a generic houseplant vine floating in mid-air
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads survive: the runner rises in a diagonal S clear of the ground instead of creeping flat across sand; every leaf is a plain undivided round oval with no trace of the two-lobed goat's-foot notch; and the big pink-magenta funnel flowers are reduced to a few 6-pixel pink blobs pressed against the stem with no funnel, no flare and no dark star throat. The whole plant also floats with the shadow detached below it.
rows.fix: Lay the runner flat and horizontal along a ground line and draw two or three large open pink-magenta funnels in three-quarter view with a dark star throat, on leaves notched into two rounded lobes.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 8-14x magnification on crops of the 440x440 PNG. The FAIL stands: all three must-reads are absent, and the asset reads as a generic round-leaved climbing vine, not Ipomoea pes-caprae.

(1) RUNNER / HABIT - judge correct, and the numbers are worse than stated. Measured green-pixel bounding box is x128-311, y95-344: 184 wide by 250 tall, ratio 0.74. The packet demands aspect 2.8, i.e. a mat nearly three times wider than tall. The drawn plant is TALLER than wide - the opposite of the spec by a factor of ~3.8. The stem is a single steep S that climbs from a base near (215,340) up-left and back right to (205,95), sitting at roughly 60-70 degrees off horizontal for most of its length. A soft dark ground-shadow ellipse is painted directly under that single base point, which reinforces the 'one upright stem rooted at a spot' reading rather than a runner trailing across sand. There is no second runner, no horizontal ground line, no sand.

(2) LEAF NOTCH - judge correct but the shape description should be sharpened for the fix. The judge said 'plain round oval'; at 8x the seven leaves are near-perfect CIRCLES (roughly 1.05:1, not ovals), each with a smooth unbroken convex outline. I traced the free tip of every leaf: the outline opposite the petiole is a clean continuous arc on all seven - there is no cleft, no dimple, not even a flattened point, so no goat's-foot lobing anywhere in the asset. Additionally the venation is wrong in a way the judge did not flag: each leaf carries a pinnate feather midrib with paired side veins running off it, whereas pes-caprae reads as a thick blade with veins fanning from the base. (3) FUNNEL FLOWERS - judge correct on absence, wrong on the size and slightly wrong on the description. There are 11 pink marks totalling 961 pink pixels, so each is about 8x12px, not '6-pixel'. Each is a flat, single-tone pale-pink capsule/tombstone: rounded top, straight parallel sides, flat or softly rounded bottom, with a thin near-white rim. No funnel silhouette, no flared corolla mouth, no radial pleats, no darker star throat, no five-point outline - zero funnel geometry of any kind. Two further errors the judge missed: they are not scattered singly but grouped in three clusters of 3-4, and critically every one of them is painted ON TOP OF a leaf blade, overlapping the lamina, rather than borne on a pedicel from a leaf axil. At full size they therefore read as pink spots/scale insects stuck on the leaves, not as flowers. (4) EXTRA DEFECT NEITHER SIDE NAMED - there are at least five small dark-green COILED TENDRIL SPIRALS drawn along and beside the stem (clearest at approx (205,130), (185,105), (290,315) and beside the petiole of the lower-right leaf). Morning glory is a twiner and has no tendrils at all; this is the pea/cucurbit motif leaking in (the very next packet entry, Beach Pea, is the species that wants tendrils). They should be removed and replaced with the stem itself twining.

FIX DIRECTION: re-lay the vine as two or three long near-horizontal runners spanning a 2.8:1 canvas with a sand-line, delete the ground shadow ellipse and the tendril coils, cut a deep V notch into the distal edge of every leaf to make two rounded lobes and re-cut the veins to fan from the petiole, and rebuild the harvest as 3-4 large side-on funnels - a flared five-lobed mouth on a visible tapering tube, pink-magenta, with a dark purple star radiating from the throat - carried on pedicels off the runner, not stamped on the leaf faces.

Note the risk that these hollow lens outlines get misread as attempted pods - they are not; they are coils, and they must not be recoloured into pods, the pods have to be drawn new.

rows.readsAs: a berry bush with purple fruit — plum is a fair guess
rows.defect: Reads as roughly the right thing, but it is the shared cane-vase again: upright and taller than wide when the must-read is a dense low thicket WIDER than tall, and the plums sit as five isolated lollipop balls perched on the cane tips instead of tight clusters held against the twigs. rows.readsAs: an upright currant or redcurrant bush
rows.defect: The growth form is inverted: bearberry is a flat trailing groundcover mat at aspect 2.4, and this is the identical upright narrow cane vase used for Bay Laurel, Beach Plum and Bilberry, taller than wide. The reddish peeling stems are the same flat brown as every other card, the leaves are small pointed ovals rather than thick blunt spoon-shaped paddles, and the white-pink urn flowers are absent — the red berries alone carry the read.
rows.fix: Redraw it as a low horizontal mat of trailing reddish stems running sideways off the base, crowded with small blunt spoon-shaped glossy leaves and dull red berries at ground level.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, and the core of the claim is confirmed by measurement, but two details in it need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN (read at 1x, then cropped and upscaled 4x-12x on the crown, a berry cluster, and the base): a single fused mid-brown trunk block rising off a dark ground-shadow ellipse, splitting at about 55% height into five straight, evenly-splayed canes that fan into an upright vase. Each cane carries alternate leaves and terminates in a tight knob of 4-6 berries. Measured ink bounding box is x143-299, y116-311 = 157 wide x 196 tall, w/h = 0.80. The packet asks for aspect 2.4 (a flat mat far wider than tall). The asset is 1.25x TALLER than wide, i.e. off by roughly 3x in the wrong direction. Must-read 1, 'a flat trailing mat with reddish peeling stems', is absent in both halves: there is no mat, and the stems are a single flat mid-brown (roughly #8B5A34) with only a soft vertical gradient - no red cast, no peeling/shredding texture, no bark detail of any kind.

SHARED-CHASSIS CLAIM: CONFIRMED. I rendered Bilberry (bbox 146x237, w/h 0.62) and Bay_Laurel (147x225, w/h 0.65) side by side. All three are the same fused-trunk-into-five-splayed-canes vase, the same brown, the same ground-shadow ellipse, the same alternate leaf spacing, and the same terminal cluster knob; they differ ONLY in cluster colour (Bearberry red, Bilberry blue-black, Bay Laurel white-grey) and slight leaf width. Bearberry is however the SHORTEST and WIDEST of the three (0.80 vs 0.62/0.65), so 'identical' should be read as 'same chassis, same parameters family' rather than pixel-identical.

LEAF: claim is correct. The leaves are elongated pointed ellipses / lanceolate almonds with a tapered tip at both ends and a lighter central midrib streak, matte medium sage-green, roughly 3:1 long-to-wide, held on visible short petioles spaced out along the cane. The must-read wants small thick blunt-tipped paddle/spoon leaves, dark and glossy, CROWDED on trailing stems. Nothing about the drawn leaf reads as a spoon: no blunt rounded tip, no widening toward the apex, no crowding (there is bare cane between leaves), and the green is too pale and too matte for 'dark glossy evergreen'. Bay Laurel's leaves are narrower and Bearberry's are a touch broader, but they are the same shape primitive.

HARVEST - THIS IS WHERE THE CLAIM IS PARTLY WRONG. The judge says the urn flowers are absent and implies the berry read is fine by omission. Correct on the urn flowers: there is no white-pink pendant urn anywhere - I zoomed each of the five clusters and every element in them is a full sphere, not a bell or a nodding urn. But the BERRIES are also wrong, not just the flowers. What is drawn is five terminal pom-poms of 4-6 bright cherry-red spheres, each carrying a large pale grey-white specular blob covering nearly a third of the berry, perched as a knob on the naked apex of a tall cane. The brief asks for small DULL red MEALY berries scattered AMONG the leaves of a creeping mat. So: wrong saturation (bright glossy cherry, not dull matte mealy), wrong finish (the oversized white highlights are the single loudest feature in the image and are easy to mistake for white flowers at thumbnail size - they are highlights, not urns), and wrong placement (held clear above the foliage on bare stalks instead of nestled in among the leaves).

SCORE: zero of three must-reads read. The organism as drawn is a generic upright berry-bearing shrub sapling and is indistinguishable at a glance from Bilberry and Bay Laurel with the cluster recoloured. FIX DIRECTION: this needs the groundcover/mat chassis, not a tweak - low horizontal runners spreading sideways to roughly 2.4x the height with reddish-brown peeling stems, dense crowded small blunt spoon leaves in dark glossy green overlapping along those runners, dull matte red berries sitting down inside the leaf mass with no specular blob, and a few small nodding white-pink urn bells at the shoot tips.

rows.readsAs: a generic herb sprig or an ash seedling — nothing poisonous, nothing nightshade

Both identity features are missing: no dull purple-brown drooping bell flowers anywhere, and no glossy black cherry-sized berry cupped in a flared green five-point star — only three lilac pinheads at the apex, too small to resolve as anything.

Verified at full size and at 6x/12x magnification of the apex (pixel-decoded crops). The FAIL stands, but two parts of the original claim need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: one perfectly straight vertical stem running the full height of the canvas (bare spike above the apex cluster, bare stalk from y~300 down to the ground shadow), carrying SEVEN mirror-symmetric OPPOSITE leaf pairs. Row scans at y=150/200/250 show a leaf blade of near-identical width on both sides of the single central stem column at every node. Blade length decreases only marginally toward the apex; every leaf sits at the same ~35 degree upward pitch. There is not one branch anywhere in the silhouette. The read is a generic pinnate/fern-frond ladder plant, not a nightshade.

MUST-READ 2 (shiny black berry cupped in a flared green star): CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM. The judge called these 'three unreadable lilac pinheads.' At 12x they are FOUR discrete spheres, and they are NOT lilac -- the berry body is near-black aubergine (sampled RGB ~8,12,18 / ~15,24,19). What makes them scan pale at full size is that each berry carries a blown-out white specular (sampled ~137,138,136) covering roughly half its visible face. So the black-berry pigment IS present; the highlight is destroying it. Three further faults: (a) scale -- the whole cluster is only ~30x22px inside a 237px-tall plant, i.e. each berry is ~10px, nowhere near 'cherry-sized'; (b) count/arrangement -- a tight 4-berry umbel bunched against the stem, whereas the spec calls for a solitary berry; (c) THERE IS NO CALYX AT ALL -- not a small one, not a green one, nothing. No five-point star, no flared sepals, no green geometry behind or under the berries. The calyx is the single most diagnostic element of the harvest and it is entirely unmodelled.

MUST-READ 3 (coarse branching herb with unequal leaf pairs): ABSENT and INVERTED. The packet's leaf spec is 'alternate oval pointed leaves, often paired unequally with one large and one small'; the render gives strictly opposite, strictly equal pairs. The habit spec is 'coarse branching'; the render is a single unbranched axis. This is the defect that most damages identity -- belladonna's silhouette is a sprawling, irregularly forking bush, and the asset is the geometric opposite of that.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT THE ORIGINAL JUDGE DID NOT NOTE: proportion. The subject bounding box is roughly 85-120px wide by 237px tall, an aspect of ~0.36-0.50 against the packet's aspect: 0.8. The plant is far too narrow and too rigidly columnar even before the branching problem is addressed.

ONE THING THAT IS FINE (do not 'fix' it): leaf colour. Sampled lamina is ~RGB 72,84,59, a muted olive -- a correct match for 'dull dark green'. It looks brighter in exposure-boosted crops only.

FIX PRIORITY: (1) rebuild the habit as a coarse forking bush with 2-3 side branches leaving the main axis at different heights; (2) make leaf pairs alternate and unequal, one large one small at each node; (3) replace the 4-berry umbel with one solitary cherry-sized glossy black berry seated in a flared green five-point star calyx, and cut the specular down to a small offset dot; (4) add drooping purple-brown bell flowers nodding beneath the branch axils; (5) widen the silhouette toward aspect 0.8.

rows.readsAs: a pink daisy or a coneflower on a fern stalk
rows.defect: The flower head is a neat radially symmetric daisy with a round disc and short even petals — the exact opposite of the ragged firework head of long narrow tubular florets that IS Monarda. No leafy bracts under the head, no sign of a square stem, and the leaves are drawn as a fine pinnate ladder of narrow slivers rather than toothed lance-shaped opposite pairs.
rows.fix: Replace the daisy with a shaggy two-tier whorl of long lavender tubular florets spraying off a domed head, and set a ruff of leafy bracts directly beneath it.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified by reading the 440x440 PNG, then re-decoding it and re-reading three gamma-boosted nearest-neighbour crops (8x on the head, 6x on the mid-stem, 3x on the whole plant) so nothing small could hide in the dark background. All three packet must-reads are absent, so the FAIL stands, but one third of the stated cause is wrong.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS. One perfectly straight, smooth, round green stem runs from a small ground shadow to the top of the frame, uniform in width, unbranched, with no facets, no corner highlights and no angular silhouette anywhere along it -- nothing reads as a square stem. Attached to it are NINE pairs of leaves, evenly spaced from the very bottom of the stem to about 40px below the flower. Each leaf is a long narrow sliver (roughly 8:1 length-to-width), swept upward at ~35 degrees, pale grey-green with a lighter midrib line, and its margin is perfectly smooth -- there is not a single tooth or serration on any of the eighteen leaves. The terminal 40px of stalk above the top leaf pair is completely bare: no involucre, no leafy bracts, no whorl of anything under the head. At the very top sits ONE small flower head, about 40px across (only ~13% of the plant's height): approximately twelve broad, blunt, rounded petals in flat salmon/coral pink, spaced at even angular intervals with clean notched gaps between them, radiating from a solid round olive-gold disc that occupies the middle third of the head. It is a textbook composite/daisy -- Asteraceae, not Lamiaceae.

MUST-READ SCORECARD. (1) 'ragged firework head of narrow tubular flowers' -- ABSENT. The head is the neat radial daisy described above; there are zero tubular florets, zero shaggy protruding tubes, zero asymmetry, and the disc is a filled circle rather than the crowded pincushion Monarda shows. (2) 'square stem' -- ABSENT; a single round shaft, confirmed at 6x. (3) 'leafy bracts under the flower head' -- ABSENT; the stalk under the head is bare. The declared harvest, 'a shaggy crown of lavender tubular flowers on a domed head', also fails twice over: the crown is neither shaggy nor domed, and the hue is salmon/coral pink, not lavender.

WHERE THE PRIOR JUDGE IS WRONG. They wrote 'the foliage is a fine pinnate ladder rather than toothed lance-shaped opposite pairs'. The arrangement half of that is incorrect. At 6x the leaves plainly attach in OPPOSITE (very slightly sub-opposite -- the right leaf of each node sits a couple of pixels higher than the left) PAIRS at discrete nodes on the main stem, which is what the packet asks for, and their outline is lance-shaped, and the grey-green leafColour also matches the packet. So opposite-pair lance foliage is present and should NOT be re-derived by the fix. The real foliage defect is narrower: the leaves are far too NARROW (willow slivers, not lance blades), completely UNTOOTHED, too NUMEROUS (nine pairs marching evenly to the ground), and too uniform -- which combined with the unbranched stem is why the plant reads as a single fern frond or a Chamaenerion/willowherb rather than a mint-family herb. Everything else in the prior claim is accurate as written.

WHAT THE FIX NEEDS. Replace the composite head with a Monarda inflorescence: a flattened dome of many long thin lavender tubes bursting outward and downward at irregular angles from a knobbly centre, ragged in silhouette; ring the base of that head with a whorl of small leafy pink-tinged bracts; give the stem visible square facets (two darker edge lines / a flat-sided silhouette); and widen the leaves to true lance blades with coarse teeth, cutting the node count to roughly four or five opposite pairs so the head dominates the plant instead of being a 13% ornament. Aspect (0.6, tall and narrow) and leafColour are already correct and can be left alone.

rows.readsAs: a blueberry bush
rows.defect: It reads as a low blue-berry shrub, but it is pixel-for-pixel the Bearberry chassis recoloured, and both features the note says separate bilberry from blueberry are inverted: the stems are plain flat brown instead of green and sharply angled, and the berries are gathered into clustered bunches at the cane tips instead of borne singly in the leaf axils. The pink-green globe flowers are absent, and the shrub is a narrow upright vase rather than a low dense mound.

rows.readsAs: a generic lollipop shade tree — a linden or a kids-book apple tree
rows.defect: The trunk is a plain flat mid-brown column with no white bark, no peeling papery strips and no black diamond scars, so the single most identifiable feature of a birch is entirely absent. The crown is a dense round lollipop of large round leaves instead of a narrow airy crown of fine drooping twigs with small triangular toothed leaves, and the trunk is thick and stubby rather than slender. Nothing indicates sap or a tap either.

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD after pixel inspection (5x crop of the trunk, 3x crop of the crown, plus per-scanline colour sampling of the 440x440 PNG). Packet mustReads: (1) slender bright white peeling bark with black diamond scars, (2) narrow airy crown of fine drooping twigs, (3) small triangular leaves. Zero of the three are present, and the harvest cue (clear sap running from a tap) is absent as well.

TRUNK — the judge is exactly right and the numbers are worse than the prose. Every scanline from y=270 to y=350 samples the SAME single fill, rgb(107,74,46), a mid saddle-brown; the only other values in the trunk band are edge antialias pixels. There is no white anywhere on the bole, no horizontal lenticel dashes, no peeling curls, no black chevron/diamond scars, no grain, no hue break at all. Three further trunk defects the judge did not name and that a fix must also address: (a) it does not taper — width is a constant 28px at y=300 and 28px at y=340, i.e. a parallel-sided extrusion, where birch is a taper with a slight flare; (b) it has no root flare and no ground contact — the bole terminates in a fully ROUNDED capsule end at about y=365 and floats above the separate elliptical drop shadow, reading as a popsicle stick pushed into the leaves rather than a tree growing out of soil; (c) no tap, spile, bucket or sap bead appears anywhere on it, so the species' actual harvest is unrepresented.

CROWN — the judge is right in substance, wrong in two details worth correcting because they change the fix. It is NOT a 'dense round lollipop'. It is a broad, FLATTENED green cloud, wider than tall (crown spans roughly x 95-350 by y 60-270), and it is not dense: the interior is an empty airbrushed green haze with a soft light blob in the middle, and the leaves are arranged only as a single ring around the rim. So the crown fails twice over — the outline is a wide blob instead of a narrow upright plume, AND the interior has no drawn structure whatsoever. There are no twigs, no branchlets, no pendulous shoot lines anywhere in the image; nothing droops. The leaves are large near-circular ovate discs with a bold central midrib and a few herringbone side veins — roughly 25-30px across on a 440px canvas, i.e. huge relative to the tree, and rounded rather than triangular. They read closest to a generic apple/pear leaf. Overall silhouette is a generic broadleaf shade tree.

ONE THING THE JUDGE MISSED (and it does not rescue the asset): there ARE five pale tan vertical strands hanging in the crown, each a chain of ~8-10 beige circles, at roughly (200,140), (250,120), (263,175), (196,215) and (255,140). These are presumably an attempt at birch catkins. They fail as catkins for three reasons: they are beaded strings of discrete circles rather than tapering scaly cylinders; they hang from nothing — no twig, petiole or branch attaches to any of them, so they float inside the green haze; and their pale beige reads as generic dangling blossom/fruit filler. They are also the only non-generic element in the piece, so they cannot carry the identity alone.

PROPORTION — packet aspect is 0.5 (height twice the width, i.e. a slender upright). The drawn tree is about 305px tall by about 260px wide, an aspect near 0.85. Too squat for a birch even before the bark question.

Verdict: reads as a generic cartoon shade tree, not a birch. The defining white/black bark is not merely small or hidden in a place the first judge failed to look — a per-pixel scan proves the trunk is one flat brown value. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: an agave or a century plant with a daisy on a wire
rows.defect: The rosette is made of broad flat pale-grey sword blades spread like an agave, not short fleshy cylindrical finger-like leaves, and they are turgid and prominent rather than already shrivelling. The must-read of a LARGE many-petalled pink flower sitting FLAT on bare gravel with NO VISIBLE STEM is directly contradicted: a small pink daisy is held on a long conspicuous bare stalk high above the rosette, so the two defining traits of bitterroot are both reversed.

rows.verifyWhy: Upheld, and the original judge described it accurately; I add scale numbers and two corrections. WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a single symmetrical fan/rosette of roughly 22-24 long, BROAD, FLAT, sharply-pointed sword blades radiating in a near-semicircular spray about 260px wide on a ~440px canvas, sitting on a soft elliptical ground shadow. Each blade is pale whitish sage-green (not grey-green), fully turgid, has a distinct darker midrib and fine herringbone side-veining, and tapers to a needle tip. The reading is agave / yucca / young fan-palm — a hard, fibrous, spiny-leaved xerophyte, not a soft succulent. Rising from the centre is a thin olive stem: it is visible for the WHOLE height of the plant (traceable from the ground line up through the rosette) and then continues ~110px as a completely bare stalk above the leaf tips, terminating in a small radially-symmetric pink flower roughly 40px across (~15% of the plant's width) with about a dozen short blunt petals and a magenta centre disc. PACKET mustRead: 'large many-petalled pink flower sitting flat on bare gravelly ground - fleshy finger-like leaves already shrivelling - no visible stem'. All three are inverted. (1) The flower is SMALL and ELEVATED, not large and ground-hugging; real Lewisia rediviva has a bloom as wide as or wider than its whole leaf rosette, here the leaves outspan the flower ~6:1. (2) 'No visible stem' is violated twice over — there is a long conspicuous bare peduncle AND the stem is drawn showing through the rosette down to soil level. (3) The leaves are broad flat blades at full turgor rather than short, blunt, cylindrical fleshy fingers, and there is zero shrivelling/withering cue, which is the defining state of the plant at flowering time. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM: (a) calling it 'a small pink daisy' undersells one thing that is right — the flower IS many-petalled and radially symmetric, so the petal count is on-target; the failure is purely its scale and its elevation, and a fix should keep the petal geometry and drop the flower to the ground while enlarging it ~3x. (b) the claim implies nothing correct survives — in fact the GROUND-LEVEL ROSETTE arrangement is correct and reusable; only the individual leaf morphology (broad pointed sword -> short blunt fleshy cylinder, half of them limp/browning) needs replacing. Also absent but not a mustRead: no gravelly substrate texture and no thick pale forked taproot (the stated harvest). Aspect target is 1.5 (wide) but the canvas is square. As drawn a viewer would name this an agave, so the identity read fails.

rows.readsAs: a grapevine

The heads are NOT 'pink pompoms' - at 4x they resolve as flat, face-on radial RINGS: a dark maroon-plum disc with a ring of 10-14 small pale cream-white beads set around its rim and one or two ochre specks at the centre. A fixer told 'tighten the bunch into a cylinder' would be working from the wrong starting geometry; the head has to be replaced with a pendent 8-12 cm axis bearing 20+ stalked units.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM (2): 'thin willow lances rather than broad glossy sharply-toothed ovals' is right on shape but incomplete. The leaves are narrow lanceolate blades about 5:1, mid dull green, and their margins are perfectly SMOOTH - not a single tooth is drawn anywhere on any leaf. There is also no specular gloss on the upper surface and no paler underside; the reference asks for 'dark glossy green above, paler beneath'. So three separate leaf attributes fail, not one. There is no red flush, not on the tips, not at the base, not one pixel. All three must-reads (leafless articulated fleshy stems; opposite candelabra branching; red flush on older segments) are absent. TWO CORRECTIONS to the original claim, neither of which rescues it. Glasswort is the inverse silhouette (point at top, widest at base) and its ribs are fully FUSED into one closed outline with no separated tips and no bladders. They plainly come off the same rib/strap-bundle generator, but Glasswort is the degenerate fully-fused, apex-up variant, not a straight recolour — a fix that only re-tints the kelp bundle will not help. (2) Also worth logging for the fix: the packet asks for aspect 1.2 (roughly as wide as tall, a low sprawling succulent clump); the rendered plant measures 44 wide x 240 tall = aspect 0.18, off by nearly 7x, which is why it reads as a spire. And the leaf colour is a dull desaturated sage (row averages around R76 G110 B87), not the 'bright translucent green' the packet specifies. FIX DIRECTION: give it a low branching clump (aspect ~1.2) of short cylindrical segments with real width constrictions between them, paired opposite side shoots off the main axes, brighter translucent green, and crimson on the lower/older segments.

rows.readsAs: a grapevine — the strongest read in the batch

rows.readsAs: a fern or a low sago palm
rows.defect: The fronds are only ONCE-cut — each is a solid green lance with sawtooth notches nicked into its two edges, so the twice-pinnate structure (pinnae themselves divided) is absent and up close it reads as a serrated blade, not a fern leaf. The rosette is a low sideways-spreading fan roughly twice as wide as it is tall, not the upright shuttlecock funnel called for. The brown scaly stalk bases are entirely missing; the crown is uniform green.

rows.readsAs: a young cannabis plant, or a stylised conifer

rows.readsAs: a generic purple-leaved herb on a stick
rows.defect: This is the Gentian armature repainted — identical stem, identical eight opposite leaf pairs at identical spacing and angle, identical bead-string flower spike. The leaves are smooth untoothed ovals, so the toothed margin is absent; the stem is a plain round-looking green line with no square section and no hairs; and the flower spike is a single thin column of beads with no tiered whorls stepping out from it. rows.readsAs: a blueberry bush — the exact organism the reference says it must not be

Here every berry is drawn in a tight terminal cluster of five or six at the top of each cane, which is the blueberry read, inverted from the must-read. The stems are also thick woody brown poles, not sharply angled green twigs, the bush is a dense narrow bundle rather than open and airy, and there are no pink urn-shaped flowers. Zero of the three must-reads are present, and the whole chassis is shared with Juniper Berries.

rows.readsAs: a speckled bird's egg or a marble floating in black space

rows.readsAs: a generic broadleaf tree with pale fruit

rows.readsAs: a bare forked sapling with four small green sparklers stuck on it

rows.readsAs: a sparse twiggy shrub carrying a few blue-grey berries

rows.readsAs: a woody stem carrying two spiky tan seed pods — closer to a rambutan or a sea urchin than a kiwi

rows.readsAs: a generic twiggy garden bush with white blobs on the tips
rows.defect: The identity cue — rusty orange wool on the leaf undersides and young stems — is nowhere on the render; stems are plain mid-brown and every leaf shows only flat dark green. Silhouette is the shared shrub fan shared with Lingonberry and Marsh Rosemary.

rows.readsAs: a scallop shell, or a splayed palm fan / firework burst
rows.defect: Wrong organism entirely. The render is a symmetrical spray of ~11 pale rounded rays radiating from a single point at the bottom centre, floating on empty background over an ellipse shadow. There is no rock or bark substrate, no flat crusty rosette, no lobed edge with a chalky pale margin, and no raised cup discs anywhere. It is a radiating fan with a defined foot — exactly the stem-and-frond reading the reference note forbids.

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at full size, again boosted, and again at 3x on the base (crop x80-360 / y210-340), plus a pixel scan. The FAIL stands: this is the wrong organism. What is actually on the canvas: a single pale sage fan occupying bbox x87-352, y137-286 (265w x 149h). Its base is a SOLID triangular wedge that converges downward to a sharp V point at roughly (220,286) — one basal origin, like the umbo of a scallop or the crown of a palm-fan petiole. From that wedge, straight unbranched rays with rounded (capsule) tips splay outward through the upper half. Annular scans at r=70 and r=100 around the hub both return 12 discrete segments, not eleven — correct the judge's count to TWELVE rays. The rays are near-mirror-symmetric but not exactly so (left and right members differ slightly in length and angle), and the outermost pair on each side lies nearly horizontal. Beneath the wedge sits a soft elliptical drop shadow spanning roughly x130-330, y278-308, sampling 5,8,11 against a 7,9,15 background — a faint blur, NOT a rock, NOT bark, with no rim, no facet, no texture, nothing that reads as a substrate. The shape floats ON the shadow, it does not cling to anything.

Against the reference row (form: moss, aspect 1.4; leaf: flat overlapping leathery lobes in a rosette on rock, or fine antler-like branching tufts; mustRead: flat crusty rosette clinging to rock or bark / lobed edges with a paler chalky margin / small raised cup discs on the surface; note: not a plant, no stems or roots, drawn as a crust or antler-tuft on a substrate, never as foliage) — all three must-reads are absent, none of them merely small or hidden:
1. No substrate of any kind, so no crust CLINGING to anything. The only non-background element besides the fan is the drop shadow.
2. No lobed margin and no chalky pale edge. A full-image color census shows the entire body is ONE flat fill, RGB 174,191,175, covering 11,160 px; every other color in the body is a 1-2 step antialias variant of it. There is zero internal shading, zero mottling, no white/sulphur-yellow/rust patch, no rim value change anywhere. The judge did not mention this, and it is worth recording: the asset is a flat vector silhouette, not a painted thallus.
3. No cup discs. I looked specifically for small raised discs on the wedge and along the rays at 3x; there is not a single darker or lighter spot on the body.

The one line of defense available — the alternate reading 'fine antler-like branching tufts' — does not rescue it. Antler-tuft (fruticose) lichen means repeated dichotomous forking: each branch splits into two, then two again, giving a tangled coral mass with no single origin. Here every ray is a straight, unbranched, uniform-width capsule emanating from ONE point, which is exactly the stem-and-frond / radiating-fan reading the note forbids. It reads as a scallop shell, a palm/fan-palm leaf, or a stylized sunburst.

One further correction to the claim's wording: it calls the base 'a single basal point over a cast shadow' — accurate, but it understates that the base is a substantial filled triangular mass roughly 90px wide at the top narrowing to a point, i.e. the fix must remove a body, not just re-splay lines. Fix direction: replace the whole silhouette with a low, wide, irregular crust hugging a rock or bark form that occupies the lower third of the frame, give it lobed and overlapping margins with a paler chalky rim, break the single flat fill into grey-green/sage patches with rust-orange and sulphur-yellow blotches, and stipple small raised cup discs (apothecia) across the surface. Nothing should rise from a single stem point.

rows.readsAs: an ornamental red-leaved twig with red berries — a barberry or a young sumac
rows.defect: Every stated must-read is contradicted rather than merely missing. The leaves are large salmon-red simple blades, six of them alternating up a bare dark stem — not mid-green pinnate leaves of 9-17 leaflets. No root, no runner, nothing below ground. The colour alone (red foliage, red fruit) sends a stranger to a berry shrub.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at full size and at 3-5x zoom on the tip, the mid-stem nodes and the base. The FAIL stands; all three must-reads are contradicted rather than merely faint, and no small or off-centre feature rescues any of them.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a single unbranched, perfectly straight vertical dowel-stem, dark olive-brown with a lit left edge, running the full height of the frame. Off it hang SEVEN (not six -- correct the count) simple, entire, lanceolate blades, alternating left/right/left/right/left/right/left, each ~70px long, each with ONE pale central midrib and no lateral veins, no petiole, no rachis and no leaflets. Colour is coral/salmon-red with a lighter pink core and a darker rust rim -- nowhere near the required dull mid-green. Between the leaf nodes sit FIVE clusters of three small round spheres in bright orange-red, seated flush against the stem at the node (they are tight triplets on the stem, not 'pinned along' it loosely, and they are unmistakably berries/drupes -- smooth, spherical, specular-highlighted -- not buds and not flowers). At the bottom the stem is cut off FLAT, ~15px above an elliptical cast ground-shadow: no soil line, no taproot, no ropey yellow root, no horizontal runner, nothing below ground at all. At the top the stem ends in a bare blunt cut with no inflorescence, no spike and no terminal leaflet.

MUST-READ 1 'pinnate leaflets in neat opposite pairs': ABSENT and contradicted. Every blade is a single undivided lamina attached directly to the stem; there is no rachis anywhere in the image, so nothing can even be misread as compound. The arrangement is also alternate, not opposite.
MUST-READ 2 'upright spikes of small pale blue-violet pea flowers': ABSENT and contradicted. The only reproductive structures are orange-red berry triplets. There is no violet/blue pixel in the asset and no spike/raceme form of any kind.
MUST-READ 3 'long straight yellow woody roots and horizontal runners': ABSENT. Confirmed at 5x with a 2.4x brightness boost -- the region below the stem is pure background plus shadow. The harvest organ, which is the entire point of this species, is not depicted.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM: (a) there are seven blades, not six; (b) the stem is not 'bare' -- it carries the five berry triplets directly, so the read is a berried twig rather than a leafy-only shoot; (c) the judge's 'barberry or young sumac' gloss is loose -- sumac is itself pinnate, so citing it undercuts the point. With entire lanceolate red-flushed leaves and tight triplets of round red berries on a single straight cane the silhouette reads closest to a Nandina/spicebush/red-leaved dogwood shoot. The substance of the claim is right on every count that matters.

FIX DIRECTION: rebuild the leaf as a true pinnate frond -- a visible rachis carrying 9-17 small oval leaflets in opposite pairs plus one terminal leaflet -- recolour to dull mid-green, replace the berry triplets with slim upright spikes of pale blue-violet pea flowers in the upper leaf axils, and add the defining harvest: a long straight yellow woody taproot with horizontal runners exposed below the soil line.

rows.readsAs: a clump of sago-palm or sword fern growing out of the ground

rows.readsAs: a stiff green fern or feather-frond with a small lilac tip

The pale blue-lilac spike is present but is a small pixel-scale bead chain crammed at the very top, easy to miss at icon size.

rows.readsAs: an upright garden shrub with red berry clusters — a coffee or cotoneaster bush

rows.readsAs: a water lily floating on a pond
rows.defect: The harvest that names the asset is absent. That is the whole asset. Nothing else is drawn anywhere in the frame.

Against the packet row (harvest: 'a chain of fat sausage-linked pale rhizomes, pierced with round holes in cross-section'; mustRead: 'round dish-shaped leaf on a central stalk . sausage-chain rhizome . the ring of holes in the cut root'; note: 'here the harvest is the rhizome, so show the root chain pulled from the mud'): must-reads 2 and 3 -- the two that separate Lotus Root from Lotus -- are 100% absent. The named harvest, which is the entire reason this species exists as a separate entry from 'Lotus', was never drawn.

TWO CORRECTIONS to their stated cause, both of which change what the fix should touch:
1. They say the pads have no central stalk at all. Not quite -- each pad carries a short dark-green dash near its center (the front-center pad carries two, at roughly (240,215) and (285,205); the left and right pads one each). These are clearly an attempted petiole/peltate-notch mark, but they are drawn flat ON the pad's top surface, horizontally, ~30px long, so they read as a vein or a split, not as a stalk. So must-read 1 is not absent so much as drawn wrong: the geometry exists but is coplanar with the pad. Don't add a stalk from nothing -- rotate/extend the existing mark into a vertical petiole that pierces the water line.
2. 'lie flat on the water instead of being held high on stalks with upturned rims' is correct on both counts, and the rim half is the more damaging one: the pads are pure flat ellipses with a top-down gradient, zero bowl, and their edges intersect the water ellipse rather than floating above it, which is exactly the water-lily silhouette. The packet's leafColour ('blue-grey green, water-repellent') is also missed -- what is painted is a bright mint/spring green.

One defect the original judge did not report: framing.
