Along it are ELEVEN pairs of sessile, narrow lance leaflets, and the mid-node crop shows both leaflets of a pair springing from the SAME node band on opposite sides — so the pairing is genuinely opposite, not alternate; the judge did not claim otherwise but it is the one leaf spec that is met. Every leaflet sweeps outward and DOWN-curving with a pale central highlight stripe, and the pairs are evenly spaced and evenly graded in length (longest low, shortest at the top), which is exactly the rachis-and-pinnae read of a palm/cycad frond. Correction to the judge's wording: it is not a FERN frond (no pinnules, no subdivision, no crozier); it reads as a single pinnate palm/ash-type frond. The gestalt conclusion is right, the organism named is slightly off.

MUST-READ 1 - square branching stems: ABSENT, exactly as claimed. The stem is a single smooth round taper of uniform width with faint darker node bands; zero side branches, zero axillary shoots, no angular/quadrangular facet or edge-highlight anywhere. Nothing about the stem says Lamiaceae.

MUST-READ 2 - flat domed clusters of tiny white flowers: ABSENT. Measured the near-white pixels: bounding box x219-228, y89-133 - a 10px wide by 45px tall column (4.5:1 TALL), 241 white pixels total (~1.2% of the subject). It is roughly eight to nine white lumps stacked vertically on the naked stem tip, the topmost slightly hooked over. So the judge's 'vertical string of white beads' is literally correct and geometrically confirmed - it is the inverse of a flat-topped corymb, which would have to be WIDE and SHORT and sit as a plate over the foliage. At thumbnail size it reads as a grub/caterpillar or a cattail spikelet clinging to the frond tip. Additionally: the flowers are pure blue-white (sampled 224,224,240 / 201,201,216) with NO purple speckling at all, so the packet harvest line 'speckled purple' is also unmet - the judge did not mention this.

MUST-READ 3 - pale silvery bracts under each flower head: ABSENT, as claimed. There is no bract collar, no whitened involucre, nothing beneath the white column but bare green stem. Worse, the packet's 'whitish dusting on the upper leaves' is inverted: sampling an upper leaf (200,140 = 91,108,90) against a lower leaf (200,290 = 130,157,124) shows the UPPER foliage is DARKER and duller than the lower, the opposite of the frosted-top-leaves cue that makes Pycnanthemum identifiable in the field.

VERDICT: three of three must-reads are missing, the flower - the single diagnostic organ - is drawn as the wrong shape class (erect spike instead of flat dome), and the habit is a frond rather than a branching square-stemmed herb. Nothing is 'present but small' or hidden anywhere in the frame. FAIL upheld.

FIX DIRECTION: replace the apical bead column with two or three WIDE, SHORT flat-topped domes (each ~3-4x wider than tall) held at the tips of a stem that FORKS at least twice into opposite pairs near the top; render the stem with a visible angular edge highlight so the square section reads; ring each dome with a collar of pale silver-white bracts; dust the top two or three leaf pairs pale/frosted so they are lighter than the lower leaves; and add fine purple speckling into the white florets.

rows.readsAs: a cycad or a young palm carrying one gourd
rows.defect: The crown is a rosette of stiff feather-pinnate fronds - exactly a cycad - where papaya needs deeply lobed palmate hands on long stalks. Only ONE fruit is drawn where the row asks for a cluster of small five-angled fruits hugging the stem, and it is a smooth round-shouldered gourd with faint ribs rather than sharply five-angled. The trunk is heavy and clubbed rather than slim and leaf-scarred, and it carries an amputated stub branch on the right that stops in mid-air and reads as a render artefact. That trunk is shared pixel-for-pixel with Nipa Palm Fruit.
rows.fix: Swap the feather fronds for five or six palmate lobed leaves on long stalks, and hang a ring of six small yellow fruits with visible sharp longitudinal ridges directly against the trunk under the crown.

rows.readsAs: a low rosette of round leaves with a red seed spike - a wild ginger or a sorrel, roughly right
rows.defect: The basal mound of rounded fleshy leaves reads well and is one of the few silhouettes in this batch that is not a shared template. But two must-reads miss: the leaf stalks are thin and green, with no sign of the red petioles the row calls out, and the seed head is drawn as the same generic vertical bead string used on Mountain Mint, Mugwort and Nettle - small round beads rather than flat papery winged discs. The leaves are also plain round rather than kidney-shaped with a notch at the base.
rows.fix: Recolour the leaf stalks crimson so they read against the green, and replace the bead string with overlapping flat translucent crimson discs so the seeds look papery and winged.

rows.readsAs: five pink daisies on bare wires - a sparse aster sprig, not a herb mat
rows.defect: The plant has no foliage. The must-read calls for very small paired leaves crowded along creeping wiry stems, and what is drawn is a bare skeletal fan of straight yellow-green lines radiating from a central point with nothing on them - the crowded leaf mat that IS a thyme is absent. The flowers are also wrong in kind: five widely spaced ray daisies with pale pink petals and a dark eye, rather than dense rounded heads of tiny lipped rose-purple flowers. The low wide aspect is the only must-read that lands.
rows.fix: Crowd every stem with pairs of tiny dark grey-green oval leaves until the mat reads as dense foliage, and replace the daisies with tight rounded pompom heads of small purple-pink flowers at the shoot tips.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 5x-20x crops of the 440x440 canvas. The verdict stands, but the stated cause is partly wrong and the correction matters for the fix.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a single ground contact point at ~(220,270) from which ~10-12 straight tapered dark-olive spokes radiate upward-outward in a symmetric V/chevron fan, ~230px wide x ~115px tall (so the aspect:2 'wider than tall' requirement IS met numerically). Five pale-lilac flowers sit on five of those spoke tips (far left, left, centre-top, right, far right). The remaining ~6 spokes terminate bare in empty background, so mustRead 3's 'flower heads at EVERY shoot tip' also fails on count, not just on form.

CORRECTION TO THE JUDGE'S CLAIM — 'no foliage at all' is not literally true. There IS a leaf layer and it is placed correctly: short PALE SAGE-GREEN straight bars, ~6-14px long and 1-2px thick, sit on the stems, and at several nodes near the base two of them radiate OPPOSITE from the same point (a proper opposite-pair node — visible around x=195-250, y=225-250 and x=145-175, y=235-250). So the opposite-paired arrangement the packet asks for is already encoded in the geometry. The defect is that each leaf is STROKED AS A BARE ZERO-WIDTH LINE with no blade: no oval outline, no width, no midrib, no taper. At 1x they read as crossing wires, and because they cross the spokes at shallow angles the whole base resolves as a chain-link / lattice mesh rather than a leafy mat. Value is also inverted: the leaves are LIGHTER (pale sage, ~#b9c49a) than the stems (dark olive, ~#5b6b2e), where the packet calls for dark grey-green leaves — so the foliage reads as highlight lines on twigs. Density is also far too low: roughly 2-4 leaf sticks per spoke with long bare runs between them, versus the 'crowded along creeping wiry stems' the packet requires.

FLOWERS — the judge is correct here. Each of the five heads is a 12-rayed daisy: separate pointed pale-lilac (#dcc0e2) ray petals radiating from a large filled gold-brown disc (~#7a6410, about 40% of the head diameter). That is an Asteraceae capitulum (aster / erigeron / echinacea), NOT a thyme head. The packet wants 'dense rounded heads of tiny rose-purple lipped flowers' — a compact pompom with no disc and no individual visible rays. The big brown disc is the single loudest wrong signal: it is what makes the plant read as a daisy. Colour of the rays is acceptably in the rose-purple family; hue is not the problem, form is. Heads are also isolated singletons spaced ~55px apart with black gaps between, so there is no massing.

SILHOUETTE — not a creeping mat. It is a radial spray from one point (a hand-fan / whisk), with an unbroken pointed apex at the ground and no horizontal creeping runners, no ground-hugging mass, no overlapping foliage volume. A viewer reads 'small daisy plant', not 'thyme'.

BAND: FAIL upheld. Two of three must-reads are absent as readable identity (paired leaves present as geometry but unreadable as foliage; flower heads are the wrong organ type), and the third (low creeping mat) is satisfied only by bounding-box ratio, not by form. FIX ORDER: (1) replace the flower primitive - kill the brown disc, replace the 12 separate rays with a dense clustered pompom of tiny lipped florets; (2) give the existing leaf sticks a filled oval blade 3-5px wide in dark grey-green and darken them below the stem value; (3) triple leaf density along each stem; (4) flatten and spread the fan into a creeping mat with horizontal runners instead of a single-point radial spray, and put a head on every spoke tip. The limb/branch skeleton itself is already the right topology - do not re-derive it.

rows.readsAs: a frost-killed or albino bottlebrush - a dead white plant
rows.defect: The entire plant is rendered chalk-white. The row's headline must-read is a two-tone leaf - dark green ABOVE, white-felted UNDERNEATH, so the plant flickers silver - and painting the whole thing white destroys exactly that read; there is no green anywhere except a sliver of stem at the base. The tall reddish-purple grooved stem is invisible under the foliage column, and the leaves are chassis A blades with sawtooth edges rather than deeply pinnately cut leaves with pointed lobes. It is Monkshood's silhouette with the saturation removed.
rows.fix: Paint the leaf upper surfaces dark green and show white only on the reversed, upturned leaflets, and expose a tall reddish-purple grooved stem running the full height.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL upheld, with two corrections to the stated cause. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS: a single erect axis, plant bbox x184-259 / y93-332 (76 x 240 px, w/h ~0.32 against the packet's aspect 0.5 -- slightly too narrow). Along that axis sit about seven stacked radial WHORLS of entire, undissected lanceolate blades, each whorl a full 360-degree rosette pinned at a node, so the silhouette is a symmetric bottlebrush / dwarf-conifer column, not a leafy herb. At the apex (y93-135) there IS a narrow beaded ivory-khaki spike with no petals -- that third must-read ('narrow drab flower spires with no showy petals') is genuinely PRESENT and the first judge did not mention it; it is the one thing the asset gets right, though it is cream-khaki (~174,175,145) rather than dull greenish-grey and it is the same value as the foliage so it barely separates as a distinct organ. COLOUR MEASURED over all lit plant pixels (n=11,216): 51.4% desaturated white, 42.3% pale grey, 6.2% green, 0.0% red/purple. So 93.7% of the plant is chalk white. CORRECTION 1 to the claim: it is NOT true that 'the whole plant is painted chalk white' -- there is a stem, and it is visible. A thin olive-green stem (~(71,84,45), 4-5 px wide) runs from the ground shadow up to the lowest whorl at y~300, and thin olive slivers show between whorls higher up. CORRECTION 2: that stem is smooth and untextured -- no groove, rib or flute is drawn -- and it is olive-green, not reddish-purple; the red-channel count of 0 confirms the judge's 'no reddish grooved stem' verdict even though they wrongly implied no stem exists at all. WHY IT STILL FAILS: the headline identity is the BICOLOUR leaf -- dark green above, white-felted beneath, so the plant flickers silver. Here there is no dark green surface anywhere on any blade, so there is nothing for the white to contrast against; the 'silver flicker' read is destroyed not by the white being present but by the green being absent. And the blades are entire -- no pinnate cutting, no pointed lobes, no rachis -- so must-read 1 ('silver-white undersides on CUT leaves') fails on both halves. Must-read 2 fails outright. Two of three defining must-reads absent, and the organism reads as a frosted bottlebrush / white conifer sprig rather than a tall cut-leaved herb. FIX DIRECTION: paint blade upper faces dark grey-green and reserve the chalk white for the reversed/undersides and blade edges only; recut each blade into 5-9 pointed pinnate lobes off a central rachis; re-arrange the leaves ALTERNATE up the axis rather than in radial whorls; recolour the stem reddish-purple and add vertical groove striations; keep the apex spike as drawn but shift it toward dull greenish-grey so it separates from the foliage.

rows.readsAs: a tropical tree with feathery leaves and small yellow fruit - close enough to a neem
rows.defect: The crown is not a broad rounded shady canopy; it is a hollow ring of about a dozen isolated pinnate sprays pinned around a soft green glow blob, so it reads sparse and spidery, with the blob doing the work the foliage should do. The leaflets are straight and blunt rather than sickle-curved and toothed, and the loose sprays of small white flowers named in the must-read are entirely absent - only three yellow-green fruits appear. The trunk is a flat brown bar with no taper or bark.
rows.fix: Fill the crown with overlapping drooping pinnate sprays so the canopy silhouette is solid and dome-shaped, curve the leaflets into sickles, and add two or three loose sprays of tiny white flowers.

rows.readsAs: a corn cob, or a green succulent column - certainly not a nettle
rows.defect: The leaves are featureless smooth green ovals overlapping so tightly that they fuse into one solid vertical cylinder with no gaps and no visible stem. Every diagnostic is gone: no heart-shaped base, no coarse teeth, no bristles anywhere, no tiered spacing between leaf pairs, and the drooping stringy green flower tassels in the leaf axils are replaced by a single cream bead spike sticking out of the top. A stranger would not name a plant at all, they would name a vegetable.
rows.fix: Space the leaf pairs into distinct tiers with visible square stem between them, cut a heart-shaped base and coarse saw teeth into every leaf, and hang limp green catkin strings from the leaf joints.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the full 440px render plus 6x/14x/18x crops of the crown, the base and the left silhouette edge. VERDICT UPHELD, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and the fix brief must not be written against them.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a single vertical column of leaves running from y~110 to y~318, ~80px wide, dead straight sides. About nine OPPOSITE PAIRS of leaves are stacked with almost no vertical gap, each pair attached at a shared node on a visible dark-green central axis that runs the full height of the column. Below the foliage a bare, straight, flat mid-green stalk ~10px wide runs from y~318 down to the ground shadow at y~355. On top, a single erect cream/ivory knobbly spike ~10px wide x 45px tall stands straight up out of the leaf mass.

CORRECTION 1 - "no stem" is FALSE. There IS a stem: a clean bare green petiole/stalk stub below the leaf mass, plus a continuous darker-green midrib/rachis line threading every leaf node up the whole column. The real defect is not absence, it is that the stalk is a featureless smooth round-section green stick - not square in section, not grooved, and carrying zero bristles - and that it is completely buried by leaf overlap for the entire 200px of foliage, so the must-read "upright square bristly stem" never becomes readable anywhere on the plant.

CORRECTION 2 - "featureless" leaves is FALSE. Each leaf carries a broad pale specular highlight and faint diagonal lateral-vein hatching converging on its own midvein; the paint is not blank. And the must-read "opposite ... leaves in tiers" IS actually satisfied - the pairing and the tiering are the clearest thing in the image. The judge under-credited this.

WHAT GENUINELY FAILS: (a) LEAF SHAPE. Every leaf is an elongate lance-ovate blade ~40px x 16px with a tapered-rounded base and a blunt tip. Zero cordate/heart bases, zero basal lobes. The 14x edge crop shows the silhouette as one smooth continuous soft curve, scalloped only by leaf tips - not a single serration, tooth, or projecting hair anywhere on the outline. So "coarsely toothed heart-shaped bristled" is absent in all three of its terms. (b) HARVEST. The packet demands drooping stringy green catkin-like flower tassels hanging from the LEAF AXILS. What is drawn is one erect, rigid, cream-white beaded column standing TERMINALLY on the apex - wrong colour (cream vs green), wrong count (one vs many), wrong attachment (terminal vs axillary), wrong direction (erect vs drooping). Nothing hangs anywhere in the image. (c) The leaf packing is so tight (pairs touching, no internode showing) that the whole thing resolves as one solid green capsule.

GESTALT: the judge's "corn cob" is fair - a straight green cylinder of tight overlapping opposite leaflets on a central rachis with a pale spike on top reads either as a corn ear or as a single pinnate frond (sumac/fern). It does not read as a herb. Two of three must-reads are absent; the surviving one (opposite tiers) is present but degenerate. FAIL stands.

FIX BRIEF: open the internodes so the square bristly stem shows between tiers; give each leaf a cordate base with two basal lobes flanking the petiole, a serrated margin, and stubble bristles breaking the silhouette; and replace the terminal cream spike with several drooping grey-green stringy tassels hanging from the leaf axils partway down the stem.

rows.readsAs: the exact same palm tree as Mountain Papaya, with a grey fruit instead of a yellow one
rows.defect: The single defining fact about nipa - NO VISIBLE TRUNK, fronds erupting straight out of the water and mud, with the cannonball fruit head sitting at ground level - is contradicted on every point. The render gives it a tall thick brown trunk that occupies the lower two thirds of the frame, and parks a small grey fruit ball high in the crown notch. Worse, the trunk is identical to Mountain Papaya's down to the same amputated right-hand stub branch, and the frond crown is the same stamp; only the fruit colour differs. There is also no water or mud.
rows.fix: Delete the trunk entirely - spring the huge upright feather fronds directly from a single point at ground level - and set a large spiky brown cannonball fruit cluster on the ground at that point.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld. Packet mustRead: (1) no visible trunk, fronds erupting directly from water and mud; (2) huge upright feather fronds fanning from a single point; (3) spiky brown cannonball fruit cluster at the BASE. Aspect 0.7, form palm.

What is actually on the 440x440 canvas: a tall solid mid-brown trunk running from y~390 up to y~185 — roughly 47% of the frame height and the single most dominant shape in the image. At y~200 it forks; the right limb is a thick brown branch angling up-right that ENDS in a blunt rounded cut, poking clear of the fronds on the right side. I cropped and 4x-upscaled the fork region to confirm this: it is unmistakably an amputated stub branch, not a leaf petiole or a frond base. A crop of the bottom region (3x) shows the trunk simply terminating in a rounded capsule end sitting on a flat elliptical drop shadow — bare dark background all around it. There is no water line, no mud, no basal rosette, no clump of frond bases at ground level, and no fruit anywhere near the bottom of the frame. Must-read #1 is not merely weak, it is inverted: the asset's loudest feature is the exact thing the species is defined by NOT having.

The crown is a fan of pinnate fronds with fine regular leaflets, mid-to-dark green, radiating from the fork at y~190 and spanning x~120-320. This is the ONE must-read that partly lands — the fronds are correct in leaflet character and they do radiate from a single point — but they radiate from the top of a trunk rather than erupting from the ground, and they arch outward and downward like a coconut/cycad crown instead of standing as huge stiff upright feathers, so even #2 reads only halfway.

Corrections to the original claim, which is right in verdict but imprecise on the fruit: the judge said the fruit is 'parked high in the crown'. The fruit IS elevated and wrong, but it is not up in the frond canopy — it is a small cluster nestled in the crotch of the trunk fork at about y~180-205 (roughly 42% down from the top, i.e. mid-frame, well above ground but below the frond mass). More importantly the judge did not note that the fruit is also the wrong COLOUR, TEXTURE and SIZE: at 4x it is a bunch of ~12 smooth pale cream/beige-to-tan ovoid pebbles, reading like a small bunch of grapes or a clutch of eggs, about 30px across. The packet calls for a LARGE round woody head of tightly packed BROWN ANGULAR fruits — a spiky dark-brown cannonball. So the harvest fails on position, scale, hue and surface, not position alone.

The cross-reference to Mountain Papaya is accurate and I verified it by opening that PNG: same trunk width and taper, same fork at the same height, same up-right amputated stub branch with the same blunt rounded terminus, same radiating pinnate crown. The only differences are that Nipa's crown sits slightly lower and is a warmer/greener hue where Papaya's is paler sea-green, and the fruit swaps Papaya's single yellow ribbed ovoid for Nipa's pale cream cluster. So 'identical down to the same amputated stub branch' is fair — it is one shared chassis with a recoloured crown and a swapped fruit token, not a palm-specific build.

Band FAIL, not POLISH: the defining identity of Nipa is a trunkless mangrove palm whose fronds burst straight out of the mud with a woody cannonball head sitting in the water at their feet. This asset reads as a generic trunked tree-palm with a small pale berry bunch, so 2 of 3 must-reads are absent and the primary one is actively contradicted. Fix requires deleting the trunk and stub branch entirely, planting the frond bases at a mud/water line low in the frame, and replacing the pale pebble bunch with a large dark-brown faceted spiky sphere resting at ground level between the frond bases.

rows.readsAs: a thin fern sprig or a single sparse leaf - an almost empty frame
rows.defect: The pods are missing. This asset is named for its pods and the must-read leads with clusters of long bean-like green pods hanging from the stem; not one pod is drawn. There are no waxy flowers either, no aerial roots gripping anything, and no bark or host to climb - the plant floats free on a wire stem. The leaves are small flat dark slivers in a herringbone ladder, the opposite of thick fleshy waxy oblong leaves alternating up a vining stem. It is also the emptiest render in the batch, mostly background.
rows.fix: Hang two or three hand-like bunches of long slender green bean-pods from the stem joints, fatten the leaves into thick waxy oblongs alternating up a climbing stem, and anchor it with pale aerial roots gripping a bark surface.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but ONE part of the claim is factually wrong and would send a fixer after the wrong thing.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN THE FRAME. 440x440 canvas. The entire subject sits inside a bounding box of x 192-244, y 98-328 -- 53px wide by 231px tall, i.e. 12% of the frame width and an aspect of ~4.4:1 against the packet's specified 1.2. Nothing exists outside that box except a flat dark ground ellipse. Content: one dead-straight rigid vertical stem (mid-green, ~(44,81,33)) running the full height, carrying ~11 OPPOSITE pairs of narrow lanceolate leaflets swept up at ~30 degrees, all the same size, terminating in a bare lower third of stem that plunges into the shadow ellipse. That is a pinnate fern frond / horsetail sprig, full stop.

CORRECTION 1 -- 'Not one pod is drawn' is WRONG as stated. There IS a pod-ish element, and the judge missed it. At approximately x 202-232, y 108-126 (immediately above the topmost leaf pair, crossing the stem) there is a diagonal chain of THREE round lobed blobs running upper-left to lower-right, each with a darker core. Only visible under magnification with brightness boost -- at native size it reads as a smudge or a dead pixel cluster. Measured RGB inside it: (9,11,10), (15,14,10), (26,38,16) against a background of (5,6,12). That is a delta of 3-30 -- functionally invisible. And even when you CAN see it, it is wrong on every axis the packet asks for: dark khaki-brown/near-black instead of green; three short round lobes instead of long slender beans; one single object stuck on the stem instead of a hand-like hanging cluster; and it does not hang -- it lies diagonally across the stem, reading more like an insect or a fungal blight on the plant than a vanilla pod. So the practical conclusion ('the pods do not read') stands, but the fix is NOT 'add pods from nothing' -- it is 'the pod geometry exists and must be rebuilt as 4-6 long slender green beans hanging DOWNWARD in a splayed hand from a node, at 2-3x the current length, in a green light enough to separate from the background.'

CORRECTION 2 -- 'thin DARK herringbone slivers' gets the colour backwards. The leaflets are a fairly LIGHT sage green, measured (76,115,80) and (87,128,92) at blade centres -- lighter and more desaturated than the packet's 'flat mid-green, thick and waxy', not darker. They are the brightest thing in the frame after the stem. Darkening them would make the asset worse. The defect is purely SHAPE and ARRANGEMENT: they are narrow pointed slivers roughly 6:1 long-to-wide, in symmetrical opposite pairs, where the packet calls for thick fleshy OBLONGS (~2.5:1, blunt-tipped) ALTERNATING along the stem. 'Herringbone' is otherwise an accurate description.

CORRECTION 3 -- confirmed accurate: no flowers anywhere (the packet's waxy pale yellow-green flowers are entirely absent), no aerial roots at any node, no host bark or trunk. I verified this by bounding-box scan, not by eye -- there is genuinely nothing in the frame outside the 53x231 box. The lower third of the stem, where aerial roots gripping bark would live, is completely bare.

MUST-READ TALLY. (1) 'clusters of long bean-like green pods hanging from the stem' -- ABSENT as a readable feature (one invisible three-lobed brown lump exists, see Correction 1). (2) 'thick fleshy leaves on a vining stem' -- ABSENT; thin slivers on a rigid non-vining vertical rod. (3) 'aerial roots gripping bark' -- ABSENT entirely, and so is the bark. Zero of three identity must-reads land.

ORGANISM READ. A viewer shown this frame cold names it a fern, a bracken sprig or a horsetail. Nothing about it says epiphytic orchid, and nothing says 'harvested for its pods' -- which, per the packet note, is the ONE thing that distinguishes this species from every other orchid. FAIL is correct.

FIX PRIORITY: (a) rebuild the pod cluster as the dominant feature -- long, slender, green, hanging, multiple; (b) replace sliver leaflets with thick blunt alternating oblongs; (c) add aerial roots at the nodes and a bark surface for the stem to climb; (d) widen the silhouette -- 12% frame width against a 1.2 target aspect is far too sparse.

rows.readsAs: a cream-coloured yucca or flax clump with one thin seed stalk
rows.defect: The huge silver-white feather plume that IS pampas grass is rendered as a 4-bead string about 12px tall on a bare wire - it is smaller than a single leaf blade and reads as a rat-tail, not a plume. Only one stalk, and the foliage is bleached cream-tan rather than the blue-grey green called for, so the clump looks dead.

rows.readsAs: a young palm or tree fern with a walnut stuck to the trunk
rows.defect: Both identifying must-reads are absent. There is no prop-root cone - the forked brown trunk runs straight into the ground shadow. The crown is a flat rosette of pinnate feather fronds with fine side-barbs, i.e. palm/fern fronds, not long undivided sword straps, and there is no spiral screw arrangement anywhere. The fruit is a small striped acorn-sized ovoid tucked against the trunk instead of a large segmented orange ball hanging below the crown.
rows.fix: Rebuild on a screwpine chassis: undivided strap leaves in three visible spiral tiers around the branch tip, a splayed cone of stilt roots lifting the trunk clear of the ground, and a fruit ball at least a third of the crown width with visible polygonal segments.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with corrections. I read the 440x440 PNG at 1x and then re-cropped and magnified three regions (trunk base 5x, crown 3x, fruit 8x) and pixel-scanned the colour masks to measure the parts.

MUST-READ 1 — 'leaves spiralling around the stem in a screw pattern': ABSENT, and the judge is right about why. The crown is ~13 PINNATE COMPOUND fronds: each has a pale central rachis with roughly 20 narrow leaflets per side, all angled forward, with clear dark gaps between the leaflets. These are feather fronds, not the single undivided sword-like strap leaves Pandanus must have — the saw-toothed margin the reference calls for is not a toothed edge on a strap, it is genuinely separate leaflets. Arrangement is a flat, near-planar radial fan (green mask spans x113-326, y54-187 — 213 wide by only 133 tall, i.e. a fan, not a 3D rosette). There is no 3-ranked screw, no spiral tiering, no sense of leaf bases wrapping the stem. Combined with the stiff blue-green colour and the short stout trunk, it reads most strongly as a SAGO PALM / CYCAD, secondarily a young palm — the judge's 'young palm or tree fern' is the right neighbourhood.

MUST-READ 2 — 'cone of thick prop roots holding the trunk off the ground': ABSENT. Confirmed, and it is worse than the judge described. There are zero root forms of any kind — not a small cone, not a partial flare, nothing. But the claim that the trunk 'runs straight into the ground' is wrong: the trunk is a constant-width cylinder (brown span measures 29-30px at y=250, 300, 340 and 370 — no basal flare whatsoever) that TERMINATES IN A ROUNDED STUB at y~386, floating clear above the cast shadow ellipse centred near y~395. A soft dark ellipse sits under the convergence point as a ground shadow. No soil, no crown texture, no flower plume.

CORRECTION 1 - the blades are not 'circles'. They are slightly ovate/egg-shaped, each about 80-90px across, tilted outward so the long axis follows its own stalk, and each carries a faint pale midrib line running from the petiole junction to the tip. What is genuinely absent is everything that makes the blade rhubarb: no cordate base (no basal notch or lobes where the stalk meets the blade), no triangular apex, no wavy margin, and critically no crinkling or puckering anywhere - the outline is a clean smooth bezier arc and the interior is a plain soft gradient with zero surface relief. The stalk colour (vivid red-orange) is also correct per leafColour. The defect on the stalks is narrower than 'strings' implies - they taper from roughly 14px at the crown to 6px at the blade, so they read as slender rather than thread-thin. Stalk run from crown to blade attachment is roughly 175-200px; blade diameter is roughly 80-90px, giving a blade-to-petiole ratio near 0.45. Rhubarb's defining proportion is the opposite: the blade should be as wide as or wider than the petiole is long, and should visually dominate the plant. Must-read 'leaves far larger than expected relative to the plant' = INVERTED, exactly as claimed.

Net: one of three must-reads present (crown fan + red colour), two absent, and the two absent ones are the identity anchors. Strip rhubarb of its enormous puckered blade and nothing in this silhouette says rhubarb - the read is a bunch of long-stemmed lollipops. FAIL upheld.

Fix direction: keep the crown fan and stalk colour exactly as is; roughly triple blade area so each blade is wider than its stalk is long; give the blade a cordate base with a notch straddling the petiole junction and a soft triangular apex; add a wavy/scalloped margin and interior pucker via radiating vein creases with light-dark banding between them; thicken the stalks to read fleshy. With five blades at the required size they will overlap heavily - reduce to three stalks if needed rather than shrinking the blades back down.

A dark ellipse ground shadow sits under the trunk. Nothing else is present.

The claim says the render 'leads with the pale hibiscus flower the packet note explicitly says not to feature' — that is not what is drawn, and the claim contradicts itself two clauses later by calling the same objects 'five magenta daisies'. 2. The claim is CORRECT that the defining harvest is absent. mustRead #3 'fat waxy crimson calyces hugging the stem' has no representative anywhere in the frame: nothing swollen, nothing fleshy, nothing sitting against a stem. The only red mass in the asset is the five flat flower discs, which are held AWAY from the stem on stalks — the opposite of a calyx hugging it. A pixel scan of all 18,943 opaque non-background pixels finds NOT ONE where g exceeds r — the leaf mass is uniformly salmon/terracotta (~rgb 152,80,64 to 168,88,72), the branchlets are olive-brown where r>=g. The reference row demands leafColour 'mid green with red veins and stalks'. Caulerpa lentillifera has slender wiry upright axes so densely covered in stalked spherules that the axis is barely visible; here the axis IS the whole drawing and the spherules are three stickers.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM'S READING: 'spring onions' is not quite right, because there is no swollen white bulb and the base narrows to a point rather than widening. It reads as a clump of eelgrass / a tuft of chives / a leek silhouette. That does not change the verdict.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS: replace the wide blades with 4-7 thin wiry upright axes (2-3px), crowd each with 15-30 small translucent bright-emerald spheres on short visible stalks so the sphere mass dominates the axis, and run a horizontal creeping stolon along the ground from which two or three separate shoot clusters rise. FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: an agave or aloe rosette

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of the three stated causes are mis-measured and one real defect was missed. What is actually on the 440x440 canvas (measured, and inspected at 3x/6x/8x crops):

LEAF MASS — bbox x62-377, y150-353 = 316 x 204 px. Eleven to twelve blades radiating from one basal point in a flat, near-bilaterally-mirrored fan (the left set is close to a mirror of the right set about the stem). Each blade is LANCEOLATE, roughly 3:1 length:width with an acuminate point, carrying a drawn midrib plus a herringbone of pinnate side veins. The judge's word 'narrow spear' overstates it — these are broader than agave spears — and because of the pale top-lit gradient the mass reads less like an agave/aloe rosette than like a white water-lily / chrysanthemum bloom. That correction does not rescue the asset: the identity leaf is a CABBAGE-SIZED OVATE blade, and nothing here is ovate.

MARGINS — CONFIRMED at 6x on the left-hand leaves: every edge is a clean straight-then-arc geometric contour. Zero crinkle, zero undulation, zero lobing, zero serration, not even a wobble in the antialiasing. The single defining must-read, 'huge thick wavy-crinkled ovate leaves with lobed undulating edges', is wholly absent. This is the reason the asset fails and it is where the fix must go: the blade OUTLINE needs deep undulating lobes and a rippled margin, and the blade must be re-proportioned to broad ovate (roughly 1.3:1), not lanceolate.

FLOWER — the judge's '~18px dome cap' is wrong in size and in form. The white element is x200-230, y80-90 = 31 x 11 px, and it is a hollow CRESCENT ARC (a rim), not a filled dome, sitting on a dark slate-grey triangular wedge (rgb 8,11,17 at its centre) that reads as a receptacle. Together they read as a tiny parasol or a pin head. It has no granularity, no individual florets, no branching. At 31 px it is 9.8% of the 316 px leaf-mass width, so 'dome of tiny four-petalled white flowers held in a broad FROTH above the leaves' fails: the fix is a wide, granular, many-floret cloud spanning most of the leaf-mass width, not a bigger cap.

STEM — not a hairline; it is 4-5 px wide (green pixels at x215-220). MISSED BY THE JUDGE: this stem is painted IN FRONT of the whole leaf mass, running unbroken from the flower head at y~90 all the way down to y~353 at the base, so it visually bisects the rosette into two mirror halves. That is an occlusion-order defect independent of the shape problem — the peduncle should emerge from behind/among the leaves, not overlay them.

COLOUR — the judge did not raise it, and it should NOT be changed. Body samples are ~rgb(140,168,168) to rgb(151,181,180), a cool desaturated glaucous grey-green that is roughly on-brief; it only reads white-ish because of the strong top-lit gradient across the upper blades.

MUST-READ TALLY: 'cabbage-sized crinkled blue-grey leaves' FAIL (no crinkle, wrong blade shape; colour ok). 'low spreading dome shape' PARTIAL — the mass is genuinely wider than tall (316 x 204) but its outline is a spiky star, not a dome. 'white flower cloud on top' FAIL (31 px pin). rows.readsAs: a generic fern sprig with a mauve pin on top

Verified at 3x-6x zoom on the flower head, the stem and the base. FAIL stands: all three must-reads are absent and the asset reads as the wrong organism, but two details of the original claim are wrong and should not be carried into the fix.

The fix target is a wide, airy, semi-transparent flat-topped froth of many tiny florets several times wider than this cap, not a de-spiked blob.

rows.readsAs: a single opaque olive leaf blade, or a paper bag

The colour is a dull opaque olive-yellow with no translucency or glow, so the 'vivid translucent grass-green' read is gone too; only the tiny disc holdfast is correct.

UPHELD, but two parts of the original claim need correcting and one must-read the judge ignored is actually present.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a single tall goblet/funnel-shaped opaque blade on the dark canvas. It rises from a narrow stipe at the base (~x210-235) and flares smoothly outward to a maximum width of ~123px at the very top, where it is terminated by a dead-flat horizontal cut. Three to four pale hairline strokes run the length of the blade and converge at the base, reading unmistakably as a midrib plus lateral veins. A large dark cast-shadow ellipse sits on the ground plane, and inside it a small pale-green ellipse (~x200-250, y~345-356) sits where the stipe meets the ground.

MUST-READ 1 - paper-thin translucent green sheets: ABSENT. Sampled fill is fully opaque (alpha 255 everywhere) and runs rgb(144,155,85) at the top of the blade, (133,144,79) mid, (91,98,54) at y=240, (48,52,30) at y=340. That is a dull yellow-olive/khaki with R approximately equal to G, darkening to near-black toward the base under a heavy vertical shading ramp. The reference calls for 'vivid translucent grass-green, almost glowing'. The strong opaque top-lit-to-dark-bottom gradient is exactly what makes it read as a thick solid object rather than a membrane. Judge is CORRECT here.

MUST-READ 2 - ruffled lettuce-like frilled margins: ABSENT, and I verified this by measurement rather than by eye. Scanning left/right silhouette extents every 6px from y=78 to y=258 gives a perfectly monotonic profile with zero oscillation: L goes 158,159,160,162,163,163,163,163,163,163,163,163,163,163,164,165,167,168,170,172,175,178,181,184,187,190,193,196,199,201,204 and R mirrors it. A frilled margin would show sawtooth swings of 5-15px; this shows +/-1px of anti-aliasing noise in the straight section and then a smooth continuous taper. There is not a single crenulation, lobe or wave anywhere on either edge. Judge is CORRECT that the ruffle is absent.

CORRECTION 1 to the claim - 'both margins are dead-straight lines' is only half true. The margins are near-vertical and straight ONLY in the upper region (y=96 to y=156, where L holds at 163 and R at 277). Below y~160 both margins curve smoothly and continuously inward in a long concave taper down to the stipe. The correct description of the defect is 'perfectly smooth, unbroken vector-like edges with zero high-frequency detail', not 'straight lines'. A fix that merely bends the outline will not help; the edge needs a high-frequency wavy/lobed margin.

CORRECTION 2 to the claim - the judge said nothing about the veins, but the 3-4 pale converging hairlines are an independent identity-breaking defect and arguably the biggest one after the missing ruffle. The reference explicitly says 'no true leaves'; sea lettuce is a two-cell-thick membrane with NO midrib and NO venation. Drawing a midrib and laterals is what actively converts this into 'a single leaf blade'. Those strokes must be deleted, not just recoloured.

CORRECTION 3 to the claim - MUST-READ 3, the tiny disc holdfast at the base, IS PRESENT and readable. Zooming the base at 6x shows a distinct small pale-green ellipse seated under the stipe, clearly separate from the dark ground shadow. The judge's write-up implies nothing of the identity survives; one third of it does, and a fix pass should keep it.

CONFIRMED - the top is genuinely a flat horizontal clip. The blade first appears at y=77-78 spanning x=158 to x=281 with squared corners and no taper into it; at 5x it is a razor-straight horizontal terminus. It reads as the render being cut off by a bounding box, not as an organic apex.

BAND: FAIL stands. Two of three must-reads are absent, the single missing one (the frilled margin) is the entire visual identity of the organism, the palette is olive rather than glowing grass-green, and added false venation pushes the silhouette further toward a generic leaf. Fix priority: (1) rebuild both margins with deep irregular lettuce frills and let a few lobes fold/overlap, (2) delete the midrib/vein strokes, (3) reprofile to a vivid light grass-green with a much shallower value ramp and lighter overlap tinting to sell translucency, (4) terminate the top with ruffled lobes instead of a straight cut, (5) keep the existing base holdfast disc.

rows.readsAs: a broken render — a succulent rosette with a flower floating detached in the sky above it
rows.defect: The pink star flower is stranded in empty space roughly 80px above the plant with no stem, pedicel or contact of any kind between them; it reads as a stray sprite, not a flower in a leaf axil. Beneath it the plant is an upright bouquet of five fat rounded pale paddles, not a low mat sprawling flat and rooting at the nodes; there are no opposite pairs, no visible red-purple stems, and no narrow leaves.
rows.fix: Attach the flower to the plant — tuck it into an actual leaf axil against a stem — and rebuild the body as a horizontal sprawling mat of reddish stems running out sideways with plump narrow leaves in opposite pairs along them.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, and the floating-flower claim is confirmed at the pixel level rather than merely by eye. Measured on the 440x440 PNG: the pink flower occupies bbox x[206,234] y[97,120] (a 28x24px 6-petal star, mid-pink petals rgb 216,144,184 around a pale yellow disc rgb 243,230,168 — on its own it is the one genuinely well-drawn element). The green body occupies bbox x[128,312] y[189,310]. I ran a per-row median-subtracted scan of the intervening band (x150-290, y118-192) specifically to hunt for a faint stem the other judge might have missed: from y=122 through y=188 the maximum deviation from each row's own median is 3-5/255, i.e. pure vignette noise. There is NO stem, thread, hair, or connector of any kind. CORRECTION to their figure: the empty gap is 68px, not ~80px — the substance of the claim is right, the number is slightly overstated.

The body is confirmed as five broad ovate paddles radiating up-and-outward from a single point that tapers to a wedge and terminates at y=310 (rows 298-310 narrow 112px -> 22px, then nothing). That is a basal rosette / fan, i.e. a lotus- or aloe-like crown, not a mat. PARTIAL CORRECTION to their wording: they call it 'upright', but the overall silhouette is actually wider than tall — 185w x 122h, ratio 1.52. It is the individual blades that point upward. That still misses the packet's aspect: 2.4 is mandated (a low, wide, sprawling mat) and 1.52 is far too tall and compact.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT THE OTHER JUDGE UNDERSTATED: they wrote 'reddish nodes' as if only the nodes were missing. I ran a red-channel census over every non-background pixel (r > g+18 and r > 60): 291 such pixels exist and their bounding box is x[206,234] y[97,120] — exactly and only the flower. There is not one red-purple pixel anywhere else in the image. The packet's leafColour is 'mid green with red-purple stems', and no stem of ANY colour is drawn at all — the paddles simply fuse into each other at the base. So the failure is not just missing nodes, it is a total absence of the stem structure the species is built on. The leaf colour itself is also off: a pale desaturated sage/mint (sampled rgb 153,190,175 / 159,197,181 / 144,180,166) rather than mid green.

Must-read scoring: (1) 'low mat sprawling flat and rooting at the nodes' — ABSENT; upright fan converging to one basal point, zero nodes, zero roots, zero sprawl. (2) 'plump narrow succulent leaves' — HALF PRESENT; the blades read fleshy and thick, but they are broad ovate paddles roughly 2:1 length-to-width where sea purslane needs narrow oblong fingers nearer 4-5:1, and they are not in opposite pairs. (3) 'pink star flower tucked against the stem' — the star flower is drawn and legible, which is real credit, but it cannot be 'tucked against the stem' when no stem exists and it sits 68px away in open void.

One further flaw neither of us should let through: each paddle carries sharp straight-line angular vein strokes (visible as L- and V-shaped segments in the 3x crop) that read as cracks or fractures in the blade. Venation of that kind is wrong for a fleshy succulent leaf regardless of the other issues.

Two of three must-reads are absent and the asset reads as a generic succulent rosette with a detached flower decal, not as Sea Purslane. FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond with one mauve daisy stuck on the end
rows.defect: This is the Sea Lavender image with a daisy swapped for the dome. Every must-read fails: the stem is ramrod-straight and unbranched, not sprawling and zigzag; the leaves are smooth pointed lances with entire margins, not thick pinnately lobed fleshy leaves with rounded lobes; there is one radial many-rayed daisy where the reference needs four-petalled cross-shaped flowers; and the fat two-jointed corky seed pods, which are half the identity, are nowhere in the image.
rows.fix: Kink the stem into a visible zigzag with alternating side branches sprawling low and wide, cut deep rounded lobes into each fleshy leaf, and hang several fat two-segment corky pods off the upper stem next to four-petalled lilac crosses.
rows.verifyWhy: I looked at the full 440px render and then re-cropped and 5-6x upscaled the flower head, the mid-stem leaf zone, and the stem base, and I measured the plant bbox numerically. The FAIL stands: all three mustReads (fleshy lobed leaves / sprawling zigzag branching over sand / lilac cross-shaped flowers with jointed pods) are absent. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS: one perfectly vertical, unbranched olive stem running from a dark ground-shadow ellipse to the apex; roughly 11 OPPOSITE PAIRS of entire-margined, blunt-tipped elliptic blades in pale sage-grey-green, each with a drawn pinnate midrib-plus-side-vein pattern and faint pale speckling; and a single terminal flower head. Bare stem for ~60px between the shadow and the lowest leaf pair; nothing else anywhere in frame. CORRECTIONS AND SHARPENINGS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM: (1) 'The Sea Lavender image with a daisy swapped for the dome' is right about the chassis but overstated as an image identity. I opened Sea_Lavender.png side by side - it is unmistakably the same generic straight-stem/paired-frond/shadow-ellipse generator, but with different leaf parameters: Sea Lavender's leaflets are narrow dark spearheads with no speckle and a 53px-wide bbox, Sea Rocket's are broader, paler, veined and speckled with a 79px bbox. Say 'same chassis, re-parameterised leaf' rather than 'same image'. (2) The flower is worse than 'a many-rayed daisy'. At 6x it is a complete Asteraceae capitulum: about 12 narrow pale-lilac ray florets radiating from a large solid gold-brown central DISC that fills roughly 40% of the head diameter. The disc is the loudest wrong-family signal - Brassicaceae has no disc at all. It is also a SINGLE terminal head, where sea rocket carries a raceme of many small four-petalled crosses up the stem. (3) 'smooth entire-margined lances' is correct on margin but slightly off on shape and misses a second error: the blades are broader than lances (elliptic, rounded tips), they read as thin and leafy rather than thick and succulent, AND they are arranged OPPOSITE in pairs when the brief specifies ALTERNATE. The pinnate structure exists only at the whole-plant level (the entire plant is one feather), which is a garbled rendering of 'pinnately lobed leaf' - the lobing belongs INSIDE each leaf, as rounded fleshy lobes, not as separate leaflets on the main axis. (4) 'fat two-jointed corky pods absent entirely' is confirmed - I checked the base crop and the full stem length, there is no fruit, no pod, no silicle of any kind, and no sand/beach substrate either, only the generic dark ellipse shadow shared with every other card in this batch. (5) DEFECT THE JUDGE DID NOT NAME: aspect. The packet asks for 1.6 (wider than tall, a low sprawling beach herb). Measured non-background bbox is 79 x 254 px = 0.31 w/h, about 5x too narrow. This is a real miss, not a convention mismatch - Sesame in the same batch asks 0.4 and measures 0.46, so the pipeline can honour aspect. The 0.31 figure is the numeric form of the missing sprawl. FIX DIRECTION: abandon the single-stem frond chassis for this species entirely - build a low, wide, multi-branched zigzag mat (target w/h ~1.6) of thick blue-green leaves each cut into 3-5 rounded fleshy lobes along its own midrib, alternate at the kinked nodes; replace the capitulum with several small four-petalled lilac-white crosses in a short raceme; and add the diagnostic fat two-segment corky pods (a squat lower joint with a larger beaked upper joint) on the stem below the flowers. Sand-toned ground would help but is secondary to those three.

rows.readsAs: a multi-stemmed berry shrub
rows.defect: The overall read is right — slim multi-stemmed upright trunks, small oval leaves, purple berry clusters at the shoot tips — and it is the only asset in the batch with its own structure. But the trunks are warm orange-brown rather than slim grey; the berries are plain spheres with no five-pointed starry crown scar at the tip; and the narrow strap-petalled white flowers are entirely absent, so two of the three must-reads are unreadable at this size.

rows.readsAs: a small plain fern sprig — no identifiable crop

What remains is the shared ladder stamp shrunk to about 40% of the frame: a bare straight stem with nine plain lance leaflets and absolutely nothing else, floating small in a large empty field.

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but the stated cause is partly wrong and the fix must be aimed differently.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS (440x440; verified at 1x, at 4x nearest-neighbour crops, and at a 2.6x global brightness lift to rule out dim-but-present features):

1. A single dead-straight vertical stem, flat mid-green, ~4px wide, no taper, no node swelling, no texture. It runs y~110 to y~315 and sits on a flat elliptical drop-shadow. Plant bbox is roughly 110px wide x 205px tall, i.e. ~25% of frame width and ~47% of frame height — the judge's "~40% of the frame" understates the height slightly but the scale complaint is fair: the subject is small and centred with a large dead margin.

2. CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM — leaflet count is wrong. There are FOURTEEN leaflets in SEVEN strictly OPPOSITE pairs, not "nine". Every one is a scalloped column that is WIDEST AT ITS FLAT TOP and steps down through ~5 narrowing scale rows to a NARROWER ROUNDED BOTTOM. Narrow end DOWN = pendulous. I tried to refute this and could not. Zoomed 7x-8x on the apex, the fan and the base, and ran a colour scan over the whole 440x440 canvas.

SPADIX — claim CONFIRMED, and it is worse than stated. A pixel scan for pale khaki/cream (the only non-green hue present) returns exactly ONE mass in the entire image: 7px wide x 38px tall, bbox x236-242 / y122-159. That is a single perfectly vertical column, aspect 1:5.4, sitting at the dead apex of the tallest stem and TERMINATING it. At 7x it resolves as ~8 stacked pale-tan bead lobes with visibly scalloped left/right edges — a plantain / timothy-grass / bottlebrush catkin. Reference demands 'a stubby green finger (spadix) angled out sideways from the flat stem' and the note explicitly says 'not from the tip.' Every one of the four properties is inverted: it is thin not stubby, tan-cream not green, vertical not angled, and apical not partway up. There is no second spadix hidden lower in the tuft — the colour scan proves it, and the base crop confirms it.

STEM — claim CONFIRMED. The stalk under the spike is a uniform-width round green rod ~5-6px, drawn identically to the leaf blades. There is no flattened scape, no leaf-like spathe continuing past the spadix (the stem simply ends in the beads), and therefore nothing for a lateral spadix to jut FROM. This is the structural root cause: the generator built a grass culm topped by an inflorescence, which is the wrong architecture entirely.

CRIMPED MARGIN — claim is directionally right but the stated cause is WRONG and this matters for the fix. The judge says 'no crimped leaf margin.' In fact a crimp WAS attempted, just in the wrong geometry: short bright-green rectangles are stamped across the blades. They are strictly axis-aligned HORIZONTAL bars regardless of blade angle, so on the diagonal and arching blades they cross at the wrong angle and overhang both edges — they read as ladder rungs / bamboo nodes, not as an undulating edge. Worse, several of these dashes float completely detached in empty background (clearly visible above and left of the tuft in the fan crop) — stray marks with no leaf under them. So the fix is not 'add crimping'; it is 'stop stamping perpendicular bars and displace the blade OUTLINE into a wave, and clip the marks to the blade.'

LEAF FORM — an additional must-read failure the judge did not name. 'Fan of upright sword leaves' is not met. The blades are constant-width tubes with ROUNDED blunt tips, no taper to a point, no midrib (reference asks for an off-centre midrib), and they arch outward and downward almost to horizontal like a spider plant or fountain grass. Non-background bbox is 256w x 185h, aspect 1.38 wide — the packet specifies aspect 0.4, i.e. tall and narrow. The silhouette is a low spreading fountain, not an upright emergent iris stand. All blades converge to a single point at the ground with no rhizome, no swollen fan base, and no planar (two-ranked) arrangement.

The judge's summary 'reads as a generic grass tuft' is fair but slightly imprecise: it reads specifically as an arching ornamental grass or spider plant topped by a timothy/plantain seed head. Nothing in the drawing says Acorus. Identity absent on three of three must-reads plus the aspect. FAIL stands.

It has no lateral spread, no pinnate rhythm and no fan flare; the outer edge is a pair of smooth converging curves with only the rounded rod-ends breaking the top edge.

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then cropped and nearest-neighbour zoomed the head to 18x, and sampled raw pixels. FAIL stands, but two parts of the stated cause are wrong and the fix should be made against what is actually there.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN. A fountain of ~20 flat, tapering, arching blades springing from one ground point, each with a painted pale midrib highlight, spanning roughly x140-x325 and y150-y310; a black elliptical contact shadow at the base; one bare unbranched stalk running up the centre of the tuft and continuing clear of it to y~132; and at the top, a head occupying only about 34px wide x 22px tall.

MUSTREAD 1 - 'a bare round stalk topped with a ball of tiny flowers'. HALF PRESENT. The bare leafless stalk is genuinely there and is clean and readable - credit that, do not redraw it. The ball of tiny flowers is ABSENT. CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM: it is not a 'flat disc' and not a 'lozenge'. It is a CRESCENT - a shallow arc, thickest at the crown, tapering to two down-curved points at left and right, like a tiny opened parasol or a mushroom cap - sitting over a separate dark-olive DOWNWARD-POINTING CHEVRON/WEDGE (sampled RGB 20,32,27) whose apex meets the stalk. The judge did not mention that dark wedge at all. Together the two shapes read as a small mushroom on a stem, not as any allium. A horizontal pixel scan across the crescent at y=122 returns the identical value RGB(208,192,224) for 18 consecutive pixels with only 2px of antialias at each end: it is one flat fill with no gradient, no beading, no radiating pedicels, no floret separations, no globe shading. There is no sphere and nothing granular anywhere in the head.

MUSTREAD 2 - 'grassy tubular leaves at the base'. PARTIAL, and this is the axis that collapses onion into garlic. A grassy tuft is present, but the blades are drawn FLAT with a specular midrib stripe, moderately broad, and are the same blade the Wild Garlic render uses. The batch-013 packet is explicit about this: Wild Garlic's row says 'broad flat pointed elliptic blades' with the note 'interpreted as ramsons - broad flat leaves, NOT the narrow tubular leaves of chives or onion', while Wild Onion's row asks for 'narrow tubular or channelled leaves'. Both renders got the same broad flat blade, so the one leaf trait written specifically to separate the two species is not honoured on either. No channelling, no round cross-section, no tube.

MUSTREAD 3 - 'a papery membrane bursting under the flower head'. ABSENT, and the judge is right on this one. The only candidate is the dark-olive chevron under the crescent, but it is leaf-green and fully opaque, it reads as the shaded underside of the cap rather than a pale tan sheath, and it shows no split, no tearing, no curled-back papery flaps. Even read as charitably as possible it does not communicate a bursting spathe.

CORRECTIONS TO THE JUDGE'S WORDING. (a) 'smooth white lozenge' is wrong on colour: the onion head samples RGB(208,192,224), a clear pale LILAC, while the Wild Garlic head samples RGB(224,220,232), near-white. That lilac tint is in fact the single most correct thing in the render, since the packet asks for pink-white flowers - keep the hue, replace the geometry. (b) 'nothing distinguishes it from the garlic beside it' is very nearly right but slightly overstated: the two differ by that head tint and by a marginally greyer, less saturated leaf green (onion leaf RGB 88,126,80 vs garlic 80,131,64, so the requested grey-green is faintly honoured). Everything structural - tuft silhouette, blade shape, midrib treatment, ground shadow, stalk, head geometry - is the same chassis with a hue swap. For contrast, the sibling Wild Chive in the same folder did get a distinct head (a lilac ray-daisy with a brown centre - also botanically wrong for an allium, but at least not a duplicate), which proves the head shape is a per-species parameter that was simply never set for onion or garlic. (c) 'featureless flat disc' understates it: it is featureless, but as a crescent, and the missing dark wedge is part of why it misreads as a mushroom.

BAND. Two of the three must-reads (the ball of tiny flowers; the bursting papery membrane) are absent, the third is only half met, and the head positively misreads as a different organism. That is a FAIL, not a POLISH. FIX ORDER: (1) replace the crescent+wedge with an actual spherical umbel - a hemisphere-to-globe of many small individual six-tepal florets on short radiating pedicels, silhouette scalloped not smooth, keeping the RGB(208,192,224) lilac and adding deeper pink at the shaded lower florets; (2) add a pale papery spathe split into two or three recurved tan flaps immediately under that globe; (3) narrow the leaves to round-section tubes with a rim highlight and a soft dark channel line so they stop being the ramsons blade; (4) enlarge the head - at 34px on a 440px canvas it is too small to carry the identity even once redrawn.

What is true is that there is no support (no pole, stalk, twig or neighbouring stem), the stem is a free-floating open S-curve rather than a helix wrapping anything, and the curls sit beside the stem rather than gripping. WHAT I SAW. 440x440 render. I measured silhouette area and tube width against a radial background model (the vignette is identical across all nine PNGs, so the model is fair to the dark King Snake). Vine silhouette area = 27,284 px; head/neck tube width, sampled as the maximum vertical run at 6px steps back from the snout tip, plateaus at 40-41 px. Across the batch: Water 27,950 / VINE 27,284 / Garter 26,029 / Racer 24,678 / Rat 24,202 / Whip 23,330 / Grass 23,081 / Tree 18,280 / King 16,481. Neck-tube plateau: VINE 41 / Water 39 / Whip 39 / Rat 37 / Grass 35 / Garter 37 / Racer 31 / Tree 27 / King 24. The aspect-12 species is the FATTEST-tubed and second-largest-silhouette snake in a nine-member family, and the aspect-4 King Snake is the THINNEST. So the cue is not flattened, it is reversed.

CORRECTION 1 (the judge's central factual claim is false). They wrote that Vine 'is rendered at exactly the same thickness as the aspect-4 King Snake.' It is not. Vine's tube is roughly 70% wider than King's (41 px vs 24 px at the neck) and its silhouette carries 65% more ink (27,284 vs 16,481). A stacked same-scale crop of Vine/Tree/King makes this unmistakable: Vine's tube is visibly the fattest of the three and King's the slimmest — Vine's coil has a small pinched inner hole precisely because the tube is so thick. The defect is therefore worse than reported, and the fix is not 'differentiate Vine from King'; it is 'shrink Vine's tube by roughly 3-4x', because Vine currently sits at the wrong END of the family's thickness range.

CORRECTION 2. 'It is visually the Tree Snake in a different green' is only half true. Same chassis, yes: identical coil path and crossover, identical rib-hatch texture, identical head ellipse, identical white-oval-plus-slit eye, identical forked tongue at the identical exit point. But it is not a recolor — Vine is a SCALED-UP Tree Snake: 49% more silhouette area (27,284 vs 18,280), 50% wider neck tube (41 vs 27), larger bbox (294x157 vs 267x130). The hues are also genuinely distinct (Vine body samples (127,178,60), Tree (48,138,64)). Calling it 'the Tree Snake in a different green' understates the problem: the batch note calls the TREE snake 'startlingly thin, pencil-width', and the Vine Snake — which is supposed to be thinner still — is drawn half again fatter than it.

MUST-READ 2 — 'long pointed dart-shaped snout': ABSENT, confirmed at 7x zoom. The head is the family's generic smooth ovoid, roughly 41 px wide over about 48 px of length before it merges into the coil — call it 1.2:1, a blunt egg. There is no elongated rostral, no lance, no dart taper; the anterior end simply rounds off where the tongue exits. Aggravating detail the judge missed: Vine's headFrac spec is 0.04, the SMALLEST in the batch, yet its head measures the LARGEST of the nine (41 px vs King 24, Tree 27, Racer 31). Head size is scaling with body scale, not with headFrac.

MUST-READ 3 — 'horizontal keyhole-shaped pupils': ABSENT. Vine's pupil measures 2 px wide x 8 px tall (w/h 0.25) — a hard vertical slit — inside a 10x10 white sclera.

CORRECTION 3. The judge called this 'the same vertical slit used family-wide.' Not family-wide. Measured pupils in this batch: Vine 2x8, Tree 2x9, Garter 2x9, Grass 2x9, Whip 3x9, Water 3x8 are vertical slits; but King is 10x10 and Rat Snake is 10x11 — fully ROUND — and Racer is 6x11, intermediate. The renderer therefore already supports at least round and slit pupils; what it lacks is a horizontal/keyhole variant. That matters because the fix is a new pupil mode, not a per-species override of an assumed-global constant.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT (unreported by either pass). Posture is inert. Vine's spec posture is 'crawling', as are Garter, Grass, King, Racer and Whip; only Rat, Tree and Water are 'coiled'. All nine render as the identical closed coil. Nothing in this image reads as crawling, and no S-curve or draped-loop posture exists in the family.

The foot gold is the byte-identical palette used for the bill (RGB 224,177,60 and 201,162,79). This is the defining booby signature and it is simply not drawn.

2) MUST-READ 'long tapered dagger bill running straight into the forehead' -- HALF present, and the judge's description of it is FLATLY WRONG. The bill is not 'a short blunt cone'. It measures 59px long (x100-159) on a 440px canvas, tapering from 10px deep at the base to a single-pixel point, and it is roughly 1.3x the skull diameter. That is a genuine long tapered dagger and it should NOT be on the fix list as 'too short'. What actually fails is the second half of the must-read: the bill does not run straight into the forehead. The skull is a perfect sphere and the bill is pinned onto it with a visible dorsal STEP -- the sphere bulges up and back above the bill's top line. A booby/gannet skull is one continuous wedge from bill tip to nape; this is ball-on-a-stick. Secondary: the bill is saturated egg-yolk gold rather than the pale horn/bluish-grey of a booby.

3) MUST-READ 'forward-set eyes flanking the bill giving a binocular stare' -- ABSENT. Confirmed. One black disc with a white catchlight sits high on the SIDE of the sphere, roughly a head-radius behind and above the bill base, in strict lateral profile. No second eye, no forward convergence toward the bill, no dark facial mask, and the packet asks for 'prominent' eyes -- the single eye is small relative to the sphere. The bird gives a side-on pigeon glance, not the booby's face-on stare.

4) 'VISUALLY THE SAME BIRD AS GANNET' -- CORRECT, and now quantified. Booby vs Gannet: bill length 59px vs 57px; bill and foot palettes byte-identical (224,177,60 / 201,162,79); head sphere 99x71 vs 102x73; foot bbox within 2px on both axes (196-243 vs 194-244); identical egg body, identical grey comma wing band, identical wedge tail, identical shadow. A full-image compare shows only ~2.5% of pixels differing beyond a perceptual threshold, and that delta is a sub-pixel scale/offset of the same drawing, not a species difference. VERDICT: the single feature that IS the booby (blue or red webbed feet) is absent, the binocular forward-eye read is absent, and the head/bill read is only half satisfied. One of three must-reads partially present. FAIL stands.

Do NOT lengthen the bill -- it is already correctly long.
