Verified at 3x/6x crops of the 440x440 master. The FAIL stands — all three must-reads are missing — but two of the stated causes are wrong and the fix brief needs correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS: a near-spherical dark dome half-submerged in water, with three concentric pale ripple ellipses and a blue submerged-body reflection under it, a thin dark neck tube rising from the front-left of the dome, a round head with a pale rim-light arc over the crown, a small black eye with a single white specular dot, and a short saturated yellow-orange bill.

MUST-READ 1 — 'hook-tipped bill on a long snaky neck': FAILS, but NOT for the reason given. The bill is NOT straight. At 12x it is a quadrilateral wedge whose culmen slopes slightly down-forward and whose gonys sweeps up steeply, so the tip is a blunt point sitting BELOW the line of the gape — there is a genuine downward droop drawn in. What is absent is the cormorant hook proper: no mandible split, no terminal nail overhanging the lower jaw, and the bill is far too SHORT and too DEEP (roughly 0.6 head-diameters long and nearly half as deep as it is long) to read as the long slender fish-hook bill of a cormorant. It reads as a stubby parrot-ish or duck-ish beak. It is also uniformly yellow across the whole bill, where a cormorant is grey-horn bill with yellow confined to the gape/facial skin. The NECK is also mischaracterised: it is thin, not thick — about 14px wide against a ~55px head, so noticeably slender. Its real defect is that it is SHORT (~50px, under one head-length) and RIGID: a single straight tube with one slight forward lean, no S-kink, no sinuosity. So 'short thick tube' should be 'short, thin, ramrod-straight tube with no S-curve'.

MUST-READ 2 — 'wings held open to dry in a heraldic pose': FAILS, and this is the killer. The identity pose is entirely absent. Correction to the claim: there IS wing information drawn — a dark crescent band arcs across the dome, reading as a folded wing over the flank — so it is not that wings were omitted, it is that they are drawn CLOSED, i.e. the exact opposite of the required open heraldic spread. No open wing breaks the silhouette anywhere; the outer contour is one unbroken convex arc from crown to waterline.

MUST-READ 3 — 'low-slung body with a stiff wedge tail': FAILS as stated. There is no tail of any kind. The rear of the body is a smooth circular arc that runs straight down into the waterline with zero projection, notch or wedge. The body is a ball, not low-slung: bird-only bounds are ~186 x 127px, aspect ~1.45, against the spec's aspect 2.8. headFrac measures ~0.30 against a spec of 0.20.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT THE ORIGINAL JUDGE DID NOT NAME: the posture is wrong at the spec level. The row calls for posture 'upright' (the rock-perched drying stance), but the asset is drawn SWIMMING — floating in water with ripple rings and a submerged reflection. That is the Pelican row's posture from the same packet, which suggests a pose-assignment slip rather than only a drawing miss. Fixing the pose to upright-on-a-perch is a prerequisite for must-reads 2 and 3 to be drawable at all.

The judge's gestalt call is correct: with a round black floating body, a rim-lit round head and a short yellow bill, this reads as a coot, grebe or dark duck on a pond, not a cormorant.

rows.readsAs: a dark pigeon or grouse standing on the ground
rows.defect: The asset is not flying — it sits on the family egg body over a cast ground shadow with the two yellow chicken feet visible underneath. The deeply forked scissor tail is absent; the rear is a fan of straight dark streaks with no fork. The wings are not long crooked M-shapes, they are the chassis crescent smeared sideways and do not leave the body as separate airfoils. There is no hooked bill and no scarlet throat pouch of any kind.
rows.fix: Rebuild it airborne with no feet and no ground shadow: two very long angular M-kinked wings spanning the full canvas width and a hard deep V-fork in the tail, plus a scarlet inflated pouch under the chin.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG raw, then re-decoded it and re-rendered at 2x with a 0.42 gamma lift (the asset is near-black on a near-black field, so the first read understates it), plus 5x-10x crops of the head, the feet, the rear of the body, and both wing tips. FAIL stands, but three of the stated causes need correcting.

CONFIRMED, and it is the fatal one: THIS BIRD IS ON THE GROUND, and the reference row says posture: flying. Two pale-yellow three-toed feet sit at roughly x150-185, y262-272, splayed toes pointing left, drawn OVER a dark elliptical cast ground shadow centred about (175,268) that spans x120-235. The bottom of the body ellipse rests on that shadow. There is no airborne cue anywhere: no tilt, no lift, no motion streaks, nothing under the wings. Nothing in the image is flying.

CONFIRMED: the body is the family egg chassis. Side-by-side with Cormorant.png from the same packet, it is the same fat horizontal ovoid with the same speckled fill, the same featureless grey ball head, and the same yellow bill primitive. Only the colour, the water plane and the neck length differ. The Frigatebird is that chassis in grey with two wings pinned out.

CONFIRMED: no scarlet throat pouch. There is no red or scarlet pixel anywhere in the file. The throat is the same flat mid-grey as the head. Zero gular sac, inflated or otherwise.

CONFIRMED but MIS-DESCRIBED: no deeply forked scissor tail. Correct that it is absent, but it is NOT 'a fan of straight streaks'. The two streaked structures are the WINGS, one left one right (see next paragraph). Behind the body, at roughly x225-260 y210-235, there is a blunt ROUNDED pale-grey lobe overlapping the rear of the ovoid, with one thin dark spike angling down-right below it. That is the whole of the tail apparatus: a rounded stub, not a fan, and not remotely forked. A fix must ADD a long deep V-scissor, not merely re-shape existing streaks.

CONFIRMED: no crooked M-wings. Both wings are straight tapering blades with 4-6 parallel dark feather-separation streaks running lengthwise. The right one leaves the shoulder near x235 and runs almost dead horizontal to a point at x400, y243; the left mirrors it from x150 down to a point at x30, y252. Total span is genuinely long (~370px of a 440px canvas), so 'long' is satisfied — but there is no elbow, no wrist crook and no downward-then-upward angle change anywhere along either blade. They are flat glider paddles. The M is absent, not merely shallow.

WRONG, and this part of the claim should not be actioned as written: 'no hooked bill'. There IS a hook. The yellow bill at roughly x88-118, y168-186 is a wedge whose tip turns DOWN into a small hook with a visible notch on the underside. The real defect is different and worse: that exact hooked-wedge bill, same shape, same yellow, is also on the Cormorant in this packet, so it is the family's stock bill primitive and carries no Frigatebird identity. It is also far too short and blunt — a frigatebird bill is long, slender and deeply decurved at the tip, roughly the length of the head; this one is well under half that. So: don't add a hook, LENGTHEN and slim the bill so the hook stops reading as the shared family stub.

On the 'dark pigeon or grouse' read: close but I would sharpen it. Brightened, it reads as a mid-grey egg-bodied DOVE or pigeon with two straight paddle wings held stiffly out to the sides while standing. The nearest real-world match is a cormorant spreading its wings to dry — which is to say, the asset lands on a DIFFERENT species' must-read from inside its own packet.

What is present and readable: a bird, a bill with an eye, a long total wingspan, feather streaking. What a Frigatebird needs and does not have: flight, the forked scissor tail, the M-crooked wings, the long slender bill, the scarlet pouch. Four of five identity cues absent and the required posture inverted. FAIL is correct.

rows.readsAs: a generic white seabird or gull chick
rows.defect: The overall white body with a grey wing and a pointed pale bill is roughly in the right zone, but all three must-reads are missing: the head is pure white with no buff-yellow wash, there is no dark facial mask or dark bare skin around the eye and bill base, and the wingtip is mid-grey rather than jet black. The bill is also too short and too blunt to read as a plunge-diving dagger.
rows.fix: Wash the whole head and nape buff-yellow, ink a black mask around the eye and gape line, and hard-cut the outer third of the wing to true black.

rows.readsAs: a grey-white gull or duckling standing on a shadow
rows.defect: The enormous bill and slung throat pouch — the entire identity — are absent; the bill is the family's short yellow cone, shorter than the head. The bird is standing on two long visible legs over a ground shadow rather than swimming, and the legs are the family's thin sticks, not the very short heavy set called for. The neck is not long and is not kinked back onto the shoulders; the head sits directly on the egg body. Body is the same chassis as Booby and Gannet in a slightly dirtier grey.
rows.fix: Give it a bill at least twice head-length with a deep sagging elastic pouch hanging beneath, and set it low on the waterline with the neck folded back in an S onto the shoulders and the legs hidden.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD as FAIL, but two of the three stated causes are measurably wrong and must not be fixed against.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS (440x440; creature bbox x84-348, y130-298, so 265x169). A pale grey-white egg torso with a scallop/feather noise fill, a separate sphere skull sitting on top-left of the egg, one grey crescent 'wing scoop' arcing across the torso, a grey wedge tail spiking off to the right (out to x=348), two thin yellow stick legs with splayed toes, and a hard black cast-shadow ellipse on the ground beneath the feet. Eye is a single black dot with a white catchlight, forward on the skull. Background is flat navy, nothing else in frame.

MUST-READ 1 - 'enormous bill with a stretchy throat pouch slung beneath': the POUCH IS GENUINELY ABSENT. At 4x magnification the bill is one flat opaque yellow-orange wedge, no lower-mandible division, no gular skin, no sag, no bulge, nothing hanging below the jawline - the throat under the bill is just the plain grey neck cylinder running down into the body. This alone is the whole identity of the organism and it is not drawn. HOWEVER the judge's description 'the family's short yellow cone, shorter than the head' is FALSE on measurement: the yellow bill bbox is x84-148 (65px), the free projection past the skull front edge is ~59px, and the skull is only ~48px across - so the bill is ~1.2-1.35x head diameter, i.e. LONGER than the head, not shorter. It is also NOT the family's bill shape: at 26px max depth it is a thick blunt wedge, visibly fatter and blunter than the thin needle daggers on Booby.png and Gannet.png, which I opened side by side. So the bill was given a species-specific tweak; it just stops at roughly heron/tern scale. The fix is not 'lengthen the family cone' - it is REPLACE the wedge with a true pelican bill: ~2.5-3x head length, a straight narrow upper mandible with a nail hook at the tip, and a deep distensible pouch slung under the full length of the lower mandible, drawn as a separate soft form that hangs below the jaw line and swells toward the throat.

MUST-READ 2 - 'heavy body on very short legs': PARTIALLY present and the judge got this backwards. The legs are NOT 'long' - the yellow leg bbox is y274-297, i.e. only 24px of exposed leg against a 169px creature height (~14%), which is genuinely short. The real defect here is that legs, feet and toes are visible AT ALL. The reference posture is 'swimming'; this asset is a standing biped on dry ground with a hard elliptical drop shadow, and there is no waterline, no waterline occlusion, no reflection, nothing anywhere in the frame indicating water. The fix is to sit the body IN water with the belly and legs cut off by a waterline, not to shorten the legs further.

MUST-READ 3 - 'long neck kinked back onto the shoulders': ABSENT, judge correct. The skull sits directly on the egg torso joined by a short straight pale-grey stub about one skull-width tall. There is no length to kink with and no S-curve laying back onto the shoulders. Consequence: with a short bill and no retracted neck, the head-to-body relationship reads as a gull/tern chick.

CHASSIS - judge correct, and I confirm it explicitly after opening Booby.png and Gannet.png at full size beside this. All three are ONE BODY: same egg torso outline, same sphere skull placed at the same anchor, same single black eye-dot with the same catchlight, same grey crescent wing-scoop with the same sweep, same grey wedge tail spiking right, same pair of thin yellow stick legs with the same 3-toe splay, same cast-shadow ellipse. Pelican differs from the other two only in (a) a dirtier grey-tan plumage wash instead of white, and (b) the fatter bill wedge noted above. Nothing about its silhouette, mass distribution, neck carriage, limb form or stance is pelican-specific.

VERDICT: reads as a generic small white-grey waterbird chick. Zero of the three must-reads are readable as pelican; one (short legs) is coincidentally satisfied by the shared chassis rather than by any pelican intent. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a generic green cartoon fish / vaguely a bass-shaped decal
rows.defect: The large hinged bucket mouth - the single feature that IS a bass - is not weak, it is entirely absent: the head tapers to a bare geometric point with no mouth, lip or jaw line drawn anywhere. The dorsal is one crown of four flat triangles, so there is no spiny-front-joined-to-soft-rear structure either; only the moderately deep compressed body reads. No lateral black stripe, no head/operculum break.
rows.fix: Draw the jaw: cut a wide gape line from the snout back past the eye with a heavy hinged lower jaw and a blunt upper lip, and split the dorsal crown into a spiny triangle set joined by a low membrane to a rounded soft rear lobe.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 4x, 8x and 16x magnification of the 440px master (crops of head, snout, dorsal and whole silhouette). The FAIL stands: two of three must-reads are absent. CORRECTIONS AND ADDITIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM FOLLOW.

(1) MOUTH - claim essentially correct, with one correction. The head is a bare geometric wedge that tapers to a needle point at approximately (327, 205); at 16x there is no gape, no jaw hinge, no lip, no maxilla, and no upper/lower jaw division anywhere on the head. The claim's 'no mouth, lip or jaw line drawn at all' is very slightly wrong in the literal: there IS one vestigial stroke - a roughly 7px dark diagonal dash at approximately x 290-297, y 215-217, sitting INSIDE the lower head well short of the snout tip and detached from the silhouette edge. It is about 3 percent of body length, does not touch the outline, and is indistinguishable from the stray shading flecks scattered over the same area. It does not read as a mouth at any zoom. The bass's defining feature - the huge hinged bucket jaw whose hinge runs back past the rear margin of the eye - is not drawn. This alone is disqualifying for a largemouth/smallmouth bass.

(2) DORSAL - claim correct in substance, wrong in the count and the adjective. It is not 'four flat triangles': it is FIVE sharp-apexed sawteeth on ONE continuous, undivided, flat dark-olive membrane (apexes at approximately x 222, 245, 268, 289 plus a leading one near x 205, spanning x 200-291). The teeth are pointed, not flat. What matters is that the claim's conclusion holds exactly: there is no notch, no gap and no change of form anywhere along the fin, so there is no spiny front section joined to a soft rear section. A bass reads as a tall spiny anterior comb, a deep notch, then a distinctly ROUNDED soft-rayed posterior lobe. Here the whole fin is one uniform zigzag comb whose teeth merely get shorter toward the head, which is also backwards - the spiny anterior should be the taller half. Must-read failed.

(3) BODY - the claim is generous here, not harsh. Measured length approximately 180px against maximum depth approximately 62px = aspect 2.9, matching the specified 2.8, so the depth NUMBER is right. But the shape is a symmetric almond/lens pointed at BOTH ends: there is no blunt rounded snout, no rising forehead or nape, no flattened belly, and the caudal peduncle pinches to a sharp point where the tail fan attaches instead of holding a broad peduncle. So 'moderately deep body reads' overstates it - the profile reads as a leaf, not as a laterally compressed perciform.

(4) WHAT THE JUDGE DID NOT MENTION, SO THAT A FIX DOES NOT RE-DERIVE IT. The asset is not featureless; only the head is. Already present and readable: a curved operculum/gill-cover arc behind the eye, a continuous lateral line running the full body length, dense scale stipple across the flank, a small fan-shaped pectoral fin low on the flank (around x 235-270, y 200-215), a dark anal-fin mass under the belly, and a properly forked caudal fin. Keep all of these.

(5) NEW DEFECT NOT IN THE ORIGINAL CLAIM. The eye is a white ring with a small black pupil (cartoon googly-eye read) and it is MIS-PLACED: it straddles the dorsal contour of the head. The eye spans roughly y 188-200 at x 297-310, while the head's upper outline at that x sits at about y 192, so the top arc of the white ring protrudes roughly 4px outside the silhouette and is visible against the black background. Fix the eye placement inward and down at the same time as the mouth.

VERDICT: FAIL upheld. Two of three must-reads (hinged bucket mouth, spiny-joined-to-soft dorsal) are missing outright, the third is only numerically satisfied, and the result reads as a generic green cartoon fish with a spike-comb crest.

rows.readsAs: a yellow bluegill or a generic yellow pancake panfish - it is the Sunfish render in another colour
rows.defect: Zero of the three must-reads survive. There is ONE saw-tooth dorsal, not two separate fins. There are NO dark vertical bars - the flank carries only the same uniform dot-mesh scale hatch as every other fish here. The pelvic and anal fins are the same olive-yellow as the body with no orange or red anywhere. On top of that the body is drawn as a near-round pancake (roughly 1.3:1) when the row asks for 2.8:1, which makes it read as the Sunfish rather than a perch.
rows.fix: Rebuild it at a true 2.8:1 with a humped nape, split the crown into a distinct spiny front dorsal and a separate soft rear dorsal with a real gap between them, paint 6-7 hard dark vertical bars from topline to belly, and colour the pelvic and anal fins orange-red.
rows.verifyWhy:
I decoded the PNG and re-rendered it at 3x, 5x and 7x, plus a 3.5x contrast-stretched luminance pass, and measured the pixels. The FAIL stands, but two of the stated causes need correcting.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: an olive/chartreuse lens-shaped (almond) fish facing right, forked olive tail, one white-ringed black eye, a curved dark operculum arc behind the head, one small pectoral fan with a dark triangle at mid-flank, a small dull-olive ventral lobe under the belly, and a single continuous saw-tooth crest on the dorsal line. Body is covered in the family dot-mesh scale hatch.

MUST-READ 1 - 'two separate dorsal fins, the front one spiny': ABSENT, judge correct. At 7x the dorsal is ONE unbroken olive polygon with 5 sharp triangular teeth, sitting from just behind the head to mid-body. There is no gap and no soft rear lobe; the topline from the crest back to the caudal peduncle is completely bare. The identical 5-tooth crest appears on Bass, Sunfish and Walleye in this same batch, so it is a shared chassis part, not a perch feature.

MUST-READ 2 - 'dark vertical bars down green-gold flanks': CAUSE MISSTATED, verdict still fails. The claim 'no dark vertical bars anywhere (just the family dot-mesh hatch)' is not accurate: there IS a deliberate low-frequency vertical banding unique to this asset. Column-mean luminance across the body mask oscillates with a period of ~19px and ~7 full cycles (troughs at x=177,198,216,235,254,275,293 at lum ~116-129; peaks at x=187,207,226,245,264,284,303 at lum ~147-159). Bass, drawn with the same hatch, is flat by comparison (110-114 across its whole flank, ripple +/-3). So the count is right (~7 bands, correct for a perch). It fails for two other reasons: (a) INVERTED POLARITY - the bands are rendered as BRIGHTER vertical sheen columns over the ground, not as dark bars over a lighter gold flank; at natural contrast the eye reads light stripes; (b) contrast is far too low (~25% luminance swing, smooth sinusoidal) so at normal viewing it dissolves into the dot mesh. The fix is not 'add bars' - it is to flip the existing 7-band modulation to dark-over-light and roughly triple its contrast, and give the bands hard vertical edges instead of a sine falloff.

MUST-READ 3 - 'orange-red pelvic and anal fins': ABSENT, judge correct and I confirmed it numerically. Scanning every foreground pixel, there are ZERO pixels with hue < 45 degrees at saturation >= 30. The hue histogram is 15,481 px in the 60-degree (yellow) bucket, 302 at 75, 48 at 45, 14 at 30, and the remainder is the blue-grey rim/shadow. The ventral lobe under the belly at 7x is a dull olive, DARKER than the body, i.e. not merely 'the same olive-yellow as the body' as claimed - it is a desaturated shadow tone. Either way there is no warm fin colour anywhere on the asset.

ASPECT - the '~1.3:1 pancake' figure is measured wrong, though the defect is real. 1.30 is the full foreground bbox (197x151), which includes the tail fan and the dorsal spikes. The convention that reproduces the packet specs for the rest of the family is the bright body mask: Bass measures 2.80 against a spec of 2.8, Walleye 4.02 against 4, Sunfish 1.16 against 1.5. Perch on that same measure is 166x103 = 1.61 against a spec of 2.8 - about 57% of spec, so still badly under-elongated, but not 1.3.

ONE CHASSIS: all four family members are the same drawing. Identical almond body outline, identical 5-tooth dorsal crest, identical pectoral fan with dark triangle, identical operculum arc, identical eye, identical ventral lobe, identical forked tail; only body aspect, hue and mesh density change. Because the Perch is squashed to 1.61 while Sunfish sits at 1.16 and Bass at 2.80, the Perch silhouette lands nearer the Sunfish end, so the judge's gestalt call - 'reads as the Sunfish in yellow' - is fair. Nothing on this asset identifies it as a perch: not the fin count, not the bar contrast, not the fin colour, not the proportion.

rows.readsAs: a pale green bluegill / panfish - broadly the right thing
rows.defect: The deep round pancake body does read, but the other two must-reads do not. There is no dark ear-flap tab on the gill cover - only diffuse mottling near a faint gill arc. There is no tiny mouth on a small head: the head is not differentiated at all and the snout ends in a bare point with no mouth drawn. The caudal fin also sits as a flat detached paddle with a stray thin dark line running vertically through it.
rows.fix: Add a solid black opercular ear-flap tab at the rear edge of the gill cover and a small blunt terminal mouth on a short rounded head, and reattach/clean the caudal paddle so it joins the peduncle without the stray stroke.

rows.readsAs: a generic gold baitfish or minnow with a spiky crown
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads are present. The eye - the feature the animal is NAMED for - is the same tiny white-ringed black dot used on the Bass and Sunfish, with no size increase, no cloudy milky pupil and no reflective bloom. The dorsal is one saw-tooth crown, not two fins with a spiny front. The caudal is uniform olive with no white tip on the lower lobe. The snout ends in a bare point with no mouth and no canine teeth.
rows.fix: Blow the eye up to 2-3x the family default and fill it with a milky opaque glassy pupil plus a hot reflective highlight, then add the white flash on the lower caudal lobe.
rows.verifyWhy: Verdict upheld, but two parts of the stated cause are wrong and the worst defect went unnamed. WHAT I SAW (440x440 canvas; fish bbox 222w x 74h, x109-331, y158-232, aspect 3.0 against the packet's 4.0). THE EYE (mustRead 'large cloudy glassy reflective eye'): a hard white annulus centred (315.5,197.5), outer extent x312-319 / y194-201 = 8 x 8 px, ring pixels ~[210,208,205], pupil sampled at (316,196) = [20,23,27] which is the page background colour [8,13,19] showing through -- an empty black hole, no milky/cloudy fill, no highlight dot, no reflective bloom, no iris ring. CORRECTION 1 to the claim: it is NOT 'the same' bead as the neighbours -- measured white-ring boxes are Bass 11x11, Perch 11x11, Walleye 8x8. The walleye's eye is ~27% SMALLER in diameter than the two family members whose packet rows do not even ask for a special eye, on the LONGEST body in the family. The defect is worse than 'no size increase'; it is an active size decrease. CORRECTION 2: the cited comparison to Sunfish is loose -- Sunfish's white pixels scatter across a 90px span (its gill-flap/edge highlights), so the shared white-ring-plus-black-dot bead is specifically the Bass/Perch one. UNNAMED AND LARGER DEFECT: the eye is not seated in the head at all. Column scan of the body silhouette gives dorsal contour top=200 at x=314 and top=201 at x=316, while the ring spans y194-201 -- so roughly 60-70% of the eye floats in the black background ABOVE the snout's topline, tangent to it, reading as a bubble stuck onto the outside of the head rather than an eye in a skull. Any fix must re-anchor it inside the silhouette before enlarging it. DORSAL (mustRead 'two dorsal fins with a spiny front one'): claim confirmed and understated. There is ONE continuous saw-tooth ridge of 5 triangular spikes, and it runs the ENTIRE back from just behind the nape to the caudal peduncle with no gap and no soft rear lobe. A percid's spiny dorsal should sit over the front third only, with a separate soft dorsal behind it; here the single ridge spanning the whole topline reads as a stegosaur/scenery frill, not a fin pair. CAUDAL (mustRead 'white tip on the lower lobe'): confirmed absent. Both lobes are identical dull olive [~150,140,80] fading to near-black at the tips; sampled lower-lobe tip (112,232)=[8,12,18] and (115,228)=[20,22,23] -- the lower lobe is DARKER at the tip than the upper, the exact inverse of the marking asked for. HEAD: claim confirmed -- at 14x the snout is a bare pointed wedge with no mouth line, no jaw hinge, no gape and no canines; the only marking there is fine vertical hatch fill. There is also no operculum/gill line anywhere, so headFrac 0.28 is unreadable -- the head is not demarcated from the body, the whole animal is one lens/spindle with mesh scale texture and a faint grey lateral line. NET: all three must-reads are absent, and the silhouette (pointed lens body, full-length saw ridge, undifferentiated head) does not read as a percid at all. 'Generic gold baitfish' is a fair summary.

rows.readsAs: a pink cartoon axolotl - correct animal, mascot-grade
rows.defect: Gills and smile land, but the third must-read is absent: there is no fin crest anywhere. The back is a smooth unbroken curve and the tail is a constant-width pink sausage with a blunt rounded tip. Where the caudal fin should be there are instead two dull grey-mauve circles overlapping behind and below the tail, offset from the tail axis and not attached to the tip - they read as a smeared shadow blob, not a fin. The head is a bulbous egg rather than the wide flat spade the reference asks for, the lower gill fan hangs off the throat and tangles with the foreleg so it reads as a pink hand, and the four limbs are dark chocolate-brown against a pink body, so they look glued on from another animal.
rows.fix: Delete the two grey discs and replace them with a real translucent fin membrane: a continuous crest that starts mid-back, thickens over the tail base and tapers the tail to a paddle-shaped point, tinted the same pink as the body; and re-tint the limbs to the body pink.

rows.readsAs: an albino/leucistic axolotl - a stranger names the other species in this batch
rows.defect: This is the Axolotl file recoloured. All three must-reads fail. (1) The body is not a pale pink translucent eel - it is the axolotl's short fat lozenge at roughly aspect 3 instead of the specified aspect 8, opaque cream-yellow with the axolotl's blotches, with a huge quarter-length head instead of headFrac 0.12. (2) The gills are the same two salmon-pink fans in the same two positions as the axolotl, one of them slung under the throat, rather than a bushy blood-red pair swept back behind the head. (3) Worst, the note says the eyes are skinned over and invisible, yet the render carries a large glossy black eye with a white catchlight, front and centre on the skull - the one feature that makes an olm an olm is contradicted rather than merely missing. The limbs are also short bent lizard pegs in olive-brown, not vestigially thin three-toed threads, and the same stray grey discs sit behind the tail.
rows.fix: Rebuild it off the axolotl chassis entirely: stretch to a genuine aspect-8 near-cylindrical pale-pink translucent eel body with a small blunt snout, delete the eye and leave a faint skin-covered depression, move the gills to a single bushy crimson tuft immediately behind the skull, and reduce the limbs to four thread-thin sticks with three visible toes.
rows.verifyWhy:
I looked at Olm.png at full size, then at 5x crops of the head and the limb row, and I measured the silhouette bounding boxes of both family members. The FAIL stands, and the shared-chassis charge is provable by number, not just by eye: the bright-pixel bbox of Olm.png is 272x108 px = aspect 2.52; Axolotl.png is 339x134 px = aspect 2.53. The two renders are the SAME outline at 0.80 scale. The reference rows ask for 3.5 and 8 respectively — the one proportion that is supposed to separate these two species has been collapsed to a single value, and neither species gets its own number. Correcting the claim's figure: it is 2.5, not 'roughly 3', and the spec is 8, so the body is a third of the required length-to-depth. A column scan shows why: the trunk is only 36-48 px deep over x=190-250, but the tail is a fat pale slab 61-71 px deep over x=100-160 — the tail is WIDER than the body it hangs off. That is a larval paddle-tail, not an eel taper; there is no point at which the animal narrows toward the tip.

HEAD / EYES (the identity contradiction — confirmed, and worse than stated). The head ellipse runs x=294-353, ~59 px of the 272 px total = headFrac ~0.22 against a specified 0.12; the claim's 'quarter-length' is right in substance (it is essentially the Axolotl's 0.25). At 5x the head carries a large glossy black pupil with a white specular catchlight, sitting centred and high on a domed skull, plus a drawn upcurved smiling mouth line running the width of the muzzle. The row says 'eyes: hidden' and the note says 'Eyes are skinned over and invisible'. So this is not an omission that a viewer could read past — the render asserts the opposite of the identity feature, and the mouth it is paired with is verbatim the OTHER row's mustRead ('wide flat head with an upcurved smiling mouth', Axolotl). A stranger shown these two side by side names both of them Axolotl.

GILLS. The claim is accurate and I confirm the placement. There are exactly two salmon-pink feathery branched fans, identical in draw to the Axolotl's: one rises off the nape just behind/above the skull, the second hangs DOWNWARD off the throat/chest below the jawline, into the shadow. I will give the asset the one point it earns — the dorsal fan is technically 'behind the head', so the mustRead 'bushy red external gills' is not wholly absent — but it is salmon pink rather than red/crimson, it is a flat splayed axolotl fan of long individual filaments rather than a bushy tuft, and the ventral copy is anatomically nonsense on any salamander. Three pairs is the Axolotl's requirement, not the Olm's; the render gives the same two-fan arrangement to both, so the gills also fail to discriminate.

LIMBS. Confirmed at 5x: four thick, short, dark olive-drab pegs with rounded club ends and no digits at all — not merely 'not three-toed', but toeless. The mustRead demands 'tiny spindly legs with three toes' and the note explicitly says 'vestigially thin, not lizard-like'; these are the opposite on both counts, and they are the same olive pegs the Axolotl render uses, unchanged in hue even though the Olm's body was recoloured. The olive reads as a foreign colour bolted onto a cream body.

COLOUR. Body is cream/ivory with pale yellow mottled blotches — the Axolotl's markings recoloured, exactly as claimed. 'Pale pink translucent' is not met: there is no translucency cue (no darker internal mass, no light bleed at the edges), and the blotching actively works against it by reading as opaque skin pattern.

WHAT TO FIX, in order: (1) re-proportion to a genuine aspect 8 with a tapering tail thinner than the trunk, so the two family members stop sharing one bbox; (2) shrink the skull to headFrac 0.12 and DELETE the eye and the smiling mouth entirely, replacing them with a blank skin-covered head, since the current eye contradicts rather than omits; (3) move the gills to a single crimson bushy tuft pair behind the skull and remove the throat-hung fan; (4) replace the olive club pegs with thread-thin pale limbs carrying three visible toes.

WHAT I SAW (440x440, read at 3x and 8x zoom on head/tail/feet, plus pixel sampling).

MUST-READ 3 - 'broad fan tail and slender bill with a white cere': FAIL on two of three counts, but NOT the count the judge named.

The must-read's word 'slender' is actually SATISFIED. What fails is (a) the colour — sampled mean RGB 214,171,62, saturated golden yellow, where a rock pigeon's bill is dark slate grey; and (b) the cere. A fixer told 'narrow the bill' would narrow an already-slender bill and still fail.
  - Cere: judge is CORRECT and it is worse than stated. I thresholded the whole image for near-white (r>225,g>225,b>215) and the Pigeon contains ZERO such pixels — no white cere knob, and not even a white eye catchlight (the light dot at the eye is mid-grey). For contrast the Dove in the same batch has 549 near-white pixels. There is no white anywhere on this asset.

Combined with the saturated yellow bill, yellow feet and low-slung globular body, the duckling read the judge describes is real.

DEFECT THE JUDGE MISSED, and it is the bigger one. The Pigeon and the Dove in this 2-species batch are ONE CHASSIS RECOLOURED. I rendered both at identical crop and scale side by side. FIXES, in priority order: (1) build a real pigeon body — lengthen to ~1.9 aspect, give it a neck column and a deep jutting breast, and kill the torus ring band, which is the single largest silhouette artifact and is shared with the Dove; (2) broad squared fan tail replacing the blade; (3) recolour bill from golden yellow to dark slate and add the white cere knob at the base; (4) recolour legs from amber to coral red; (5) move the green from a crown cap to a soft neck-side sheen, and differentiate the Dove chassis so the two are not one drawing.

(3) TAIL — judge correct in direction, wrong in one detail. Crop at 6x (85,185 / 120x120): the tail roots high on the rump, bulges up briefly, then sweeps DOWN and forward, ending in a splayed dark five-strand tuft level with the hock. Additional defect the judge missed: the tail is THICK — at its root it is nearly as wide as the hind cannon bone, so it reads as a limb/trunk stub rather than the required THIN wire. (4) NOT IN THE CLAIM BUT DECISIVE — SHARED CHASSIS. Side-by-side with Pig.png this is one body in two colours. Identical rump-to-withers topline arc, identical deep barrel torso, identical short columnar legs, identical two-toe cloven hoof pair, identical head dome, identical eye+ear-triangle placement, identical two-nostril snout disc, identical shaggy streak fill. GEOMETRY (measured). Crisp rim-lit body spans x=137 (tail point) to x=338 (snout tip), 201px long; max depth 42px at x=221-245. Aspect ~4.8 against spec 5 -- the ELONGATION is correct. What is wrong is the profile: maximum depth falls at x~233, dead centre of 137-338, and the two ends taper as mirror images. It is a symmetric almond/leaf lens, not a torpedo (deepest ~1/3 back, then a long straight flank into a caudal peduncle). Surface carries a regular hexagonal/diamond scale net plus vague dark mottle. No pale bean rows anywhere. Must-read 3 half-met (length yes, form and markings no).

MUST-READ 1, duck-bill snout full of teeth -- ABSENT, and the judge's placement is WRONG. The head is a plain triangular wedge: a straight rim-lit dorsal line and a straight rim-lit ventral line converging to a point. No mouth, no gape, no jaw line, no lip, no nostril, no flattening. The wedge from the opercular arc (x~285) to the tip (x=338) is 53px = 0.26 of body, close to spec headFrac 0.28, so the PROPORTION is right and only the modelling is missing. Correction: the head is NOT literally identical to the tail point -- it is a little longer and shallower (19px deep at 30px from the tip vs 24px at the tail) and it carries an opercular arc and an eye. Correction on the teeth: they do NOT run rearward past the gill under the throat. Seven white hooks occupy x=299..339 -- entirely FORWARD of the gill arc at x~285 and reaching the snout tip. That is exactly where a jaw belongs. The defect is that there is no jaw for them to sit in: they are hung on the outside of an unbroken ventral outline like a comb of ticks, pointing down and rearward, so they read as a fringe or barbels rather than dentition.

EYE (not in the claim, worth fixing). A hollow white ring, 10x10px at x=321-330 / y=191-200, unfilled except a dark comma. The crisp topline at that x is y=199-200, so the ring sits almost entirely ABOVE the dorsal outline -- it floats off the head like a washer or bubble rather than sitting in the skull.

MUST-READ 2, dorsal fin far back near the tail -- ABSENT. Correction: there are SIX hairline strokes, not five, at x=216-217, 230-231, 244-245, 258, 271-272; each 1-2px wide and 7-11px tall, delta only ~18-30/255 against background, i.e. invisible at native size. Two further corrections. (a) Position: they span 33%-61% of body length measured back from the snout, so centre-to-slightly-forward-of-centre, where a pike's dorsal belongs at ~70-90%. (b) Attachment: the spines do not touch the fish. The crisp topline at x=217 is y=181; the lowest spine pixel there is y=173, an 8px gap. They are anchored to the GHOST silhouette, not the body. There is no membrane or web of any kind between them -- no fin outline exists, only bare bristles.

GHOST SILHOUETTE -- CONFIRMED. A second, larger, soft green lens sits offset upward from the crisp rim-lit body: it reaches y=169-172 at x=232-244 where the crisp back is at y=181 (11px proud above the topline) and y=228 at x=208-228 where the crisp belly is y=222 (6px below). It reads as a dark-green halo/double exposure and is what the dorsal bristles are planted in.

FINS. Anal fin absent -- confirmed; a ventral scan of y=222-275 finds only the smooth ghost bulge (x=194-256), no fin. Pelvic fins also absent. Correction/credit the judge omitted: a PECTORAL fin IS drawn, as a dark angular blade at x~250-290 below the midline, and it is the one fin rendered as a fin. Caudal is present, forked and acceptable.

VERDICT. Two of three defining must-reads are missing outright and the third is half-wrong. The silhouette reads as a green leaf with a forked tail -- a generic lens-bodied fish -- and nothing in it says Esox. FAIL upheld. Fix order: (1) cut a real mouth -- long flattened bill with an articulated jaw line running back under the eye, teeth INSIDE it; (2) move the dorsal to ~75-85% aft of the snout and draw it as a webbed fin with a visible membrane on the crisp body, plus a matching anal fin below it; (3) shift max body depth forward to ~1/3 and flatten the aft flank into a peduncle; (4) replace the hex scale net with rows of pale bean spots; (5) delete or re-register the offset ghost lens; (6) seat the eye inside the head instead of on top of the topline.

rows.readsAs: a clump of soap bubbles / a bunch of peeled white grapes / a cauliflower — not a mushroom with hanging teeth
rows.defect: The identity must-read — a pom-pom of LONG icicle spines cascading downward over the whole mass — is essentially absent. The silhouette is ~85% large smooth glossy spheres with hard specular highlights; the spines are a short, sparse band roughly one-fifth of the body height, confined to a narrow horizontal strip across the middle, and they are drawn BEHIND a further layer of spheres that occludes their lower halves. So the teeth do not hang off the underside of the mass at all — they appear to grow out of its equator and then get swallowed. Nothing about the surface is shaggy; Hericium reads as a fuzzy white waterfall and this reads as bubble wrap. The remaining must-reads pass (no cap, no stem, no gills; creamy-white colour; single unbranched mass), and the render itself is clean — centred, uncropped, with a ground shadow — but the one must-read that IS the organism is missing.
rows.fix: Invert the mass-to-spine ratio: shrink the interior spheres so they only suggest the lumpy core, then draw the spines as the outer silhouette — long tapered icicles (40–60% of body height) emitted from the BOTTOM and lower-front of the mass, dense enough that the blob's lower edge is entirely a fringe of hanging teeth, and drawn in front of everything so nothing occludes them.

I read the 440x440 PNG at 1x, then re-cropped and upscaled three regions (whole body 4x, lower band 6x, right flank and left flank 10x) and ran a row-by-row pixel profile of the mass. The FAIL stands, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and the fix should be aimed elsewhere.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A single unbranched globose mass occupying x 125-315, y 75-297 (190 x 222 px) on black, centred, with a soft ground-shadow ellipse. Colour is correct: creamy white with warm tan/ochre shading in the crevices, no cap, no stem, no gills, no branching, no substrate stub. That part of the reference row is satisfied.

The mass is built from roughly 35-40 large smooth glossy spheres with strong specular highlights and hard sphere-on-sphere occlusion contours. At 1x this reads as a cluster of peeled grapes / soap bubbles / a pile of small puffballs. The row profile confirms the silhouette is a bumpy stack of circular arcs everywhere except one small patch (see below): the outline at the top (y 75-200), the whole left flank (x 125-145), the bottom (y 265-297) and the bottom-right are pure smooth sphere arc, no fuzz, no teeth.

SPINES - WHERE THEY ARE. There IS a spine layer and it is competently drawn: pale near-white tapering icicles, correct value separation from the body, correctly vertical and pointing down, with varied lengths and a ragged lower edge. They occupy a horizontal band from y~200 to y~265 spanning x~140 to x~315. That band is 65px of a 222px-tall mass = ~29% of the height, and it sits at 56%-86% of the way down the body, i.e. across the waist/lower-middle. Above it, 125px (56% of the mass height) is bare spheres. Below it, another ~30px (14%) of bare spheres. By area the smooth-sphere fraction is ~85%, so the other judge's 85% figure is accurate.

CORRECTION 1 - THE SPINES ARE NOT SHORT. Individual spines measure ~45-50px from attachment to tip, which is ~21% of the mass height. That is a correct, generous Hericium tooth length. Do not lengthen them. The defect is COVERAGE and PLACEMENT, not spine length.

CORRECTION 2 - THEY ARE NOT OCCLUDED BY SPHERES, THEY ARE PAINTED ON TOP OF THEM. At 10x on the left/centre band the spines are drawn ABOVE the sphere layer in z-order and simply terminate mid-face on a sphere; the sphere's shading and its lit rim continue past and around each spine tip. So they read as pale wax drips / streaks lying flat on the front of the balls, not as teeth hanging in front of empty air. The stated cause ('lower halves occluded by a further layer of spheres') is the wrong diagnosis - nothing is drawn over them; they just have solid sphere behind and below them, so they never break a contour.

CORRECTION 3 - ONE PATCH READS CORRECTLY. On the right flank, roughly x 285-315 / y 205-260, about a dozen spines hang free off the underside of a sphere straight into the black background, with black between and below them and a ragged tooth-edge silhouette. That patch (~10-15% of the perimeter) is exactly right and is proof the primitive itself is good. The claim that the spines are universally swallowed is false. Whatever is producing that right-flank behaviour is what needs to be applied to the whole underside.

WHY IT STILL FAILS. The reference must-read is 'a rounded white pom-pom of long hanging icicle spines, spines ALL cascading downward from a single unbranched mass.' In the real organism the spines ARE the silhouette - the entire outward-facing surface is a shaggy white beard and no smooth flesh is visible at all except a small rear attachment knob. Here the teeth are a decorative fringe across the waist of a bubble pile: ~85% of the visible surface and ~90% of the outline is bare glossy sphere. At thumbnail size the band would collapse to a smudge and the asset would read as a cluster of white spheres, i.e. the wrong organism. The fix is a generator-level change, not a nudge: push the sphere cluster BEHIND the spine layer, drop the sphere count/size so they only supply the underlying lumpy volume, and emit spines from the entire lower and outer surface of the mass (front face and both flanks, from y~150 all the way to the bottom of the silhouette) so that teeth - not sphere arcs - form the bottom and side outline. Keep the current spine length, taper, colour and the right-flank hang-into-void treatment.

Only the RED half fails, and it fails absolutely: a full-image scan for warm pixels (r >= g) returns 85 hits and every one of them is inside the off-white eye ring at x=341-343. There is not one warm pixel anywhere on the body, rear or otherwise. The judge is right; the flank is a single flat desaturated sage-green from snout to peduncle. MUST-READ 2 (dorsal and anal set far back, framing the tail like a paddle) — fails, but I am correcting the judge's numbers, which understate how far FORWARD the dorsal is. Measured from the snout: the dorsal lobe runs x=290 down to x=190, i.e. 31%-72% of body length back, centred at ~51% — dead mid-body, not 45-70%. The anal runs x=245 to x=178, i.e. 50%-77%, centred ~63%. So the two fins are not even opposed — the anal sits noticeably further aft than the dorsal, which no real fish does and which kills any read of a paired rear cluster. Behind the rearmost fin edge (x=178) there is a bare 58px stretch — 23% of body length — of naked peduncle before the caudal starts. The judge's 'bare gap before the caudal so they never frame the tail' is exactly correct. Both fins are smooth rayless rounded lobes in a dark desaturated green, painted BEHIND the translucent body layer so the overlap reads as an internal shadow; they do protrude past the outline (so 'tucked behind the silhouette' overstates it — they are visible, just unreadable as fins, more like bruises than fins). The caudal itself is the one thing closer to right: a dark rounded truncate fan at x=71-120 with faint ray spokes, roughly the right paddle shape — but it hangs off a needle-thin peduncle point and is darker than the body, so it floats detached rather than continuing the paddle. MUST-READ 3 (bony flattened head with a small upward mouth) — fails. At 13x the snout is a bare wedge tapering to a needle point identical in construction to the tail end: no mouth aperture, no jaw line, no lip, no upward gape, no head plating or bony flattening, no head/trunk demarcation. CORRECTION to the judge: an opercle IS present — a faint dark vertical-curved gill arc at x~300, about 27% back from the snout, close to the packet's headFrac 0.22. It is very low contrast (dark green on green) but it is there, so 'no opercle' is wrong. Also present: a bold white-ringed dark-pupil eye, but it is misplaced — it straddles the dorsal outline at x~341-345 with its upper half outside the silhouette, only ~9% of body length from the tip, and it is large and high-contrast against a packet spec of 'eyes: small'. Net: with zero red, mid-body rather than rear-set fins, no mouth or jaw, and a lens/leaf body outline pointed at BOTH ends, this reads as a generic green wrasse or leaf-fish, not an arapaima. FAIL upheld. Fix order: (1) drive dorsal and anal aft to ~78-95% of body length, opposed to each other, so their rear edges nearly meet the caudal and the three form one paddle; (2) put warm red-orange scale edging on the posterior third, strongest along the rear scale margins and the fin bases; (3) build an actual head — flatten and broaden the snout dorsally, add a mouth line running up to a small upward-angled gape, keep and strengthen the existing opercle arc, and drop the eye back and down so it sits fully inside the head.

rows.readsAs: A wooden ruler, a stick of butter, or a burlap-wrapped knife handle — the blunt-ended tan slab does not read as a living fish
rows.defect: The silhouette is a flat-sided slab squared off at BOTH ends: the head end terminates in a blunt vertical face and the tail end in another, so the animal reads as a cut length of dowel rather than a fish. Two of the three must-reads are entirely missing. (1) No barbels — the chin is a bare blunt corner; nothing projects from it. (2) No steeply upturned drawbridge mouth — the jaw is a single straight horizontal dark slot scribed low on the snout face, almost parallel to the lateral line, which is the exact opposite of the near-vertical oblique gape that IS the arowana. (3) The long ribbon dorsal and anal fins are only half-present: they exist as a flat grey rim hugging the top and bottom edges, indistinguishable from an outline stroke, with no rays, no depth, and no flare. The caudal is a tiny dark wedge with three or four stray hair-rays hanging off the left end, so small and so disconnected from the blunt body face that it reads as damage. The all-over square knurl texture reads as woven basketwork or canvas, not as the arowana's big metallic mosaic scales, and the flat khaki colour carries no sheen. The eye disc sits at the extreme upper-front corner of the block rather than on a modelled head.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: cut the snout back into an oblique wedge and swing the lower jaw up to a near-vertical hinged plate that meets the upper jaw at the very top of the head, then hang two long forward-curving barbels off its tip — and give the dorsal/anal ribbons real width with visible rays so they read as fins instead of an outline.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 5x-16x crops of head, tail, dorsal edge and mid-flank. The FAIL stands: 0 of 3 must-reads are readable.

MUST-READ 1 - 'steeply upturned drawbridge mouth': ABSENT. Their description is directionally right but wrong in detail. The mouth is NOT a 'straight horizontal slot'; it is a single thin dark 1px stroke rising roughly 10-15 degrees from lower-left to upper-right, starting at about the lower third of the head depth and ending short of the snout front edge at roughly mid-depth. There is no gape, no jaw articulation, no lower-jaw silhouette bulge, no notch in the outline where a mouth would open. It reads as an engraved scratch on a solid block, not a jaw - and certainly not the near-vertical hinged drawbridge that IS the arowana. FIX TARGET: the mouth must be cut into the SILHOUETTE (an oblique 55-75 degree jaw line with the lower jaw projecting past the upper), not drawn as a line on top of an intact rounded snout.

MUST-READ 2 - 'two barbels projecting from the chin': ABSENT, confirmed at 16x. Nothing at the chin - no stubs, no faint strokes, no pixels outside the outline anywhere on the lower snout. Their claim is correct without qualification.

MUST-READ 3 - 'long ribbon dorsal and anal fins running to the tail': GEOMETRICALLY present, VISUALLY absent. Their claim is correct and I confirm it: top and bottom each carry a uniform flat grey band roughly 4-5px deep at 440px, identical value on both edges, running most of the body length. Zero ray lines, zero membrane, zero depth variation, no taper toward either end. At normal size it reads unambiguously as a stroke/outline rim on a shape, not as fin tissue. One thing to add for the fix: the grey band does NOT run to the head - it terminates in an abrupt square vertical step about 20% back from the snout, and that step is a large part of what makes the ends read as machined. The band also does not run onto the caudal.

SILHOUETTE: their 'wooden ruler / butter stick' read is accurate. Body is a rounded-rectangle of near-constant depth for its whole length. PARTIAL CORRECTION to 'blunt vertical faces at BOTH ends': the two blunt faces are not the same defect and need different fixes. The TAIL end is a true flat vertical cut with rounded corners and NO caudal peduncle taper at all - full body depth right up to the cut. The HEAD end is a rounded-rect cap with a vertical front face over the middle ~60% of depth; the harder square break the eye catches there is actually the dorsal/anal grey band ending in its own vertical step behind the head, not the body outline.

CAUDAL: their claim is correct. It is a small dark-olive leaf/spike protruding from the tail face, about one sixth of body depth, plus three or four hair-thin faint diagonal streaks extending well past it into the background. Those strays do read as scratches/damage rather than rays.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY GOOD (the previous judge did not mention any of it, and none of it rescues the asset): the eye is well formed and prominent as specified - a black pupil with a clean white sclera ring, set high and well forward. There is a clear curved operculum/gill arc behind the head. There is a pectoral fin drawn as a dark triangle with 3-4 radiating ray lines on the mid-flank - the only structure in the whole image with ray detail - but it lies entirely INSIDE the body outline with no separation, so it reads as an engraved chevron/arrow rather than a fin. Aspect measures close to the requested 5 and headFrac close to the requested 0.2, so proportion is not the problem. Scale texture is a fine uniform checkerboard that reads as basket weave, not as the large arowana scales.

NET: strip away the eye and the flank chevron and the object left is a textured lozenge with a rim and a spike. It reads as a generic blunt minnow at best and as a butter stick at worst. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a generic tan plush monkey, indistinguishable from the Capuchin and Macaque in the same batch
rows.defect: The long dog-like muzzle that IS the baboon is absent — the face is the family's flat button snout with no jaw projection at all. The tail is the shared smooth C-curve, not the sharply kinked-then-hanging profile the note calls out, and there is no shoulder cape.

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG, then re-read it at 6x on the head, 4x on the tail, 5x on the feet and 3x on the whole body. The FAIL stands, and it stands for a harder reason than the original judge gave: this asset is the Capuchin chassis recoloured. Rendering Capuchin.png side by side, the two are the same drawing — same round frontal skull with a dark cap band across the brow, same two round side-set ears, same close-set white eyes, same egg-shaped torso, same two stubby forelimbs framing a pale belly, same squat hind legs with paddle feet, same tail springing from the same point on the animal's right. Baboon is that figure scaled up, tinted tan and given darker blotches. There is nothing baboon-specific anywhere on it; it reads as a generic macaque/capuchin monkey posed face-on and upright, not a quadruped dog-faced baboon.

MUST-READ 1 (long dog-like muzzle with close-set eyes) — HALF PRESENT, and correct the judge here. The eyes ARE close-set: two small white orbs sitting near the midline of the face with only a narrow bridge between them. Do not touch those. The muzzle is the failure. At 6x the lower face is a rounded ball with a small darker patch bearing two nostril dots and a short curved mouth line — so calling it a 'flat button snout' is fair in effect but slightly wrong in detail (there is a nose and a mouth, they are simply painted flat onto a sphere). There is zero forward projection: no snout mass, no jaw depth, no length from the eyeline to the mouth, no muzzle silhouette breaking the head's circular outline. Because the head is drawn dead face-on, a baboon muzzle can only read here as a long forward-thrust cylinder foreshortened toward the viewer, or the head must be turned to three-quarter/profile. Neither was attempted. The single feature that IS the baboon is absent.

MUST-READ 2 (tail kinked sharply upward at the base then hanging down) — ABSENT, and it fails in two ways, not the one the judge named. Correct: it is a smooth continuous C-curve with no kink or break anywhere along it, exactly the shared family tail. Additional defect the judge missed: the tail ROOT is in the wrong place. It attaches high on the animal's right flank at roughly mid-torso/shoulder height, well forward of and above the rump, so it appears to sprout from the ribcage rather than the hips. And the distal end does not hang — it curls up and inward, ending with the tip raised, so the second half of the note ('then hanging down') is unmet independently of the missing kink. A fix must move the root down to the rump, put a hard angular break just past the base, and drop the remainder vertically.

MUST-READ 3 (cape of long hair over the shoulders in males) — ABSENT, judge correct. At 3x the shoulders are the plain smooth torso outline in the same flat fur as the belly. There is no mane, no fringe, no shaggy break in the silhouette edge, no tonal separation between a shoulder mantle and the back. The only tonal variation on the torso is soft round blotches scattered over the whole trunk, which read as generic mottling, not a cape. The head cap band is a hairline marking, not a shoulder cape, and it is shared with the Capuchin so it cannot carry the identity.

Other observations: feet at 5x are undifferentiated rounded paddles with no toes and no hand/foot distinction, which is wrong for a primate of any kind. Posture is specified 'quadruped' but the figure is drawn upright and frontal with the forelimbs hanging free, so the posture spec is not met either. Aspect reads far squarer than the specified 1.7. Two of three must-reads are wholly absent and the third is half-present; the asset does not read as the named organism.

VERDICT UPHELD, but two of the three stated causes are factually wrong and must not be fixed against.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440; silhouette occupies x148-288, y128-300, so ~140w x 172h). A face-on, hunched, pot-bellied ape blob: round ball head sitting directly on the shoulders with no neck, a dark elliptical cap/brow band across the forehead, two small rounded ears on the sides (left one smaller and partly behind the skull, right one a fuller rounded lobe), pale tan muzzle with two nostril dots and an upturned smile line, normal white-ringed round eyes. Torso is a wide trapezoid with a light rim-light stroke down both flanks and around the belly. Below the belly sit two large dark rounded thigh/knee ellipses that stop ~24px ABOVE the ground line. Outboard of those, two dark limb columns run down the OUTSIDE of the torso and do reach the ground, ending in flat splayed plinth-shaped foot pads. A dark navy cast-shadow ellipse with its own rim highlight sits between the feet and reads almost like a bowl the animal is standing in.

CLAIM 1 -- 'the arms are SHORTER here than on any other asset in the batch, tucked as stubs against the torso'. WRONG on both counts. (a) The arms are not stubs and are not tucked: they are full-height columns descending from the shoulder region all the way to the ground with flat foot pads. (b) They are not the shortest in the batch. Marmoset and Capuchin use the identical flush-limb treatment (measured: same all-blob silhouette, two ground pads, zero arm/torso separation), so the Gibbon is tied with them, not the minimum.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG WITH THE ARMS -- and this is the real defect. The arm columns are drawn FLUSH with the torso silhouette edge: from y164 (shoulder) to y240 the outer contour is a single unbroken line, so the arm has no readable outline of its own and only separates from the body value-wise in the bottom ~35% (y240-300). Compare directly against the other three apes in the same batch, where the arm is a DETACHED column with clear background gaps between it and the torso: Orangutan arms run x124-148 and x296-320, y232-316, giving a ~200px span on a 208px-tall body; Gorilla and Chimpanzee both show the same detached outer columns down to y336. So the batch's arm-span ranking is exactly inverted: Orangutan, Gorilla and Chimpanzee -- whose rows do NOT make arm span the headline -- all show a bigger, clearly readable arm span than the Gibbon, whose note says 'the arm span is the dominant proportion'. The must-read 'arms far longer than the legs, reaching the ground' fails on the 'far longer than the legs' half; the shoulders do not sit higher than the hips and nothing about the proportion reads as brachiator.

CLAIM 2 -- 'no hook hands'. CORRECT AND CONFIRMED at 9x magnification. The two ground contacts are flat, splayed, symmetric pad/plinth shapes, pixel-for-pixel the same foot form used across the family. There is no hook, no elongated curved hand, no finger mass anywhere on the asset.

CLAIM 3 -- 'posture specified upright and rendered as the same squat as the thirteen quadrupeds'. CORRECT. The chassis is verifiably shared with Chimpanzee and Orangutan: same face-on ball head, same dark brow-band ellipse, same eye/nostril/smile stamp, same rim-lit trapezoid torso, same inner thigh ellipses, same plinth feet. Only hue, scale and arm separation change. Row asks for posture: upright; what is drawn is the family crouch.

MUST-READ TALLY. (1) arms far longer than legs, reaching the ground -- FAIL (they reach the ground but read as no span at all). (2) long hook-shaped hands -- ABSENT. (3) no tail at all -- PRESENT and correct; the silhouette is genuinely tailless, and this is a real differentiator since Capuchin and the other monkeys in the batch do carry visible tails. One of three identity must-reads present, and the one the note calls dominant is the one that reads least. The asset reads as a small generic brown ape-blob interchangeable with the Chimpanzee, not as a gibbon.

FIX DIRECTION: detach the arm columns from the torso outline with real background gap (at least the Orangutan's separation), start them at the shoulder not the hip, extend them so the hand pads land at or below the foot line while the thigh ellipses stay clearly shorter, and replace the flat plinth pad with a curved elongated hook hand. Do not shorten or lengthen a 'stub' -- there is no stub to work from.

Round ball head with a dark elliptical 'beret' cap across the crown that reads as a hat brim rather than fur; two large round paddle ears set on the sides at eye height; two big white-ringed eyes; a very short flat muzzle with two nostril dots and an upcurved smiley mouth line. But it is pure shading: the silhouette below the jaw is a smooth arc that runs straight into a concave notch at the shoulder, with zero added mass, zero widening of the lower head, and no beard fringe of any kind. It also floats: it emerges from behind the left hip with no visible tail base and sweeps up and forward into a plain C. So 'no bare gripping tip' is confirmed; 'no thickness' is not accurate and should not be the fix instruction - the fix is taper + base mass + a pale bare distal segment.

'READS AS A RECOLOURED CAPUCHIN' - CONFIRMED IN SOURCE, not just visually. port/v2/packages/art/src/faunaoverrides2.ts line 1358 is `'Howler Monkey': (c,g,p,n) => primate(c,g,p,{hue:'#3b2b22', build:'monkey', tail:true}, n)` - byte-identical to line 1360 `'Capuchin': ... {hue:'#6b4a30', build:'monkey', tail:true}` and line 1359 Spider Monkey, differing only in the hue hex. I tried to refute this and could not — the verdict stands, but TWO of the three stated causes are wrong and would send a fixer at the wrong pixels. What is actually on canvas (440x440; creature bbox x116-298, y128-295): a squat, barrel-chested pale-grey ape sitting face-on, torso ~104px wide x ~108px tall, with four short uniformly-dark-grey stub limbs and a dark C-hook tail off the left hip. It reads as a macaque or a juvenile gorilla, not a langur.

MUST-READ 1, 'tail far longer than the body' — ABSENT, but NOT for the reason claimed. The judge said the tail is 'clearly shorter than the body'; that is measurably false. I traced the tail centreline through the mask: tip (154,149) -> (133,164) -> (121,191) apex of the bulge -> (137,221) -> merges into the rump at ~(158,230), root approx (175,235). Straightened arc length ~130px. The trunk (shoulder y167 to seat y275) is ~108px, head+body (y128-275) is ~147px. The real defect is threefold: (a) it is nowhere near the ~1.5-2x head-body a langur needs; (b) it is THICK — ~8-9px constant width, no taper — so it reads as a heavy macaque/howler hook rather than a langur's whip-thin line; (c) it is coiled into a tight C that stays inside the animal's own height instead of sweeping out past the silhouette, so even the length it has does not read. Fix = a long tapering sweep that exits the bbox, not merely 'make it longer'.

MUST-READ 2, 'black face and hands framed by pale grey fur' — HALF absent, and the judge's description of the other half is wrong. Face: correct that there is no black mask. Sampled face RGB (237,152)=(157,143,130), lower face luminance ~105-140, against cranium/coat luminance ~150-185 — the face is a barely-darker warm grey, no mask read. The ONLY dark element on the head is a horizontal band across the brow (y142-148, x~214-254, luminance ~75) which reads as a hat brim / brow ridge, not a face mask, and it is mid-dark grey (RGB ~75), not black. HANDS: the judge is flatly wrong that these are 'the same mid-grey as the coat'. Hand (210,245)=(70,71,68) and foot (196,272)=(66,67,65) against coat (237,200)=(181,175,157) — a very strong contrast. But it does not deliver the must-read either, because the dark tone covers the ENTIRE limb (shoulder to fingertip, and the tail too) as generic chassis limb shading, so there is no hand-specific marking; and at 8x the hands are featureless rounded stubs with no digits. So the correct statement is: hands ARE dark, face is NOT, and the dark is limb-wide rather than a hand marking.

MUST-READ 3, 'slender long-limbed build with a crest on the crown' — ABSENT, and the judge did not mention it at all. The build is the opposite of slender: a wide barrel torso (bbox 183w x 168h, wider than tall) on short stubby limbs, packet asks aspect 1.4. And the crown silhouette from y128-140 is a smooth unbroken dome — no peak, no notch, no tuft. The dark brow band is on the forehead, not the crown, and does not break the outline, so nothing in the silhouette reads as a crest.

Things I checked that are FINE and should not be touched: eyes are correct (small whites with dark pupils, 'normal' per packet); ears are two round side flaps at x~208-215 and x~258-268, y150-160, present and legible; posture is quadruped/seated as specified; the pale grey coat with soft mottling is the right colour family. Net: zero of three identity must-reads read, and the silhouette is the shared stocky-ape chassis. FAIL upheld.

The brown trunk alone is x135-337, y170-200 = 203x31 = 6.55:1, but that trunk is a near-constant-height 30px parallel-sided strip that is never seen alone - it sits inside a grey collar that carries the read. So the judge's '~3.5:1' is right in substance (actual 3.9:1) and the 'not eel-like at all' verdict is correct. CORRECTION 1 - the halo is NOT offset. Column profile at x=230 top-to-bottom: y158-166 flat grey (59,62,69), y167-168 pale rim stroke (94..115), y169-201 brown body (95..125), y201-202 pale rim stroke (128,128,132), y203-212 flat grey (59,62,69). What it actually is: a flat, untextured, hard-edged dark-grey collar of uniform thickness wrapped around the whole body and separated from it by a 2px pale rim, terminating in an abrupt vertical cut just behind the eye (x~305). It reads as a double outline / ghost. It is almost certainly MEANT to be the continuous median fin fold (dorsal+anal running the length and merging into the tail, which would be correct lungfish anatomy and would justify the extra depth) - it does taper into the tail wedge at x~130 - but with zero ray texture, zero membrane variation, perfect top/bottom symmetry and a flat single value it reads as an aura, not as fin. At 8-10x the tail is a SOLID triangular wedge, x117-140 (23px long) by 28px tall at its base, tapering to a clean sharp point at (117,185). It is pointed and continuous. Its real defect is VALUE: the wedge is rgb(30,31,36)-(46,54,62), i.e. near-black, against a body of rgb(103,89,83) mid-brown, with a hard value break at the join, so it reads as a black spike pasted onto the end rather than tissue continuous with the fish. Separately there ARE ~7 hair-thin filaments radiating in a fan from the wedge tip out to x~85 - I found them only under 4x contrast boost: they are rgb(8,12,18) against bg rgb(5,6,12), a delta of 3/255, i.e. geometrically present and optically invisible. Those ghost filaments are what produced the judge's 'stranded scribble' impression at 1:1. CORRECTION 3 - the limb fins are NOT absent. Behind the head at x258-295, y175-208 there is a large and clearly visible paired-fin structure: a broad rounded FLESHY LOBE/paddle bulging well past the ventral outline on a slender stalk running up to the shoulder, plus a fan of ~7 dark straight rays radiating forward-and-down from a hinge near (268,175). Saying 'entirely absent' would send a fixer to add fins that are already there; the actual instruction is 'replace the lobed paddle with two pairs of thin whip filaments'. WHAT DOES READ: smooth scaled skin (fine stipple/dot texture over the whole trunk) and a small blunt head - the head end is a blunt rounded cap with a small dark pupil in a bright white ring and a faint mouth line, ~35px of 223 = headFrac ~0.15, matching the row. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG (the fix list):

1. SCUTES ABSENT — CONFIRMED, and the proof is stronger than the original claim. mustRead #1 is 'rows of bony scutes ridging the back and flanks'. The flank carries a uniform all-over checkerboard of light square dots covering the entire body from gill to peduncle. It is not organised into rows, has no dorsal midline row, no lateral row, no ventral row, and no keels. Critically, the topline SILHOUETTE is a single smooth clean arc with a bright rim highlight and zero serration or bumps — a sturgeon's scute row must break the outline, and here nothing does. The decisive evidence: the IDENTICAL dot/checker mesh appears on Paddlefish in the same family batch, whose own mustRead is 'smooth SCALELESS skin'. The texture is therefore a shared chassis fill that carries no species meaning for anyone. Fix must add discrete raised plates that deform the dorsal and lateral silhouette, not more stipple.

2. BARBELS ABSENT — CONFIRMED. At 7x with 3.2x gain there is not a single filament under, beside or in front of the snout. The snout underside is a clean straight taper. mustRead #2 asks for 'four barbels under a long pointed snout'; the snout half IS delivered (a long, sharply pointed cone, roughly a quarter of body length, correctly wedge-shaped in profile), so only the barbels need adding — four of them on the VENTRAL surface, set back from the tip, ahead of the mouth.

3. THE SNOUT-TIP LOZENGE — real defect, but described imprecisely. It is MID-GREY (lighter than the dark dorsal fin), not 'dark grey', and it is not fully detached: the cone's point does penetrate a few pixels into the ellipse's left end, so the two overlap at a single point. The failure is not a gap, it is placement and reading — a smooth tilted ellipse balanced on the very apex of the nose, meeting the head at a point too narrow to read as continuous flesh, so it scans as a foreign blob stuck on the nose rather than as anatomy. It is also anatomically misplaced regardless of attachment: a sturgeon's mouth is a ventral, protrusible tube set well BACK on the underside of the head, never at the rostrum tip. Fix is to remove it from the tip and rebuild the mouth as a ventral feature behind the barbels.

WHAT THE ORIGINAL JUDGE GOT WRONG — DO NOT 'FIX' THE TAIL:

4. The claim that 'the tail is a small symmetric fork, not an upturned asymmetric one' is incorrect and must be struck. Measured on the brightened 7x crop, the fork junction sits at the peduncle and the UPPER lobe runs roughly 1.8x the length of the lower lobe (~495px vs ~279px at that magnification), sweeping clearly up and back above the body axis while the lower lobe is short and drops only slightly below it. That is a heterocercal, shark-like, upturned asymmetric tail — exactly what mustRead #3 asks for. Nor is it small: it spans about 40% of body length. mustRead #3 is SATISFIED and is the one thing this asset gets right.

CHASSIS NOTE (family-level, worth recording): stripped of the snout cone and the tail, the Sturgeon and the Paddlefish are the same drawing — identical lens-shaped body outline, identical low arched ray-fanned dorsal sail sitting above the back, identical small triangular pectoral fan in the same position, identical curved gill arc, identical single lateral line, identical flank stipple. Only the rostrum and caudal shape were varied.

BAND: FAIL upheld. Two of three must-reads are absent (scutes entirely, barbels entirely) and the head terminates in a misread blob; what remains reads as a generic pointed-snout fish on the shared primitive-fish chassis, not as a sturgeon.

WHAT I ACTUALLY SAW (440x440 canvas, decoded and pixel-measured, plus 5x-14x crops of head, tail and upper-left corner):

1) SILHOUETTE - the judge's 'soft continuous ovoid' is FACTUALLY WRONG. I measured the bright body mass: bbox x165-299, y170-240, i.e. 135 long x 71 deep. Per-row extents show the front edge pinned at x=297-299 for y=190..222 and the rear edge pinned at x=165-167 for y=186..226 - roughly 55% of the body depth on each end is a DEAD-STRAIGHT VERTICAL edge. Top and bottom edges are likewise flat across the middle ~60% of the length. The outline is a rounded rectangle / superellipse with a corner radius of about 18-20px (~26% of body depth). It is emphatically NOT an ellipse, and it is NOT the Pufferfish outline stretched: I rendered the sibling Pufferfish.png side by side and that one is a true continuous ovoid with curvature everywhere. So the box PROPORTION is attempted and half-delivered.

2) WHY IT STILL FAILS THE IDENTITY MUST-READ - 'rigid armoured box-shaped carapace' needs armour, not just a brick outline, and there is zero armour language anywhere. At 14x on the upper-left corner the surface is a stipple of small horizontal dash-scales (ordinary fish scale mesh) running unbroken around the rounded corner, over a soft airbrush gradient with brown blotches and a single cream rim-light hugging the curve. There is NO hexagonal/polygonal plate tessellation, NO corner keel or ridge line, NO value break between a top plane and a side plane (nothing that would state a squared or triangular cross-section), and no hard corner anywhere - every corner is smoothly filleted. The one long horizontal line across the flank is a lateral line and the one curved vertical line behind the head is a gill/operculum arc; neither reads as a plate seam. Net read: a soft, scaly, brick-shaped generic fish, not a rigid box of bone. Aspect is also over-long at 1.90 measured against the spec's 1.6, which pushes it further toward 'stretched normal fish'.

3) TAIL - judge is right that it fails, described roughly right. The caudal is a broad rounded fan with radiating spoke-rays, standing about 85% of the body depth tall, attached directly to the flat rear edge at a single point with no peduncle. Nowhere near 'tiny fin poking out of a shell'. Same for the dorsal and anal, which are sizeable soft lobes emerging continuously from the outline rather than small stubs protruding past a carapace rim.

4) FACE - judge's 'no mouth or pursed lips at all' is WRONG. There IS a mouth: a thin dark down-curved hairline arc about 20px long low on the snout (visible at 12x, roughly source x760-870 region of the head crop), plus a short dark tick below the eye. What is absent is any PURSING - no lip volume, no protruding beak, no highlight or shadow giving the mouth mass; it is a single hairline stroke that disappears at thumbnail size. Judge's 'small flat eye dot' is also WRONG in detail: the eye is a properly constructed glyph - dark pupil, cream/white sclera ring, and a specular highlight at upper-left. Its real defect is SCALE: it is ~9px across on a 135px body (~6.7% of length), which fails the spec's 'eyes: prominent' / 'big eyes'.

5) FAMILY/CHASSIS - the judge's conclusion is right in substance even though the outline claim is wrong. Everything EXCEPT the outline is shared verbatim with Pufferfish.png: identical eye glyph at identical relative size and placement, identical dorsal and anal lobe shapes, identical pectoral fan with radiating rays, identical caudal fan with the same spoke pattern, identical gill arc, identical cream rim-light along the top, identical blotch vocabulary. Only the outline (rounded-rect vs ellipse), the scale-mesh direction (diamond vs horizontal bands) and the hue (yellow vs olive-tan) differ. Two of two members of this family are one chassis.

FIX DIRECTION: do not redraw the silhouette from scratch - the rounded-rect proportion is the one thing that is already right. Shorten it toward 1.6, then add the armour: hard-cornered facets with a distinct top-plane/side-plane value break, a visible dorsolateral keel ridge running the length, hexagonal plate tessellation replacing the scale stipple, and the fins reduced to small stubs protruding past the carapace rim. Enlarge the eye substantially and give the mouth pursed lip volume rather than a hairline.

rows.readsAs: an ordinary pet rabbit, in brown
rows.defect: The whole identity of a hare is absent. The body is a pudgy round egg, not lean or angular, and the hind legs are two short dark pegs with no hock, no elongated foot and no rangy thigh — the animal is shorter-legged than the Rabbit asset it is supposed to out-run. The ears are dark brown over their full length with no distinct black tip, so the one marking called out is not readable either. Side by side with Rabbit.png this is the same silhouette in a warmer hue.
