rows.verifyWhy:
I read the PNG at full size and then re-cropped and 4x-upscaled the ears, head and leg region, and pixel-measured the figure against Rabbit.png and Jackrabbit.png. The FAIL stands, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and must not be fixed as written.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A warm mid-brown cartoon rabbit in a crouched three-quarter-front pose on a soft ellipse shadow. Torso is a single smooth egg with a convex topline and a pale rim-light arc running over the shoulder; a spiral swirl mark sits on the rear haunch. Head is a separate sphere with one large white-ringed eye with a dark pupil and a bright catchlight, a short muzzle, a 4-line whisker fan, and two white rectangular incisors below the nose. Two upright ears, dark-brown outer with a salmon-pink inner well.

CORRECTION 1 - THE HIND LIMB IS NOT A FEATURELESS PEG. At 4x the rear limb is clearly a two-part boot: a thick thigh/shank mass descending from the hip and angling forward-down, and then an elongated flat foot laid along the ground with a defined heel and toe. There IS a bend at the ankle and there IS a foot. The front limb is the short peg the judge described (a stub with a small rounded pad). So the fix is not 'add a hock/thigh/foot' - those exist. The defect is that the whole hind limb is buried under the belly: measured dark-limb vertical extent is only ~36px against a 182px-wide body (0.20), and the belly line sits almost on the shadow. It reads as a crouch, not as a rangy stander.

CORRECTION 2 - 'SHORTER-LEGGED THAN THE RABBIT' IS ONLY MARGINALLY TRUE AND MISSES THE POINT. Normalised leg extent: Hare 36/182 = 0.20, Rabbit 39/171 = 0.23. That is noise. The real finding is that Hare, Rabbit and Jackrabbit are ONE CHASSIS: identical egg torso with the identical topline rim-light arc, identical haunch swirl, identical head sphere with the identical eye, identical 4-whisker fan and identical twin-incisor rectangle, identical hind boot and front peg, identical shadow ellipse. Only ear length, overall scale and hue change. There is no proportional leg differentiation at all, in either direction.

CORRECTION 3 - THE LONG-EAR MUST-READ IS ACTUALLY DELIVERED. The judge implies the ears read as an ordinary pet rabbit's. They do not. Ear height / body width measures Rabbit 52/171 = 0.30, Hare 80/182 = 0.44, Jackrabbit 92/162 = 0.57 - a correct, readable family ladder, and the Hare's ears are visibly and unmistakably longer than the Rabbit's. That half of must-read 1 passes and should not be 'fixed'.

CONFIRMED DEFECT A - NO BLACK TIP. Verified at 4x: the outer ear is one flat unmodulated dark brown (~#4a3a2b) from base to apex, with a smooth pink inner well. There is no darker cap, no terminal band, no tonal shift anywhere near the tip. Must-read 'black-tipped' is wholly absent.

CONFIRMED DEFECT B - NO LEAN ANGULAR BODY, AND THE PROPORTION IS INVERTED. Torso-only measurement: Hare 182 wide x 98 tall = 1.86; Rabbit 171 x 86 = 1.99. The Hare's torso is proportionally ROUNDER than the Rabbit's - the opposite of the spec note 'leggier and rangier than a rabbit'. The topline is a single unbroken convex curve with no shoulder, no rise over the hip, no waist, no angularity anywhere.

BAND. One of three must-reads readable (long ears), and that one only half-delivered because the black tip is missing; the other two ('long rangy hind legs', 'lean angular body') are absent and the body proportion actively contradicts the reference note. The asset reads as the family's generic rabbit chassis in a slightly darker brown with the ears stretched. FAIL upheld.

FIX DIRECTION. Keep the ear length. Add a dark terminal cap to the top ~20% of each ear outer. Do not rebuild the hind limb from scratch - extend and expose it: raise the belly line off the shadow, lengthen the shank so the hock stands clear of the torso silhouette, and drop the elongated foot forward so it reads as a separate ground contact. Flatten the topline and pull a waist in behind the ribs so the torso stops being the Rabbit egg.

WHAT I MEASURED (440x440 png, pixel-scanned silhouette; creature bbox x133-296, y85-327, so 164 wide x 243 tall).

1) EARS -- the judge is WRONG. The claim 'only marginally longer than the head, not enormous' does not survive measurement. The ear pair runs from y=85 (tips) to the skull join at y~203: 118px of ear. The skull runs x214-296 (76-82px long) and y202-270 (68px tall). Do not shorten anything here; this is the one identity cue that landed. (Missing black tips, but that is the Hare's mustRead, not this one.)

2) HIND LEGS -- the judge is HALF wrong on anatomy, right on the conclusion. 'Thin stubs under the belly with no thigh, hock or foot' is not what is drawn. At 10x the rear limb is a distinct L-shaped bent limb: a thick dark shank descending from under the rump at x159-185, y288, angling down-forward, then breaking at a clear hock into a flat forward-pointing plantigrade foot that runs along the ground line to y=327. There is also a pale circular haunch disc on the flank (centre ~x170,y277, ~50px across) standing in for the thigh. So hock and foot EXIST. What actually fails is scale and identity: the whole visible limb is only ~40px on a 243px animal (16%), it is tucked entirely under the belly, the 'thigh' is a flat shaded circle rather than a modelled propulsive mass, and the foot is short and stubby where a jackrabbit's defining hind foot is long and elongated. 'Very long powerful hind legs' does NOT read. Fix the proportion and the foot length, not the absence of parts.

3) EYE -- the judge is right on placement, slightly unfair on size. The eye is not a bare dot: it is a proper eye, black pupil + white sclera ring + specular highlight, spanning x252-265 / y224-237, ~13-14px, i.e. ~20% of head height. But its placement is exactly as described: centre (258, 231) sits at 42% down the 68px skull (essentially mid-height, not high) and at 59% back-to-front along the 76px skull (FORWARD of centre, not far back). The mustRead 'large eye set high and far back on the skull' fails on both position terms and is only borderline on size.

4) THE CHASSIS FINDING IS CORRECT AND IS THE REAL DEFECT. Read against Hare.png and Rabbit.png in the same batch, these are unmistakably ONE body with parameters nudged: identical rounded topline arc, identical rump with the same pale haunch disc, identical fused L-stub limbs with the same forward foot, identical skull lobe + short muzzle + two-tooth white incisor block + 3-4 straight whisker rays, identical two-tone dark-outer/pink-inner ear. Only the fill hue differs (Jackrabbit lightest tan, Hare mid-brown, Rabbit greyer brown) plus a small parametric stretch -- Jackrabbit is the tallest/narrowest (164x243 vs Hare 185x230, Rabbit 174x168) with the longest ears. That stretch is real, so 'the Hare chassis with the fill lightened' understates it by a hair, but the shared-body verdict stands.

5) PROPORTION MISSES the original judge did not raise. Packet asks aspect 1.5 (long and low); measured bbox aspect is 0.67, and even excluding the ears the body is only 164x130 = 1.26. Packet asks headFrac 0.28; the skull is ~80px against a ~164px body, i.e. ~0.5. The oversized round head on a short compact body is what makes this read as a pet bunny rather than a lean desert hare.

WHAT IT READS AS: a generic long-eared pet rabbit. One of three mustReads present. FAIL stands.

The only white on the head is the sclera ring of the single large eye. There is one thin 1px dark stroke running from just below/behind the eye down-forward onto the muzzle, but it is a jaw/mouth seam line, not a tear-stripe — a tear-stripe must be a broad rust band on a white ground running eye-to-mouth-corner, and there is no white ground for it to sit on.

But that dark occupies only the bottom ~15% of each limb and its shape is a HOOF, not a stocking. It therefore not only fails to deliver the black-legged read, it makes the wrong-organism read worse. The belly is plain rust identical to the back; the darkness under the barrel is cast shadow/background, not black fur.

SILHOUETTE: confirmed barrel-chested, flat level topline with no arched back and no raised rump, four straight tubular column legs, short thick neck with the head carried above the shoulder line, and an over-long tapering muzzle ending in a terminal nostril dot (a red panda's muzzle is short and blunt). Combined with the ram-horn crescent and the hoof-capped feet, the organism reads as an orange lamb or young ram — the original judge's call is correct.

No hidden or small-but-present feature was found that would rescue this. Fix order: (1) paint the white face mask — white muzzle, white cheek patches, white brow arcs and white ear rims — and lay the rust tear-stripes on it from eye to mouth corner; (2) kill the ram-horn crescent and replace it with two upright rounded white-fringed ears; (3) run jet-black up all four legs to shoulder/hip and across the whole belly, and remove the hoof caps in favour of plantigrade paws; (4) fatten the tail to roughly body-depth thickness with a fur-broken silhouette and lighten the rings toward cream; (5) shorten the muzzle and drop the head so the topline runs shoulder-high-to-rump rather than neck-up.

The two dark ovals below the eyes read as blank nostrils and the white-ringed googly eyes are far too prominent for the small eyes the row asks for.
rows.fix: Clip the speckle pass to the disc path so no marks land outside the silhouette, then rebuild the disc outline as a rhombic wing — concave trailing margins sweeping back from the wingtips to a narrow tail base with a pair of small pelvic fins — instead of a straight-cut triangle.
rows.verifyWhy:
I decoded the 440x440 PNG and re-read it at 3x-8x zoom over the disc, the upper-right edge, the trailing margin and the tail tip.

CONFIRMED (with a correction to the description): the marking pass is genuinely NOT clipped to the silhouette. A column scan at x=336..372 finds non-background pixels sitting 14-31px ABOVE the first solid-body pixel, i.e. a cloud of ~4-5 soft round blobs floating in open water off the upper-right leading edge, spanning roughly x 330-375, y 128-172. The judge's word 'dark' is wrong: these are the LIGHT speckle brush rendered at low opacity over near-black water (measured luminance 15-21 against a background of 8-10), so they read as dim grey smudges, not dark spots. They are also not fully stranded - the cluster straddles the edge, with two blobs wholly outside and two or three half on / half off the rim. Fix is a clip to the disc path on the speckle pass; nothing else in the image leaks (the trailing margin at 8x shows speckles cut cleanly at the edge).

REFUTED - the identity claim. The judge says the disc is 'a straight-cut triangular wedge with no wing curvature' and that 'the ray read is carried almost entirely by the barbed whip tail'. Both are wrong. The disc is a broad delta with a blunt apex at top-centre (snout), and BOTH upper margins are convex arcs sweeping down-and-out to lateral wingtips at approx (148,215) left and (391,212) right; the right leading edge even carries a bright rim highlight along the curve. The trailing margins then run back inboard from each wingtip and converge in a shallow V at a small notch at bottom-centre where the tail attaches. That is the correct top-down topology of a ray disc: snout forward, pectorals flaring, tail exiting the rear. The disc is ~270 x 110px (about 2.4:1), matching the aspect 2 row.

All three mustReads are present and readable:
  - 'flattened disc of wing-like pectoral fins fused to the head' - present. One continuous fused delta, no separate head, no neck, wingtips taper to thin points.
  - 'eyes on top with gill slits and mouth underneath' - present. Two eyes sit clearly on the DORSAL surface just behind the leading edge, plus two dark oval spots inboard/below them reading as spiracles. Gills and mouth are correctly not visible because the view is from above; the judge did not mention this mustRead at all.
  - 'slender trailing tail' - present. A long slender whip about 1.4x disc width sweeps from the bottom-centre notch down-left, ending in a pale cream barbed spine (a flat arrowhead with hatched serrations at 4x).

What the judge IS right about, as polish rather than identity failure: the trailing margins are dead-straight cuts with zero undulation or concavity; the wingtips are sharp acute corners instead of the rounded/swept points a real ray carries; and there are no pelvic-fin lobes flanking the tail base (that notch at 8x is a bare V). Note pelvic fins are not on the mustRead line, so their absence is not a missing must-read.

Additional polish notes the judge missed: the central shading gives the disc a domed 'hood/tent' silhouette rather than a flat wafer, which is the one thing that softens the ray read; the barb at the tail tip is an oversized flat cream arrowhead that reads a little like a paper dart against the near-black tail; the tail sweeps FORWARD across the front of the animal rather than trailing behind it; and the two dorsal spots below the eyes read as nostrils, which on a ray are ventral (they should be spiracles, sited just behind and outboard of the eyes).

Band: POLISH, not FAIL. The organism reads as a stingray at full size and every mustRead is legible; the defects are one clipping bug and a set of margin-quality misses. Ranked fixes: (1) clip the speckle pass to the disc path, (2) round the wingtips and put a gentle concave undulation in the trailing margins, (3) add small pelvic lobes at the tail base, (4) flatten the central dome so the disc reads as a plate not a hood.

rows.readsAs: a grey draped mound / closed umbrella with cartoon eyes and a string; at best a generic cartoon stingray, never an eagle ray
rows.defect: Both must-reads that separate an eagle ray from any other ray are absent. There is no pointed duck-bill snout — the head end is a plain blunt curve, and nothing projects ahead of the body at all. The whip tail is present but is roughly the same length as the body, not far longer. The disc reads narrower than it is deep, the opposite of a ray. It is a sharp angular VERTEX - the two straight leading edges meet at a ~68 degree point at (249,128), with a bright rim highlight running down the right edge from it. The defect is that this vertex is merely the corner of the disc, never modelled as a head; a fix must ADD a duck-bill rostrum forward of that vertex, not round off a curve that isn't there.

MUST-READ 3 (sharply pointed wings, often white-spotted) - THE CLAIM IS FALSE IN BOTH PARTS. The wings are not 'one smooth convex arc folded downward'. There are two distinct acute lateral tips: at the left tip (136,211) the leading edge leaves at -36 deg and the trailing edge at +30 deg, an included angle of ~66 deg; at the right tip (364,211) the included angle is ~55 deg. And a wingspan absolutely does read - 229 px span against 107 px depth is 2.1:1. The white spotting the reference row asks for is also PRESENT and abundant (the pale ovals over the whole disc). This is the one eagle-ray cue the asset actually carries and it should not be touched.

MUST-READ 2 (long whip tail far longer than the body) - FAILS, but not by the amount stated. The tail is not 'only body-length'. Its arc from (229,236) to (77,311) is ~175 px: 1.6x the 107 px disc depth, but only 0.76x the 229 px disc width. It under-delivers 'far longer', it is not merely body-length.

CHASSIS FINDING CONFIRMED AND QUANTIFIED. Eagle Ray vs Manta Ray silhouette IoU = 0.926, and their bounding boxes agree to within 1 px on every edge (Eagle x75-364 y128-311 widest span 136-364; Manta x74-365 y127-311 widest span 136-365). They are the same drawing in a different hue - Manta is a colder navy with a couple of extra bubble blobs at upper left, Eagle is mid grey-blue with the spot field. Stingray is the same chassis scaled ~1.2x (bbox x30-409 y102-337, span 276) in tan, with a longer tail carrying a white barb - IoU 0.566 against Eagle purely because of that scale-up, not because the shape differs. So all three rays in this batch are one tent-shaped pony. Because the snout is the single feature that separates an eagle ray from a manta, its absence plus the byte-near-identical outline means this card reads as 'generic ray' and specifically as the same organism as the Manta Ray card. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a dark blue-grey draped mound with googly eyes — the identical shape to the Eagle Ray, only darker
rows.defect: The packet's own note warns against a near-side view, and that is exactly what was drawn: the wings are folded down into a drooping skirt so the huge triangular wingspan — the single feature that makes a manta a manta — never appears. There are no cephalic horn lobes flanking the head, and no wide terminal mouth; the front of the head is a featureless blunt curve with cartoon eyes sitting on top like a stingray's. The wings are not triangular or pointed, just one smooth convex arc. The silhouette is indistinguishable from the Eagle Ray in this same batch, so nothing but hue tells the two apart.
rows.fix: Draw from above/front with the pectorals spread into two long sharply pointed triangles wider than the body is long, and put two forward-projecting horn-like cephalic lobes on either side of a wide rectangular terminal mouth at the front of the head.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and one is understated. WHAT I ACTUALLY SEE (440x440; creature bbox x=74..366, y=126..312, i.e. 293 wide x 187 tall, ~18,200 body px): a single smooth blue-grey DOME — a low cone / parasol / limpet cap — with a lit ridge running from an apex near (248,127) down-right to a corner at (366,211) carrying a bright white rim highlight. Two small round eyes with white sclera rings and black pupils sit ON TOP of the dome at ~(215,157) and ~(282,157), both facing the viewer, each with a dark oval spiracle immediately below and outboard of it. Body is stippled with pale bokeh-style spots. A thin whip tail exits a small notch at the bottom centre ~(232,236) and curves down-left to (74,300); an elliptical drop shadow sits under it.

CORRECTION 1 — 'near-side view' is wrong. This is NOT a side view. It is a front/three-quarter DORSAL view of a disc whose pectorals are drooped downward into a bell, so the disc reads as a mushroom cap seen from slightly above-front. The failure is real but the cause is 'wings drooped into a cone' (the wing plane is rotated to point down, killing the span), not 'the camera is at the side'. A fix that only rotates the camera will not fix this — the wing plane has to be flattened out.

CORRECTION 2 — 'the pectorals are folded into a drooping skirt [with no points]' is overstated. I zoomed both lateral extremes at 10x with contrast boosted. There IS a corner on each side: a fairly acute ~40 degree tip at (366,211) where the white leading-edge rim meets the trailing edge, and a shallower, slightly blunted corner at ~(136,213) on the left. So the outline is a broad low cone with two corners, not a fully rounded skirt. It still fails the must-read: these are the corners of a cone, not 'huge triangular pointed wings wider than the body is long'. There is no wing that reads as a separate swept, scythe-tipped appendage; there is no leading-edge sweep, no wing/body distinction, and the span never exceeds the drawn mass in a way a viewer would call a wingspan.

CONFIRMED — no cephalic lobes, no terminal mouth. I contrast-boosted the entire body (3.4x gain) and inspected the head front and the whole lower edge at up to 9x. There is no mouth line, no mouth aperture, no pair of forward horn lobes anywhere. IMPORTANT TRAP: two grey circular blobs float just off the upper-LEFT edge at roughly (150,145) and (155,165), and could be mistaken for cephalic lobes. They are NOT — they are ambient bokeh particles: they are disconnected from the silhouette (outside the alpha mask), they are dimmer than the body, and the Eagle Ray in this same batch carries the identical particle motif mirrored onto its right side. Do not 'fix' those into horns; real cephalic lobes must be drawn as two forward-projecting paddles flanking a wide, straight, terminal mouth slit at the front of the head.

CONFIRMED — stingray-style eyes on top, plus stingray-style spiracles. The eye+spiracle pair layout is exactly the dorsal arrangement the Stingray row calls for, on the animal whose note explicitly says 'mouth is at the front of the head, not underneath as in stingrays'.

CONFIRMED AND QUANTIFIED — one chassis with the Eagle Ray. I built alpha masks of both and measured: Manta bbox 293x187, Eagle bbox 290x184, silhouette IoU = 0.9227. Same dome, same apex ridge, same white rim on the same side, same two ringed eyes at the same height, same two spiracles, same tail exit point and same tail curve. They differ only in hue (Manta a colder/darker slate, Eagle a lighter blue-grey) and in the random spot scatter. The Stingray (IoU 0.571 vs Manta) is the SAME dome again, just larger and tan, and is the only one of the three that earns a distinguishing feature — the pale barb near its tail tip. So the family is one chassis in three colours, and the Eagle Ray fails its own must-read ('pointed duck-bill snout jutting ahead of the wings') on the identical geometry.

SCORECARD against the reference row — must-read 1 (huge triangular pointed wings wider than body is long): ABSENT. Must-read 2 (two horn-like cephalic lobes flanking a wide terminal mouth): ABSENT, and the head instead carries the stingray dorsal eye/spiracle set the note forbids. Must-read 3 (thin whip tail with no barb): PRESENT and correct — the tail is a clean thin whip, barbless, clearly distinct from the Stingray's barbed tail. One of three identity must-reads readable, and the two that are missing are the two that make a manta a manta. The asset reads as a generic domed ray or a parasol, indistinguishable from its batch-mate. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a stingray — the tan colour, spotted skin, top-mounted eyes and barbed whip tail get a stranger to the right answer
rows.defect: It gets there on colour and tail rather than on form. The disc is not a flat kite of fused pectorals: it is the same drooping rounded mound as the other two, so the wing spread and the kite corners never read, and the body looks deeper than it is wide. The barb is a single pale spearhead stuck on the very tip of the tail rather than a serrated spine set on the tail's upper surface. Eyes are correctly on top, but they are oversized white cartoon discs and the grey ovals beneath them read as a second pair of eyes. The tail also emerges from under the belly rather than from a defined tail base at the rear of the disc.
rows.fix: Flatten and spread the pectorals into a wide kite-shaped disc seen from above, wider than long with clear side corners, and move the barb onto the upper surface of the tail a third of the way along, serrated rather than a spearhead tip.

rows.readsAs: a tall yellow discus / freshwater angelfish
rows.defect: The deep striped disc and the long trailing filaments off the dorsal and anal are genuinely there and read well, but there is no mouth drawn at all and no spine on the gill cover, and the disc is drawn tall-and-narrow with vertical stripes so it reads as the FRESHWATER triangular angelfish the note explicitly rules out rather than a Pomacanthid. The 'tail' is a flat trapezoid stuck on the right edge with no peduncle joining it to the body.
rows.fix: Give it a small terminal mouth and a visible backward-pointing spine on the gill cover, and round the disc toward circular with a horizontal or arcing band pattern so it stops reading as a freshwater angel.

rows.readsAs: a tiny needlefish or gar
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. The head is not a blunt bulldog head — it tapers to a sharp point with the eye stuck on the very tip; there are no cirri tufts anywhere above the eyes; and the dorsal is not a single long continuous fin down the whole back but four sawtooth triangles confined to the middle third, the same crest stamp used on the disc fish. The whole animal is also rendered at roughly a fifth of the frame width, a fragment floating in a large empty canvas with its cast shadow detached far below it.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a short, tall, blunt bulldog snout with the bulging eyes set high on it and a pair of branched cirri tufts rising above them, and replace the sawtooth crest with one unbroken low dorsal running nape to tail base.
rows.verifyWhy:
I read the PNG at full size, then decoded it and re-rendered two nearest-neighbour crops (7x on the whole animal, 18x on the head) plus a pixel row-profile, so every number below is measured, not guessed. VERDICT UPHELD — but three of the four factual claims in the original finding are WRONG and must not be used as the fix brief.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Fish + fins occupy x 123-316, y 175-214 in a 440x440 frame. Facing RIGHT (eye at right, caudal fan at left).

CORRECTION 1 - the head does NOT taper to a sharp point and the eye is NOT on the tip. The snout end is a BLUNT, essentially squared-off rounded cap: the silhouette holds full body depth (right edge x=316) across rows 197-204 and only rounds off in the last 2-3 rows. There is no taper at all. The eye is a small white-ringed disc centred near x=300, y=193, i.e. ~16 px BEHIND the snout tip and set high in the upper half of the head. So 'high-set eye near a blunt front end' is literally present. What is missing is head MASS: the head is exactly the same depth as the trunk, with no steep forehead, no jowl, no thick lip, and NO MOUTH DRAWN ANYWHERE. Only a single thin curved opercular arc at x~272 hints that a head region exists. The mustRead asks for a blunt BULLDOG head; the drawing gives a blunt tube end. Half-met, and the missing half is the reason the head has no character.

CORRECTION 2 - the dorsal is NOT four detached sawtooth triangles. It is ONE CONTINUOUS FIN with a solid base: at rows 182-190 the fin scans as a single unbroken run from x=202 to x=284 (83 px, no gaps); the notches only appear in the top ~6 rows (176-181), where the profile resolves into FIVE peaks, not four (row 176 runs: 202-205, 220-225, 240-245, 261-265, 282-284). So 'continuous' is satisfied; 'sawtooth crest instead of a fin' and the count are the accurate complaints. The real failure is EXTENT: the fin spans x 202-284, which is only 43% of the 191 px body length, sitting from ~17% to ~60% of the way back from the snout. It stops 32 px short of the head and 77 px short of the tail. A blenny's dorsal must start just behind the skull and run almost to the caudal peduncle. As drawn it reads as a mid-back spiky crest, not a full-length dorsal.

CORRECTION 3 - it is NOT rendered at a fifth of frame width. The animal spans 194 of 440 px = 44% of frame WIDTH. What is true is that it is only 40 px tall = 9% of frame HEIGHT, so the painted area is small and the composition looks empty; that is a framing/height observation, not a width one.

CONFIRMED, AND IT IS THE DECISIVE ONE - THERE ARE NO CIRRI. I swept every pixel in x 284-340, y 168-190 (directly above and forward of the eye) against the per-row background: every delta sits at 13-15, identical to the background vignette noise elsewhere on those rows. Nothing is drawn there. The feathery supraorbital tufts, the single most diagnostic blenny feature, are entirely absent.

WHY IT STILL READS AS THE WRONG ORGANISM. The body TUBE alone measures 191 x ~18 px = roughly 10.6:1. The packet asks for aspect 4.5. The overall silhouette only reaches 4.85 because the dorsal crest adds height; strip the crest and the animal is more than twice as slender as spec, a uniform-diameter rod with no depth change from snout to caudal peduncle. That rod, plus a mid-back spiky crest and no cirri, is what produces the needlefish/pike read. headFrac 0.25 is effectively unreadable — nothing demarcates a head.

SHADOW. There is a detached elliptical cast shadow roughly x 175-295, y 235-265. It is real and it is detached, but 'far below' overstates it: the gap from the belly (y~212) to the shadow's top edge is ~23 px, about 1.2 body depths. Still wrong (a swimming pose should either ground the shadow or omit it), but it is a secondary defect, not the reason for the band.

FIX BRIEF: deepen the body to ~4.5:1 and give the anterior third visible head bulk with a steep blunt brow and a wide terminal mouth; extend the dorsal to run from just behind the skull to the caudal peduncle as a low continuous membrane (drop the 5-tooth sawtooth); add two feathery branched cirri tufts rising above the eye; reattach or remove the cast shadow.

rows.readsAs: a yellow disc fish with an eyespot
rows.defect: The near-circular plate body is right, but the dark bar that masks the eye is absent — instead the dark wedge sits back near the tail and the eye itself is drawn as a large white-ringed target mid-flank, which is the exact opposite of the concealing bar. The pointed tweezer snout is a tiny yellow nub barely protruding past the body outline. The dorsal is the shared sawtooth crest, and the whole silhouette is the family chassis in yellow.

rows.readsAs: a plain red aquarium fish
rows.defect: The oversized white-ringed eye and the short deep red body do read, but the two clearly separate dorsal fins are not there — there is one soft rounded hump on the back and nothing else — and the large mouth is absent entirely, replaced by the same scribed jaw wedge every other fish in this batch has. Body, texture, eye and shadow are the shared chassis.

rows.readsAs: a plain orange sunfish
rows.defect: The single feature that makes a clownfish a clownfish — three white bands edged in black — is completely absent. The body is uniform orange with only the shared hatch texture on it, not one band of any colour. The fins are not rounded paddles either: it wears the batch's five-tooth sawtooth crest on the back. What is left is the family chassis recoloured orange, and it is the same drawing as Parrotfish with a different hue.

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with two corrections to the stated cause. Packet must-reads: (1) three white bands edged in black on orange, (2) rounded paddle-shaped fins, (3) blunt stubby snout; aspect 2.0, headFrac 0.3, eyes prominent.

WHAT I SAW (read at 1x, then re-cropped and nearest-neighbour upscaled 4x-9x over head, dorsal, tail and flank, plus a per-pixel colour scan):

BANDS - ABSENT, CONFIRMED NUMERICALLY. Body bbox is x159-307, y159-265. Of 12,884 opaque body pixels: 11,041 orange, 1,413 dark ink (outline/hatch/shadow), and only 60 white (0.47%). Every one of those 60 white pixels sits in columns x=281-290 - i.e. they are the sclera ring of the eye. There is no white pixel anywhere else on the fish. A per-column mean-luminance profile across the whole body shows no periodic light/dark structure at all: values wander 78-120 with the hatch texture and fall off only at the two silhouette ends. So there is not even a faint, low-contrast, or wrong-coloured attempt at banding - not white, not dark, not vertical, in any place. The colour histogram of the body is 100% orange/brown ramps (168,72,24 / 240,96,24 / 192,72,24 ...).

WHAT COULD BE MISTAKEN FOR MARKINGS (and is not): there ARE three ink lines on the flank - a dark arc curving down behind the eye (operculum/gill line), a second dark line lower and further back near the pectoral root, and a pale hairline running lengthwise from snout to tail base (the lateral line). None of these is a band: two are head-local gill strokes and the third is horizontal, running along the fish rather than across it. All three appear identically on the Parrotfish, so they are chassis furniture, not Clownfish markings.

FINS - THE CLAIM IS PARTLY WRONG. The judge said the fins are 'the shared sawtooth crest, not rounded paddles'. The DORSAL is indeed a crown of ~5 free-standing sharp triangular spikes in dark brown standing clear above the topline - wrong for an anemonefish, which has one continuous, only slightly notched, soft-edged dorsal. The PECTORAL is a small angular wedge, also not a paddle. But the CAUDAL is in fact a rounded-cornered fan with radiating ray spokes - that one IS a rounded paddle, and it is the correct shape for a clownfish. So must-read 2 fails on the dorsal and pectoral, not on all fins; a fix must reshape the dorsal into a low continuous fin and round the pectoral, and should leave the tail alone.

SNOUT - ABSENT, an additional failure the original claim did not name. The head end is a smooth, unbroken taper to a fairly pointed oval tip. There is NO mouth drawn anywhere - no lip, no jaw line, no mouth slot. Must-read 3 ('blunt stubby snout') therefore has nothing to read at all.

PROPORTION - a further defect not named. Measured body bbox is 149 x 107 px = aspect 1.39, against the packet's requested 2.0. The fish is a deep near-disc plate, which is exactly why it lands in parrotfish/butterflyfish territory.

CHASSIS - the 'identical to the Parrotfish' claim is very nearly right but overstated. Side by side, Clownfish and Parrotfish share: the same almond/lens deep-disc body, the same scale-hatch texture and its row spacing, the same pale lateral hairline, the same gill arc, the same white-ring black-pupil eye at the same relative position, the same small triangular pectoral wedge, the same rounded ray-spoked fan tail sitting slightly detached behind the caudal peduncle, and the same small anal bump under the belly. The ONE difference is the dorsal: Clownfish gets the sawtooth crown, Parrotfish gets a low smooth dorsal slab. So it is one chassis recoloured orange with a different dorsal decal - not literally the same drawing.

BAND: FAIL. Two of three must-reads (the bands, which ARE the organism, and the snout) are wholly absent, the third is only one-third present, and the silhouette is off-spec aspect. This reads as a generic orange reef disc, not as Amphiprion.

rows.readsAs: a blue damselfish or a blue cichlid
rows.defect: The deep compressed oval and the forked tail are present and this is one of the closer reads in the batch, but the dorsal is not a single continuous fin — it is the shared row of four detached sawtooth triangles with bare topline showing between them. It is also indistinguishable from Tang and Surgeonfish except for the exact shade of blue.
rows.fix: Join the dorsal spines with a continuous membrane so the fin runs unbroken from nape to tail base.

rows.readsAs: a small pale minnow
rows.defect: The two separate dorsal fins are actually there as two small humps with a gap between them, and the eye is set high, but the belly is completely bare — there is no fused pelvic suction disc, no pelvic fins at all — and the head is not big or blunt: the body tapers to a point at the snout exactly as it does at the tail, giving a symmetric spindle with no head mass. It shares that spindle with Blenny and Wrasse.
rows.fix: Add the fused pelvic disc as a visible oval sucker on the underside beneath the pectoral, and widen and blunt the front third into a broad frog-like head with the two eyes set close together on top.

rows.readsAs: a sea urchin, or a tick
rows.defect: This is not a fish silhouette at all. It is a red-brown ellipse with straight white and red quills radiating in every direction — forward, backward, up and down — with no tail fin, no caudal peduncle, no head separated from the body and only a single dot for an eye. The zebra banding is present, but the fan of dorsal spines reads as an all-around spine halo and the feathery separated pectoral rays are absent (the forward and rear quills are the same stiff needles as the dorsal ones). A stranger names an urchin or a mite before they name a fish.
rows.fix: Rebuild the fish silhouette first — a banded oval body with a real head, mouth and a fanned caudal fin — then restrict the long quills to a dorsal fan above the back and give the pectorals broad feathered, membraned rays sweeping out sideways like wings.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 1x and again at 3x/5x/6x crops of the head, rear and full body. The FAIL stands, and the core of the claim is accurate, but several specifics need correcting before anyone works a fix against it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS. A single smooth brick-red ellipse, roughly 1.55:1 wide, centred in frame with a soft rim-light along its upper-left and a shadow under its lower-right. Across it run SIX dark-brown vertical bands, drawn as lens/almond shapes (pointed top and bottom, fat in the middle) rather than as bands wrapping a body. From the ellipse edge radiate roughly eighteen rigid, perfectly straight rods arranged as a full 360-degree halo, evenly spaced like the spokes of a sun or the spines of an urchin. Each rod is the SAME primitive: a slightly tapered spindle, rounded at the tip, with a hard two-tone split down its long axis (a pale grey-white face and a dark grey underface), and about half of them carry a red-brown wash on the upper half instead of white. A black bead eye with a small white specular dot sits at the extreme front-upper edge of the ellipse. That is the entire asset.

MUST-READS (aspect 1.5 / headFrac 0.3 / eyes normal / posture swimming):
1. 'Fan of long venomous dorsal spines' — NOT MET, and this is the load-bearing failure. Spines exist in quantity but they are not a fan and not dorsal. They radiate from every point of the perimeter: I confirmed at 6x that one rod exits horizontally FORWARD from the snout position, directly where the mouth should be, and at 5x that three more exit rearward from the tail position; several point straight down from the belly. A lionfish's spines fan upward and backward from a dorsal ridge, which is what makes the silhouette read; a radial halo reads as echinoderm or arthropod. The rods are also stiff, hard-edged and uniform-width — real spines are filamentous, unequal in length, and carry membrane between them.
2. 'Feathery separated pectoral fin rays spread like wings' — ABSENT, exactly as claimed. There is no membrane, no webbing, no plume, no fan of finer rays, and no appendage at the pectoral position that differs in any way from the other seventeen. Every appendage is the same rigid spindle. This is the second identity-defining must-read and nothing on the canvas gestures at it.
3. 'Red-brown and white zebra banding' — HALF MET, and the other judge under-described this by calling it merely 'a banded ellipse'. Banding is genuinely present and is the one thing working: six clean vertical dark bands on a red-brown ground. But there is NO WHITE in the banding at all — it is dark brown on brick red, so the high-contrast zebra read that carries a lionfish at thumbnail size is missing. The only white in the piece is on the spine rods. The bands are also lens-shaped rather than parallel-sided, so they read as segment plates on a shell rather than as pigment stripes on a flank.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM. (a) 'One dot for an eye' is slightly wrong: the eye is a black bead with a white specular highlight, so it is a two-tone glossy bead, not a bare dot. It still fails, but for a different reason — it has no orbit, ring or lid, and it is parked on the bare curve of the ellipse with no head for it to belong to. (b) 'No tail fin, no caudal peduncle' — CONFIRMED at 5x; the rear terminus is an unbroken elliptical arc with nothing but spine rods coming off it. (c) 'No head' — CONFIRMED at 6x and stronger than stated: there is no snout, no mouth line, no jaw, no opercle/gill line, and no taper or notch anywhere separating a head mass from the body. The specified headFrac of 0.3 is not expressed by a single pixel. (d) 'Not a fish silhouette at all' — CONFIRMED; strip the colour and the outline is an ellipse with radial spikes, which is the sea-urchin/tick silhouette the judge named.

VERDICT. Two of three must-reads are wholly absent, the third is present only in structure and not in colour, and the underlying body has none of the fish scaffolding (peduncle, caudal fin, head mass, mouth) that the spines are supposed to decorate. Nothing here is 'present but small' or 'drawn where the judge did not look' — I went looking specifically for a hidden pectoral plume and a hidden tail and neither exists. FAIL is correct and this needs a rebuild from the silhouette up, not a polish: build a proper fusiform fish body with a distinct head third and a fanned caudal fin, restrict the spines to a dorsal ridge fan with membrane between them, add webbed feathery pectorals as the largest single feature, and repaint the bands as alternating red-brown and WHITE.

rows.readsAs: a cyan sunfish; the Clownfish drawing in a different colour
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads is present. There is no beak — no fused tooth plate, no mouth of any kind, just the shared scribed jaw wedge; the forehead is not blunt or bulging but the same gently tapering almond nose every disc fish in this batch has; and there are no large paddle pectorals for rowing, only the single shared belly lobe. Pixel for pixel this is the Clownfish silhouette recoloured cyan.
rows.fix: Give it a heavy fused parrot beak with a visible seam between upper and lower plates, and steepen the forehead into a blunt vertical bulge above it.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 4x, 9x and 16x crops plus a contrast-boosted snout crop, and side-by-side against Clownfish.png at identical crop/scale. FAIL upheld: two of the three must-reads are absent, and the third is present but unreadable.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN. A cyan almond/disc body, nose-right, spanning roughly x157-315, y151-266 in the 440px canvas -- body length ~158px, body depth ~115px, so the rendered aspect is ~1.37:1 against the packet's specified 2.6. That alone is the wrong body plan: a parrotfish is an elongated oval, this is a plate. Features present: a small round white-ringed eye with a Pac-Man-notch pupil high and far forward; one long scribed opercular arc curving from the topline down behind the eye to the belly; dense stamped scale rows; a low rounded dorsal lobe over the mid-back with three or four thin ray filaments trailing up and back; a small anal-fin nub under the belly; a detached palm-frond fan tail at far left; and -- contra the judge -- a pectoral fin.

CORRECTION 1 (the judge is wrong on the pectorals being absent). A pectoral IS drawn. At source x~222-275, y~207-238 there is a triangular fan with about eight radiating ray strokes, apex pinned at the gill arc and spreading back and down across the flank. The defect is not absence, it is prominence and shape: it is rendered as a translucent inset the same cyan as the body with only faint dark ray lines, roughly 40x30px on a 158px body, and it is a narrow swept triangle, not a broad rounded rowing paddle. It reads as a body marking, not as a limb. Any fix must ENLARGE and RE-TONE the existing fan (broad rounded blade, own value separation from the flank, tips clear of the ventral line), not add a fin that isn't there.

CORRECTION 2 (the judge is wrong that it is a pure Clownfish recolour). Everything below the topline is identical to Clownfish.png -- same almond outline, same eye size and placement, same single gill scribe, same faint triangular pectoral in the same pixel neighbourhood, same detached fan tail, same anal nub, same scale stamps. The one silhouette difference is the dorsal: Clownfish carries a three-point sawtooth crest, Parrotfish a low smooth lobe with thin trailing filaments. So it is the same chassis with a swapped dorsal and a hue change, not a straight recolour. That distinction matters because the chassis, not the paint, is the thing to fix.

CONFIRMED FAILURES. (a) 'fused beak-like teeth plates' -- absent, and absent at every contrast level I could pull. At 16x with a 2.2x contrast lift the snout tip (x~305-315) is bare: no beak, no lip, no tooth plate, no terminal line of any kind. The only mouth-adjacent mark is a faint dark horizontal scribe at y~225-230 running x~250-290, i.e. the shared family jaw wedge, and it dies ~25px short of the snout tip so it does not even close as a mouth. (b) 'blunt bulging forehead' -- absent. The dorsal-to-snout profile is a single smooth convex arc that tapers to a point, the same almond taper carried by Clownfish, Butterflyfish and the rest of the disc set; there is no steep brow, no forehead bulge, no break in the curve above the eye.

Net: the asset reads as a generic cyan reef disc. The two features that make a parrotfish a parrotfish -- the fused beak and the bulging blunt head -- are not on the canvas, and the third is drawn too small and too flat to register.

rows.readsAs: a spotted yellow disc fish

rows.readsAs: a pale blue disc fish; the Tang drawing in a lighter blue

The forehead is not steep, it is the same gentle almond taper, and the dorsal is the shared four-tooth crest on the middle third rather than a long low fin running the whole back. With all three must-reads gone what remains is the chassis, and it is the same drawing as Tang two rows down.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 4x bicubic and 10x nearest-neighbour on crops of the tail base, head and back. Packet row 11: aspect 1.7, headFrac 0.25, mustRead = scalpel-like spine at the base of the tail / oval compressed body with a steep forehead / long low dorsal fin running the whole back.

MUST-READ 1 (scalpel spine at tail base) - ABSENT. I upheld this but the judge described it imprecisely. It is not that the caudal peduncle is bare; there IS NO CADUAL PEDUNCLE AT ALL. At 10x the body ellipse's rear edge meets the caudal fin directly - the fan's ray convergence point sits ON the body outline with zero narrowing, no wrist, no keel. The silhouette there is a clean unbroken arc. Inside it there is only the generic scale-row texture plus one faint pale horizontal streak (a lateral-line highlight artifact, not a blade); no dark slash, no notch, no protruding spine, no scalpel-yellow accent. So the fix is not 'add a mark' - it needs a narrowed peduncle built first and the blade hung on it, otherwise there is nowhere anatomically for the spine to live.

MUST-READ 2 (oval compressed body + steep forehead) - HALF PRESENT, and the judge undersold the half that works. The body IS a deep, laterally-compressed disc and that part reads fine. But it is drawn nearly circular - body-only width:height is roughly 1.15, against the packet's 1.7 - so the front profile is just the same circular arc as everything else. There is no separately modelled steep forehead: the head crop shows one smooth even curve running from under the crest down to a blunt taper, with a single cyan mouth line and a curved gill-cover line as the only head detail. No small pointed grazing snout either. It reads as a generic round reef disc (butterflyfish/tang territory), not a surgeonfish head.

MUST-READ 3 (long low dorsal running the whole back) - ABSENT, judge correct. What is there is the shared family crest: five hard-edged sawtooth spikes on a flat slab base, TALL rather than low, and confined to the front third of the back sitting directly above and behind the eye. The entire rear half of the back, from mid-body to the tail, is completely bare. It is also flat-shaded vector-style with hard polygon edges, against a painterly stippled/scaled body - a render-style mismatch on top of the anatomy miss.

OTHER: caudal is a broad triangular ray-fan, not the family's lunate/crescent tail; anal fin is a small unshaped nub under the belly; pectoral is a faint translucent triangle low on the flank. The judge's 'this is the Tang drawing in a lighter blue' is fair and I confirmed it by opening Tang.png - same disc body, same five-spike crest, same fan tail, same eye, only a deeper blue and slightly smaller. Neither carries its family's tail-base spine, so the two are currently indistinguishable except by hue.

VERDICT: one of three must-reads half-present, the name-giving feature absent, and the asset is chassis-identical to its sibling species. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a blue tang, or just a blue fish
rows.defect: The round plate body and the big swept tail are there and the royal blue helps it land near a blue tang, but the sharp tail-base spine is absent, the snout is a blunt rounded taper rather than a small pointed grazing mouth, and the tail is a broad triangular sweep rather than a crescent. It is the Surgeonfish and Damselfish drawing in a third blue.

rows.readsAs: a teal sunfish
rows.defect: Every must-read fails. The eyes are not set far back and high away from the mouth — the single eye sits right at the snout tip, as close to the mouth as it can get; there is no erectile trigger spine on the forehead at all, just two soft rounded humps well behind the head; and the body is a plump symmetric oval, not a leathery diamond, with no rowing second dorsal and anal fins (the second dorsal is a small blob and the anal is the shared belly lobe). It is the Clownfish/Parrotfish silhouette in teal.
rows.fix: Push the eye far back and high onto the upper rear of the skull, well separated from the mouth, plant an erect trigger spine on the forehead, and re-cut the body into an angular diamond with tall symmetric soft dorsal and anal fins.
rows.verifyWhy:
Measured the PNG at 440x440 and re-cropped the head, back, belly and tail at 6-14x. Silhouette bbox x126-313, y139-262. The tail fan occupies x126-178; the body proper runs x~180-313 (133px long) with a max depth of ~120px (excluding fins) -> body aspect ~1.1, near-circular; overall aspect with tail ~1.5 against the packet's 1.8. Column profile (top/bottom of the green mask): x=200 157/254, x=220 140/260, x=260 146/249, x=291 180/232, x=310 200/214. That is a smooth convex almond/lens, fore-aft near-symmetric, pointed at both ends, with no angular corners anywhere -- not a leathery rhombus with straight converging dorsal/ventral edges and a pinched peduncle.

MUST-READ 1 (eyes set far back and high, well away from the mouth) -- FAILS. The white sclera ring measures x286-296, y191-202, so the eye centre is (291, 196.5). The snout tip is x=313, i.e. the eye sits 22px behind the tip on a 133px body = 16.5% of body length, roughly 1.5 eye-diameters from the nose. At x=291 the body spans y180-232 (local mid 206), so the eye is only 9.5px above local centre out of 52px of depth -- it reads as a centred eye on a tapering snout, not an eye pushed up under the dorsal profile and set a third of the way back. So the judge is right that the eye is at the snout and not far back/high.

CORRECTION to the judge on the mouth: there is NO mouth drawn at all. At 14x on the snout (source x270-318, y180-228) the head is a clean smooth taper -- no lip line, no jaw notch, no dark mouth stroke, nothing. The only linework forward of the eye is a pale horizontal lateral-line stripe that passes just below the eye and dies out about two-thirds of the way to the tip, plus a faint dark curved gill arc behind and below the eye. So "right beside the mouth" is not verifiable and is the wrong phrasing: the defect is the eye's absolute forward/central placement PLUS a completely absent mouth (a triggerfish's small terminal chisel mouth at the end of a long snout is itself a missing read).

MUST-READ 2 (erectile trigger spine on the forehead) -- FAILS, absent. There are exactly two dorsal elements, both dark-teal rounded humps drawn BEHIND the body outline and rising only ~15px above the back: a rear one at x~215-240 and a forward one at x~253-272 (peak ~x262). The forward one sits 41-60px behind the snout tip, i.e. over the mid-back, not on the forehead, and its profile is a rounded bump, not an erect spike. The dorsal contour from x=272 to the snout at x=313 is an unbroken smooth curve with nothing on it. No spine, no trigger, no locking first-dorsal group of any kind.

MUST-READ 3 (rowing second dorsal and anal fins) -- CORRECTION, the judge overstated this. The fins are not absent: besides the two dorsal humps there is a small dark ventral nub peeking below the belly at x~203-225 (visible only as a ~10px bulge past the outline). The real failure is that these are vestigial rounded bumps, fore-aft OFFSET rather than mirrored (rear dorsal 215-240 vs anal 203-225), roughly half the anal's size difference, and painted behind/under the silhouette so they read as background lumps rather than the tall matched sculling pair that defines the balistid.

Other observations for the fix: the caudal is a large dark D-shaped fan with radiating ray lines butted flush against the rear point with no peduncle (it does touch the body, so it is not detached, but there is no narrow caudal wrist); a hatched fan-shaped pectoral is drawn INSIDE the silhouette at mid-body (x~250-285, y~200-230) where it reads as a dark smudge over the flank rather than a fin; the flank carries dense bright dash-rows reading as ordinary fish scales plus one bright full-length lateral stripe, so the surface reads scaly, not leathery/plated.

Verdict: the judge's band and their overall gist ("Clownfish/Parrotfish silhouette in teal") stand. Two of the three must-reads are genuinely absent or inverted and the third is present only as vestigial bumps. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a barracuda or a small piranha
rows.defect: The cigar body is right, but the dentition is drawn as a row of about seven big white sawtooth fangs running the whole jaw line, which reads as a predatory barracuda rather than a pair of protruding buck teeth, and the large fan pectoral fins that are supposed to be doing the swimming are absent entirely — there is no pectoral fin on the flank at all. Body, hatch texture and tail are the shared elongate spindle it uses with Blenny and Goby.

rows.readsAs: a crouched brown cartoon rabbit
rows.defect: The must-read that IS the agouti — slender delicate legs with hoof-like claws under a high rump — is absent: the body is the shared ball and the legs are two stubby dark pegs poking out of the belly outline with no joint, no length and no foot. Erect pink-lined ears and a whiskered wedge face complete the rabbit read.
rows.fix: Redraw the legs as long thin two-segment columns that leave the silhouette at a visible shoulder and hip, ending in three small dark hoof-like nails, and raise the body clear of the ground so the leg length is the first thing seen.
rows.verifyWhy:
I read the PNG at full size, then at 4x, then at 8x with a 2.2x brightness boost over the lower body so dark-on-dark limbs separate, and I measured the silhouette column-by-column. The FAIL stands, but three parts of the stated cause are factually wrong and must not be fixed against.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN. Silhouette spans x=142..296, top of back y=157, ground contact y=262 (440x440 canvas). Head faces right. Body is one smooth convex ovoid.

LIMB COUNT IS WRONG: there are TWO limbs, not four. At y=255 exactly two dark masses exist -- x=177..213 and x=229..236 -- and nothing between them but the ground-shadow ellipse. There is no far-side pair at any opacity; I checked the boosted crop and the pixel map. Reporting 'four pegs' will send a fix at the wrong problem: the creature is standing on one hind leg and one foreleg.

'JOINTLESS PEGS' IS HALF WRONG. The foreleg (x=226..241, y=236..262, only ~26px long against a ~105px body) IS a jointless peg -- a rounded-top column that flares into a small blunt pad, no shoulder, no wrist, no digits. But the HIND limb is not a peg at all: it is a thick blunt BOOT. A wide column drops from the haunch, bends at roughly ankle height, and turns forward into a broad flat foot lying along the ground from x~177 to x~213. That is a plantigrade rabbit slipper, ~36px of sole. It is the single strongest reason the asset reads lagomorph, and it is the opposite of the defect described.

'POKE OUT OF THE BELLY' IS WRONG FOR THE HIND LIMB. There is a drawn haunch: a pale crescent arc runs from about (170,232) up over (200,205) and down to (232,240), enclosing a shaded thigh disc, and the hind limb emerges from the bottom of that disc. The attachment is anatomically placed. Only the foreleg drops straight off the unbroken belly line with no shoulder mass.

MUST-READ 2 IS GENUINELY ABSENT -- the judge is right on substance. 'Slender delicate legs with hoof-like claws': the two limbs present are thick, dark, undifferentiated and short. No hock, no cannon, no elongation, no digits, and above all no hoof-like nail tips -- both feet terminate in soft rounded pads. Nothing on this asset says cursorial.

MUST-READ 1 IS ALSO NOT MET, and the previous judge did not raise it. 'Arched hunched back rising to the rump': the topline reads 202,185,177,172,167,164,161,159,158,157 from the rear, holds 157 across x=196..214, then falls 159,161,162 to the neck. The peak sits at mid-back, ~38% forward of the rump, and the rump itself is a dome that falls away. Worse, the head is carried HIGH -- crown at y=152..166, level with or above the back peak -- where an agouti carries the head low under a hip-peaked arch. The result is a ball with a bump in the middle, not a rump-loaded arch.

MUST-READ 3 IS MET. 'Essentially no tail' -- the rear dome at 8x is completely clean, no tail, no stub, no tuft. Credit where due.

GESTALT CONFIRMS 'BROWN CARTOON RABBIT', and there is more evidence for it than was cited. Two narrow ERECT TRIANGULAR ears with pale inner surfaces stand well clear of the crown. The eye is a large white-ringed disc with a black pupil and a specular dot -- cartoon, not the small dark agouti eye. Below the blunt muzzle hangs a WHITE INCISOR BLOCK, a rectangle split by a vertical seam into two buck teeth, drawn outside the mouth line; agoutis show no such thing in profile. Add the ball body and the flat slipper hind foot and the read is unambiguous.

CHASSIS NOTE for the family pass: two pale seam arcs are visible -- one ringing the head where it meets the body, one ringing the haunch. Both look like generic chassis part-boundaries rather than agouti-specific fur breaks, worth checking against the other 20 rodents.

MEASUREMENTS vs SPEC: silhouette aspect 154/105 = 1.47 against aspect 1.7 (too tall/round, feeding the ball read). Head length ~50px = 0.32 of body length against headFrac 0.27 (slightly oversized). Posture quadruped and eyes prominent are nominally satisfied.

FIX DIRECTION: this needs four limbs, not four better pegs -- a long slender hind limb with a real hock and a narrow hoof-tipped foot standing OFF the ground plane, a matching slender foreleg with a visible elbow, and far-side partners at reduced value. Then drop the head below a topline that peaks over the hips, shrink the ears to small rounded flaps, and delete the external white incisor block.

rows.readsAs: a beaver, mostly — or an otter carrying a beaver's tail
rows.defect: The flat crosshatched paddle tail lands and this is the only asset off the family chassis, but the body is long, low and otter-like rather than stocky and humped, and the big orange chisel incisors are simply not drawn — the muzzle is closed and blank, so the single most recognisable rodent feature is missing.

rows.readsAs: the Agouti image again, a brown cartoon rabbit
rows.defect: Pixel-for-pixel this is the Agouti chassis with a marginally different flank shade. The blunt squared-off brick head that IS the capybara is absent — the head is a small round wedge with a tapered whiskered muzzle and erect pointed ears — and a stub tail is visible where the reference says none. The barrel body sits on peg stubs with no hint of a webbed foot, and the eyes/ears/nostrils are not set high on the skull.

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but one of the three stated causes is factually wrong and must not be fixed.

WHAT I SAW (read at full size, then re-cropped and magnified 6-8x on head, rump and feet):

HEAD - the FAIL stands. The head is a small egg/teardrop in profile whose front third narrows continuously into a pointed muzzle; the nose ends in a tiny dark point with three whisker pairs radiating from it, and a pair of flat cream chisel incisors hangs off the underside of that point. There is no blunt vertical brick face, no flat square muzzle-front, no deep boxy jaw - the profile is a squirrel/agouti wedge. headFrac measures right (head is ~0.28 of body length) but the SHAPE is the wrong organism's. This alone is the defining must-read and it is absent.

EYES/EARS/NOSTRILS - the judge's claim is HALF wrong and needs restating so the fix aims correctly. The EARS are in fact set high: two tall upright triangular points sit on the crown of the skull. The defect is not their height, it is their FORM - they are tall pricked squirrel triangles where a capybara wants small, short, rounded ears set far back. The EYE is genuinely mis-sited: one large white-ringed round eye with a black pupil sits at mid-height on the side of the head, roughly level with the muzzle line, not up near the crown, and it is drawn as a big cartoon eye rather than the packet's 'eyes: small'. The NOSTRIL is a small dark point at the very tip of the tapered muzzle, i.e. on the front of a cone, not on a high flat rostrum. So: ears high but wrong shape; eyes and nostrils genuinely low.

TAIL - the judge is WRONG here; do not 'remove a tail'. There is no tail stub. The dark shape they read as one is the HIND LIMB: at 8x you can see a thigh column dropping from under the haunch swirl and a foot that turns and extends FORWARD (leftward past the body edge is only the heel), with a matching smaller foreleg stub further right. The rear silhouette behind the rump is a clean, unbroken curve. The 'no visible tail' must-read is actually SATISFIED.

BODY - a single smooth egg blob with a decorative haunch swirl outlined in a thin white arc. Legs are two short dark stubs; no webbing, no toe splay. Silhouette bbox is 215x128 = aspect 1.68 against the packet's 2, so it is also too short/round for a barrel-bodied animal. The topline peaks at x~194 (mid-body, rump side) versus ~150-155 over the shoulder, so 'rump higher than shoulders' is present only incidentally as the dome of a generic blob, not as a read.

SHARED-CHASSIS CLAIM - confirmed quantitatively. Cropped to their own bounding boxes and resampled to 128x128, Capybara vs Agouti silhouette IoU = 0.852 and Capybara vs Guinea_Pig = 0.827 (Capybara vs Beaver, a genuinely differentiated rodent, = 0.399). Agouti's aspect is 1.66 against Capybara's 1.68. Side by side the two are the same body blob, same haunch swirl, same two limb stubs, same head, same ear pair, same eye, same incisor plate - Capybara is only rendered slightly larger and a shade browner. 'Effectively the same image as Agouti' is accurate.

FIX TARGET: rebuild the head as a blunt rectangular brick with a flat vertical muzzle face and a squared jaw; drop the eye to small and raise it to the top edge of the skull; move the nostrils to the top-front of the flat muzzle; swap the tall triangles for small rounded ears; stretch the body toward aspect 2 with visible short splayed legs. Leave the tail alone - there isn't one.

rows.readsAs: a plain brown rabbit with a squirrel tail glued on
rows.defect: The bold dark-and-pale back and face stripes — the entire identity of a chipmunk — are completely absent; the coat is an unbroken flat brown gradient from nose to rump. There are no cheek pouches either. All that survives is a tail held up behind, on the same shared ball body as Agouti and Capybara.
rows.fix: Paint the stripe set on: five dark dorsal stripes separated by cream ones running shoulder to rump, plus the dark eye-stripe and pale brow stripe on the face.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with two corrections to the stated cause. I decoded the PNG and read it at 3x and 6x (head, back, feet crops), plus ran luminance scans across the torso and face, plus a 4-up against Ground Squirrel / Hamster / Gerbil.

MUST-READ 1 — 'bold dark and pale stripes along back and face': GENUINELY ABSENT, confirmed instrumentally, not just by eye. Vertical luminance columns through the torso (x=180/200/220/240/260, y=155..275) return a single smooth ramp — roughly L 100 to 145 — with no alternating bands anywhere. Horizontal rows along the topline (y=170/180/190) are equally monotonic. The only non-gradient values in the whole coat are isolated single-pixel spikes (L~154-162) that are the 1px pale outline strokes of the head circle and the haunch circle, and the eye's white sclera ring on the face column (L 229/239/217 at x=275) — that ring is an eye, not a face stripe. There is no dorsal banding, no eye-stripe, no pale supraorbital line. The face is a plain sphere.

CORRECTION A to the claim: 'the coat is unbroken flat brown' is imprecise and would mislead a fixer into merely adding shading. The coat is NOT flat — it carries a strong radial gradient, a thin pale rim-light along the entire topline, a pale stroke where the head sphere meets the torso, a pale stroke ringing the haunch, and a long pale lozenge highlight running down the middle of the tail. So pale marks DO exist on this asset; none of them is a stripe. The correct diagnosis is: zero longitudinal banding and zero tonal contrast beyond lighting — the tail lozenge is the one pale marking present and it is a specular highlight, not a chipmunk stripe.

MUST-READ 2 — 'tail held up behind': PRESENT and the judge correctly credited it. A thick tail arcs up off the rump and forward over the back. It is however a smooth lozenge, not a plume.

MUST-READ 3 — 'bulging cheek pouches': GENUINELY ABSENT. At 6x the head is an unmodified sphere with a small cone muzzle projecting forward; there is no cheek swelling, no jaw mass, nothing below or behind the whisker root. Confirmed.
