The bill is a slim straight dagger with neither a hook nor stoutness. The feet are three bare splayed toes with no web between them.
rows.fix: Add webbing between the toes and give the bill a stout hooked tip so it commits to the gull read the note asks for.

rows.readsAs: a brown grouse or partridge standing in a field
rows.defect: The flying posture is absent — it stands on two yellow legs on a cast shadow. The white flash at the base of the primaries, the field mark that identifies a skua in the air, is nowhere: the wing is the uniform grey family swoosh. The heavy hooked pirate bill is a short blunt yellow triangle with at most a faint droop, no raised cere and no strong hook. The bulk that is present is round game-bird bulk, not a barrel chest driving long wings.
rows.fix: Render it in flight from below with a bold white crescent across the base of the primaries on each wing, and rebuild the bill as a short deep dark hook.
rows.verifyWhy:
I zoomed the 440x440 PNG (pixel-decoded and upscaled 4-10x at the head, flank, tail and feet) and measured the alpha/contrast bbox. VERDICT UPHELD, but two of the four stated causes are described wrongly and one is outright wrong.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a near-spherical, heavily mottled warm-brown body (bbox 115,140 - 323,287 => drawn aspect 1.41 against the packet's spec aspect 2.2) sitting on two short bright-yellow legs planted on a black elliptical ground shadow. A small round head sits directly on the ball with NO neck. Across the flank is one large folded-wing oval, outlined by a dark rim and filled with tan/cream speckle stippling; behind it a solid dark grey-brown primary/tail wedge sweeps back and right to a sharp point at x~323, with a few thin barb strokes hanging beneath it. This is a grouse/quail/partridge silhouette. The judge's read is correct.

1. POSTURE - CLAIM CORRECT. Packet posture is 'flying'; the asset is a standing biped on a cast ground shadow with wings folded. Nothing about it is airborne.

2. WHITE FLASH AT THE BASE OF THE PRIMARIES - ABSENT, CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, BUT THE JUDGE MIS-DESCRIBED THE WING. I counted pixels with R,G,B all > 195 across the entire image: exactly TWO, at (145,156) and (145,157), value 219,219,220 - that is the eye catchlight. There is no white anywhere else. HOWEVER the wing is NOT 'uniform grey': it is a warm mottled brown/tan folded-wing oval with cream speckling, distinct from the darker grey-brown tail/primary wedge. There IS a pale blue-grey rim light (mid-grey, ~150-180, not white) tracing the dorsal contour of the crown and mantle - a lighting edge on the silhouette, not a plumage flash, and it is on the mantle top edge, nowhere near the primary bases. A fix must add an actual white patch at the wrist/primary bases, not brighten the rim light.

3. 'PIRATE HOOK IS A SHORT BLUNT YELLOW TRIANGLE' - PARTLY WRONG. At 9x the bill is NOT blunt: the tip clearly turns DOWN into a downcurved point that drops below the gape line, with a notch behind it. A hook exists. What actually fails is everything around it - the bill is short and shallow-based (roughly 22px long on a 209px-wide animal) rather than the deep, heavy skua bill; it is flat saturated yellow rather than dark grey/black with a horny nail; and at thumbnail scale the hook is ~5px, so it reads as a generic fowl/finch bill. Do not 'add a hook' - lengthen and deepen the bill, darken it, and enlarge the existing hook.

4. 'BARREL-CHESTED BULKY GULL BUILD' (third must-read, which the judge did not name) - ALSO FAILS. It is bulky, but it is a gamebird ball, not a gull: no neck, no long body, folded wing does not project past the tail, legs are far too short and set mid-belly.

5. ADDITIONAL DEFECT NEITHER JUDGE MENTIONED: the feet are unwebbed yellow stick toes (a forward toe bar plus a rear hallux) - skua feet are black and fully webbed. Wrong colour and wrong topology.

Band FAIL: it reads as the wrong organism (galliform, not a seabird), the spec posture is not attempted, and one of three must-reads (the white primary flash) is verifiably absent to the pixel.

rows.readsAs: a white kiwi chick
rows.defect: The pure white plumage is the only must-read delivered, and it is also what every other white bird in this batch has. The required short BLACK hooked bill with tube nostrils is instead a long straight bright yellow dagger — wrong length, wrong colour, wrong shape, no tube. The long narrow pointed wings are the painted crescent plus one short grey point. Posture is specified flying and the bird is standing on legs over a ground shadow.
rows.fix: Cut the bill to a third of its length, paint it black, add the nostril tube, and put the bird aloft on two long narrow pointed wings.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 5x crops of the head and the feet, then compared against Petrel.png. FAIL stands, and it stands on two of the three must-reads being flatly absent.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a near-spherical body (drawn extent roughly 200x155 px, aspect ~1.3, not the specified 2.0) in chalk-white with a coarse net/scale texture; a small round head set directly on the shoulders with no neck; a small black eye with a white catchlight (eyes: small is satisfied); a single folded wing lying flat along the flank, outlined by a thick mid-grey crescent swoosh; a solid mid-grey pointed tail wedge projecting horizontally off the rear; two thin golden-yellow legs with three splayed toes each planted on the ground; and a hard black elliptical cast shadow beneath. It is standing, weight on its feet, in a terrestrial biped pose.

MUST-READ 1 - 'entirely pure white plumage': PARTIAL. The body and head are white, but the plumage is not entirely white: a heavy mid-grey crescent outlines the folded wing across the whole flank and the tail wedge is solid mid-grey. The bill and both legs are bright golden yellow. A real Snow Petrel is unbroken white with a BLACK bill and bluish-grey feet, so the two brightest non-white accents on this asset are exactly the two parts that should not be coloured.

MUST-READ 2 - 'short black hooked bill with tube nostrils': ABSENT. Confirmed at 5x. The bill is a straight, unhooked, fine-pointed dagger in warm amber/gold, about 0.9x the head diameter long, angled slightly down-forward from the face. There is no decurved tip, no nail at the end, no raised nostril tube on the culmen or the sides, and no black anywhere on it. The judge's description of this feature is accurate in every particular.

MUST-READ 3 - 'long narrow pointed seabird wings': ABSENT. There is no extended wing at all. The only wing present is a folded one pressed to the body and read purely as a grey outline crescent plus a lighter inner covert patch. Nothing spans, nothing is held out, nothing tapers to a primary tip. The specified posture 'flying' is not drawn; the feet crop shows two yellow legs and splayed toes standing on a shadow ellipse, so the judge's 'stands on legs over a shadow rather than flying' is exactly right.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM: (a) 'reads as a white kiwi chick' is directionally right but imprecise as a fix target - the bill is far too short and too thick for a kiwi (a kiwi's is 2-3x head length and needle-thin) and the asset has a prominent projecting tail wedge a kiwi does not have. It reads as a generic plump cartoon chick or a rounded shorebird toy, not specifically a kiwi. Fixing it toward 'not a kiwi' would be aiming at the wrong target; it needs to be aimed at 'petrel in flight'. (b) The bill is gold/amber rather than saturated yellow, but the substance of the claim holds. (c) The claim omits three further defects worth carrying into the fix: the aspect is ~1.3 against a spec of 2.0; the grey wing swoosh and grey tail break the 'entirely pure white' requirement; and the legs are yellow when they should be bluish-grey.

FAMILY EVIDENCE (strengthens the FAIL): Snow_Petrel.png is the same chassis as Petrel.png with only a colour swap - identical round body, identical head placement and eye, identical straight yellow dagger bill, identical grey wing crescent, identical grey tail wedge, identical yellow three-toed feet, identical shadow ellipse. Snow Petrel is Petrel recoloured white. This is the one-chassis-many-colours defect, and it means the fix cannot be a local touch-up of the bill: the whole flying-seabird chassis (spread narrow pointed wings, elongated body, no ground shadow, no legs planted) has to be built before the species-specific black tube-nosed bill is worth drawing.

rows.readsAs: a small white bird with a notched tail
rows.defect: The forked tail is the one genuine shape edit in the batch and it does read, though it is a shallow notch in a short grey spike rather than deep trailing streamers. The black cap over the crown is entirely absent — the head is uniformly white, so the strongest tern field mark is gone. The long narrow pointed wings are the shared folded swoosh over a spherical body, and the specified flying posture is not rendered; the bird stands on legs over a shadow.
rows.fix: Add a solid black cap from bill-base over the crown to the nape, and deepen the tail fork into two long thin streamers well past the wingtips.

rows.readsAs: a long thin olive-green fish, closest to a needlefish or a blade of eelgrass with an eye on it
rows.defect: The tube snout - the identity feature - is a 1-2px hairline spike with no volume, no taper and no pinhole mouth, and an IDENTICAL dark hairline spike sticks out of the tail end, so at a glance the animal is symmetrical and you cannot tell which end is the head except by the eye. The ringed bony armour is only a faint stipple of dots and dashes; there are no visible bony rings breaking the silhouette, which is a smooth unbroken lens. A large translucent grey-green triangular wedge sits across the mid-belly reading as a stray shard rather than a fin.
rows.fix: Give the snout real volume - a short tapering tube roughly one eye-diameter deep ending in a tiny dark pinhole mouth - and replace the tail-end spike with a small fan-shaped caudal fin so the head end is unambiguous.

rows.readsAs: a seahorse - named instantly and correctly
rows.defect: The single dorsal fin is drawn as a flat dark-olive ellipse floating in open water with a clear gap of roughly its own width between it and the body - it never touches the animal, so it reads as a stranded blob or a detached leaf rather than a fin, and it is a muddy dark olive that matches nothing else in the figure. Secondary: the snout is a fat blunt rounded lozenge that reads more duck-bill than horse muzzle, and the ring armour is line-only (hairline diagonals with no relief or plate edge on the silhouette), so it reads as stripes rather than bony plating.
rows.fix: Reattach the dorsal fin to the back of the trunk as a small ridged fluttering membrane in a lighter tint of the body colour, so it grows out of the silhouette instead of floating beside it.

rows.readsAs: a bare red-orange winter shrub or a sea fan; most people would land on 'coral' but a fair few would say 'a leafless bush'
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are not visible. There are no cup-shaped polyps on the surface: the only polyp attempt is a cluster of pale pink out-of-focus blobs floating BEHIND and BETWEEN the trunks, detached from the branches entirely, reading as bokeh haze rather than as anything sitting on the colony. There is no rough calcified texture either -- every branch is a flat, smooth, uniform-width stroke with a single soft gradient and no grain, pitting or chalkiness. The five basal trunks are dark brown round-ended cylinders that read as tree trunks or splayed fingers, and the fine dichotomous twigs with their tapering tips read as woody branches, not as stony coral. The colony also sits small in the frame, occupying roughly 45 percent of the canvas width.
rows.fix: Kill the floating blur cloud and instead stipple actual polyp cups -- small ringed dimples with a dark center and a lit upper lip -- directly along the top edge of every branch and trunk, and break the branch strokes with a coarse chalky noise so the limbs read as calcified stone rather than smooth wood.

rows.readsAs: a nuclear cooling tower, a terracotta flower pot, or an orange lampshade -- not a living organism
rows.defect: The silhouette is a mathematically clean truncated cone: perfectly straight sides, perfect bilateral symmetry, and a crisp white-lipped elliptical rim at the top. Nothing about it is irregular, and irregularity IS the identity of a sponge. There are no osculum holes on the surface at all -- the only opening is the single mouth-like top rim, and the 'pores' are soft brown blurred blotches airbrushed onto the cone with no rim, no shadow, no depth and no actual perforation, so they read as mud stains or rust on a manufactured object. It is not a cooling tower - a hyperboloid tower has concave waisted flanks, and these flanks are perfectly straight. Upheld, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and the real defect list is different.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON CANVAS (read at 1x, then 6x on head, gills, tail and dorsal, plus a screen-blended brightened pass so the dark fins resolve):

1. MOUTH DISC — real defect, mis-described. There is a large pale-rimmed ellipse at the front of the animal, taller than the body is deep, filled flat blue-grey and ruled with ~10 evenly spaced HORIZONTAL lines. It is NOT opaque and it is NOT painted on top of the snout: the layering is the reverse of the claim. The body/snout is drawn OVER the disc — the flank covers the disc's rear third and the pale conical snout wedge sits on top of the disc's middle, tip ending about 60% across it. The disc's forward rim then continues past the snout tip. So it reads as a translucent funnel/collar the head is poking into (lamprey-sucker read is fair; 'hand mirror glued on the front' is not — nothing is glued in front of anything). It does not read as a gape: there is no dark cavity, no jaw line, no rakers, no opening — a uniformly filled plate cannot read as 'held open while feeding'. The eye, a tiny white ring dot, is placed ON the disc's upper-left quadrant rather than on the head, which cements the plate-not-opening read.

2. GILL SLITS — the claim is FLATLY WRONG. The gill lines are NOT inside the disc. Behind the head, on the flank, there are FIVE long dark curved arcs sweeping from the dorsal line almost to the ventral line — they span nearly the full body depth and are the single best-executed must-read on this asset. The horizontal ruling inside the disc is separate interior texture, not the gills. Do not 'move the gills out of the disc' — they are already correct; touching them would break the one thing that works.

3. TAIL — claim correct. Deeply forked caudal, upper and lower lobes equal length and equally pointed, with fine radiating FIN RAYS visible in both lobes. That is a bony-fish/mackerel caudal. A basking shark needs a lunate heterocercal tail with a clearly longer upper lobe and no ray striation.

4. DORSAL — 'ghost dorsal' is half right. It is not faint-and-missing: it is a LARGE rounded dome sitting on the back, roughly a third of body length. Two flaws: it is painted in a near-background dark value so it separates from the body as a detached blob rather than an attached fin, and its shape is a symmetric rounded hump — upright, not the tall soft-triangular DROOPING fin the packet asks for. A matching dark blob sits under the belly (pelvic/anal), same value problem.

5. DEFECT THE OTHER JUDGE MISSED — the skin. The entire flank carries a hexagonal/reticulated SCALE texture with light speckle highlights. Sharks have no visible scales; this is the strongest single cue pushing the chassis toward bony fish, and it is untouched by any of the stated causes.

BAND: FAIL stands. Of the four identity must-reads only the gill slits read. The gaping mouth is absent (a filled plate stands in for it), the conical snout is present but swallowed by that plate, and the dorsal is present but neither drooping nor readable in value. Body + tail + scales together read as a scombrid, so the animal reads as the wrong organism, not as a shark needing polish.

FIX ORDER: (a) replace the filled ellipse with an actual gape — dark cavity interior, visible upper/lower jaw rim, opening AFT of a conical snout tip that stays outside it, and move the eye off it onto the head above/behind the jaw corner; (b) strip the hexagonal scale texture for shark skin; (c) rebuild the caudal as an unrayed lunate fin with a longer upper lobe; (d) lift the dorsal into body value and give it the drooping soft-triangle profile. Leave the five flank gill slits alone.

Looked at the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 6-11x nearest-neighbour crops of head/jaw, dorsal and tail, plus pixel probes. The FAIL stands: this is a deep-bodied bony fish with fangs, not a great white. Zero of the three must-reads are met.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (with corrections to the first judge):

1) COUNTERSHADING - their claim is CORRECT. Vertical pixel probes at x=150/200/250/300 give a flank that is uniform mid-grey top to bottom: at x=250 the dorsal surface is ~(100,111,116) and the ventral edge ~(107,119,123); at x=300 the top is ~(105,115,124) and the belly ~(89,99,105), i.e. the belly is if anything DARKER. Nothing on the body exceeds ~130 luma except the teeth (177). There is no white belly and no boundary line of any kind - only a faint lighter lateral streak along the mid-flank, which is a lateral-line stripe, not countershading.

2) DORSAL - verdict CORRECT, description WRONG in a way that matters for the fix. It is not a translucent ghost. It is an OPAQUE dark-charcoal shape, sampled at (250,148) = (46,53,61), i.e. much darker than the body, composited in a BEHIND-body layer so it reads as a shadow. Its shape is a low rounded DOME/semicircle, not a triangle, and it rises only ~18px above the topline on a body ~104px deep (~17%). A great white's first dorsal should be a tall raked triangle roughly a third of body depth, in body colour, continuous with the topline. An identical dark rounded blob sits behind the ventral line under the mid-body (the pelvic/anal group) with the same wrong colour and wrong z-order.

3) TAIL - verdict CORRECT (it is not a broad crescent) but 'symmetric' is FACTUALLY WRONG. Measured: peduncle at (133,201); upper lobe tip at (65,140) = ~91px; lower lobe tip at (93,235) = ~52px. The upper lobe is 1.75x the lower, so the fork is markedly asymmetric. The real defect is different: both lobes are thin dark needles with almost no membrane area, the fin is drawn in the same near-background charcoal as the dorsal, and there are faint radiating fin-RAY striations trailing past the lobe outline into the water. That is a bony-fish swallowtail. A great white needs a thick, broad, near-lunate caudal with substantial area in both lobes and a keeled, hard-cornered peduncle.

4) TEETH/MOUTH - their claim is CORRECT and is the loudest defect. Seven cream-white cones hang BELOW the head's lower edge, entirely outside the silhouette; the front three float in open water beyond the snout with nothing behind them. Critically, THERE IS NO MOUTH AT ALL - no jaw line, no dark gape, no crescent slung under the snout. The teeth are narrow needle fangs, not triangular serrated blades. The snout itself is a flat 2D wedge tapering to a sharp point (pike/needlefish), not a conical shark rostrum. Four thin dark gill bars sit forward on the cheek.

5) THINGS THE FIRST JUDGE MISSED, which drive the piranha read as much as the teeth do:
   - The entire flank is tiled with overlapping crescent SCALE rows. Sharks have smooth denticle skin with no visible scale pattern; this reads as a carp/piranha.
   - Proportion is badly off: body runs x=133..378 (245px) by 104px deep = aspect ~2.4 against the packet's 3.8 (~3.0 even counting the tail). The result is a deep almond/lens body, not a torpedo.
   - The eye is a bold white ANNULUS with a dark crescent pupil, a cartoon googly ring, against the packet's 'eyes: small'.
   - The pectoral is a small rounded droop rather than a stiff pointed wing.

Net: conical snout over serrated triangular teeth = absent (no mouth); grey/white countershading line = absent; tall triangular dorsal + broad crescent tail = both absent. Nothing rescues this to POLISH.

rows.readsAs: a fish next to a floating domino or battery

I scanned the pixels: the vertical runs at TH=70 go x=348 [195,208], x=349 [196,207], x=350 [195,210], x=351 [177,238], x=352 [168,250] - a single unbroken occupied span with no background column anywhere between the body and the bar. What actually produces the judge's (correct) 'domino bolted to a fish' read is three things:

The snout tapers to a needle: it is only 12-16 px deep at x=346-350 (runs [195,208] then [196,207]) and it butts flat, at 90 degrees, into a bar that spans y=152..252 (101 px, 19 px wide, x=351..369, straight parallel sides, fully rounded ends, ~5.3:1). Two masses meeting over a 13 px contact with no fillet, no blend, no head volume behind it - so the eye separates them into two objects even though they touch. The whole head is that 19 px slab: no mouth, no nares, no cranium, no under-slung jaw.
(b) THE EYES READ AS PUNCHED HOLES. They sit correctly at the outer tips (y~152-160 and y~244-252), which does satisfy 'eyes at the outer tips', but each is a bright white annulus around a centre sampled at (360,157) = rgb(16,22,28) - i.e. the centre is the BACKGROUND colour. They read as grommets / rivet holes / screw eyes in a metal plate, which is what pushes the slab toward 'hardware'.
(c) THE BASE ORGANISM IS A BONY FISH, NOT A SHARK. The body is a deep, symmetric almond pointed at BOTH ends, covered in a regular diamond/reticulated SCALE pattern (visible at 7x). Bright bbox is 132..369 x 152..252 = 237 x 100, aspect 2.37 against a target aspect of 4.3 - so 'slender grey body' FAILS; it is a tuna/mackerel torso, roughly half as long-for-depth as it should be. So the dorsal is ~35% of body depth, and the rise profile is a symmetric rounded dome, not a tall backswept sickle. Worse, it is painted a dark olive - markedly darker than the body - so it reads as a shadow or a far-side lump sitting behind the fish rather than a fin on the silhouette. There is a matching dark dome under the belly that reads the same way. The hammerhead's signature is a first dorsal taller than the body is deep and strongly falcate; this is the opposite.

Supporting (not must-read): the gill slits are ~6 dark dashes at x~284-310, i.e. 40-85 px BEHIND the head on a ~172 px body - they sit mid-flank like flank striping instead of immediately behind the head. Only one small pectoral fin is visible, low and far back at x~305-330.

Give the head actual volume (a flattened cranium wedge carrying the bar, with an under-slung crescent mouth), fillet the cephalofoil into that head instead of butting a slab onto a 13 px needle, taper the cephalofoil (thicker at the centre, thinner at the lobes) and give the lobes a leading-edge sweep so it stops being a constant-width pill; make the eyes solid dark orbs with a small specular instead of white rings around background-coloured holes; rebuild the first dorsal as a tall falcate fin at least as tall as the body is deep, drawn in body tone ON the silhouette rather than as a dark shadow behind it; stretch the torso to ~4.3 aspect; replace the diamond scale texture with denticle/countershading; and convert the symmetric forked tail to a heterocercal one with a long notched upper lobe.

VERDICT UPHELD, BUT TWO OF THE FOUR STATED CAUSES ARE FACTUALLY WRONG. I decoded the 440x440 PNG and re-rendered it at 4x-16x on the tail, gills, dorsal, eye and pectoral. What is actually there:

CORRECTION 1 - THE ASYMMETRIC TAIL IS PRESENT, NOT ABSENT. The judge's headline claim ('symmetric rayed fan') is flatly wrong. At 9x the caudal is a two-bladed fork with a clearly LONGER UPPER LOBE: the upper blade runs from the peduncle up-and-forward to a tip roughly 1.8x the reach of the lower blade, and it is swept at a shallower angle. There are no fin rays anywhere - both lobes are smooth solid blades. The must-read 'asymmetric tail with a long upper lobe' READS. Its real weakness is value, not geometry: both lobes are a near-black blue-grey barely a step off the background plate, so at native 440px the whole tail sinks into the void and the fish looks tail-less. Fix contrast, do not redraw the asymmetry.

CORRECTION 2 - THE FIVE GILL SLITS ARE PRESENT AND COUNTABLE, NOT A SMUDGE. At 12x I count EXACTLY FIVE discrete, evenly spaced, vertical dark-grey bars on the flank behind the head, correctly angled and correctly placed. They are not a smudge and not a hatch blur - they are five clean slits. The defect is contrast and layering: they are mid-grey painted UNDER the bright diamond scale checker, so the scale texture reads over the top of them and at native size they collapse to a grey patch. This is a value/layer-order fix, not a redraw.

CORRECTION 3 - THE DORSAL IS NOT A GHOST, IT IS THE WRONG SHAPE. It is a solid, opaque, clearly visible dark-grey mass sitting on the back - visible even in the unzoomed read. But at 9x it is a ROUNDED SEMICIRCULAR DOME: a half-disc with no apex, no leading/trailing edge distinction, no rearward sweep. The must-read 'triangular dorsal fin' genuinely fails, but because it was drawn as a hump, not because it faded out. Give it an apex and a swept trailing edge.

CONFIRMED - THE JUVENILE CUE IS ABSENT. I cropped Shark.png and Reef_Shark.png at matching coordinates: the eye is the identical small cream ring with a dark pupil, the pectoral is the identical short swept blade, the dorsal is the identical dome, the gill bars are the identical five, the tail is the identical fork. Juvenile Shark is a straight rescale of the shared family chassis with no enlargement of eye or fins and no slimming of the body. The note's entire content is unexpressed.

THE REAL REASON THIS FAILS - WRONG ORGANISM, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE JUDGE SAID. The animal reads as a SCALED BONY FISH - a sardine/herring/mackerel - because of features the judge only gestured at: (a) a dense diamond SCALE CHECKER tiled over the entire flank from shoulder to peduncle, catching specular highlights; sharks have smooth denticled skin and show no scale pattern at any scale; (b) a deep silver belly and a sharply pointed TERMINAL wedge snout; (c) the mouth is not a ventral crescent slung back under the snout - instead there are SEVEN small white triangular teeth floating along the underside of the snout's leading edge with NO drawn jaw line or gape behind them, so they read as detached white specks at native size and as a needlefish's beak at zoom; (d) the eye sits at the very tip of the head AND STRADDLES THE DORSAL CONTOUR - its upper half protrudes outside the body silhouette into the background, an outright placement bug neither judge named.

So: three of the packet's must-reads are physically on the canvas (asymmetric tail, five gill slits, pectoral blade), one is malformed (dome not triangle), the juvenile note is unexpressed - and none of it rescues the read, because the chassis underneath is a teleost. FAIL stands. The fix list is: strip the scale checker, replace the dome with a triangular dorsal, raise value contrast on tail and gills so the existing correct geometry survives at native size, move the eye fully inside the silhouette and enlarge it plus the fins for the juvenile cue, and replace the row of floating teeth with an underslung crescent mouth.

Damningly: Reef Shark's eye is 10 x 10 on a 298 px body and Great White's is 14 x 14 on a 312 px body, and BOTH of those rows specify eyes:small. Mako's row specifies eyes:prominent / 'large black eye' and its eye is the smallest-relative in the group. Must-read fails outright.

What is wrong is the execution - the 7 spikes hang outside the silhouette below the chin with NO mouth or jaw line drawn anywhere, so they read as decals stuck under the throat. FAMILY CHECK - ONE CHASSIS, NINE COLOURS. Confirmed by the 9-up strip: Basking, Great White, Hammerhead, Juvenile, Mako, Reef, Shark, Tiger, Whale all share the identical fusiform body outline, the same low rounded dorsal hump in the same position, the same unequal forked tail, the same white eye annulus, the same gill-dash row and the same low swept pectoral. The real tail defect is form, not asymmetry: both lobes are thin straight needle blades meeting at a deep sharp V notch, with a faint low-alpha ghost fan/ray webbing filling the gap between them. That is a lunate tuna/mackerel caudal, not a shark heterocercal tail, which needs a broad FLESHY upper lobe continuous with the body axis (with a subterminal notch near its tip) and a much smaller ventral lobe. So must-read 'asymmetric tail with a longer upper lobe' is technically satisfied but the organism read is wrong. (3) MOUTH - CONFIRMED EXACTLY. There is no mouth of any kind. The snout is a long thin wedge tapering to a needle point and simply ends; no crescent, no gape, no underslung slit, not even a jaw line. Must-read 'crescent mouth set under the snout' is ABSENT. The judge also missed the single strongest non-shark signal: the entire flank is covered in an even honeycomb/dotted SCALE grid. Sharks have no scales - this bony-fish scale field plus the terminal eye and the lunate rayed tail are what make it read as a mackerel. Pectoral is a low swept blade behind the gills, acceptable; there is a small ventral bump mid-body. FIX ORDER: replace the dome with a tall straight-edged triangular first dorsal drawn IN FRONT of the body on the topline; cut in an underslung crescent mouth set back from the snout tip and move the eye back off the point and inside the silhouette; kill the scale grid for a smooth denticle-matte flank; rebuild the caudal as a fleshy heterocercal lobe rather than two needle blades with a ray fan; reduce the gill slashes to five.

rows.readsAs: a barracuda with faint banding

rows.verifyWhy: Verdict upheld, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and the real wrong-organism drivers were not named. WHAT I SAW at 6x on the head crop (orig x280-400, y150-250): the snout is a long, extremely acute needle-cone. The topline and the ventral line converge to a single sharp point roughly 45px forward of the eye, with no vertical front face, no squared leading edge, no broad flattened shovel. The mustRead 'blunt square-fronted snout' is not merely weak, it is INVERTED — this is the sharpest snout in the batch, sharper than the Mako's. That part of the claim is correct and it is the identity-defining failure on its own. TAIL — THE CLAIM IS WRONG. It is NOT the family symmetric fan. Measuring off the 6x tail crop: peduncle/fork centre at orig (128,202), upper lobe tip at (62,153), lower lobe tip at (95,228). Upper lobe = ~82px, lower = ~42px, a ratio of ~1.95:1. The upper lobe IS the longer one and it is clearly readable as such. The actual defect is its SHAPE, not its symmetry: it is a needle-thin straight spike of a deeply-forked tuna/scombrid caudal, with a lower lobe of nearly equal width at the base, rather than the broad, soft, trailing heterocercal sweep a tiger shark needs. Any fix should thicken and curve the upper lobe and shrink the lower one — do not lengthen it, it is already long. STRIPES — the claim is directionally right but mis-described. They are not 'smudges'. At full size I count roughly six discrete broad vertical bands running top-to-bottom across the mid-flank at even spacing, correctly placed and correctly oriented. They fail on CONTRAST only: they are perhaps 8-10% darker than the surrounding body value, and they sit under a bright hex mesh that carries far more local contrast than they do, so the mesh wins the eye. Fix is a value push on the existing bands, not new geometry. THE THREE THINGS THE JUDGE MISSED, which are what actually make this read as a barracuda/mackerel rather than any shark: (1) the entire body is tiled in a dense hexagonal BONY-SCALE mesh with individually lit scales — sharks have no visible scales, and this single texture is the loudest wrong-clade signal in the image; (2) the teeth are drawn as seven separate white fangs hanging BELOW the jaw line, outside the body silhouette, in a barracuda/anglerfish arrangement, instead of a crescent mouth slung under the snout; (3) the dorsal fin is a low rounded dome hump sitting behind the head, not a tall triangular first dorsal. Correctly present and worth keeping: a row of ~7 thin dark gill slits behind the jaw, a swept pectoral wing, a pelvic fin, and the small ringed eye set high and well forward. Net: one of three must-reads (stripes) present but under-contrasted, one (upper tail lobe) present in length but wrong in form, one (blunt square snout) absent and reversed — and the scale mesh plus external fang row push the whole asset out of the shark clade. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a mackerel with grey mould blotches
rows.defect: Every must-read fails. The head is the same pointed cone as the rest of the family with the mouth nowhere in evidence - certainly not a huge flat terminal mouth spanning the front of a boxy flattened head - and the tiny eye sits at the extreme tip of the snout, not at the corner of a broad head. The markings are irregular soft grey-brown blotches, not a white checkerboard of spots and lines, and they read as discolouration. No flank ridges of any kind. Same fan tail.

FAIL upheld, but the diagnosis needs correcting on several points and the real defect is bigger than the one stated. I cropped and upscaled the head (5x), the whole body (3x) and the snout (11x over a light matte) and measured the silhouette from the decoded pixels.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS: this does not read as a shark at all, it reads as a generic bony fish on the family lens chassis. The silhouette is a symmetric almond/leaf pointed at BOTH ends, with the opaque body bbox at x135-366, y156-242 = 231x86px, aspect 2.69 (about 3.0 if the faint caudal fin out to x~80 is included) against the packet's required 4.5 - far too stubby and deep-bellied for any shark. The caudal fin is a symmetric homocercal forked fish tail with visible radiating fin RAYS drawn in, not a heterocercal shark tail. The dorsal is a single soft rounded triangle at mid-back; there is a low anal/pelvic lobe under the belly and a small rounded pectoral low on the right. The entire flank is covered in a dense staggered lattice of overlapping crescent SCALES - unmistakable bony-fish scale texture. So before any whale-shark must-read is even considered, the chassis is the wrong order of animal.

MUST-READ 1 (huge flat terminal mouth on a boxy flattened head) - ABSENT, and the judge is right. The head is not modelled at all: the two body outlines simply converge to a single sharp triangular point at x=366. At 11x with a light matte I can confirm there is NO mouth line, no jaw, no lip, no opening of any kind anywhere on the snout - not terminal and not slung underneath. There is a faint horizontal boundary running forward to the tip, but that is the edge of the paler ventral colour panel, not a mouth. No boxy or flattened head, no squared front.

EYE - the judge's description is WRONG in two ways. The eye is not tiny: it is a large, high-contrast bright-white annulus (~13px outer diameter, roughly 15% of body depth) with a black pupil and a specular highlight, which directly contradicts the packet's 'eyes: small' and is one of the loudest features in the whole image. Nor is it at the very snout tip: its centre is at about x=337, roughly 29px (more than two of its own diameters) behind the tip at x=366, sitting above the midline on the upper taper. So the eye is forward and dorsally placed, but it is oversized and set back, not a tiny dot at the point. It is still wrong for the species - whale shark eyes are minute and sit at the outer corners of a wide flat head - but the fix is 'shrink it drastically and move it out to the head corner', not 'move it back from the tip'.

MUST-READ 2 (checkerboard of white spots and lines) - FAILS, though the judge under-described what is there. There are TWO separate marking layers. (a) A regular, grid-regular lattice of pale crescent scallops over the whole flank - regular, yes, but it reads as fish scales, not spots: each mark is a scale-shaped arc in staggered overlapping rows, the contrast against the body is very low, and there are no white cross-lines at all. (b) Five or six soft, irregular, dark greenish-grey blotches (upper mid-back, upper shoulder, mid-flank, lower mid, lower rear) - these are the 'mould' the judge saw, and they are correct as described: irregular, soft-edged, and DARK on a pale body. The polarity is inverted from the species: a whale shark is a dark body carrying crisp bright-white dots in ordered rows with white bars between them. Nothing here is white and nothing forms a checkerboard.

MUST-READ 3 (prominent flank ridges) - the judge's 'no flank ridges' is broadly right but not literally true. There IS a thin pale horizontal stroke running along the flank, broken into two segments: a long one from the tail end forward to about mid-body at the vertical midline, and a short second segment just behind/below the eye. It reads as a single bony-fish lateral line, one pixel-thin and low contrast. That is not the whale shark feature, which is a set of three thick raised longitudinal keels standing proud of the flank. So: one thin lateral line present, zero ridges.

ONE FEATURE THE JUDGE MISSED THAT IS PRESENT: behind the eye, in the shoulder region (roughly x=305-345), there is a run of about eight dark near-vertical hatch strokes that read convincingly as gill slits. That is the only shark-family cue in the drawing. It is over-counted (8 rather than 5) and the strokes are thin scratches rather than the whale shark's very long slits, but the feature exists and should be kept and thickened rather than re-added from scratch.

NET: three of three must-reads fail, and the underlying chassis is a scaled bony fish with a rayed forked tail, so this cannot be polished into a whale shark - it needs the shark body plan (long 4.5 aspect torpedo, heterocercal tail with a long upper lobe), then a wide squared-off flattened head carrying a full-width terminal mouth, tiny eyes pushed out to the head corners, three raised flank ridges, and the scale lattice replaced by a dark ground with a bright white spot-and-bar checkerboard.

rows.readsAs: a small tan sheep or a hornless-ish lamb toy

The 'slim antelope-like legs' are the same four thick straight posts as the Sheep and the Takin, and the barrel is the same depth as the Goat's, so nothing about it is antelope-built. Tailless like the rest of the family.

MUST-READ 1 - 'black-and-white facial mask stripes': GENUINELY ABSENT, and the measurement is unambiguous. Over the whole head region (3,273 non-background pixels) there are ZERO pixels above L=210 and only 116 below L=45 - and those 116 are the eye pupil and the two thin engraved lines for the nostril and the mouth corner. A luminance transect straight down the muzzle at y=140/150/158/166/174 returns the SAME bucket (L~104-143, mid-brown) at every single sample from the eye to the nose tip. There is no white cheek, no white throat, no white on the muzzle bridge, no black eye-to-nose bar, no dark chin. CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM: what the other judge called 'a vague darker smudge at the eye' is not a smudge and not a marking - at 8x it resolves into the EARS. MUST-READ 2 - 'short vertical horns hooked sharply backward at the tips': PARTIALLY PRESENT, and the judge is right that the hook is missing. Two horns are drawn, they are short (about a third of head height) and they are vertical, so the 'short vertical' half reads. But the tips do not hook: the near horn is a nearly straight slightly forward-leaning prong, and the far horn actually curves gently FORWARD/outward at its tip - the opposite of the chamois' near-right-angle rearward crook, which is the single most diagnostic thing on the animal. Additional defect the other judge did not name: the horns are pale cream/bone, the same bone colour the Goat, Ibex and Sheep horns use in this batch. A real chamois' hooks are jet black, and black horns against a tan face would have carried half the identity on their own. Pale + unhooked means the horns actively read as generic caprine.

MUST-READ 3 - 'slim antelope-like legs': the claim is right in effect but wrong in description. They are NOT 'thick straight posts'. The real problem is the one the other judge was reaching for: I rendered Goat.png at the identical crop and the limbs are pixel-for-pixel the same construction - same taper, same fetlock band, same two-toe hoof, same near-vertical hind leg with no hock angulation, and the same rump facet wedge, same topline, same barrel and same muzzle/eye geometry. So the legs are the family-standard limb, not anything antelope-specific; 'slim antelope-like' is not differentiating this asset from the goat next to it.

OTHER OBSERVATIONS: no tail is visible at all on the rump (chamois has a short black tail; not a listed must-read but the rump is bare). No dark dorsal stripe, no pale rump patch. The coat is a uniform khaki-tan with a light shaggy stroke texture across the shoulder and flank.

NET: the only feature that reads is 'has two short horns'. Stripped of the black mask and the hooked tips, this silhouette is the batch's shared goat chassis in tan - it would be read as a young goat or a generic small ungulate, not a chamois. FAIL stands.

FIX ORDER: (1) black eye-to-muzzle bar + white cheek/throat/muzzle-bridge mask - this alone converts the asset; (2) recolour the horns black and put a hard rearward crook in the top ~25% of each; (3) add a short dark tail and differentiate the limb from the Goat's.

rows.readsAs: a white sheep — it is very nearly the Sheep.png asset in a cooler white
rows.defect: Placed beside Sheep.png this is the same animal: same white woolly flank texture, same ram-curl horn, same muzzle, same posture. Every discriminator the packet note names is missing — there is NO chin beard under the jaw, NO tail at all (let alone one flicked up over the rump), the coat is woolly rather than flat, and the face is a broad bulbous down-turned snout rather than a straight narrow goat profile. The horn is a curled ram's horn, not a backward-sweeping goat horn.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at full size and at 6-14x crops of head, chin/jawline, rump, belly and feet, plus a normalised-silhouette comparison against the rest of the family. The FAIL stands and the judge's description is accurate on every point I could check; I am correcting/sharpening three details.

MUST-READ 1 'backward-sweeping horns' - ABSENT, AND INVERTED. At 14x the single horn is a segmented/ribbed band that leaves the brow, arcs up and BACK over the skull, then rolls DOWN and FORWARD in front of the ear, finishing low beside the eye. It closes into a near-complete ring. That is a ram's spiral curl, not a horn sweeping backward and away. Correction to the judge, in their favour: side by side with Sheep.png at the same zoom, the Goat's curl is drawn MORE closed than the Sheep's (the Sheep's leaves a gap and its tip stops higher). So this is not a shared-horn slip in which the goat merely inherited the sheep's horn - the goat is the more ram-like of the two animals.

MUST-READ 2 'chin beard' - ABSENT. At 9x on the jaw and throat, the underline of the head is one unbroken smooth curve from the blunt nose back into the neck and on into the chest. No tuft, no dangling strands, no silhouette bump, not even a shaded suggestion of one. The only marks under the muzzle are a thin straight mouth line and a small nostril hook.

MUST-READ 3 'short upright tail flicked up over the rump' - ABSENT. At 9x the rump is a clean convex hemisphere. There is no tail in any form: not up, not down, not a stub. I swept the region above, behind and below the hip and found nothing but the smooth fleece arc.

NOTE DISAMBIGUATORS ('tail up, coat flat, face straighter and narrower') - all three fail. Coat: the flank and rump carry long shaggy hair strokes, and the belly ends in a hanging woolly fringe with bare smooth legs emerging from underneath it. That fringe-plus-bare-legs construction is verbatim the SHEEP row's must-read ('thick woolly fleece blurring the body outline / narrow bare face and legs sticking out of the fleece'), so the Goat is currently scoring the Sheep's identity rather than its own. Face: the muzzle is broad and deep with a blunt bulbous nose that swells downward and overhangs the mouth line - the judge's 'broad bulbous snout' is exactly right; it is not the straight narrow goat profile.

SAMENESS CLAIM - CONFIRMED QUANTITATIVELY. Masking out the background and normalising both to their bounding boxes, Goat vs Sheep silhouette IoU is 0.927; the whole batch is one chassis (Goat/Ibex 0.905, Goat/Chamois 0.908, Sheep/Ibex 0.892). Shared parts: identical topline and croup arc, identical straight-column foreleg with the same slight hock kink behind, identical dark two-toed cloven hoof, identical neck set, identical head shape and eye placement, identical horn construction. Real differences between Goat and Sheep are only: colour temperature (Goat a cool grey-white, Sheep a warm tan), overall scale in frame (Goat bbox 186x187 px vs Sheep 210x209), and the ear - the Goat carries a noticeably LARGER dark teardrop ear swept back-and-down plus a small nub at the horn base, where the Sheep's ear is a small dark ellipse. That ear is the one thing the judge slightly understated by calling the two heads simply 'the same muzzle'; it is nevertheless a sheep-shaped difference, not a goat cue.

WHAT IS CORRECT: the cloven, dark, two-toed hooves; the quadruped posture and 1.5-ish aspect; the prominent amber-irised eye called for by the eyes:prominent field.

VERDICT: zero of three must-reads read, all three note disambiguators fail, and the asset reads to me as a white ram. FAIL upheld. The fixes this needs, in order: (1) replace the closed ram curl with a horn that leaves the brow and sweeps back and up away from the skull without curling forward; (2) add a chin beard hanging clear of the jaw so it breaks the silhouette; (3) add a short upright tail flicked up over the croup; (4) flatten the coat to a short close-lying pelt and delete the hanging belly fringe; (5) narrow and straighten the muzzle, removing the downward bulb at the nose.

rows.defect: The massive backward-arcing knobbed horns that ARE the ibex are not there.
