UPHELD, but two parts of the original claim are wrong and the fix brief must not be written against them.

WHAT I ACTUALLY SAW (440x440, cropped and upscaled 5-10x on head, jaw, barrel and rump).

HORNS — the verdict stands, the stated cause is half wrong. There are TWO horns drawn (a near one and a slightly offset far one), not one. They rise from the brow, arc up and BACK over the crown, then curl DOWN and slightly FORWARD to terminate beside the cheek just behind the eye — a closed ram/mouflon curl, not a scimitar. Measured: the horn arc occupies roughly 42 x 35 source px against a head that is ~72 px from muzzle tip to back of skull, so each horn is about half a head-length and its tip never passes the back of the skull, let alone reaches the shoulder. 'Massive' and 'backward-arcing over the shoulder' are genuinely absent. HOWEVER the judge's 'no knobbed ridges' is FALSE: each horn is explicitly drawn with 6-7 transverse segment bands (alternating light/dark cross-ridges) clearly visible at 10x. The ridging is the one ibex cue that landed. The problem is that it is not exclusive — I rendered the Goat and the Sheep heads at the same crop and BOTH wear the identical curl at the identical scale with the identical transverse banding. So the horn does not fail for lack of ridges; it fails for lack of LENGTH and for being the family's shared default horn. The fix is a horn 2-3x head-length sweeping back in an open arc over the withers, keeping the ridge banding it already has (and taking the plain curl off the Ibex so Goat/Sheep/Ibex stop sharing one horn asset).

BEARD — the judge's 'no goat beard under the chin either' is also partly wrong, and the correction matters. There IS a fringe of dark hair strands hanging off the underside of the jaw and down the throat, ~15 px long, absent on the Sheep and Goat. But it is NOT a beard: at 3x on the whole body the identical strand fringe runs continuously along the entire belly line, the topline, the chest and the rump. It is a global shaggy-coat fringe pass that happens to cross the jaw. There is no discrete chin tuft, no separation between jaw hair and throat/chest hair, so nothing reads as a beard. Fix = a distinct, denser, darker wedge of hair pendant from the chin point specifically, terminated so it visually separates from the chest fringe.

BODY — the judge is correct and I confirm it stronger than stated. This is the family chassis, and specifically it is the SHEEP asset: skull outline, eye placement and iris ring, nostril dash, mouth line, the dark oval ear on the cheek, the four straight cylindrical legs and the small dark cloven hoof are the same construction as Sheep.png pixel-for-pixel in placement; only fringe density and hue differ. The barrel is a slim even tube with no shoulder mass, no crested neck, no chest depth — 'stocky muscular' does not read at all. A real ibex is deep-chested with a heavy neck and short thick legs.

TWO ADDITIONAL DEFECTS the original judge did not report: (1) flat pale quadrilateral/wedge facets are visible where the limb masses meet the barrel at BOTH the shoulder and the hip — at 6x on the rump it is an unshaded flat plane sitting on top of the haunch, a limb-attachment seam that breaks the silhouette and the painterly surface. (2) There is NO tail at all; the rump ends in a bare abrupt curve.

Band: FAIL. Two of three must-reads (massive backward-arcing horns; goat beard) are not readable, the third (stocky muscular body) is contradicted by the shared slim chassis, and side-by-side with Sheep.png this animal is not distinguishable as a different species.

rows.readsAs: a sheep — correct, and the only asset in the batch whose reference and render agree
rows.defect: The fleece and the bare face-and-legs-out-of-the-fleece boundary do read, but the short drooping tail is completely absent — the rump ends in a bare curve. The fleece is also a painted-on stripe texture rather than a mass that blurs the outline: the body silhouette is the same hard-edged barrel as the Goat's, so the fleece never softens the profile the way the reference asks.
rows.fix: Add the short drooping tail hanging off the rump, and break the fleece silhouette with irregular clumped lobes so the outline goes woolly instead of staying a clean barrel edge.

rows.readsAs: a shaggy golden goat or a small yak — not a bison-built goat-antelope
rows.defect: The long shaggy golden coat is the one must-read that lands, and it is the most distinct asset here. But the horns do not sweep outward then back like a wildebeest's — there is one pale bent tube emerging from a dark blob on the crown, ambiguous in count and direction. There are no humped shoulders: the topline is the family's level line with only a token rise, and the legs are the family's standard-length posts rather than short thick ones. The muzzle is the same bulbous down-curved family snout with no arched Roman nose.
rows.fix: Rebuild the front end for bison proportions — raise a distinct shoulder hump above the topline, shorten the legs by about a quarter while thickening them, and replace the single tube with a clear symmetric pair of horns that go out sideways from the crown before hooking back.

rows.readsAs: a white downy chick or a small grey-and-white quail poult
rows.defect: The identity must-read is inverted: the bill is a short straight yellow-orange cone that if anything tips slightly DOWN, with no upward sweep and no needle thinness - it is the same bill as the Curlew and the Snipe in this batch. There is no crisp black-and-white pied patterning either; the body is a uniform soft white-grey mottle with a grey wing crescent, no blocked black cap, nape or wing panels. The legs are yellow-ochre, not long blue-grey, and they are short and stubby rather than long.
rows.fix: Draw a genuinely long, hair-thin black bill that sweeps clearly upward past the top of the skull, and repaint the body as hard-edged black blocks (crown/nape, two wing bars, wingtips) on pure white, on long slate-blue legs.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified by rendering the PNG at 1:1 and again at 5x/6x zoom on the head, body and feet, plus a pixel-mask measurement of the bill and leg geometry (440x440 canvas).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Subject bbox x75-363, y109-319 (288 x 210 incl. bill; body-only ~225 x 210). A round white ball body, a small white ball head on top-left (head ~54px across, top of skull y109), a yellow-ochre bill projecting left, a mid-grey hard-edged crescent across the shoulder, a mid-grey wing-tip smudge and a mid-grey wedge tail running down-right to x363, and two thin ochre two-jointed legs with flat foot-bars.

MUST-READ 1 - 'thin needle bill sweeping strongly upward': ABSENT, and this alone is the FAIL. I masked the bill's yellow pixels and walked it column by column. It spans x79 (tip) to x~148 (base). Per-column vertical midline: 137.0 at x79-84, 136.5-137.0 through x88-140, 136.5 at x144. That is a DEAD-FLAT horizontal axis over its whole 69px length - zero curvature, zero sweep, in either direction. CORRECTION TO THE FILING JUDGE: they said the bill 'tips slightly downward'. It does not. It is perfectly horizontal (tip sits 0.5px below the base centreline, i.e. within antialias noise). The downward impression comes from the upper edge dropping 6px from base to tip while the lower edge rises 5px - a symmetric taper on a level axis, not a droop. So the correct defect statement is 'straight and level' not 'downcurved'. Their second point is right though: it is a solid ~12px-thick tapering cone/dagger, not a needle. It is also not as short as they imply - 69px is ~1.28x head diameter - but it is far short of the avocet's near-2x needle, and with no upsweep at all the head reads as a tern or a small gull, not an avocet. The packet's own note ('The bill curves up, not down - the opposite of a curlew's') is the whole identification and it is not delivered.

MUST-READ 2 - 'crisp black-and-white pied patterning': PARTIAL, and the filing judge described this one WRONG. There is NOT 'just a uniform soft white-grey mottle'. There are three distinct, hard-edged dark shapes on the white body: a bold C-shaped arc sweeping from the nape down around the shoulder and back (sampled RGB 91,92,93), a dark wedge at the wing tip, and the tail wedge (darkest sample 53,55,59) against body white (253,253,254). So blocking exists and its edges are crisp. What actually fails is (a) the dark is MID-GREY, not black - the darkest pixel on the bird is ~53, nothing approaches black; (b) the pattern is a decorative swoosh/crescent, not the avocet's blocked scapular and wing panels; and (c) the head and nape are pure white (sampled 240,241,242 at the crown) with no black cap or nape stripe at all, which is the avocet's most legible plumage cue after the bill. A fix aimed at 'add pattern, it's currently flat' would be aimed at the wrong thing - pattern is present, it is the wrong pattern in the wrong value range and in the wrong places.

MUST-READ 3 - 'long blue-grey legs': PARTIALLY WRONG AS FILED. Colour: the judge is correct, the legs sample 189,153,75 / 224,177,60 - clearly yellow-ochre, no trace of blue-grey. Form: 'short stubs' is an overstatement. At 6x zoom they are proper thin two-segment bird legs with a rearward-bending hock and flat three-bar feet, running from the torso underside (y~259) to the ground line (y~319) - about 60px, ~28% of figure height. So they are medium, articulated and legible; the defect is that they are the wrong colour and not long enough for a wader, NOT that they are shapeless stubs.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT THE FILING JUDGE DID NOT NAME: the packet asks for aspect 1.8. Measured aspect is 1.37 including the bill and ~1.07 body-only - the torso is a near-circular ball, not the long low shorebird chassis. Combined with the level dagger bill and short ochre legs the silhouette reads as a plump white gull/tern chick.

VERDICT: FAIL upheld. The single defining must-read (strongly upswept needle bill) is measurably absent - the bill is straight and horizontal - and the pied blocking is grey-on-white decoration with an all-white head. The asset does not read as an avocet.

rows.readsAs: a buff-coloured downy chick or a small partridge poult
rows.defect: The one feature that IS a curlew - a very long, smoothly downcurved bill up to a quarter of the profile - is absent. The rendered bill is a short straight yellow cone barely longer than the head, pixel-for-pixel the same bill drawn on the Avocet, Godwit, Sandpiper and Snipe. The legs are short and stubby, not long bare wading legs, and there is no neck: the ball head sits directly on the egg body.
rows.fix: Replace the cone with a long dark bill roughly a quarter of the total width that curves smoothly downward through its length, and stretch the legs to at least twice the current length with visible bare tibia above the joint.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of the three stated causes are wrong and must not be fixed as stated.

WHAT I SAW (440x440 PNG, read at native size and again at 5x zoom on head and feet, plus pixel measurement of the silhouette):

BILL — the defect is CURVATURE, NOT LENGTH. The judge's 'barely longer than the head' is measurably false. The ink bbox of the whole animal is x101-337 (237px profile). The gold bill runs x106 to x~166 = ~61px, i.e. 26% of the total profile length — which actually MEETS the packet note's target ('the bill can be a quarter of the total profile length'). Against the head ball (~36px across, x163-199) the bill is ~1.7 head-lengths. So it is not short. What is absent is the downcurve, and absolutely so: the bill centreline is y=156 at the tip (x106) and y=156 at the base (x165, span 151..161) — a perfectly symmetric wedge about a dead-horizontal axis, zero deviation from a straight line, and not even tilted downward. It is a straight gold triangular cone with a sharp point. The must-read 'very long SMOOTHLY DOWNCURVED bill' is therefore not readable at all; the one feature that IS a curlew is missing. The fix is to bend it, not to lengthen it — lengthening a straight cone will produce a godwit or a snipe, not a curlew.

CHASSIS — the judge is RIGHT that it is the shared family bill, and I verified it numerically. Bill lengths across the batch: Curlew 61px/26% of profile, Avocet 64px/22%, Snipe 63px/22%, Godwit 63px/24%, Sandpiper 57px/24%, Oystercatcher 60px/32%. Every one of those centrelines is flat (Avocet tip-mid 137 -> mid 136.5; Snipe 149 -> 148.5; Curlew 156 -> 156). Side-by-side 5x crops of the Curlew, Avocet and Snipe heads are the SAME drawing: identical smooth sphere-shaded ball head, identical small black eye dot with the same upper-left white specular pip in the same relative position, identical gold-amber straight wedge attached at the same height, only the body/head hue differs. Avocet's 'strongly upswept' and Snipe's 'eye high and far back' fail for the same reason. This is one head primitive in three colours.

LEGS — the judge's 'short stubs' is WRONG as described. There are two properly articulated bare legs in ochre-yellow, each with a clear rear-bending joint (tarsal bend), a straight tibia above and tarsus below, and a three-toed forward foot with a visible hind claw on the near leg. They are not stubs. They ARE too short: they clear only ~38-40px between the belly line (y~255) and the toes (y~293) against a body ball ~126px tall, so about 0.3 body-heights, and the plumped round belly hangs almost to the substrate. 'Long bare wading legs' does not read — but the fix is lengthening the existing two-segment leg, not building a leg where none exists.

NECK — the judge is CORRECT. There is no neck. The head sphere is fused directly onto the body sphere with a short taper of overlap; no neck column exists at any width. A curlew carries the head on a distinct slim neck.

BODY/PLUMAGE — the one must-read that partly survives. The body is mottled/speckled pale buff-brown with darker scalloped wing coverts and a small round head, which is in the right family of markings for 'streaked brown body on a small round head'. But the body is a near-circular ball (much rounder than the 1.4 aspect implies once bill and tail are subtracted), giving a chick-like or quail-like read rather than a wader's elongated horizontal body. A dark wedge tail with a few filament vanes trails right.

OVERALL: it reads as a generic plump round shorebird chick with a straight cone bill. Two of three must-reads (downcurved bill, long wading legs) are not readable, and the bill — the identifying feature the note explicitly warns about ('drawing it short or straight destroys the identification') — is straight. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a plain brown chick or a young brown quail
rows.defect: The very long straight bill that defines a godwit is not drawn - the bill is the batch's standard short yellow cone, roughly one head-length, with no pale base and no length at all. The breast is a flat uniform mid-brown wash with no cinnamon tone and none of the dark chevron barring called for. The legs are short yellow stubs rather than the long dark legs of a godwit, and the body is the same neckless egg as every other bird here.
rows.fix: Give it a bill two to three head-lengths long, straight with a very slight upward tilt and a pale pink base fading to dark tip, and bar the cinnamon breast with a stack of dark chevrons.
rows.verifyWhy:
I read the PNG at full size and then re-cropped it at 4x-8x on the head/bill, the breast, the legs and the tail, and sampled raw pixel values. The FAIL stands, but two of the three stated causes are described wrongly and would send a fix in the wrong direction.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Bird silhouette occupies x88-345, y124-304 (257 x 180 px). The bill is a straight golden-yellow cone spanning x88 to x150 on rows y142-y156: 62 px long against a ~48 px head diameter, i.e. about 1.3 head-lengths and ~24% of the total profile. So the judge's phrasing 'the same one-head-length cone' understates the length -- length alone is not the failure. The real failure is shape and identity: (a) it is a THICK cone, ~14 px deep at the base tapering to a point (23% aspect), where a godwit's bill is a fine near-parallel needle; (b) it is dead horizontal and symmetric about its axis -- the required faint UPWARD tilt is completely absent; (c) the 'pale base' is absent, and I verified this by sampling rather than by eye: the bill is #e0b13c at x150 (base), #e0b13c at x120 (mid) and #e0b13c out to x106, with only antialias ramp (#b18d34, #8a6e2b) in the last few pixels of the tip. Zero tonal break anywhere along it.

THE CHASSIS FINDING, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE. I opened Curlew.png and Sandpiper.png alongside. Godwit, Curlew and Sandpiper are literally the same drawing with the hue changed: identical squat oval body, identical concentric dark wing-arc scrolls, identical straight yellow cone bill at the identical angle, identical yellow legs and feet, identical flat dark tail wedge, identical head circle and eye placement. The Curlew -- whose reference row says a straight bill 'destroys the identification' -- carries the exact same straight cone. So the judge's instinct that the bill is a batch part rather than a Godwit bill is correct and is provable, not impressionistic.

CORRECTION 1 -- THE BREAST IS NOT FLAT. The claim 'a flat uniform mid-brown' is wrong as stated. At 8x the breast and flanks carry a dense scalloped feather texture: rows of small lens/scale-shaped LIGHT marks over the ground colour. A fix brief that says 'add texture, there is none' will be re-adding what is already there. What is actually wrong is: (i) the texture is a generic all-over body scallop -- the identical texture appears on Curlew and Sandpiper -- not a breast-specific marking; (ii) it is LIGHTER than the ground, i.e. highlights, where godwit chevrons are DARK bars; (iii) the marks are lens/scale shaped, not V-shaped chevrons; (iv) there is no breast/back tonal separation at all -- sampled breast front at y200 reads #9b6a3e to #ca8b51 and the mantle reads the same family (#a97444, #cf8e53), a sandy tan-brown, not cinnamon/rufous. So the VERDICT 'no cinnamon tone, no dark chevron barring' is right; the reason 'flat uniform, no texture' is not.

CORRECTION 2 -- THE LEGS ARE NOT STUBS. The claim 'short yellow stubs' is half wrong. At 5x the legs are properly built: ~40 px of exposed leg from the belly line to the toes against a ~100 px body depth, each leg with a correctly backward-bending intertarsal joint and a foot with forward toes plus a visible hind toe. They are articulated wader legs, not stubs. What IS wrong is the colour and the stance: sampled tarsus #c9a24f, a yellow-ochre, where the must-read demands LONG DARK legs; and the tibia is buried in the belly so the bird stands low and squat rather than tall, which is why they read short. The same yellow leg part is reused verbatim on Curlew and Sandpiper.

OTHER OBSERVATIONS. Eye is present and correct for 'normal': a dark round eye at (~178,143) with a white catchlight, not oversized. Tail is a single flat dark blade projecting right to x345 with no rump/tail-band articulation. There is a heavy dark crescent arc across the shoulder (sampled #442f1b at 300,230) that reads as a scroll ornament rather than a wing edge.

BAND. All three defining must-reads fail: the bill is a stock thick straight untilted cone with a uniform saturated yellow and no pale base; the legs are yellow, not dark; the breast has neither cinnamon ground nor dark chevrons. The organism reads as a generic squat brown wader -- closest to a kiwi or rail in posture -- and is indistinguishable in form from two of its own batch-mates. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a black chick or a sooty ball-shaped fledgling crow
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail simultaneously. The bill is the shared short yellow cone, not a long straight orange-red chisel. The plumage is uniformly near-black over the whole body with no white at all, so the bold black-and-white blocking that makes the bird identifiable at a glance is entirely missing. The legs are the same thin yellow stubs used across the batch, not stout pink legs, and there is no red eye ring - just the same small black bead eye.
rows.fix: Draw a long, thick, blunt-tipped orange-red chisel bill about 1.5 head-lengths, split the body into a hard black hood and back over a clean white belly and wing bar, and put thick pink legs and a red eye ring on it.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but one of the three stated causes is factually wrong and the fix list must be corrected. WHAT I SAW (440x440, pixel-sampled as well as looked at): a fat charcoal oval body in left-facing biped stance, small round head at upper-left, a wing plate laid over the flank, a low-contrast pointed tail wedge trailing back-right with 6-7 fanned primary lines, two short gold legs, and a cast shadow ellipse.

MUST-READ 1 -- 'long straight orange-red chisel bill': HALF PRESENT, and the judge's description of the defect is WRONG. The bill is NOT short and it is NOT a shared stubby cone. Measured bounding box x110-166, y155-165: 56 px long by 11 px at the base, on a head that is only ~50 px in diameter -- so the bill is LONGER than the head is wide and is roughly a quarter of the ~220 px total profile, which is the correct oystercatcher proportion. It is also dead straight and horizontal. The two real defects are (a) COLOR: sampled #c59d37 (197,157,55), a mustard/amber gold at hue ~40deg, where the species needs orange-red at hue ~10-15deg (something near #E8471F / #F0532A); (b) TIP SHAPE: it tapers continuously to a needle point, i.e. a dagger, where an oystercatcher bill is near parallel-sided along its length and ends in a blunt vertical chisel. Do not lengthen this bill -- recolor it and square off the last ~15% of its length.

MUST-READ 2 -- 'bold black-and-white blocked plumage': GENUINELY ABSENT. The judge is exactly right here and I confirmed it numerically. Body samples across head, breast, wing and flank return #2c3035, #30343a, #22252a, #191c20, #0f1012 -- luminance 15 to 50 across the whole animal. A histogram of every non-background pixel in the body bbox found only 3 pixels above luminance 192, and those 3 are the white catchlight in the eye. The only other pale marks are ~130 pixels of cool grey rim-light (~#6b737c) tracing the top-left contour of the head and the wing edge -- that is edge lighting, not plumage. There is no white breast, no white belly, no white wing bar, no white rump. The internal value range is charcoal-on-charcoal, roughly a 2:1 luminance ratio where the species needs a hard ~10:1 split with a clean terminator at the waterline: solid black hood/back/wing, solid white breast and belly, plus a white wing stripe.

MUST-READ 3 -- 'stout pink legs and a red eye ring': ABSENT, but again partly mis-described. The legs are the same amber gold as the bill and carry zero pink -- that part stands. 'Thin stubs' is not accurate though: leg bbox is x200-245, y255-288, so 33 px tall with a ~6-7 px stroke, and they are articulated -- visible tarsus, a hock kink, and three splayed forward toes. The defects are colour (gold, needs a fleshy pink ~#E39AA6) and LENGTH: at 33 px the belly nearly rests on the ground, so the bird has no stilt. The red eye ring is flatly missing: the eye is a plain ~10 px black bead with a white catchlight and no orbital ring of any colour. Worse, being black-on-near-black it barely separates from the head at all, so the packet's 'eyes: prominent' is also unmet -- the scarlet iris plus red orbital is the single highest-contrast feature on a real oystercatcher's head and here that whole area is a void.

WHAT IT READS AS: the judge's 'sooty ball-shaped crow fledgling' is close but not right. A crow read is blocked by the bill, which is far too long, thin and straight for any corvid. With a long pale dagger, a near-black body, a mostly hidden tail and stumpy legs it reads as a generic dark rail or a kiwi-ish ground bird -- an unidentifiable dark shorebird chassis. Nothing in it says Oystercatcher.

BAND: FAIL stands. Two of three must-reads are wholly absent (pied blocking; pink legs plus red eye ring) and the third is present only in its geometry, not its colour or tip. This is not a polish-level gap -- the entire diagnostic colour story of the species (orange-red bill, pink legs, red eye, black-and-white body) is missing, and only the bill length is salvageable as-is.

rows.readsAs: a small round grey chick - plausibly a plover, but only because the generic chassis happens to be plover-shaped
rows.defect: The stubby bill and dark bead eye are present and the body is compact, so this is the one asset the shared chassis nearly serves. But the head is not large relative to the body - it is the same small ball head used on every other bird, so the big-headed look is missing; the eye is small rather than the demanded big dark eye; and the body is the batch's horizontal egg rather than a compact upright carriage. It is indistinguishable from the Sandpiper in this batch apart from hue.
rows.fix: Enlarge the skull to roughly 0.3 of the body and the eye to about twice its current diameter, and tilt the body from horizontal to a more upright, chest-forward stance so the big-headed silhouette reads.

rows.readsAs: a pale buff chick that could pass as a small sandpiper
rows.defect: The straightish bill of roughly head length is present and the mottled buff tone is right, so the identification is not actively wrong - but this is simply the family's base chassis with nothing added. The body is a fat neckless egg rather than a horizontal crouched wader with a visible neck and slimmer chest, and the legs are short thick stubs rather than long thin wading legs. It is identical to Curlew and Plover in this batch except for hue.
rows.fix: Slim the body, raise it on legs at least twice as long and half as thick, and add a short visible neck so the crouched horizontal wader posture reads instead of a chick's ball.

rows.readsAs: a dark brown downy chick or a young grouse
rows.defect: The extremely long straight dagger bill - the single feature that makes a snipe a snipe - is absent; the bill is the batch's short yellow cone. The eye is set dead-centre on the cheek, not high and far back on the skull, so the snipe's distinctive head geometry is gone. The back carries only generic random speckling with no bold cream longitudinal stripes; nothing on this bird distinguishes it from the Godwit except being slightly darker.
rows.fix: Draw a straight dark dagger bill about three head-lengths long, shift the eye up and back toward the rear crown, and lay four crisp cream stripes running front-to-back along the mantle.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL stands, but the headline cause is WRONG and would send a fixer to add a bill that is already there. CORRECTION 1 - THE BILL IS PRESENT AND IT IS LONG. I zoomed the head 5x and pixel-measured it. A straight, unbroken, saturated-yellow dagger runs from tip x=79 to the skull front at x=139 (bill/skin colour boundary x=148): 60-69px of exposed bill against a 49px skull diameter, i.e. ~1.3-1.4x head length, tapering from ~12px at the base to a 1px point, dead straight with zero curvature. It is the joint-longest bill in the whole batch - Plover 12px, Sandpiper 50px, Oystercatcher 52px, Curlew 56px, Avocet 67px. It is emphatically NOT 'the batch's short cone'. THE REAL BILL DEFECT is different and worse: it is the GODWIT'S bill, to the pixel. Godwit tip x=88, skull front x=148, boundary x=157 - 60px exposed, 69px to boundary. Identical. Because the Snipe skull is slightly larger (49px vs Godwit 44px), the Snipe's bill/head RATIO is actually LOWER than the Godwit's. So 'extremely long' is unmet not by absence but by non-differentiation: it needs to grow to roughly 2-2.5x skull length (~100-120px) to out-read the Godwit, and to thin down - a snipe bill is a needle-thin probe, not a 12px-base wedge. CORRECTION 2 - THE EYE, direction of error restated. Not 'dead-centre on the cheek'. Skull disc centre is (163.5, 145.5) with r=24.5. The eye disc (dark pupil x152-162, y137-146, white catchlight at its ANTERIOR edge x155-156) centres on (157, 141.5). That is 6.5px FORWARD of skull centre (-0.27r, i.e. toward the bill) and 4px ABOVE it (-0.16r). So it is already marginally high but placed ANTERIORLY - the exact opposite of 'far back'. The fix must push it POSTERIOR toward the nape by ~0.5r and UP toward the crown by a further ~0.3r; a fixer told 'it's centred' might only raise it and leave it forward, which would still fail. Damningly, the Godwit's eye sits at the identical normalised offset (skull centre 170,146 r=22; eye centre 164,142.5 => -0.27r, -0.16r). Eye placement here is a chassis constant, not a species read - which is why 'eyes: prominent' in the row buys nothing. CORRECTION 3 - THE BACK, confirmed absent, and I checked hard for faint stripes rather than taking the claim on trust. I re-rendered the back region (150,155,200x110) as a contrast-stretched greyscale for both birds. The Snipe carries the same procedural scalloped feather-fleck texture as the Godwit - short elongated pale dashes tiled along the body flow - plus two dark structural arcs (an upper scapular crescent and a lower wing-oval outline) and a hatched tail-primary fan. There is no continuous cream line anywhere, not even faint: nothing runs nape-to-tail, and the classic 4-stripe braces are entirely missing. Godwit's flecks are marginally more elongated, Snipe's marginally rounder; that is the whole difference. FAMILY FINDING, which is the real charge: Snipe and Godwit are one chassis in two hues. Same skull disc, same normalised eye offset, same bill length to 0px, same body oval, same dark wing-arc crescent, same tail wedge with the same hatched fan, same short kinked yellow legs with the same splayed toes. Body boxes 278x186 vs 259x180 (aspect 1.49 vs 1.44, both undershooting their specced 1.8/1.9). The Snipe is drab olive-tan, the Godwit is cinnamon. Two of three must-reads (eye placement, back stripes) are flatly absent and the third is present but non-distinguishing, so the asset reads as 'generic brown wader', specifically as the Godwit in a duller colourway. FAIL. Minor credit not in the original claim: the legs ARE correctly short and thick for a snipe, and the head IS slightly larger than the Godwit's (49 vs 44px) which nods at the specced headFrac 0.36 vs 0.30 - the dumpy short-legged big-headed carriage is half-there and should be preserved, not reset, when the bill/eye/stripes are fixed.

rows.readsAs: a spotted appaloosa pony or a Jacob-type sheep
rows.defect: The body is the shared ungulate barrel — flat topline, upswept belly tuck, four column legs with fetlock bands ending in blocky hoof-like feet at the corners of the body — with a long wedge muzzle set on no neck. It is not a cat body of any kind, so the 'stocky heavy-boned cat body' must-read is absent. The dark markings are scattered irregular blotches over the back and flank rather than the required rows of solid spots, and there are no neck stripes at all. Worst of all the rear of the animal simply terminates in a bare curved rump: there is NO tail drawn anywhere, so the 'short thick tail' must-read is entirely missing.
rows.fix: Rebuild on a feline chassis — shorten the muzzle to a rounded broad skull, add a visible neck, arch the lumbar spine, bring the legs in under the body on digitigrade paws with toes — then add the short thick tapered tail off the croup and align the spots into longitudinal rows with two dark stripes down the neck.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with three corrections to the stated causes. I decoded the PNG and re-rendered it at 5x-14x plus contrast-stretched crops of the rump, head, neck and feet, and I measured the ink bounding box.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Ink bbox is x114-325, y146-276 (W212 x H131, aspect 1.62 against a spec aspect of 2 -- the body is shorter and chunkier than spec). A pale bone/cream quadruped in left-facing profile, barrel torso with a shallow belly tuck, a high rounded croup, a pale shoulder plate, four straight column limbs and a head carried straight off the shoulder mass with zero neck.

1. SHARED CHASSIS -- CONFIRMED, and quantitatively. Sand Cat's ink bbox is x115-324, y146-276: identical to this asset within one pixel. Topline, belly tuck, shoulder plate, limb columns and feet are the same forms in all three assets of this batch; only colour, markings, ear shape and tail differ. So 'one chassis' is right. But the chassis does NOT read as an appaloosa foal. The long tapering down-tilted snout with a bead nose at the tip, the domed rump and the flat splayed foot discs read closer to a tapir/peccary or a juvenile bear. Nothing about the head is equine. Fix the noun in the defect report or the art fix will chase the wrong target.

2. FEET -- the judge's 'hoof-like feet' is WRONG as description though right as a complaint. At 8x each foot is a flattened dark-olive OVAL PAD lying flat on the ground with three shallow toe grooves scored across it. It is not a hoof, cloven or solid. It is also not a cat paw: no toe bulbs, no digit separation, no claw, no wrist/pastern. It reads as a blunt lozenge stamped under the leg column. The fix is 'build a real digitigrade paw', not 'unhoof it'.

3. HEAD -- 'wedge muzzle on no neck' CONFIRMED. The muzzle is long and tapering with the eye set very far back; nose-to-eye is roughly half total skull length, where a Fishing Cat's muzzle is short and blunt with a broad whisker pad. There is a horizontal mouth line, no cheek ruff, no whisker pad, no jowl. Head is oversized: skull length ~75px against a 212px body, headFrac ~0.35 against a spec 0.23. The judge did not mention ears; there ARE two -- a larger crescent-shaped dark-olive blob on the top-rear of the skull and a smaller rounded one behind it. Low and rounded is not wrong for this species, but they are colour blobs on the skull dome, not modelled ears. The ONE unambiguously feline cue in the entire asset is the eye: a large amber iris with a genuine vertical slit pupil and a white catchlight.

4. TAIL -- 'NO tail drawn at all, the rump simply terminates' is CORRECT, verified two ways. (a) A contrast-stretched 8x-12x crop of the rear shows the rump as a bare rounded dome running uninterrupted into the hind-leg column; there is no stub, no hanging tail, no tail tucked against the far flank. (b) The per-column ink profile from the left edge of the bbox rises monotonically -- x114:7, 115:26, 116:38, 117:42, 118:45, 119:48, 120:51 ... -- which is a smooth dome. A tail of any kind would appear as a narrow isolated spur of 3-8px columns; there is none anywhere. DECISIVE: this is a defect in this asset, not an engine limitation. Both siblings in this same batch on this same chassis have tails drawn -- Sand Cat carries a clearly banded tail with a dark tip swept back and down, Wildcat carries a ringed tail with a dark blunt tip. The tail machinery exists and is used one file over. The 'short thick tail' must-read is therefore missing outright, and it is the single highest-value fix.

5. MARKINGS -- 'scattered irregular blotches rather than rows' is CORRECT. The dark chocolate marks vary from ~2px flecks to ~14px blobs, several merging into compound masses over the shoulder and mid-flank, with no longitudinal row structure whatsoever; the real animal wears small, evenly sized, solid spots in tidy fore-aft rows. Also note the base coat is pale bone/cream, not the olive-grey the row calls for, so 'olive coat' is only marginally met.

6. NECK STRIPES -- the judge's 'there are no neck stripes' is PARTLY WRONG. At 12x there ARE roughly six to eight thin dark dashes over the neck and upper shoulder, running fore-aft. They are genuinely drawn, but they are faint, sparse, irregularly spaced and read as random dark hairs rather than stripes; from the sheet at 1x they vanish. The must-read still fails, but the correct fix is to strengthen, lengthen and regularise the streaks that already exist into parallel neck bands -- not to add stripes from scratch.

BAND. FAIL stands. Of the three must-reads: 'stocky heavy-boned cat body' fails because the body is stocky but is not a cat -- wrong skull, no neck, pad-lozenge feet, wrong head fraction; 'olive coat with rows of solid dark spots and neck stripes' fails on all three sub-clauses (base too pale, blotches not rows, stripes vestigial); 'short thick tail' is absent entirely. Nothing readable identifies this as a Fishing Cat except the slit pupil.

rows.readsAs: a cream pony or donkey foal with a lemur's ringed tail stuck on
rows.defect: Identical chassis to the other two: straight flat topline, deep slab barrel with the belly swept up into a flank tuck, four straight column limbs leaving the silhouette at the body's corners with pastern bands and blunt hoof-shaped feet. The head is a long narrow forward-tapering wedge carried level on no neck with a single high-set amber eye — the exact opposite of the required 'broad flattened head with low wide-set ears'; the ears here are two small dark triangles pinned high on the crown, not low and wide. The 'short stocky legs with furred feet' must-read fails twice — the legs are long slender columns, and the feet are hard-edged hooves with no fur ruff. Only the banded black-tipped tail is present, and it hangs limply against the hind leg where it reads as an attached foreign part rather than growing from the croup.

rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, but three of the four descriptive details in the original claim are wrong and would send the fix in the wrong direction. What I actually saw at 4x-12x crops of the 440x440 PNG:

CHASSIS (claim correct). This is the pony/ungulate chassis in cream. Deep barrel chest, straight topline with high withers, a croup that slopes down to the tail root. Forelegs are long tapering columns with a knee break; hind legs have a pronounced hock angle and a straight cannon below it. Standing height under the belly is roughly equal to body depth. There are visible plate/seam boundaries at the shoulder and haunch where a tan wedge overlaps the flank -- the shared-chassis joint. mustRead 'short stocky legs' is absent: these are the longest, thinnest legs a cat could be given.

HEAD (claim correct in substance). A long forward-tapering wedge. The muzzle projects well past the eye and ends in a small dark round nose; the jaw line is a thin horizontal sliver. Head length is only about 0.21 of nose-to-rump against a required headFrac 0.27, and the shape is the exact inverse of 'broad flattened head'. The sand cat's defining wide, low-slung, flat-topped skull is nowhere present.

EARS (claim WRONG in description, right in conclusion). They are NOT 'small dark ears'. They are two mid-sized warm taupe/brown triangles -- a taller sharp spike overlapping a broader lower triangle behind it -- together about one third of head height and clearly readable at full size. So ear mass already exists. The defect is placement and axis: both sit high and central on the crown, pointing up and angled back, giving a shepherd-dog/fox read. The fix is to widen, lower and splay them onto the sides of the skull (and widen the skull to receive them), not to enlarge or darken them.

FEET (claim WRONG in description, right in conclusion). They are NOT 'hard-edged hooves'. Each foot is a soft, slightly blurred flat olive-brown ellipse, wider than the leg it sits under, carrying 2-3 faint vertical toe-split lines -- a pad/hoof-disc hybrid. Toe articulation is therefore already present. What fails 'furred feet' is that there is zero fur volume anywhere on the lower leg: the cannon is a bare, smooth, hairless taper right down to the disc, so the foot reads as a hoof cap rather than a broad fur-brushed paw.

TAIL (claim WRONG). The tail does NOT 'hang flat against the hind leg'. It arcs clearly out into open background, well separated from the hind leg by empty dark pixels, curving down and forward, and reads as a distinct appendage. It is the one must-read that lands: alternating cream and dark-brown bands with a solid dark rounded tip. Its real weaknesses are milder -- it is a uniform-diameter tube (striped-sock silhouette, no taper and no fur fringe) with hard-edged high-contrast rings, and it plugs into the rump beneath a visible tan wedge seam.

UNMENTIONED CREDIT: the eye is a genuinely feline prominent amber iris with a vertical slit pupil, correctly matching 'eyes: prominent', and the coat is a well-judged pale sand cream with painterly directional fur strokes across the flank. Coat color and eye are keepers.

NET: 1 of 3 must-reads readable (banded black-tipped tail). Head/ear must-read absent and inverted; leg/foot must-read absent. The organism reads as a pale hound or a small ungulate, not a sand cat. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a zebra foal, and a broken render at that
rows.defect: The render is broken: a solid dark horizontal bar of uniform thickness runs straight across the image from the mid-flank forward through the shoulder, through the entire skull, and out past the tip of the muzzle, cutting the head in half. It is a stray straight stroke unrelated to any coat marking and it dominates the silhouette. Underneath it is the same shared pony chassis as the other two — flat topline, deep barrel with an upswept belly tuck, four straight column legs at the corners with pastern bands and blocky hooves, wedge muzzle on no neck — so 'sturdy build heavier than a house cat' fails because it is not a cat build at all. The vertical black stripes are hard-edged and evenly spaced right down the barrel and across the face, which reads as zebra rather than a mackerel tabby. The ringed black-tipped tail is the only must-read that lands.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but the primary stated cause is WRONG and must not be fixed against. I cropped and 8-14x nearest-neighbour zoomed the head, topline, tail and feet of the 440x440 render.

CORRECTION 1 - there is NO broken render and NO horizontal bar. Nothing runs from the mid-flank through the shoulder into the skull. The topline crop (x150-330, y140-210) shows a clean unbroken back-to-neck-to-crown contour with no crossing geometry whatsoever. What the judge saw is a thin (2-3px at native res) mid-tone MOUTH/JAW line that lives entirely inside the head: it starts at the cheek just below and behind the eye and ends well short of the muzzle tip (it stops around 60% of the way along the snout, it does not exit past the nose). It is a legitimate, if too-straight and too-dark, mouth line, not a bar, not uniform thickness, and it does not slice the head in half. Do not 'fix a broken render' - there is nothing broken to fix.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS:

(a) mustRead 'broad head' is ABSENT. The skull is a long, low, narrow tapering snout - equine/tapir/lemur in profile - with the muzzle occupying roughly half the head length and ending in a rounded tip carrying a big dark oval nose patch. There is no cat cranium, no short face, no width. Worse, THERE ARE NO EARS: what sits on the crown are two flat dark-brown rounded ovals painted onto the skull surface with no pinna outline, no triangular point, no ear opening, no silhouette break at all - the head's outline is completely smooth over the top. They read as head spots. This is provable from the family sheet: the sibling Sand Cat in the same batch DOES carry two real triangular ears that break its silhouette, so the missing ear here is an asset-level omission, not an engine limitation.

(b) mustRead 'sturdy build heavier than a house cat' fails for the reason the judge gave, and the judge is right that it is one shared chassis. Rendered side-by-side, Fishing Cat / Sand Cat / Wildcat are the SAME body with only colour, markings and head length swapped: identical deep flat-topped barrel, identical level topline with a small withers bump, identical thick short forward-carried neck, identical straight columnar forelegs set as vertical posts, identical hind limb with a fat thigh and a straight unflexed cannon (no cat hock angle), and identical wide flat splayed plantigrade feet with 3-4 shallow toe grooves planted flat on the shadow ellipse. Nothing here is felid: no high-riding shoulder blade, no low-slung sinuous crouch, no compact round digitigrade paw, no deep chest-to-tucked-waist taper. It reads as a small pony / okapi / bovid calf, and Wildcat is the member of the trio where that is most damaging because the striping pushes it all the way to 'zebra'.

(c) The markings claim is fair. The stripes are hard-edged, high-contrast near-black bars of fairly even width and even spacing, dropping from the dorsal midline down the flank and continuing over the shoulder and across the top of the muzzle as 4 discrete vertical face bands. Mackerel tabby is thinner, softer-edged, lower contrast, and the face carries an M-brow plus fine cheek lines, never full vertical bars across the nose bridge. Combined with (a) and (b) this is a striped ungulate.

WHAT IS GENUINELY RIGHT (the judge did not credit it): mustRead 1, 'thick blunt-ended tail with dark rings and a black tip', is fully PRESENT and the best-drawn feature on the asset - a thick tapering tail with about seven clean dark rings and a solid dark blunt club tip. It is only mis-posed (it hangs down and curls forward toward the hind legs rather than trailing). The amber slit-pupil eye is also correct and is the only unambiguous cat cue in the whole render.

FIX ORDER: give it a real felid skull (short broad cranium, muzzle shortened to about a third of head length) with two ears that BREAK the silhouette; rebuild the limb model off the established cat chassis (angled hock, high shoulder, compact round paw) instead of the shared pony chassis; then soften and thin the stripes and replace the muzzle bars with an M-brow and cheek lines. Keep the tail and the eye as-is.

rows.readsAs: a pale grey coiled snake, or a length of grey ribbed hose coiled on the floor
rows.defect: Pale washed-out colouring and the limbless coil are present, but the third must-read is absent: the head is a small narrow rounded lozenge no wider than the neck, not a BLUNT WEDGE, and there are no heat-sensing pits anywhere on the snout — nothing on the loreal area at all. The head is also far too small for the body mass and is the identical head used on the other two assets. The dorsal ribbing wrapping right over the top of the tube reads as segment rings, not scales, pushing the whole thing toward earthworm. rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but two of the judge's three stated causes need correcting and one must-read they implied missing is actually present.

WHAT I SAW. A coiled olive-grey torus, ~2 turns, head emerging at right with a red forked tongue. I decoded the PNG and measured the silhouette rather than eyeballing it, and cross-measured Snake.png and Cave_Snake.png as controls.

MUST-READ 1 - 'broad triangular head much wider than the neck': ABSENT, and the defect is WORSE than the judge described. At 14x the head is a smooth symmetric almond/leaf, widest at the eye (mid-head), tapering to a point at the snout and tapering just as smoothly backward until it dissolves into the ringed neck tube. There is no rear jaw flare, no venom-gland cheek bulge, no constriction. Measured maximum head cross-section is 37px (columns x=294..312 span 34-37px). The body tube measures 47-60px (x=180/200/220 give 50/47/40 top arc and 60/59/58 bottom arc). So the head is roughly 0.65x the width of the body, i.e. NARROWER than the body, not 'exactly as wide as the neck'. Min-chord thickness probes give head-mid 32.0 vs neck stub 39.0 at (278,232) and 57 further back - the neck TAPERS DOWN into the head, the exact inverse of viper anatomy. The judge's 'identical head used on the other two assets' is confirmed within a few percent: max head cross-section Viper 37 / Snake 35 / Cave Snake 31, head length Viper x288-330 (~42px) vs Snake x288-332 (~44px). The packet gives the viper headFrac 0.09 against Cave Snake's 0.05, and that near-doubling produced a head 6% wider than the plain colubrid's - visually nothing.

MUST-READ 2 - 'thick stocky body with a zigzag dorsal band': the ZIGZAG IS ABSENT, confirmed numerically. Over 23,221 subject pixels the viper's saturation mean is 5.9% with sd 1.8 and a single hue cluster (80/8 = 43%, 136/8 = 31%, both effectively neutral at 6% sat). Control: Snake.png measures sat mean 30.8, sd 5.8, with hue spread across 16-40 - that is its brown dorsal blotching. So the engine CAN paint dorsal markings; the viper simply got none. This is an omission, not an engine limit - important for the fix. I brightness-boosted the body 3.2x and re-read it: still zero blotch, saddle, chevron or band. The only surface detail anywhere is transverse scute ribbing, and that ribbing is drawn along the OUTER (dorsal) face of the coil for the entire length - belly scales rendered where the back should be. The judge did not mention this; it is an additional defect.

CORRECTION on the 'stocky' half: the judge says it is 'the same slender 8:1 rope torus as the two colubrids'. Directionally right but imprecise. Aspect 1.3 did move the dial slightly - the viper's tube is 47-60px against the plain Snake's 42-50px (~10-15% thicker) - and it is essentially identical to Cave_Snake's 49-58px, which is spec'd aspect 8. Coil radius, turn count and total body path are identical across all three. So girth is not literally unchanged, it is changed by an amount far too small to read as an ambush-bodied viper, and the tell is that the aspect-8 cave snake is just as thick.

CORRECTION in the asset's favour: MUST-READ 3, 'vertical slit pupil', IS PRESENT and is the one thing drawn well. At 14x there is a crisp pale-cream eye disc with a clean black vertical slit through its centre. The judge's framing ('zero viper identity') sweeps this away; it should be preserved by any fix, not redrawn.

BAND. 1 of 3 must-reads readable. The two that carry the identity - the triangular gland-flared head and the zigzag dorsal - are both absent, and side-by-side with Snake.png and Cave_Snake.png this is visibly the same chassis, same head, same tongue at the same angle, differing only in hue. It reads as a generic grass snake. FAIL stands.

FIX TARGETS, in order: (1) give the head a rear-wide wedge - flare the posterior third to ~1.6-1.8x the neck tube (target ~60-70px against the current 37) and cut a real constriction behind the jaw so the neck steps DOWN from the head instead of tapering into it; (2) add a dark zigzag/chevron dorsal band running the coil - reuse whatever path paints Snake.png's blotches, which already works; (3) rotate the scute ribbing to the ventral face; (4) push girth well past Cave_Snake's so aspect 1.3 actually separates from aspect 8; (5) keep the slit pupil exactly as is.

rows.readsAs: a coiled tan-brown snake — the most convincing of the three, thanks to the blotches

rows.readsAs: a California quail

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at Lark.png at 1x, then cropped and nearest-neighbour upscaled the head (10x), feet (12x), tail (10x) and full body (4x), and measured the ink bounding box against Sparrow.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a sandy/khaki egg-shaped body standing near-vertical, head-ball set high and forward, a shoulder-arc wing with a scapular sweep, a single dark-brown triangular tail wedge tapering to a knife point projecting horizontally back, a long thin sharply pointed saturated-yellow bill, one round black eye with a white catchlight, two yellow legs, and a tall multi-filament plume on the crown.

THE ONE-CHASSIS CLAIM IS CORRECT AND I CONFIRMED IT DIRECTLY. Side by side with Sparrow.png the two are the same drawing: identical egg body, identical shoulder-arc/scapular wing overlay, identical dark wedge tail with the same little fanned hatch marks under it, identical head ball, identical eye, identical yellow leg form, identical fine speckle/streak texture. Measured ink bbox: Lark 166x132 px (aspect 1.26), Sparrow 159x133 px (aspect 1.20) — a 4% difference in footprint. The reference asks for aspect 1.6 and the note explicitly forbids the upright perching finch; what is drawn is the upright perching finch, 0.34 short of the demanded aspect. Lark's only real departures from Sparrow are a longer/sharper bill, a slightly larger head ball, a marginally paler tint, and the crest.

MUST-READ 1 — streaky brown ground-bird plumage: PARTIALLY PRESENT. There is genuine fine streak/fleck texture on the mantle and flank and the tint is a plausible sandy-brown. But it is pixel-for-pixel the same texture Sparrow carries, so it identifies nothing.

MUST-READ 2 — slight peaked crest at the BACK of the crown: FAILS, but the other judge described its position wrong. The crest is NOT rooted at the front of the crown. A single stalk rises from the CENTRE-TOP of the skull, arcs up, and then splits into a fan of four to five thin spikes that splay both forward over the bill and backward. The mass leans forward, which is presumably what read as 'front'. The defect is magnitude and shape as much as placement: it stands roughly 40% of head height above the crown as a discrete separate plume with visible gaps between filaments — a hoopoe/titmouse/quail topknot. The reference wants a SLIGHT peak, i.e. the rear of the crown feathering up into a low continuous point that is part of the head outline, not a stalked ornament sitting on top of it.

MUST-READ 3 — long straight hind claw: FAILS, but the other judge's stated cause is factually wrong and would send the fix in the wrong direction. The foot is NOT 'the same three-forward-toe stick'. At 12x each foot is a two-element fork: one long toe running forward and down-left, and one SHORT stub running backward and down-right at roughly a third the front toe's length. A rear-facing digit IS present on both feet. What is missing is its length and its geometry — the lark's diagnostic hallux is a long, nearly straight spur running back along the ground, comparable in length to the middle toe. The fix is to extend and flatten the rear stub that already exists, not to add a toe that isn't there.

OTHER CORRECTION: 'reads as a California quail' overstates the bill. The bill here is a long thin pointed yellow dagger, noticeably longer and sharper than Sparrow's short cone and more lark-appropriate than quail-appropriate. The quail read comes entirely from the rotund upright body plus the stalked topknot, not from the head furniture generally.

VERDICT: FAIL upheld. Two of three must-reads are absent or wrong (crest placement/magnitude, hind claw), the explicit anti-note (horizontal long-bodied ground bird, not an upright perching finch) is violated by the silhouette and confirmed by measurement, and the asset is the Sparrow chassis recoloured with an ornament bolted on. The single readable feature is a plumage texture shared with its neighbour.

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL stands, but their headline reason is FACTUALLY WRONG and must not be actioned. THE FORKED TAIL IS PRESENT AND IT IS THE BEST THING IN THE ASSET. Zoomed 7x with gamma boost, and confirmed by a per-column luminance scan of the 440x440 source: the tail leaves the body as a solid wedge at x~250, a dark notch opens at x=274, and from there two separate, tapering streamers run out to x~326 — at x=280 the scan returns TWO bright runs, y217-224 and y229-235, with a dark gap at y225-228; by x=324 they have diverged to y214-215 and y240-241 and thinned to 1-2px points. Notch-to-tip is ~52px of a ~76px tail, i.e. the fork is ~68% deep, and the tail is ~55% of body length. That is a genuinely deep fork with long outer streamers, correctly proportioned for a barn swallow. It is also NOT generic family furniture: Starling in the same batch has a single short undivided wedge. Whoever fixes this asset must LEAVE THE TAIL ALONE. Its only real defect is contrast — the streamers are painted only ~4-10 luminance units above the dark backdrop, so at 1x they are a faint whisper and are easy to miss (which is almost certainly how the first judge read them as one spike); lifting them 15-20% in value would make the signature feature actually legible.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ABSENT (2 of 3 must-reads):
1. WINGS — must-read is 'long narrow pointed swept-back wings'. What is drawn is a single broad scalloped leaf/teardrop lying FLAT along the back, running shoulder to tail base with a blunt rounded tip and a pale rim highlight. It is somewhat longer and more raked than Starling's rounded oval, so 'the family's folded comma stroke' understates it slightly — call it an elongated folded leaf — but it is broad, blunt-tipped and closed, never a narrow pointed scimitar, and it is a PERCHED wing, not an extended flight wing. Absent.
2. BILL — must-read is 'tiny flat bill with a wide gape'. What is drawn is a long bright-yellow triangular dagger, roughly 0.55x the head diameter, straight and sharply pointed, with no gape line at all. The judge is right; I add that it is pixel-for-pixel the same yellow dagger part used on Starling and Swift. Absent, and wrong in colour too (a swallow's bill is dark).
3. POSTURE — packet says posture: flying. Body is a long horizontal squashed ellipse; at its underside sit two pale-yellow perching feet with splayed forward toes and a hind toe, resting directly on a hard-edged dark elliptical GROUND SHADOW. One correction to their wording: there are no 'planted legs' — there is no visible tarsus at all, the feet are tucked flush under the belly. The failure is planted feet + splayed toes + a ground-contact shadow ellipse, which kills any read of flight. It reads as a bird crouched on the ground, exactly as claimed.

THE DEFECT THE FIRST JUDGE MISSED, and it is the biggest one: Swallow and Swift are THE SAME DRAWING. Rendering both side by side, they share the identical head sphere, identical yellow dagger bill, identical eye, identical folded leaf wing with rim light, identical twin-streamer forked tail, identical yellow splay-toed feet and identical ground-shadow ellipse — only hue (slate blue + orange belly lozenge vs. warm grey) and body squash differ. The packet's own Swift note demands the opposite ('the swift has stiffer sickle wings, a much shorter notched tail, and no long streamers') and the asset gives the swift the swallow's streamers. Two species in one family sharing one chassis is disqualifying on its own.

SUPPORTING CUES THAT DO LAND (not must-reads, worth preserving): glossy slate-blue back and a large warm-orange underside lozenge give a credible barn-swallow colourway; the head is small and rounded at roughly the specified headFrac. Net read: a generic passerine chassis crouched on the ground with a correct swallow tail bolted on. Fixes, in priority order — (a) open the wing into a long narrow pointed swept-back scimitar and lift the body off the shadow into true flight, (b) replace the yellow dagger with a tiny dark flat wide-gape bill, (c) differentiate from Swift, (d) raise the tail streamers' contrast. Do not touch the fork itself.

rows.readsAs: a drab brown bird lying on its belly
rows.defect: This is the Swallow render recoloured grey-brown, and it misses every must-read. There are no scythe-shaped crescent wings swept far back — just the folded comma stroke on the flank. The bill is a pointed yellow wedge, not a tiny bill with an enormous gape. The must-read explicitly demands a cigar body with almost no visible legs, and the render puts two bright yellow legs with splayed toes prominently under the body, planted on a ground shadow. It also has the long undivided pointed tail the packet's note warns against, so it fails as a swift AND as the swallow it was mistaken for.
rows.fix: Draw two stiff backswept sickle wings spanning wider than the body length, shorten the tail to a small notched fan, and delete the legs, feet and shadow entirely.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, and the shared-chassis diagnosis is confirmed by direct comparison: I opened Swallow.png alongside Swift.png and they are the SAME drawing. Identical pose (horizontal, head left), identical round ball head, identical yellow dagger bill, identical two-leaf wing pair, identical yellow feet, identical ground-shadow ellipse, identical twin tail streamers. Swift is the Swallow chassis with the palette swapped (slate-blue + rufous belly -> warm grey-brown + pale cream speckling). At 5x and 12x magnification, and again with a 3.2x brightness lift to read the silhouette against the near-black field, all three must-reads fail.

(1) 'scythe-shaped crescent wings swept far back' - ABSENT, judge correct in substance, slightly over-stated in wording. It is not merely a 'folded comma stroke': there are TWO distinct wing plates. The upper/far wing is a long tapering speckled blade that does sweep backward and point down toward the tail base, so there is a hint of sweep. But the lower/near wing is a broad rounded paddle covering the entire flank, and neither plate has the concave trailing edge that makes a sickle. Both lie flat ALONG the body rather than projecting free of it, so the silhouette is a fat spotted oval, not a crescent-winged dart. Nothing here reads scythe.

(2) 'tiny bill with an enormous gape' - ABSENT, judge correct. The bill is a saturated yellow straight-sided triangular dagger roughly 0.45x the head diameter, base as tall as the eye, tapering to a sharp point well clear of the head. There is no gape line, no mouth corner carried back under the eye, no wide flat mouth. It is the loudest chroma on the head and reads tern/pipit.

(3) 'cigar body with almost no visible legs' - CONTRADICTED, judge correct with two corrections. What is visible is the FEET, two of them, bright saturated yellow, toes splayed fore-and-aft with a rear spur; the tarsi are barely drawn. They hang below the belly line and OVERLAP the dark elliptical ground shadow rather than being firmly planted on it, but they are unmissable and are the second-loudest element in the piece. Additionally the body is not a cigar: it is a bulky ovoid with a deep sagging belly, about 2:1, the 3.0 aspect coming entirely from the tail. Also note the ground-contact shadow conflicts with the packet posture 'flying' - the piece is composed as a perched/standing bird.

CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM: 'the long undivided pointed tail' is WRONG in detail, and the truth is worse for the asset. The tail is NOT undivided. There are TWO separate long thin dark streamers, one upper and one lower, diverging into a deep fork, projecting roughly the body's own length past the rump, plus a fan of thin raked barb/speed hatch lines below them. That is precisely the Swallow's 'deeply forked tail with long outer streamers' (Swallow mustRead, row 7) and precisely what the Swift note forbids: 'a much shorter notched tail, and no long streamers.'

One further defect neither pass named: the plumage is heavily flecked with pale cream spots over grey-brown with a pale rim light, which reads starling/thrush. A swift is uniform sooty blackish-brown with at most a small pale throat patch. Colour is not in the mustRead list, but the spotting actively pushes the read toward the wrong family.

FIX DIRECTION: this needs a new silhouette, not a repaint. Narrow the body to a true cigar, delete the feet and the ground shadow entirely, replace the twin streamers with a short shallow-notched tail no longer than about a third of the body, replace both leaf plates with two narrow sickle wings that project clear of the body with concave trailing edges and tips swept back past the tail, shrink the bill to a near-invisible dark stub with a gape slit running back under the eye, and flatten the plumage to uniform sooty brown.

rows.readsAs: a red chicken chick — the Cardinal image with the crest deleted
rows.defect: The saturated block-red plumage reads, but the squared tail must-read is contradicted by the family's long pointed dagger tail, and the short conical bill is the same small thin wedge used on all nine. The larger problem is that it is pixel-for-pixel the Cardinal body in the same red, separated only by the absence of a crown tuft, so the two are not distinguishable as different species.
rows.fix: Square off the tail, deepen the bill into a short heavy cone, and differentiate from Cardinal by giving it black wings and tail against the scarlet body plus a slimmer, longer-bodied silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a generic spotted newt or smooth-skinned lizard
rows.defect: The armoured must-read is entirely absent: the skin is a smooth airbrushed gradient with soft random blobs, no squared scale rows, no keeled rows and no lateral skin fold along the flank. The trunk is a fat rounded oval rather than an elongate 6:1 body, and the tail — while long — reads about the same length as the trunk, not far exceeding it. Legs are bare dark sticks with no feet or toes.
rows.fix: Rebuild the trunk as an elongate cylinder with visible rows of squared scales and cut a dark horizontal granular fold line the full length of the flank, then extend the tail to roughly twice the trunk length.

rows.readsAs: a chameleon
rows.defect: The eye is a flat concentric target disc set flush into the cheek rather than a cone turret protruding from the skull, and the casque is only a low bump behind the crest; the legs are also over-long featureless stilts.
rows.fix: Push the eye out of the head as a protruding cone with a small pinhole pupil at its tip, and raise the casque into a distinct helmet ridge above the skull.

rows.readsAs: a small tan rodent wearing a ruffled collar
rows.defect: The frill and pink gape do land, but everything behind the head is wrong: the body is a featureless tan egg, the hind limbs are missing entirely (only two tiny nubs poke out under the middle), and the tail is a 1-2px hairline wire with no mass at its base, so it reads as a mouse tail rather than a whip tail. The whole animal is also drawn small and pushed into the right-of-centre band with a large dead zone top-left.
rows.fix: Give the tail real thickness at the base tapering over its length, and add a full sprawling hind limb with a splayed clawed foot so the body reads as a lizard under the frill.

rows.readsAs: a chubby orange shell-less tortoise or fat newt
rows.defect: The beaded bumpy skin — the single strongest identity cue — is absent: the surface is a smooth airbrushed orange gradient with soft blurred dark smudges, no bead granulation and no crisp black-and-orange banding. The trunk is a near-circular balloon instead of a heavy elongate body, and the fat tail arcs up and forward over the back like a carrying handle rather than lying low and straight behind as a sausage.
rows.fix: Replace the smudge blotches with a dense field of discrete raised beads in hard black-and-orange bands, and drop the tail to a low straight fat sausage trailing behind the hips.

rows.readsAs: a spiky tan tortoise or hedgehog-ish blob
rows.defect: The horn crown and the flank fringe are visible and correct, but the body shape must-read is inverted: it is a TALL vertical egg standing on end, not a flat wide pancake disc, so the profile is domed instead of low and plate-like. It also carries a large pale fat curled tail sweeping off the rear, directly contradicting the very short tail the form requires — the same curled tail as the Gila Monster.
rows.fix: Flatten the body into a low wide disc no taller than the leg length and cut the tail back to a short blunt stub.

rows.readsAs: a wingless mosquito or a damselfly abdomen with pins stuck in it
rows.defect: The identity must-read — a twig-thin CYLINDRICAL elongated body of roughly constant diameter — is absent. What is drawn is a bulbous sphere head plus a second sphere thorax followed by a segmented cone that is fat at the base and tapers to a needle tip, so the topline is beaded and the silhouette is a carrot, not a stick. The second must-read fails too: the legs are five short unjointed straight pins hanging almost vertically from one ventral midline row, all raked back at the same angle, with no knee, no elongation and no left/right pairs — the opposite of spindly legs stretched out in line with the body, and several of them terminate in mid-air above the shadow. The head sphere also grossly overshoots the 0.08 headFrac spec. Only the two long straight antennae are correct.
rows.fix: Rebuild the body as a single near-constant-diameter cylinder (head barely wider than the thorax, abdomen tapering only in the last 15%) and replace the pins with three PAIRS of long two-segment legs — the front pair stretched forward past the antennae and the rear pair stretched back along the abdomen, each with a visible femur/tibia bend and a tarsal contact on the shadow line.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG, then re-read it at 5x, 8x, 10x and 20x crops of the head, the leg row, the abdomen and the antennal node, and measured the silhouette column-by-column from the decoded pixels. The FAIL stands: the identity must-read, a twig-thin near-constant-diameter elongated body, is genuinely absent. But three parts of the stated cause are wrong and would send a fix to the wrong place.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (measured, opaque-body threshold, original 440px coords): the body occupies x141-333, y199-222 -- length 192px. Its vertical diameter along that run goes 20px (head sphere, x148-165) -> 26px (thorax sphere, peak at x172, the single widest object in the image) -> a pinched 9px waist at x189 immediately behind the thorax -> swelling BACK OUT to a 17px maximum around x243, i.e. at the abdomen's own mid-length -> tapering to a 5-6px point at x331. So the judge's "fat-based carrot abdomen" is not correct: the abdomen is a wasp-waisted SPINDLE/LENS, thinnest where it meets the thorax and fattest in its middle. That makes the beading worse, not better -- the profile has three separate bulges (head ball, bigger thorax ball, mid-abdomen swell) separated by two constrictions. Nothing in the silhouette is a cylinder of constant diameter. Confirmed sphere head and second, larger sphere thorax as claimed.

The abdomen is additionally ruled with ~8 flat vertical ring lines drawn straight across the taper, with a hard specular rim along its top edge; together with the point at the tip it reads as a dragonfly/wasp gaster or a mosquito rear, not as a twig. Overall the organism reads as a generic winged-insect/ant chassis, not a phasmid.

LEGS -- the judge's count and their grounding claim are both wrong. There are FOUR leg lines, not five. Three of them are straight, unjointed, near-vertical tapering pins hanging from the anterior quarter of the abdomen at x=189, 208 and 227; the entire rear two-thirds of the abdomen (x240-333) is legless, and the thorax sphere itself carries NO legs at all. The fourth limb is at the front, and it is NOT a pin from the midline row: at 20x it originates from the antennal junction at approximately (124,200) -- i.e. in front of and below the head, at the base of the antennae -- and runs down-right to a foot at (142,237), and it DOES carry a visible bend/knee about a third of the way down (it reads as a narrow V, possibly two near-parallel front limbs converging at one foot). So "no knees" is true of the three abdominal pins but false of the front limb, and "a single midline row" is false for that limb. What is true and is the real defect: only 4 limbs are drawn where 6 are needed, they are all in one plane at one tone with no darker far-side pair, they are ~15px long against a 192px body (real phasmid legs equal or exceed body length), and they hang near-vertically instead of being held stretched fore-and-aft in line with the body, which is the second explicit must-read and is missing.

GROUNDING -- "several ending in mid-air above the shadow" is not what I see. All four feet land at y=233-237, a reasonably consistent ground line, and every tip falls INSIDE the cast shadow ellipse, which spans about x106-240, y228-252. The genuine ground defect is different: the shadow only sits under the front half of the animal, so the rear two-thirds of the abdomen (x240-333) overhangs bare background with nothing beneath it.

WHAT READS: the antennae are correct and are the only must-read satisfied -- two long, thin, straight antennae sweeping up-left from a node ahead of the head, about a quarter of body length, well separated. Also noted against the reference row: eyes are specified "small" but the drawn eye is a single glossy black bead with a blue-white specular highlight occupying roughly a third of the head sphere's diameter; headFrac is specified 0.08 but the head sphere measures ~20/192 = 0.10-0.12 of body length, and the thorax sphere behind it is larger still. Full bbox including antennae and legs is 225 x 52 = aspect 4.3 against a specified 5, so aspect is the one numeric that is close.

FIX DIRECTION: rebuild the trunk as one uniform-diameter tube roughly 6-8px thick over its whole 190px length with no head ball, no thorax ball and no mid-abdomen swell (segment it with faint ring lines only, never with diameter change); give it six long limbs, three per side with visible femur/tibia knees, the front pair reaching forward alongside the antennae and the rear pair trailing back alongside the abdomen; move the front limb's origin off the antennal node onto the thorax; and extend the cast shadow to sit under the full body length.

rows.readsAs: a fat brown piranha swimming next to an unrelated floating light bulb
rows.defect: The lure is a free-floating glowing orb sitting in open water above and to the RIGHT of the head, completely detached — there is no illicium stalk, no arch, nothing connecting it to the fish, so it reads as a stray particle rather than the organ that names the animal. The jaw is not upturned or enormous: the mouth is a single straight hairline slit across the middle of the face with a row of small even triangles stamped under it, no gape, no long needle fangs. The body is the family oval covered in the shared crosshatch mesh.
rows.fix: Draw the illicium as a physically attached tapering stalk rising from the top of the snout and arching FORWARD over an opened, upturned gape, with the glow bulb at its tip — and open the mouth into a real hinged jaw carrying long unequal fangs instead of a decal tooth row on a closed slit.
rows.verifyWhy: FAIL stands, but the stated cause for the lure is WRONG and must not be fixed as described. THE ILLICIUM STALK EXISTS. Under a gamma-0.30 stretch of the region x220-350 / y110-230 a 3px-wide line is clearly drawn from the dorsal-front of the skull at approx (283,184) — on the silhouette edge, above and forward of the eye, correct origin — running up-and-forward to the esca bulb whose core sits at approx (305,146). Length ~28px on a 440px canvas (body is 149px long). It IS attached at both ends: at y=184 the body outline is at x=281 and the stalk base is at x=282-284, they touch. The judge did not see it, and neither did I on the first 1x read, for a measurable reason: the stalk pixels are rgb(13,12,12) against a background of rgb(9,14,20). Luminance 11.4 vs 12.2 — a contrast ratio of about 1.03:1, i.e. hue-only, no luminance step at all. It is drawn and it is invisible. So the FIX IS A VALUE FIX, NOT A MISSING-ORGAN FIX: do not author a new illicium, raise the existing one's value (pale bone/greenish, or emissive gradient warming toward the esca) so it separates from the water, and add the forward ARCH the reference asks for — today it is a straight ~70deg spike that plants the bulb up-and-behind the snout tip rather than dangling it in front of the mouth. THE JAW CLAIM IS RIGHT, AND WORSE THAN STATED. There is no mouth on this fish at all. The pale hairline the judge called a 'closed slit' sits at y=209-211 and runs from x=155 to x=280 — that is 84% of the body length, starting 12px in from the TAIL-end edge (body spans x143-292) and terminating at/just past the eye at x=270, stopping 12px short of the snout. A line that starts near the tail and ends at the eye is a LATERAL LINE, not a jaw; nothing in this asset opens. No gape, no upper/lower jaw division, no jaw outline, no upturned corner, no maxilla. Second correction: the teeth are not 'small even triangles'. They are 7 pale, thin, tapered NEEDLE slivers at x230/240/250/259/268/278/287, y222-234, evenly pitched ~9.4px, slanted forward-down at ~65deg — needle-shaped but tiny (~12px = 9% of body height, where the reference wants 'long'). The damning detail the judge missed is that they are DETACHED: a clear ~12px band of blank flank separates the tooth tips from the hairline above, so they read as tally marks stamped on the cheek rather than dentition set in a jaw. WHAT DOES READ: the body is a clean globular egg, x143-292 by y148-277 (aspect ~1.15 vs the spec's 1.4 — rounder than asked, which suits 'round globular' fine), and it is the one must-read fully satisfied. The eye is a small pale ring with a dark pupil, correctly placed high and forward. FINS ARE ALSO SHORT: only ONE fin exists, a dark radiating caudal fan behind the body's left edge, and it is nearly as low-contrast as the stalk; there is no dorsal, no pectoral, no anal, so 'tiny fins' (plural) is not met. The body is also covered in dense concentric arc hatching that reads as ribbed scales, where an anglerfish should be naked and warty. NET: of three must-reads, only the globular body reads at native size; the lure is drawn but rendered at 1:1 contrast so it reads as a stray glowing particle beside the fish; and the enormous upturned fanged gape — the feature that carries the identity alongside the lure — is genuinely absent, not small or hidden. Priority order for the fix: (1) cut a real gape — a big upturned maw opening from the snout to below the eye with interlocking long fangs crossing the opening; (2) raise the illicium's luminance and arch it forward over that new mouth; (3) add pectoral/dorsal stubs and lift the caudal's value; (4) drop the ribbed hatching for soft flesh.

rows.readsAs: a green fish wearing a bubble helmet with a green box inside it
rows.defect: The transparent dome does read (a clean circle over the front of the head), but what is inside it is a single flat mint-green RECTANGLE — one solid slab, not two upward-pointing tubular eyes; there is no barrel form, no pair, no upward gaze. Worse, the two dark spots that should be the nostrils on the FRONT of the face are sitting on top of that green slab inside the dome, so they read as a pair of pupils on a face — the render produces exactly the misreading the packet's note warns against. The rest is the family lens body with the shared scale mesh, cyan belly-dot chain and triangular tail wedge.
rows.fix: Replace the slab with two distinct vertical green cylinders side by side inside the dome, each capped with a bright lens facing straight UP, and move the two dark nostril pits down onto the snout at the front of the head, outside the dome and clearly below the barrels.

rows.readsAs: a pink puffer-ish fish with a big nose — close to blobfish but not obviously gelatinous
rows.defect: The pink colour, the slumped oval mass and the bulbous drooping snout lobe all read, and this is the closest the chassis gets to its target. But the whole body is covered in the family crosshatch SCALE mesh, which directly contradicts the must-read 'no scales' and makes it look armoured rather than gelatinous; the mouth is a faint straight hairline under the nose with no downturn at all, so the defining frown is absent; and the tail is the same stiff triangular wedge every other asset in the batch wears rather than a flimsy translucent fin.
rows.fix: Strip the scale hatch entirely and render the surface as smooth, slightly translucent jelly with soft sag folds, then cut a clearly downturned frowning mouth line under the drooping nose.

rows.readsAs: a bright red needlefish or a chilli-pepper-coloured cutlassfish
