rows.defect: The long glowing chin barbel — the single feature that names this animal — is entirely absent; nothing hangs from the jaw, the underside of the head is a clean empty curve. The body is also saturated CRIMSON RED rather than the specified eel-like black, so it reads as a tropical surface fish, not an abyssal one. The fangs are four tiny white spikes at the very tip of the lower jaw, far too short and not transparent. Only the cyan photophore row along the belly is doing its job, and it is the same dot chain reused on Barreleye, Lanternfish and Viperfish.
rows.fix: Add a long barbel hanging from the chin — a slender filament at least a third of the body length with a glowing bulb at its end — and repaint the body near-black with only a dull red sheen.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified by decoding the PNG and re-rendering four nearest-neighbour zooms (head 6x, snout tip 16x, mid-body 9x, and a 2.6x-brightness-boosted crop of the whole region UNDER the jaw) so nothing dark could hide against the near-black backdrop.

BARBEL — CLAIM CONFIRMED, and confirmed under brightening, which is the only way this call is safe. The subject occupies bbox x104-352, y175-210 (248x35 px, aspect 7.09 — the packet asks for 7, so proportion is dead on). Head is at the RIGHT. In the boosted crop (x250-440, y190-280, gain 2.6) the entire area beneath the chin is bare background: the only non-background pixels below the ventral silhouette are (a) the six fang spikes and (b) the elliptical soft drop-shadow that every asset in this set carries, which sits ~40 px below the fish and is clearly the ground shadow, not an organ. There is no stalk, no filament, no glowing tip, no stub, not even a 1-px seed of one — forward of the snout, below the chin, or anywhere along the ventral line. The first-named must-read is 100% absent.

BODY COLOUR — CLAIM CORRECT IN DIRECTION, WRONG IN DEGREE. Do not fix against 'saturated crimson'. Sampled pixels: core flank rgb(124,32,46) = #7C202E, ventral/snout highlight rgb(152,64,79) = #98404F, tail stalk rgb(54,15,24) = #360F18, dorsal ridge rgb(81,70,82). That is a DARK muted wine/brick red at roughly 30-40% lightness with a grey-violet dorsal trim band — not a bright tropical crimson and not a needlefish palette (a needlefish would read silver/green). It is nonetheless plainly RED, and the must-read demands an eel-like BLACK body, so this must-read still fails: the hue must go to near-black (charcoal/blue-black) with at most a faint warm sheen. The fix is a value+desaturation move, not merely 'less saturated crimson'.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY PRESENT (the judge did not credit these, and they should not be repainted away): (1) NEEDLE FANGS ARE PRESENT — at 16x I count six pale white-grey needles, ~4-6 px long, hanging below the ventral edge across the front ~15% of the head, downward-pointing. They are opaque white rather than the specified TRANSPARENT, they are small, and there is no drawn gape at all — no mouth line, no jaw articulation, no dark oral cavity; the teeth are simply planted along an unbroken silhouette edge, so the head reads as a sealed tube with spikes glued on rather than as a jaw. Call this must-read partially met / needs a real gape. (2) PHOTOPHORE ROW IS PRESENT AND GOOD — approximately 14 pale-blue (light cyan) oval lights in a single continuous row along the lower flank from tail stalk to cheek; this is the strongest element in the asset. (3) A rayed, swept-back PECTORAL FIN and a gill-cover arc at mid-body (x~250-300), and a small dark caudal fan plus a red spike at the tail. (4) Eye is a white ring with a dark comma pupil high on the head, correct scale for 'normal'.

BAND: FAIL upheld. Two of three must-reads fail outright (barbel absent, body red not black) and the third is only half-met (fangs present but opaque and mouthless). Critically, with the barbel gone the only remaining identity cues are 'elongate + ventral photophore row', which is verbatim the must-read of its own family sibling Lanternfish in this same batch — so the asset does not merely lack a feature, it collides with another member of the family it is being judged against.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM: 'entirely absent' barbel = correct. 'The underside of the head is a clean empty curve' = mostly correct but imprecise — the ventral edge carries a dark purple-grey trim band and six fangs, and the pectoral fin overhangs the belly line at mid-body; it is the CHIN specifically that is bare. 'Saturated crimson red' = overstated; measured #7C202E dark wine. 'Reads as a bright tropical needlefish' = wrong read; it reads as a dark-red elongate deep-sea fish, essentially an unlabelled lanternfish/viperfish, not a tropical species.

rows.readsAs: a brown piranha with white spikes stuck on its face
rows.defect: The stocky dark-brown mass and the alternating up/down white fangs do roughly carry the idea, but the head has no mouth: the fangs float on bare cheek with no jaw line, no lip and no gape behind them, and one spike overlaps the eye. The 'huge blunt head' does not exist as a form — it is simply the front half of the same oval used for Blobfish, undifferentiated from the trunk. The deep pitted grooves and ridges on the skull, a stated must-read, are nowhere on the render; the only texture is the shared crosshatch mesh, and it is applied to the REAR half of the body while the head is left flat.
rows.fix: Build an actual blunt boxy head with a hinged gaping jaw so the fangs sit in a mouth, and carve the characteristic pits and bony ridges into the skull as visible sculpted grooves rather than leaving it a smooth oval.

rows.readsAs: a small silvery fish with glowing dots on its belly
rows.defect: The cyan photophore chain along the lower flank reads well and the silver-blue body is right in tone, but the eye — specified prominent and the animal's signature along with the lights — is rendered as the same tiny white ring used on the 'small eyes' assets in this batch, so the oversized-eye must-read is invisible. There is no adipose fin before the tail, and the tail is the shared flat triangular wedge with no fork cut into it. Body is also shorter and deeper than the 3.5 aspect asks for.
rows.fix: Enlarge the eye to occupy most of the short blunt snout, then cut a real V-fork into the caudal fin and add the small adipose nub ahead of it.

rows.readsAs: a piece of nigiri sushi, or a silver loaf wearing a red dome
rows.defect: Nothing about this is a ribbon. The body is a short fat silver sausage of roughly 4:1, not the 'many times longer than it is deep' ribbon the reference and the aspect 18 both demand. The crimson crest is rendered as one enormous SOLID pink dome slab that caps the entire length of the back and is taller than the fish is deep — it is a filled shape, not a crest of individual elongated dorsal rays, and it is not concentrated over the head where the oarfish crest actually rises. The long trailing oar-like pelvic streamers are missing entirely; there is one small grey fin mid-flank and a couple of stray wisps at the tail end. The overall silhouette reads as food, not an animal.
rows.fix: Redraw the body as a genuinely ribbon-thin silver band many times longer than deep, run the red dorsal fin as a fringe of separate fine rays the whole length, elongate only the first few rays into a crest plume over the head, and hang two long paddle-tipped pelvic streamers below.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of the stated causes are measurably wrong and the fix must be made against the corrected numbers.

MEASURED (pixel bbox scan of the 440x440 PNG, then a per-column depth profile every 6px):
- Silver body: x 124..349, y 190..222. Length 226px. Trunk depth is a near-constant 25-28px along the whole body (max 33px only at the pectoral fin, which is a fin overhang, not trunk). True aspect = 226/27 = 8.4:1. The judge's '4:1 short fat silver sausage' is WRONG by a factor of two — this is not a sausage, it is a long low bar with a proper dotted-scale silver texture, blunt-squared at both ends. Against the asked-for 18:1 it is still less than half as long as it needs to be, so the must-read 'ribbon-flat, many times longer than deep' is only half met: the fix is roughly a 2.1x horizontal stretch (or a 2.1x depth reduction), NOT the 4.5x the judge's number implies.
- Crimson crest: x 138..337, y 167..192. Spans 200px = 88% of the 226px body length. Max height 23px, at x 214-260 — MID-BODY. Body depth there is 27-28px, so the crest is ~85% of the body depth, not 'taller than the fish is deep' as claimed; that overstatement is minor and does not change the verdict.
- Crest structure at 12x zoom: one perfectly solid, flat, uniform crimson slab. Zero internal ray separation, zero ray tips, no scalloped or combed upper edge, no gaps to background. Judge is exactly right here.
- Crest at the HEAD end (14x crop of x290-350): the crest tapers monotonically to ZERO right at the head. The head is the one place on the animal with no crest at all. So it is not merely 'not concentrated over the head' — it is inverted: the plume is shortest where it should be tallest. This is the single most damaging defect and the primary fix.

CORRECTION TO 'the oar-like pelvic streamers are missing entirely':
- At 3x brightness boost over x80-150 there ARE trailing filaments — about 5-6 hair-thin dark streamers fanning backward off the TAIL TIP (x~108-118), plus a small pale pointed caudal lobe. They are drawn, just at luminance barely above the background so they vanish at 1x. So 'missing entirely' is inaccurate; they are (a) in the wrong place — a caudal fan, not two pelvic streamers hanging from the belly, (b) the wrong form — a radiating spray of equal hairlines with no oar-blade tips, and (c) effectively invisible at render contrast.
- The belly (2.6x boost over x150-290) carries exactly ONE shallow rounded ventral lobe and nothing else. No pelvic streamers hang from it. Confirmed absent where the spec wants them.
- ADDITIONAL spec violation the judge missed: the must-read says 'no tail fin', but there IS a small pale pointed tail-tip lobe at the posterior, so a tail fin is present and should be removed.

SILHOUETTE: the judge's 'piece of nigiri sushi' is apt and I saw it too — a solid pink slab sitting on a pale rice-textured bar. Present and correct: silver colour, dotted scale texture, prominent ringed eye at the right (correct headFrac, small head), a triangular pectoral fin, a gill arc, a mouth line.

VERDICT: identity carriers 2 and 3 are absent as specified (the crest reads as a solid mid-body dorsal slab rather than a plume of elongated rays over the head; the pelvic oar-streamers do not exist and a forbidden tail fin does). Carrier 1 is half met at 8.4:1 against 18:1. It reads as a generic silver fish wearing a red saddle, not an oarfish. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a tripod fish — a fish standing on three long stilts on the seabed
rows.defect: The three stiff stilt rays are long, clearly weight-bearing and splay into small contact feet on the floor, and the two pectoral feelers sweep forward past the snout like antennae — the identity lands immediately and the silhouette is the only one in the batch that escapes the family oval. Minor: the eye is drawn as the same bright white ring-and-pupil used everywhere else rather than the tiny vestigial eye the reference calls for, and the three stilts are spaced evenly like insect legs instead of reading as a pelvic pair plus the lower caudal lobe.
rows.fix: Shrink the eye to a barely-there dark speck and re-space the stilts as two pelvic stilts under the chest plus one trailing from the lower tail lobe.

rows.readsAs: a grey blimp with teeth — indistinguishable from the Fangtooth in this same batch apart from colour
rows.defect: The first dorsal ray drawn out into a long lure whip over the head — a stated must-read and half of this animal's identity — is completely absent; there is no filament of any kind above the body. The body is a fat head-heavy teardrop of about 2.5:1 where the reference asks for a slim 6:1, so 'slim dark body' fails too. The fangs are the same floating white spike decal used on Fangtooth, stamped on a face that has no mouth line or jaw at all, so they do not read as fangs that close OUTSIDE the mouth past the eyes — they read as spikes glued to a cheek. The photophore row is four dots confined to the rear third of the belly instead of running the body.
rows.fix: Add the long dorsal lure whip arcing forward over the head with a light at its tip, and re-proportion the body to a slim elongated 6:1 with a hinged gaping jaw so the oversized fangs visibly close outside it past the eye.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but two of the three stated causes need correcting before anyone fixes against them.

WHAT I MEASURED (440x440 canvas, silhouette threshold vs the #04050b background). Live silhouette spans x=102..339 (238px) and peaks at 58px deep at x=289. The caudal fin occupies x=102..~140, so the body proper is ~198 x 58. That is 3.4:1 body-only, 4.1:1 including the tail fin -- NOT 'about 2.5:1' as claimed. The judge understated it; the shape is meaningfully longer than a Fangtooth oval. The verdict still stands because the packet asks for aspect 6 and this is 3.4-4.1, and because the taper is wrong in the way described: max depth sits at x=289, only 50px behind the nose tip at x=339, i.e. the widest point is 25% back from the front, and depth falls monotonically from there to the peduncle. It is a head-heavy teardrop. headFrac is asked at 0.2; the fat anterior bulb runs roughly x=250..339, ~45% of body length, and there is no gill line or jaw line anywhere to demarcate a head at all, so headFrac is unreadable rather than merely wrong.

LURE WHIP -- CLAIM CONFIRMED, ABSENT. I cropped the entire region above and forward of the head (x150-350, y80-190) at 5x. It is empty water. The only dorsal structures on the whole animal are (a) a low soft translucent hump over the MID-back and (b) about five short vertical ray ticks roughly 10px tall rising from that hump, all of them well BEHIND the head, none of them elongated, none over or forward of the skull. There is no filament, no whip, no tip light. The single most identity-bearing must-read is genuinely missing, not small and not hiding.

FANGS -- CLAIM CONFIRMED AS COPY, ONE DETAIL WRONG. I rendered Fangtooth.png at the same crop and boost for direct comparison. Viperfish and Fangtooth carry the identical kit: the same ~7 white bidirectional spikes (each spike points BOTH up and down from a common horizontal axis, which is why it reads as a jagged decal stripe rather than as teeth rooted in two jaws), the same white-ring/dark-pupil eye at the same relative position, the same short dorsal ray ticks, the same hatch-texture patch on the flank, the same lateral stripe. The only differences are hue (ice-blue vs copper), a slightly longer tail stalk, and the photophores. They are the same chassis. CORRECTION to the claim: it is not quite true that there is 'no mouth or jaw line'. There IS a faint dark slate line drawn behind/under the fang row -- but it is only about a third the length of the fang row, is far lower contrast than Fangtooth's own mouth arc, stops short of any jaw hinge, and the snout terminates in a smooth unbroken rounded curve with no gape. So the fangs do not and cannot 'close outside the mouth' as the packet requires: there is no mouth for them to close outside of. Nor do they pass the eyes -- the tallest spike merely reaches eye height.

THIRD MUST-READ, WHICH THE JUDGE DID NOT MENTION AND WHICH IS PARTLY PRESENT: photophores. There IS a real photophore row -- five bright ventral half-domes plus a horizontal lateral stripe -- but it is confined to the narrow caudal peduncle around x=155..205 only. It does not run the length of the body, and it is one row, not 'rows'. Compounding it, the packet says 'slim dark body' and this body is a pale ice-blue/near-white gradient, i.e. light, not dark.

NET: one must-read absent outright (lure whip), one present only as a reused decal that contradicts its own wording (fangs, no mouth), one half-present on the wrong 25% of the body and in the wrong value key (photophores on a light, fat body). The asset reads as recoloured Fangtooth. FAIL is correct. Fix priority: (1) add the first dorsal ray as a long forward-arcing whip over the head with a lit tip, (2) cut a real gaping jaw with an upper and lower jaw line and re-root the fangs to those jaws pointing in ONE direction each so they interlock outside the closed mouth, (3) stretch to 6:1 and move max depth back off the nose, (4) darken the body and extend the photophore row forward along the whole ventral line.

rows.readsAs: A green leaf, or at best a generic needle-snouted minnow / young garfish — nobody names a killifish
rows.defect: Two of the three must-reads are simply absent and one of them IS the identity. (1) There is no flattened-topped head with an upturned mouth: the front of the fish is a bare symmetric spearpoint with zero head structure — no flat dorsal profile over the skull, no gill cover, no jaw line, no mouth aperture at all, and the topline over the 'head' slopes DOWN to the point instead of running flat. The small white eye ring is stuck onto the dorsal contour with roughly its upper half hanging over black background outside the silhouette. (2) The dorsal fin is not set far back near the tail: the faint dark hump above the topline spans about 38-70 percent of body length measured from the tail, centred near mid-body and biased toward the head — the exact opposite of the posteriorly-placed killifish dorsal — and it is rendered as an out-of-focus dark smudge painted behind the crisp body outline, with no rays, no defined edge and no visible attachment. (3) The caudal is the only must-read partly delivered: it is roughly rounded, but it is a dull dark near-rectangular slab, blurrier and much darker than the body, joined to the rear point by a single hairline pixel with no caudal peduncle, so it reads as a detached paddle rather than a tail fin.
rows.fix: Rebuild the front third: flatten the dorsal profile from the eye forward into a straight table-top, cut the snout short and blunt, and terminate it in a small upturned superior mouth whose lower jaw juts past the upper — then slide the dorsal fin back so its origin sits behind the anal-fin origin at roughly 70-80 percent of body length, give it a hard rayed edge in front of the body silhouette, and blend the caudal onto a short peduncle instead of a hairline join.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified by decoding the PNG and re-rendering the fish at 5x-14x with contrast boost, plus per-column silhouette measurement. Fish occupies x130-307, y174-225 in a 440x440 frame; caudal fin x130-159, body proper x160-307 (147 px long, max depth 48 px at x~230) -> aspect ~3.7 against the packet's 3.6, which is fine. Packet mustRead: 'flattened topped head with an upturned mouth . dorsal fin set far back near the tail . rounded paddle tail fin'.

MUST-READ 1 (flat-topped head + upturned mouth) - GENUINELY ABSENT, and the judge described it correctly. The front third is a smooth symmetric needle taper to a single point at x=307. The dorsal contour falls continuously from y=174 at x~232 to y=202 at the tip; there is no flat plateau anywhere over the head. There is no mouth aperture, no jaw line, no lip, no chin, and no operculum/gill-cover line at all - the pixel map from x=270 to the tip shows only body-green with the species' faint vertical barring; nothing that could be read as a mouth exists anywhere on the head, upturned or otherwise. This is the feature that IS the killifish, and it is not drawn.

EYE - the judge UNDERSTATED this. The white ring (outer bbox x292-299, y192-200, dark pupil at x294-297/y196-198) does not straddle the contour half-and-half: the body silhouette at those columns does not begin until y=200-201, so about eight of the ring's nine pixel rows sit on pure background (luminance 13-14) and only its bottom row touches green. It reads as a detached floating ring perched above and forward of the topline, not as an eye set into a head.

MUST-READ 2 (dorsal set far back near the tail) - ABSENT as specified; the judge's numbers need correcting. There IS a dorsal: a low dark-green dome painted behind the body outline, rising above the pale topline from about x=205 to x=272 - i.e. roughly 31% to 76% of body length measured from the tail, peaking at ~50-55%. So it is centred essentially at MID-BODY, not 'biased toward the head' as claimed. Its maximum projection above the topline is only ~9-10 px. The stretch of topline from the peduncle (x160) to x~205 - exactly where a killifish's dorsal belongs - is bare body outline with no fin. Also partly wrong: the judge said 'no rays'. Under contrast boost there ARE about five thin dark vertical ray strokes inside the fin, some poking slightly above its margin. What is true is that the fin has no crisp outer rim - the top edge is a soft blur with no defined edge, so it reads as a shadow ridge rather than a fin.

MUST-READ 3 (rounded paddle tail) - partly delivered, and here the judge was too harsh on one point. The caudal is a distinctly darker slab at x130-159 with a clear fan of rays radiating from a base point on its right side, so it is not featureless. The real defects: its outer margin is a flat, truncate, rounded-corner RECTANGLE rather than a convex rounded paddle; its value is much darker than the body so at 1x it reads as a detached block; and there is effectively no caudal peduncle - the body narrows from 19 px at x=159 to 4-7 px at x=160-165 and the fin abuts the body's needle point on a hairline.

NOT MENTIONED BY THE JUDGE (in the asset's favour, but not enough to save it): a pectoral fin IS present as a dark wedge below the midline at x~255-272 behind the head, and a shallow anal-fin ridge runs under the belly at roughly x=200-255. So fin coverage is not the issue; placement and the missing head anatomy are.

Net: the silhouette is a symmetric lens/leaf with a point at each end, a mid-body shadow-dorsal, a rectangular tail block and a floating eye. It reads as a generic pointy aquarium fish, not a killifish - two of three must-reads, including the identity one, are missing. FAIL upheld. Fixes needed: build a flat-topped head profile with a defined operculum line and a visible superior/upturned mouth at the snout tip; move the eye down so it is fully inside the head silhouette; move the dorsal fin back to roughly the last third of the body (about 10-35% of body length ahead of the caudal peduncle) and give it a defined rayed edge; give the caudal a convex rounded margin, lift its value toward the body, and add a real peduncle between body and fin.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon lollipop tree with brown berries — nobody says oak
rows.defect: Every one of the four must-reads is missing. The crown is a narrow ball perched on a bare pole, taller than wide, instead of a broad spreading crown as wide as it is tall — and there is not one visible branch, so no spreading limb frame exists. The leaves are small spiky sawtooth fronds with pointed serrations, the opposite of the deeply lobed rounded oak outline. The acorns are four featureless brown spheres floating on the crown face with no nut taper and no scaly cup at all — they read as berries or cherries. The trunk is a flat, smooth, evenly-shaded brown stick with no fissures, no plates, no texture whatsoever.
rows.fix: Rebuild the oak on its own chassis: a short thick fissured trunk that forks low into 3-4 heavy sinuous limbs carrying a crown visibly wider than it is tall, with round-lobed leaf blades and acorns drawn as an oval nut sitting in a visibly cross-hatched scaly cup hanging at twig ends.
rows.verifyWhy:
I looked at the 440x440 PNG at full size and then re-cropped it at 3x-10x (crown, canopy interior with a contrast stretch, the four acorns, and the whole trunk) and measured the pixel bboxes. The FAIL stands on all four must-reads, but two of the stated causes are described wrongly and the fix should be made against what is actually there.

1) CROWN / BRANCHES — upheld, and the measurements back it. Foliage bbox is x99-340 by y55-241 = 242 wide x 187 tall; the trunk runs on down to y384, so the whole organism is 242w x 330h (h/w = 1.36 against a target aspect of 1.1). The crown is a single ovoid ball occupying only the top 57% of the height, sitting on 145px of bare pole — it is NOT as wide as it is tall and it does not spread. Branches: genuinely zero. I contrast-stretched the canopy interior (crop 150,90,160x160, min/max stretch) specifically to hunt for dark limb strokes hidden inside the green, and there is nothing structural in there at all — just a soft blurred green wash. The only non-green pixels inside the crown are 1-3px specks at x200-212 / x241-253 / x274-283, which are the antialiased edges of the four acorns, not twigs. The trunk rises as one unforked capsule and simply disappears under the leaf mass; no crotch, no scaffold limbs, no twigs carrying the leaf clusters.

2) LEAF OUTLINE — the verdict is right, the description is wrong. They are NOT 'spiky sawtooth' leaves: at 10x each blade has a completely smooth, unbroken (entire) margin with no serrations at all. What is drawn is a narrow, straight-sided, acute-tipped lance blade with a single faint midrib, and these blades are stacked in radiating palmate fans of roughly 7-9 from a common base point. The fan silhouette is what reads as 'sawtooth' at 1x. So the 'deeply cut' quality is arguably present, but cut the wrong way: palmate rays from one point, reading as a fern frond / hemp-or-palm rosette, instead of the oak's broad, ROUNDED lobes cut pinnately toward a central midrib along an elliptic blade. The correct fix is not 'de-serrate' — it is to replace the radiating spear-fan with a single elliptic blade bearing 5-9 rounded pinnate lobes and rounded sinuses, alternate and clustered at twig ends.

3) ACORNS — fully upheld, description accurate. Four identical circles, ~14px, filled with a radial brown gradient and a bright white specular hotspot at upper-left. Perfectly circular in outline: no ovoid nut body, no pointed apex, no stalk, and no cup whatsoever — not even a suggestion of a cap, let alone the scaly imbricate texture the reference calls for. They read as polished berries/marbles or chocolate beads scattered on the foliage. They are also not attached to anything (no peduncle, no twig), which compounds the missing-branches problem.

4) BARK — fully upheld. The trunk is a uniform-width capsule, 27px wide and dead constant from y249 to y377 (no taper, no flare), filled flat mid-brown with only a soft left-bright/right-dark vertical gradient. Zero fissures, zero bark strokes, zero plates, zero ridges. It ends in a rounded lollipop tip that floats above the ground shadow ellipse instead of flaring into a root buttress.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT the first judge did not name, and which is very visible at 1x: the canopy is HOLLOW. Leaf clusters are drawn only around the rim; the middle of the crown is a large featureless blurred green fill with a lighter blotch in it, so the crown reads as a wreath or a lily-pad silhouette with a bald patch, not as a mass of foliage. Also the green is a bright saturated mid-green, not the 'deep matt green above, paler beneath' the reference asks for, and no pale undersides are shown anywhere.

Net: a green ball of fern-fans on a smooth brown stick with four glossy brown beads. The judge's 'generic cartoon tree with berries' summary is fair; it does not read as Quercus.

rows.readsAs: a palm, yucca or dracaena — a spiky tropical rosette tree, not a willow
rows.defect: The identity must-read is not merely weak, it points the wrong way: every leaf blade radiates UPWARD and OUTWARD from the crown in a stiff starburst, so there is not a single drooping, pendulous or whip-like twig anywhere in the image. The blades are long and lance-shaped, which is right, but they are all one flat mid-green with no silvery pale undersides, so the crown does not flicker two-tone. The trunk is the identical smooth brown pole from the Oak card — not grey, not fissured, not leaning. The catkins are pale beaded vertical strings glued to the crown face rather than soft grey buds on hanging twigs.
rows.fix: Invert the twig direction — hang long weeping strands from an arching high crown down past the trunk toward the ground, and put two-tone green/silver on the blades so the drooping curtain reads at thumbnail size.
rows.verifyWhy: I tried hard to refute this and could not. Verified at 1x, 2x, 4x and 8x magnification plus pixel sampling. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE: a smooth brown vertical pole trunk (x 215-236) rising into a soft circular radial-gradient green blob crown ~230px wide, with ~30 short straight lance blades (each ~35-45px long) stamped around the blob's edge pointing radially outward, five vertical strings of cream beads floating inside the blob, and a flat black ground ellipse. MUST-READ 1 'mass of long slender drooping whip-like twigs' - GENUINELY ABSENT, and inverted, so the FAIL stands. Nothing hangs below the crown outline; nothing curves; there is not a single twig stroke anywhere in the image connecting leaf to branch - each blade floats free on the gradient. CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM: 'every blade radiates stiffly UPWARD' is overstated. It is a full 360-degree starburst, and roughly the lower third of the blades DO point downward-and-outward (down-left at the lower-left rim, several down-right at the lower-right rim, and one steep near-vertical blade at bottom-centre-left that projects below the crown next to the trunk). The defect is therefore NOT leaf direction - it is that every element is a short rigid straight lance attached directly to the crown ball with zero twig armature, so the silhouette is a spike-ball. The fix is not 'rotate the leaves downward'; it is 'grow long pendulous twig strands that fall well below the crown mass and past the upper trunk, and hang the small lance leaves ALONG those strands'. Also correcting 'reads as a palm or yucca': the crown is a complete round ball with a spiky fringe, not an apical fan of fronds, so the nearer read is a dandelion clock / thistle head / spiky pom-pom on a bare stick; the palm impression comes only from the untextured pole plus the near-vertical crest of blades at the crown's top. MUST-READ 2 'narrow lance leaves' - PRESENT and well drawn (this is the one thing the asset gets right; at 8x each blade is a clean elongated lance with a pointed tip). But 'showing pale undersides' is ABSENT, and the judge is correct here: a colour histogram of every green pixel in the crown returns only saturated greens (dominant bins approx RGB 64,96,48 / 80,112,48 / 112,176,80); there is no desaturated pale or silver-green anywhere in the image. Each blade does carry a lighter green midrib highlight, but it is applied identically to EVERY blade, so it reads as uniform gloss rather than a flipped pale underside - the crown does not flicker. MUST-READ 3 'fissured grey trunk often leaning over water' - ABSENT, and the judge's chassis claim is literally verified by pixel sampling: at x=222, y=280/300/320/340 both Oak.png and Willow.png return exactly RGB(107,74,46), and the trunk span at y=310 is 215-236 (Willow) vs 210-236 (Oak). Same flat brown fill, same taper flare into the crown, same rounded popsicle bottom cap, same ground shadow ellipse. Zero bark texture, zero fissure, zero grey, zero lean. HARVEST: the catkin claim is also correct in substance - five columns of 7-9 discrete round cream beads (approx RGB 224,208,160) spaced like a pearl necklace, with no stalk, no attachment point and no twig tip; they sit ON the crown gradient mid-blob. The right-hand pair near x=245-255 overlaps and smears into a doubled blob. They should be soft fuzzy tapering cylinders, silvery-grey turning yellow, not beaded strings. FAMILY VERDICT: Oak and Willow in this batch are ONE CHASSIS - identical trunk (byte-identical colour), identical soft green radial-gradient crown blob, identical ground shadow; only the leaf stamp shape and the harvest sprite differ. Score: 1 of 3 must-reads present, and the single defining one is inverted. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a duckling or coot chick with a yellow beak — most strangers would say 'duck' or 'blackbird'
rows.defect: The casque — the single feature that IS a hornbill — is completely absent: the bill is a plain flat yellow wedge with nothing sitting on top of it, and it is barely downcurved (the upper edge is almost straight). The tail is a short pointed spike poking off the right flank, not a long broad fan. There is no bare coloured throat or eye skin and no lashes; the eye is a plain black bead with a grey ring. The body is a neckless squat egg with the belly nearly on the ground, so the whole thing reads as a waterfowl chick, and it is indistinguishable from the Toucan in the same batch apart from the bill's orange band.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: add a large hollow casque as a separate raised ridge riding the whole top of the upper mandible and rising above the crown, lengthen the bill to roughly half the body length with a real downward sweep, then lengthen the body and extend a long broad banded tail well past the rump so the silhouette stops being an egg.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but the headline cause in the original claim is WRONG and must not be used to drive the fix. THE CASQUE IS PRESENT. Cropping the head at 5-6x (src 440x440, crop x60 y100 w150 h110) shows the bill is built from three plates, not one: a lower mandible, an upper mandible, and a SEPARATE yellow crescent blade riding on top of the basal half of the culmen, divided from it by a thin dark sliver of background that runs back to the head. That blade is a casque. It survives at 2x and is still legible in the unmagnified 440px render as a raised yellow ridge over the rear of the bill. So 'nothing riding on top' is false, and the fix is NOT 'add a casque' — it is 'make the casque read': it is the exact same flat yellow as the bill with no hue/value separation, it is only about a third of bill height, and it covers only the basal half, so it merges into the wedge at thumbnail size. Give it a distinct value (or a red/orange cap as on rhinoceros/great hornbill), lift it above the culmen line, and carry it forward over more of the bill.

What the claim gets RIGHT: (1) the bill is not downcurved. Both the culmen and the tomium are dead straight lines converging on a point; the bill is a dagger/paper-dart, not a decurved horn. 'Barely downcurved' is generous — there is essentially zero decurve, only a slight downward tilt of the whole wedge. (2) There is NO bare coloured throat skin and NO bare orbital skin and NO lashes. Confirmed at 6x with contrast boost: the head is a plain uniform grey ball, the throat and neck column are the same grey as the body with no patch, no ring, no colour break anywhere; the eye is a small flat black dot with one white specular pip and no eyelid, ring or lash strokes. That entire must-read is absent, not merely weak. (3) The tail is wrong. It is a dark charcoal wedge springing from the mid-flank ABOVE the vent, angled down-and-back, tapering to a single point, about 90px long against a ~200px body, with 5-6 thin filament strokes hanging under it. It reads as a folded wing-tip or a dart, not as the long BROAD banner a hornbill needs — no width, no squared or graduated end, no rectrix separation. 'Short spike off the flank' is a fair description of the placement and shape, though it is not especially short — the failure is width and attachment point, not length.

Where the claim overshoots: it does not read as a duckling — the bill is genuinely huge (roughly 40% of body length), gape-lined, and casqued, which no duckling has. And it is not literally indistinguishable from the Toucan: side by side, the Hornbill has the casque blade, a full-length gape line, plain yellow bill and a tail wedge; the Toucan has orange bands on the bill, no casque and no tail at all. BUT the family-level charge underneath it stands and is the biggest defect here: Hornbill and Toucan are ONE CHASSIS. Identical plump egg-shaped body, identical wing arc with the same stipple, identical small round head on the same short grey neck column, identical three-toe yellow feet in the same stance, identical ground shadow ellipse. Everything below the neck is the same duck-shaped body in two greys; only the bill and one tail wedge differ. Net: 1 of 3 must-reads present (casque, under-contrasted), 2 of 3 absent (decurve, and the bare throat/eye skin with lashes), tail wrong in form and attachment, body a clone of the sibling asset — FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a black bird with an oversized yellow bill — a stranger would probably guess toucan, but only from the bill colour, not the body
rows.defect: The bill is present and oversized (about 55-60% of body length) with one orange band, but it is drawn as a straight tapered dagger coming to a needle point — exactly the straight cone the reference warns against — instead of a deep, blunt-tipped, slightly downcurved banana. The vivid yellow-white bib is entirely missing: the breast and throat are the same flat near-black as the rest of the body, so the most recognisable colour block on the animal is gone. There is no blue bare skin ringing the eye; the eye ring is plain pale grey. And the body underneath is the identical squat neckless duckling egg used for the Hornbill, with the belly on the ground and a stub tail off the flank, rather than a slim long-tailed perching bird.
rows.fix: Give the bill real vertical depth with a blunt rounded tip and a downward curve, then paint a large cream-to-yellow bib covering the whole throat and upper breast with a hard black border under it.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon lollipop tree with five sunflowers stuck to it
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads survive. The crown is a bumpy cumulus blob that is round-to-slightly-wide, not a flat-topped umbrella — there is no flat table-top line and no horizontal layering, the fine sprigs radiate outward in a starburst including straight up. The bare trunk is a plain straight stick with no branch fork at the top to spread an umbrella from. The paired white thorns at the nodes are absent: the only white marks are short dashes painted on the TRUNK face, which read as bark scratches or claw marks, and there are no nodes to pair them at. The flowers are five large bright-yellow ray-petalled daisy heads with dark brown centres — those are sunflowers, not cream puffballs, and they are the loudest thing in the frame, so they drive the whole read. No seed pods anywhere.
rows.fix: Rebuild the crown as a flat-topped umbrella: fork the trunk into 2-3 upswept limbs near the top and hang two or three broad, thin HORIZONTAL foliage slabs off them with a hard flat top edge and sky visible under the lowest layer; then replace the yellow daisies with small pale-cream fuzzy pom-pom spheres and add paired white spines along the limbs.
rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, and their description is accurate on every point I could check at 3-5x zoom; I add corrections of emphasis and one partial credit.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN (440x440, tree occupies roughly y=25..385): a single unforked brown column, ~34px wide, running from a rounded capsule tip at y~385 (no root flare, no ground contact other than a soft grey ellipse shadow) straight up and tapering into the crown mass. It never forks. There is no branch structure at all — the wide horizontal boughs that make an acacia's umbrella are simply absent, so the crown is a mass balanced on a stick.

CROWN — must-read 'flat-topped umbrella crown' is ABSENT, confirmed. It is a soft airbrushed cumulus: 4-5 overlapping round lobes, grey-green, with a domed bumpy TOP edge (highest lobe at top-centre, falling away on both sides) and an equally rounded, blobby UNDERSIDE. An umbrella crown needs a flat/slightly convex top plane and a distinctly flat, raised, shadowed underside with clear sky between it and the trunk; neither exists here. It reads as a cloud, and at low zoom the whole thing reads closer to a broccoli/lollipop tree.

HORIZONTAL LAYERING — ABSENT, confirmed, and I can be specific for the fix: there are ~28 fine pinnate sprigs and they are laid out as a RADIAL STARBURST about the crown centre. At top-centre two sprigs point vertically straight up (I measured them at 3x — they run from about y=110 to y=250 in a crop, dead vertical); on the left flank they angle down-left at ~45 deg; on the lower edge several point straight down. Every angle of the compass is represented. Nothing is horizontal-layered.

FOLIAGE TEXTURE — this is the one must-read that is genuinely PRESENT and well drawn, and the FAIL judge did not credit it. Each sprig is a proper twice-pinnate frond: a dark central rachis with ~14-20 tiny paired oval leaflets stepping along both sides. The 'very fine feathery' half of must-read 3 is met; only its 'in horizontal layers' half fails. Do not rebuild the leaflet primitive — re-aim and re-layer it.

THORNS — ABSENT as a read, confirmed, but their phrasing 'the only white marks are dashes on the trunk face' understates a near-miss worth knowing. There are about ten cream-white horizontal dashes, each ~14px long and 3px thick, and they are arranged in TWO loose vertical columns hugging the left and right inner edges of the trunk face (left column at roughly y=280,300,325,345,370,395; right at y=305,325,375,395). So a pairing intent may exist, but the left and right dashes are offset in height rather than aligned, they lie flat ON the bark and never break the silhouette, they sit on the bare lower trunk where there are no nodes, and they are horizontal rather than angled outward. Result: bark scratches / claw marks, exactly as claimed. The fix is to align them into same-height pairs, move them to branch nodes up in the crown, angle them outward-and-up, and let them protrude past the trunk edge so the silhouette carries them.

FLOWERS — confirmed and this is the single loudest defect. Five heads, ~34px across, each with 12-14 sharply pointed yellow ray petals radiating from a large dark olive-brown disc. Two of them sit low and central, flanking the trunk, at the exact scale and pose of a sunflower head. The packet asks for cream puffballs (small pale spherical pompoms of radiating stamens). These are saturated chrome yellow with a brown eye, and they hijack the read: the asset says 'tree with sunflowers stuck on it'.

HARVEST — the packet also lists flat or curled brown seed pods; I found none anywhere on the tree.

NET: one of three must-reads is half-present (fine feathery leaflets, wrongly distributed), two are absent, and the flower primitive actively asserts a different plant. This is not a polish-level gap — the crown architecture and the flower type both have to be rebuilt, so FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a melon or gourd tree — a green bush on a stick with four striped fruits in it
rows.defect: The defining feature is simply not drawn. The trunk is the family's standard narrow brown stick, the same width as the Acacia's and the Tamarind's — there is no swollen barrel, no massive girth, no smooth grey bark, no taper. Nothing about the silhouette says baobab. The stubby root-like top branches are absent; the stick just disappears into the foliage. The crown is a dense, fully leafed green ball, which is the opposite of the recognisable state the reference calls for (sparse to bare). The pods are four round striped gourds sitting flat INSIDE the crown on tiny 6px stems, resting on the leaves like apples in a bush — they do not dangle, there is no long cord, and their round shape reads as melon rather than an elongated velvety pod.
rows.fix: Replace the stick with an enormous smooth grey barrel trunk occupying most of the frame width, wider at the base, tapering to a flat shoulder, and sprout a few short bare crooked root-like branches from the top; drop the leaf ball almost entirely and hang two or three elongated grey-brown pods below the branches on long visible cords.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD. I decoded the PNG and measured it, not just eyeballed it. The reference row demands three must-reads: (1) enormously swollen smooth grey barrel trunk, (2) short stubby root-like branches at the top, (3) hard velvety pods dangling on long stalks; the note adds that the bare dry-season 'upside-down tree' silhouette is the recognisable state, and 'leaf: sparse, absent for much of the year'. Must-read 1 and 2 are entirely absent and 3 is wrong; the asset reads as a generic cartoon fruit tree.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Content bbox is 194 x 303 px (x122-315, y69-371). The trunk occupies x~192-226, y~270-371: a dead-parallel-sided column 33 px wide over its whole ~100 px length (33 px at y291, 33 at y326, 33 at y354 - it in fact narrows by 1-4 px going UP, the opposite of a baobab's basal swell), terminating in a rounded popsicle-stick cap at the bottom with no root flare and no ground contact flourish. Trunk width is 17% of crown width where a baobab's should be 70-100%+. Its fill is literally one flat colour, RGB(107,74,46), identical at x196/205/210/215/222 and at y290/310/330/350 - no bark texture, no vertical fluting, no lenticels, no core-to-edge shading; the only gradient anywhere on it is the soft fade into the foliage at the top (y262-284 ramps 50,61,31 -> 99,72,44). Brown, not grey; matte flat, not smooth-skinned.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM (the verdict stands but three details are off):
- 'same width as the Acacia's' is not literally true. Measured across the family: Baobab trunk 33 px, Acacia 28 px, Tamarind 25 px. The Baobab is marginally the WIDEST of the three (+18% over Acacia) - but 18% is invisible and 33 px is still a stick, so the substance of the claim (one shared chassis) holds. Note also the Acacia trunk carries pale horizontal bark tick-marks while the Baobab's is completely untextured, so they are not pixel-identical; they are the same parallel-sided rounded-bottom stick with different surface decoration.
- '4 pods on 6px stems' understates the stem. Measured on the lower-centre pod: stem runs approx y180-192 at x198-203, i.e. ~12 px long and slightly hooked, against a pod diameter of ~35 px - so the stalk is about a THIRD of the pod's own width. Still a stub, still not a cord (a real baobab pod hangs on a stalk 1-2x the pod's length, clear of the foliage), but the fix target is ~12px -> ~60-90px, not 6px -> long.
- 'sitting flat inside the foliage' is right: all four pods are embedded in the leaf mass with foliage overlapping their lower edges, none hangs below or outside the crown outline.

CONFIRMED AS CLAIMED:
- No top branches of any kind. I scanned every row for brown pixels: between y98 and y211 (the whole crown) the brown pixel COUNT per row is 3-10, and those pixels are scattered at the four pod positions - they are pod stems. There is no branch armature at all; the trunk simply disappears into a foliage ball. The defining stubby root-like crown branches are absent, not merely small or hidden.
- The crown is an opaque mid-green haze disc roughly 190 px across with palmate lobed leaf clusters ringed around its perimeter and a solid green wash filling the interior. Fully leafed and dense, the exact opposite of the sparse/bare state the note calls recognisable. In fairness the leaf SHAPE is fine - the clusters are genuinely palmate-lobed with 5-7 lobes and match the leaf field - so leaf drawing is not the defect; crown density, opacity and the missing branch structure are.
- The pods read as melon/gourd: perfect spheres with strong vertical light-and-dark striping (like a watermelon rind), tan-grey with a short brown hooked stem. Baobab pods are elongated ovoid velvety grey-brown capsules, unstriped.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT NEITHER JUDGE NAMED: the reference asks aspect 1 (square). The rendered content is 194 wide x 303 tall = 0.64. The silhouette is half again taller than it is wide, so even the gross proportion is a lanky tree, not the squat baobab mass.

FAMILY NOTE: all three tropical trees in batch-001 share one chassis - a flat-fill, parallel-sided, rounded-bottom brown stick (25-33 px) rising into a soft blob crown with harvest items pinned inside the foliage. The Baobab is that chassis with different leaves and fruit, which is why it cannot be rescued by polish. The trunk has to be rebuilt as a bulged barrel roughly the crown's width, grey and smooth, with a flared root base and 3-5 short blunt branches forking off its flat top - and the crown thinned to a sparse or bare armature so those branches show.

rows.readsAs: a generic round leafy shade tree; nobody names the species
rows.defect: The billowing feathery dome half-works — the blob is round and the pinnate comb sprigs give a genuinely fine texture — but it is built as a spoke rim, every sprig radiating outward from the centre like a dandelion clock, with a soft empty green haze in the middle instead of layered foliage masses, so it reads as a starburst rather than a billow. The hanging pods fail outright: I can find only three or four dark olive-brown lozenges (upper centre, mid left, lower centre-right) buried among the leaves at low contrast, and they read as shadows or dead leaves. They are not cinnamon-brown, not knobbly, not crooked, and critically not HANGING — nothing dangles below the canopy line and there is no cluster. The trunk is again the identical featureless family stick.
rows.fix: Move the pods to the canopy's lower edge so they hang clear of the foliage in a cluster of 4-6, and repaint them in high-contrast cinnamon brown with a crooked, lumpy, constricted outline; then break the spoke rim by clumping the sprigs into 3-4 overlapping rounded foliage masses.

rows.readsAs: a small green ant
rows.defect: None of the three must-reads are present. The body is not a soft pear-shaped bulbous sac — it is the family's three-bead ant string (sphere head, smooth ovoid thorax, ribbed ovoid abdomen) with a hard waist pinch between beads, which is the exact opposite of an aphid's single undivided teardrop. There are no cornicles: the two thin rearward spikes at the abdomen tip are the same tapered leg strokes used everywhere else in the batch, at the same weight and colour, so they read as a hind leg pair and not as paired tubes rising off the back of the abdomen. There is no stem and no beak at all — nothing is being fed on, and the head bead has a big glossy ant eye and antennae where the rostrum should be.
rows.fix: Redraw the body as ONE undivided fat teardrop (widest at the rear, narrowing smoothly to a small tucked head, no waist), plant a needle rostrum from under the head into a green stem segment drawn behind the animal, and add two short thick pale TUBES standing up off the rear dorsal surface — noticeably shorter, blunter and lighter than the legs so they cannot be misread as limbs.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 5x, 11x, 12x and 15x crops of the head, the abdomen tip and the whole silhouette. The FAIL stands: zero of the three must-reads land, and the asset is the generic ant/cartoon-bug chassis tinted yellow-green.

MUST-READ 1 - 'soft pear-shaped bulbous body': ABSENT, and the judge described it correctly. The body is three discrete beads on a string with two visible pinch constrictions: a round ball head, a large egg-shaped thorax, and a rear egg-shaped abdomen. Head-to-thorax and thorax-to-abdomen both show a hard narrow waist with a rim-lit highlight running down the gap, so the segmentation is emphasised rather than hidden. Thorax and abdomen are near-equal ovoids, which is exactly the ant proportion. An aphid must be ONE undivided teardrop/pear sac with no waist, widest at the rear, the head a small nub merged straight into it. Nothing in this silhouette is soft or undivided.

MUST-READ 2 - 'pair of tube-like cornicles on the rear': ABSENT, but the judge's DESCRIPTION of what is there is wrong and must not be used as the fix brief. There are not 'two rearward spikes at the abdomen tip.' At 11x the abdomen tip carries exactly ONE bent hind leg: a short horizontal femur stub projecting straight back off the rear pole, a clear knee vertex, then a long tibia angling down-left to ground level. A second, straight leg drops from under the mid-abdomen. So the rear-most element is a single unambiguous jointed leg (it terminates at the ground plane, so it cannot be misread as a tube), not a spike pair. Nothing anywhere on the dorsal rear projects upward or backward as a short paired tube. The cornicles - the single most diagnostic aphid feature - were simply never drawn.

MUST-READ 3 - 'needle beak stuck into a stem': ABSENT, judge correct. There is no stem, leaf, twig or plant of any kind in the 440x440 frame; the creature stands free on a bare cast-shadow ellipse. The head is occupied by a large glossy black eye with a white specular dot (note the reference row asks for eyes:small - this is drawn prominent and shiny, another ant/mascot cue) plus two long forward-and-up swept antennae springing from just above the eye. One correction for the fix brief: at 15x there IS a tiny darker nub, roughly 2-3px in the source, on the lower-front edge of the head. It is a mouth bump, projects less than a quarter of the head radius, and does not read as a rostrum at any viewing size - so the judge's 'no needle beak anywhere in the frame' is right in effect, but the artist should know a mouth anchor already exists at that spot and the fix is to extend it into a long ventral needle angled down-forward into new stem geometry, not to add a mouth from scratch.

Other observations for the fix: six leg strokes reach the ground in a walking/crawling stance (aphids should read as squat and near-sessile with legs barely visible under the sac); the abdomen carries vertical hatch striping, which reads as an abdominal-tergite/bee band rather than aphid cuticle; measured bounding box is about 144x80px, aspect ~1.8 against the spec'd 1.5. Overall this asset would be indistinguishable from a green ant, and would also be indistinguishable from any other three-bead crawler in the family if only its colour were changed.

rows.readsAs: a grey housefly or mosquito
rows.defect: The head is the family's sphere bead with a single enormous central glossy eye — that is a FLY head, and it is what a stranger names first. The must-read blunt WIDE head with the eyes pushed out to the corners is absent, so the widest point of the animal is the thorax rather than the skull. The wings also violate the packet's explicit note: instead of one broad plate tented roof-like along the back in an inverted V, they are a splayed multi-lobed FAN of thin translucent straws radiating backward and outward past the abdomen, more like a feather duster or a sheaf of grass than membranous forewings, and the venation is straight parallel lines with no cross-veins or leading-edge thickening. Nothing in the silhouette says cicada.
rows.fix: Replace the sphere head with a short blunt trapezoidal skull that is WIDER than the thorax and push one hemispherical eye onto each front corner, then collapse the wing fan into a single long triangular forewing plate lying flat along the back from the thorax to well past the abdomen tip, angled down at the trailing edge so the tent shape reads in profile.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld. I decoded the PNG and measured it, then viewed the body at 5x, the head at 9x, the wing at 7x, and a hard-thresholded silhouette. Packet row: aspect 1.8, headFrac 0.28, eyes prominent, mustRead 'broad transparent veined wings tented roof-like over the body / blunt wide head with eyes pushed to the corners / short stout barrel body', note 'wings held tent-like over the back at rest, not spread flat'. Two of the three must-reads are absent and the note is directly violated.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a left-facing two-ball chassis. Ball 1 (head) occupies x129-172, max vertical extent 39-43px. Ball 2 (thorax) occupies x175-207, max extent 48px. Behind that a pale abdomen lobe runs x~205-260 and hangs to y=234 (below the thorax's y=221). Six thin straight straw legs with no joint, no femur swelling, no tarsal hook. Total ink bbox x129-318, y166-235.

HEAD - CONFIRMED ABSENT MUST-READ, WITH ONE CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM. It is the undifferentiated family sphere bead, and the thorax IS the widest point as claimed: head 40px vs thorax 48px, so the head is ~17% NARROWER than the segment behind it and the effective headFrac reads ~0.22 against the specified 0.28. There is no blunt wide skull, no flat frons, no corner-mounted eye pair, no clypeus wedge. CORRECTION: the judge called it 'one enormous central eye'. The eye is not central - it is a dark round disc ~14px across sitting on the UPPER-FRONT quadrant of the sphere, at roughly the 10 o'clock position, with a tiny specular pip inside it. That distinction matters for the fix: the eye is already off-axis and forward, so the repair is to widen the head capsule into a blunt transverse block and split/duplicate that disc onto the two front corners, not to move one eye. As drawn, one big off-centre dark disc on a ball is the canonical fly-head read.

ANTENNAE - A DEFECT THE JUDGE DID NOT MENTION, and it is doing real damage. Two long curved whip antennae sprout from the rim of the eye itself and sweep up-and-back, one ~30px long. Cicadas have minute bristle antennae that are nearly invisible at this scale. These long whips are the single strongest signal pushing the asset toward mosquito/moth and should be cut to stubs.

WINGS - CONFIRMED, AND THE CLAIM UNDERSTATES IT. There is no single broad plate tented in an inverted V. There are 4-5 separate elongated blade lobes fanned radially from a hub at the thorax/abdomen junction at roughly +15, 0, -10 and -25 degrees, spread flat and backward - exactly the 'not spread flat' the note forbids. They overshoot the body badly: the fan reaches x=318 while the abdomen ends near x=260 and the rearmost leg near x=270. Venation is straight bright-white parallel strokes of uniform weight; the judge is right that there is no leading-edge thickening, but the worse problem is that many of those strokes ESCAPE the membrane outline entirely and float as loose spikes against the background - a dense bundle of short straws erupts below the wing root under the abdomen line, and several long ones project past the rear lobe edges into empty sky. That free-floating-line failure, more than the fan angle, is what produces the feather-duster read. The membranes are also blown so bright (near-white overlay) that they erase the body beneath them.

PARTIAL CREDIT THE JUDGE MISSED: must-read 3, the short stout barrel body, is weakly present - the head+thorax+abdomen chain is short and stout, and an abdomen lobe does exist under the wing wash. But it is painted over by the white wing overlay to the point of near-invisibility, so it does not carry the identity on its own.

NET: the silhouette is small-ball head, bigger-ball thorax, straw legs, radial straw fan at the rear. It reads as a grey dipteran (housefly / mosquito) or a feather duster, exactly as the original judge said. FIX ORDER: (1) rebuild the head as a blunt transverse block wider than the thorax with a paired eye at each front corner; (2) cut the whip antennae to bristle stubs; (3) collapse the wing fan to ONE broad membrane per side tented in an inverted V along the back, its tip stopping at or just past the abdomen tip, with venation clipped inside the membrane, a thickened costal leading edge, and the membrane alpha dropped enough that the barrel abdomen reads through it.

rows.readsAs: a gold beetle or cricket with a mantis arm
rows.defect: The raptorial foreleg lands — the folded triangular hooked grasping arm at the front is the one genuinely species-specific piece of drawing in this whole batch and it is legible. But the body fails its must-read: instead of a FLAT oval leaf-shaped brown plate it is a tall bulbous dome with a pronounced crest, taller than it is deep, with separate curved plates over the back that read as beetle elytra. In profile it has real volume where a water bug should read as a squashed leaf. The head is also barely there — headFrac 0.12 has collapsed the head into a tiny black dot at the junction where the arm meets the dome, with no distinct capsule, and the short piercing beak tucked under the head is completely absent.
rows.fix: Flatten the dorsal profile — drop the crest so the body becomes a low wide oval with a straight flat topline and a leaf-like pointed tail — and add a small distinct head capsule ahead of the shoulder with a short dark beak angled back under it.

rows.readsAs: a long-legged spider or harvestman on a black field
rows.defect: The long splayed legs are present and dominant — they sweep nearly the full frame width — so the primary cue survives, but everything around them is wrong or missing. The water surface is entirely absent: there is no water plane and no dimples denting it under the feet, so the animal is floating in a void above a detached oval shadow with no contact points at all, which strips the single behaviour that makes a strider a strider. The body is not a narrow slim boat — it is the same three-bead ant string as the aphid and cicada, with a bulbous rounded thorax bead and the same ribbed abdomen bead. The leg tips run out to roughly x=20 and x=425 in a 440px frame, effectively grazing both edges. The whole asset is also rendered near-black on a near-black background and is the least legible image in the batch.
rows.fix: Draw a horizontal water plane through the leg tips with four soft elliptical dimples pressed into it directly under the feet, then lift the body value several steps so the animal separates from the background, and slim the thorax and abdomen into one narrow tapered boat hull.

rows.readsAs: a turtle — a stranger names it correctly on sight
rows.defect: The exact failure the reference note warns about is present: the shell is a separate hat, not the body wall. A horizontal rim line cuts across mid-body and below it sits a plain rectangular trunk slab that the legs hang from, so the dome covers only the upper half of the trunk instead of the whole trunk. The dome is also rendered semi-transparent — the dark background gradient is clearly visible through its upper-left quadrant, which makes it read as a glass cloche set over the animal rather than as keratin plate. The concentric scute rings are drawn as thin uniform arcs with no plate edges, reinforcing the glassy look. Secondary issue: a yellow-green triangular wedge floats below and behind the head where the front limb should be, disconnected from the front leg column, so the forelimb reads as two unrelated pieces.
rows.fix: Make the shell the silhouette: drop the shell rim down to just above the leg tops so the domed carapace forms the entire trunk outline, delete the rectangular trunk slab, make the dome fully opaque, and have the neck and both legs emerge from under the rim.

rows.readsAs: a small brown cartoon tortoise
rows.defect: The high domed shell reads, but the trait the animal is NAMED for is completely absent: the plastron is a plain flat unmarked slab with no transverse hinge line and no closed-box state, and it sits so high that the underside is a wide open gap. The feet are not elephantine, scaly or clawed — each leg is a plain flat-bottomed rectangle with three scratched notches. The shell pattern is a concentric spiderweb fan, not a scute mosaic. Side by side it is the same drawing as the Tortoise asset in a slightly darker brown.
rows.fix: Draw the plastron as a deep vertical wall closing the belly with a clear horizontal hinge seam across its middle, and rebuild the legs as tapering scaly columns ending in a splayed round foot with visible claws.

rows.readsAs: a green tortoise — the Box Turtle image recoloured
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail. The shell is the same tall hemispherical dome as the Box Turtle and Tortoise, the exact thing the reference note forbids ("the shell is low and streamlined, not high-domed like a tortoise"). The feet show no webbing at all — they are the identical flat rectangular columns with toe notches. The head is not extended forward on a wrinkled neck; it sits on the same short smooth stub as every other asset. Nothing but hue distinguishes this file from Box_Turtle.png.
rows.fix: Flatten the carapace to roughly half its present height with a long low streamlined teardrop topline, break its surface into a mosaic of flat polygonal scutes, and widen the hind feet into webbed fans with the skin visible between splayed toes.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, with three corrections to the stated causes. I read the 440x440 PNG, then re-read it at 4x, and pixel-measured the silhouette against Box_Turtle.png and Tortoise.png.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a semi-elliptical dome carapace decorated with 4 concentric arc ribs crossed by radial spokes; a flat rim band under it; four columnar legs; an ovoid skull with a hooked upper beak plate, a lower jaw plate and a white-ringed eye, carried on a short smooth neck cylinder; one pointed triangular blade hanging below the head that stands in for a front limb. No tail.

MUST-READ 1 - 'low flattened domed shell with a scute mosaic'. FAILS, but NOT for the reason given. The judge said it is 'the same tall tortoise dome as Box Turtle and Tortoise'. Measured dome height / dome half-width (apex to rim, left half, which the head cannot contaminate): Pond 71/96.5 = 0.74; Box_Turtle 65/80.5 = 0.81; Tortoise 63/101.5 = 0.62. So it is NOT the same dome as the Tortoise - it is TALLER than the Tortoise. The real defect is worse than described: the family's three dome profiles are interchangeable (0.62-0.81) and the ordering is INVERTED against the packet, because the one that must read 'tall domed' (Tortoise) is drawn the flattest and the one that must read 'low and streamlined' is drawn taller than it. Overall creature bbox 242x159 = aspect 1.52 against a spec of 2.0 (Box is 1.41 at a spec of 1.6), so the elongation that would sell 'streamlined' is not there either. Separately, 'scute mosaic' is absent outright: the surface is concentric growth arcs + radial spokes, the exact tortoise pyramid-growth pattern reused, not a tiled polygonal mosaic.

MUST-READ 2 - 'webbed clawed feet'. FAILS. 'No webbing' is correct. 'Identical flat rectangular columns' is imprecise: at 9x the foot is a columnar leg ending in a slightly flared, rounded-bottom pad carrying four short pale claw slashes. So the CLAWS are present; it is only the webbing that is missing. There is no toe separation at all, therefore nothing for a web to span. Box_Turtle's foot at the same zoom is the same shape, same flare, same four claw slashes - the pond turtle was given the tortoise foot verbatim, which the packet's own Tortoise row defines as 'stumpy and clubbed with no webbing, UNLIKE a turtle's'. This is the single most fixable item: split the pad into 4-5 splayed toes and fill the interdigital gaps with a translucent membrane.

MUST-READ 3 - 'head extended forward on a wrinkled neck'. FAILS, but the judge's phrasing is half wrong. 'No forward extension' is FALSE - the head does clear the shell's front rim by about a full head-length (head spans x 283-344, shell front rim at x ~285; head is ~60px of a 242px total, headFrac ~0.25 against a spec of 0.22). What is genuinely absent is the WRINKLED NECK: the connector is a plain smooth cylinder with no rings, folds or skin texture. And because the extension is pixel-identical to Box Turtle's and Tortoise's, it carries no distinguishing information even though it exists.

CHASSIS / 'INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM BOX TURTLE' - substantially true. Pond is drawn ~15% larger (bbox 242x159 vs 206x146) and fractionally longer, and the carapace fill has slightly softer mottled blooms; raw overlaid-silhouette IoU is 0.75, almost all of that gap being scale rather than form. Skull outline, beak plate geometry, eye, the triangular pseudo-limb blade, the foot pad with its four claws and the concentric-arc carapace pattern are the same construction at the pixel level. Hue (olive green vs amber) is the only immediately readable difference. This asset reads as 'the tortoise chassis, tinted green', not as a freshwater slider.

rows.readsAs: a tortoise floating with two stumpy paddles stuck on

MUST-READ 1 — 'pale branching thicket with no algal colour' — FAILS. The whole colony is saturated blood crimson. Mean colour over all non-background ink measures RGB ~124,32,45; the lit canopy branches sample around 240,50,70 and the lower trunks around 130,30,40 (a darker maroon 'shade' tier). Nothing about it is pale. The note is explicit: 'drawn as a Lophelia-type white branching colony, not a tropical reef head'. CORRECTION to the claim: calling this 'the exact tropical-reef colour the note forbids' mis-names the defect. #9b1f2a is precious-coral / Corallium blood red, not a tropical-reef rainbow hue, and red precious coral is in fact azooxanthellate — so 'algal colour' is the wrong axis to argue on. The defect is simply that it is not PALE and not WHITE. Diagnose it as a wrong hue token, not as algal symbiont colour.

MUST-READ 2 — 'cup polyps opening at the branch tips' — FAILS, and the judge described this one correctly. At 6x on the upper-left canopy, every terminal is a blunt, round-capped rod (lineCap:'round') with absolutely nothing on it — no calyx, no flare, no cup, not even a bud. The only polyp-like elements are ~90 soft pink out-of-focus blobs. CORRECTION of detail: they are not specifically 'low on the trunks'. They form a DISC-shaped bokeh cloud centred at roughly 45% of colony height, densest at the middle where the trunks converge, spilling sideways well past the trunks into empty water on both flanks and a few floating over the mid-canopy. They read as marine snow / bubbles / a depth-of-field particle pass, and they sit IN FRONT OF the trunks rather than being attached to any branch. Zero cup morphology exists anywhere in the image.

SOURCE CONFIRMATION (packages/art/src/invertoverrides.ts): line 1167 is `'Deep-Water Coral': X({ hue: '#9b1f2a', kind: 'branch' })` against line 1166 `'Cold-Water Coral': X({ hue: '#efe4cf', kind: 'branch' })` — the SAME sessileBody 'branch' path, differing only by the hue token. The 'polyps' loop at lines 991-995 places 90 softMark blobs at `cx + cos(a)*d, base - H*0.45 + sin(a)*d*0.7` with `d = r()*H*0.55` — a random disc centred at 45% height. The recursion's terminal points (the `d > 5 || len < 5` bail at line 980) are never captured or used, so no polyp can ever land on a branch tip by construction.

CORRECTION to 'identical geometry': not literally identical. I masked both PNGs and overlaid them (red = Deep-Water ink, green = Cold-Water, white = shared). The five trunks, their x-offsets, lean angles and the outer canopy envelope register pixel-on-pixel white; the fine terminal twigs and the bead positions diverge in red/green fringes because the `r()` jitter stream differs per species (mask IoU 0.53, i.e. shared chassis, differing twig noise). So it is the same chassis and the same silhouette with a hue swap and a different noise seed — 'only a hue change' is right in intent and right at the source level, but do not expect a byte-identical skeleton.

EXTRA DEFECT NEITHER JUDGE NAMED: the trunks are truncated round-capped stubs that stop a few pixels ABOVE the ground shadow ellipse — the colony floats, with no holdfast, encrusting base or substrate attachment. A stony coral colony must be fused to rock at the base.

Band is FAIL rather than POLISH because the row carries only two must-reads and both are absent: with the colour wrong AND the tip polyps wholly missing, the asset reads as red precious coral / a gorgonian — precisely the wrong organism the note warns against — and nothing remains to carry the identity.

NET: reads as a generic deep-bodied reef fish (tang/discus family), not a dorado. Missing forehead + dorsal stopping a third short of the tail + blunt rounded rear + aspect 2.4 vs 3.4 is well beyond polish. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: three bare winter saplings or a dead shrub at night
rows.defect: It reads as leafless trees, not a fungus. There are three separate stems rising from three separate points instead of one dense cluster from one thick base, and the branching is fine, wiry and repeatedly bifurcating to sharp hairline points - the opposite of the required blunt or forked fleshy tips. The mass is open and airy rather than dense, and the outline is a tree crown, not an antler clump.
rows.fix: Fuse the stems into one thick fleshy base, thicken every branch so the taper is gradual and the branch stays plump to its end, and cap each tip with a rounded blunt or two-pronged fork.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld — the asset reads as a small grove of three bare winter saplings, not a Ramaria clump. Verified at 1x and at 5x crops of the base (x130-320,y230-340) and both crown halves.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Three pale cream poles rise from three SEPARATE ground contacts at roughly x=170, x=210, x=265 (image is 440x440), with 15-20px of black gap and clean rounded stroke-ends between them; no shared fleshy foot, no common stipe, only a single soft elliptical ground shadow underneath all three. Each pole is smooth and slightly tapering and runs BARE for its lower ~120px (y=325 up to y=230) before any branching begins — a trunk-and-crown tree schema. The left two poles lean toward each other and CROSS in an X at y~235; the right pole splits in a clean Y at the same height. Above that the mass explodes into 4-6 orders of branching and ends up spanning x=50 to x=390 (~77% of the frame width) while the three feet occupy only ~25% — the crown is far wider than tall and far wider than its own base, i.e. an umbrella/tree-crown envelope. Interior ink coverage inside that envelope is very low; it is mostly black.

MUST-READ SCORING. (1) 'dense upward-branching antler cluster from one thick base' — fails on all three terms: not dense (airy, see-through), not upward (the outer crown branches run horizontally and several on the left at y~200-230 angle DOWNWARD-outward), and not one base (three separate bases). (2) 'branches dividing repeatedly into blunt or forked tips' — fails. (3) 'no caps and no gills anywhere' — PASSES; there are none, and the cream/pale-ochre colour with slightly paler branch highlights is on-palette.

CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM. (a) The tips are NOT 'sharp hairline points'. Zoomed 5x, every terminal twig is a CONSTANT-WIDTH hairline of about 2px that ends in a flat/square stroke cap — there is no taper to a spike at all. The real defect is that the branches never change calibre: the trunk is ~10px and every branch above the first fork is the same 2px wire, so there is no fleshy 3-5px blunt finger anywhere. Fixing 'sharpness' would fix nothing; the fix is calibre falloff by order plus visibly rounded, thick terminal knobs. (b) 'bifurcating' is too generous. The dominant branching mode is MONOPODIAL/alternate, not dichotomous: the right crown clearly shows one long axis continuing outward for ~90px with four short side twigs sprouting off its upper edge at ~30-40 degrees. That alternate-twig-off-a-continuing-axis pattern is precisely what makes the eye call 'tree'. Coral fungus needs equal-armed Y forks at narrow (20-30 degree) angles with both arms continuing upward. (c) The judge's 'three separate stems from three separate points' is CORRECT and confirmed at pixel level.

FIX DIRECTION: one thick common base occupying most of the footprint width; branching starting within ~15% of ground height (kill the bare trunk region); dichotomous Y forks, max 3-4 orders; all arms biased strongly upward so the silhouette is taller than wide and columnar/antler-shaped; branch width stepping down 10->7->5->4px with rounded blunt caps; crowd the branches so the clump reads solid.

rows.readsAs: orange-tipped matchsticks or corn dogs stuck in a brown bread roll

The stalks are hairline sticks of uniform width and the fertile heads are smooth speckled capsules with no roughened swelling, so they read as matches rather than stromata.
