One nuance the judge did not mention and a fixer needs to know: two of the 16 spokes lie exactly on the horizontal midline (one left, one right of centre), and at thumbnail size those two collinear strokes can be misread as a girdle. They are not - they are ordinary radial spokes of the same family, they run inward to the hub rather than around the cell, and they are drawn in the identical hairline as the other 14. Do not 'fix' this by thickening them; the groove has to be a belt with two edges and a shaded channel that visibly cinches the silhouette.

FLAGELLA (mustRead 3) - CONFIRMED ABSENT, both of them. At 9x brightness gain the entire field outside the disc is flat background noise; the lit bounding box is exactly the disc and nothing else. There is no trailing longitudinal whip below/behind, and no transverse flagellum wrapped inside a groove (there is no groove to wrap in).

PLATES (mustRead 1) - the judge implied nothing polygonal is present; that is slightly overstated and worth correcting. The spoke x ring grid does produce closed quadrilateral cells. But they are annular sectors tiled uniformly around a single centre - the pattern of a centric test, not an armour of interlocking plates with distinct apical / precingular / postcingular series and asymmetric suture lines. So mustRead 1 is half-drawn and reads as the wrong structure. Colour is roughly on brief (amber/olive-brown) but the linework carries no armour substance, which the judge got right.

THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE THE JUDGE DID NOT CITE: this asset is the SAME CHASSIS as Radiolarian.png in the same folder. Side by side, Radiolarian is the identical construction - one circle, concentric rings, radial spokes to a hub, radial glow fill - differing only in hue (crimson vs gold) and spoke count. The dinoflagellate is a hue-swap of the radiolarian sphere-lattice. That is not an interpretation, it is a shared geometry.

ONE PART OF THE CLAIM TO CORRECT: 'reads as a centric diatom' collides with nothing in this batch - Diatom.png here is drawn as a pennate boat with a raphe and transverse striae, a completely different and quite good asset. The wrong-organism collision is specifically with Radiolarian, not with the diatom.

DEFECT THE JUDGE MISSED: the packet specifies aspect 0.8 and the render measures 1.000 - a perfect circle. Even before the girdle and flagella, the egg/top-shaped proportion of a thecate dinoflagellate is gone, which is part of why it defaults to the generic sphere chassis.

Score: 0 of 3 must-reads readable (plates half-drawn and wrong in kind; girdle absent; both flagella absent), wrong aspect, and identity-collides with a sibling asset. FAIL stands.

FIX DIRECTION: this needs a bespoke chassis, not a tweak. Egg/top silhouette at ~0.8 w/h; a deep transverse girdle belting the equator, drawn as two edges with a shaded recess that pinches the outline; a shorter sulcus groove running down the hypotheca from the girdle; the theca tessellated into irregular interlocking polygons with raised sutures (apical series above the girdle, postcingular below), not a radial hub-and-spoke; a transverse flagellum shown as a ribbon curled inside the girdle and a longitudinal flagellum trailing from the sulcus past the silhouette edge.

rows.readsAs: a Paramecium — a green ciliate ellipse fringed with cilia
rows.defect: Wrong organism outright: the cell is a blunt symmetric ellipse fringed all the way round with short bristles, which is the ciliate read, and it is literally the same drawing as this batch's Paramecium recoloured green. Every Euglena must-read is missing — there is no spindle body drawn to a tail point (both ends are equally blunt), there is no long anterior whipping flagellum at all, and there is no red eyespot anywhere (nothing red appears in the image).
rows.fix: Redraw as a smooth unciliated spindle rounded at the front and tapering to a sharp posterior point, with one long single flagellum emerging from the anterior reservoir and a small bright orange-red eyespot at its base.
rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD, and the mechanism is worse than stated: this is not merely the Paramecium OUTLINE recoloured, it is the entire Paramecium ciliate chassis INCLUDING ITS INTERIOR ANATOMY, re-run with a different cilia seed and a green palette. Measured, not eyeballed. (1) SILHOUETTE: PCA on the painted mask gives long axis 248.6px at -20.0 deg for Euglena and 250.1px at -20.0 deg for Paramecium — the same pose to within 1.5px and 0.0 deg. The width profile along that axis is a symmetric lens peaking at ~135px near the centre and falling off at the SAME rate toward both poles (Euglena ends: -124:18px ... +124:8.5px; Paramecium -126:2.2px ... +124:9.5px). Both poles are equally blunt. There is no rounded-anterior/drawn-out-posterior asymmetry anywhere; mustRead #1 ('a spindle body, rounded at the front and drawn to a tail point') is 0%% met. Body aspect works out to ~1.85 vs the packet's 2, so the ASPECT is roughly fine — the failure is purely the taper law, and a fix must not be mistaken for a stretch. Mask IoU between the two species is 0.8815; the 1,746 Euglena-only pixels are NOT a localised feature — their bounding box (96,139)-(342,301) spans the whole rim, i.e. the difference is per-cilium random jitter alone. (2) EYESPOT: I scanned all 193,600 pixels. Strict red test (r>g+18 AND r>b+18 AND r>70) = 0 hits. A deliberately loose warm test (r>g+6 AND r>b+6 AND r>50) = 0 hits. The judge's 'nothing red is in the image' is literally true — there is not one warm-biased pixel on the canvas. mustRead #3 absent. (3) FLAGELLUM: nothing protrudes past the cilia fringe at either pole; the silhouette extent matches Paramecium's within ~1px, so no filament exists at any length or opacity. mustRead #2 absent. CORRECTIONS / ADDITIONS to the original claim, all of which change what the fix must touch: (a) the claim stops at 'ellipse fringed with cilia' and misses the interior — at 3x zoom the green cell carries the Paramecium's two pale contractile-vacuole RINGS (lower-left and upper-right of centre), a dark olive macronucleus OVAL between them, and the thin pale oral-groove LINE running through all three. Every one of those is a ciliate organelle and is pixel-for-pixel in the same place in Paramecium.png. Deleting the cilia alone would still leave a ciliate. (b) 'literally this batch's Paramecium recoloured green' is not exact — the cilia are individually jittered differently, so it is the same generator/chassis with a different seed, not a copied file. The fix therefore has to be at the chassis level (Euglena must not route to the ciliate body builder at all), not a per-asset recolour or a hue tweak. (c) the cilia are drawn as a dense, fairly long fringe (~10-18px spikes) around 100%% of the rim, which additionally makes the surface read as ciliated rather than as Euglena's smooth striated pellicle — worth saying because Euglena should have NO surface fringe at all, not a shorter one. WHAT IS ACTUALLY PRESENT that could be salvaged: only the grass-green chloroplast colour, which is correct per the packet's colour line. Nothing else in the image is Euglena. Band FAIL stands: all three mustReads are absent and the asset reads unambiguously as a ciliate.

rows.readsAs: a foraminiferan shell, though the halo reads as a sun-animalcule's spines
rows.defect: The chambered coil is the strongest read in the batch — chambers enlarge convincingly along the spiral and the dark aperture on the final chamber is clear. But the pseudopodia are drawn as dozens of straight, rigid, unbranching needles radiating evenly from the whole cell, which is exactly the heliozoan look the note warns against, instead of fine branching threads netting outward from the aperture. The shell walls show no pores, and the colour is a pale mint-green rather than chalky white or honey calcite.
rows.fix: Replace the straight spine halo with a fine anastomosing net of branching threads issuing from the aperture only, and retint the shell to chalky honey-tan with visible fine wall pores.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of hot-pink medicine capsules on black
rows.defect: All three must-reads fail. The cells are not densely crowded — there are about nine sparse rods with large empty gaps, so the field is not stained pink by their density; the brine around them is flat near-black navy. There are no angular salt crystals anywhere. No cells are flattened into squares or plates; every one is the same rounded capsule used by Acidophile, Cryophile, Methanogen and Nitrogen-Fixing. It is that identical rod chassis with the hue dialled to magenta, and it is barely separable from Nitrogen-Fixing Bacteria, which is the same pink at lower saturation.
rows.fix: Pack the frame edge-to-edge with cells so the brine itself glows hot pink from their sheer density, scatter angular halite crystals through the liquid, and flatten a proportion of the cells into irregular square plates.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld. I tried hard to refute it — decoded the PNG, ran a connected-component analysis on the pink mask, and gamma-lifted the whole field to 0.30 to hunt for low-contrast crystals hidden in the shadows. Nothing survives for the defence.

WHAT IS THERE: roughly 11 rods (not 'about nine' — the judge undercounted slightly), every one the identical capsule primitive: straight shaft, hemispherical cap at each end, same diagonal specular highlight stripe. They sit in only 4 connected clumps — a 5-rod tangle upper-left (bbox 72,54-204,201), a 4-rod tangle lower-centre (110,289-258,385), and two lone rods (227,94 and 303,319). Pink ink covers 7.14% of the 440x440 canvas. An 8x8 occupancy grid has the entire top row, entire bottom row, the whole middle band (row 5), and both outer columns completely empty. So the 'big gaps' characterisation is correct and if anything understated: the centre and the entire right half are void.

MUST-READ 1 — 'densely crowded rods staining the whole field hot pink': FAIL. 7% coverage is a scatter, not a crowd, and the density-tinting the packet note specifically calls for ('the brine should be tinted by their density, not dyed') cannot happen at that spacing.

CORRECTION TO THE JUDGE ON THE BRINE: they said 'flat black'. It is worse than flat black — it is flat BLUE-black. Mean background RGB over all non-cell pixels is (7.2, 10.0, 16.1): the BLUE channel is the highest of the three. The field is tinted the opposite hue from the one the identity requires. Under an extreme gamma lift it resolves as a smooth cool blue-grey vignette with a faint noise dither and nothing else. Critically, this exact value (7.2, 10.1, 16.1) is also the mean background of Nitrogen-Fixing_Bacteria.png — it is a shared, entirely unmodified backdrop, not a brine that was drawn and then under-tinted.

MUST-READ 2 — 'angular salt crystals scattered through the brine': ABSENT. Confirmed by measurement, not eyeballing: the pink-mask component list returns exactly 4 components and ZERO components under 40px, i.e. there are no small scattered objects of any kind. At gamma 0.30 (a lift that would expose anything above ~2/255) the empty field shows no straight edges, no facets, no cubes, no rhombs. The judge is right.

MUST-READ 3 — 'some cells flattened into irregular squares or plates': ABSENT. Component bounding boxes are all elongated capsule forms (e.g. 65x25, 57x75 for a crossed pair); nothing is square, nothing is a plate. At 3x magnification every element is unmistakably the same rounded-cap rod. FAIL.

ONE FEATURE THE JUDGE MISSED (does not rescue it): at 3x, several rods carry a thin transverse septum line across the shaft — clearly visible on the right-hand vertical rod in the upper cluster and on two rods in the lower cluster. That is a real drawn detail, a binary-fission division line. But it is a generic bacterial cue, not a halophile cue, and it does not stand in for crystals or plates.

CONFUSOR CLAIM — CONFIRMED AND STRONGER THAN STATED. Halophile and Nitrogen-Fixing Bacteria share family 'rod', share aspect 2.2, share the identical capsule chassis, and share a pixel-identical backdrop. The ONLY separator is hue: Halophile's rods are saturated magenta, NFB's are desaturated salmon. Worse, NFB is the DENSER and better-distributed of the two — 11 separate components spread across most of its occupancy grid versus Halophile's 4 clumps — so Halophile loses its own defining 'densely crowded' must-read to the very species it is supposed to be distinguished from.

FIX DIRECTION: the rod chassis itself is fine and does not need re-deriving. What is missing is (a) 4-6x more rods, packed and overlapping so they fill the frame edge to edge with no void quadrants; (b) a warm magenta wash on the brine itself, driven by cell density — brightest where rods pile up, so the black field becomes stained pink rather than staying blue-black; (c) a scatter of small angular hard-edged salt crystals (cubes/rhombs with straight facets and specular corners, deliberately NOT capsules) through the gaps; (d) a handful of cells swapped from rods to flattened irregular square plates. Items (b), (c) and (d) are the three things that would make this stop reading as Nitrogen-Fixing Bacteria with the saturation turned up.

rows.readsAs: orange segmented worms or noodles — a recoloured copy of this batch's Cyanobacteria
rows.defect: The defining structure is absent: there is no bean-shaped cell trailing a long twisted ribbon stalk. What is drawn is four evenly stacked horizontal filaments each with a sphere at its midpoint and ladder hatching along it — the identical construction used for Cyanobacteria, orange instead of teal. Nothing mats into ochre sludge; the background is the same empty navy. And the note's specific warning is violated head-on: the rust colour is painted onto the whole cell body rather than onto a secreted stalk.

Each tube is one continuous smooth cylinder with a rounded cap at both ends. Each carries a single sphere sitting ON the tube at roughly its MIDPOINT (not at an end) - spheres at approx (185,100), (305,175), (195,268), (243,325). Each tube is split into two halves by that sphere: the half on one side is bright saturated orange with a specular top highlight and is crossed by ~10-12 straight transverse hatch ticks perpendicular to the tube axis (classic septa / cell-division rungs); the half on the other side is a plain darker brown tube with a pale highlight line and NO hatching. Nothing else is in the frame - no substrate, no mat, no particulate, no haze. The bottom 100px band is uniform dark navy.

I looked hard for a small bean at the strand ends; every end is a plain rounded cylinder cap, and at 4x the top-left cap is just the tube's own hemispherical terminus. The only candidate cell-like body is the midpoint sphere, and it fails on three counts: it is a perfect sphere, not a bean/kidney; it sits mid-filament with tube on BOTH sides, so nothing 'trails behind' it; and it is the same rust orange as the tube. The stalk is equally absent: the tubes have zero helical twist - the hatch marks are straight perpendicular rungs, not the diagonal/chevron banding a twisted ribbon would produce, and the tube silhouette has no ribbon edge, no flatness, no torsion.

MUST-READ 2 - 'the stalk crusted in rust-coloured iron oxide': not readable, because there is no stalk/cell distinction to hang the crust on. The rust is a smooth glossy gradient on a clean-edged tube; nothing reads as encrustation or accreted mineral.

MUST-READ 3 - 'stalks matting into an orange ochre sludge': ABSENT, as claimed. The four strands are evenly spaced, parallel, non-touching, and non-crossing, and the background is flat dark navy with no ochre wash whatsoever.

NOTE VIOLATION ('the rust colour belongs to the secreted stalk, not to the cell body'): confirmed violated, but state it precisely - it is not that a correct cell got mis-tinted; there is only ONE body in the drawing and the entire thing, sphere included, is painted rust orange to brown. The spec's 'cells themselves near-colourless' has no representative on canvas at all.

CORRECTION 1 to the claim: it is not literally the Cyanobacteria file recoloured. Side-by-side with earth-microbe/Cyanobacteria.png, that image has FIVE tubes including a crossing X pair in the middle band, with four spheres; this one has FOUR tubes, no crossings, four spheres, and a different curvature set. So it is the same shared filament-chassis primitive re-run with a different seed and an orange ramp, not the identical drawing. The judge's structural point stands - the construction, the mid-filament sphere, and the ladder hatch are the same chassis - but the file is not a straight recolour.

CORRECTION 2 to the claim: 'ladder hatch' should be recorded as running over only about half of each tube (the segment on one side of the sphere), not the full length. This matters for the fix, because that half-hatched tube plus a mid-filament sphere is precisely the Cyanobacteria must-read ('beaded chains of identical cells strung end to end · occasional larger paler cells set into the chain'), so the current drawing actively asserts the WRONG species identity rather than merely omitting features.

BAND: FAIL. Two of three must-reads are wholly absent and the third is unrepresentable; the asset reads as an orange cyanobacterial filament, not as a stalked iron-oxidizer. The fix is a redraw of the primitive, not a tint: kill the septa hatching and the mid-filament bead, put a small pale bean-shaped cell at ONE END of each strand, make the trailing element a helically twisted flat ribbon (visible torsion/edge flips along its length) rendered in crusty rust, and let several ribbons tangle and merge into an ochre sludge mat behind them.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of pale grey capsules on black — generic bacteria
rows.defect: The gas bubbles that the note says must carry the identity are entirely absent — not one bubble is drawn. The cells are also not clumped in irregular packets; they are evenly spread across the frame in the same loose diagonal scatter as every other rod asset here. There is no dark anoxic sediment or sludge; the background is the same empty navy void. With hue and habitat removed, this is indistinguishable from Cryophile.
rows.fix: Bunch the rods into two or three tight irregular packets bedded in dark anoxic sludge and send a rising train of methane bubbles up out of the cluster.
rows.verifyWhy: UPHELD, with two corrections to the stated causes. WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: nine pale blue-grey capsules scattered across a 440x440 frame, plus nothing else. Connected-component analysis finds 8 blobs above threshold; PCA on each gives lengths 57-100px and widths 20-25px, i.e. nine rods (the blob at (238,330) is two rods meeting in a V/elbow). MUST-READ 1 'short blunt-ended rods clumped in irregular packets' - HALF PRESENT. The blunt ends are genuinely there and the judge did not credit them: at 5x zoom on the bottom pair the caps are full hemispheres with no taper and no point, and a faint transverse septum/division line is drawn across several rods. But 'short' fails on measurement - the packet specifies aspect 2, and measured per-rod aspects are 2.56, 2.74, 2.86, 3.27, 3.96, 4.04 and 5.04 (mean ~3.5, max 5.0). These are medium-to-long rods. CORRECTION TO THE JUDGE ON CLUMPING: it is not true that there is zero clustering - one two-rod contact exists, the V-junction at (238,330) where two blunt rods meet at roughly 90 degrees. The judge's conclusion still stands, because the other seven rods stand isolated with 40-90px of empty gap between them, and that single V is the generic scatter-chassis overlap motif (Cryophile shows the same V plus a T-junction). It reads as random crossing, not as an irregular methanogen packet. MUST-READ 2 'gas bubbles rising away from the cluster' - ABSENT, and this is the killing defect since the note designates the bubbles as the identity carrier. Proven, not eyeballed: no component of any size is round (every blob has area >1100 and is elongated); at 6x brightness boost the field is still bare; and after fitting the background's radial luminance profile, the maximum deviation of any pixel more than 30px from a rod is 2.0/255, which is 8-bit gradient banding. There is categorically nothing hidden in the dark. MUST-READ 3 'cells embedded in dark anoxic sediment or sludge' - ABSENT, confirmed by the same measurement. The backdrop is a pure smooth radial vignette running from RGB 5,6,12 at the corners to 10,16,22 at centre, with zero texture, zero particulate, zero sludge band and only 1555 unique RGB values in the whole file. DEFECT THE JUDGE MISSED - WRONG HUE, AND IT IS THE SIBLING'S HUE: the packet asks for 'pale grey-lilac, faintly translucent'. Delivered brightest-cell average is RGB 171,199,209, i.e. R<G<B by a wide margin - a cold blue-grey. Lilac requires R at or above G with a blue lean, so the hue is off in the wrong direction, and what it landed on is literally Cryophile's specified 'cold blue-white cast'. THE CRYOPHILE COMPARISON IS CORRECT AND CAN BE SHARPENED: both files are the same rod-scatter chassis; Methanogen brightest-cell RGB 171,199,209 vs Cryophile 203,245,249 gives R/B ratios of 0.818 and 0.815 - the SAME hue to three decimals. The only differences are brightness (peak luminance 201 vs 244), coverage (6.7% vs 9.5% of frame) and rod count (9 vs ~11). Nothing in this image distinguishes the two organisms. The one thing the asset honours is the note's negative requirement - the rods are plain and unflagellated, correct for an archaean. Not POLISH: there is nothing here to adjust. Both the bubble stream and the anoxic sediment substrate have to be authored from nothing, and the body colour has to be pulled off Cryophile's blue toward grey-lilac, before this reads as a methanogen at all.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of salmon-pink capsules on black — the Halophile image at lower saturation
rows.defect: The root nodule is missing entirely: there is no host tissue, no enclosing nodule wall and no leghaemoglobin pink flush around the cells — the surround is the same empty navy as every other asset, so the pink appears on the rods instead of in the tissue, which inverts the reference. The cells are loosely scattered rather than densely packed inside anything. The swollen irregular Y-shaped bacteroids are absent; the couple of Y shapes visible are just two plain rods crossing at a corner, same rounded capsule as everywhere else.
rows.fix: Enclose the whole field in salmon-pink nodule tissue with the rods packed tight inside it, and mix in genuinely swollen, branched, club-headed Y bacteroids among the plain rods.
rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 master at 1x, at 3x nearest-neighbour, at 7x bicubic on the two rod junctions, and at 6x brightness gain to hunt for faint background structure. What is actually on the canvas: 13 salmon-pink capsules, all struck from one identical primitive (uniform width end to end, hemispherical caps, one white specular sweep down the long axis, a soft dark contact shadow), scattered loosely across the frame at roughly 12 percent coverage with large empty gaps. Nothing else is drawn. All three must-reads fail.

MUST-READ 1 'short rods packed densely inside a plant root nodule' - ABSENT on all three counts. There is no nodule: no host tissue, no enclosing wall, no cortical boundary, no vascular strand, not even a soft containing envelope. The rods are also not dense (13 cells with wide black gulfs between them, not a packed interior) and not short - I measured the bottom-left horizontal rod at about 65 x 17 px, an aspect near 3.8:1, against the packet's stated aspect 2.2 and the word 'short'. So even the plain-rod baseline is off-spec before the nodule is considered.

MUST-READ 2 'swollen irregular Y-shaped bacteroid forms among the plain rods' - ABSENT. I confirm the judge on the substance and sharpen the count: there are TWO junctions, not one. Upper-left (approx x30-160, y120-230) two separate whole capsules overlap at their lower ends into a V. Centre (approx x180-320, y155-285) three-to-four capsules cross into a loose X/K. At 7x both resolve as plain capsules merely laid over one another - each keeps its own rounded cap and its own constant girth right through the overlap; there is no swelling, no club or pear taper, no branch emerging from a single cell body. Zero of the 13 cells differs in width or silhouette from the other 12, so there is no 'among the plain rods' contrast at all. One thing the judge did not mention that a fixer must know: several rods carry a thin dark transverse line at midpoint. That is a fission septum, and at thumbnail size it can be mistaken for a feature that is doing the bacteroid work. It is not - it reads as binary division and should not be counted as credit.

MUST-READ 3 'the surrounding nodule flushed pink' - INVERTED, and worse than a simple omission. The judge said the pink lands on the rods instead of the tissue, which is correct, but the backdrop is not neutral. At 6x gain the background resolves as a blue-grey radial vignette: corner pixels RGB 5,6,12; brightest background region 9,14,20 - blue dominant, B > G > R everywhere in the field. So the canvas actively pushes cool blue exactly where leghaemoglobin should be flushing warm. The colour spec is doubly inverted: it calls for pale CREAM rods inside SALMON-PINK tissue, and the render gives salmon-pink rods (edge sample 49,30,39, core reading as a mid salmon) on cold blue nothing. Cream appears nowhere in the image.

I also verified the Halophile comparison directly rather than taking it on trust, and it is accurate and in fact understated. Halophile.png is not merely similar - it is the same generator: the same scatter of plain uniform capsules with the same specular sweep and the same dark radial vignette, differing only in hue (hot magenta vs salmon) and in count. This is not 'reads like a desaturation', it is a demonstrable hue swap on a shared rod-family chassis. Halophile's own must-reads (salt crystals, whole-field staining, flattened square plates) are likewise missing from it, which is consistent with one untailored rod primitive serving the whole microbe rod family.

Verdict: the asset carries none of the three identity cues. Stripped of the filename it reads as generic pink bacilli, indistinguishable from the neighbouring Halophile. FAIL upheld. Fix order: (1) draw the nodule first - a warm salmon-pink host-tissue field with a defined wall filling most of the frame, the pink belonging to the tissue not the cells; (2) restate the rods as pale cream, shortened to aspect ~2.2, packed densely inside that field; (3) add three or four genuinely swollen, irregular, branching Y and club bacteroids among them so the contrast against the plain rods is visible at thumbnail size; (4) kill the blue vignette, which fights the leghaemoglobin cue.

rows.readsAs: a ciliate — probably a paramecium, from the all-over cilia fringe
rows.defect: The cilia fringe is present and well drawn and the ciliate read lands, but the outline is a plain symmetric ellipse: there is no asymmetric slipper or shoe profile, no blunt anterior against a narrower tapered posterior, so the shape that names this species is missing. The oral groove is reduced to a short straight tick beside the centre and does not read as a diagonal groove cutting into the cell side. The khaki-olive tint is duller than the pale grey-green called for, and the body is the same ellipse used for this batch's Euglena.
rows.fix: Reshape the outline into a true asymmetric slipper — broad rounded front, narrowing tapered rear, one flank straighter than the other — and cut a clear diagonal oral groove running back from the front into the side with denser cilia lining it.

rows.readsAs: a long branching chain of lemon-yellow beads - a streptococcus chain or a bent bead necklace
rows.defect: The signature is a flat packet of EXACTLY FOUR spheres and the packet note says a chain reads as something else entirely - what is drawn is roughly 25 spheres in a Y-shaped, three-armed chain. Colour is wrong too: bright lemon-yellow, not salmon pink to red-orange. And there is no heavy layered envelope rim on any cell; each sphere is a plain glossy ball with a soft dark edge, the same bead used inside the Sulfur-Oxidizing filaments.
rows.fix: Draw four spheres only, in a 2x2 flat packet with the cells pressed flat against each other, recoloured salmon-to-red-orange, each ringed by a thick double-line envelope so the wall is visibly several times heavier than the cell outlines elsewhere in the family.
rows.verifyWhy: I looked hard for a way to refute this and could not. VERIFIED COUNT (not eyeballed): I thresholded the specular highlights and ran a connected-component pass — 26 discrete highlight blobs, one per sphere, areas 60-209px, no other blobs. So the drawing is 26 cocci, not four. The judge's 'roughly 25' is accurate; call it 26. LAYOUT: they are strung as a branched filament, not a packet. Reading the 2x upscale: a five-sphere near-horizontal run across the upper left (x~65-215, y~125); a junction at its left end from which a six-sphere chain descends to the lower left; a second junction near (120,225) feeding a six/seven-sphere chain that runs left-to-right along the bottom left and terminates in a short two-sphere spur pointing down-right; and from the RIGHT end of the top run, a long unbroken ten-to-twelve-sphere diagonal sweeping down to the lower right corner (ending ~(370,315)). Two clear branch points, three to four arms — the judge's 'three-armed branching chain' is a fair description of the silhouette. There is nowhere in the frame a readable sub-group of exactly four in a flat 2x2 square; every cluster is either a linear run of five-plus or a junction of three arms. This is precisely the failure the packet note warns against verbatim: 'a lone sphere or a long chain reads as something else entirely.' What it actually reads as is a streptococcus/staphylococcus chain, or — worse inside this batch — as the yellow sulfur granules of #5 Sulfur-Oxidizing Bacteria, whose reference row literally specifies 'bright lemon-yellow sulfur globules'. COLOUR: sampled, not guessed. The dominant bright-pixel buckets are 224,192,64 / 192,160,32 / 160,128,32 / 128,96,32 / 224,160,64 — hue ~42-48 degrees, i.e. goldenrod-amber with brown-gold shadow. There is not one pixel in the salmon-to-red-orange band (hue ~5-15) anywhere in the frame. The judge's 'bright yellow' is right in substance; I'd refine it to saturated goldenrod/amber rather than lemon, but it is nowhere near pink-red. ENVELOPE RIM — the one place worth correcting the judge's phrasing: at 9x zoom on a single cell each sphere is NOT bare. It carries a soft radial gradient plus a thin pale arc (about 1-2px at native scale) along its upper-left limb. But that arc is a light-source rim highlight, present only on the lit side and absent on the shadowed lower-right limb — it is not a wall. There is no closed band of differing value ringing the cell, no concentric layering, and nothing that reads as an unusually thick envelope; the cells look like plain glossy plastic beads. So the must-read 'an unusually thick layered cell envelope drawn as a heavy rim' is genuinely absent, and the judge is right, but a fixer should know the render already has a rim-light channel to work with — the fix is to add a closed, full-circumference multi-value envelope band, not to add lighting from scratch. NET: of three must-reads, the tetrad is absent (fatal on its own per the note), the heavy layered envelope is absent, and the glossy sheen is the only one present — and it is present in the wrong hue. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a radar sweep screen, or a red dartboard/wheel - a flat UI graphic, not an organism
rows.defect: It is a flat 2-D wireframe: one circle outline, three concentric rings and twelve straight spokes, filled with a red radial glow. Not one spine crosses the outer circle, so the defining halo of long fine radiating needles is entirely absent - the silhouette is a plain unbroken disc. The shell reads as red-on-black rather than clear glassy silica, there is no nested inner shell, and the 'dark central capsule' is a soft glow rather than a body. Nothing about it is three-dimensional or glassy.
rows.fix: Push a few dozen long straight needles out well past the shell so the silhouette is a spiked star, and rebuild the sphere as a lattice of hexagonal holes shaded to read as glass, with a small opaque dark capsule visible through it at the centre.
rows.verifyWhy:
I tried to refute this and could not; the FAIL stands, and the judge's geometry is accurate down to the counts. What is on the 440x440 canvas: a hard-edged crimson disc centred at (220,220). Pixel-measured structure -- FOUR concentric circles at r=32, r=65, r=98 and the outer rim at r=132-134, plus EXACTLY 12 straight spokes on a perfect 30-degree pitch (measured crossings at 0/29.5/59.75/90/119.75/149.75/180/209.75/239.75/269.5/299.25/329.25 deg, identical set at r=60 and r=120). That is a polar/radar grid, not an organism. The judge said 'three concentric rings and twelve spokes over one circle' -- correct on every number.

SPINES: absent, and I verified this the hard way rather than by eye. A 180-angle radial sweep returns an outer ink radius of 132-135 px at EVERY angle (variance under 3 px, i.e. antialias jitter only). A whole-image scan for any pixel with R>=10 gives a maximum radius of 134 with a hard cliff (counts per radius ring: 132->848 px, 133->546, 134->110, 135->0). Dropping the threshold to R>=8 only picks up the background dither (8,11,17 vs bg 5,6,12) scattered uniformly to the corners, not directional needles. So the defining halo of long fine straight radiating spines is 100% missing; every spoke terminates ON the outer circle instead of piercing it, which is what turns the silhouette into an unbroken disc. This alone is a must-read failure.

COLOUR: the judge is right that it is red, and it is worse than 'red' -- there is no glass reading whatsoever. Lattice lines run 216,76,91 at the rim down to 118,43,54 on the inner rings; the fill is a red radial gradient from 131,48,59 at centre falling smoothly to 20,15,20 at r=126 before the bright rim stroke (161,59,72). Hue is pinned around 350-355 deg everywhere -- zero cool/cyan/white highlights, zero iridescence, no specular hits that would say silica.

TWO CORRECTIONS to the judge's wording, neither of which saves the asset:
(1) 'no nested inner shell' is the weakest part of the charge and should not be cited as the fix target -- that must-read is qualified 'sometimes', so it is optional, and the r=32 and r=65 rings are arguably a nested-ring attempt. Do not let a fixer spend effort there.
(2) The judge missed a defect that IS load-bearing: the colour row also calls for a DARK CENTRAL CAPSULE, and the centre is the BRIGHTEST point of the image (131,48,59 falling monotonically outward), i.e. the capsule is inverted into a glow. The judge also under-charged must-read #1: 'a hollow SPHERE of glass built as an open geometric lattice'. A lattice of sorts exists, but nothing reads as a sphere -- the latitude rings are perfect circles with no foreshortening into ellipses, there is no volumetric shading, no terminator, no near-side/far-side lattice differentiation. It is a flat 2-D wheel seen face-on.

Net: of three must-reads, the spine halo is entirely absent, the 'hollow sphere' half fails (lattice yes, sphere no), and the palette is inverted from clear-glass-with-dark-capsule to opaque-red-with-bright-core. It reads as a radar sweep screen / dartboard, not a radiolarian. FAIL upheld. Fix priority: (a) push 20-40 fine straight spines well past the shell edge so the silhouette becomes spiky -- this is the single change that recovers the identity; (b) repaint shell to pale cool silica with iridescent rim and a dark inner capsule blob; (c) foreshorten the horizontal lattice rings into ellipses so it reads as a sphere.

rows.readsAs: a single spherical colony ball tiled with pale overlapping scales - a scaly seed pod, a pinecone, or a Volvox coloured red
rows.defect: Scale is 'field of many' and the identity is a bloom, but this is one compact sphere floating in black. The water is not discoloured at all - the background is the same near-black void as every other asset in the batch - and there are no surface streaks or swirls. The cells are pale pinkish-white lens shapes with concentric contour rings, reading as scales or onion slices; none carries a girdle groove, and the red only survives as narrow gaps of ground colour showing between them, so the ball reads pale, not brick-red.
rows.fix: Replace the ball with a rust-red field: flood the whole frame with brick-red stained water, run two or three lighter swirl streaks through it, and scatter the plated cells at high density across that field with a clear horizontal girdle groove cut across each cell.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at full size and at 4x/10x zoom on the 440x440 PNG. What is actually drawn: ONE compact globe centred in the frame, roughly 175px across, tiled with ~40 pale salmon overlapping ellipses (lens/scale shapes) each carrying a bright white cell-wall rim, sitting on a solid red base sphere with a charcoal shading crescent at upper-left and lower-right. It reads as a single colonial sphere -- a Volvox / morula / scaly seed pod -- not as a bloom. Packet requires aspect 0.9, scale 'field of many', family 'plated', colour 'brick red to rust brown, STAINING THE SURROUNDING WATER', and three mustReads.

MUSTREAD 1 (armoured plated cells with a girdle groove, packed at huge density): HALF present. Density is genuinely there -- the cells are packed edge-to-edge with heavy overlap, and the white rims do give a plated/armoured cell-wall impression. The GIRDLE GROOVE is genuinely absent, and I am correcting the judge's phrasing here: the cells are NOT featureless. Every cell carries a fine dark thin CONCENTRIC INNER ELLIPSE, roughly centred inside the cell outline. That mark reads as a nucleus, a pore, or a lens ring -- it is a closed centred ring, not a transverse equatorial furrow. A girdle groove must run all the way across the cell's width, sit off-centre (dividing epitheca from hypotheca), and notch the cell silhouette where it meets the edge. None of the ~40 cells does any of that. So the defect is real but the fix is not 'add a missing line' -- it is 'move and reshape the line that is already drawn': take the existing centred inner ellipse and convert it to an off-centre full-width transverse groove with an edge notch, plus a second short longitudinal sulcus.

MUSTREAD 2 (the water itself discoloured rust-red by the bloom): ABSENT, judge is exactly right. I sampled background pixels at ten points -- (10,10),(430,10),(10,430),(430,430),(220,20),(220,420),(20,220),(400,220),(100,100),(340,340) -- and got RGB 5,6,12 in the corners rising only to 6,9,15 near the mid-edges. That is the standard blue-black void with a faint BLUE-grey vignette, i.e. the only tint in the water is cool, the opposite of rust. There is zero red anywhere outside the globe's own silhouette. This is the single biggest miss: the species is defined by staining its medium and the medium here is empty black.

MUSTREAD 3 (streaks and swirls of concentrated cells at the surface): ABSENT, judge is right. No streaks, no swirls, no surface line or horizon, no windrows, no density gradient of any kind. The cells are distributed evenly over a sphere with no directional flow.

SCALE: also wrong and worth stating explicitly -- packet says 'field of many' but the art commits to a single bounded object with a lit rim and cast shading, which is what makes the Volvox misread inevitable regardless of the cell detail.

CORRECTION TO THE JUDGE'S COLOUR CLAIM: 'the red survives only as thin gaps between pale scales' is inaccurate. The red gaps are not thin -- there are broad red-orange wedges across the upper third and down the mid-right, and I sampled 181,60,48 inside one at (220,150), which is a genuine brick red and on-spec. The base sphere under the tiling is fully red. The real cause of the pale read is the SCALE FILL itself: the lens shapes sample at 208,138,133 / 198,136,132 / 183,112,107 -- a washed salmon-pink -- and they are too opaque and too whitened, and they cover roughly 75-80% of the disc. So the judge's conclusion (the thing reads pale, not brick-red-to-rust-brown) stands, but the fix is to darken and desaturate the plate fill toward rust and drop its opacity so the red base bleeds through, NOT to widen the gaps.

VERDICT: FAIL upheld. Two of three mustReads are wholly absent, the third is half-present with the defining girdle mislocated as a centred ring, the scale is a single organism instead of a field, and the colour spec's 'staining the surrounding water' clause is contradicted by a measured 5,6,12 background.

rows.readsAs: a speckled egg or a smooth grey river stone freckled with rust
rows.defect: The pale ground with scattered red-orange specks does get the watermelon-pink idea across, but it is painted as a shaded 3-D ellipse lit from the upper left and vignetted into black, so it reads as one solid object rather than a snowfield. There is no granular snow-crystal texture anywhere - the ground is a smooth airbrushed gradient. The cysts are flat soft dots with no thick wall and no rim, and not a single one shows the green chloroplast core the reference calls for, so the 'still green-cored' must-read is missing outright.
rows.fix: Kill the egg-shaped vignette and fill the frame edge to edge with faceted white snow granules, then sit clearly outlined thick-walled round cysts among them - with a green core left visible in about a quarter of the cells.

rows.readsAs: five long segmented filaments - readable as bacteria, but the beads make them look like snakes that each swallowed an egg
rows.defect: The filaments are stacked as five neat near-parallel horizontal bands with even gaps, a diagram layout rather than a tangled mat, and nothing overlaps or crosses. Each filament carries exactly ONE large sphere instead of being stuffed along its whole length with refractile granules, and that sphere is the same lozenge primitive that builds the coccus chain and the Thermophile rod. Worst of all the filament and the granule are the same pale yellow, so the lemon-yellow-globules-in-a-chalk-white-tube contrast that is the whole point does not exist. There is no dark sediment or vent surface under the mat - just void.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of generic orange rod bacteria on a slide - could be any bacillus
rows.defect: The rods themselves are fine, but they are sparse and randomly angled with big empty gaps and a stray pair drifting alone at the bottom of the frame - the opposite of the dense streaming bands the reference asks for. There is no banded mat and no sense of flow direction. The pale sinter mineral crust and the steam are both completely absent; the background is the same flat near-black void used everywhere in this batch, so nothing says hot spring. The rods also carry no visible thick wall - they are the plain glossy lozenge primitive stretched to aspect 2.
rows.fix: Pack the rods shoulder to shoulder into two or three curved bands that all flow the same way, and put them on a pale cream sinter crust with steam haze at the top so the heat context is visible.

rows.readsAs: a tortoise
rows.defect: Reads as a tortoise, but the carapace is a semi-transparent glassy dome with a thin concentric wireframe laid over it — it reads as a glass cloche or a covered-wagon canopy sitting on the animal rather than as keratin scutes, and you can see the body silhouette THROUGH it. Only two legs exist in the whole render (one fore, one hind); the far pair is entirely absent, so the animal reads flat and two-legged. The legs themselves are straight-sided featureless rectangles with three nick marks at the bottom for toes. Geometrically identical to s1 and s17 — pure hue swap.
rows.fix: Make the shell opaque with a hard rim-thickness edge and real raised scute polygons instead of drawn arcs, and add a dimmer far-side fore and hind leg behind the body so the animal has four legs.

rows.readsAs: a tortoise
rows.defect: Same identical tortoise geometry as s0 and s17 with only the hue changed to pale blue-grey, which is the family defect in its purest form. The pale palette makes the already-translucent shell dome read almost as an empty glass bubble — the wireframe grid and the body behind it show straight through, and shell and sky are nearly the same value at the top edge. Again only two legs are drawn; the far pair is missing. Legs are flat untapered rectangles.
rows.fix: Opaque, value-separated carapace with a dark rim and raised scutes, plus the missing far-side leg pair — and vary the shell profile/limb length from s0/s17 so the three are not one mesh in three colours.

rows.readsAs: a stubby long-bodied furry dog or weasel
rows.defect: Coherent and namable as a short-legged furry quadruped, but it is the batch chassis with fur texture on top: the same generic snout-blob head with one big round eye and a dot nostril, the same horizontal forward-right neck carriage, the same constant-diameter tube legs dropping out of the bottom of a uniform barrel with no shoulder or hip. The forelimb region is a separate pale lozenge pasted over the torso with a visible seam, and the two hind legs fuse into one slab so the animal reads as having three legs. Bottlebrush tail is a flat brush stroke stuck on at the barrel's end rather than emerging from a croup.
rows.fix: Give the limbs an actual joint break (elbow/stifle) and stagger the near and far hind legs so they separate, and let the torso taper into a haunch that the tail grows out of.

rows.readsAs: a jellyfish, or a mushroom cap on roots
rows.defect: The dome-plus-hanging-strands silhouette does read as a jellyfish or a stalked fungus, but there is a stray unfilled parallelogram outline sitting on the upper-left of the cap that is plainly a render artifact, not anatomy. The three pink dots read as eyes but are scattered without symmetry and one is half-buried under the cap rim so it is clipped. All ten tentacles are the same uniform-width noodle, all terminate at exactly the same ground line with a blunt flat cut, and none taper — they read as spaghetti props rather than as tentacles or roots.

rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL upheld, but several of the stated causes are wrong and one much worse defect was missed. Packet reference row is NONE (procedural — judge coherence and against batch siblings), so I rendered s13/s14/s16/s17 alongside: every one of them faces RIGHT, tail LEFT, head with a visible eye and muzzle, four legs with feet, subject centered and filling the frame. That is the batch convention s15 is measured against.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (measured on the 440x440 PNG; body bbox lum>45 is x172..381, y272..364, i.e. 209x92 px; only 2.56% of frame pixels are lit; bbox area is 9.9% of the frame):
- LEFT END: a genuinely well-drawn two-lobed FORKED CAUDAL FIN — upper and lower triangular lobes meeting at a clean peduncle, painterly warm-cream rim light on both leading edges. This is the strongest part of the asset and is correctly placed at the tail end per batch convention.
- MIDDLE: a competent fusiform torpedo trunk, desaturated sage/teal-grey with a continuous cream dorsal highlight ridge. Rendering craft here is fine.
- RIGHT END (= the HEAD end by batch convention): THE HEAD IS ENTIRELY ABSENT. The trunk terminates in a hard, perfectly vertical FLAT-CUT WALL (a straight geometric seam, not anatomy) at approx x=352. Out of that truncation emerge two thin tapering stick appendages: an upper one arcing up-right to a rounded club tip at (381,291), and a lower one angling down-right to a hoof/club at (378,340). There is NO cranium mass, NO eye, NO jaw, NO muzzle, NO ear anywhere in the frame — I brightness-boosted 2.6x and zoomed 10x on x300-390/y280-360 to confirm. The other judge said 'no readable head-to-body relationship', which implies a head exists but is illegible; the truth is harder — there is no head object at all, and the flat vertical truncation where it should attach is itself a render artifact.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM:
1. 'legless' — OVERSTATED. There IS one prominent stick limb ending in a hoof at lower-right (the lower of the two front appendages), plus TWO tiny vestigial dark triangular nubs on the ventral line at approx x=305 and x=340 — the leg system fired but generated near-zero-length limbs. The trunk carries no walking legs, so the read is legless, but the fix target is 'limbs generated at ~0 length' not 'limbs missing'.
2. 'entire left half of the frame empty' — WRONG. The upper caudal lobe reaches x=172, which is 48 px LEFT of the frame midline (x=220). The empty band is the left 39% (x<172), not the left half.
3. 'top 60% ... empty' — CONFIRMED and precise: topmost body pixel is y=272 = 61.8% down the frame.
4. 'shoved into the lower-right quadrant' — CONFIRMED. Body centroid approx (276,318) vs frame center (220,220): +56 px right, +98 px down.
5. 'hovering above its ground shadow' — PARTIALLY RIGHT. The trunk belly (approx y=338) does float roughly 7-10 px above the shadow ellipse (shadow occupies y approx 345..385, centered x approx 255), but the LOWER CAUDAL LOBE dips to y=364 and does cross into the shadow. So it is the torso/limb that hovers, not the whole organism.
6. 'three vertical tick marks stranded at the far LEFT edge at mid-height, completely detached' — FULLY CONFIRMED, exactly as described. Three pale vertical bars at x=58..73, y=305..321, with approx 100 px of pure background between them and the nearest tail tip. Clear feature-placement bug (spines/quills/frill emitted at a detached origin).
7. 'pale-teal torpedo' — accurate for the trunk color.

VERDICT: the craft is not the problem — the fin and the dorsal ridge are well painted. The ASSEMBLY is broken. An organism with no head, a hard vertical seam where the skull should mount, near-zero-length legs, and three detached tick marks a hundred pixels off-body cannot be named by a stranger; the closest read is 'a fish body with a cow's leg where its face should be'. FAIL stands. Fix priority: (a) generate the head/cranium at the front attach point and remove the flat-cut wall, (b) fix the detached spine-row origin at x approx 58-73, (c) restore non-zero limb length on the trunk, (d) recenter and scale the subject — it currently fills under 10% of the frame and sits 98 px below center.

rows.verifyWhy:
Packet row: batch-002 entry 11, reference row NONE (procedural) -- so the only test is internal coherence, judged against the batch. I read the 440x440 PNG whole, then at 4x-9x on head, dorsal line, mid-torso, legs, feet and tail, plus scanline alpha runs to measure widths. VERDICT UPHELD, but MOST OF THE STATED CAUSES ARE WRONG -- do not fix against their list.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN (the real reason this fails):
1. TORSO. Confirmed and it is the whole defect. The dorsal line is a scalloped chain of ~6 circular lobes running rump-to-shoulder, and the notch between each pair cuts down about a third of a lobe radius, so the rim light climbs over each lobe and dives all the way into the valley between them. The profile is cumulus cloud / bunch of grapes, not a spine. This is the largest single mass in the drawing and it reads as inorganic. Correction to their wording: these are NOT hard-edged seams. At 9x the interior boundaries between lobes are SOFT tonal overlaps (one sphere's radial shading darkening over its neighbour) and the lower half is unified by a single smooth belly slab, so 'every seam showing' is false -- the failure lives entirely in the SILHOUETTE notches along the top, not in interior linework. The fix is to shallow or fully merge the dorsal notches into one back curve (and drop the arbitrary straight horizontal tonal step that runs across the belly), not to repaint interior seams.
2. LEGS. Eight legs, and they are genuinely hard to parse as four pairs -- they are near-black, the lowest-contrast element on the model, and they sit against a dark ground shadow. Their bottoms are square-cut on the ground line with only a small toe nub on about half of them, so 'no foot' is fair. But 'hairline two-pixel dark sticks with no hip' is factually wrong: scanline measurement gives each leg 12-13 px wide at the upper shank and 9-10 px at the ground (measured at y=320 -> eight runs of 12-13 px; y=372 -> eight runs of 9-10 px), each carries a bright rim-light stripe on its leading edge, several show a knee angle change at mid-shank, and each one meets the belly through a visible broad haunch cone. The fix is contrast/value on the shanks and a real foot termination, not thickness or hips.

WHAT THE FAILING JUDGE GOT WRONG -- these are all fine and must not be 'fixed':
- HEAD IS NOT A PINHEAD ON A WIRE NECK. At 5x the head is fully modelled: a brow ridge, a tapered muzzle with a nostril mark, a proper eye with dark iris and a white specular highlight, TWO upright pointed ears (the near one crisply drawn, a second point behind it), and five whiskers fanning off the right side of the muzzle. Measured: head ~44 px across (49 px including whiskers) on a neck ~30 px wide against a torso ~167 px long. The neck is a thick tapered column that blends continuously into both the skull and the shoulder mass -- no join visible, no wire.
- TAIL IS NOT DETACHED. The barbed arrowhead is fused to the shaft: same fill, one continuous rim light running from shaft into barb. The tail tapers correctly out of the hip. The only real criticism at the tail is that it roots on a discrete rump BALL that reads as a stuck-on sphere.
- SAIL IS NOT A FLAT PASTED CRESCENT. It is a translucent membrane with two internal curved ribs/fold lines and a bright leading-edge highlight, arcing forward over the shoulders. Its weakness is different: the base is not rooted -- the dorsal lobes show straight through it and its lower spur simply overlaps the lobes with no muscle or attachment flare.
- The back also carries small dark bristle/hair marks the judge did not mention.

BAND REASONING: this is a near-POLISH that I still call FAIL on coherence, not on identity. Head, neck, tail and sail are all drawn at a high, deliberate fidelity; the torso and legs are at primitive-assembly fidelity, and the mismatch sits on the biggest mass in the frame, so the animal reads as a good alien head and sail bolted onto a heap of bubbles on bars. Merging the dorsal lobes into one back curve and raising the leg value alone would lift this to PASS -- everything else is already there.

rows.readsAs: a broken render — a dark six-legged dinosaur outline with a rod skewered through its body
rows.defect: A dead-straight pale grey bar runs the full length of the torso from the rear haunch to the shoulder and breaks OUT past the silhouette on the left, with four translucent pink and blue discs threaded onto it like beads. It sits on top of the body, ignores the body's form entirely, and reads as a rendering artifact impaling the animal. Compounding it, the body fill is almost pure black against a near-black field, so only the green rim-light is visible and the creature reads as an empty outline. It also has SIX legs where every other quadruped in the batch has four, and a bulbous lobe on the rear-left that reads as a second head.

rows.verifyWhy:
Packet row is 'reference row: NONE (procedural or unlisted - judge coherence)', so there are no must-reads to defend; the test is whether the thing reads as one coherent animal. It does not, and the FAIL stands - but three of the four stated causes are described wrong, so fix against this instead.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. A six-legged long-necked grazer in left-facing side view on a 440x440 canvas: rounded cranium on a thick upward-sweeping neck at x~330-380 with a broad soft snout lobe and two tiny dark dots stacked VERTICALLY (they read as eye-over-nostril, not a pair of eyes; no mouth line, no ear); a run of seven-plus large triangular dorsal spikes from x~95 to x~250; a barrel torso; a big featureless sphere at the rear; six thin stick legs ending in ball feet; a soft elliptical ground shadow. As an alien megafauna silhouette that is coherent - it is not the wrong organism.

THE DECIDING DEFECT (judge is right that it exists). A dead-straight, unshaded, near-white rod runs horizontally across the torso at y=232-241, from x~86 to x~278 - roughly 190px, about 65% of the body length. It is the BRIGHTEST THING IN THE IMAGE: peak luminance 208.6 at (95,229), against a torso-core mean of 33 and a background mean of 12-19. It has no taper into or out of the body, no form shading, no attachment to any anatomy, and a small cross/fletch tick at its left tip (visible at src x~96-101) that makes it read as a lance with a crossguard. It is a stray primitive sitting on top of the creature. That alone is a FAIL: at thumbnail size the animal reads as having a stick through it.

CORRECTION 1 - IT DOES NOT BREAK THE SILHOUETTE. I scanned rows y=226..241 pixel by pixel. At y=238, luminance is flat background (14-15) from x=60 all the way to x=82, then jumps at x=84 (22) -> 86 (102) -> 90 (186). x~84-88 IS the body's rim edge in the notch between the dorsal spike run and the rump lobe, so the bar's bright tip coincides with the rim and never enters empty field. Same at the other end: at y=238 the bar reads 118 at x=265 falling to 100 at x=277, drops to 55 at x=279 (plain torso fill), and the neck rim does not start until x~287. BOTH ENDS TERMINATE INSIDE THE SILHOUETTE. 'Breaks out past the silhouette on the left' is false - the correct description is that it stops flush against the rim in the rear notch, which is why it looks like it exits.

CORRECTION 2 - THE DISCS AND THE BAND ARE TWO SEPARATE FEATURES. Under the bar there is a salmon/dusty-pink horizontal flank BAND (roughly a rounded-end rectangle, src x~135-250, y~240-255). Sitting on that band are FOUR hard-edged translucent circles: three pale grey-blue (centres src x~150, ~192, ~233) and one salmon-pink (centre src x~170). The count of four is right, but the pink is not disc-colour variation - one disc is pink and there is also a pink band beneath all four. Their centres sit BELOW the bar line; the bar crosses their upper third, so 'threaded like beads' is directionally right but geometrically the rod grazes their tops. The discs are their own defect independent of the bar: perfectly circular, uniformly translucent, hard-edged, with zero conformance to the barrel of the torso, so they read as bubbles or a UI overlay rather than as skin markings.

CORRECTION 3 - THE FILL IS NOT NEAR-BLACK, BUT THE CONTRAST IS GENUINELY BAD. Measured means: background left of body 11.8, background above the back 18.8, torso core 33.1, rump lobe 53.1, head 60.8, torso upper band 87.6. So the body fill is a dark OLIVE (sample RGB 30,35,18), roughly 2-3x the field, and the interior mass plus its dorsal-to-belly gradient do read once you look - the upper torso is clearly lighter than the field. But sRGB contrast ratio between torso core and field is only about 1.2:1, so the read is carried overwhelmingly by the yellow-green rim light. 'Only the rim-light reads' overstates it; the accurate statement is that fill-to-field contrast is ~1.2:1 and needs the body value lifted or the field darkened, not that the fill is absent.

CORRECTION 4 - THE REAR LOBE IS NOT A SECOND HEAD. (4) The skirt bottom carries a fringe of five short rounded foot-nubs with four dark slots between them, spanning x~183..285, y~345..368, sitting on the cast-shadow ellipse.

It reaches the baseline; it is not dangling and it is not off-axis support. Its real defect is that it is a lone, unpaired, un-jointed stick crossing outside the silhouette with no mirror on the right, so it reads as a prop/staff rather than a limb.

CORRECTION 2 — 'three pink dots float unattached to the right' is FALSE for one of the three. The largest dot, ~9px with a distinct dark ring around it, sits INSIDE the body at ~(301,191), just above the dome's lower-right edge, and actually reads as a single lone eye. Only the other two float: ~(317,232) and ~(300,272), both unambiguously in the dark teal background outside any silhouette, with nothing connecting them. So the defect is two stranded background specks plus one orphan monocular eye, not three stranded specks.

WHY IT STILL FAILS: the judge's core organism read is right. There is no head end anywhere — no muzzle, snout, neck, ear pair, jaw or paired eyes; the dome is a smooth featureless bell. There is no tail. There are no legs other than the five stub nubs and the one unpaired left bar. The scalloped rim + flat bell + pinched stalk + flared fringed foot is the exact silhouette grammar of a mushroom (cap, ring, stipe, basal volva) or a sea fan / gorgonian, and at thumbnail size that is what it will read as in a fauna slot. The single ringed eye dot is the only animal cue in the whole image and one eye on an otherwise faceless bell is not enough to carry an animal identity. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE (440x440 canvas): (1) A flat teal slab spanning x~72-368, y~365-385, ~20 px tall. Measured fill is rgb(33,116,108) at x=120, x=220 and x=330 and falls only to rgb(31,108,102) at its bottom -- i.e. an essentially unmodulated solid fill, no gradient, no texture, no interior modelling. Its top edge resolves in ONE pixel (y=365 rgb(27,90,87) -> y=366 rgb(33,113,106)) while every plant element carries a 6-10 px blur radius, so the judge's 'only crisp thing in the image' is literally measurable, not rhetoric. Profile is a dead-straight top with tapered rounded ends and a soft dark elliptical drop-shadow beneath it -- an edge-on plate/lens. (2) Eight stems: straight, uniform-width (~4-5 px) vertical bars, slightly splayed, no taper, no curve, no node, no sheath, with flat hard-cut tops AND bottoms. Their colour is rgb(22,18,35) to rgb(37,30,54) against a rgb(10,10,21) background -- only 8-25 levels of separation, which is why they are nearly invisible at normal exposure. (3) Seven heads: soft blue-white lumps, rgb(188,214,230) core, built from one or two overlapping blurred circles. At 10x the top-left head is a featureless octagonal smudge: no petals, no radial symmetry, no calyx, no bract, no shading gradient. (4) At 6x gain over the entire frame there is NO leaf, NO frond, NO basal rosette, NO soil, NO root, and nothing hiding in shadow. The organism occupies only x~130-315, y~210-340 -- about 42% of frame width and 30% of height, floating in the upper-middle with the whole top half empty.

TWO DEFECTS THE ORIGINAL CLAIM MISSED, and they are the worst ones: (a) EVERY stem terminates in a soft flat cut roughly 25 px ABOVE the slab. Sampled down column x=147: y=340 is stem tail rgb(25,21,39), y=350/355/360 are pure background rgb(11,10,21), then y=364 is slab. The plant is not standing on the ground plane, it is suspended over it. (b) The LEFTMOST individual's head is detached from its own stem -- the blob bottom ends near y=250 and its stem does not begin until y~262, with clean background between. Conversely the stem at x~215 has a hard flat top and no head at all. So the render contains a headless stem and a stemless head in the same frame.

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM: 'no stem structure' is wrong as written -- stems are present and countable (8 of them). The accurate defect is that they are structureless and disconnected: untapered rectangles at near-background contrast, floating free at the bottom and, in one case, at the top too. 'Green plastic tray' is the wrong colour and the wrong object: the slab is teal/cyan rgb(33,116,108), and its silhouette (flat top, tapered ends, cast shadow) reads as a dish/plate/petri seen edge-on or a UI progress bar, not a walled tray. Everything else in the claim holds: the capsule bar is hard-edged, opaque, and the sole crisp element; the heads are blurred white blobs on pin stems; there is no leaf and no base; and the composite reads as cotton swabs standing in a dish, not as a plant.

FIX DIRECTION: the slab needs to become a painted ground/rosette (soft edge, value modelling, hue tied to the plant) or be removed; stems must land on and merge with the base, gain taper and curvature and enough value separation to be visible unbrightened; heads need petal/floret structure instead of a blur; at least one leaf or basal frond must exist; and the crispness budget must be inverted -- the organism should be the sharpest thing in frame, not the furniture.

rows.readsAs: cotton candy on a stick
rows.defect: The identity of a plant — foliage structure — is absent. The canopy is one amorphous pink amoeba blob with a bite out of its right side and no leaves, no clusters and no internal branching, and it sits on a perfectly straight, untapered, uniform-width brown rod with no branch, no fork, no root flare. Nothing in the image says organism rather than confection.
rows.fix: Replace the single blob with discrete leaf or frond clusters hung off two or three forking branches, and taper the trunk with a root flare at the base.
rows.verifyWhy:
FAIL UPHELD, but two parts of the stated cause are wrong and would send the fix to the wrong layer.

WHAT I ACTUALLY SAW. 440x440. A magenta-pink foliage mass occupying roughly x=140-325, y=25-250 (about 185px wide x 215px tall), sitting on a thin dark-brown vertical stem that runs from behind the mass at y~250 down to a flat cut at y~385, over a separate soft elliptical drop shadow. I read the full-size PNG, then 3x-5x nearest-neighbour crops of the canopy, stem and base, then a luminance contrast-stretch of the canopy (measured range only 59.5-168.5, so I remapped it to full 0-255 to expose any interior structure).

CORRECTION 1 - it is NOT 'one amorphous blob'. Under contrast stretch the canopy resolves into roughly 18-20 DISCRETE overlapping soft spheres, each carrying its own radial centre highlight, unioned into a metaball mass, plus a global top-left key gradient (upper-left lobes bright, lower-right lobes dim). So the puff/mass layer is present and functioning correctly. This matters: the missing thing is not 'the canopy'; it is the LEAF-SPRITE layer that should be scattered on top of the mass. Same-batch sibling flora-h0-s11 proves the generator can do it - that asset draws individual pinnate leaf sprites with visible midribs, radiating outward from visible branch stubs at the crown, over the same kind of soft haze mass. flora-h0-s10 has ZERO leaf sprites and zero branch stubs. This is a dropped/zero-count layer, not a style variant, and it is exactly why the asset reads as cotton candy rather than a plant.

CONFIRMED: no internal branching anywhere. The stem vanishes behind the mass at y~250 with no fork, no crown stubs, no branch strokes inside the mass, and no darker interior separating foliage clusters. Silhouette edge is smooth circular arcs with a soft gaussian falloff - no serration, no scallop, no leaf points anywhere on the outline. The concave notch the other judge called 'a bite out of its side' is real: a large re-entrant gap on the right between the upper-right and lower-right lobe groups, which with the overall S/C-shaped outline is what makes it read as an amoeba.

CORRECTION 2 - 'perfectly straight uniform-width rod with no taper' is directionally right but factually off. Measured stem widths (background-relative threshold): 12px at y=260, 12 at y=280, 12 at y=300, 12 at y=320, 11 at y=340, 11 at y=365, 10 at y=378, 10 at y=382. So it DOES taper about 17% - but the WRONG WAY: it is thinnest at the ground and thickest at the crown, the inverse of a real trunk. Centre-x measured 220.5 at every sampled row, so it is dead vertical with zero curve, lean or sway.

CONFIRMED: no root flare. The stem terminates in a flat horizontal cut at y~385 with no widening, no flare, no ground-contact detail; the only ground cue is the detached ellipse shadow, and the stem tip does not even meet the shadow's visual centre convincingly.

SCALE DEFECT the other judge did not quantify: an ~11px stem carrying a ~185px-wide canopy is a ~17:1 canopy-to-stem ratio. That alone destroys the plant read regardless of the foliage fix - the stem needs to be several times thicker with a flared base before the mass looks supported.

EXTRA DEFECT they missed: an isolated near-black single-pixel speck inside the canopy at approximately (185,161), with no surrounding form or shading. Reads as noise/dirt, not as a berry or a gap.

DEPTH: the canopy's total luminance spread is only 59.5-168.5, and most of the mass sits in a narrow mid band, so beyond the shallow top-left gradient the mass has no lit-versus-shadow separation and no sense of volume behind the front lobes.

BAND. The must-read that constitutes the identity of a canopy plant - readable foliage (leaves and/or branch armature) - is genuinely absent, not merely small or drawn where the judge did not look; I looked at 3x-5x and under contrast stretch and there is nothing there. Against the batch, flora-h0-s11 sets the bar with real leaf sprites and this asset is far below it. FAIL stands.

FIX ORDER: (1) restore the leaf-sprite scatter layer over the existing puff mass - the mass layer is fine, keep it as the soft backing haze; (2) draw branch stubs from the stem into the mass so the foliage has something to hang on; (3) thicken the stem ~3x and reverse the taper so it is widest at the ground, with a root flare meeting the shadow; (4) break the smooth arc silhouette with leaf points; (5) remove the stray dark pixel at (185,161).

rows.verifyWhy:
Verified at 4x and 7x zoom plus per-pixel column scans of the 440x440 PNG. Packet row for this species is reference row: NONE (procedural) -- so the bar is coherence, judged against its batch siblings. FAIL upheld, but three parts of the stated cause are wrong and one is understated.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Subject ink occupies x 93-323, y 232-387 of a 440x440 frame. Left group: FOUR stalk positions, not five -- pixel scan at row 300 gives runs at x 98-101 (4px), x 125-138 (14px, clearly a fused double), x 155-161 (7px) and x 175-184 (10px). They carry FIVE white heads, two of which have merged into one lumpy two-lobed amorphous mass around x 125-150 with no separating edge. Right of that, ONE lone stalk at x 309-313. Below everything, a flat teal slab.

CLAIM 1 -- 'same teal-slab defect as s1': CORRECT and systemic. I opened flora-h0-s1 to check: it carries the identical primitive at the identical height, same hard straight top edge, same tapered ends, same soft drop shadow, same floating stalks. In s12 the slab spans y 365-387, x ~72-368, and is a uniform #268886 with only a ~1.4% top-to-bottom ramp (#288E8B at y367 to #23807F at y386). It is a flat vector trapezoid with zero painterly texture, zero soil, zero material read -- and it is the ONLY crisp-edged object in the frame, which is exactly backwards. This is a shared template primitive across the flora-h0 set, not a per-species accident; fix it in the generator, not in this one asset.

CLAIM 2 -- 'five stalks shoved into the left-bottom quadrant': MISCOUNTED and mislocated. Four stalk positions (one being a fused pair), five heads. And the group is not in the left-bottom quadrant: it spans x 93-190 and y 232-350, i.e. it straddles the left-of-centre band and its feet stop at mid-canvas, well above the bottom edge.

CLAIM 3 -- 'a sixth IDENTICAL stalk stranded FAR off to the right': WRONG on both counts. The lone stalk sits at x~311, which is 71% across, not the far right -- the true right margin (x 325-440) is empty. It is also not identical: it is thinner (5px vs 7-14px), it is shorter (head centre y~268 vs y 240-252 for the group), and its head is visibly smaller (~26px vs 30-38px).

CLAIM 4 -- 'nothing connecting it': CORRECT, and much worse than stated. NOTHING in this image is connected to anything. Every stalk, including the four in the group, fades out into pure background between y=330 and y=352, while the slab top is y=365. So all five stalks float 13 to 35px above the ground plate. No root flare, no soil, no contact shadow on the slab. The plant is levitating.

CLAIM 5 -- 'two-thirds of the canvas empty': CORRECT in spirit. The top 232px (53% of the frame) is entirely empty background; total subject ink is well under 10% of the canvas.

DEFECTS THE JUDGE MISSED, and these are the ones that actually damn it. (a) The stalks are flat, untapered brown rectangles -- constant width from head to foot, no node, no curve, no thickening at the base. (b) There is NOT A SINGLE LEAF, bract, sheath or blade anywhere on this plant. A flora asset with zero foliage. (c) The heads are blown-out cream gaussian blobs (sampled #D2CDBE and #E5DFCE) with no internal structure at all -- no pappus filaments, no seed texture, no petals, no calyx, no rim light. They read as out-of-focus bokeh lights, not as botany. (d) The whole organic portion is genuinely out of focus: head edges ramp over ~8px, so no part of the plant has a readable silhouette edge.

BAND. With no reference row there is no must-read to miss, so this rests entirely on coherence -- and it fails coherence. A flat vector ground slab, a plant that does not touch it, no leaves, structureless heads, an untapered rectangle stalk model, and a subject filling under a tenth of the frame. This needs re-composition and re-rendering in the painterly engine (root the stalks into a textured ground, add foliage and pappus structure, fill the canvas, kill the slab primitive), not touch-up. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a flat clip-art Christmas tree icon
rows.defect: This is not a painted organism, it is six solid untextured triangles stacked on a hairline stick. Every must-read of a conifer is absent: no needle texture, no branch, no bark, no taper, no root. The triangle edges are razor-straight vector edges and the trunk is a 3px line that does not extend into the canopy and does not touch the crown.

rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440x440 PNG at full size and then at 4x/6x/7x nearest-neighbour crops of the crown, the mid-tiers and the trunk, plus a per-row pixel scan. The FAIL stands, but two specifics in the claim are wrong and should not be carried into the fix.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE. Six stacked isoceles triangles in one flat brick/rust fill, over a soft dark ground ellipse, plus a bare trunk stub below the lowest tier. Row-scan tier boundaries: apex y=41, tier breaks at y=85, 132, 180, 228, 275, crown bottom y=323. Tier pitch is 47-48px EVERY time and the base widths run 20, 50, 78, 106, 138, 164px - an exact arithmetic progression of ~+28px per tier. That machine-perfect regularity is itself a large part of why it reads as clip-art: no tier is longer, droopier, shorter or rotated, nothing responds to gravity or light.

CORRECTION 1 - the trunk is NOT a 3px hairline. It is a constant 8px-wide rectangle spanning x=216..223, from y=323 (crown bottom) down to y~388 where it meets the shadow ellipse. 8px against a 164px crown is still absurdly thin (a ~1:20 trunk:spread ratio; a real conifer of that spread reads nearer 1:8), and it is a RECTANGLE - width is literally identical at y=335, 350, 365 and 380 - so 'no taper' is correct, but the fix target is 'thin untapered 8px rectangle', not 'hairline'.

CORRECTION 2 - 'does not reach the crown' mis-describes the geometry. The trunk is simply not drawn above y=323 at all; instead the tiers connect to each other through an 8px-wide neck of FOLIAGE colour at each break row (measured R>110 runs of 8px at y=132, 180, 228, exactly 8px at each). So the tiers are not floating and there is no gap - the defect is that the join is an 8px pinch of leaf colour rather than a visible woody bole passing behind the boughs. It reads as six triangles skewered on nothing.

EVERYTHING ELSE IN THE CLAIM IS CONFIRMED. Fill is effectively one flat colour: sampled down the centre at y=60/110/170/225/275/310 gives R,G,B of 160,72,53 -> 165,74,54 -> 165,74,54 -> 168,75,55 -> 169,76,55 -> 165,74,54, and across y=320 from x=150 to x=295 it never leaves 158-162,71-73,53. That is under 7% total luminance variation across the entire crown - a faint canvas gradient, nothing more. There is no needle texture, no needle-clumped or sawtooth silhouette, no individual bough or branch, no shadow of an upper tier falling on the tier below, no cast light direction, no bark grain (trunk is a flat brown ramping only 46->37 in R top-to-bottom, and darker at the base, i.e. lit backwards), no root flare or basal spread, no cone, no dead lower limbs. Every edge is a razor-straight vector hypotenuse with nothing but 1px antialias on it - confirmed at 6x in the crown crop and 4x in the lower crop.

The only non-flat pixels in the frame belong to the background vignette and the ground ellipse, not to the organism. Under the HD engine law (painterly canvas, no flat vector primitives) this is exactly the thing the law forbids: it is a six-triangle icon, not a painted conifer. FAIL upheld.

FIX TARGET: break the silhouette with needle/frond clumping so the hypotenuses stop being straight lines; vary tier pitch, length and droop off the arithmetic ladder; draw a real tapered bole that is visible passing behind the tiers and flares into a root base; shade each tier against the one below with a directional light; add bark strokes on the trunk.
