rows.readsAs: A woolly lamb or young sheep with a long pointed face — an anteater-headed sheep, not an aardvark
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing or broken. (1) The snout is long but it is a flat narrow wedge with a separate thin blade of a lower jaw hanging under it like a stray sliver — nothing tubular, nothing of the blunt fleshy pig-disc nose. (2) There are no tall rabbit ears at all; instead a large flat oval disc is plastered against the side of the head with the eye sitting inside it like a lemur eye-patch or a satellite dish, and behind it sit two small dark rounded nubs. The one feature that is 100 percent of an aardvark's silhouette is absent. (3) The back is flat with a mid-spine sag instead of the steep hip arch, and the tail is a thin high-set lamb crescent, not a thick tapering kangaroo tail. On top of that the pelt is dense white fleece strokes (an aardvark is near-naked pinkish-grey with sparse bristles), the feet end in small dark cloven hooves instead of heavy digging claws, and the forelimbs and hindlimbs are the same length so the massive aardvark hindquarters never appear.
rows.fix: Rebuild the body, not the paint: raise the rump so the topline arches to its peak over the hips and drops away to a low shoulder and a low-carried head, thicken the hindlimbs and haunches to roughly 1.4x the forelimbs, replace the hooves with wide splayed claw-toed digging feet, swap the fleece strokes for near-bare grey-pink hide, and most urgently delete the flat cheek disc and stand two tall narrow leaf-shaped ears up off the crown clear of the eye.
rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict UPHELD, but several stated causes are wrong and must not be fixed as written. I read the PNG at 1x and then re-cropped and upscaled the head (9-10x), the topline, the tail and the feet.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY READS AS: a woolly lamb/goat barrel on four equal short legs with a long pointed nose stuck on the front. The aardvark gestalt (low-carried head, rear-loaded arched body, near-naked coarse hide, huge digging forefeet) is absent.

MUST-READ 1 - 'long tubular pig-like snout': PARTIAL, and the judge described it wrongly. It is NOT just 'a flat narrow wedge'. The muzzle is genuinely long (it projects about a third of the head length past the skull), it tapers from a broad base, and it terminates in a slightly SWOLLEN blunt rounded nose tip carrying a single small dark nostril dot - so a pig-disc reading is partly attempted at the tip. What fails is the mass: the muzzle is drawn flat-sided and blade-thin in profile with no cylindrical volume, so it reads as a shrew/opossum snout, not an aardvark's fleshy tube. The 'detached-looking lower-jaw blade' is really a thin dark mouth seam that runs dead straight from the nostril back into the cheek, sitting well ABOVE the jowl's lower contour; a narrow pale sliver of muzzle hangs below that seam and detaches visually. Fix = give the muzzle depth/roundness and drop the mouth seam onto the actual jaw contour, not lengthen it.

MUST-READ 2 - 'tall rabbit-like ears': FAILS, and the judge undercounted what is there. There is a LARGE tilted ellipse (pale rim + dark brown inner concha) covering essentially the entire side of the skull - a face-on saucer ear, bat/lemur-like, not a cheek patch. The eye (small dark bead with white catchlight) is painted INSIDE that dark concha, low and forward - anatomically the eye sits inside the ear. Behind and above the disc rises a rounded-triangular dark lobe that clears the skull line; it is NOT a 'small nub', it is roughly a third of head height and reads as a genuine second ear. A third dark lobe sits below/forward of the disc at the jaw. So ear STRUCTURE exists and is oversized; what is missing is the tall, narrow, upright, elongated donkey/rabbit PAIR standing above the crown. Fix = replace the saucer with two long upright ears and move the eye out onto the face.

MUST-READ 3 - 'arched back and thick tapering kangaroo tail': FAILS on the back, MISDESCRIBED on the tail. Topline: a gentle fleece dome that peaks over the MID-back and slopes down to the rump, with the head carried HIGH on a short neck - the exact inverse of the aardvark's low head / high hips. No hip arch. Tail: it is NOT 'a thin high-set lamb tail'. It leaves the rump on a broad base roughly as thick as a hind leg, then holds a near-constant width and hooks DOWN AND FORWARD, ending blunt at about hock level - a pony/cat tail curve. Its real defects are (a) it barely tapers and (b) it curls forward instead of trailing behind as a heavy cone.

COMPOUNDING (judge correct on all four): dense cream/white painterly fleece strokes cover the whole barrel where near-bare hide is required; each foot ends in two dark rounded toe-pads with white crescent nails that read as small cloven hooves, no long digging claws; fore and hind limbs are the same length; and the forequarter is actually DEEPER than the hindquarter, so the massive aardvark hindquarters are not merely missing, they are inverted.

rows.readsAs: a coiled earthworm with a giant leaf or spade stuck on the front
rows.defect: The body lies completely flat in the coil plane -- nothing is reared, so the single loudest must-read (front third raised vertically, taller than wide) is simply not drawn. The hood is a huge flat elliptical plate fused INTO the head rather than spread behind it: the eye sits on the plate, the snout and tongue emerge from its lower right edge, and a large wedge is notched out of the lower left as if the disc were bitten, which reads as a render defect. The plate is nearly as large as the entire coil.
rows.fix: Rebuild the pose: lift the front third of the body off the coil into a vertical S standing above the base, put a normal wedge head on top of it, and draw the hood as a symmetric rib-fanned cape flaring behind and below that head, narrower than the coil and with no notch cut out of it.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but three of the four stated causes are described wrongly and would send a fixer to the wrong shape.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440; I decoded the PNG and re-rendered crops at 4x-8x on the head, the hood margin and the coil). Measured tan-pixel bounding box of the animal is x 75..372, y 127..283 = 297 wide x 156 tall, aspect h/w = 0.53. The row demands aspect 1.1 and the note says 'the reared cobra is taller than it is wide'. The drawing is almost exactly TWICE as wide as it is tall. So the judge's core point is correct and decisive: NOTHING rears. There is no vertical front third, no S-neck, no lift off the coil plane. The head/hood sits at the same height as the coil, immediately to its right, in pure side-by-side flatland. That single miss is enough to fail the row on its own.

CORRECTION 1 - 'the hood is fused into the head, the eye sits on the plate'. FALSE as stated. There IS a discrete head: an almond/lens shape roughly 65px long lying horizontally, drawn ON TOP of the hood disc with its own clearly visible outline (a darker rim runs from mid-disc out to the right). The eye sits on that head shape, not on the plate - and it is a good eye: white sclera with a black vertical slit pupil, no lid, exactly the 'fixed lidless stare' the row asks for. The real geometric failure is different and worth stating precisely: the head is entirely CONTAINED INSIDE the hood's silhouette. The snout tip stops well short of the disc's right edge, so the disc extends past and around the head on all sides. The hood therefore does not 'spread BEHIND the head' - it engulfs it, and the head reads as a decal painted on a plate rather than a skull in front of a fan. Fix = push the head forward so the snout clears the hood outline and the hood's widest points sit level with or behind the jaw hinge.

CORRECTION 2 - 'the snout and tongue emerge from its lower edge'. FALSE. The red forked tongue emerges horizontally from the snout tip at the disc's vertical MIDLINE, level with the eye, and crosses over the face of the disc before exiting its right edge. Nothing emerges from the lower edge. (The tongue itself is fine: red, clearly bifurcated, correct scale.)

CORRECTION 3 - 'a big wedge is notched out of its lower left'. WRONG LOCATION AND WRONG SHAPE. The disc's lower-left quadrant is a clean smooth arc. The damage is on the BOTTOM edge, centre and centre-right (source x roughly 275..330): the margin is scalloped into two convex lobes meeting at sharp downward cusps, like the edge of a scallop shell or an open fan. The hood's radiating rib lines run down and terminate on that scalloped edge, so it may be an intentional fan skirt rather than a boolean-subtract bug - but it reads as a defect because the cusps are sharp, asymmetric, and the fan margin plus the near-circular disc plus the ribs together read as a shell, not as spread cervical ribs.

CORRECTION 4 - 'nearly as large as the entire coil'. Overstated on width. The hood disc is ~115px wide against a coil ~230px wide, so about half the coil's width. It IS however as TALL as the entire coil is tall (~130px vs ~150px), and against headFrac 0.07 it is enormous - the head lens alone is ~0.22 of total length. So 'grossly oversized' is right, 'nearly as large as the coil' is not.

WHAT THE JUDGE MISSED, AND IT IS AS BAD AS WHAT THEY CAUGHT - THE BODY IS NOT A SNAKE. The coil is a fat tube of CONSTANT diameter all the way around, wrapped with heavy transverse rings/annuli that read as an earthworm segment or a corrugated vacuum hose. There is no scale texture anywhere on the body (the only scale-like marks in the whole image are the hood ribs). There is no taper: the free end sitting inside the coil is a blunt rounded stub, not a tapering tail tip. A snake's defining silhouette - thick middle tapering to a fine tail - is absent. Read cold, this asset is an annelid/ammonite with a scallop-shell fan and a lizard head glued on.

SCORECARD AGAINST THE THREE MUST-READS: 'flared hood spread behind the head' - PARTIAL/FAILED (a hood-sized disc with rib lines exists, but it surrounds the head instead of spreading behind it, and its scalloped fan margin reads as shell). 'front third of the body reared vertically' - ABSENT, measured 0.53 aspect against a required 1.1. 'coiled base with a fixed lidless stare' - the lidless slit-pupil eye is PRESENT and is the single best thing in the image; the coil is present but reads as worm, not snake, and it is not a 'base' because nothing rises from it. Two of three must-reads fail. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a dark red-brown earthworm coiled in a ring

The head is the family's rounded bud, no wider than the neck -- there is no blocky triangular pit-viper skull, no cheek flare, no set-off behind the jaw. The mouth is closed with the standard tongue poking out, so the white mouth lining that gives the animal its name is nowhere in the image. The build is not noticeably heavier than the Mamba beside it; it is the identical tube, only darker and more desaturated, and the value is so low the pale blotches barely separate from the ground.

UPHELD, but two of the stated causes are wrong and the fix must be aimed differently. What I actually saw, at 8-9x zoom on the head and with numeric silhouette/luminance measurement of all five family PNGs:

MUST-READ 3 (white mouth lining shown in a gape) — ABSENT, and the judge understated it. They wrote 'the mouth is closed'. There is no mouth AT ALL: no gape, no lip seam, no mouthline of any kind is drawn on the head. The head is a featureless ovoid carrying exactly two decals — a white sclera with a vertical slit pupil, and a hot-pink forked tongue drawn as a 'Y' stuck to the snout tip. I ran a connected-component scan for bright pixels over the whole 440x440 image: at luminance>150 there is exactly ONE component, an 11x11 blob at (301,202) — the eye. Dropping the threshold to 90 adds only one more, a 5x3 pale dorsal blotch at (147,201). There is no white lining anywhere in the asset. The pink tongue is the shared family tongue decal (pixel-identical construction and angle on Mamba and Viper) and does not read as a cottonmouth gape.

MUST-READ 2 (blocky triangular pit-viper head much wider than the neck) — ABSENT, judge correct. The head is a smooth tapered almond/lens, roughly 50px long x 39px deep, tilted ~20 deg, pointed at the snout and merging straight into the body with no jaw angle, no temporal flare, no loreal pit, no neck constriction. I cropped Mamba and Viper heads at the same zoom: all three are the SAME primitive with only hue swapped — same lens outline, same white eye oval with slit pupil in the same relative spot, same tongue Y. Nothing distinguishes this skull from the slender-snake skull.

MUST-READ 1 (thick heavy-bodied build) — ABSENT, and the judge was too generous. They said 'no heavier than the Mamba'; it is LIGHTER. Measured foreground silhouette area: Cottonmouth 30,669 px, Mamba 34,768, Viper 31,549, Rattlesnake 35,696, Cobra 39,681. Cottonmouth has the SMALLEST silhouette of all five venomous snakes, and the whip-thin Mamba out-masses it by 13%. Bbox 275x255 vs Mamba 302x255. Both render as the same tight torus coil regardless of the packet's aspect 7 vs 10.

CORRECTION — 'so desaturated the blotches barely separate' is the WRONG DIAGNOSIS and will send the fix to the wrong knob. Cottonmouth is the second-MOST saturated body in the family: mean foreground chroma 0.335 vs Mamba 0.186, Viper 0.404, Rattlesnake 0.429, Cobra 0.483. The defect is EXPOSURE/VALUE, not chroma. Mean foreground luminance: Cottonmouth 34.0 — far the darkest — vs Mamba 48.8, Cobra 58.6, Viper 70.9, Rattlesnake 82.3; its P50 is 28.3 and P90 only 57.9, i.e. 90% of the animal sits below mid-dark. Brightened 3x, the coil is NOT the Mamba's bare tube: it carries clear salmon/rust crossbands and a row of pale dorsal blotches plus scale ribbing, all of which are real geometry that has been crushed into near-black by the albedo/value ramp. So the markings exist and are correctly differentiated from the Mamba — they are simply invisible at shipped brightness. Fix the base value (lift the dark end so the crossbands read), not the saturation.

FAMILY CHASSIS: yes, this is the shared snake chassis — same torus coil footprint, same head lens, same eye decal, same tongue — carried by Cottonmouth, Mamba and Viper alike. The asset reads as 'a generic dark snake coil', not as a cottonmouth. FAIL stands on all three must-reads.

rows.readsAs: the Cottonmouth image recoloured grey
rows.defect: The reference calls for a very long slender whip-like body and the render gives the opposite: the same thick constant-diameter tube as every other member, coiled into the same doughnut despite the posture being specified as crawling. The head is the shared rounded bud, not a narrow coffin wedge, and there is no long fixed grin mouthline -- just the shared closed snout and tongue. The surface is the same coarse transverse ribbing, which contradicts the required smooth uniform scales.
rows.fix: Halve the body diameter and quadruple its length into a long shallow travelling S across the frame, then give it a narrow elongated coffin head with a straight mouthline running well back past the eye.
rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but three of the stated causes are wrong and would misdirect a fix. WHAT I SAW (440x440, read at 1x, then cropped and upscaled 8x on the head and 5x on the coil, and again at 2.6x brightness because the asset is very dark): a mid-grey snake wound into a flat ~1.75-turn spiral doughnut lying on an ellipse shadow, head emerging at the right at roughly 4 o'clock with a red forked tongue.

MUST-READ 1 'very long slender whip-like body' — ABSENT, and this is the fatal one. Measured silhouette masks (bg-delta > 30) give Mamba bbox 301x154 px (area 26,550) vs Cottonmouth 272x137 (area 22,384): identical 1.96 bbox aspect, Mamba merely ~11% larger overall. Normalising both silhouettes into a 256x256 box, mask fill fraction is Mamba 0.567, Cottonmouth 0.595, Viper 0.541 — i.e. at aspect 10 the Mamba is drawn only 5% less 'solid' than the aspect-7 Cottonmouth and is FATTER than the aspect-2 Viper. Normalised silhouette IoU: Mamba-vs-Cottonmouth 0.864, Mamba-vs-Viper 0.848, Cottonmouth-vs-Viper 0.874. All three are one chassis; aspect 10 has essentially no effect on tube diameter. It reads as a heavy-bodied viper, not an elapid whip.

CORRECTION 1 — the judge said 'thick constant-diameter tube'. Not true. There IS a real taper: the innermost half-turn is roughly half the diameter of the outer turn and terminates in a rounded blunt stub lying on top of the coil at about (300,192) in the 440px frame. The defect is that the taper is compressed into the last half-turn while ~80% of the visible body is one fat constant diameter, and there is no whip-thin terminal third and no fine tail point. A fixer told 'constant diameter' may just add taper and still ship a fat snake.

CORRECTION 2 — the judge said 'it is the Cottonmouth image recoloured grey'. Overstated. Raw pixel-aligned IoU between the two silhouettes is only 0.664; Mamba is ~11% larger, its spiral is slightly more open (bigger inner hole), and its head ellipse is genuinely a bit narrower and more pointed than the Cottonmouth's. It is the same generative chassis with two parameters nudged, not the same bitmap. Same conclusion, different repair: the coil generator itself must branch on aspect/posture, not just be re-tinted.

MUST-READ 2 'narrow coffin-shaped head' — ABSENT, confirmed, but the judge's phrasing invites the wrong fix. Side-by-side 8x crops of the Mamba and Cottonmouth heads show the SAME primitive: a bare smooth ellipse fused straight onto the body tube, no neck constriction, no jawline, no nostril, no temple flare, no straight-sided snout taper, no squared muzzle. It carries exactly one feature, a white circular sclera with a black vertical-slit pupil — identical on both animals. The Mamba head is already the narrower of the two, so simply narrowing the ellipse will NOT produce a coffin head; the head needs angular geometry (widening at the temples, straight-sided taper, blunt-squared snout) that the primitive does not possess. Side note: the packet lists eyes 'normal' yet the render gives a vertical slit pupil — wrong for a mamba (round pupil), and it is the Viper eye reused.

MUST-READ 3 'smooth uniform scales with a fixed grin mouthline' — ABSENT on both halves, confirmed. There is zero mouth geometry: no lip seam, no jaw line, no gape, nothing. The red forked tongue simply abuts the snout tip with no opening. And the scale treatment is coarse crescent transverse bands wrapping the FULL dorsal circumference at high density, reading as a caterpillar/millipede or a ribbed hose — these are belly scutes mistakenly wrapped over the whole body, not overlapping dorsal scales. The judge's 'coarse transverse ribbing' is correct.

EXTRA (unreported by the judge): the body carries scattered soft pale blotches (roughly 8-10 blurred light dots along the flank and top of the coil) — a leftover Cottonmouth/viper blotch pattern. A mamba should be plain and uniform; the spotting actively fights the identity.

POSTURE: packet says 'crawling'; the render is a coiled doughnut, topologically the same pose as the four coiled species in the batch. Confirmed.

VERDICT: only one of three must-reads is even partially served (slender-ish head), and the asset is not distinguishable from Cottonmouth or Viper in the same family batch. FAIL stands.

rows.readsAs: a coiled tan snake -- readable as a rattlesnake, but only because of four small beads
rows.defect: The rattle is present as a short chain of four pale beads at the lower left, which is the one identity marker in this entire batch that actually landed -- but it is tiny, low-contrast, and reads as loose pebbles beside the body rather than as a segmented horny tip continuous with the tail. The other two must-reads fail: the head is the shared rounded bud with no broad triangular arrow shape and no thin neck behind it, and the neck is not reared in an S -- the whole animal lies flat in the coil plane like the rest of the family.
rows.fix: Scale the rattle up two or three times, taper the tail into it so the segments read as a continuation of the body, and lift the neck off the coil into an S with a wide arrow-head at the top.

rows.readsAs: a khaki earthworm coiled in a ring, indistinguishable from the Mamba but for hue
rows.defect: All three must-reads are missing. There is no zigzag or diamond dorsal chain anywhere on the body -- the only surface incident is the family's transverse ribbing, so the single marking that identifies an adder is absent. The head is the shared rounded bud with no broad triangle and no sharp set-off from a thin neck. The body is not short and heavy; it is the same medium tube coiled into the same doughnut as the ten-aspect Mamba. Only the vertical slit pupil survives, and it is on every asset in the batch.

rows.verifyWhy:
Verdict upheld, but two parts of the stated cause are wrong and the chassis defect is understated. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS (440x440, inspected at 3x/6x/9x crops plus a silhouette/colour scan): a tan-olive snake wound into a flat two-turn spiral lying face-on, head emerging at the right on a low neck, forked red tongue flicking out, tail terminating bluntly at the inner turn. Body bbox 78,130-361,269 = 284x140.

MUST-READ 1, 'broad triangular head sharply set off from a thin neck' — ABSENT, judge correct. Measured the vertical extent column by column through the head/neck: neck spans 31-34px at x=284-292, head peaks at only 35px at x=290-294, then tapers smoothly to 10px at the snout (x=324). Head-to-neck ratio ~1.13. There is no temporal flare, no angular jaw corners, and no pinch behind the skull — it is a smooth almond/ovoid bud seen in profile, continuous with the neck. For scale, Mamba's identical bud measures neck 24-25 / head 28, ratio ~1.16 — the SAME construction at a smaller gauge. Correction to the judge's wording: it is not a 'rounded bud' in the sense of a sphere; it is an elongate almond with a pointed snout. That does not save it — an adder head must read as an arrowhead, and this does not.

MUST-READ 2, 'zigzag or diamond dorsal chain pattern' — ABSENT, judge correct. At 6x on the outer coil the only surface incident is the transverse scute/rib chain, a regular high-frequency ladder running perpendicular to the body axis, uniform from neck to tail tip, and carried identically by all five assets in the batch. Colour scan confirms: every top colour bucket falls in one tan/olive family (2,1,1 / 4,4,2 / 4,3,2 / 3,3,2 / 2,2,1), i.e. a single hue with shading variation only — there is no second chromatic population anywhere on the body, which any painted dorsal chain would produce. I did find something the judge did not mention: roughly four or five faint, soft, roughly circular darker smudges scattered on the outer and inner coil. They are low-contrast, isolated, not aligned on the dorsal midline and do not chain into chevrons or diamonds. They read as noise/highlight artifacts, not as a pattern, and they do not satisfy the must-read — but they are worth naming because a fix pass will see them and should overpaint rather than reuse them.

MUST-READ 3, 'short thick heavy body' — the judge's stated cause is WRONG in its evidence though right in its conclusion. The drawn silhouette aspect is 284/140 = 2.03, which MATCHES the spec aspect of 2 exactly; the asset is not stretched. And the tube is measurably fatter than the Mamba's, not 'the same medium tube': body pixel area 20951 vs Mamba's 15828 (+32%), tube gauge 31-35px vs Mamba's 24-28px. The reason the two look alike is the reverse of what the judge said — the Mamba is the one violating its spec, drawn on this same coil at bbox aspect 299/145 = 2.06 when it is speced aspect 10 and posture 'crawling'. Nonetheless the must-read still fails: the Viper's tube holds one uniform gauge from neck to tail with no thickening at midbody and no abrupt short tail — it terminates in a blunt rounded cap of the same diameter at the inner spiral. It reads as a generic medium snake tube, not as a stocky adder.

WHAT IS PRESENT: vertical slit pupil in a white sclera, crisply drawn and readable at 9x; forked red tongue; a coil that genuinely 'sits low and flat' per the note; correct tan/olive adder colouring. The judge is right that the slit pupil is family-wide (Mamba and Rattlesnake carry the identical eye and the identical red tongue).

CHASSIS FINDING — MORE SEVERE THAN 'SHARED RIBBING'. This is not five snakes sharing a scale texture; Viper and Mamba are the same drawing recoloured. Same two-turn flat spiral with the same winding path, same head bud at the same angle, same slit eye, same forked tongue, same rib ladder — grey vs tan is the only difference a viewer can name. Rattlesnake is that same chassis plus one bolt-on (a pale segmented rattle at the tail tip, which does read). That the pipeline CAN attach a species-specific feature is the proof that the Viper's three missing must-reads are omissions, not limitations. Fix order: (1) rebuild the skull as a wide-temporal arrowhead with a genuine pinch behind it, target head-to-neck ratio 1.6+ rather than 1.13; (2) paint a dark zigzag/diamond chain along the dorsal midline in a second value that survives the colour scan as a distinct population; (3) thicken midbody and shorten the tail to a quick taper so 'heavy-bodied' reads against the Mamba beside it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE CANVAS. A taupe/grey-brown bird floating in water: an ellipsoid dome body sitting about 40% submerged, three thin pale-blue ripple rings around it and a dark blue shadow disc beneath. The body is dappled with pale cream speckles and carries one dark curved band arcing across the flank (reads as a wing-coverts line) with a large pale speckled oval below it (folded wing). The rear of the dome simply ends in a curve -- there is NO tail of any kind, not even a stub. A thin tube neck rises from the middle of the back, sweeps up and FORWARD in a shallow curve at roughly 40-50 degrees off vertical, and carries a perfectly spherical head. Eye is a small black bead with a white catchlight, set high and forward -- correct and legible. MUST-READS, ONE BY ONE (packet row 3: aspect 1.5, headFrac 0.24, eyes small, posture biped; mustRead 'long thick neck held upright / flat rounded bill / heavy body on webbed feet'; note 'Read as Canada goose: black neck and head with a white chinstrap').
1) LONG THICK NECK HELD UPRIGHT -- ABSENT. The neck measures roughly half the head's diameter in width and only about 1.3 head-diameters in total length; a goose needs ~0.75x head width and 2.5-3 head-lengths. It is also carried forward, not upright. CORRECTION to the original claim: the neck is not literally 'bill-width' -- it is about equal to the bill's base depth but thicker than the bill's midshaft -- and the failure is as much SHORTNESS as thinness. Fix needs both: thicken to ~0.7-0.8 head width and lengthen to a vertical column with only a slight forward set at the base.
2) FLAT ROUNDED BILL -- ABSENT, and the judge's description is right in effect but slightly off in shape name. It is not a cone of revolution; it is a flat tapering wedge that ends in a sharp point, and it is socketed into the side of a spherical head at eye level like a carrot in a snowman -- there is no forehead continuity at all. A goose bill is deep at the base, blunt/rounded at the tip, and runs in an unbroken line into the skull. Both the tip shape AND the head-bill junction need rebuilding.
3) HEAVY BODY ON WEBBED FEET -- ABSENT, confirmed by direct evidence rather than assumption: I brightened the lower 200 rows by 3.5x and the underwater volume is nothing but a translucent continuation of the body blob plus the water disc. Worse than a hidden-feet problem, the POSTURE ITSELF contradicts the spec: the row says 'biped', but the asset is rendered swimming, with the identical water treatment (ripple rings + shadow disc) used by Duck, Eider and Swan. 4) CANADA GOOSE COLOUR READ -- ENTIRELY ABSENT, exactly as claimed. Head and neck are the same mid taupe-brown as the body; there is no black anywhere on head or neck and no white chinstrap. The only lighter passage on the head is a thin rim-light along the crown/upper-right from the lighting pass -- that is a highlight, not a cheek patch, and it sits on the crown rather than running from behind the eye under the chin where a chinstrap belongs.

Duck is the same asset: same amber pointed wedge bill, same spherical ball head, same speckled dome body at the same waterline, same three ripple rings and shadow disc -- only the hue (olive vs taupe) and the neck differ. ORGANISM READ. Thin forward-leaning neck + pointed yellow spear bill + speckled brown body floating low = grebe (or a duck decoy). The judge's 'grebe or loon' is a fair read. Nothing in the silhouette says goose.

rows.readsAs: a swan, or possibly a white goose

Row-width scan puts the top of the back at y~174 and the belly line at y~236 (row width collapses from ~180px to ~66px there, i.e. torso ends and only legs remain), with the pads bottoming out at y~268. So torso depth ~62px and ground clearance ~32px -- half a body-depth of open daylight under the belly, and in the 4x crop it reads as a wide dark ARCH between fore and hind limbs. The torso itself is a smooth rounded tube (torso length ~186px over depth ~62 = ~3.0 aspect vs the packet's 2.4), with no dorsal flattening, no heavy shoulder/rump mass and no wedge taper. This is the family sausage. CORRECTION to the claim: the legs are not actually 'tall' in proportion (~32px against a 62px body, roughly 0.5 body-depths); they are straight, untapered, evenly-thick columns set at the four corners with a wide gap between them, and it is that STANCE plus the tube torso -- not leg length -- that destroys the low-slung read. The fix is to drop the belly to near ground, shorten and splay the limbs, and flatten/widen the dorsal line, not merely to shorten the legs.

MUST-READ 2 -- white stripe running back over the face: ABSENT, and the mark is inverted exactly as claimed. CORRECTION to the wording: it is not that there is 'no white'; the entire animal, head included, is a cream/white base coat, so the head is almost all white. What is missing is the badger's DARK facial ground carrying a white blaze from nose over the crown plus the dark eye-to-ear bands. Instead the head carries dark marks that run the WRONG AXIS: at 14x I count two dark bands crossing the muzzle transversely (near the nose tip and mid-snout, perpendicular to the snout axis) and two-to-three more dark bars dropping vertically over the crown/forehead -- i.e. the flank barring simply continues onto the head. That reads lemur/civet/okapi, never badger. The only large dark mass on the head is a solid round near-black disc on the cheek/side of the skull (sampled RGB 21,24,30 -- NOT background, which is 5,6,12, so it is a filled dark ear/eye-patch blot, not a hole punched through the head). Also worth logging: the eye is a large goggle -- a dark ring ~12px across with a pale iris and dark pupil on a head of ~40px -- while the packet specifies eyes: small. A badger's eye is a tiny bead.

MUST-READ 3 -- long straight digging foreclaws: ABSENT, confirmed at 16x on the forefoot. Each foot is two stacked flat grey ovals (near and far foot) carrying two-to-three short faint vertical seam lines that read as toe divisions. Nothing projects past the pad outline -- no claw tips, no forward-raked spikes, no fore/hind differentiation at all (hind foot at 6x is the same pad shape). It reads as a blunt hoof/pad.

FLANK PATTERN: the claim is accurate and I can be more specific for the fix. There is one long horizontal dark band running nearly the full body length at mid-flank, with roughly twenty tapering vertical bars hanging off it up onto the back and down onto the lower flank -- a comb/rake, tiger- or okapi-like. This is the dominant visual event in the whole asset and it must be deleted outright; the badger's signature must move to the head as a longitudinal blaze on a dark face.

OTHER: the tail is a small pale rounded lobe at the top-rear of the rump -- undefined but roughly the right short nub, so not a failure point. There is also a stray black arrowhead notch on the hind leg near the pad (x~250,y~250) that reads as an artifact.

Verdict: wrong organism. FAIL upheld.

rows.readsAs: a beige dachshund with a squirrel tail

rows.readsAs: an orange dachshund; identical to the Fisher card in a warmer hue
rows.defect: All three must-reads are absent. There is no pale orange throat bib — the throat is the same tan as the rest of the body, so the single diagnostic that names a marten is missing. rows.verifyWhy:
Looked at the 440px master, then at 6-8x crops of head, throat, tail, and a 3x full-body crop, and side-by-side against Fisher.png at the identical crop. The FAIL stands, but two of the three stated causes are misdescribed and one true defect the other judge never mentioned is the worst of the lot.

CONFIRMED — SAME CHASSIS AS FISHER. This is the decisive finding. Cropping Marten and Fisher at the exact same rect (80,140,300x140) gives two images that overlay: identical loaf-shaped body tube with a straight topline and a pale rim-light stripe along the spine, identical stumpy column legs with the same shoulder blob and the same haunch blob, identical toe-pad feet, identical head shape, identical two-dark-disc ear treatment, identical tail (drooping cone + one-sided bristle comb). Only the hue differs (Marten warmer tan/ochre with brown head; Fisher greyer mauve) plus a slightly longer Fisher tail. The 'Fisher card in a warmer hue' claim is verified literally, not rhetorically.

mustRead 1 — 'bushy full-length tail': ABSENT, and the other judge did not raise it. The tail is roughly one third of body length, angles down-back, and is drawn as a SMOOTH tapering cone (flat mid-brown fill with a lighter belly highlight) with a comb of dark bristle strokes applied only along its upper edge. It reads as a feather or a leaf, not as a bushy cylindrical brush, and it is nowhere near full-length. Fix: lengthen to ~0.7-0.9 of body length, give it a cylindrical bushy volume (fur silhouette on BOTH edges, not a one-sided comb), and carry it out behind level or in a soft upward curve.

mustRead 2 — 'pale orange throat bib': ABSENT. Confirmed. But the reason is inverted from what a fix would naively do. The body is already uniformly pale cream-tan; the HEAD is the darker element (mid brown) and the front-leg/chest mass is a darker brown blob. So there is nothing for a pale bib to contrast against — there is a slightly creamier band where the neck meets the head, but it is unbounded, reads as generic neck ruff shading, and is not orange. The judge's phrasing 'throat is the same tan as the body' is right in effect. Fix requires TWO changes, not one: darken the trunk to rich chocolate-brown mustelid coat, THEN lay in a bounded, hard-edged apricot/pale-orange patch from under the chin down across the chest between the forelegs.

mustRead 3 — 'large rounded ears on a foxy face': the judge's description is WRONG on both halves, though the must-read still fails. (a) The ears are NOT nubs. There are two clearly drawn large dark-brown rounded DISCS on the skull — one at the crown, one further forward over the brow, each about a third of the head height. They are large and they are rounded. The defect is that they are painted FLAT onto the skull surface as pads and barely break the head silhouette, and the forward one sits so far down the brow that it reads as a dark facial marking / mask spot rather than an ear. Fix: keep the size, move both back onto the crown, and push them OFF the silhouette so the outline of the head shows two cup arcs. (b) The face does not lack sharpness — it is over-sharp in the wrong way. The muzzle is a long, thin, near-parallel tube that projects well forward of the eye and ends in a small dark button nose, with no brow stop and no cheek mass. It reads shrew/anteater, not fox. A foxy marten face is a SHORT triangular wedge: broad at the cheeks and eyes, tapering over about half this distance, with a visible stop under the forehead. So 'no foxy sharpness' should be corrected to 'muzzle far too long and tubular; needs shortening into a broad triangular wedge with a defined brow stop.'

Net: aspect ~3 is roughly right, but zero of the three must-reads read, and the asset is not an independently drawn organism — it is the family chassis recoloured.

rows.readsAs: a pale grey-beige dachshund
rows.defect: The colour IS the mink and it is wrong: the render is a washed pale greyish-beige body with a slightly darker brown head, nowhere near glossy dark chocolate, and there is no sheen. No white chin patch is visible. The body is the family loaf on tall straight legs rather than elongate and low.

rows.verifyWhy:
Upheld, but the stated cause is only half right and the half that is wrong is the half a fix would be made against. Packet row (batch-001 #4): aspect 3.6, headFrac 0.21, mustRead = glossy dark chocolate fur / elongate low body / white chin patch. Two of the three must-reads are absent.

COLOUR - the judge said 'washed pale greyish-beige with a slightly darker head'. Pale is right, 'slightly darker head' is wrong and it matters. Sampled at 440x440: mid-body flank (230,200) #836B5E lum 111; upper back (200,190) #93837C lum 134; head cheek (310,168) #422C21 lum 48; shoulder (300,180) #604536 lum 74; muzzle #674D3D; tail (130,215) #745140 lum 87. A 16-bin histogram over the creature (10,102 non-background px) puts 60%+ of the fur in the lum 90-138 band (#785848 / #886858 / #887868 / #987868) and only 3.2% in the lum-43 chocolate bin. So the head is not slightly darker, it is 2.3x darker than the flank. The real defect is a TWO-TONE split: a mid-brown cap covering head + neck + hips + tail sitting against a pale sandy-tan torso tube, i.e. a bicolour animal, which no mink is. Uniformly multiplying the whole palette down would keep that split intact and still fail; the fix has to collapse the two tones into one dark #2E211A-#3A2A20 coat, then re-lift only cheek/flank highlights.

SHEEN - 'no sheen' is correct as a verdict but the judge missed the one specular element that IS drawn: a thin pale grey-lavender rim light runs the full length of the spine (edge pixels reach ~#B0B0B8, the ridge band reads #93837C). Against the pale body it does not read as gloss, it reads as a grey dorsal stripe - an added wrong marking, not a missing one. That rim needs removing/retoning, not brightening.

WHITE CHIN PATCH - absent, confirmed quantitatively. A scan of the whole creature box for px with R>200,G>195,B>190 returns exactly ONE pixel, at (318,172), and that is the eye catchlight. A 14x zoom on the chin/throat (x280-340, y160-210) shows lower lip, chin and throat all uniform brown #5A3C2C grading to #735D50 with no marking of any kind. The pale area below the jaw is just the body's tan fur, not a chin patch.

ELONGATE LOW BODY - this one partially reads and the judge did not credit it. The torso IS a long straight tube and the animal is unmistakably elongate. But 'low' fails: the legs are long, straight and pillar-like with open daylight under the belly (torso depth ~50px, belly clearance to ground ~32px, ratio 0.64 where a mustelid wants ~0.3), so it reads dachshund-on-stilts rather than low-slung. Measured silhouette bbox is x102-337 by y162-260 = 236x99, aspect 2.38 against the spec'd 3.6 - the short upcurled tail and the tall legs both eat the ratio.

OTHER DEFECTS THE FAIL DID NOT NAME, all visible at zoom and all needing fixes: (1) the torso is covered in a repeating brick/masonry hatch that reads as basketweave or brickwork rather than fur - it is the single most conspicuous thing on the body at full size; (2) head morphology is wrong for a mustelid - a large near-face-on rounded ear disc with a dark inner pit plus a second domed ear behind it, both far too big and too tall, where a mink's ears barely clear the fur; the muzzle is long, narrow and down-curved (shrew/opossum) instead of short and blunt; (3) a stray black arrowhead/chevron polygon floats on the left hind leg at approximately (185,243), unattached to any limb form; (4) the feet are pale pink-tan toed pads with drawn toe lines - mink feet should be dark and partly webbed; (5) the tail is a short upswept stubby paddle with a fringed underside, carried high, where a mink's is ~1/3 body length, fuller, and carried low.

rows.readsAs: a fat beige rat, or another dachshund
rows.defect: The tail is a thin bare rat-like curl that is narrow at the base and hooks upward — the opposite of the thick muscular tail that tapers from a wide root, which is the otter's signature. The body is a deep chunky loaf standing high on four column legs, not a sleek streamlined tube, and the muzzle is a narrow dog snout with no broad whisker pad and no whiskers drawn.
rows.fix: Replace the tail with a thick flattened cone as wide as the hips at the base, drop the belly to the ground and taper the torso continuously into the tail, and give the face a wide flat whisker pad with radiating pale whiskers.
rows.verifyWhy:
Viewed at 1x and at 5x/12x crops of head, tail and feet. The FAIL stands — two of the three must-reads ('thick tapering muscular tail', 'broad whiskered muzzle with tiny ears') are absent and the animal reads as a long-snouted dachshund/opossum loaf, not a river otter. But three parts of the stated cause are wrong and must not be fixed as described.

TAIL (must-read ABSENT, but not for the reason given). The judge says 'narrow at the base and hooked upward'. What is actually drawn: the tail attaches at the rump as a BROAD wedge — the widest point of the whole tail, roughly as deep as the hip is tall — and then IMMEDIATELY steps down to a constant ~5px sausage for its entire remaining length. So the base is not narrow; the defect is that there is no taper at all after the base, i.e. a wide anchor block abruptly bolted to a uniform tube with a blunt rounded tip. Direction is also mis-stated: the tail rises UP and BACK over the rump, arcs over the top, and then hangs DOWN in a question-mark hook whose tip points at the ground below the hock. It is not 'hooked upward'; it is raised then curled downward. 'Bare' is correct and is the sharpest part of the finding: the tail is flat solid mid-brown with zero fur strokes and zero shading, against a body that is heavily fur-textured, so it reads as rubbery/naked next to a furred animal. FIX: replace with a straight, thick, horizontally-trailing rudder that starts as thick as the hips and tapers continuously to a point along the ground line, dorsoventrally flattened, carrying the same fur texture as the body. Do not merely widen the existing curl.

MUZZLE (must-read ABSENT — judge correct). At 12x the head is a small smooth dome with a pencil-thin conical snout projecting far forward, roughly as long as the braincase and no wider than the eye, ending in a tiny dark nose dot. There is no whisker pad, no swelling, no vibrissae anywhere — I looked specifically for small strokes and there are none. A curved mouth line runs back from the snout base. This is a shrew/anteater snout, and it is the single feature that most destroys the ID.

EARS (judge omitted this — a CORRECTION in the asset's favour). 'Tiny ears' IS partially satisfied: there are two small dark brown ellipses on the crown, near-ear and far-ear, sitting flat on the skull dorsum behind and above the eye. They are readable as tiny ears. Their weakness is that they break the silhouette not at all — the head outline is a perfectly smooth dome — but do not report the ears as missing.

BODY (judge overstates). Measured: body length nose-to-rump ~160px, body depth ~48px, so aspect ~3.3 against the spec 3.2 — the RATIO is on target and 'chunky loaf' as a proportion complaint is wrong. What is wrong is the modelling, not the ratio: the topline is dead flat with a thin pale rim-light and no fusiform rise-and-fall, the belly is a flat-bottomed sag with a distinct shoulder hump and a separate hip lump, and there is no continuous head-neck-body taper — the head is stuck on the front of a barrel rather than being the leading point of a tube. So 'sleek streamlined tube' fails on contour, not on length.

LEGS (judge overstates). Ground clearance is ~20px against a 48px body depth (~0.4), so the legs are genuinely short, not 'column legs standing high'. They are, however, straight untapered vertical posts with no crouch and no visible flex; the pale cream feet do show splayed toe lines but no webbing. The posture problem is stiffness, not height.

A woodpecker's entire identity is a zygodactyl grip on vertical bark; here nothing is gripping.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DRAWN: a cream/bone-coloured earthworm in a ground-crawling S-curve, resting on a soft elliptical cast shadow. At the anterior there is a bulbous head knob roughly 1.4x the body diameter, and behind it a second smaller bulb, i.e. a two-lobed prostomium/peristomium head — worse than the claim states, which reports only one knob. Set on the upper-left of the front bulb is a single small hard black dot eye with a tiny specular highlight; the packet says eyes: hidden and the note says the animal has no eyes, so this is an explicitly contradicted feature, confirmed. CHASSIS: I rendered Ice_Worm.png and Marine_Worm.png at the same crop for comparison. All three are the identical body - same S-curve path, same head knob with the same black dot in the same place, same crescent-ring stack, same blunt tail stub. Ice Worm is the chassis in grey, Marine Worm is the chassis in pink with straight bristle spikes added, and Lancelet is the bare chassis in cream with nothing added at all. So the claim's phrase 'the cream-recoloured family annelid' is literally accurate: this asset carries zero species-specific geometry. MUST-READS, one by one. (1) 'translucent blade-shaped body pointed at both ends' - ABSENT on all three counts. The body is fully opaque cream against the dark ground with no see-through anywhere; it is a round tube, not a laterally flattened blade, and it has no dorsal fin fold or caudal fin. Correcting/extending the claim: the FAILURE IS AT BOTH ENDS, not just the head - the posterior terminates in a blunt rounded stub the same width as the body, so 'pointed at both ends' is missed at the tail as well as at the head. (2) 'rows of V-shaped muscle chevrons visible through the skin' - ABSENT. There are arcs on the body, and I looked hard at whether they could be read generously as chevrons; they cannot. They are transverse annuli lying perpendicular to the body axis, each a full crescent wrapping the tube with a cast shadow beneath it, and they are pixel-for-pixel the same rings that appear on Ice Worm and Marine Worm. Myotomes must be forward-pointing V/< blocks angled along the axis and seen THROUGH the skin; these are opaque surface segment collars. (3) 'fringe of oral tentacles where a head would be' - ABSENT. The head bulb is completely smooth-shaded; there is not a single tentacle, cirrus or filament anywhere on it. The note's 'stiffening notochord line running end to end' is likewise absent - there is no axial line of any kind. SECONDARY MISSES the claim does not mention: posture is specified 'swimming' but the asset is drawn crawling on a ground plane with a contact shadow; headFrac is specified 0.10 but the two-lobe head bulb occupies well over that and is emphasised rather than hidden; aspect is specified 7 but the body measured along its path is roughly 12-14 diameters long. Nothing in the claim is wrong. It reads as the wrong phylum on sight - an annelid, not a cephalochordate - and all three must-reads are genuinely missing, so FAIL stands.

rows.verifyWhy:
UPHELD, but two parts of the stated cause need correcting before anyone fixes this.

WHAT I ACTUALLY SAW (read at 1x, then cropped and nearest-neighbour upscaled 4x over the whole body and 10x over head / mid-back / tail): a khaki-taupe worm lying in a shallow S-curve, three-quarter side view, head at lower-left, tail at upper-right. The body is a stack of roughly 26-28 full-width crescent discs, each one lens-shaped and overlapping the next along the body axis so the topline scallops. A bulbous, near-spherical pale head cap sits at the front carrying one small dark eye with a white specular dot (eyes: small and headFrac 0.1 are both satisfied - those are the only reference fields this asset actually meets). The tail is blunt: the last crescent simply ends, no taper, no pygidium, no anal cirri. Roughly 30 straight red-brown rods, about one per segment, stand out along both flanks - vertical on the far side, splayed down on the near side. Cast shadow below, dark navy vignette background.

THE DEFINING MUST-READ IS ABSENT. 'Two rows of overlapping scale plates roofing the whole back' - the elytra, the feature the animal is named for - are not drawn. At 10x on the mid-back there is no midline, no left/right pairing, no second layer of geometry sitting on top of the dorsum, and no free posterior plate edges casting onto the segment behind. Every crescent is the full width of the tube and is the tube's own segment boundary. FAIL is correct.

CORRECTION 1 (the judge described the defect imprecisely, and the imprecision would misdirect the fix): they wrote 'no overlapping scale plates anywhere' and called the back 'plain crescent-ring segmentation'. The overlap IS there - the segment discs are drawn as genuinely overlapping shingled crescents with cast shading in each groove; that is why the topline is scalloped rather than smooth. What is missing is not overlap, it is the second, DORSAL layer: paired elytra, left and right of a visible midline, each an independent plate with its own outline and free trailing edge, roofing the back so the segments beneath are only visible at the flanks. Instructing an artist to 'add overlap' would change nothing, because the chassis already overlaps. The instruction has to be 'add a paired dorsal plate layer on top of the existing segment stack'.

CORRECTION 2 (an omission that changes the count of missing must-reads from three to two-and-a-half): the judge did not mention bristles at all. The third must-read, 'bristle tufts poking out between the scales', is PARTIALLY served - the ~30 red-brown rods are present on both sides and are read as bristles. But they fail in form as well as position: each is a single stiff rod, not a tuft or fan, and they emerge from the flank seam rather than from between dorsal plates (there are no plates for them to emerge between). Combined with the ball head, the evenly spaced rigid rods make the animal read as a millipede or a hairy caterpillar, not a scale worm.

CORRECTION 3 (the aspect charge is right in substance but overstated in degree): the reference asks for aspect 3, a short flattened oval. The rendered body is a round tube whose centreline arc-length to diameter is about 6:1 (tube diameter ~40-45px, arc ~250px), so it is roughly double the specified elongation - not the 8:1 to 10:1 of the rest of the family, but nowhere near a 3:1 oval. There is also no flattening at all: the head is shaded as a sphere and the trunk as a cylinder, so 'flattened oval segmented body' fails on the flattening as well as on the proportion.

SHARED-CHASSIS CHARGE CONFIRMED. I measured silhouettes: Scale Worm bbox 227x123px, Marine Worm bbox 216x126px, near-identical S-curve pose, identical crescent-disc construction, identical straight-rod bristles, identical blunt tail, identical ball head with one small eye. The only differences are hue (khaki vs pink) and a slightly thicker tube. Polychaete Worm is the same construction again on a flatter arc in orange. Three of the five assets in this family are one chassis in three colours, and Scale Worm - which is the one species here whose identity depends on a structure none of the others have - is the worst-served by that.

What this asset would need to pass: shorten to ~3:1, flatten the dorsum, and lay a paired double row of overlapping elytra over the whole back with visible plate edges, letting bristle tufts (not single rods) escape from the gaps between plates.
